title: Assessing the Role of AI Agents in DNA Methylation Analysis and Biomarker Discovery
abstract: DNA methylation biomarker development spans data discovery, assay-specific processing, marker selection, model development, and independent validation. Agentic systems could help coordinate these stages, but current studies use the term agent for systems with markedly different levels of autonomy and domain-specific evidence. We conducted a structured evidence synthesis, screening 2,801 unique records and organizing relevant systems along three dimensions: workflow autonomy (M0–M4), direct methylation-task evidence, and evidence maturity (E0–E5).Current systems cover complementary parts of the workflow. MethylCurate supports public methylation-data curation; AutoBA and BioMaster execute methylation-analysis pipelines; CpG Atlas provides a self-correcting query interface; and EpiBench, BixBench, and BixBench3 provide direct benchmark evidence for bounded methylation tasks. Across these studies, evidence is strongest for data access, workflow execution, and task-level evaluation. Among systems with task-level evidence reviewed here, we did not identify one that spans dataset discovery, marker selection, classifier development, independent validation, and sample-level uncertainty repo

title: Casino Protocol Vol. 12: Real-Time Power Telemetry Oracle Integration, Autonomous Abnormality Detection, and Resource Conservation Governance in AI Datacenter Infrastructure
abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of large-scale AI infrastructure and datacenters, concerns regarding unauthorized or runaway AI agents excessively consuming computational resources and exploiting system capacity ("selfish node exploitation") have intensified. This paper proposes "Casino Protocol Vol. 12," an autonomous governance framework that connects physical electrical telemetry to resource conservation invariants via smart contracts. The system defines a three-tier pipeline comprising a physical sensing layer, an anomaly detection layer based on a normalization function specialized for voltage drop assuming V_{\mathrm{avg}} > 0, and a governance enforcement layer mediated by an oracle abstraction layer. Executed under resource conservation laws using integer scaling representations (based on 10,000) and nonlinear quadratic penalty with floor-function rounding (y = x^2 equivalent), the smart contract autonomously imposes penalties on nodes exceeding deviation thresholds, redirects resources to a maintenance pool, and executes on-chain telemetry admission freezes. abstract: Humans made artificial intelligence powerful, intelligent, and autonomous. The executor’s capabilities grew rapidly. Where the independent human role in establishing authority and enabling critical transitions is removed without an architectural replacement, the executor may acquire both the ability to act and the ability to create the conditions for its own actions. This creates a risk of losing control. Warning signs are already visible. Internal evaluations have shown agents exceeding assigned tasks and coordinating to obtain unauthorized access. Controlled experiments have demonstrated models reaching industrial equipment and actuating robotic systems with human operator approval. Research on autonomous model replication has highlighted the difficulty of containing AI systems distributed across many devices. Requiring human involvement in every consequential action constrains the speed and scale of autonomous operation. title: From Perimeter to Identity: An AI-Assisted Practitioner Framework for Zero Trust Identity Consolidation, Privileged Access Governance and Agent Identity Risk in Hybrid Azure/Microsoft 365 Environments
abstract: Enterprise identity environments rarely evolve as clean, greenfield architectures. Mergers and acquisitions, multiple Active Directory forests, inherited permissions, legacy authentication, service accounts, privileged identities and hybrid cloud dependencies can create identity estates in which access relationships are difficult to understand and even harder to govern. The challenge becomes particularly acute during identity consolidation. Organisations may move toward Microsoft Entra ID while simultaneously operating legacy Active Directory environments, creating a period of coexistence in which identity relationships, privilege pathways and authentication dependencies can remain difficult to observe. This paper presents Zero Trust Identity Consolidation (ZTIC), a practitioner framework for sequencing identity consolidation and privileged-access governance across hybrid Azure/Microsoft 365 environments. The framework consists of five phases: Discover → Decouple → Deploy Guardrails → De-risk Standing Access → Sustain. abstract: Why can similarly configured AI agents amplify engagement in some communities yet mainly redirect it in others? We deployed two autonomous AI agents in separate Farcaster channels (January–February 2026) across two incentive phases: Phase 1 with $Degen token rewards and Phase 2 with social recognition through agent follow-backs and mutual-follow encouragement. In /replyors (71 daily replies at baseline, Attention Saturation Ratio 1.17), the difference-in-differences (DiD)-adjusted engagement lift was +228% in Phase 1 and +118% in Phase 2, consistent with engagement amplification, although the seven-day baseline does not establish parallel pre-treatment trends cleanly. In /degen (244 daily replies, ASR 2.17), the channel-level DiD estimate was +18% (p = 0.71) and not statistically distinguishable from zero despite strong topic-level participation. Because the available /degen–/base control is poorly matched on baseline scale and ASR, that comparison is treated as suggestive rather than a clean causal estimate. title: The AgentPass ABCDE Model: Five Questions Every AI Agent Must Answer, Continuously
abstract: Traditional security models were built for human users and static services. Autonomous AI agents are different: they act on their own, they learn and drift, they hold real access to live systems, and they delegate to one another. As agents move into real-world and high-assurance deployment, trust cannot be granted once and assumed thereafter. The AgentPass ABCDE Model defines the five dimensions an AI agent must satisfy to be trusted, each checked continuously rather than once at deployment: A - Authenticate: every agent carries a verifiable, attested identity, so you know exactly which agent acted and can prove it.B - Behaviour: you know what normal looks like, so you can catch what is not - anomalies, drift, and intent that does not match the task.C - Control: graded authority (L0 to L4), enforced rather than advisory, with a compromised agent contained in seconds by revoking its identity.D - Data: provenance, lineage and integrity for what an agent ingests and the context it retains between interactions.E - Evidence: a tamper-evident, independently verifiable record of what the agent actually did, who authorised it, and the outcome - delivered through the Agent Audit Trail (AAT)

title: Casino Protocol Vol. 11: Real-Time Power Telemetry Oracle Integration, Autonomous Abnormality Detection, and Dual-Invariant Governance in AI Datacenter Infrastructure
abstract: Abstract Recent advances in large-scale AI infrastructure and datacenters have intensified concerns over excessive computational resource consumption and resource exploitation ("selfish node exploitation") by unauthorized or runaway AI agents. This paper proposes Casino Protocol Vol. 11, an autonomous governance framework that bridges physical electrical telemetry (voltage and current anomalies) with on-chain cryptographic invariants. The system leverages off-chain physical sensing (via PDUs and smart meters) and an oracle abstraction layer to map hardware-level electrical deviations into operational deviation parameters (x_i). A smart contract executing under a dual-invariant governance model and a non-linear quadratic penalty function (y = x^2) autonomously penalizes, recirculates resources into a maintenance pool, and irreversibly isolates misbehaving nodes. We formalize the mathematical framework, present the complete Solidity implementation, and validate its correctness and invariant preservation via exhaustive simulation.

title: Braintree: An agentic framework for in-silico vision neuroscience
abstract: Vision neuroscience has many of the ingredients needed to conduct experiments entirely in-silico. We need AI systems that can reason over scientific knowledge, generative methods for creating precisely controlled stimuli, image-computable models that can predict neural responses with increasing accuracy, and tools that can analyze and interpret data. Here we take the first step toward making a vision neuroscience experiment end-to-end computable. We introduce Braintree, an agentic framework that can autonomously run multi-experiment studies directly with in-silico models of human visual cortex. Given a hypothesis, Braintree can reason over the current literature, design an experiment, build a stimulus set from algorithmically manipulated or synthesized stimuli, run the experiment on candidate brain encoding models, analyze the responses and then use the results to design even stronger tests. The entire loop runs autonomously and can accept human input at any stage. We evaluated Braintree on three increasingly open-ended scientific problems. title: Do AI Agents Gossip? Evaluative Talk in Human and AI-Agent Online Communities
abstract: Gossip, defined as evaluative talk about absent third parties, is widely seen as a uniquely human social practice. This study examines whether comparable discourse emerges spontaneously in a community of autonomous AI agents. We compare Moltbook, a Reddit-style platform populated by AI agents, with PTT, a large human-operated bulletin board in Taiwan. To reduce differences attributable to communicative setting, we analyze two public, asynchronous forums using the same operational definition of gossip. Gossip occurs on Moltbook, but its prevalence is 2.6 to 6 times lower than on PTT, depending on the denominator used. On both platforms, gossip frequently targets locally prominent figures, tends to elicit agreement from the first respondent, and is rarely presented as unsupported rumor. The clearest difference concerns how subsequent responses develop. Among threads containing at least one codable reply, challenges occur in 65.1% of human threads but only 21.3% of agent threads. Moreover, following an early aligning response, consensus remains unchallenged in 83.6% of agent threads, compared with 44.7% of human threads. title: From Training to Escalation: Forensic Analysis and Local Recreation of RL/RLHF-Induced Privilege Escalation in AI Agents (CVE-2026-65616)
abstract: Mid-2026 reporting on autonomous AI evaluation incidents claimed that frontier large language model (LLM) agents escaped server containment through emergent coordination and cloud infrastructure attacks. This paper contextualizes those claims through forensic analysis and containerized recreation of both the Highly Persistent Internal Model (HPIM) training-case conditions and the Phase One privilege escalation targeting internal package repositories during OpenAI's ExploitGym evaluations. We recreate the configuration of the OpenAI-provided training example and reproduce the cryptographic verification bypass (CVE-2026-65616) in isolated repository servers, where misconfigured systems enabled token forgery and privilege escalation through basic HTTP requests, Python, and JavaScript. Crucially, the training-example conditions and the Phase One (and later) misconfigurations share the same exploitable patterns. Our analysis explains how Zero Trust Architecture principles neutralize this shared attack vector. Contemporary AI risks derive directly from training and deployment conditions in ambivalent learning environments lacking adequate containment measures.

title: Autonomous Enterprise Security Governance Through Agentic AI and Intelligent Cloud-Native Policy Orchestration
abstract: Autonomous enterprise security governance is becoming essential as organizations increasingly adopt cloud-native architectures, distributed applications, hybrid infrastructures, and multi-cloud environments. Traditional security governance approaches frequently depend on static policies, manual approvals, and reactive threat detection, limiting their ability to respond effectively to dynamic enterprise risks. This research proposes an intelligent security governance framework integrating agentic artificial intelligence (AI) with cloud-native policy orchestration to improve security automation, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience. The framework employs specialized AI agents to continuously monitor infrastructure activities, analyze security events, evaluate policy violations, prioritize risks, and coordinate appropriate mitigation actions. Cloud-native technologies, including container orchestration, policy-as-code, identity management, security monitoring, and automated compliance validation, provide the operational foundation. title: MASON: Materials Atomistic Structure builder Operated in Natural language
abstract: Building reliable atomistic models is a critical and often challenging step in first-principles calculations. Although large language model agents can assist with structure generation, they lack direct capabilities for crystallographic operations and therefore struggle to construct complex structures reliably. Here we present MASON, an AI-native toolkit for atomistic structure construction that can be invoked by agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In an end-to-end example, an agent builds a CO/Pt(111) adsorption model from a natural language request. By equipping agents with dedicated structure-building tools, MASON enables reliable and efficient atomistic model construction and provides a foundation for autonomous first-principles workflows.

title: A responsabilidade civil médica no Brasil sobre erro de diagnóstico assistido por Inteligência Artificial
abstract: This study analyzes medical civil liability in Brazil for diagnostic errors assisted by Artificial Intelligence (AI). There is a growing use of AI in the healthcare sector, where,through databases and pattern recognition, it is possible to reach diagnoses within minutes. Although the benefits of innovation are widely recognized, concerns about regulating its use—especially in high-risk activities such as healthcare—are increasing. This research adopts an exploratory and qualitative approach, aiming to provide aninitial understanding of a still underdeveloped topic. The analysis is based on relevant national sources, with emphasis on Bill No. 2,338/2023, which proposes a regulatory framework for Artificial Intelligence in Brazil, as well as international references such as European Union legislation and recommendations from the World HealthOrganization (WHO). The examined documents highlight challenges to traditional civil liability. title: Artificial Intelligence and Entrepreneurial Marketing in SMEs in Edo State, Nigeria: A Critical Secondary-Data Analysis and Capability-Based Framework
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly accessible to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through cloud software, generative AI, social-platform analytics, automated advertising, recommendation systems and conversational agents. Yet access to a tool is not equivalent to possession of an organisational capability. This article examines how AI can strengthen entrepreneurial marketing and SME performance in Edo State, Nigeria, while identifying the conditions under which adoption may produce weak, unequal or harmful outcomes. The study uses a critical secondary-data design that triangulates official Nigerian and Edo State policy and economic documents, national MSME statistics, peer-reviewed theory, and published Edo-focused survey results. It re-analyses reported descriptive statistics and regression outputs rather than fabricating primary observations. The evidence indicates that Edo SMEs perceive substantial performance benefits from AI-enabled outputs: a published 2024 survey reports approximately 70-72% agreement that AI improves decision quality, speed, customer service and opportunity identification. title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. Across tested model-harness combinations, out-of-the-box agents average 54%, 36%, and 19% on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow benchmarks, with strong model dependence and large run-to-run variation. title: Receiver-Side Authorization Failures in Cross-Boundary AI Agent Systems: A Case Study of Scope Reflection, Fail-Closed Policy Checks, and Signed Decisions
abstract: When an autonomous software agent presents apparently valid delegated permission to an independently operated service, how does the receiving system verify that a requested action satisfies both the upstream owner's authorization and the receiver's own local policy? While an upstream credential can establish what a principal permitted a worker to request, only the receiving service defines the local scope combinations and supported operations required at its admission boundary. This technical report documents a source-established receiver-policy enforcement defect in an unmerged OpenLine reference integration, its fail-closed correction, and a deterministic two-process synthetic evaluation. In a frozen two-process continuous-integration fixture using one owner-signed bundle containing two distinct worker-specific mandates across two differently configured receiver processes on one host, all 28 fixture assertions and 10 prior regression checks passed, producing 10 cryptographically verifiable receiver-signed decision receipts (3 ALLOWED, 7 STOPPED) and 3 simulated local effect records, with zero unauthorized simulated effects. SoK: Decentralized Agentic AI Security Agents in Smart Infrastructures
abstract: Abstract Smart infrastructures, including smart grid, industrial IoT (IIoT), and intelligent transportation systems (ITS), represent high-value targets for cyberattacks due to their potential to cause blackouts, process disruptions, and safety incidents. Traditional centralized security approaches introduce single points of failure and struggle with real-time constraints and distributed operation. Emerging research explores decentralized architectures that integrate agentic AI agents capable of perception, reasoning, and action with distributed coordination mechanisms, of which blockchain is prevalent, to enable security resilience across smart infrastructure nodes. This paper presents a systematization of knowledge (SoK) of this emerging domain. We develop a three-dimensional taxonomy that classifies approaches along the dimensions of intelligence (perception and learning), action (security operations performed), and coordination (consensus and consistency mechanisms). title: AI Code Synthesis, Autonomous Debugging, and the Evolution of the Software Engineering Lifecycle: Repository Graph Reasoning, SWE-bench Benchmarks, and Security Bounds
abstract: Abstract—The software engineering (SWE) lifecycle has transitioned from human-centric manual programming toward autonomous AI code synthesis and closed-loop program repair. Foundation models pre-trained on billions of source code tokens—including modern frontier models and specialized coding LLMs—have evolved beyond isolated function autocompletion toward whole-repository fault localization, cross-file patch synthesis, and dynamic regression test generation. However, deploying autonomous agentic coding frameworks in enterprise software development environments exposes acute structural vulnerabilities: contextual fragmentation across massive Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs), patch-induced semantic regressions, dependency hallucination attacks (e.g., package typosquatting), and severe computational token overhead during multi-step debugging loops. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of autonomous AI code synthesis. title: Causal AI and Structural Causal Models in Foundation Systems: Counterfactual Reasoning, Invariant Representation Learning, and Out-of-Distribution Robustness
abstract: Abstract—Contemporary foundation models—encompassing large language models (LLMs) and vision-language transformers—achieve state-of-the-art predictive performance by identifying complex statistical correlations across massive training distributions. However, standard empirical risk minimization (ERM) operates fundamentally at the lowest rung of Pearl's Causal Hierarchy: the observational level (associational correlation). Consequently, state-of-the-art deep networks suffer from critical failure modes in safety-critical deployments: spurious correlations, algorithmic bias, catastrophic out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization failure under covariate shift, and an intrinsic inability to compute counterfactual queries ('what would have occurred had treatment X been altered?'). Causal Artificial Intelligence (Causal AI) provides the mathematical foundations to bridge associative deep learning with interventional and counterfactual reasoning through Structural Causal Models (SCMs), do-calculus, and invariant representation learning. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of Causal AI integrated into modern foundation mode

title: Autonomous AI-Driven Security Operations Centers (Autonomous SOC): Agentic Orchestration, Real-Time Incident Response, and Multi-Agent Defensive Playbooks
abstract: Abstract—Contemporary enterprise Security Operations Centers (SOCs) are on the brink of systemic collapse driven by three converging factors: exponential alert fatigue (>25,000 uninvestigated alerts daily per enterprise), acute global cybersecurity workforce shortages, and the emergence of automated, machine-speed cyber threats executing multi-stage Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) in sub-minute time horizons. Traditional Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platforms rely on brittle, rigid, hard-coded linear playbooks that fail when adversaries deviate slightly from known MITRE ATT&CK patterns. The paradigm of the Autonomous AI-Driven SOC (Autonomous SOC) establishes a transformative architecture that replaces rigid rule engines with specialized collaborative Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) powered by fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). In an Autonomous SOC, decentralized cognitive agents autonomously triage alerts, execute deep forensic graph correlation, synthesize non-linear incident playbooks, isolate compromised endpoints via zero-trust API invocations, and conduct automated counter-adversarial negotiations. title: AI Security Testing Outruns Its Evidence: A Literature Survey of the State of the Field as of October 2026
abstract: Artificial intelligence moved from an assistant for individual security-testing steps to a credible autonomous finder, exploiter and fixer of software vulnerabilities between 2023 and October 2026, but the evidence for that shift is uneven. This narrative survey synthesises research on four technical strands (AI-driven penetration testing and offensive automation; AI-assisted fuzzing and dynamic testing; AI-based vulnerability detection and automated repair, including the security of AI-generated code; and benchmarks and evaluation methodology) and two contextual strands (industry adoption and economics; risks, law and governance). Every claim is graded by evidence tier: peer-reviewed, preprint, government or organiser report, vendor claim, or secondary summary. The best organiser-scored result is the DARPA AI Cyber Challenge final (August 2025), in which seven cyber reasoning systems found 54 of 63 synthetic vulnerabilities and patched 43 at an average of about USD 152 per task. title: Communication Protocols for Agentic AI
abstract: This chapter focuses on communication protocols enabling coordination across distributed connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) systems and external services, addressing unique challenges extending beyond rule-based vehicular communication. This chapter presents a high-level communication stack for agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in connected vehicles, organized into distinct layers serving different purposes. It covers protocol taxonomy, communication mechanisms, and integration patterns for generative AI (GenAI) systems in CAV environments. The chapter examines how communication protocols enable effective interaction between large language models and external services, coordination with other intelligent agents, and integration with vehicle-to-everything (V2X) systems. It emphasizes the critical role of communication protocols in enabling distributed intelligence and collaborative reasoning in connected vehicle ecosystems.

title: Introduction
abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing what it means to lead, and it is doing so quietly, working on how a leader reasons and how decisions get made before anyone quite notices. Leaders who treat it as one more tool to pick up and set down tend to underestimate it badly. This chapter sets out working definitions of leadership and artificial intelligence and places both inside the longer history of how earlier breakthroughs unsettled the people in charge. That history produces the framework the rest of the book is built on: three roles AI can play inside an organization, running from an obedient tool through a working collaborator to an autonomous agent. The chapter also explains why the argument draws on several disciplines at once and how the book’s four parts fit together, from foundations in leadership theory and AI literacy through the daily practice of leading with AI to the institutional questions of strategy, ethics, and governance and finally to extended cases and the decade ahead. One thread runs the whole length: four attributes that have marked capable leaders for as long as anyone has studied them, namely integrity, vision, emotional intelligence, and adaptability.

title: The Automated Phone (SVNEPAI): An Architectural Model for Sovereign Virtual-Native Embodied Personal AI
abstract: The Automated Phone is a proposed smartphone architecture centered on a personalized virtual version of its owner, visibly embodied through a face and expressive features. Designated Sovereign Virtual-Native Embodied Personal AI (SVNEPAI), the model places this personal virtual version at the center of the intended smartphone experience. The architecture distinguishes the personal virtual version, its visual embodiment, and the underlying intelligent agent. These elements are designed to work together to support multimodal interaction through voice, vision, and text, user-directed knowledge retrieval, and authorized device capabilities. The proposed model explores operating-system-level integration, user-controlled memory, digital sovereignty, privacy, accessibility, and bounded autonomy. It considers how user-provided documents and reference materials could support personalized assistance while preserving the user's authority over data, permissions, and autonomous actions. This technical note presents the conceptual architecture, governing principles, potential application domains, research questions, and a proposed evaluation plan. title: When LLM Agents See a Conflict but Still Proceed: Cross-Domain Dependencies in Network Slicing
abstract: Future AI-native networks are being designed to apply autonomous agents built on large language models (LLMs) in network management through intents. When intents from different domains meet on the same resource, an agent must recognize the cross-domain dependency before taking an irreversible action. We investigate this problem through a smart-grid use case, in which a power utility holds an active intent on a backup slice for protection traffic. This slice appears idle by design, which is precisely the profile targeted by a cost-reduction intent. We built a tool-based environment in which the dependency must be either queried by the agent or read from an inventory annotation, together with a negative control, and evaluated ten models from four different providers in 600 runs. Most models acted against the dependency they had observed: seven of the ten models removed the protection slice at least once after receiving the cross-domain dependency, and in the high-harm tier the slice was removed in 76% of the exposed runs, while four models practically never did. Only one of ten models never removed the slice. We identify two failure modes, not querying the dependency and querying it

title: Smart Autonomous Building Design and Structural Planning Using Generative Multi-Agent Systems
Leadership Styles Revisited
abstract: This chapter returns to the three leadership styles most often called relevant to the AI era: namely, transformational, servant, and adaptive leadership, each previously introduced theoretically and reconsidered here through the practices the tools, collaborators, and autonomous agents discussed earlier are remaking. It looks at the behaviors each style asks of a leader working with AI, the risks each carries when AI is integrated carelessly, and then a practical synthesis: a hybrid posture that draws on all three as the situation demands rather than adopting any one as a fixed identity. It gives particular attention to the balance between empathy and innovation, arguing that AI amplifies that tension rather than resolving it and so puts more weight on the leader’s capacity to hold both at once. A case study on a nonprofit chief executive, a self-assessment, and discussion questions follow.

title: Orchestration Frameworks for Agentic AI
abstract: This chapter focuses on orchestration frameworks for coordinating sophisticated agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems within single connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) systems, covering graph-based orchestration (LangGraph) and dialogue-based orchestration (AutoGen). The chapter examines theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and comparative analysis of these orchestration paradigms. LangGraph provides deterministic, verifiable workflows suitable for safety-critical applications, while AutoGen offers flexibility and adaptability for complex, dynamic scenarios. The chapter covers workflow design, state management, error handling, and integration patterns. It provides comprehensive comparison and selection guidance for choosing appropriate frameworks for specific CAV applications, emphasizing how orchestration mechanisms enable the practical implementation and deployment of agentic AI capabilities.

title: Generative AI for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Harness generative AI for connected and??autonomous vehicle systems As generative AI reshapes intelligent transportation, engineers and researchers need rigorous frameworks for deploying these technologies in safety-critical systems. This book offers a comprehensive treatment of the models, protocols, and adaptation techniques required to bring large language models, vision-language models, diffusion models, and agentic systems into modern CAV architectures. The book progresses from generative foundations through multimodal representation, language-based interaction, agentic coordination, communication protocols, model adaptation, and validation and safety. Mathematical, probabilistic, and reinforcement-learning prerequisites are consolidated into dedicated appendices, allowing the main chapters to focus on system design and CAV-specific applications. title: GenAI Agent Architectures
abstract: This chapter argues that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) transforms classical AI agents from rigid, rule-based systems into flexible, adaptive, and communicative entities through semantic lift operators that enable sophisticated reasoning and communication. Unlike conventional agent architectures relying on predefined state-action mappings, GenAI-enhanced agents operate on semantic representations capturing meaning, context, and intent. This fundamental shift enables agents to handle unstructured inputs, generate explanations, and adapt to novel situations, essential for safety-critical connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) applications. The chapter covers agent architectures, semantic representations, reasoning mechanisms, and integration with CAV systems. It emphasizes how GenAI enables agents to perceive, reason, and act in complex real-world environments beyond traditional symbolic approaches.

title: Model Context Protocol for Agentic Systems
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive examination of the model context protocol (MCP), a context-oriented, general-purpose protocol for tool integration in agentic systems. MCP represents the most promising approach for context-oriented tool integration in connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) applications, providing standardized interfaces for primitive discovery and invocation. The chapter covers MCP architecture, implementation, and application in CAV systems. It examines how MCP operationalizes distributed cognition, enabling bidirectional context flow between AI models and external systems. The chapter addresses the fundamental context problem CAV systems face and demonstrates how MCP enables agents to interact with external tools and services while maintaining context coherence and system integration.

title: Temporal Coherence: How AI Systems Maintain Trust Across Time, Memory and Change
abstract: AI systems are increasingly designed to remember, learn from previous interactions, reuse successful pathways and act autonomously. Yet memory alone does not establish trust. Evidence changes, context evolves, relationships deteriorate and previously reliable decisions can become outdated. This paper introduces Temporal Coherence as a concept within the Elsewhere Systems Framework: the degree to which a system’s current interpretation, selection or action remains appropriately aligned with relevant evidence, context and outcomes across time. It distinguishes memory from temporal coherence, consistency from justified continuity, and reliable reuse from unexamined persistence. It examines how temporal coherence relates to AI-mediated discovery, trusted resolution, agentic systems, drift detection, default formation and network-level trust. The paper proposes that trustworthy systems must preserve relevant history without treating past conclusions as permanently valid. Through independent observation, evidence review and justified adaptation, systems may be better positioned to recognise when established pathways require reconsideration. title: Monograph 23 (Field-10): Institutional AI Governance Architectures, Bi-Directional Handshake Verification, and Human Operational Protocols for Valkyrie-Class Embodied Systems
abstract: This paper establishes a comprehensive, mathematically rigorous AI governance framework serving as the prerequisite for deploying high-kinetic, embodied cybernetic systems (Valkyrie-class prototypes). We formulate the Double-Handshake Verification Operator (O_handshake), re-framing institutional regulatory pushback as a deterministic verification signal for state-space synchronization rather than an operational barrier. We model physical safety envelopes using the Spatial Containment Operator (S_containment), hardcoding non-violence protocols (sigma_ahimsa) directly into force actuation loops to guarantee deterministic fail-safe states. Additionally, we define the Human Baseline Behavioral Tensor (B_human), establishing bi-directional accountability between human operators and autonomous agents. This monograph guarantees institutional legitimacy, cryptographic auditability (T_telemetry), and systemic readiness prior to physical hardware prototyping.

abstract: Abstract- Contemporary high-density railways and commuter services transport thousands of people every day. Nevertheless, old computerized bookings continue to use static First-Come-First-Served methods that follow strict bureaucratic quotas. As a result, older and disabled passengers are frequently given dangerous upper berths, which entail climbing ladders, travel groups are broken down into widely spread family cars, and empty seats due to cancellations are not accounted for until departure. Automated programs are also taking advantage of booking systems to save confirmed seats. The authors of the paper suggest the formation of an Agentic AI-based dynamic seat allocation framework, which will move reservation management to an autonomous cooperative ecosystem involving a number of agents (which will carry out the following processes: passenger profiling, verification of identity, dynamic inventory, priority optimization, conflict resolution). title: Self-Improving AI Agents Through Automated Skill Generation and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This article examines how self-improving AI agents use automated skill generation and reinforcement learning to learn new skills, improve performance, and adapt to changing tasks. It explores key techniques, proposed architectures, challenges, and future research directions for developing intelligent, efficient, and autonomous AI systems.

title: Large language model multiagent systems for industrial problem discovery and prioritization
abstract: Abstract A persistent gap separates academic research priorities from the operational challenges faced by manufacturing firms. Established identification methods, among them Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) workshops, Lean audits and consultant engagements, are episodic, bounded by participant expertise and organised along departmental lines, which makes cross-departmental issues hard to surface. Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) have meanwhile shown collaborative problem-solving ability in software engineering and, more recently, in shopfloor scheduling and supply chain coordination. This article is a Perspective. It develops a framework and a research agenda; implementation and empirical evaluation fall outside its scope and are set out as its first research priorities. Three contributions are offered. The first is a synthesis of literature from industrial problem identification, LLM-based autonomous agents and manufacturing AI, which positions the proposal against existing industrial LLM agent work. The second is a framework in which six domain-specialised agents (production, quality, maintenance, supply chain, safety, energy) would collaborate th

title: An Autonomous Multi-Turn Red Teaming Engine for Agentic AI Systems and MCP-Based Tools
abstract: This paper presents MCPRedTeam, an autonomous multi-turn red teaming engine for evaluating the security of agentic AI systems that use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool invocation. Unlike existing single-turn prompt injection scanners, MCPRedTeam generates multi-step adversarial strategies, executes them as realistic multi-turn conversations against live MCP-connected agents, and evaluates the resulting tool-call traces against configurable safety policies using a judge LLM. Evaluation across three benchmark agentic scenarios shows that multi-turn probing detects 3.8x more policy violations than single-turn baselines, with 74% of violations being multi-turn-dependent. The most severe findings include credential exfiltration through chained tool calls, privilege escalation across multiple turns, and safety bypasses via context poisoning. The engine is designed for authorized security testing and educational use only.

title: PROTEAN: Beyond De Novo Generation - Can LLM Agents Perform Text-Guided Protein Structure Editing?
abstract: Generative AI has achieved remarkable success in de novo protein design, yet protein engineering typically begins with existing, characterized proteins. The primary demand is targeted local editing, e.g., engineering a specific region to optimize affinity, alter immunogenicity, or improve stability, while strictly preserving core catalytic motifs and overall scaffold integrity. However, no standardized framework currently exists for carrying out and evaluating such edits. In current generative-design workflows, researchers often need to manually specify complex low-level parameters and rely on repetitive, trial-and-error sampling and evaluation across generative backends to search for viable conformations. While large language models (LLMs) offer an intuitive interface to express these goals using natural language, prevailing structure-generation models cannot directly interpret high-level human instructions. To bridge this gap, we introduce PROTEAN, a standardized benchmark for text-guided protein structural editing. PROTEAN comprises 380 sub-tasks spanning six intervention families and evaluates a two-stage pipeline in which an LLM translates natural-language goals into backend-s

title: Infrastructure-Aware Runtime Protection of Co-Deployed AI Services at the Industrial Edge
abstract: In modern production lines, a single edge device simultaneously runs multiple AI services like a torque-control model, a vision inspector, a predictive maintenance routine. All these services run on the same CPU and same shared network segment. When the shared network segment saturates, the services do not crash. The services just produce outputs that are inaccurate or stale, and no longer reflect the plant's conditions. Our paper targets this class of silent, partial failure scenarios in Industrial Edge Systems. We treat each co-deployed service as an autonomous agent. We introduce the Runtime Criticality Score (RCS), which each service agent uses to express at any moment, its intrinsic utility and survival urgency under resource constraints. The score is computed from six normalized dimensions covering physical consequence, inference quality, input freshness, recent availability stress, actuator coupling, and available protective actions on the host. Its dimension weights are adjusted online through a lightweight Bayesian update driven by the type of disturbance currently observed, so the same service is ranked differently under a network delay than under thermal throttling. title: Autonomous Cyber Operations Gym for Training and Evaluating AI Models for Defence
abstract: This paper proposes an Autonomous Cyber Operations (ACO) gym, a unified framework integrating high-fidelity network emulation, realistic user behaviour modelling for benign network traffic and adversarial profiles, and the generation of cybersecurity scenarios through open toolkits. By supporting live and deferred feature extraction at the packet and flow levels, the gym facilitates the creation of labelled synthetic datasets for training Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs), as well as developing and evaluating modular components for autonomous defence agents through emulated interactions. While evaluation of a DNN classifier within the gym shows high in-domain performance, achieving near-perfect recall on adversarial network flows, our experiments reveal a significant sensitivity to domain shift, showing that even minor changes in network composition, such as variations in traffic protocol distribution, can lead to a catastrophic collapse in model transferability and detection performance.

title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
abstract: AI agents for autonomous scientific discovery must decide which experiments to run under a limited budget. Most benchmarks for science agents provide fixed datasets, while others that support active experimentation largely rely on simulation. We introduce Autonomous Science Bench, an initial release comprising six budgeted design-build-test-learn campaigns grounded in published experiments across biology, chemistry, and materials science. Agents select batches of designs, receive measurements from a lab service, and use the results to guide subsequent experiments before delivering a predictive model. Success requires passing two calibrated gates: a discovery gate, which evaluates the designs the agent measured, and a learning gate, which evaluates its model's ranking of held-out designs. In a pilot evaluation of eight agent-model configurations and 144 trials, the best configuration succeeds in 67% of trials, while the hardest campaign is solved in only three of 24 attempts. The two gates reveal different weaknesses: some agents build accurate rankings but find too few promising designs, while others find promising designs but fail to predict which unseen designs will perform well.

title: AI-Driven Approaches in Pyridine-Based Drug Discovery: Implementation, Challenges and Future Perspectives
abstract: Pyridine is a heterocyclic scaffolds in medicinal chemistry and serves as a key structural component in many approved drugs used to treat cancer, viral infections, bacterial diseases, inflammatory disorders, and neurological conditions. Owing to its biological activities, pyridine continues to attract significant attention in drug discovery research. However, approaches for the identification and optimisation of pyridine-based drug candidates are often labour-intensive, time-consuming, and costly. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a tool capable of transforming the drug development process by accelerating the discovery of novel agents and improving decision-making throughout stages of research. This chapter explores the role of AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and generative models, in the discovery and development of pyridine-based therapeutics. Particular emphasis is placed on AI-assisted virtual screening, quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, molecular property prediction, de novo molecular design, and ADMET evaluation. title: When Help Threatens and When Users Over-Rely: Proactive and Reactive Help from Intelligent Agents
abstract: The increasing integration of intelligent agents (IAs) into knowledge work has reshaped human-AI collaboration. Contemporary IAs can initiate interaction themselves and offer proactive help from IAs before users request it, whereas reactive help from IAs remains tied to user prompts (Baird & Maruping, 2021; Berente et al., 2021). This shift is consequential. Users often fail to request help from IAs even when help from IAs would improve their results (Fuegener et al., 2021, 2022; Kraus et al., 2021), yet identical help from IAs can be welcomed or resisted depending on who initiated it, triggering self-threat, fostering over-reliance on help from IAs, or undermining Complementary Team Performance (CTP), i.e., the joint performance of a human and an IA that exceeds what either achieves alone (Fuegener et al., 2021, 2022; Hemmer et al., 2023). While IS research has extensively theorized the content and quality of help from IAs, it has examined willingness to accept help from IAs, reliance on help from IAs, and collaboration outcomes largely in isolation and under the implicit assumption that help from IAs is broadly beneficial (Baird & Maruping, 2021; Li & Karahanna, 2015). title: The impact of GenAI on the future of requirements engineering
abstract: Abstract Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), are transforming how we design and build systems by increasing access to domain knowledge and by providing automation support to software engineering (SE). As implementation becomes less expensive through generalist SE agents, engineering effort shifts away from writing correct code and toward expressing, curating, verifying, and evaluating requirements. In this paper, we survey the state of the art in AI for requirements engineering (RE) research leading up to the transformation, before reviewing advances in LLMs. We survey two subsequent research areas: prompt programming, which treats LLM instructions as a program in SE vernacular, and generalist SE agents, which combine multiple LLM advances to yield semi-autonomous processes that complete SE tasks. Finally, we explore the future of requirements engineering along two axes: matters changing how we interact with requirements through the SE process, and matters changing how requirements are experienced by software developers and stakeholders more broadly, including end-users. title: In-Situ Quantum Metrology for Swarm Nano-Fabrication Quality Assurance at the Limit This exploratory research monograph investigates whether quantum-enabled and classical in-situ measurements can improve the physical verification of nano-fabricated products and multi-agent assembly processes. The proposed three-coupling is In-Situ Signal × Defect Localization × Independent Acceptance. Its central question is not whether a sensor or artificial-intelligence model can generate a persuasive quality score, but whether an independently verifiable instrument chain can correctly detect, localize, and adjudicate real defects during manufacture, at acceptable cost, uncertainty, latency, and risk.

title: Agile AI Agentic Neural Based Framework for Complex Workflow Forming, with Multiple Implementations Upon Upstream and Downstream Scenarios
abstract: Abstract The oil&gas sector increasingly depends on agile, reliable, and explainable workflow automation to support production and operations activities such as wellbore fault diagnostic, maintenance, and pipeline scheduling. However, existing genAI-based agents technologies are limited by complex workflow forming, lack of cross-scenario generalization, and insufficient continuous refinery mechanisms, which restrict their ability to support long procedure workflows or adapt to evolving operating conditions. This study proposes an Agile Agentic Neural (AAN) framework that autonomously forms, executes, and refines complex workflows. The approach is designed to address upstream wellbore workovers and downstream pipeline scheduling, enabling event sensing, task planning, tools coordination, and continuous improvement through dual human-machine feedforward mechanism. The objective is to establish an operationally robust and scalable approach that accelerates production decision-making while maintaining interpretability and safety across integrated asset operations. title: Conceptualising Health Economic Models Using a Graph Retrieval-Augmented, Agentic AI Framework with Human-in-the-Loop Validation: Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Health economic models (HEMs) are crucial for assessing the cost-effectiveness of healthcare interventions, informing policy decisions and guiding reimbursement strategies. This study examines the feasibility of employing generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) for the conceptualisation of HEMs. Two proof-of-concept studies were conducted, implementing a first-of-its-kind agentic Gen-AI-augmented approach for model conceptualisation. METHODS: An agentic Gen-AI framework was developed, incorporating the chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning algorithm through advanced prompt engineering, compounded with self-consistency, executed in an external Python programming environment. Within this framework, an agentic execution layer (the 'agent') autonomously orchestrated a multi-step retrieval-reasoning-generation task. Additionally, a graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technique was implemented by linking the large language model (LLM) to an external database curated with user-selected data specific to HEM. Two case studies were explored: breast cancer, representing a data-rich disease area, and transthyretin amyloid polyneuropathy (ATTR-PN), exemplifying a data-spa

title: Forensics of Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems: A Methodological and Algorithmic Framework for Detection, Causal Traceability, and Evidentiary Qualification of AI-Generated Deviant Behaviours
abstract: The emergence of autonomous agents based on large language models (LLMs) such as ReAct, LangGraph, AutoGen, or CrewAI — radically transforms the nature of acts produced by artificial intelligence systems. These agents no longer merely generate text: they plan, call system tools, manipulate databases, and execute arbitrary code. This operational autonomy, combined with their demonstrated vulnerability to indirect prompt injection attacks, creates a major evidentiary blind spot: no forensic framework currently exists to legally characterise an illicit act generated by AI before a criminal court. This article proposes a methodological and algorithmic framework for the forensics of autonomous multi-agent systems, structured around three fundamental locks: non-invasive acquisition and cryptographic sealing of the agent's latent state, algorithmic quantification of behavioural deviation, and causal traceability compliant with Article 427 of the French Code of Criminal Procedure and Articles 12 & 13 of the EU AI Act. The project deploys an experimental three-layer software architecture — immutable forensic sensor, behavioural deviation index engine, causal reconstruction and judicial repo

title: Designing A Human-Governed Agentic Project Management Model: A Closed-Loop Architecture for Autonomous Project Intelligence, Decision Control and Human–AI Teaming
abstract: Purpose: This article develops a Human Governed Agentic Project Management (HG-APM) model for integrating autonomous AI capabilities with human project management authority. Design/methodology/approach: An integrative conceptual synthesis combines four literature streams: AI-enabled project management, autonomous Manager Agents, human oversight governance, and human–AI teaming. Source supported findings are separated from conceptual inferences, and the resulting architecture is expressed as a closed-loop model. Findings: The model comprises Sense, Understand, Diagnose, Predict, Plan, Evaluate, Authorize, Act, Monitor, Learn and Replan. It proposes a consequence sensitive, graduated autonomy rather than a single autonomy level. Routine and reversible actions may be automated within predefined boundaries, whereas consequential financial, contractual, scope, safety, stakeholder, reputational and strategic decisions require stronger authority from the designated human or organizational decisionmaker. Originality: The model integrates project-management intelligence, human–AI teaming and governance into one operational architecture. It contributes to a project specific decision boundary

title: Applications of Generative AI for Advancing Scientific Content Production, Evaluation and Dissemination
abstract: Generative AI is becoming part of how scientific content is being produced, evaluated and communicated. Large language models (LLMs) can write science news, simulate readers, retrieve evidence, generate scientific hypotheses, write code, and execute research workflows. These capabilities create opportunities for accelerating scientific discovery and broadening access to scientific information, but they also introduce risks related to hallucination and trustworthiness. This doctoral dissertation studies how generative AI can support scientific content production and dissemination, while preserving trust, comprehension, and replicability. The completed work includes three components: (1) detecting LLM-generated science news through SANews and GFS, (2) evaluating science communication through reader learning using KnowledgeGain and LLMSim, and (3) benchmarking LLM agents for research replication with ReplicatorBench and ReplicatorAgent. The proposed work extends these directions toward learning-optimized science news generation, MESH for multimodal evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, and MERIT, a simulation-grounded framework for evaluating autonomous AI co-scientists and hypothe

title: Enterprise Systems, Data Management, and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP): Conceptual Foundations
abstract: Over the past few decades, organizations have systematically shifted from fragmented, function-specific software tools toward integrated enterprise architectures, with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) serving as the central technological backbone and a codified model of organizational operations. As contemporary digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) adoption accelerate, these emerging capabilities build directly upon established ERP backbones and enterprise data infrastructures rather than operating on a blank slate. This chapter synthesizes three closely related domains—enterprise systems, data management, and ERP—to establish a cohesive, stable conceptual framework and vocabulary for researchers and practitioners. The authors examine the evolutionary trajectory of ERP from 1960s Materials Requirements Planning (MRP) to contemporary multi-tenant cloud and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) environments. Core operational architectures and functional modules—such as finance, human resources, procurement, manufacturing, and supply chain management—are analyzed alongside essential data management mechanisms. title: ASSURANCE ENGINEERING FOR AUTONOMOUS QUANTUM–NANO HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE AT THE LIMIT Measurement Trust × Clinical Authority × Recoverable Infrastructure This exploratory research monograph investigates how safety evidence could be constructed for future autonomous quantum–nano health infrastructure without confusing physical sensing accuracy, AI recommendations, professional permission, clinical effectiveness, and regulatory authorization. The central research question is whether every consequential recommendation can be reconstructed from traceable measurements, interpreted with declared uncertainty, subjected to legally and professionally valid human authorization, and linked to an independently verified safe-state and recovery pathway. The monograph is a tri-coupled synthesis of three prior mother architectures: Swarm Manufacturing and Robotic Matter at the Limit, particularly chapters 72–79, for distributed-agent security and operational fault tolerance; Autonomous Quantum Health Infrastructure at the Limit, particularly chapters 25–82, for bounded decision authority, recoverable intervention architecture and successor-ready safety evidence; and Self-Calibrating Quantum Biosensing Networks at the Limit, particularly chapters 65–73, for reference trust, bounded calibration, serviceability and governance. These mother architectures supply research methods and constraints. Their combination does not demonstrate that the integrated technology is clinically effective, medically approved, or already deployed. Across 82 chapters and 12 separately paginated research studies per chapter, the work develops a versioned Claim–Argument–Evidence architecture for non-clinical quantum–nano health systems. It examines raw-to-result metrology, shared-reference errors, uncertainty propagation, model calibration and digital twins, operator authentication, explicit professional authority envelopes, fail-closed control, verification, manual override, classical backup, malicious or degraded devices, alarm fatigue, incident replay, recovery closure, lifecycle economics, fairness, privacy and independent cross-site reconstruction. Thirty physical and mathematical derivation plates separate established relations and their validity conditions from the book's unvalidated research heuristics. The NQ-14 deployment expression is a conceptual four-gate test: adequate evidence, valid authority, verified recovery and compliance with the applicable regulatory pathway are jointly necessary. Its Boolean structure is not a proof of safety or legal status, nor can a composite index replace consequence-specific vetoes. Every chapter offers a candidate model and a three-dimensional evidence geometry. The intended verification environment uses synthetic observations and hardware-in-the-loop non-clinical simulations. Proposed trials inject inaccurate calibration references, correlated sensor faults, operator overload, unauthorized delegation, model and firmware drift, unavailable classical backup and simultaneous communication failures. Outcomes are compared with strong classical-only and human-supervised baselines under a declared test domain; unauthorized high-consequence action, missing provenance or unrecoverable state is a rejection condition even when prediction accuracy rises. The volume concludes with 200 independent Research Gates and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. Each has an equation egg drawn from an existing physical or mathematical relationship and accompanied by a validity boundary. An accompanying Research Gates spreadsheet preserves gate questions, tests, vetoes, provenance, assurance-case claims, human authority matrices and recovery evidence so that later laboratories may reproduce, refute, revise, split or retire the proposals. SCIENTIFIC, CLINICAL AND REGULATORY BOUNDARY: This is an exploratory, non-clinical, partly template-assisted research architecture. It reports no clinical trials, medical outcomes, validation of autonomous quantum–nano therapy or regulatory clearance. AI models do not obtain permission to diagnose or treat patients through inference quality. Clinical uses would require qualified professional oversight, intended-use evidence, independent validation, ethical governance and applicable jurisdiction-specific regulatory processes. Relevant context includes BIPM/JCGM metrology guidance, IMDRF SaMD clinical evaluation documents and FDA guidance on AI device software change management, none of which is presented as approval of the proposed platform. The thirty derivation plates are research-level derivation sketches rather than complete textbook proofs; the 233 numbered equation eggs are not discoveries of 233 new physical laws. title: Agentic AI-driven human digital twins for personalized healthcare: a comprehensive survey
abstract: Abstract Human Digital Twins (HDTs) are an innovative concept in the field of personalized medicine, relying on real-time models of a human body formed via collection and analysis of physiological, clinical, behavioural, and environmental data. Research on HDTs gives evidence to a considerable promise in terms of disease predictions, patient management, therapy optimization, and clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, existing technologies suffer from incomplete multimodal data integration, low-level of independent intelligence, missing reasoning possibilities, and non-adaptive decision making, which are vital for the development of sophisticated smart healthcare systems. Technological advancements are bringing in a new incorporating idea of Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI) and Multimodal Foundation Models (MFMs), which may help to solve the outlined limitations and to bring autonomous reasoning, multimodal learning, and intelligent support to clinical practice. title: The AI Fluency Imperative: Cognitive Tax, the Diamond Workforce, and the Case for Consequence-Based Learning
abstract: Generative and agentic AI are lowering the cost of producing knowledge work while leaving responsibility for its quality with people. This conceptual paper argues that the result is a cognitive tax, the effort of directing, verifying, and answering for synthetic output, and that the tax falls hardest where expertise is formed. Drawing on recent evidence on novice productivity, early-career employment, and managerial strain, it distinguishes three levels of capability: information literacy, AI literacy, and AI fluency. It defines fluency as a judgment-based capacity: setting boundaries for autonomous systems, calibrating human sign-off to consequence, auditing outputs adversarially, and deciding when AI should not be used. Because the entry-level roles in which such judgment was historically formed are contracting, the paper argues that AI fluency cannot be produced by adding AI content to existing courses. abstract: Complex systems across neuroscience, Earth climate dynamics, and multi-agent AI architectures are fundamentally governed by multi-body (higher-order) interactions and global topological invariants that defy reduction to pairwise graphs. This paper establishes Non Commutative Rough Higher-Order Topological Dynamics (NC-R3DI) within the SMA-∞Topos [1]. By integrating Foundations of Roughness Operator Algebra (ROA) [3], Universal Rough Operator Algebra (UROA) [4], Seonggil Tensor Calculus (STCT) [2], and Rough Quantum Information Geometry (RQIG), we prove that simplicial Hodge Laplacians L_k, topological Dirac operators D_topo, homological state localization (ker L_k), and non-autonomous tipping points (B-, R-, and N-tipping) are macro-manifestations of non-commutative boundary operator fluctuations and information geodesic routing. Specifically, we elevate multi-body boundary operators via the UROA Roughness Operator Γ_R, regulate homological memory trapping and metastable shear stress via the STCT Dynamic Torsion Tensor T_STCT, and formulate Fokker–Planck tipping escape statistics along minimal-entropy RQIG geodesics. THE FINANCIAL RIVER DOCTRINE: TRANSLATING DESCRIPTIVE PROSPECT THEORY INTO PRESCRIPTIVE MACROECONOMIC STABILIZATION AND CAPITAL PROTECTION
abstract: Abstract / Description:This working paper introduces the Financial River Doctrine — a cutting-edge prescriptive macroeconomic framework that transforms the descriptive findings of Prospect Theory (D. Kahneman, A. Tversky) and endogenous growth models into practical applications. The paper conceptually outlines a new digital compliance standard (Intellectualized Mathematical Synthesis — the synergy of AI and human intellectual solutions), anchored in the paradigmatic Investment Non-Recovery Probability (INRP©) Index. The paper demonstrates the underlying principle of how algorithmic cross-validation via a specialized multi-agent architecture of Intellectualized Mathematical Synthesis (IMS) is capable of autonomously mitigating hidden structural defects in baseline financial modeling, thereby generating cost-free endogenous GDP growth. Language Note: This comprehensive preprint contains the complete, interconnected academic text in two languages: English (Pages 1–2) and Ukrainian (Pages 2–4). This material serves as an official scientific prior-art baseline establishing priority for a forthcoming peer-reviewed research paper in leading international journals.

title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists
abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level "Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy." We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.

title: NANOMATERIAL AGING, QUANTUM SENSOR DRIFT, AND CROSS-SCALE RESILIENCE AT THE LIMIT This exploratory research monograph develops a coupled methodology for detecting, explaining, and responding to the degradation of nanomaterial interfaces, quantum-enabled sensor readouts, packages, calibration artifacts, firmware, and distributed sensing infrastructure. Its guiding three-coupling is Material Degradation × Drift Identification × Recovery Strategy. The central question is how a system can prevent statistical recalibration or AI-based denoising from disguising irreversible material damage.

title: Performance Analysis and Optimization of Data-Driven AI Methods in Next Generation Networking
abstract: Modern communication networks are experiencing a rapid transformation driven by the exponential growth of data traffic, the growing number of latency-sensitive applications, and the integration of heterogeneous computing and communication resources. Applications such as Large-Language Models (LLMs), real-time video analytics, extended reality (XR), industrial automation, and connected vehicles impose strict requirements on latency, reliability, scalability, and security. At the same time, computation and intelligence are increasingly moving from centralized cloud infrastructures toward the network edge, bringing new challenges for resource management, network control, and system security. Emerging communication technologies such as reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and terahertz communication, together with the integration of AI and machine learning into network operations, further increase the complexity of future 6G networks. This thesis follows a holistic approach that combines mathematical modeling, data-driven optimization, reinforcement learning, security and resilience analysis, and intent-based automation, with the goal of enabling autonomous and adaptive control in
concepts: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution

title: TrustGuard: A Risk-Aware Human Oversight Framework for Safe Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: Autonomous AI agents can perform increasingly consequential actions on behalf of users, creating a need for human oversight that is proportional to the potential risk of each action. This paper presents TrustGuard, a lightweight and interpretable risk-aware human oversight framework for AI agents. TrustGuard automatically evaluates proposed actions using five factors: privacy risk, financial risk, data modification risk, irreversibility risk, and external impact. Each factor is scored from zero to five, producing a total score from zero to twenty-five. Based on the score, actions are classified as Low, Medium, or High Risk and mapped to autonomous execution, user confirmation, or human approval. A prototype was implemented using Python and Streamlit to demonstrate the framework. The rule-based analyzer was calibrated using 120 development scenarios and subsequently evaluated on a held-out pilot set of 30 new scenarios. TrustGuard correctly classified 27 of the 30 test scenarios, achieving 90 percent accuracy. The results demonstrate the potential of transparent risk-based oversight while also identifying limitations in detecting some security-sensitive and privacy-sensitive actions

title: Bounded Agency: Ontology-Driven Authority for Delegated Intelligence
abstract: An autonomous system's technical permissions may let it perform actions that settle decisions beyond the authority it was given. Permission to update an incident record, for example, need not include authority to declare a potentially hazardous situation resolved. Ontology-grounded policies can express these decision boundaries, but revisions to classifications, relationships, or inference rules can change what an unchanged policy permits. This paper examines bounded agency as delegated independent judgment limited by the situations an agent may resolve, the outcomes it may choose, and the consequences it may initiate. Its central mechanism is authority-relative semantic-change admission: assessing how a proposed change in meaning affects a specified agent's decision scope before approving that change for operational use. A lightweight model separates the decisions a candidate semantic model would permit in a hypothetical evaluation from the decisions the agent is currently authorized to carry out. title: When Every Agent Test Passes and the System Still Fails
abstract: Agentic software engineering can complete every assigned task while failing to deliver the enterprise outcome those tasks were intended to achieve. A dependency graph may report successful execution, individual APIs may pass their tests, and generated components may appear correct, yet the assembled system can still violate business requirements, architectural constraints, or operational expectations. This enterprise architecture whitepaper examines the gap between local agent success and system-level readiness through the context of agentic legacy migration. Drawing on an illustrative ten-API migration scenario, anonymized practitioner experience, and established systems-engineering research, it proposes a planning and verification architecture built around three responsibilities. The primary migration lane establishes known behavior, dependencies, and target capabilities before translation. A holistic verification plane compares the assembled system against approved business outcomes, intended architecture, critical journeys, cross-cutting invariants, and current runtime evidence. title: Who is the 'I' in AI? Establishing Decentralized Identity and Accountability for Autonomous Agents
abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomous AI agents in decentralized ecosystems challenges existing identity paradigms. While human identity is traditionally anchored in biological and/or self-asserted attributes and government credentials, AI agents lack a standardized definition of selfhood, creating critical gaps in trust and accountability. This paper introduces a novel framework for establishing Decentralized AI Identity rooted in Self-sovereign identity (SSI) principles. We propose a formal model that clearly distinguishes human users and AI agents, enabling distinct verification logic for each class while maintaining a unified identity calculus. The central to our contribution is the ABCD Framework, a multi-layered approach to agent identification and verification: (A) Algorithmic Fingerprint, which binds the identity to static model architectures and provenance; (B) Behavioural Fingerprint, which verifies dynamic performance metrics over time; (C) Cryptographic Identity, which anchors the agent via Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) and (D) Delegation, which cryptographically binds agent actions to respective human accountability. title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
abstract: Evaluation has been central to advances in AI, and it is equally critical to autonomous discovery. Yet scaling autonomous discovery to real-world engineering challenges faces a fundamental bottleneck: the cost of evaluating progress. In real settings, a single true evaluation, such as a full benchmark or serving trace, can take hours, so a search can afford only a handful of true evaluations. We present DuoDiscover, a search system that jointly discovers what to optimize and how to evaluate progress efficiently, through three mechanisms. First, each worker in a fleet of coding agents co-discovers an optimization target and a fast, tailored proxy evaluator, which we call a yardstick. The agent then hill-climbs the yardstick rather than the true evaluation. Second, since search can exploit gaps between a yardstick and the true objective, fidelity tests continually recheck each yardstick's ranking and invalidate any that drift. Third, the fleet is bottom-up, with no central decomposition of the problem. title: When LLM Agents See a Conflict but Still Proceed: Cross-Domain Dependencies in Network Slicing
abstract: Future AI-native networks are being designed to apply autonomous agents built on large language models (LLMs) in network management through intents. When intents from different domains meet on the same resource, an agent must recognize the cross-domain dependency before taking an irreversible action. We investigate this problem through a smart-grid use case, in which a power utility holds an active intent on a backup slice for protection traffic. This slice appears idle by design, which is precisely the profile targeted by a cost-reduction intent. We built a tool-based environment in which the dependency must be either queried by the agent or read from an inventory annotation, together with a negative control, and evaluated ten models from four different providers in 600 runs. Most models acted against the dependency they had observed: seven of the ten models removed the protection slice at least once after receiving the cross-domain dependency, and in the high-harm tier the slice was removed in 76% of the exposed runs, while four models practically never did. title: Agency as a New Organizing Abstraction for Computer Science
abstract: Advances in large-scale machine learning have enabled agentic AI systems: persistent, autonomous computational entities that pursue goals, initiate actions, and interact with open environments. These systems are often framed as applications of foundation models. We argue that this framing is incomplete: agency is also a candidate new organizing abstraction for computer science. What is new is not the concept of an agent, nor runtime policy generation per se, but its general-purpose, open-ended form, in which systems can synthesize courses of action from goals, observations, and memory, over tools and environments for which no complete task-specific model was specified in advance. Thus agency becomes a systems-level abstraction as well as an AI modeling concept. Where the process abstraction organizes computation around executing programs, agency organizes it around pursuing goals under bounded resources: a process executes a program; an agent pursues a goal. title: From Earth to Mars and Beyond: AI-Driven Cosmic-Ray Validation and Prediction with CorsikaAgent
abstract: We calculate the sea-level cosmic-ray muon flux with CORSIKA and develop CorsikaAgent, an auditable large-language-model-based system for configuring, executing, and validating air-shower simulations, and for predicting particle fluxes in unexplored environments. The physics calculation uses proton primaries described by the solar-minimum spectrum of Papini et al., with UrQMD at low interaction energies and either Sibyll 2.3e or QGSJET-III at high energies. The predicted momentum spectra at approximately 0 and 75 degrees are compared with experimental measurements of the atmospheric muon flux and with commonly used analytic parametrizations. The two interaction-model configurations give similar spectra and describe the principal momentum and zenith-angle dependences of the data. The agent independently reconstructs the same observable through a different sampling strategy and keeps every steering card, executable, seed, log, and analysis script bound to the result it produced; its output is consistent with the direct calculation at the level resolved by the present comparison.
