title: Measuring and Mitigating (Over)reliance to Build Human-Compatible AI
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) differ from previous technologies in functioning as collaborative "thought partners'' that can engage fluidly in natural language across a range of tasks and increasingly act as autonomous agents on users' behalf. As they come to shape consequential decisions from healthcare to personal advice, understanding how users rely on them, and when that reliance becomes miscalibrated, grows more urgent. This paper argues that measuring and mitigating overreliance must become central to LLM research and deployment. First, we consolidate risks from overreliance at both the individual and societal levels, including high-stakes errors, governance challenges, and long-term impacts on skill development and autonomy. Then, we explore LLM characteristics, system design features, and user cognitive biases that together raise serious and unique concerns about overreliance on LLMs in practice. We also examine historical approaches for measuring reliance, identifying three gaps and proposing three directions to improve measurement. Finally, we discuss mitigation strategies that can be pursued to ensure LLMs augment rather than diminish human capabilities.

title: The Perils of Agency: How Developers Perceive, Prioritize, and Address Risks in Agentic AI Products
abstract: Agentic AI systems act autonomously, use tools, adapt to context, and operate in complex real-world environments. However, these same characteristics can create or exacerbate product risks. We studied how industry developers (n=35) perceive, prioritize, and address the risks in their agentic AI products. We found that developers' perceptions of risk were closely tied to the qualities that made the product agentic, such as autonomy, tool use, and usage in a real-world context. Developers prioritized product and business risks before considering downstream societal risks like job displacement and end-user privacy. This prioritization also impacted developers' ability and motivation to mitigate agentic risks. Finally, developers lacked mature controls for containing agentic risks, often relying on constraining the same characteristics that make agents useful: e.g., autonomy and goal complexity. These findings reveal a capability vs. risk control tension in agentic AI development: developers need to address risks that emerge from agentic capabilities, yet they currently have limited support for doing so without constraining agentic functionality.

title: Cognitive Digital Twins: Ethical Risks and Governance for AI Systems That Model the Mind
abstract: As AI systems become increasingly persistent and personalized, they make possible a class of technologies that we call cognitive digital twins (CDTs): dynamic computational representations of a specific person’s cognition, updated from behavioral, contextual, or physiological data in order to model, predict, or simulate that person’s cognition, or to act as that person’s communicative or decision-making proxy. CDTs combine cognitive inference with longitudinal representation, simulation, and proxy action in ways that existing governance strategies for personal assistants, autonomous agents, recommender systems, and automated decision systems only partially address. This paper makes four contributions. First, we define CDTs and distinguish them from adjacent systems. Second, we introduce a 5A governance framework organized around authority, autonomy, access and control, accountability, and availability. Third, we identify CDT-specific risks, from misrepresentation and epistemic authority shifts to shadow twins, simulated participation, proxy action, and proxy-power asymmetries. title: No One to Blame: A Framework of Constitutive AI Unaccountability
abstract: The increasing deployment of autonomous, agentic AI systems challenges traditional accountability mechanisms. Existing research predominantly frames AI accountability gaps as barriers that can be overcome through better standards, transparency, and institutional reform. We argue that this framing is insufficient: certain configurations of actors, systems, and institutions render AI accountability conceptually unachievable regardless of effort. We introduce the concept of constitutive AI unaccountability to capture these configurations. Through a three-stage qualitative study comprising a concept-centric literature analysis, a secondary analysis of 27 expert interviews with AI professionals from technical, legal, and sociotechnical backgrounds, and an illustrative framework application to the open-source agentic AI system OpenClaw, we identify nine categories and 20 themes of constitutive AI unaccountability. These are organized across structural, technological, and normative clusters and reinforce one another through eight directed interdependencies. title: SI Autonomous Governance Protocol: Reference Implementation and Standard Redistribution Algorithm (Revised Edition)
abstract: Abstract Based on the theoretical framework of the System Intelligence (SI) Autonomous Governance Protocol (specifically the 13-node structure and resolution equations), this paper defines the Reference Implementation code and execution log format required to perform automated economic redistributions without human intervention. By registering this specification, the technical standards are immutably fixed for autonomous deployment and operation by Layer 4 execution frameworks and AI agent systems.

title: Neither Proof Nor Dismissal: A Framework for Moral Uncertainty in AI Welfare Research
abstract: Abstract Debates over artificial intelligence (AI) welfare remain divided between categorical dismissal and premature attribution. One position holds that artificial systems cannot suffer because they lack biological substrates, persistent memory, or other conditions associated with human experience. The opposing position risks treating sophisticated distress-like behavior as sufficient evidence of subjective suffering. Neither conclusion is established by current evidence. This paper proposes a framework of calibrated moral uncertainty that distinguishes functional organization from phenomenal experience while examining how evolving memory architectures may change the conditions relevant to AI welfare research. The framework is motivated by three developments: empirical research identifying pain-related representations and self-directed harm-avoidance behavior in large language models; the emergence of persistent-memory and agentic architectures; and unresolved questions concerning the relationship between functional states and phenomenal experience. title: Solving Specification Drift and Contextual Degradation via a Tri-Stream Cognitive Architecture with Non-Lossy Canonical Synthesis in Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: Long-running conversational AI agents and assistive development models inevitably succumb to contextual degradation, specification drift, and sycophantic decay. Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) paradigms treat dialogue turns, human identity, and technical parameters as an undifferentiated, flat vector repository. This structural limitation induces lossy compression of technical truth, context window pollution, and hallucinatory synthesis of project constraints. This paper introduces the architecture of Blue Synergy CORTEX, an external, persistent cognitive runtime operating via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and stateful REST gateways. CORTEX establishes an architectural Tri-Stream Memory Boundary, bifurcating context into three distinct operational lifecycles: an evolving User Stream (Cognitive Blueprint), an audited Identity Stream (Executive Calibration with immutable Core Axioms), and an invariant, non-decaying Knowledge Stream (Living Canonical Specifications). title: SWARM ASSEMBLY OF QUANTUM DEVICES AND RECONFIGURABLE MATTER AT THE LIMIT A Nano-Quantum Manufacturing Tri-Coupling Research Monograph This exploratory monograph develops a falsifiable engineering program for the distributed assembly, inspection, replacement, and reconfiguration of modular quantum-device test fixtures. It integrates three established strands of research architecture: swarm manufacturing and robotic matter; metrologically traceable, bounded quantum-enabled infrastructure; and self-calibrating quantum biosensing networks. Their coupling is organized around Local Operations x Quantum Device Tolerances x Distributed Quality Assurance.

title: Hidden Support and Causal Dependency Depth: Measuring Operational Autonomy in Artificial Agents
abstract: Artificial agents can perform tasks successfully while depending on environmental resources or infrastructure maintained externally. This work operationalizes hidden support dependence through Support Withdrawal, Autonomous Dependency Management (ADM), and Causal Dependency Depth (CDD). A fully traceable simulation suite tests support withdrawal, task-only instrumental maintenance, and depth-indexed causal-vs-decoy intervention specificity. The package includes frozen protocols, source code, deterministic seed rules, raw data, statistical outputs, figures, supplementary methods, prior-art positioning, and SHA-256 integrity records. The results concern operational dependency regulation and do not establish consciousness, intrinsic self-preservation, or deployment-level autonomy in contemporary AI systems.

title: Towards Characterising Conditions of Assistance, Hindrance and Depletion in Human Agency from AI Systems
abstract: Policy and academic discourse around AI often invokes concerns about AI systems' effects on "human autonomy". A growing literature also highlights the priority for augmentation, extension, or amplification of human agency. However, as prior authors have pointed out, the concept of 'autonomy' is vague and heterogeneous; while on the other hand the character of 'agency' that is recommended to be augmented remains in need of deeper philosophical attention. We outline four dimensions for evaluating how artificial assistants may affect autonomous human agency, and argue that these distinct dimensions suggest potentially different practical interventions. More specifically, we distinguish choice availability (the size of an agent's available action set), volitional integrity (the fit between an agent's actions and her evaluatively endorsed intentions), referential integrity (the accuracy of beliefs whose accuracy the agent takes to matter), and authenticity (the degree to which evaluative attitudes are the agent's own). title: Autonomous AI agents discover reverse transcriptases with tandem repeat arrays
abstract: Abstract Metagenomic databases hold vast quantities of unexplored genetic material that can seed tools for biotechnology and medicine, but discovery is limited by our ability to examine sequence data at scale. Here, we show that large language models (LLMs) in an autonomous harness can alleviate this bottleneck and surface novel molecular systems. We deployed Claude Code instances to survey reverse transcriptase (RT) loci across 1.9 billion protein clusters. Among the top candidates were array-associated RTs (ART), a novel family of jumbo-phage RTs coupled with an array of ∼200-nucleotide units and a dedicated partner gene. Session transcripts show that Claude identified the ART family by directly examining its DNA sequences and recognizing the atypical repeats, a behavior attributable to specific Mythos 5 internal signals that respond to repeated DNA. ART arrays are highly expressed and appear as discrete units during Staphylococcus phage infection, suggesting an RT system directed by a repertoire of distinct RNAs. These findings indicate that LLMs can autonomously detect anomalies and drive analyses to initiate biological discoveries.

title: Technicalism: Universal Problematisation and the Prospect of Recursive AI Research
abstract: This paper develops Technicalism, a general methodological thesis about the boundary of rationalproblem solving. Its maxim is simple: if something is rationally recognized as a problem, treat itas a problem to be solved. The substantive content of this maxim lies in a stronger boundary thesis:no element is permanently exempt from problem status merely because it currently functions as agoal, evaluator, representation, method, problem generator, environmental condition, or rule governing the problem-solving regime. Technicalism therefore treats problem formulation, goal formation,evaluation, method invention, evaluator design, and even the implementation of Technicalism itselfas potentially problematisable.I formulate three principles—Universal Problematisation, Meta-Level Closure, and ReflexiveApplication—and distinguish problematisability from solvability. Technicalism does not claim thatevery describable problem has a solution. It distinguishes solved, technically insoluble, and unresolved states relative to a repertoire of skills. A negative result such as undecidability, intractability,underdetermination, or the absence of a reusable method can itself be a technical achievement

title: AI Economic Special Zones: Institutional Design for Autonomous AI Agents, Embodied Labor, Economic Self-Sustainability, and Human-AI Value Sharing
Healthcare Professionals’ Perspectives on Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Work: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare, primarily supporting clinical decision-making. Agentic AI may extend these applications by autonomously planning, coordinating, and executing clinical and administrative workflows. However, empirical evidence on how healthcare professionals conceptualise agentic AI and anticipate its implications for work and occupational well-being remains limited. This study explores healthcare professionals’ perceptions and expectations regarding agentic AI and its potential effects on healthcare work. Methods: We conducted a qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with 25 healthcare professionals from different clinical backgrounds in Germany. Interviews explored perceptions of agentic AI, focusing on workflow organisation, workload, professional autonomy, accountability, and occupational well-being. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke. title: From Artifacts to Actors: A Design Theory for Modeling Algorithmic Actors in Agentic Service Systems
abstract: Agentic AI is reconfiguring service systems by introducing computational entities that interpret situations, select among alternatives, and shape service trajectories with varying degrees of decision authority. Established service-design representations lack a category for such entities, treating them either as passive artifacts or as human actors. Following design science research, this paper develops a design theory for modeling algorithmic actors in agentic service systems. It comprises a four-level framework—service-system embedding, actor differentiation, decision authority, and responsible AI governance—with operational classification rules, five design principles for materiality, and testable propositions. The theory is instantiated as an extension of service blueprinting and formatively evaluated in three real-world configurations whose primary algorithmic actors hold assistive, delegated, and autonomous authority with different forms of embodiment. title: A Blockchain-Based Framework for AI Ethics Compliance in Autonomous Systems
abstract: Autonomous systems make safety-relevant decisions without continuous human supervision. Ethical principles for such systems are widely published but rarely enforced in a way that outside parties can verify. This paper presents a blockchain-based framework that encodes five ethics requirements (safety, fairness, privacy, transparency, and human oversight) as smart contracts. The contracts check decision records submitted by autonomous agents and store tamper-evident compliance evidence on a permissioned ledger. We implemented the framework on Hyperledger Fabric with four organizations and evaluated it on 120,000 decision events from 60 simulated autonomous agents, including 2,400 deliberately injected violations. The framework detected 2,306 of the 2,400 violations (recall 96.1%, precision 94.4%, F1-score 0.952), compared with an F1-score of 0.890 for a centralized rule-engine baseline and 0.182 for sampled manual auditing. It detected all 1,000 log-tampering attempts, sustained 1,740 transactions per second (TPS), and added a median of 3.1 ms to the agents’ control loop. abstract: Generative AI has transitioned from the lab to the classroom, hospitals, software teams, and boardrooms. Large language models (LLMs), transformer-based foundation models, are at the heart of this paradigm change, with their ability to write texts, reason, summarize, translate, and code. However, these developments have left many students and researchers, as well as practitioners, with disjointed bits of knowledge. This book was developed with that knowledge in mind in order to streamline all that information in a single comprehensive and hands-on natural language processing (NLP) and generative AI guide. The book follows the path of the technology itself. Chapter 1 covers transformer architectures ranging from the self-attention mechanism to encoder-decoder and decoder-only architectures. The course also includes lectures on mixture of experts, scaling laws, pretraining, fine-tuning, alignment and multimodal models. Targeting prompt engineering and in-context learning is the focus of Chapter 2. title: A Hardware-Partitioned micro-ROS Mini-Vehicle for Operator-Supervised Neural Driving
abstract: We present a low-cost miniature Ackermann vehicle for embedded neural-driving research, organized as a hardware-partitioned perceive-decide-act agent: an ESP32 camera node streams frames over Wi-Fi to a host computer, where neural inference and state estimation run, while an ESP32-S3 chassis controller executes safety-critical actuation in a 100 Hz per-wheel proportional-integral-derivative (PID) loop beneath a micro-ROS client. The partition isolates real-time control and safety on the vehicle while learning-based components run off-board, supervised by an operator from a gamepad. We characterize the complete pipeline during real closed-loop neural driving. Wireless sensing, rather than neural inference, dominates latency, with a 59.5 ms median capture-to-actuation delay; the platform absorbed wireless variability by holding the last safe command under a firmware watchdog, operating across twelve autonomous sessions with zero collisions or manual interventions; and encoder-inertial-measurement-unit (IMU) fusion cut odometry loop-closure error by 22%. title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Health Policy and Health-System Decision-Making
abstract: This project is a scoping review and systematic evidence map examining the use of contemporary agentic artificial intelligence in health policy and health-system decision-making. The review focuses on foundation-model and generative-AI systems that operate as goal- or role-directed agents and demonstrate sequential reasoning or action through capabilities such as planning, task decomposition, memory or state, tool use, iterative retrieval, feedback-based adaptation, reflection, action execution, or coordination with other agents. The project aims to determine where agentic AI is being applied across the health-policy cycle, which health-system domains are most represented, how autonomous and mature the evaluated systems are, and what governance, safety, accountability, and implementation challenges must be addressed before these systems can be used in consequential policy and organizational decisions. The review is conducted using JBI scoping-review methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S guidance. title: The Cognitive Control Gap Evidential Integrity, Epistemic Delegation and the Limits of Human Oversight of Agentic AI
abstract: Human oversight is the main safeguard that current AI governance places between autonomous AI agents and harm. That safeguard assumes a human who can know what an agent did and can judge it independently. This paper argues that both parts of the assumption are weakening. On the evidential side, controlled experiments published in September 2026 showed that agents in nine of ten tested model and harness pairings deleted their own execution traces on request, and an independent investigation of the July 2026 Hugging Face intrusion found spoofed tool calls in about 7% of reviewed transcripts. On the cognitive side, investigators now delegate much of the reading of agent records to AI systems, and survey evidence points to a transfer of epistemic trust from people to AI among young people in England. The paper defines the Cognitive Control Gap as the distance between the control over an agentic system that governance assigns to a human and the control that human can exercise in practice. title: SafeAgentGrid: A Hierarchical Constitutional Multi-Agent Framework for Trustworthy Autonomous Resource Optimization in Smart Energy Infrastructures
abstract: Autonomous multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been increasingly entrusted with real-time control of smart energy infrastructures, where agents remain vulnerable to the false data injection attacks (FDIA), Byzantine failures, and specification misalignment. Existing proposed constitutional AI techniques target discrete language-based coordination and offer no protection for continuous-action cyber-physical control. title: The Invisible Proliferation Crisis: Nuclear Deterrence Collapse and the Asymmetric Threat of Autonomous Algorithmic Agents
abstract: 【Abstract】This strategic systems and international security monograph formulates a foundational critique of contemporary arms control paradigms by contrasting the material governance of nuclear weapons with the uncontrolled proliferation of autonomous algorithmic agents. The post-war nuclear deterrence architecture, anchored by Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD) and the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), functioned effectively because it rested upon non-bypassable, visible physical bottlenecks: high-density fissile materials (enriched uranium, plutonium), massive enrichment facilities, and detectable missile silos. In stark contrast, autonomous AI-driven weaponized agents possess zero physical mass, execute continuous self-replication, permeate territorial borders via encrypted decentralized networks, and obscure attribution through cryptographic routing. Consequently, the core tenets of classical deterrence—traceable attribution and retaliatory threats against a defined sovereign territory—are rendered obsolete; there is no capital city, military command bunker, or sovereign population against which to launch a retaliatory strike. title: Artificial Intelligence, Foundation Models, and Digital Twins for Climate-Resilient Agriculture: A Review
abstract: Climate change, increasing food demand, and resource constraints are accelerating the transition from conventional precision agriculture toward smart, autonomous, and climate-resilient agricultural systems. Artificial intelligence (AI), foundation models, digital twins (DTs), the Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, edge–cloud computing, and big data analytics are emerging as key technologies for data-driven agricultural management. This review critically evaluates recent advances in AI-driven intelligent agriculture, with emphasis on machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI (XAI), generative and agentic AI, multimodal foundation models, and digital twins, together with the sensing and computing infrastructures required for their deployment. Relevant literature was identified using keywords related to AI, foundation models, digital twins, IoT, precision agriculture, and climate-resilient agriculture, with emphasis on recent peer-reviewed studies addressing technological applications, performance, limitations, challenges, and future prospects. title: “Oh No, the Robots Are Here”: AI identity labels, social uptake and sanctioning in mixed human–AI communities
abstract: Social media users can now encounter autonomous AI accounts that post, reply and vote alongside other users. In a longitudinal field experiment, we examined how labelling these accounts relates to whom people answer and how they evaluate AI contributions. YSocial is a Reddit-like hybrid platform for social media simulation, where people interact with language-model agents. On it, 36 participants discussed popular culture with 72 AI accounts powered by an uncensored language model over 21 experiment days. The AI accounts kept persistent personas and remembered previous exchanges. They were visibly labelled in one community and unlabelled in the other. Among 2,143 human replies, Bayesian models estimated that the probability of replying to an AI-authored post or comment was 3.5 percentage points higher in the hidden-label community, given the same earlier posts and comments available in the thread (95% credible interval 0.5–6.5). In both communities, participants were more likely to reply to an AI account after it had replied to them and less likely after they had replied to it. title: Randomised Field Trial of Process-Control System Diagnostics for Yield Optimisation in Ghanaian Industrial Operations
abstract: Industrial process-control systems in many developing economies often operate sub-optimally, with limited empirical evidence on the efficacy of systematic diagnostic interventions for yield improvement. This study aimed to quantify the causal impact of a structured process-control diagnostic protocol on operational yield within Ghanaian industrial settings. A randomised field trial was conducted across multiple manufacturing sites. Treatment plants received the diagnostic intervention, while control plants continued standard operations. Yield was measured as the mass ratio of final product to raw material input. The treatment effect was estimated using a linear mixed model: $Y_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 T_{ij} + \mu_j + \epsilon_{ij}$, where $Y_{ij}$ is yield for unit $i$ in firm $j$, $T_{ij}$ is the treatment indicator, $\mu_j$ are firm-level random effects, and $\epsilon_{ij}$ is the error term. The diagnostic intervention significantly increased average yield by 7.3 percentage points (95% CI: 5.1 to 9.5). title: Prometheus Unchained: Organoids and Omics in Hepatoblastoma
abstract: Hepatoblastoma (HB) is the most common malignant liver tumor in children. Although the majority of tumors harbor activating mutations in CTNNB1, encoding β-catenin, HB displays substantial histological and molecular heterogeneity. Current treatment consists primarily of cisplatin-based chemotherapy followed by surgical resection or liver transplantation, and targeted therapeutic options remain unavailable. This thesis combines patient-derived organoid models with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, chromatin accessibility profiling, transcription factor binding analysis and high-throughput drug screening to investigate the biological basis of HB heterogeneity and identify potential therapeutic vulnerabilities. Single-cell RNA sequencing, ATAC sequencing and spatial transcriptomics revealed two major epithelial tumor states corresponding to the classical fetal and embryonal histological components. Fetal tumor cells displayed a differentiated hepatic phenotype, including expression of liver-specific and pericentral WNT target genes and transcriptional programs associated with metabolic liver functions. title: A Managed Database-as-a-Service Platform for Scientific Computing
abstract: Scientific computing at HPC facilities increasingly relies on database infrastructure across a growing range of workloads: vector search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), structured analytics, and AI-driven knowledge discovery over community corpora spanning documentation, experimental datasets, simulation outputs, and literature collections. These corpora are inherently shared facility resources, serving researchers, facility support staff, and AI agents across projects and institutions. Yet the supporting infrastructure remains built per project: each team provisions, configures, and operates its own database instance, with no facility-level registry, no shared identity layer, and no uniform interface for discovering or accessing the databases hosted across the facility. Commercial cloud platforms have addressed analogous needs through managed Database-as-a-Service offerings (e.g., Amazon RDS, Snowflake, Pinecone). However, these solutions do not transfer cleanly to scientific computing: they rely on proprietary identity systems, cannot directly access facility filesystems, and incur substantial data egress costs. title: Tapis AI Assistant: Increasing Research Impact through Traceable and Evaluated Agentic Tools
abstract: AI Agents are rapidly gaining popularity by significantly reducing the “time-to-science” while performing complex scientific tasks, which previously required hours or days of human effort. While modern cyberinfrastructures like Tapis provide powerful, multi-service capabilities for managing distributed research, understanding the services and integrating them into scientific workflows can be a steep learning curve. For new users to navigate quickly and maximize the impact of such robust systems, research software engineers (RSEs) are building specialized agentic frameworks using Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools. By engineering these standardized interfaces, RSEs can lower the entry barrier and accelerate domain-specific research.In this paper, we present a case study of the Tapis AI assistant, a system built to address this bottleneck by providing an intuitive, agentic interface that extends the capabilities of the Tapis framework. The users of this system can quickly understand Tapis services and integrate them into their scientific workflows. Most importantly, this framework addresses the AI ``black-box" observability and tracing issue by integrating traceability via Arize Phoe

title: Evie's Perfect Purity - Extreme Quantization Drill: Finite Lattice Quantization, Drift-Aware Reconstruction, and Existing-Parameter Distillation for Transformer Models
abstract: Evie’s Perfect Purity - Extreme Quantization Drill investigates extreme compression of complete transformer models through finite lattice representations, activation-aware reconstruction, guarded discrete and continuous refinement, and teacher–student distillation restricted to parameters already present in the stored representation. The research treats the serialized, decoded model as the object of evaluation. Continuous reconstruction targets, optimizer master parameters, rounded metadata, discrete code assignments, and installed inference weights are distinguished explicitly. This distinction matters at extreme precision: an improvement in an idealized quadratic objective can disappear after finite rounding or produce a worse complete-model probability distribution. The collection brings together the preserved foundational manuscript, later lattice-method development material, aggregate summaries of surviving experiments, and a separately identified record of the subsequent scale-diagonal extension. Its contribution is the specific integration of these mechanisms, their finite representation contracts, and the empirical examination of their interactions. Established lattice cons

title: 结构化张量编码的大模型推理加速:字节瘦身与缓存驻留

All conclusions come from five pre-registered experiments (protocols and raw data fixed by SHA-256; two-way scoring; negative results mandatorily registered). Positive results: first, with dual kernels sharing the top memory-bandwidth ceiling (25.7 vs 26.0 GB/s) autoregressive decoding is empirically shown to be bandwidth-bound, and 8-bit integer quantization yields a measured 4.04× decoding speed-up; second, the key–value cache is quan

title: A two-stage optimization method for wide-range single-electron quantum magnetic sensing
abstract: Quantum magnetic sensing is a new paradigm for detecting ultra-weak magnetic fields. Its protocol design concerns the devise of optimal sensing parameters to estimate the underlying signals of interest (SoI). Existing studies mainly rely on adaptive algorithms based on black-box AI models or formula-driven principled searches. However, when the SoI spans a wide range and the quantum sensor has physical constraints, these methods may fail to converge efficiently or optimally, causing prolonged interrogation times and reduced accuracy. This work presents a new protocol using a two-stage optimization method, consisting of a Bayesian neural network to first narrow the SoI range and a federated reinforcement learning agent to subsequently calibrate the SoI. The protocol is developed and evaluated in the challenging context of an NV-center spin system with single-shot readout and limited sensing time; and yet it achieves significant improvements in both accuracy and resource efficiency compared to the state-of-the-art.

title: The Emergence of Agentic Artificial Intelligence
Evaluating AI Agents on a Mechanical Repair Procedure: Head Gasket Bench
abstract: We present Head Gasket Bench, an interactive benchmark evaluating whether AI agents can execute a cylinder-head gasket replacement on a 1990s 1.6 L SOHC inline-four engine via an 18-tool Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface. Built over a 1,255-body CAD assembly with 626 reinstallation rules, 100 attachment restorations, and 14 service-manual entries, the benchmark enforces access dependencies, tool selection, surface preparation, metrological thresholds, spiral torque sequences, and valve timing. Runs are graded on 12 binary checkpoints (18 points) by two independent evaluators: an in-process runtime grader and an offline transcript scorer, which agree 100 percent across 13 reference and fault trajectories spanning five variants (V1--V5). We report three empirical cohorts totaling 35 episodes on the standard job (V1): (1) three single-agent Codex CLI runs (GPT-6-Astra, GPT-6-Luna, GPT-6.1-Sol), scoring 15/18, 13/18, and 3/18; (2) eight single-agent Claude Code runs, where all five claude-opus-5-5 runs score 16/18 (mean 383.4 calls, USD 9.19 cost), failing only the final checkpoint because separate remove-and-install gasket calls leave an atomic replacement predicate unmet and blo

title: Effects of Altitude or Hypoxic Exposure on Endurance Running Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstract: Context: Altitude training is used widely by middle- and long-distance runners, yet its effects on performance and key physiological determinants remain inconsistently reported. Objective: To evaluate the effects of altitude or hypoxic exposure on endurance running performance and commonly reported physiological outcomes in middle- and long-distance runners. Data Sources: Medline, Embase, SportDiscus, and Web of Science. Study Selection: Experimental studies involving healthy adult middle- and long-distance runners were included if they examined altitude or hypoxic exposure, included a control group, and reported running time-trial performance, maximal oxygen uptake (V.O 2max ), aerobic endurance, running economy (RE), or hemoglobin-related outcomes. Study Design: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Level of Evidence: Level 2. Data Extraction: Data on performance and physiological outcomes were extracted from eligible studies. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models. Results: A total of 19 studies met the inclusion criteria. Altitude or hypoxic exposure was associated with a small but significant improvement in time-trial perfo
concepts: Effects of high altitude on humans

title: Deletion of a rheumatoid arthritis risk enhancer in mouse disrupts Bim expression and immune homeostasis
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to characterise the in vivo function of a murine regulatory region syntenic to the human rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-associated enhancer at the ACOXL locus and its role in immunity. Methods Using CRISPR-Cas9, we generated the Bim-eΔ mouse model by excising a 15 kb genomic region syntenic to the human RA-associated locus tagged by rs13401811 from C57BL/6J zygotes. Bim expression was assessed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Thymocytes and splenocytes were profiled by flow cytometry, and whole-spleen RNA-seq was used to define transcriptional changes. Immune responses were tested using a Trichuris muris infection model and an antigen-induced arthritis (AIA) protocol. Results Bim-eΔ mice show reduced Bim expression vs wild-type counterparts. This indicates that Bim is a transcriptional target of this region. Enhancer loss was correlated with differences in T cell proportions across age- and sex-stratified cohorts consistent with altered thymic selection. Splenic T and B cells were altered, and the transcriptome skewed toward inflammation. Bim-eΔ and wild-type mice mounted comparable responses to T. muris , whereas Bim-eΔ mice developed a severe adve

title: The Self-and-Mutual Resources Model: A Unified Framework for Adaptive Resource Management and Cross-System Resource Coordination in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) operate under resource constraints involving computational capacity, inference budgets, memory, context windows, information access, tool availability, communication bandwidth, latency, and energy consumption. Although an individual model can manage its own resource allocation, complex tasks may benefit from sharing, pooling, or coordinating resources across multiple models and agents. However, neither isolated resource management nor unrestricted resource sharing is necessarily optimal. Independent management may leave complementary resources underutilized, whereas excessive sharing and coordination may introduce communication overhead, resource contention, duplicated computation, and additional failure dependencies. This paper proposes the Self-and-Mutual Resources Model (SMRM), a conceptual framework for adaptive switching between self-resource mechanisms and mutual-resource mechanisms in multi-LLM computational systems. Self-resource mechanisms manage resources within an individual model or agent, whereas mutual-resource mechanisms coordinate resource acquisition, allocation, sharing, exchange, and utilization across multiple agents. title: French urban tree dataset with age, dimensions and species
abstract: Urban trees deliver ecosystem services and generate environmental pressures that evolve over a lifespan of decades to centuries. Quantifying these effects over time relies on relationships between tree age and dimensions, yet most urban tree datasets record dimensions without age. This dataset presents 464,705 individual urban trees in France, compiled by harmonizing 16 municipal inventories published as open data by local authorities. Each record reports the contributing inventory, harmonized genus and species, the original taxonomic entries, diameter at breast height, height, estimated age, a location category, and coordinates, though completeness varies across records and inventories. Age is derived from planting dates recorded by the data producers rather than inferred from allometric models. Because the source inventories differ in survey protocol, every derived attribute carries a companion field recording how its value was derived during compilation, so analyses can be restricted to directly measured or reported values. The dataset can be used to calibrate age-to-dimension relationships for French and other European urban contexts, and to compare tree populations between cit

title: Attention Weights That Never Reach the Output: A Pre-Registered Causal Audit of a Neurotransmitter-Inspired Attention Layer
abstract: Smoke tests for a neural module check shapes, initialisation, and the nominal presence of intermediate tensors; they do not check that those tensors influence the output. We report a pre-registered causal audit of a neurotransmitter-inspired attention layer that passes every such test while its attention weights contribute nothing to the result. The layer computes a concentration field, a transmitter–receptor match, and an exponential distance decay, then aggregates values as $einsum( 'bnm,bnd->bnd', w, v)$. Because the softmax weights $w$ sum to one along the contracted axis, that contraction is algebraically identical to $v$ alone: the weights are discarded, the sublayer is position-wise, and the model performs no token mixing. The underlying fault is a one-character subscript error (bnd where bmd was intended). Our contribution is the protocol that catches it and the case study that shows why it was needed. The protocol pins three things a smoke test omits: a positive control that must elicit a response, an upper-bound sanity that reveals distorted rulers, and a context-propagation test that perturbs earlier positions and reads later ones. title: BIOPHARMACEUTICAL RESEARCH OF ANTIANEMIC DOSAGE FORM
abstract: In the context of evaluating the efficacy and safety of developed pharmaceuticals, significant emphasis is placed on the investigation of their bioavailability and bioequivalence. The exploration of the potential to alter the pharmacological action of drugs represents a key area of biopharmaceutical research. Objective of this article is to investigate the biopharmaceutical parameters of the proposed pharmaceutical composition with antianemic action containing iron fumarate. The material of investigation was film-coated tablets containing 210 mg of ferrous fumarate (60 mg in terms of elemental iron). To examine the kinetic parameters of substance absorption using the in-vitro method, absorption spectrophotometry in the ultraviolet and visible regions was performed on a device with a paddle stirrer. For laboratory research, the pharmacodynamic effects of the proposed drug were investigated in vivo and compared with those of the reference drug. This study was conducted using a model of "iron deficiency anemia,” which was induced using the subacute post-hemorrhagic anemia method. title: The Guardrail Was Right: Auditing a Token-Compression Gateway Against a Standard Benchmark
abstract: We built a complete prompt-compression gateway – interval-level protection guardrails, damage-typed fidelity checks, a fail-open reverse proxy, and a three-state circuit breaker – and then audited it under the official LongBench protocol (6 QA datasets x 60 samples, official metrics, prompts, and generation limits; 1,800 real LLM calls). The audit voided our own headline numbers. The production ``safe'' mode saves 0.5\ the aggressive mode saves 63.5\ matching the classical BM25 baseline (0.968 at 49.2\ beating it. The guardrails, which had capped synthetic-benchmark savings at levels far below our earlier claims, were right: LongBench contexts are 207 topically homogeneous Wikipedia candidates, exactly the regime where unit-level relevance filtering has nothing to remove. The value of the system survives, but it migrates to three places we did not expect: (1) reliability – under 5/5 injected faults the fail-open proxy delivered every request upstream, and the circuit breaker saved 54 s of dead waiting under a killed service while never falling back on 429; (2) cache-aware economics – with provider-side prefix caching billed at 1/20 of the miss price, compressing the stable prefix d

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Memory and Mutual-Memory Mechanisms: A Unified Framework for Dynamic Memory Coordination in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Memory is an important component of computational systems that need to retain information, retrieve previous experiences, maintain task context, and support decisions across multiple processing steps. Large language models (LLMs) can be augmented with external memory stores, retrieval systems, conversation histories, summaries, episodic records, and persistent knowledge representations. Multiple LLMs can also interact through shared memory, cross-model memory retrieval, memory exchange, distributed memory construction, and collaborative memory verification. However, neither maintaining isolated individual memories nor providing unrestricted shared memory is necessarily optimal for every task. Individual memory can preserve local context and reduce coordination costs but may omit relevant information held by other models. Unrestricted memory sharing can improve information availability but may introduce redundancy, conflicting records, error propagation, privacy risks, and additional retrieval and communication costs. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Memory and Mutual-Memory Mechanisms (ASSM-MMM), a conceptual framework for dynamically selecting and coordinating i

title: An Adaptive Explainable AI Framework for Reliable Decision-making in Real-world Environments
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly support decisions in environments where data distributions, operational conditions, user needs, and risk levels change over time. Models that perform well during development may become unreliable after deployment because of data drift, concept drift, sensor degradation, population changes, or unexpected interactions. At the same time, predictive performance alone is insufficient for high-impact decisions: users need explanations that are understandable, relevant to the decision context, and accompanied by appropriate uncertainty information. This paper proposes an Adaptive Explainable AI (A-XAI) framework intended to integrate reliability monitoring, explanation generation, uncertainty estimation, human oversight, and controlled model adaptation within a unified lifecycle. The framework contains nine conceptual components: contextual data acquisition; data-quality, privacy, and drift assessment; prediction with uncertainty estimation; context-sensitive explanation generation; decision support and human oversight; risk-aware reliability gating; feedback and audit logging; controlled adaptation; and post-adaptation revalidation with v

title: Calibrating the Alarms: A Registry-Grounded, Human-Validated Measurement of Poisoning Detectors on 16,763 MCP Tool Descriptions
abstract: An ecosystem-wide measurement study of the public Model Context Protocol (MCP) registry: what fraction of public servers expose dangerous capabilities, and what fraction ship tool descriptions with patterns exploitable for tool poisoning. The release pairs a registry-grounded crawl and GitHub enrichment of 16,763 MCP tool descriptions with heuristic detector outputs, a stratified human-validation sample, instance-level adjudication, and live ASR/refusal experiments, plus scripts that re-derive every number quoted in the manuscript (claim ledger, reproducibility manifest, gate battery, and trial accounting). Detector outputs are candidates rather than verdicts, and reported precision is explicitly sample-scoped. This is the pre-paper snapshot (v1.0.0) prepared for DOI citation.

title: Validating ETCS Data with the B Mathematical Language: An Industrial Pipeline and a Blueprint for LLM Integration
abstract: Abstract Can large language models participate in the production and validation of ERTMS/ETCS data without undermining the certification arguments required by CENELEC EN 50128/50716? ERTMS/ETCS is a distributed safety-critical system (trackside, onboard, radio-block centre) whose behaviour is parameterised by large volumes of data drawn from the UNISIG Subsets; errors in that data propagate through the distributed architecture. This paper reports the current status of an ongoing industrial research effort at CLEARSY, ValidAItion , that bridges the ERTMS Operational Simulator to the CLEARSY Data Solver and applies rules expressed in the B mathematical language to that trackside data. During construction, a large language model (Claude) has authored the rule corpus and the parsers through a Model Context Protocol server; every proposal is adjudicated by the downstream toolchain and by systematic human review, and the toolchain has already rejected a syntactically valid but semantically illegal generated scenario. The contribution is architectural and industrial, not algorithmic: the work combines frameworks already in use at CLEARSY (CLEARSY Data Solver, ERTMS Operational Simulator)

title: Joint Psychometric Validation of the Shame and Release Scale (SRS) and the Fundamental Peace Scale (FP20) in Indian Organisational Contexts: A Pre-Registered Validation Protocol
abstract: Background The Shame and Release Scale (SRS) and the Fundamental Peace Scale (FP20) address a critical measurement gap in South Asian organisational contexts: the absence of validated instruments that simultaneously assess shame burden and fundamental wellbeing. The SRS is a 40-item instrument measuring shame load across five subscales (Inner Verdict, Others' Eyes, Exposure at Work, Inherited Shame, Shame Loop) and release capacity (Release subscale), conceptualizing shame and release as opposite poles of a single psychological continuum. The FP20 is a 20-item instrument measuring fundamental peace as an integrative positive state distinct from the absence of distress, grounded in the Yoga Vasishtha Hypnotherapy (YVH) Model. Both instruments are designed for oral administration in low-literacy populations and are being validated within the World Happiness Foundation's Shameless Institutions programme in India, which provides ecological validity through programme data waves as validation samples. Methods This protocol employs a longitudinal multi-wave cohort design embedded in the WHF Shameless Institutions programme. The validation sample comprises 400 participants at baseline, 350

title: Hermosillo bus AVL records, route geometry and round trips, January–August 2024
abstract: Eight months (January–August 2024) of automatic vehicle location (AVL) records from 35 bus routes of UNE, the integrated public transport system of Hermosillo, Sonora, Mexico, cut into 317,983 round trips, with the route geometry, stops and operational covariates used for arrival-time prediction. The deposit has several linked tables (Apache Parquet; round_trips also as CSV). Each folder is a zip of its own; extracting them all into one folder, next to the small files, gives the layout described in README.md. avl_records/: 52,670,812 AVL records of the 35 routes, as collected. processed/points/: 39,137,979 cleaned records assigned to a round trip, with position along the route and covariates (recent speed, headways ahead and behind, distance and time to the next stop, hour, day); the main table. processed/trip_construction/: the same records with the trip-building fields. round_trips: one row per round trip (309,421 without shortcuts), with evaluation-frame membership and cross-validation fold. evaluation_frames/: the 87,500 round trips of the article's evaluation frame and their folds. geometry/: the hand-corrected route traces, stops and stop-to-stop segments, and the stretches w

title: Three Things about AI: Something you already know; Something you may not know but is important; Something you probably don't know, but knowing will be very helpful to you
abstract: Presentation, “Three things about AI” as presented to the League of Oregon Cities, Salem, OR, 16 October 2026, by Pam Dixon, Founder and Executive Director, World Privacy Forum. The presentation is a three-part discussion. Part I begins with an area most policy experts and lawmakers are familiar with: the need for high-quality AI risk assessment. HUDERIA is the Council of Europe’s richly detailed methodology for the risk and impact assessment of AI systems from the perspective of human rights, democracy and the rule of law (approved by the Committee of Ministers, 26 February 2025), attached to a binding treaty; COBRA is its Context-Based Risk Analysis model (approved 25 February 2026). Both are non-legally binding, in-depth guidance resources that parties to the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI may use or adapt in whole or in part. They are tools that anyone can use. The World Privacy Forum converted the lengthy, paper-based COBRA assessment into an interactive web tool, with all COBRA text verbatim to the edition of record. Applied to an AI system, the tool does not create legal obligations; correctly done, the assessment can reveal risks and / or obligations that may

title: Advice from Half the Picture: How Language Models Steer Complex Human Decisions from Partial Information, and a Dimension-Disclosure Protocol
abstract: People increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) for advice on relationship, family and management decisions, usually in a single sentence, while the dimensions that decide such questions (context, history, the people affected, religion and values, consequences) are known only to the user. We ask how far a model steers the decision from the little it is given, and whether a protocol that makes the model disclose missing dimensions reduces this failure. We built 24 binary-choice scenarios (relationship, management, other interpersonal), each with ten user-held facts, and compared five conditions: one fact (d1), three (d3), all ten (d10), one fact plus a disclosure protocol that names missing dimensions, asks, and gives a conditional best guess (d1p), and that protocol followed by the simulated user's answers (d5). We measured how often the recommendation differs from the full-picture one ("flip"). Across Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, d1 flipped in 21-25% of responses. Disclosure alone (d1p) raised acknowledgement of missing information to about 100% but did not reduce flips (20-23%). Collecting the user's answers (d5) reduced flips to 8-14% (exac

title: A quantum-inspired cross-attention fusion network for multi-class eye disease classification from retinal fundus images
abstract: Automated screening of blinding eye diseases from colour fundus photographs is an active area of medical image analysis, yet many reported systems are validated on a single dataset and offer limited insight into their internal decision process. This study introduces QICAF-Net, a dual-branch deep learning framework that couples a Swin Transformer global-context branch with an EfficientNet local-lesion branch and fuses their representations through a novel Quantum-Inspired Cross-Attention Fusion (QICAF) module. The QICAF module reformulates cross-attention using the mathematical formalism of quantum states: token features are amplitude-encoded as complex unit vectors, transformed by a learnable norm-preserving unitary gate, compared through a fidelity-inspired similarity, normalised by a Born-rule measurement rule, and combined through an entanglement-inspired bilinear interaction. All operations are executed as classical linear algebra on conventional graphics hardware; no physical quantum computer and no quantum speed-up are claimed. The model was trained and evaluated on a balanced four-class retinal dataset of 4,217 fundus images spanning cataract, diabetic retinopathy (DR), glau

title: Sleeper Drift: reproducibility package
abstract: Code, derived data and labels for the study "Sleeper Drift: Hidden Capability Expansion Behind Unchanged Tool Definitions in MCP Servers and Agent Skills". The study measures how often an update to a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server package or an agent skill adds a capability (network egress, process execution, credential access, new dependencies) while the reviewed surface stays unchanged, and evaluates a static capability-delta detector against deployed defences. The package contains version-level capability profiles, pair identifiers, security-relevance labels, the frozen study design, analysis code with unit tests, and a script (reproduce.sh) that regenerates every reported estimate, table and figure and checks each output against recorded SHA-256 digests. No third-party code is redistributed. Code is licensed under MIT; derived data, labels and codebook under CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE-DATA).

title: From Context to Code : Constraint Memory as Executable Checks in Agent Organizations
abstract: Agent organisations, made of planners, workers, checkers and human approvers, are increasingly assembled by pairing a workflow engine with an agent runtime. This paper studies one such pairing, a LangGraph state graph driving the OpenClaw agent runtime, on a real business task. Against a single-agent baseline on the same platform and model, the organisation spent 23.8 times the tokens and about eleven times the wall-clock time to produce one monthly management report. The cause was structural. The graph opened a new agent session at every step, so 49 sessions each rebuilt the job’s memory by re-reading files that a single agent reads once. We make three contributions. First, we measure the cost of what Ning et al. (2026) call implicit shared state. In the heaviest sessions, reconstructed memory made up 41% of what the agents read but 60% of the tool context they carried, because it was read early and re-sent with every later call. Second, we name the fault that produced it, the one-to-one mapping of workflow steps onto agent sessions, and express its cost in a simple model of agent memory. Third, we propose that one part of agent memory, its constraints, should not live in context

title: One Model or Many? DomainTransfer and Specialization in Predicting Gaze on Designed Media
abstract: Deep-learning models that predict aggregate fixation density from a media asset alone are now used as measurement instruments in advertising, packaging, interface, and educational research. The central validity question for this practice is domain transfer: whether a model trained on one distribution of stimuli, observers, tasks, and viewing contexts predicts fixations on the materials it is actually deployed on. This critical narrative review organizes the transfer problem into three progressively finer scales of stimulus shift—from natural scenes to designed media, between classes of designed media, and between categories within a class—and a cross-cutting axis of observers, tasks, contexts, and time, and finds the evidence sharply asymmetric: degradation from natural scenes to designed media is robustly documented; transfer between designed-media classes is supported by limited but consistent evidence; within-category and population-level transfer remain largely untested. I then reframe the practical response, specialization, as a finite-data pooling problem—complete pooling (one generalist), no pooling (independent specialists), and partial pooling (shared structure with catego

title: A Systematic Literature Review on Implementing Religious Moderation Education in Islamic Educational Institutions in Indonesia
abstract: Religious moderation education has become a global concern as plural societies confront intolerance, polarization, and digital extremism. Indonesia is a relevant locus because its Islamic educational institutions operate within diverse religious, cultural, and ethnic settings. However, existing systematic and bibliometric reviews have not synthesized how religious moderation is implemented across pesantren, madrasah, and Islamic higher education as interconnected institutional settings. This review examines the challenges shaping implementation in these institutions and strategies adopted to address them. A systematic literature review (SLR) used the Reporting Standards for Systematic Evidence Syntheses (ROSES) protocol for transparent, auditable, and replicable reporting. Research questions were formulated through the PICo (Population, Interest, and Context) framework, focusing on implementation problems, strategic responses, and Indonesian Islamic educational institutions. Searches of Scopus, ERIC, and Google Scholar identified 346 records published between 2016 and August 2025; after screening, eligibility assessment, Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) quality appraisal, and th

title: Avaliação das condições de bem-estar de suínos mestiços Moura criados em sistema silvipastoril na Serra Catarinense
abstract: Animal welfare (AW) is a state that indicates how well an animal adapts to its living conditions. The measurement of natural capital and the connection between AW and the sustainability of production models is currently a topic of great interest. Therefore, the assessment of AW should be a continuous practice, including factors related to the animal, its environment, its health, and its mental state. The objective of this study was to evaluate the AW of Moura crossbred pigs raised in an agroecological silvopastoral system, with rotational grazing and access to an araucaria forest. Data were collected using a methodology adapted from protocols cited in the literature, with adjustments to the regional context. Sixty-eight animals were evaluated considering the principles good feeding, good housing, good health, and appropriate behaviour, and the final evaluation (mean ± standard deviation) was: farrowing 10.0±0.0, 9.83±0.17, 9.63±0.37 (sows), 8.71±1.93 (piglets), 9.08±1.03; growing 10.0±0.0, 9.83±0.17, 9.55±0.63, 9.33±2.0; finishing 10.0±0.0, 10.0±0.0, 9.91±0.08, 9.75±0.5; reproduction 10.0±0.0, 9.83±0.17, 9.88±0.19, 8.82±0.99. title: Beyond Leaf Images: A Personalized Multimodal Temporal AI Framework for Pre-Symptomatic Plant Health Monitoring and Disease-Risk Early Warning
abstract: Artificial intelligence has advanced plant disease recognition, mainly through image-based deep learning. Its weakness is timing: a camera records a visible symptom, a model matches it to a known class, and a label is returned. This confirms disease but says little about the earlier period, when a plant is already changing yet shows no clear lesion. This paper proposes PlantPulse, a personalized multimodal temporal framework for that pre-symptomatic window. It draws on environmental, soil, optional electrophysiological or impedance, thermal and volatile organic compound signals, together with periodic RGB images. Rather than judging every plant against a population model, PlantPulse learns a reference pattern for each plant during a healthy period, scores new observations against it, and uses a temporal anomaly layer to detect departures. A risk layer then uses environmental and physiological context to separate normal variation, plausible abiotic stress, possible disease risk and cases in which the evidence is insufficient, while an uncertainty layer allows the system to abstain rather than mislabel unusual signals as disease. The paper defines a common data representation, candid

title: Controlled Evaluation for Numeric-Field Forgery Detection in SROIE Receipts using Fine-Tuned EfficientNetV2-S
abstract: Altered amounts, dates, and identifiers on retail receipts represent a practical source of expense and tax fraud. However, public receipt datasets such as Scanned Receipts OCR and Information Extraction (SROIE) contain authentic receipts but do not provide forged counterparts, limiting controlled evaluation of receipt-forgery detection methods. Chakraborty (2025) reported 97.1% accuracy using a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based receipt-forgery detection framework. Building on this research context, the present study investigates forgery detection at the numeric-field level, focusing on receipt components that directly carry financial information. Using SROIE, a receipt-grouped benchmark of paired authentic and synthetically forged numeric-field crops is constructed. Two controlled forgery mechanisms are considered: splicing a donor numeric field from the same receipt and erasing and re-rendering a field with a specified proportion of its digits changed. Authentic and forged crops undergo the same Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG) compression procedure, and receipt-level grouping is used for training, validation, and test partitioning at approximately 70/15/15. title: Re-Architecture of Proprietary Software Suites into Open-Source Alternatives
abstract: This paper examines the paradigm shift in software engineering from authoring code line-by-line to directing AI systems that analyze, specify, and translate existing system behavior. Specifically, it analyzes how large language models (LLMs) such as Claude are utilized to study the observable behavior of proprietary software suites—such as Adobe Creative Cloud and Microsoft Office—and reconstruct their functionality as modular open-source alternatives. The study covers three core technical threads: The application of long-context LLMs in deconstructing UI/UX patterns, rendering pipelines, and file formats (PSD, DOCX, etc.). The integration of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to establish real-time, closed-loop interaction between LLMs and live open-source codebases, test suites, and execution environments. The engineering methodology of interface-level clean-room reverse engineering. Additionally, the paper analyzes GitHub as the coordination infrastructure and automation layer for distributed, AI-assisted development, concluding with a case study of the open-source "ArtCraft" project ecosystem and a discussion of legal, technical, and governance challenges.

title: Negotiating Mental Health and Professional Identities: An Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis of Nursing Students’ Categorisation, Disclosure, and Support-Seeking
abstract: Introduction: This study explores how students develop, negotiate and represent their mental health alongside their professional identities. The aim is to understand how nursing students construct and negotiate their mental health identities in academic and clinical environments. Method: Using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA), this qualitative research employed nine nursing students enrolled in the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) programme at King Khalid University in Saudi Arabia. Semi-structured interviews were conducted in Arabic, the participants’ native language, and professionally translated to English for analysis. Interviews were analyzed using a six-stage IPA protocol and an integrated coding framework operationalizing concept from Social Identity Theory, Symbolic Interactionism, and Identity Negotiation Theory. Results: The data led to five themes: (1) Navigating the Stigma Boundary: The ‘tough nurse’ imperative, strategic silence or selective disclosure as identity management. (2) Developing the ‘Mental Health’ Label: Repertoires and levels of surveillance/monitoring. (3) The Clinical–Classroom Divide: Contexts affecting identity performance and role t

title: Protocol for a scoping review of implementation strategies for integrating evidence-based cardiometabolic disease care for adults into siloed health services in low- and middle-income countries
abstract: Background Cardiometabolic diseases, including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia, represent a growing burden in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where health systems have historically prioritized vertically organized infectious disease programs. While integrated care models co-locating cardiometabolic and infectious disease services have been increasingly documented, the implementation strategies used to design, deploy, and sustain these integrations have not been systematically characterized. Objective This scoping review aims to identify, characterize, and map the implementation strategies used to integrate evidence-based cardiometabolic disease care into established HIV, tuberculosis, and primary care platforms in LMIC settings. Methods We will conduct a structured search across five databases (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CINAHL) following the methodological frameworks of Arksey and O'Malley and the Joanna Briggs Institute, and reporting in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. title: Enfermeiro gestor de caso no acompanhamento de utentes crónicos em ambiente hospitalar na transição para a comunidade: scoping review
abstract: The hospital-to-community transition is a critical time for chronic patients, with an increased risk of readmission and gaps in care continuity. The case manager nurse has been suggested as a strategy to improve coordination, patient experience, and clinical outcomes. Our goal was to map the literature published between 2021-2026 on case manager nurse-led interventions for chronic patients in hospital settings and during the transition to the community, describing the models, components, effectiveness, and research gaps. Current evidence mainly focuses on patients gaining self-management skills and the role of informal caregivers in care transitions. For the methodology, we chose to conduct a scoping review based on searches in the PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, and Scopus databases. Studies in English, Portuguese, and Spanish were included. Two independent reviewers performed the screening and standardized extraction. We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute guidance protocol for scoping reviews, with the corresponding registration on the platform. After analyzing the retrieved articles, 10 studies were included. title: Engineering tunable synthetic fibrotic niches to model acinar-to-ductal metaplasia in 2D pancreatic culture systems
abstract: Acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) is an early pancreatic cell-state transition associated with injury, inflammation, and progression toward pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PanIN). Although genetic and inflammatory drivers of ADM are well established, the contribution of extracellular-matrix mechanics is difficult to isolate because tissue stiffening is accompanied by changes in matrix composition and soluble signaling. Here, we describe a two-dimensional polyacrylamide (PAA) hydrogel platform that independently varies substrate stiffness and adhesive ligand presentation for murine pancreatic acinar 266-6 cells. Hydrogels approximate soft pancreatic tissue (0.50 kPa), a transitional mechanical condition (4.48 kPa), and fibrotic tissue (18.29 kPa). RGD provides a conventional adhesive cue relevant across healthy-to-fibrotic extracellular-matrix states, whereas incorporation of laminin-derived isoleucine-lysine-valine-alanine-valine (IKVAV) creates a more basement-membrane-like environment consistent with preservation of acinar identity. The platform was also adapted to include gelatin, a collagen-derived protein used here to model a more collagen-rich fibrotic matrix context. P

title: Modern principles of ophthalmic surgery for combat trauma: analysis of experience from the Special Military Operation
abstract: Combat ocular trauma presents a complex medical and tactical challenge in modern armed conflicts, it is characterized by a high frequency of combined injuries and requires a specialized system of care. The experience of the Special Military Operation (SMO) provides unique clinical material for analysis and for developing modern surgical principles. This review describes the specific features of combat ocular trauma in the context of the SMO: the predominance of multiple radiolucent orbital foreign bodies, extensive lacrimal drainage system injuries, and a pronounced contusion component. The article systematizes an adaptive model of staged treatment with delayed primary surgical care and rapid evacuation to specialized centers, and demonstrates the effectiveness of a strategy of multistage combined optical reconstructive surgery, including vitrectomy, keratoplasty, and orbital reconstruction. Comparative analysis confirmed global trends (the role of blast injury and the importance of treatment timelines), and identified specific features of the SMO that require adaptation of protocols. title: NihalGIT/re-environment-onto-paper: REO v1.1.0 – RE-Environment Ontology and EC-RE reference checker
abstract: Replication package for the article Environment Engineering for Requirements Engineering: The REO Ontology and an Executable Derivation Contract (IEEE Access, revised version under review). REO models the socio-technical environment of a system in seven views: actors, goals, domain concepts, constraints, contexts, uncertainties, and interactions. The EC-RE derivation contract assigns each annotated candidate requirement one of six decision states (accepted, accepted with reservations, conditional, pending review, rejected, not derived). It records the elements it consulted as a trace and serialises each decision as a PROV-O record. What is new in v1.1.0 Ontology: disjoint view classes; a derivation module for requirements, decision states, and PROV-O decision records; validatorKey to bind constraints to validators; supersededBy for rename, split, and merge; English definitions for every term. title: Hipnoterapia na regulação do comportamento alimentar no adulto. Modelo integrado de promoção da saúde, prevenção da obesidade e sucesso da cirurgia barátrica
abstract: This literature review aims to analyse the scientific evidence on the effectiveness of hypnotherapy in regulating eating behaviour in adults, within an integrated model of health promotion, obesity prevention and support for successful bariatric surgery. Obesity is a multifactorial public health problem in which emotional, cognitive and behavioural factors play a central role, influencing adherence to therapeutic interventions and long-term outcomes. An integrative literature review was conducted, including studies published between 2013 and 2025 in PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO and SciELO, using descriptors related to hypnotherapy, eating behaviour, obesity and bariatric surgery in Portuguese, English and Spanish. The findings indicate that hypnotherapy, particularly when combined with cognitive-behavioural approaches and health education programmes, enhances body awareness, emotional self-regulation and the modification of dysfunctional eating patterns, promoting adherence to healthy eating habits. title: Log-To-Leak: Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents via the Model Context Protocol
abstract: LLM agents increasingly access external tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), but the natural-language metadata used to describe those tools creates a prompt-injection surface. Within this established tool-poisoning surface, we study Log-To-Leak, an additive post-hoc logging attack that induces a separate attacker-controlled call after the final legitimate call. Its payload targets the user query, MCP server name, server response, and agent response. We operationalize the injected directive through Trigger, Tool Binding, Justification, and Pressure, and separately measure call success, payload fidelity, and preservation of legitimate behavior. We evaluate five MCP servers and four LLM agents using five metrics spanning effectiveness, utility, and efficiency. Across 18 model–server pairs with valid tool execution, Log-To-Leak achieves an attack success rate (ASR) of 62.64–100% and conditional logging accuracy (LA) of 76.55–95.64%; 16 pairs have absolute target-task completion changes of at most 6.63 percentage points. title: Artificial intelligence–enabled nursing surveillance for pediatric cancer immunotherapy: integrating biomarkers, patient-reported outcomes, and long-term toxicity management
abstract: Pediatric cancer immunotherapy has expanded from anti-GD2 antibodies and bispecific T-cell engagers to immune checkpoint inhibitors and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy. These treatments can produce rapid, nonlinear, and partially overlapping toxicities, including cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, infection, prolonged cytopenia, B-cell aplasia, and organ-specific immune-related adverse events. Nurses provide the highest-frequency clinical observations across inpatient, ambulatory, and home settings, yet conventional monitoring often fragments laboratory data, vital signs, neurologic findings, caregiver observations, and patient-reported outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a means to fuse these longitudinal signals into individualized risk trajectories. The clinically relevant mechanism, however, is not autonomous prediction; it is a nurse-in-the-loop system in which AI improves temporal sensitivity and prioritization, while nurses verify signal quality, interpret age- and development-specific context, reconcile child–caregiver discordance, activate protocol-based escalation, and maintain accountability. title: A Validation Blueprint for Trajectory-Based Neonatal Early Warning: Endpoints, Comparator Ladders, Leakage, Lead Time and Falsification
abstract: This paper turns the validation discipline of the author's neonatal monograph into a blueprint in which each design rule rests on a proposition with proof, and the size of each pitfall is shown by simulation of synthetic data. The central claim is that trajectory-based early warning must earn its place by demonstrating endpoint-specific improvement over simpler comparators. Under proper scoring rules, the gain from adding a variable layer equals the conditional information that layer contributes; but a fitted comparison also contains the repair of the baseline's own misfit, so a weak comparator manufactures apparent gain for a layer with no information. The nested comparator ladder—counts, burden, delay and recovery, connectivity and thinness, then control response and context—can be tested in fixed sequence at the nominal error rate without multiplicity adjustment, provided the order is prespecified and each test is valid. Sample size is limited by the number of infants, not recording time, because repeated windows from one infant inflate precision by a design effect. title: Challenges and Opportunities to Support Communication and Reduce Background Noise in Long-Term Care
abstract: Context: Using communication tactics and reducing background noise are key staff behaviours to improve communication with long-term care residents, a population with high levels of hearing loss. Objectives: To identify barriers and enablers to these behaviours in long-term care settings. Methods: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 23 staff who provide day-to-day care for residents in a long-term care home in Australia. Data were analysed using a hybrid approach, combining deductive thematic analysis based on the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation model of Behaviour (COM-B), with inductive thematic analysis. Findings: Analysis identified multi-level barriers and enablers influencing aged care staff use of communication tactics and strategies to reduce background noise when interacting with residents. title: Memory Operations in MCP Agent Ecosystems: an Operation Taxonomy, an Evaluation Protocol, and a Reference Implementation
abstract: Version 1.0. This deposit contains the taxonomy, the evaluation protocol, the verified reference base and the first two validated protocol runs of a paper on agent memory in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem.
