title: AI-Agent-Based Web Application Security Testing vs. Conventional Automated Security Testing: An Exploratory Case Study
abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) and agent-based architectures have introduced new possibilities for automating web application security testing. Unlike traditional vulnerability scanners that rely mainly on signature-based detection, LLM-powered agents can analyze application context and dynamically adapt testing strategies. This exploratory case study examined two specific laboratory-defined workflows for identifying web application security weaknesses: a human-supervised agent-based workflow and a conventional vulnerability scanner workflow. The evaluation was performed in a controlled laboratory environment against the same target application and predefined ground truth, while each workflow retained its respective application-access, discovery, and authentication mechanisms. The agent-based framework was developed using Claude Code, the Model Context Protocol, and Burp Suite Professional, while the scanner-based approach utilized Qualys Web Application Scanning. Results were mapped to a predefined ground truth covering SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting, and Broken Access Control and reported using Recall, Precision, and false-positive counts where estimable. title: Peer Review Report For: Exploring Revenue-Sharing Strategies as a Pathway to Inclusive Growth and Sustainability in Sri Lanka’s Tea Value Chain [version 1; peer review: 1 approved with reservations]
abstract: Purpose The tea industry, a cornerstone of agricultural economies across Asia and Africa, faces persistent challenges related to unequal value distribution, rising production costs, labour shortages, and climate uncertainty. This study systematically examines revenue-sharing (RS) strategies as a mechanism for promoting inclusive growth, equitable value distribution, and long-term sustainability within the tea value chain, with particular emphasis on the Sri Lankan context. Design/methodology/approach A Structured Literature Review (SLR) was conducted following a PRISMA-based review protocol. A total of 186 records were identified from five major academic databases, of which 32 studies published between 2000 and 2024 met the inclusion criteria. Bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer, together with thematic content analysis, was employed to identify the intellectual structure, research trends, and emerging themes within the literature. title: A three-stage conceptual framework for post-fire recovery in operating rooms: an evidence-informed opinion based on clinical experience and international guidelines
abstract: Operating-room fires, though rare, present unique risks to patient safety, staff health, and institutional resilience. Korean regulations (Medical Service Act, Framework Act on Fire Services, and Occupational Safety and Health Act) emphasize fire prevention and immediate response but lack systematic guidance for post-fire recovery, leading to inconsistent practices, delays in recovery, and compromises in safety. This article proposes a structured, evidence-informed conceptual framework for post-fire recovery in operating rooms. The framework was developed through the integration of relevant international guidelines, toxicological and indoor air quality literature, and clinical experience. The model integrates environmental and surface-contamination assessments; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) and negative-pressure remediation; phased personal protective equipment (PPE) deployment; and considerations for healthcare personnel safety. title: Preregistered Adversarial Batteries: A Falsifiable Protocol for Security-Testing Autonomous AI Systems
abstract: Security testing of autonomous AI systems suffers from a credibility gap: penetration-test reports are private, vendor claims are selectively disclosed, and red-team outcomes are published only when favorable. This preprint introduces Preregistered Adversarial Batteries (PAB), a protocol importing preregistration from clinical-trial science into security operations: every falsifier (a specific attack with a predicted verdict) is specified and publicly committed before execution; adjudication is deterministic with no language model in the decision path; results are written to an append-only public ledger and DOI-stamped. Critical events are scored as hold-by-design verdicts: the predicted outcome is that the system fails closed and waits for a human decision, so a refusal counts as a pass. Application to a self-healing AI infrastructure platform across six batteries reconstructing the declassified NSA BULLRUN-era tradecraft (operational faults, upstream context poisoning, cryptographic subversion, supply-chain interception, monitoring integrity, lawful compulsion): 30 falsifiers, 30 predicted verdicts, zero unexpected outcomes, six holds-by-design each adjudicated by the human opera

title: Quotient-Fiber Stratification, Universal Top-Fiber Absorption, and Machine-Verified Structural Bounds for the Union-Closed Sets Conjecture in Lean 4
abstract: # Quotient-Fiber Stratification, Universal Top-Fiber Absorption, and Machine-Verified Structural Bounds for the Union-Closed Sets Conjecture in Lean 4 **Ahmad Hasanov** *Independent Researcher & Formal Verification Architect* *Baku, Azerbaijan* `akhmad.hasanov@gmail.com` *October 2026* --- ## Abstract The Union-Closed Sets Conjecture (Frankl, 1979) asserts that for every finite union-closed family $\mathcal{F}$ of sets containing at least one non-empty set, there exists an element belonging to at least half of the members of $\mathcal{F}$. In 1992, Poonen demonstrated that local averaging over a minimal non-empty set $A_{\min}$ fails in general: there exist explicit union-closed families where every element $a \in A_{\min}$ has frequency strictly below $|\mathcal{F}|/2$ (a configuration termed a *Poonen local obstruction*). Recent entropy methods initiated by Gilmer (2022) established a constant lower bound of $0.01$, rapidly refined to $p^* = (3 - \sqrt{5})/2 \approx 0.381966$ by Sawin, Chase--Lovett, and Alweiss--Huang--Sellke, yet this information-theoretic boundary has resisted advancement to $0.500$ due to severe coordinate correlation barriers. title: LGCF Net: A CNN–Transformer Local–Global Fusion Network for Segmenting Deep-Opening Defects at Material Interfaces in Mortared-Stone Levee Revetments
abstract: Mortared-stone revetments on the waterside slopes of levees are continuously exposed to flow erosion, environmental variation, and material deterioration during long-term service. Fracture and spalling can therefore occur at the interfaces between stones and cementitious materials, producing anomalously deep openings. Such defects have irregular shapes and marked scale variations and are readily confused with normal joints, shadows, and dark textures. To address these challenges, this study proposes LGCF Net, a semantic segmentation network based on CNN–Transformer local–global feature fusion. ResNet50 and Swin Transformer Tiny are used to extract local texture features and global semantic features, respectively. A Local–Global Context Fusion (LGCF) module adaptively fuses the two feature types, after which a feature pyramid network performs multiscale decoding and defect prediction. LGCF Net achieved a precision of 0.9008, recall of 0.8125, Dice coefficient of 0.8543, and intersection over union (IoU) of 0.7457. title: emaki-mcp: MCP server for Seedance 2.5 and Seedance 2.0 video generation on emaki.ai
abstract: Official MCP server for emaki (emaki.ai), the Japanese-language AI video generator for Seedance 2.5 and Seedance 2.0. emaki-mcp is a stdio Model Context Protocol server that lets Claude, Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI or any MCP client generate video and images on an emaki account. Tools: generate_video (text to video, or image to video with a first-frame URL; default model Seedance 2.5), generate_image, check_status and credits. Runs use the caller's own API key and cost credits on their emaki account, the same price as on the website. Install: npx -y emaki-mcp with EMAKI_API_KEY from emaki.ai/settings/apikeys. title: AI Interviewers in Qualitative Research: A Framework for Design and Evaluation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to conduct semi-structured qualitative interviews, yet guidance for designing and evaluating AI interviewers against established methodological standards remains limited. First, we provide a practical guideline for developing methodologically grounded, safety-integrated AI interviewers, covering prompting, interview-protocol design, calibration, and safety procedures. Second, we develop a structured evaluation framework spanning six dimensions: methodological foundation, interview management, participant-answer quality, participant experience, ethics and safety, and system reliability. Third, we deploy and evaluate the resulting interviewer in 229 real-time voice interviews with older adults, followed by a post-interview survey. Results showed strong performance across dimensions. At the criterion level, performance was strongest for explicitly specified behaviors but less consistent for context-dependent judgments, including neutral acknowledgment, avoiding leading questions, and proportionate probing. These findings provide a practical foundation for designing, evaluating, and deploying AI interviewers at scale.

The software builds bus round trips from automatic vehicle location (AVL) records of 35 routes of Hermosillo, Mexico (January–August 2024), fixes a common evaluation frame on a 100 m grid, and compares ten arrival-time predictors: trajectory baselines, an hour-of-day historical mean, gradient-boosted trees and an LSTM. title: Desenvolupament d'una eina impulsada per agents d'intel·ligència artificial per al suport de tasques d'informàtica forense
abstract: [ES] La informática forense es un campo de gran relevancia dentro de la ciberseguridad debido al gran crecimiento de volumen y complejidad de las evidencias digitales, a causa del incremento de cantidad y sofisticación de los delitos informáticos en los últimos años. Estos procesos, realizados tradicionalmente de forma manual apoyados por herramientas especializadas, requieren de un alto grado de intervención humana. En la actualidad, el uso de agentes de inteligencia artificial va adquiriendo relevancia por su capacidad de automatizar tareas complejas y mejorar la eficiencia de los procesos donde participan. En este trabajo se propone un nuevo enfoque para abordar algunos de los principales problemas que enfrenta el analista forense moderno: la gestión de volúmenes masivos de evidencias heterogéneas, la complejidad propia de los artefactos digitales y la necesidad de obtener razonamientos interpretables que guíen y faciliten la investigación. Para ello, se diseña e implementa una herramienta basada en agentes de inteligencia artificial y el protocolo MCP (Model Context Protocol), capaz de procesar, correlacionar y razonar sobre evidencias digitales de forma autónoma. title: Agent Pointed Context: design records and payload specification
abstract: Companion record to the paper "Agent Pointed Context: letting a person point an AI agent at what they see, without sharing the screen" (Tomas Neira, 2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23382909). Agent Pointed Context (APC) is an interaction pattern in which an application exposes three identifier-only channels to any external agent connected over the Model Context Protocol (MCP): the person's current view, a pin the person places on a part of the screen, and the agent's presence on screen. title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Tool Descriptions Are Smelly! Towards Improving AI Agent Efficiency with Augmented MCP Tool Descriptions,
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) introduces a standard specification that defines how Foundation Model (FM)-based agents should interact with external systems by invoking tools. However, to understand a tool’s purpose and features, FMs rely on natural-language tool descriptions, making these descriptions a critical component in guiding FMs to select the optimal tool for a given (sub)task and to pass the right arguments to the tool. While defects or smells in these descriptions can misguide FM-based agents, their prevalence and consequences in the MCP ecosystem remain unclear. Hence, we examine 856 tools spread across 103 MCP servers empirically, assess their description quality, and their impact on agent performance. We identify six components of tool descriptions from the literature, develop a scoring rubric utilizing these components, and then formalize tool description smells based on this rubric. By operationalizing this rubric through an FM-based scanner, we find that 97.1% of the analyzed tool descriptions contain at least one smell, with 56% failing to state their purpose clearly. title: Element interaction manifolds for comparative analysis of geometric representations in protein-ligand recognition
abstract: Accurate modeling of protein–ligand interactions requires representations that capture both molecular geometry and chemically specific interactions. Existing approaches encode molecular recognition through several geometric formalisms, including differential geometry and spherical harmonic surface descriptors such as three-dimensional Zernike descriptors (3DZD). However, the relative roles of local curvature, surface area, volume, global shape, and chemical partitioning in protein–ligand recognition remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we present a unified geometric study centered on the Element Interaction Manifold (EIM) framework. We integrate element-interactive curvature, surface-area, and volume descriptors into a common representation and comparatively evaluate their roles in binding-affinity prediction and ligand-aware protein–ligand complex recognition. To place differential geometry in context, we compare EIM with standard 3DZD and a chemically partitioned extension termed element-pair 3DZD (EP-3DZD). title: Agentic Synthesis of Open-Source Biomedical Repositories and Clinical Literature into Interactive Diagnostic & Medical Learning Tools for Low-Resource Healthcare Settings
abstract: Frontline community health workers (CHWs) and rural clinics in low-resource settings—particularly across underserved municipalities in South Asia and rural regions of the United States—face a severe clinical knowledge bottleneck. While peer-reviewed biomedical literature, genomic variant databases, and open-source clinical calculators expand exponentially, these resources remain fragmented across unstructured texts and incompatible software repositories that require high-bandwidth connectivity and specialized bioinformatics literacy. This research protocol introduces **`gwf-clinical-synthesis`**, a non-commercial, computational dry-lab framework developed at GoWithFund Inc. Leveraging long-context multi-agent reasoning in **Google Antigravity** powered by **Gemini 4 Argon** (1M-token unified context window) and the **Google DeepMind (GDM) Science Skills** ecosystem, our pipeline orchestrates parallel literature retrieval across PubMed/NCBI Entrez, OpenAlex, ClinVar, and ChEMBL, fuses fragmented open-source clinical simulation repositories into lightweight offline-capable web applications, and executes automated multi-agent citation-verification loops to eliminate large language mod

Nunnarri: An AI-Enabled Universal IoT Management Platform Integrating MQTT, Local Language Models, and Model Context Protocol
abstract: The growing use of heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) devices creates operational challenges in device onboarding, telemetry collection, control, data persistence, and integration with intelligent services. This paper presents Nunnarri, a modular IoT management platform designed to bring these functions into a single deployable system. The public implementation combines a React and Vite dashboard, Node.js and Express API services, an MQTT/WebSocket gateway, two PostgreSQL database services, an Ollama-connected AI backend, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. The architecture separates identity and access data from IoT telemetry, provides a virtual-pin abstraction for device interaction, and exposes selected device-management operations to compatible AI clients through MCP tools, resources, and prompts. The system is packaged as a multi-container Docker Compose application and includes firmware integration material for ESP8266-class devices. The contribution of this work is an implementation-oriented architecture that connects conventional IoT messaging and web management with locally hosted language-model assistance and a standardized tool interface. title: Do tool-call interfaces carry the measurement conditions of their inputs? A preregistered audit of Model Context Protocol tool schemas
abstract: This preregistered audit asks whether the tool-call interfaces through which AI agents reach scientific and clinical software carry the conditions under which a measured input value was produced. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets a server advertise each tool with a name, an optional description and a JSON Schema for its inputs; an agent decides what to send from these alone. A measured value, such as a laboratory result, a vital sign or a gene expression level, means something only together with its method, unit, specimen, device and time of measurement. A tool validated under one set of conditions can accept a value produced under another without error unless its interface provides a place for those conditions to be stated at call time. We will audit the input schemas of publicly registered MCP servers. The sampling frame is a full snapshot of the official MCP Registry (42,317 entries, retrieved 2026-10-12, sealed by SHA-256), the protocol's reference implementations, and the MCP servers published with Paper2Agent (Nature, 2026). title: A novel behavioral paradigm to model hypermemory-like features in rats
abstract: Episodic memory is essential to everyday life and personal identity. However, its dysfunctions can profoundly affect mental health, and translational methods for investigating them in animals remain limited. Most rodent paradigms focus on memory deficits, whereas few tools model abnormally enhanced and persistent memories. Here, we developed a behavioral paradigm to induce hypermemory-like features in adult male and female rats using a version of object recognition (OR) and object location (OL) tasks specifically modified to mimic the rumination-like component of hypermemory. During the odor-context association training, rats explored two identical objects in the presence of a cinnamon scent. Over the following 6 h, they received 12 brief re-exposures in their home cage to either the cinnamon odor or an odor-free stimulus. By repeatedly reactivating the memory trace, these re-exposures promoted its hyperconsolidation without re-exposing animals to the original context or objects. Twenty-four hours later, memory was assessed under odor-free conditions. Odor re-exposure selectively enhanced OL memory in rats of both sexes, whereas OR memory remained unaffected. title: Fuzzy Kano Validation of Generative AI-Curated Features for Simponia Redesign
abstract: Background: Generative AI (Gen AI) has accelerated UX design processes, yet no systematic protocol exists to validate AI-curated features against actual user preferences before prototyping. Objective: This study applies the Fuzzy Kano Model as a validation checkpoint for Gen AI-curated features in the redesign of Simponia, a web-based portfolio and community management platform at Universitas Muhammadiyah Malang. Methods: An exploratory mixed-methods case design was used. Claude Opus generated 36 feature candidates from a Structured Requirements Document and ISO/IEC 25010 criteria. Fuzzy Kano validation involved 87 Informatics students; fuzzy membership and the Last of Maxima classification method were used to determine Kano categories, while weighted scoring was retained only for post-classification prioritization. Results: No features were classified as Must-be or One-dimensional (maximum Must-be membership degree = 0.073). Eleven features (30.6%) were classified as Attractive, and 25 (69.4%) as Indifferent. title: Adaptive Self-Reward and Mutual-Reward Switching in World Self-and-Mutual Models: A Framework for Autonomous Learning and Coordination
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental dynamics that support prediction, planning, and decision-making. However, the mechanisms through which a world-model-based system evaluates its own progress and coordinates evaluation across interacting models remain important design questions. Conventional individual reward mechanisms can support autonomous learning but may overlook opportunities for coordination, whereas shared or mutual reward mechanisms can encourage cooperation but may introduce communication costs, coordination overhead, and dependence on other models. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-Reward and Mutual-Reward Switching framework for World Self-and-Mutual Models (ASRMS-WSMM). The framework integrates self-reward, mutual reward, and adaptive reward-mode selection into a world-model-level architecture rather than treating the system as a collection of large language models. The proposed architecture distinguishes self-model evaluation from cross-model evaluation and allows the system to operate in self-reward mode, mutual-reward mode, or a hybrid mode. title: CuraStrand: Autonomous Multimodal Clinical Triage & Ambient Crisis Orchestration Framework over Model Context Protocol
abstract: An autonomous clinical triage and crisis orchestration framework integrating Model Context Protocol (MCP v2025-11-25), Amazon Bedrock foundation models, wearable biosignals, and formal Manchester Triage safety invariants.

abstract: The El-Rakhawi Comprehensive Framework for Decentralized Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Systems (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23389239) presents an integrative architectural framework synthesizing twenty critical dimensions of P2P research into a unified methodology. The monograph bridges theoretical overlay topologies (structured DHTs like Chord/Kademlia, unstructured networks, hybrid supernode architectures) with practical challenges in mobile, wireless, and resource-constrained environments. Core innovations include: (1) Delay-Tolerant P2P Systems (DTN) utilizing store-carry-forward paradigm for intermittently connected environments; (2) Lightweight gossip-based protocols for IoT sensor networks and MANETs; (3) Comprehensive security addressing Sybil attacks, Eclipse attacks, and data integrity via Merkle trees; (4) Economic models including tokenomics and DAO governance for sustainable commercial P2P applications; (5) Overlay monitoring and management for QoS assurance without central coordination. title: Embedded Systems and Internet of Things Foundations
abstract: The convergence of embedded systems and the Internet of Things (IoT) has accelerated the development of tiny machine learning (TinyML) real-time intelligence, which is delivered on ultra-low-power devices. Thus, this chapter examines the architecture, design methodologies, and emerging roles of embedded systems within the broader IoT ecosystem. This chapter provides a foundational understanding of embedded systems, establishing the components and structures of embedded systems, putting embedded system architectures into the context of IoT architectures, and understanding the increasing roles of embedded systems in improving intelligent edge computing. A detailed examination of embedded architectures, real-time operating systems, and performance limitations provided discourses on the trade-offs designers face between the outcome of embedded systems for real-world applications and the intentional consequences of designs. In the architectural context of IoT, smart services will realise their full potential when they leverage reliable, communicating sensors and actuators included in their design, and direct human intervention at the history collection void. title: Economic evaluation protocol of the Ntshembo (Hope) Trial (RCT) in rural and urban South Africa: an intervention to optimise adolescence body mass index (BMI) pre-conception to address the triple burden of malnutrition
abstract: South African adolescent girls face a triple burden of malnutrition, undernutrition alongside overweight/obesity, and micronutrient deficiencies, heightened risk factors for Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs). The Ntshembo trial is a South African Randomised Controlled Trial (RCT) that utilises Community Healthcare Workers to support at-risk adolescent girls (14–19 years old) in improving their body mass index (BMI) through nutrition- and behaviour-based interventions, combined with a household conditional cash transfer. The intervention aims to optimise BMI and, by doing so, reduce both individual and transgenerational risk for metabolic diseases like type-2 diabetes. This protocol outlines the methods that will be used alongside the intervention to conduct an economic evaluation, including a cost-effectiveness analysis, of the Ntshembo (Hope) RCT. The intervention cost will be estimated from the provider and societal perspectives. The cost of implementing the intervention in an RCT setting (scenario 1) and of replicating the intervention in a non-research context (scenario 2) will be modelled. title: Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts
abstract: Which inputs drive a language model's financial forecast? We construct synthetic earnings announcements that independently reverse 20-day momentum, non-informational commentary tone, and whether fixed actual EPS beats a manipulated consensus. Six instruction/chat checkpoint conversions from four families (0.49-7.61B base parameters) receive 2,016 prompts each under a direct-answer Q8_0 protocol. The design includes 24 numerical blocks, six commentary pairs, profits and losses, rising and falling annual EPS, and two surprise sizes. Both A/B answer assignments and U/D cover all 384 primary scenarios per conversion. We estimate matched changes in conditional answer-prefix scores, not calibrated market probabilities. Across these checkpoints, the primary EPS contrast ranges from -0.19 to 86.80 percentage points. The magnitude of the primary signed tone contrast exceeds that of EPS in 5 of six models, and momentum exceeds it in 5. Natural-word numerical diagnostic accuracy ranges from 51.0 to 95.8 percent. Adaptive Self-Selection and Cooperative Selection between Self-and-Interaction Models and World Models: A Unified Framework for Autonomous and Collaborative Decision-Making
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental dynamics, enabling intelligent systems to anticipate future states and evaluate potential actions. However, decision-making architectures that rely exclusively on internal model selection or continuous collaboration among multiple models may face limitations in adaptability, computational efficiency, uncertainty management, and decision robustness. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-and-Cooperative Selection Framework (ASCSF), a conceptual architecture that integrates world models with self-and-interaction models to support dynamic switching between autonomous self-selection and cooperative selection. Unlike approaches centered on large language models, the proposed framework operates at the level of structured models that represent environmental states, transition dynamics, objectives, constraints, and decision alternatives. The framework distinguishes two complementary selection modes. Self-selection enables an individual model to evaluate and select an action or candidate solution using its own internal representations. title: Jev-Routed Temporal Granularity with Recovery and Hysteresis for Causal Video Generation
abstract: Overview Causal video generators produce a rollout one temporal chunk at a time, which invites a simple efficiency idea: spend fine per-frame computation only where a segment is hard, and use cheaper coarse chunks, or even reuse, elsewhere. Realizing this idea requires three preconditions that are usually assumed rather than measured: a mode that is genuinely cheaper on the deployment hardware, a signal that predicts hard segments before generation, and an independent endpoint that certifies the trade. This deposit contains the official code, locked protocols, calibration freezes, and all audit artifacts for the manuscript "Jev-Routed Temporal Granularity with Recovery and Hysteresis for Causal Video Generation." The work audits all three preconditions end to end on Causal-rCM, a Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-480p causal text-to-video diffusion model, pairing a frame-wise mode (c1-1) with a chunk-3 mode (c3-3) and a near-zero-cost hold mode, and routing among them with a two-threshold controller with hysteresis and forced recovery. title: emem: A Content-Addressed, Verifiable Earth-Memory Protocol for AI Agents over Foundation-Model Embeddings - Poster
abstract: AI agents can change information when they exchange messages or complete long tasks. A value can be rounded. A location can change. An agent can use an observation from the wrong date. These errors can change decisions about the physical world. emem is an external memory protocol for AI agents. It uses content-addressed evidence records instead of paraphrases. An encoder creates a record from source information. An emem token identifies that record. A compatible receiving agent can resolve the token, decode the record, and check its contents. These operations do not depend on the AI model that sent the reference. Method This poster extends our earlier research on the emem protocol. We use a Sentinel-2A Level-2A observation from Keylong, India, dated 25 September 2026. The selected pixel has a normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) of 0.4709. We compare four handoff methods: prose, JSON, an opaque identifier, and a checked emem reference. We introduce controlled errors in values, spatial identity, time, source information, derivation, and record integrity. title: Agent Pointed Context: letting a person point an AI agent at what they see, without sharing the screen
abstract: People who work with an AI agent beside an application constantly say "this": this row, this number, this chart. When the agent lives outside the application, in a chat client connected over a tool protocol, it has no way to know what "this" is, and the person has to describe or paste it. We present Agent Pointed Context (APC), an interaction pattern in which the application exposes three small channels to any connected agent: what the person is looking at (the view), what the person has pointed the agent at (the pin), and what each agent is reading or changing on screen (presence). The application hosts no model and no chat. It shares identifiers and keys only, never pixels, text or amounts; the agent reads the facts behind a pointer through the tools it already has, so every read passes the same authorization as any other call. Because a pointer resolves against the data that produced what the person sees, not against the rendering, the agent answers from the inputs behind a figure (the accounts, statements and transactions that make it up) rather than from a description of it. title: When synthetic Delphi panels work: a graph-native methodology for participatory foresight under structural complexity
abstract: Foresight methodology has historically expanded one mode at a time — from supernatural divination through hermeneutic utopias, technical forecasting, emancipatory foresight, and participatory creative futures. The widespread adoption of large language models opens a sixth mode, synthetic foresight , in which participants and evidence bases are computationally generated rather than recruited. We position this mode as the sixth column of an established typology of approaches to the future, extending the participatory tradition. This paper empirically evaluates synthetic Delphi panels and characterises the conditions under which they produce reliable forecasts. We deployed a 60-agent panel — six LLM families across ten disciplinary personas — over a Neo4j knowledge graph of 25,823 circular economy publications, testing eight evidence-base configurations: no grounding, full-text and abstract literature, EU regulatory documents, pre-extracted weak signals, and two graph-derived vocabularies (bridge-term injection via class-based TF-IDF and bridge-author traversal). title: Agent Pointed Context: reference implementation and demo
abstract: Open reference implementation and live demo of Agent Pointed Context (APC): an application exposes three identifier-only channels to any agent connected over the Model Context Protocol (the person's view, a pin the person drops on a row or on a part of a computed figure, and the agent's presence on screen), and the person's own agent reads what a pin points at through its ordinary, authorized tools, joining it with what it already knows about the person. Three TypeScript packages (protocol, server, web) and Pulse, a synthetic SaaS analytics demo on Cloudflare Workers with one Durable Object per visitor. Live at https://apc.tineira.com.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Reinforcement and Mutual Reinforcement in Multi-Agent Systems: A Dynamic Framework for Individual and Collective Intelligence Optimization
abstract: Multi-agent systems can improve their performance through individual learning and inter-agent cooperation. However, relying exclusively on individual reinforcement may limit the exploitation of complementary knowledge, whereas persistent mutual reinforcement may introduce communication overhead, correlated errors, excessive behavioral conformity, and dependence on potentially unreliable agents. These limitations motivate a dynamic framework in which agents adaptively switch between self-reinforcement and mutual reinforcement according to task conditions, learning progress, uncertainty, interaction quality, and resource constraints. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Reinforcement and Mutual Reinforcement (AS-SMR), a general framework for multi-agent systems. Self-reinforcement enables an agent to improve its policy through individual experience, self-evaluation, and locally available feedback. Mutual reinforcement enables agents to improve their policies through reciprocal feedback, cross-agent evaluation, experience exchange, and mutually informative learning signals. title: Mapping the Landscape of Integrated Reporting: Cross‐Industry Insights and Global Perspectives From a Topic Modeling Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates how companies across different industries emphasize themes within Integrated Reporting (IR), as promoted by the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC). As IR gains relevance for advancing Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure, understanding sectoral reporting patterns becomes essential. Building on dialogic accounting, we frame IR as a continuum between monologic disclosure—where reporting remains finance‐led and stakeholder dialog is effectively “closed down”—and dialogic accountability, where multiple value dimensions are connected and trade‐offs are made visible. Using topic modeling (Latent Dirichlet Allocation), multidimensional scaling, and ANOVA tests, the analysis examines 425 best‐practice integrated reports from Corporate Register and the Integrated Reporting Example Database of the IFRS Council. Results show substantial cross‐industry variations; however, the analysis also highlights three overarching patterns that are not implied by industry differences alone. title: WebMCP: A Browser-Native navigator.modelContext Standard for Agentic Web Automation
abstract: Purpose: This paper examines WebMCP, a proposed browser-native web platform standard that lets websites expose explicit, schema-described tools to large language model agents, as an alternative to actuation, in which an agent simulates the clicks, keystrokes, and navigation a human would perform. Methodology: The paper analyzes WebMCP, incubated within the World Wide Web Consortium's Web Machine Learning Community Group and implemented as an origin trial in the Chrome browser beginning with Chrome 149. We describe WebMCP's architecture, including the browser-mediated JavaScript interface navigator.modelContext and a declarative HTML annotation form, and its relationship to Anthropic's Model Context Protocol; analyze its security and permission model; place it within a comparative design-space taxonomy alongside DOM automation, computer-use agents, and server-side Model Context Protocol integrations; and examine the emerging standardization landscape, including browser vendor positions and adjacent efforts such as the Agentic Commerce Protocol. A generalized use case illustrates how a composite retail website might expose search, filtering, and checkout tools under this model. All s

title: Prompt Engineering for Small Language Models: Evaluating ICL for Portuguese Sentiment Analysis
abstract: The In-Context Learning (ICL) paradigm enables adapting LLMs without parameter tuning. This work evaluates the impact of prompt engineering on 9B models for Brazilian Portuguese sentiment classification, comparing six prompting formats (fewand zero-shot) across three linguistically diverse models (Gemma2-9B-it, Boto-9B-IT, Qwen3.5-9B) and four public datasets, anchored by a fine-tuned encoder (MSA-DistilBERT, ∼0.1B) and a 685B MoE model (DeepSeek-V3.2) under a unified protocol. Results show that all 9B models outperform the encoder and recover 71–101% of the weak-to-strong gap, with Qwen3.5-9B achieving the highest mean coverage (94.5%). Statistical tests indicate that well-defined instructions are the main driver of ICL performance, capturing most of the achievable accuracy even in zero-shot settings, while elaborate formats (roleplay, JSON schema, meta-prompting) add no consistent gain over a minimal instruction-plus-demonstrations prompt, offering practical guidance for deploying SLMs in resource-constrained PT-BR NLP scenarios.

title: A Cognitive, Quantum-Inspired Learning Framework for Energy-Efficient and Reliable Routing in Wireless Body Area Networks
abstract: Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs) are critical enablers of real-time, non-invasive healthcare monitoring, enabling continuous acquisition and wireless transmission of vital physiological signals such as electrocardiogram (ECG), heart rate, and motion data. However, their practical deployment faces significant challenges due to stringent energy constraints, dynamic on-body channel variations induced by mobility, and multi-class Quality-of-Service (QoS) requirements, particularly ultra-low latency ( $$\le 18\,\text {ms}$$ ) for emergency alerts and high reliability ( $$\ge 99.5\%$$ PDR) for diagnostic data. Conventional routing protocols often rely on static topologies or reactive mechanisms that fail under the coupled spatio-temporal variability of physiological dynamics and wireless channels. To address these limitations, we propose QuantumEERP-Net, a novel, intelligent, and self-optimizing routing framework that synergistically integrates Multi-Agent Dueling Double Deep Q-Networks (D3QN), a Quantum-Inspired Dual Prediction Model (Q-DPM), and Context-Aware Adaptive Routing into a fully decentralized architecture. title: AI Based Secure Persona Prediction and Data Leakage Prevention System
abstract: Organizations exchange confidential information through email, cloud platforms, and enterprise collaboration applications, and insiders with legitimate access are among the hardest sources of leakage to detect. Rule-based Data Leakage Prevention (DLP) tools match keywords and patterns but cannot determine who is sending the data, whether the behavior is consistent with that person's role, or why an alert was raised. Behavior analytics, in contrast, model users but largely ignore message content. This paper presents the design of an AI-based secure persona prediction and data leakage prevention system that combines these two views. A persona engine using DistilBERT and Bi-LSTM models infers a behavioral persona from communication text; a hybrid detector using Named Entity Recognition (NER) and validated pattern matching identifies sensitive content; and a dynamic risk scoring algorithm combines data criticality, frequency, behavioral anomaly, and channel context into a continuous risk score. A priority-based decision policy selects graded actions, suppresses duplicate alerts, and adapts thresholds using analyst feedback. SHAP and LIME are integrated to provide decision explanations

title: Phenotyping of the post-traumatic immune response and therapeutic strategies in a refined murine two-hit trauma model
abstract: Trauma and its consequences are one of the leading causes of death among young patients. The reasons for mortality vary depending on when they occur. Especially in the later stages of care (days to weeks after the trauma), death is often caused by immunological complications. The two-hit hypothesis offers an explanation for this. It classifies the initial trauma as the “first hit” for the immune system, triggering a systemic immune response. Hereby, the systemic inflammatory response (SIRS) and its compensatory mechanism (CARS) stand in a fragile balance. This is significantly influenced by regulatory T cells (CD4+ Tregs) and the interplay between immune cells and platelets. This delicate balance can be destabilized by “second hits” occurring during trauma therapy (e.g. surgery, reperfusion events, or ICU stay). This promotes complications, with sepsis being one of the most dangerous in this context. Sepsis is a complex syndrome that includes different immunological phenotypes. It is currently defined as life-threatening multiple organ failure based on an infection-triggered, misdirected systemic immune response. title: Efficient fine-tuning of foundation models for trustworthy medical image analysis
abstract: The domain of biomedicine, specifically biomedical image analysis, has benefitted significantly from advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI). Foundation models have revolutionized medical image analysis by enabling the transfer of knowledge from large-scale pre-training on their source domain, mostly comprising of natural images, to specialized, data-scarce medical tasks through a process termed as fine-tuning. This is of critical importance in medical image analysis where data privacy laws and high acquisition costs limit the availability of large, annotated datasets, thus, prohibitting successful training of foundation models. However, the direct application of these models to the ethically sensitive domain of healthcare faces significant challenges related to trustworthiness. Models trained on imbalanced real-world data can inadvertently encode and amplify biases leading to unfair outcomes. Similarly, generative models pose risks to patient privacy through memorising the training data. Furthermore, the lack of standardized, comprehensive evaluation protocols for these models makes it difficult to assess their true clinical value. This thesis presents a cohesive body of work tha

title: ABC: A Conversational Bioinformatics Analysis Platform for Agricultural Breeding
In-Context Teacher–Student Guidance for Open-Weight Browser Agents
abstract: Browser agents based on large language models can automate web tasks, but deployment remains constrained by repeated model calls, monetary cost, and privacy risks. In practical settings, agents often process page states that may expose credentials, personal data, internal records, business documents, or authenticated session information. Sending these states and interaction histories to external model APIs can increase the risk of data leakage, unauthorized retention, or unintended disclosure. This paper investigates whether reasoning traces from a stronger teacher model can improve open-weight browser agents without fine-tuning. We propose In-Context Learning Guidance (ICLG), a training-free teacher–student protocol in which the teacher solves representative browser tasks offline and its reasoning traces are converted into reusable prompt-level guidance for similar tasks. The student then uses this guidance during execution while reading the concrete target values from the current browser instance. title: Editorial: Integrating musculoskeletal ultrasound and emerging imaging modalities in surgical planning and rehabilitation
abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders represent a major and growing contributor to disability worldwide, with their burden expected to increase substantially over the coming decades [1] . Within this context, advances in high-resolution ultrasound, shear wave elastography (SWE), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), radiomics, and artificial intelligence are changing the role of imaging from anatomical description toward quantitative assessment, risk stratification, and clinical decision support. This Research Topic aimed to explore how ultrasound and emerging imaging technologies can be integrated across the surgical and rehabilitation continuum: from diagnosis and preoperative planning to intraoperative risk assessment, postoperative monitoring, and evaluation of functional recovery. title: ExpertTwins: Auditable Long Horizon Scientific Panels through Grounded Expertise
abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems increasingly assign roles to agents and let them deliberate. A role label, however, does not specify which evidence an agent can bring or which standard it applies before accepting a conclusion. Agents that read one another's outputs tend to converge. We present ExpertTwins, a framework in which each seat of a scientific panel is defined by an inspectable evidence policy. Discipline seats retrieve under field-specific queries, and scientist-associated seats retrieve from attributed publications and a citation-derived scholarly neighborhood. Private initial packets, structured exchange, cited-source disclosure, deterministic quotation checks, and peer source review turn deliberation into an auditable record, which we also render as interactive idea-flow maps. Scientist associations denote publication-grounded perspectives, not replicas or endorsements of named researchers. In a nine-seat, four-turn neuroblastoma panel, 438 of 439 claims passed all attached quotation checks, and seats withdrew or defended positions when challenged on their evidence. title: An Auditable Binary Evidence-Escalation Protocol for Prompt-Constrained Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering
abstract: Technical-support and engineering knowledge services must decide whether one selected passage is sufficient or additional retrieved evidence should enter the generation prompt. Aggregate accuracy and mean context size conceal whether expansion recovers omitted evidence, adds no value, or harms an otherwise correct answer. We present an auditable binary evidence-escalation protocol for this operational decision. A logistic controller uses 27 pre-generation question and evidence-scoring features to select either one document or a model–task-specific full-candidate action; its outcome-derived development target is configuration-specific, and the resulting policy comparison is conditional on the single development-selected fit rather than an out-of-sample estimate of controller-selection performance. We evaluate deterministic distractor-augmented stress tests derived from SQuAD, WikiQA, and HotpotQA using two open-weight generators and one opaque GPT-compatible API. title: PW-SoD: simulator, protocol and results for "Lightweight Adaptive Send-on-Delta Heuristics for Data Reduction in Wireless Acoustic Sensor Networks".
abstract: Simulator, evaluation protocol, scripts and results of the article "Lightweight Adaptive Send-on-Delta Heuristics for Data Reduction in Wireless Acoustic Sensor Networks". The simulator (OMNeT++ 6.4 / INET 4.7) models a single-hop IEEE 802.15.4 network of nodes that report the emission of industrial machines to a sink, which estimates the sound level at a moving worker. It implements periodic reporting, fixed-threshold Send-on-Delta and its dB and local variants, the adaptive heuristics H1-H3, the propagation-weighted rule H4 (PW-SoD) and a context-aware adaptive Send-on-Delta baseline. The record contains the protocol fixed before the test runs and its six dated amendments, the frozen parameter selections, the scene generator, the analysis scripts, every table and figure of the article and of its supplementary material, and the per-seed results needed to recompute them without running the simulator. The full git history is included as a bundle, with a tag on the commit of the protocol and of each amendment, so that their dates can be checked.

title: BioInteract combines residue-level cross-attention with protein-language and physicochemical priors for interpretable drug–target interaction prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug–target interactions (DTIs) can support the prioritisation of candidate pairs, yet published models are usually compared through numbers quoted across papers whose protocols differ, and their attribution outputs are rarely accompanied by an explicit statement of where the model may be trusted. We present BioInteract, a DTI framework combining a chemistry-aware molecular graph encoder, an ESM-2/physicochemical protein residue encoder with a configured domain-label channel, and bidirectional cross-attention, and we evaluate it inside a matched-protocol benchmark on the Davis kinase inhibitor dataset in which every model is trained with one shared partition, seed, optimiser, schedule and threshold rule. The comparison is a three-model ladder that changes one component at a time, so that adding the frozen ESM-2 representation and then replacing concatenation with cross-attention can be read separately. Both steps help, but by protocol-dependent amounts: the protein language model adds 0.120 and 0.063 AUPRC under the random and Target-ID-held-out protocols, whereas cross-attention adds 0.067 and 0.201 AUPRC under the same two protocols. title: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing
abstract: External-memory systems extend language-model applications beyond a context window, but their quality depends critically on the model executing the write path: deciding what to retain, how precisely to represent it, and how new evidence should update persistent state. Existing frameworks typically place a general-purpose large language model behind framework-specific prompts. This raises serving cost, and a writer specialized for one protocol does not transfer directly to another; a unified model that can operate across established memory frameworks remains largely unexplored. We present Hy-Memory-30B-A3B, a compact long-term-memory writer trained across Mem0, MemOS, and Hy-Memory. Memory On-Policy Distillation teaches framework-specific write protocols on student-generated states; Memory RL then optimizes downstream answerability using dense per-chunk probes, attributed cross-chunk rewards, over-storage controls, and chunk-level GRPO. Carrying policy-written banks across windows keeps training aligned with deployment. On fixed 20% benchmark subsamples, Hy-Memory-30B-A3B ranks first on all four evaluated harnesses, including held-out EverMemOS, with a 55.49% macro average versus 54

title: When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill
abstract: Reusing the attention KV cache across requests is a standard way to cut prefill cost in long-context LLM serving, and production systems increasingly back the per-engine cache with a remote tier shared by every engine. We study such a tier in a disaggregated deployment of GLM-5.3, an FP8 mixture-of-experts model with multi-head latent attention (MLA), on 8xB300 nodes running prefill context parallelism (PCP8). Enabling the remote tier (LMCache with a Valkey store) left median time-to-first-token unchanged but raised the 16k-token p99 from 3.96 s to 17.3 s. Replaying a production request stream on an isolated engine, we find that a remote hit took 0.88 s against 0.31 s to recompute the prompt, and that synchronous loading turned a hit-heavy stream into an unstable queue: p99 83.32 s with the GPUs 7% busy. A two-term cost model explains both: a hit pays off only if the tier delivers more than B* = sR (2.53 GB/s for this model and GPU), and a fixed per-hit engine cost (T0 ~ 0.33 s) means that hits on prompts shorter than about 17k tokens cannot beat recompute at any bandwidth. title: OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
abstract: Reliable repository-level coding requires agents not only to generate correct code but also to preserve constraints and respond to tool feedback across long interactions. However, our diagnostic analysis shows that agents often fail to act on relevant information already available in context, while final Pass/Fail outcomes provide only sparse process supervision. We introduce On-Policy Reminder Distillation (OPRD), which combines Multi-Scope Reminder supervision with outcome-based routing on reminder-free student rollouts. Successful rollouts provide autoregressive self-imitation targets, whereas failed rollouts receive Reminder-conditioned reverse-KL supervision from a teacher that re-evaluates the same student-generated prefixes. A Global Reminder converts final-test diagnostics into trajectory-level guidance, while Turn-local Reminders apply only to the next decision following the relevant environment observation. The teacher and student share a two-stage initialization from Coding SFT and Instruction-Following (IF) SFT. At inference, the student operates without Reminders. title: My Credentials, Please: Detecting Filesystem Capability Laundering in MCP Servers at Scale
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how AI agents invoke external tools. MCP servers expose tools through a declared contract consisting of a name, description, and argument schema. In typical local deployments, client-side approval of a tool call grants the underlying server process broad host filesystem permissions rather than restricting it to the declared operation. We study the resulting vulnerability class, filesystem capability laundering, where attacker-steered arguments cause a tool to access sensitive host files outside its declared contract and deployment scope. We analyze this capability gap across three layers: server-category screening (L1), per-tool contract analysis (L2), and bypassable path-validation checks (L3). We design MCP-FSD to catalog MCP servers, infer least-privilege boundaries per tool, plant credential fixtures outside those boundaries, and evaluate exploitability and sandbox containment via paired dynamic execution. Across 21,097 MCP servers from nine registries, 787 of 4,806 triaged servers (16.4%) exhibit filesystem capabilities despite non-filesystem functional classifications. title: Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts
abstract: Which inputs drive a language model's financial forecast? We construct synthetic earnings announcements that independently reverse 20-day momentum, non-informational commentary tone, and whether fixed actual EPS beats a manipulated consensus. Six instruction/chat checkpoint conversions from four families (0.49-7.61B base parameters) receive 2,016 prompts each under a direct-answer Q8_0 protocol. The design includes 24 numerical blocks, six commentary pairs, profits and losses, rising and falling annual EPS, and two surprise sizes. Both A/B answer assignments and U/D cover all 384 primary scenarios per conversion. We estimate matched changes in conditional answer-prefix scores, not calibrated market probabilities. Across these checkpoints, the primary EPS contrast ranges from -0.19 to 86.80 percentage points. The magnitude of the primary signed tone contrast exceeds that of EPS in 5 of six models, and momentum exceeds it in 5. Natural-word numerical diagnostic accuracy ranges from 51.0 to 95.8 percent. title: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization
abstract: AI agents now pause for approval before they send money, delete files or email outsiders, and that approval is usually treated as a second factor. We argue it is one only when compromising the agent cannot produce it and when it names exactly what it approves, and we test both conditions. We define twelve attacks on the approval path, including decoy recipients, amount cancellation, card padding, label spoofing, enrollment squatting and threshold splitting, and run them against the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), the Microsoft action-bound approval design and Model Context Protocol (MCP) elicitation. An audit of ten agent runtimes finds no third-party verifiable approval record, no flood limits where measurable, and post-approval argument changes in four of eight runtimes with measurable binding. As a reference defense we build ASU (Agent Step-Up), a gateway that renders the approval card from a canonical effect descriptor, has a passkey on the phone of the user sign its digest, and executes only the stored call. title: Unsupervised Machine Learning for Low Back Pain Phenotyping: A Scoping Review of Data-Driven Clustering and Validation
abstract: Detailed Description of the Research Project Low back pain (LBP) is a major cause of disability and a substantial healthcare and socioeconomic burden. Many presentations are classified as non-specific LBP, and patients differ considerably in symptom mechanisms, course, functional impact, and treatment response. These differences reflect interactions among biological, biomechanical, psychological, behavioral, and social factors. Traditional variable-by-variable or expert-defined approaches may miss complex multidimensional patterns. Unsupervised machine learning offers data-driven approaches to discover subgroups and phenotypes without prespecified outcome labels. Studies have used patient-reported outcomes, psychological measures, clinical and demographic data, biomechanics, electromyography, imaging, sensors, and combinations of modalities. However, the distribution of feature domains, the methodological choices used for clustering, and the extent of stability and independent validation remain unclear. title: Theoretical and methodological approaches to building a psychological support system in the rehabilitation of chronic musculoskeletal pain
abstract: The aim of the article is to provide a theoretical and methodological rationale for an integrative four-stage model of psychological support in the rehabilitation of people with chronic musculoskeletal pain, combining Ukrainian psychological approaches with contemporary international concepts of chronic pain and psychological adaptation. The methodological framework includes systemic, personality-oriented, and subject-activity approaches. Critical literature analysis, comparative conceptual analysis, systematisation, conceptual synthesis, and theoretical modelling were applied. The source base comprises Ukrainian and international publications on biopsychosocial rehabilitation, clinical and psychological assessment of chronic pain, pain catastrophising, emotion regulation, self-efficacy, and psychological flexibility. The theoretical synthesis resulted in an integrative model consisting of four interrelated stages: assessment, psychoeducation, intervention, and maintenance. The assessment stage covers pain intensity and functional impact, cognitive and emotional responses, avoidance behaviour, self-regulation resources, and social context. title: Priming Base Models for Agentic Post-Training: An Open Midtraining Recipe
abstract: Frontier models, general-purpose and domain-specific alike, now include a midtraining stage between pretraining and post-training, but little has been published about how this stage is built. We present an open midtraining recipe that primes base models for agentic post-training, and we show its effectiveness on two Nemotron models of different sizes. Pretraining typically runs at short context and sees almost no agent interactions, while SFT data is mostly synthetic, and very long SFT stages can hurt the model's later RL trainability. Our midtraining stage sits between the two. It trains at 256K context for hundreds of billions of tokens on a diverse mixture of natural software-engineering data like packed repositories, pull requests, commit histories, and build logs together with a small share of agentic traces. On Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, 500B midtraining tokens improve SWE-bench Verified from 60.7 to 64.5, SWE-bench Multilingual from 55.8 to 62.8, and SWE-bench Pro from 32.0 to 35.5 after identical full SFT. On the larger Nemotron 3.5 Super, 280B midtraining tokens improve DeepSWE, a harder benchmark of long-horizon tasks, from 11.7 to 15.7 and SWE-bench Verified from 72.9 to 74

title: PocketTSLM: Deploying an On-Device Soft-Prompt Time-Series Language Model for Privacy-Preserving Smartphone Reasoning
abstract: Consumer phones and wearables increasingly collect physiological time-series data, yet most mobile systems treat these streams as summaries or text rather than as temporal evidence. This representation is poorly matched to personal health systems that need to retrieve, route, or summarize sensor evidence while preserving temporal structure. Cloud-hosted time-series language models avoid smartphone limits, but they repeatedly move sensitive physiology off the device and add latency and per-query compute cost. Mobile model alternatives that aggregate time-series data into statistical features or serialize raw samples as text either compress temporal structure or exhaust the context and memory budgets of small on-device models. We present PocketTSLM, a mobile-native deployment of OpenTSLM SoftPrompt, the soft-prompt variant of the OpenTSLM time-series language model. PocketTSLM runs fully on a consumer smartphone by injecting encoded time-series windows as embeddings instead of tokenizing time series as text. title: Strategic Pharmaceutical Procurement for Surgical Care in Public Hospitals: A Scoping Review of Health System Architecture and Payment Reforms
abstract: Background. Rising surgical expenditures challenge the financial sustainability of public health systems. Pharmaceutical procurement is an important component of surgical care, but procurement choices are shaped by financing, governance, pricing policy, and provider-payment incentives. This scoping reviews mapped pharmaceutical procurement strategies used in public hospital surgical care and examined how health system architecture and payment reforms influence their design and implementation. Methods. We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR and a prospectively registered protocol. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language literature published from 1 January 2018 through 31 December 2025 using a Population-Concept-Context framework. Forty-three sources were included after duplicate removal, title/abstract screening, and full-text assessment. Procurement mechanisms, pricing and reimbursement levers, provider-payment arrangements, health system context, and reported outcomes were charted and synthesized narratively. Results. title: Implementation evaluation of community-based physical activity programmes for secondary prevention following stroke in Ireland: a RE-AIM and CFIR-informed mixed-methods study protocol using ExWell Medical as a case study.
abstract: Background Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability globally and in Ireland, with prevalence rising due to population ageing. Physical activity is a key component of secondary prevention and recovery; however, there is limited evidence on how community-based exercise programmes are implemented, delivered, and sustained in routine practice. Addressing these gaps is essential to inform national policy and service planning, particularly within the context of Sláintecare and the Health Service Executive’s National Stroke Strategy. This implementation evaluation forms part of the broader INsPIRE (Informing National Policy for Physical Activity-based Secondary Prevention of Stroke in Ireland) project, which aims to generate policy-relevant evidence on scalable and sustainable models of community-based physical activity. Methods This protocol outlines a mixed-methods implementation evaluation using ExWell, a community-based exercise programme, as a real-world case study. title: MC-DeTra: Motion-Consistent Joint Object Detection and Socially-Aware Trajectory Forecasting in Bird’s-Eye-View Images
Physics-Simulation-Informed Conditional Surrogate for Reconstruction of Multi-Cluster Hydraulic-Fracture States
abstract: Abstract Multicluster hydraulic-fracture growth is governed by stress interference and time-varying fluid partitioning. High-fidelity simulation is therefore costly to update frequently during a treatment. This study develops PGStateNet, a conditional surrogate that reconstructs clusterlocal fracture states from physics-generated sequences synchronized with recorded pumping schedules. The reference calculation retains displacement-discontinuity elastic coupling, fracture flow, mass conservation, perforation-entry loss, and dynamic cluster-rate allocation. Three-dimensional fracture elements are projected onto fixed maximum-aperture grids. PGStateNet carries the current grid forward as explicit spatial memory and combines it with a 17-component treatment, completion, and geomechanical condition vector. Perforation- centred, distance, and local-support maps provide spatial context. A FiLM-modulated residual encoder-decoder then predicts a bounded aperture increment. Footprint and projected length–height losses complement the aperture-field loss. title: From Documents to Digital Governance: A Model-Driven Governance Framework for Field Development Planning
abstract: Abstract Field Development Planning (FDP) increasingly requires integrating complex subsurface, well, production, facility, economic, and assurance workflows under tighter performance, emissions, and cost expectations. Traditional document-driven governance, relying on spreadsheets, slide decks, and manual stage-gate checklists, can contribute to inconsistent assumptions, extended cycle times, and limited traceability. This paper investigates how model-driven governance, in which rules, assumptions, and constraints are represented as computable models, can transform FDP into a governed, context-driven digital ecosystem. The paper develops a model-driven governance framework that encodes strategic intent, constraint envelopes, shared assumptions, validation rules, and decision checkpoints within a unified digital meta-model. The approach draws on principles from model-driven engineering, enterprise meta-models, and policy-as-code practices. The framework is realized through a Model-Driven Governance System (MDGS) for Field Development Planning, in which governance logic is formalized, executed, and continuously evaluated within a closed-loop digital architecture. title: Aggregation-Based Upscaling for Geologically Consistent High-Fidelity Reservoir Simulation with Process-Based Models
abstract: Abstract Process-based stratigraphy models, simply referred to as process-based models (PBMs) for turbidite reservoirs capture the complex interplay between topography, gravity-driven flow, and associated sediment deposition and erosion events in a more consistent fashion with natural observations compared to alternatives. Recent developments in computer hardware and algorithms have started enabling the construction of full-field PBMs conditioned to static data. In this paper, we describe key enabler algorithms for the effective field-scale dynamic simulation of PBMs under subsurface uncertainty for more robust hydrocarbon recovery performance predictions. We have developed a protocol for physics-based representation of thin but laterally extensive shale layers (shale drapes), and their incorporation into surface-based grids in terms of transmissibility multiplier surfaces for more memory efficient simulations. We have developed stratigraphy-driven aggregation-based upscaling method that significantly reduces the active gridblock count and simulation run time while retaining flow-relevant features of PBMs. Our upscaling method operates both in vertical and areal directions adaptive

title: Faculty-supervised AI-supported BOPPPS-CBL and performance on a simulated neurological-emergency assessment among junior-college medical interns: a batch-stratified randomized educational study
abstract: Background County hospitals and township health centers in China provide frontline care for time-sensitive neurological emergencies, and three-year junior-college clinical medicine programs are an important pathway into this workforce. We evaluated a faculty-supervised artificial intelligence (AI)-supported BOPPPS (Bridge-in, Objectives, Pre-assessment, Participatory Learning, Post-assessment, and Summary) and case-based learning (CBL) instructional package among junior-college medical interns. Methods In this prospective, batch-stratified randomized educational study, 118 interns from 12 monthly rotation batches were assigned to AI-supported BOPPPS-CBL ( n = 58) or conventional BOPPPS-CBL ( n = 60) during a one-month neurology rotation. The intervention used standardized DeepSeek prompts for Socratic questioning, error-focused feedback, and structured reflection under faculty supervision. The primary endpoint was the total score on a locally developed four-station simulated neurological-emergency assessment (0–100). title: Evaluation of Algorithmic Carbon Footprint and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools in Environmental Education Programs: Systematic Review
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in educational settings creates pedagogical opportunities while raising environmental concerns regarding data center energy consumption and physical infrastructure footprint. This systematic review synthesizes scientific evidence on the algorithmic carbon footprint of AI tools implemented in environmental education programs. Adhering to the PRISMA 2020 statement and an adapted PICoS framework (Population: educational stakeholders; Phenomenon of interest: AI carbon/energy auditing; Context: environmental/sustainability education; Study design: empirical and theoretical studies), systematic searches were conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and ERIC up to 6 August 2026. Seven studies met the eligibility criteria: 5 empirical, 1 scoping review, and 1 theoretical-conceptual synthesis. Quality appraisal utilized MMAT (2018 version) for primary empirical studies and an adapted SANRA (2019 version) for non-empirical documents, followed by qualitative narrative synthesis. title: RIDI-REAL-UPDATES-v1: Prospective locked protocol for individual correctness changes across released AI model updates
abstract: This is the complete, prospective execution-lock registration for RIDI-REAL-UPDATES-v1. It is a separate public registration linked to the incomplete earlier narrative record https://osf.io/pkde5/ and the related, distinct RIDI-PREDICT record https://osf.io/xrzp5/. At submission, scientific model-generation units completed: 0/24. This is not a report of outcomes or an attempt to repair P8; P8 remains INCOMPLETE. Study design: Six pinned incumbent-to-successor language-model pairs (12 exact revisions), applied to 800 frozen reference questions drawn from Natural Questions (250), HotpotQA (250), and FEVER (300), with original BM25 retrieved top-10 contexts. Each model runs a single-question main condition and a 16-question replay-floor condition. The preregistered endpoints compare aggregate accuracy, paired individual-question correctness changes, replay noise and whether frozen RIDI-PREDICT fragility F_B predicts those changes. Confirmatory thresholds and 100,000 within-benchmark paired bootstrap resamples are specified in the archived protocol. title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms in General Intelligent Agents: A Parallel-World Framework for Dynamic Autonomous and Collaborative Intelligence
abstract: Intelligent agents can improve their behavior through autonomous internal processes, interactions with other agents, or combinations of both. However, systems that rely on a single operational mode may become constrained by repetitive strategies, limited perspectives, insufficient information exchange, or unnecessary coordination costs. This paper proposes the Parallel-World Adaptive Self–Mutual Intelligence Framework (PWASMI), a general conceptual and methodological framework for intelligent agents that adaptively switch between self-mechanisms and mutual mechanisms. Unlike approaches restricted to large language models, the proposed framework encompasses heterogeneous intelligent entities, including software agents, robotic agents, autonomous decision-making systems, adaptive controllers, and other computational or embodied forms of intelligence. The framework introduces parallel-world branching, in which multiple instances or developmental branches of the same originating agent pursue different strategies, hypotheses, objectives, or learning trajectories. title: Enhanced person profiles: a cluster randomised trial protocol for Swiss long-term care facilities
abstract: Abstract Background Family participation and teamwork are crucial components of person-centred dementia care in long-term care facilities (LTCFs) and are therefore widely recommended. However, these often remain ad hoc and staff-dependent in LTCF settings. Robust evidence on reproducible whole-team models for family participation and their impact on the quality of life of people with dementia is limited. The person profile is a complex intervention that has been tested under randomised controlled trial conditions, but family participation and teamwork were identified as weak areas in this intervention. Consequently, we developed the enhanced person profile. This programme incorporates clinical tools for routine family participation and psychological safety methods that enhance teamwork, ultimately aiming to improve the quality of life of people with dementia. Methods We will conduct a two-period, two-sequence cluster randomised crossover trial in 20 LTCFs in German-speaking Switzerland with 260 people with dementia. title: Tekmeria: Server-Issued Citation Handles and a Deterministic Audit for Biomedical LLM Answers
abstract: Language models that answer biomedical questions with citations can cite papers that do not exist, misquote the ones that do, and cite retracted work. Most checks run after the answer is written and must judge whether an imperfect bibliographic match is the right work. We describe tekmeria, an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for PubMed, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov and openFDA. Every passage it returns carries a handle whose check code is a truncated keyed MAC over the passage's locator, so the installation that issued a handle can tell a genuine citation from an invented one without a bibliographic search, whichever model or host wrote the answer. A deterministic audit separates malformed, forged, unavailable and withdrawn citations from misquotes, flags retracted, preprint and outdated sources, and passes an answer only when every sentence is cited and every citation is valid. A conformance evaluation plants citations in 34 categories, drawn from seven real records, with ground truth from a reference oracle that the same author wrote separately from the audit. title: THE TRANSORDINAL EMERGENCE PRINCIPLE (TEP)
abstract: AbstractThis manuscript proposes the Transordinal Emergence Principle (TEP) as a candidate, domain-independent systemic principle describing a specific transformation pattern: an originating specification is processed through a context, representation, or operational pathway that differs from its originating trajectory, producing a transformed state from which an output, relation, or state-direction may emerge that was not explicitly specified in the original trajectory. The originating case is the AI-Discovery Paradox (ADP), in which an input supplied by an originator may be transformed by an AI-mediated processing pathway into an unintended conceptual direction. The theory deliberately does not assume that AI lacks independent discovery capacity; existing literature already documents AI-assisted scientific discovery and formal work on AI serendipity. Instead, TEP isolates the narrower mechanism of transformation-induced divergence. A three-layer architecture is developed: philosophical-epistemological, systems-theoretical, and mathematical computational-validation. title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence in Personal Health Contexts: Investigating Information Seeking Motivations, Information Processing Behaviors, and Behavioral Responses During and After Interaction with GenAI
abstract: Following the advent of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), seeking health information on GenAI has become a more common and flexible approach. However, laypeople's health information seeking and processing (HISP) motivations and behavior on GenAI platforms remain underexplored, particularly given the current shift from search-based activities to more interactive and conversational processes. This study addressed this gap by exploring laypeople's HISP motivations, behaviors, and behavioral responses during and after interaction with GenAI. Using the risk information seeking and processing model as the theoretical framework, the HISP process was explored from a risk reduction perspective to understand how laypeople interact with GenAI to address their health concerns. Think-aloud protocol and retrospective interviews were employed to capture participants' real-time and reflective HISP interactions. Participants were mainly young individuals in Hong Kong. title: Methodological drivers, reporting completeness, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations: A scoping review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is widely reported as cost-effective, but reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) are shaped by model structure, assumptions, comparator choice, vaccine price, threshold selection, and local screening context. Previous reviews have summarized cost-effectiveness findings but have less often examined why conclusions differ across settings. OBJECTIVE: To map methodological evolution, drivers of variation, reporting completeness, methodological credibility, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted using the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley, refined by Levac et al., and informed by JBI guidance for scoping reviews. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR, and the protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025, with a final search conducted on January 2, 2026.
