title: tfbs-mcp: a Model Context Protocol server for agentic transcription factor binding site analysis
abstract: tfbs-mcp is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for transcription factor (TF) binding site analysis. It exposes the steps of a binding-site study as 33 tools that a large language model (LLM) client, such as Claude Code, calls directly. Those steps run from peak extraction and dataset preparation through model training, attribution analysis, motif scanning and structure-based binding energy to validation against external peak sets and disease variants. Workflow managers such as Snakemake and Nextflow suit a fixed dependency graph that is rerun across samples. An exploratory session changes the graph with every question. With tfbs-mcp the researcher states the TF, the data and the question in natural language. The LLM then: selects the tools; fills parameters with the defaults stated in the tool descriptions; runs the work locally or as SLURM jobs; explains each choice. Naming a decision overrides the default, without editing a configuration file. Most tools derive their output directories from their inputs and return the paths they wrote, so calls chain without a workflow script. title: RIDI-REAL-UPDATES-v1: Individual correctness changes across released model updates and prediction from frozen fragility
abstract: Prospective, not yet executed. This study tests whether six pinned incumbent-to-successor language-model releases produce individual-question correctness changes even when aggregate benchmark performance is favourable, and whether the previously frozen RIDI-PREDICT-v1 fragility score F_B predicts those changes. The panel contains 800 questions (Natural Questions 250, HotpotQA 250, FEVER 300) with the byte-identical registered BM25 top-10 reference contexts from OSF xrzp5. No passage exchange will be performed. Twelve pinned instruction-tuned models will each run in main (single-question generation) and replay-floor (fixed batches of 16) conditions: 24 model-by-condition units. The optional API pair is excluded. Decoding, scoring, retries, blinding, model revisions and audit procedures are detailed in the attached protocol. A unit is retried only after a documented technical failure; no successful output or partial batch is reused. The full set of units must terminate before opening answers or performing scientific analysis. Prespecified endpoints and decisions: equal-benchmark-weight accuracy difference Delta, aggregate accept flags C0 and C1, per-question correctness disagreement

title: Traditional Chinese medicine regulating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway to intervene in vascular aging
abstract: Abstract Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) participates in the initiation and progression of vascular aging and related vascular degenerative disorders by modulating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway. Its effects involve multiple biological processes, including autophagy, apoptosis, angiogenesis, and metabolic homeostasis. This study employed a narrative review methodology. No systematic review protocol was registered, and no quantitative data synthesis or meta-analysis was performed. Relevant literature published between January 2015 and June 2026 was retrieved from the core databases CNKI, PubMed, and Web of Science using the following Chinese and English keywords: “PI3K/Akt/mTOR,” “traditional Chinese medicine,” “vascular senescence,” “vascular aging,” and “atherosclerosis.” Original experimental studies were subsequently screened. Data extraction primarily focused on experimental evidence concerning the effects of TCM formulations or isolated compounds on key phosphorylated components of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway.The inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) explicit reporting of the effects of a TCM formulation or isolated compound on key phosphorylated components o

title: HydroPrior: Offline LLM-Prior-Guided Residual Warning for Hydropower Bearing Vibration
abstract: Hydropower vibration monitoring requires early warnings with manageable inspection costs despite scarce verified fault labels. HydroPrior combines offline large language model (LLM) priors with lightweight residual-based warning. The LLM converts channel descriptions and training-set statistics into frozen operating-context features, which enter a compact forecasting correction head. Residual scoring, calibrated thresholds, and contextual confirmation then produce budgeted alerts. Evaluation uses rapid vibration transitions as proxy events and the Balanced Warning Score (BWS) to summarize event coverage and alarm burden. On a public hydropower bearing-vibration dataset, HydroPrior obtains the lowest average forecasting error among the evaluated models. Under the proxy-warning protocol, its mean BWS is 0.7492 (standard deviation: 0.0405), with a transition-hit rate of 0.9106, 0.15 false alarms per 1000 non-transition points, and 0.0199 alert coverage. Comparisons using a common confirmation mechanism and coverage budget also favor HydroPrior. The findings support the feasibility of frozen operating priors for lightweight vibration forecasting and focused warning on the evaluated uni

title: MCP-MedImg: Enabling Standardized PACS-AI Integration through the Model Context Protocol
The prison-to-community transition as a neuropeptide stress test: an allostatic continuity agenda for addiction care
abstract: In correctional settings, substance use care is often evaluated on the basis of observed abstinence or reduced use during custody, treatment attendance, readiness for change, and motivation to sustain recovery. Yet constrained access to substances does not demonstrate that stress and reward regulation have recovered. Custody may involve uncertainty, limited autonomy, disrupted sleep, and social disconnection; release reintroduces drug-associated cues while adding pressures related to housing, stigma, income, and unstable treatment access. These phases are commonly managed as separate administrative episodes, although they may constitute a single biologically and socially continuous transition.We argue that the prison-to-community transition should be investigated as a neuropeptide-sensitive allostatic sequence. We define the "carceral allostatic amplifier" as an exposure-linked, within-person worsening of stress-regulatory phenotypes across custody and re-entry, potentially accompanied by coordinated changes in candidate neuropeptide measures. It is a conditional and falsifiable construct, not a biological label: it predicts neither uniform harm across institutions nor a common tra

title: Enzymatic browning in fresh-cut fruits and vegetables: a comprehensive review of biochemical etiologies, detection techniques, and control strategies
abstract: Enzymatic browning causes substantial postharvest losses in fresh fruits and vegetables, yet the literature remains fragmented across polyphenol oxidase (PPO) biochemistry, detection technologies, and control strategies. This review synthesizes current knowledge across the browning continuum, emphasizing the emerging perspective that membrane degradation via the phospholipase D (PLD) and lipoxygenase (LOX) cascade may represent an important early event preceding PPO activation in specific physiological contexts, particularly senescence- and stress-associated browning. However, the relative contribution of membrane degradation versus direct enzyme-substrate contact varies among commodities and browning types, and membrane degradation is not always the sole or mandatory initiating event. A key mechanistic consideration is the distinction between soluble and membrane-bound PPO (sPPO and mPPO). While sPPO assays remain valuable for mechanistic screening, evidence from a limited number of comparative studies suggests they may not fully predict inhibitor performance in intact food matrices, and the extent of this limitation requires further investigation. The review also identifies a det

title: Trustworthy LLM Harnesses: A Measurement Framework for Correctness, Quality, Efficiency, Reliability, Robustness, Safety, and Fairness
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are no longer deployed as bare models. They run inside an execution harness, the control layer that assembles context, exposes tools, manages memory and state, schedules retries, and verifies intermediate results. Because the harness determines what the model sees and what its outputs are allowed to do, observed agent behavior is jointly produced by the model and the harness, yet prevailing benchmarks attribute it to the model alone. We study the problem of harness evaluation: holding the model, task distribution, environment, budget, and evaluator fixed, how can the contribution of the harness be isolated, and what does it mean for a harness to be trustworthy? We formalize the harness as a trajectory-generating policy and define the harness effect as a paired, metric-indexed contrast. We then develop measurement principles along seven dimensions—outcome correctness, quality, efficiency, reliability and reproducibility, robustness, safety, and fairness—each targeting the specific mechanisms through which a harness influences agent behavior, and grounded in established results from statistical evaluation, efficient inference, certified robustness, a

title: The Thermodynamic Data Paradigm: A Unified Architectural Framework for Closed-Loop Adaptive State Transitions Across Asynchronous Bottlenecks
abstract: Modern computing and human-machine systems are increasingly throttled by the "phase change bottleneck"—a systemic failure that occurs when high-density, high-velocity data streams encounter a localized, bandwidth-constrained processing boundary. Whether this boundary is biological (human cognitive workload), computational (Large Language Model context windows), or infrastructural (edge-mesh network constraints), standard mitigation strategies rely on lossy filtering or rigid, reactive alerting mechanisms that inherently exacerbate systemic load during crises. This paper introduces the Thermodynamic Data Paradigm (TDP), a novel, unified architectural framework that treats digital information as a multi-state fluid. By deploying a low-latency, closed-loop state engine—termed the Phase Governor—the system dynamically modulates information density across three distinct operational modalities based on shifting real-time constraints: Explicit Static (Ice), Structured Kinetic (Liquid), and Attenuated Latent (Steam). The framework continuously evaluates a composite state index derived from external systemic pressure and internal consumer absorption capacity. When critical thresholds are br

title: A qualitative case study of cybersecurity fatigue and human-centric vulnerabilities in the SaaS sector
abstract: Purpose Cybersecurity fatigue is an important organisational issue, especially in high-pressure operational contexts such as Software-as-a-Service environments. As organisations implement stricter security controls and mandatory training, this can inadvertently place psychological strain on employees. This study/paper aims to identify specific operational demands and workflow characteristics contributing to employee cybersecurity fatigue and analyse the subsequent behavioural implications. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted an interpretivist, qualitative approach, using semi-structured interviews with employees from various departments to explore the causes and behavioural impacts of cybersecurity fatigue. A single organisation was used as case study. Findings The findings identified several key contributors: workflow disruption, cybersecurity decision overload, work overload and poor understanding of risk. These were associated with secondary elements such as repetitive access requests, security checks overload, a lack of real-world examples and generic training. The study also examined how these factors impact employee behaviour, revealing that fatigue often leads to

title: Supporting data for "Advancing Acoustoelectric Imaging: Nernst–Planck Modeling, Experimental Protocols and Synthetic Aperture"
abstract: Acoustoelectric (AE) imaging offers significant potential for non-invasive, high-resolution electroanatomical mapping of biological tissues. This technique probes bio-electrical contrast at the spatio-temporal resolution of diagnostic ultrasound by leveraging the local modulation of electrical resistivity using focused ultrasound (FUS). The interaction of this modulated resistivity with biological current flow induces the Acoustoelectric Interaction (AEI) voltage, which encodes local current density and tissue resistivity. While existing studies show promising applications up to in vivo animal models, several areas warrant further investigation. These include the need for multi-physics frameworks covering concurrent electrokinetic phenomena, technical documentation for acquiring weak microvolt-range signals, and the limited depth-of-field constrained by conventional FUS-AE. This thesis addresses these gaps through an integrated approach spanning theoretical modeling, experimental standardization, and advanced beamforming.First, to investigate the composition of raw AE signals, a theoretical framework was established from the perspective of ion-mediated electrokinetics using the Ner

title: Análise forense de dispositivos móveis: desafios técnicos na extração, preservação e validação de evidências digitais
abstract: This research analyzes the main technical challenges related to the extraction, preservation, and validation of digital evidence from mobile devices. Smartphones contain information of high relevance to criminal investigations, yet their security architectures, encryption, locking mechanisms, and continuous updates restrict access and make examinations dependent on the specific state of each device. A qualitative, exploratory, and descriptive approach was adopted through bibliographic and documentary research. The corpus comprised 27 academic, normative, technical, institutional, and legal sources, organized into extraction methods, technical challenges, preservation and chain of custody, validation, and reliability. The results show that no extraction method is universally superior: suitability depends on the forensic objective, device model, operating-system version, lock state, and risk of alteration. Evidence integrity was also found to depend on more than hash calculation; it requires a documented set of decisions, controls, copies, records, and verification procedures. Reliable findings require validation of both tools and methods in the specific context, independent confirma

title: Adaptive Switching Between Parallel-World Self-Reflection and Mutual Reflection for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can improve their outputs through self-reflection, iterative refinement, and interaction with other models. However, self-reflection may repeatedly reproduce the same assumptions, while mutual reflection may introduce unnecessary communication costs, correlated errors, or misleading feedback. Existing approaches provide important foundations for self-refinement and multi-agent interaction, but a general framework that coordinates multiple reflection modes, including parallel-world self-reflection, adaptive mutual reflection among parallel instances, and cross-model reflection involving heterogeneous LLMs, remains an important research direction. This paper proposes Adaptive Parallel-World Reflection (APWR), a conceptual framework that dynamically switches between self-reflection and mutual reflection according to the evolving state of a reasoning process. In APWR, parallel worlds are defined as distinct reflection trajectories instantiated from the same underlying model but assigned different reflection objectives, perspectives, assumptions, or diagnostic priorities. Each trajectory initially reflects independently, preserving its own reasoning context

title: Between Innovation and Inequality: A Systematic Review of EdTech Business Models and Their Contradictions
abstract: Abstract This study examines EdTech business models and the tensions between their discourse of democratizing education and their documented educational outcomes. A Systematic Literature eview (SLR) following the PRISMA protocol was conducted, analyzing 112 documents, including peer-reviewed articles and institutional reports. The findings reveal that, although EdTech solutions promote personalization, flexibility, and innovative pedagogical approaches, their business models are predominantly structured around SaaS, freemium, and subscription-based models that prioritize scalability, data generation, and market expansion. This dynamic contributes to the assetization of education, whereby educational resources and user-generated data are transformed into digital assets controlled by private platforms. Furthermore, while EdTech narratives emphasize inclusion and lifelong learning, their effectiveness remains strongly dependent on structural conditions, including digital infrastructure, device accessibility, institutional support, and public policies, particularly in low- and middle-income contexts. The study also highlights concerns regarding the monetization of educational data, pri

title: Peer Review Report For: Capturing Material Thermal Responses under RF-Induced Hyperthermia: An Experimental Imaging Database [version 2; peer review: 1 approved]
abstract: Background thermography is widely used to quantify surface temperature distributions during radiofrequency heating in biomedical, material, and industrial contexts. However, reproducible datasets capturing thermal responses of biological and inert materials under controlled RF excitation are scarce. This limitation hinders the validation of electromagnetic–thermal models, the benchmarking of image-based temperature estimation techniques, and the development of super-resolution and reconstruction algorithms. To address this gap, we generated a curated thermal image dataset that documents how different materials absorb and dissipate RF energy within an ISM band. Methods We constructed a controlled RF heating system consisting of a signal generator, a 6 W power amplifier, a circulator with matched load, and a unidirectional applicator antenna operating near 2.5 GHz. Biological tissues (pork, beef, chicken) and inert materials (foam, wood, phantom) were exposed to continuous-wave RF excitation while surface temperature was monitored using three infrared cameras with low, medium, and high resolution. Thermal images were acquired under systematically varied conditions, including RF power

Adaptive Switching Between Self-Reinforcement and Mutual Reinforcement in Multi-Agent Systems: A Dynamic Framework for Individual and Collective Intelligence Optimization
abstract: Multi-agent systems can improve their performance through individual learning and inter-agent cooperation. However, relying exclusively on individual reinforcement may limit the exploitation of complementary knowledge, whereas persistent mutual reinforcement may introduce communication overhead, correlated errors, excessive behavioral conformity, and dependence on potentially unreliable agents. These limitations motivate a dynamic framework in which agents adaptively switch between self-reinforcement and mutual reinforcement according to task conditions, learning progress, uncertainty, interaction quality, and resource constraints. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Reinforcement and Mutual Reinforcement (AS-SMR), a general framework for multi-agent systems. Self-reinforcement enables an agent to improve its policy through individual experience, self-evaluation, and locally available feedback. Mutual reinforcement enables agents to improve their policies through reciprocal feedback, cross-agent evaluation, experience exchange, and mutually informative learning signals. A context-sensitive controller estimates the relative utility of these mechanisms and selects ind

title: AI Context Association (AICA): Exploring Context-on-Demand for the Agentic Web
abstract: AI Context Association (AICA) is an exploratory technical concept that investigates how individual web content elements could reference external, machine-readable context that AI agents can retrieve when needed. Modern websites are designed primarily for human users, often presenting only a subset of the information available in underlying content management systems, product platforms, and enterprise knowledge sources. Embedding all potentially relevant information directly into HTML may increase page payload, while conventional APIs and integrations can require additional implementation effort. AICA explores a lightweight association between a specific web element and a separate context resource, such as a webpage, document, or knowledge source. The objective is to investigate whether this approach can help AI agents access richer, relevant information without unnecessarily expanding the human-facing page. The concept is intended to complement existing technologies rather than replace established approaches such as Schema.org, JSON-LD, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), or WebMCP. Its potential value, interoperability, security implications, and performance benefits remain to be ev

title: Sociolinguistic compatibility in AI adoption: extending DoI–TOE in public relations
abstract: Purpose This study examines how AI adoption in public relations (PR) unfolds in the Arab region and positions that experience against global industry discourses, with attention to the linguistic and cultural conditions that shape adoption trajectories. Design/methodology/approach Guided by Diffusion of Innovations (DoI) and the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework, the study combines 20 semi-structured interviews with senior Arab-region practitioners, association leaders and academics across six countries with a directed content analysis of professional guidelines and industry reports of global, cross-regional and regional scope. Findings Adoption is early-stage and selective, concentrated in content assistance, media intelligence and reputation monitoring, driven by efficiency gains and client expectations and inhibited by skills gaps, limited Arabic-language tooling and unclear governance. International discourses converge on augmentation under norms for disclosure, oversight and capability building, while ethical risks are compounded in Arab settings by cultural–linguistic fit and uneven institutional support. title: Bridging the Social Protection Deficit in the AfCFTA
abstract: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), inaugurated in 2018 and operationalised in 2021, represents one of the most ambitious regional integration projects in contemporary global trade history. Promising to unify a market of over 1.4 billion people and generate intra-African trade gains projected at USD 450 billion by 2035, AfCFTA has attracted widespread acclaim. Yet, a critical structural omission persists within its founding charter and subsidiary protocols: the near-total absence of binding social protection provisions. This chapter critically examines this deficit, arguing that the exclusion of robust social protection mechanisms constitutes both a normative failure and a pragmatic impediment to the effective implementation of the AfCFTA. The chapter interrogates the relationship between trade liberalisation and social vulnerability in the African context, surveys comparable regional integration models, and evaluates the extent to which social protection gaps undermine political buy-in, exacerbate informality, deepen gendered inequalities, and fuel implementation resistance at specific, identifiable sites. The chapter proposes a five-pillar Social Protection Integrat

title: Adaptive Switching Between Parallel-World Self-Planning and Collaborative Planning for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly employed as planning components in autonomous agents and multi-agent systems. However, planning architectures that rely exclusively on a single planning trajectory or continuous collaboration may fail to balance strategic diversity, coordination quality, computational efficiency, and adaptability. This paper proposes Parallel-World Self-Planning and Collaborative Planning (PW-SCP), a unified framework that enables multiple planning instances of the same LLM to explore different planning directions while adaptively switching between independent planning and collaborative planning. In this framework, a parallel world represents a logically independent planning instance of the same underlying model, distinguished by its planning objective, strategic orientation, constraints, or exploration policy. Each world can independently generate and revise plans, collaborate with other parallel worlds, or interact with external LLMs of different architectures and capabilities. A context-sensitive controller selects among self-planning, intra-model collaboration, heterogeneous-model collaboration, and hybrid planning according to task complexity, plan

title: CAPB-Net: a lightweight color-adaptive boundary network for medical image segmentation
abstract: Accurate RGB medical segmentation must combine high overlap, reliable boundaries, low computational cost, and robustness to color and illumination shifts. We present CAPB-Net, a lightweight color-adaptive boundary network that places an image-adaptive color polynomial (IACP) front-end before a compact U-shaped encoder decoder. IACP predicts a per-image residual color mapping in RGB space. Its identity initialization allows the model to learn color corrections only when they improve the segmentation loss. A pyramid-kernel depthwise embedding and selective large-kernel bottleneck then provide efficient local scale diversity and boundary-aware context. Under a fixed protocol, CAPB-Net achieves the highest Dice among the compared models on Kvasir-SEG and ISIC 2018. It reaches 0.8814 and 0.9065 Dice, respectively, with 0.706M parameters and 3.943G FLOPs. A Kvasir-SEG ablation confirms the coupled effect of IACP and color-jitter training and the contribution of selective large-kernel mixing. The results suggest that compact RGB medical segmentation benefits from explicit color adaptation and efficient local context rather than simply enlarging the backbone.

title: Toward explainable traffic crash liability analysis via neural-symbolic multimodal reasoning: Integrating visual perception with legal knowledge graphs
abstract: Determining traffic crash liability relies on rigorous on-site evidence and legal provisions and involves substantial manual intervention and potential human error. However, intelligent traffic monitoring systems focus on detection and tracking and cannot provide structured, rule-grounded decision support for formal crash-liability analysis. Moreover, emerging multimodal large language models (MLLMs) suffer from object hallucination that distorts or omits physical evidence, and their opaque reasoning cannot produce explicit evidence-to-rule chains required for traceable and reviewable liability analysis. This paper proposes CrashLex, an explainable neural-symbolic decision-support framework that integrates visual perception with legal knowledge graph reasoning to align multimodal inference with predefined statutory rules and traceability requirements. Within CrashLex, a dual-query vision-language architecture employs parallel semantic and symbolic streams to mitigate object hallucination, utilizing Scene Queries for global context modeling and Perception Queries for fine-grained atomic feature extraction, respectively. The domain-specific legal knowledge graph maps these atomic fac

title: The Coupled Climate-Carbon Cycle Model Intercomparison Project (C4MIP) experimental protocol for CMIP7
abstract: Abstract. Model intercomparison projects (MIPs) have become an essential tool for systematically comparing Earth system models (ESMs) by identifying, characterizing, and quantifying common model behaviour through standardized experiments and metrics under idealized, historical, and scenario-based forcing. Over the past few decades, community MIPs have become a cornerstone of the broader climate modelling community and the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP). Here, we describe the scientiﬁc objectives of the Coupled Climate-Carbon Cycle Model Intercomparison Project (C4MIP) in the context of the seventh phase of CMIP (CMIP7) and present the complete suite of C4MIP experiments, including those contributing to CMIP7's Assessment Fast Track (AFT) and those proposed for subsequent analyses beyond the AFT. The proposed experimental protocol maintains backward compatibility with previous CMIP phases while introducing new experiments. In addition to the traditional biogeochemically (BGC) and radiatively (RAD) coupled versions of the 1pctCO2 experiment, the new experiments include concentration-driven BGC and RAD variants of the abrupt 2×CO2 experiment, a suite of emissions-driven

title: DIGITAL TWINS FOR HARDWARE-IN-THE-LOOP MODELING OF MOBILE MEDICAL DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS
abstract: The rapid development of mobile medical diagnostic systems, wearable sensors, the Internet of Medical Things, edge computing, and artificial intelligence enables a transition from episodic physiological measurements toward continuous personalized patient monitoring. At the same time, increasing hardware-software complexity requires safe validation of sensing, computing, communication, and diagnostic components before their use with real patients. Hardware-in-the-Loop has already been applied to pacemakers, artificial pancreas systems, automated ventilation, circulatory support, and other medical devices; however, physiological models used in medical HIL environments are typically specialized test models rather than dynamically synchronized digital twins of individual patients. Contemporary Patient Digital Twins increasingly use wearable and IoMT data for personalization, monitoring, and prediction, but they are rarely used as real-time physiological HIL environments for validating physical mobile medical hardware. This paper proposes an integrated Patient Digital Twin–Hardware-in-the-Loop architecture in which a dynamically personalized twin operates in two interconnected modes: as

title: Agda-native AIR: an Agda-native artificial intelligence reasoning environment
abstract: Interaction, retrieval and evaluation infrastructure that lets AI coding agents work with the Agda proof assistant: AgdaDojang, programmatic access to Agda proof states and hole filling; agda-mcp, a Model Context Protocol server that exposes type checking, goal introspection, live scope, type and definition queries and corpus search to any MCP client; agda-strux, structured extraction of Agda libraries into retrieval-friendly corpus data; and deterministic proof-completion benchmarks and reports.

title: Adelic Spectral Isomorphism and Continuous Operator Trace Formulas for Motivic L-Functions
abstract: Adelic Spectral Isomorphism and Continuous Operator Trace Formulas for Motivic L-Functions --- • Series Context Note: This monograph constitutes Part 1 of a five-part foundational series exploring advanced spectral methods, automorphic representations, and arithmetic geometry. • Primary Focus: Rigorous mathematical establishment (SAC-01 through SAC-05) and structural resolution of local-global patching obstructions. --- Abstract This resolution establishes an exact structural spectral isomorphism between the arithmetic \bm{L}-functions attached to algebraic varieties over global fields and the continuous trace spectrum of differential and integral operators acting on adelic symmetric spaces. Traditionally, analytic characterizations of high-rank motivic \bm{L}-functions have encountered severe methodological barriers due to local-global patching obstructions and the lack of explicit integral representations. By constructing a continuous adelic trace operator \bm{\mathbf{T}_s} via Arthur-Selberg trace expansions and spectral decompositions of automorphic kernels, this framework entirely bypasses traditional Euler system limitations. title: GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING IN MATHEMATICS EDUCATION: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into Problem-Based Learning (PBL) environments presents new challenges and opportunities for education. The objective of this research is to investigate how AI has been used to promote critical thinking, argumentation, and complex problem-solving within the context of mathematics education or STEM fields. To this end, a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted, guided by the PRISMA protocol, analyzing empirical studies published since 2020 and indexed in the Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, and ERIC databases. The results indicate that AI transcends the function of a content repository, assuming pedagogical roles such as 'Socratic Coach,' 'Design Partner,' and 'Object of Critical Analysis.' The analysis highlights that the tool's effectiveness depends intrinsically on the quality of prompt engineering and human mediation. Furthermore, AI 'hallucinations' and mathematical inconsistencies do not necessarily need to be perceived as critical flaws; they can emerge as effective pedagogical catalysts for the refinement of logical validation by students. It is concluded that the integration of AI into PBL requires p

title: The anthropometric debt of Venezuelan industry: between the law and the reality of the worker
abstract: The objective of this study was to analyze the validity and applicability of anthropometric and biomechanical studies conducted on Venezuelan workers as a basis for the ergonomic design of workstations in the national industry. A comprehensive literature review was conducted in the form of an academic essay, incorporating critical analysis. The following databases were consulted: Scopus, Dialnet, Latindex, RePEc/IDEAS, EconPapers, and MIAR. The following criteria were used to compile the sample of studies. The study considered five inclusion criteria. The preliminary results indicate that the anthropometric and functional measurement protocols that have been validated among Venezuelan workers have the potential to facilitate ergonomic assessments through the use of predictive models and low-cost instruments. However, it should be noted that limitations, including issues related to sample size and representativeness, as well as potential biases associated with gender and age, have been identified. The conclusions indicate that incorporating these findings reinforces a rigorous approach to ergonomics that is applicable to the Venezuelan context, making ergonomic assessment more acces

title: Does psychology have a truth-telling problem? Survivance as truth-telling pedagogy in psychology education
abstract: Truth-telling and reparative praxis have become central concerns in higher education, particularly in settler-colonial contexts where public institutions have denied, minimized, or excluded histories of violence, dispossession, and exploitation. Psychology education holds a specific responsibility within this work as psychological research, assessment, diagnosis, and practice have participated in colonial projects through racialized theories of intelligence and health, clinical pathologization of systemic harms, extractive research, and training models that position Euro-Western knowledge as universal. Symbolic response and deficit framing limit reconciliation-oriented teaching when institutional language, course content, and professional training leave colonial authority intact or position Indigenous Peoples primarily through harm. This article adapts survivance and health survivance scholarship into a pedagogical framework to guide curriculum design, testimony protocols, case teaching, research assignments, supervision discussions, and assessment in psychology education. Practical tools, including a survivance-informed planning matrix and a psycholonization audit, are proposed to

title: "Agent Task Recovery After Tool-Effect Commit: A2A\/MCP Crash and Adversarial Receipt Evidence"
abstract: "This dataset provides source and replication evidence for a deterministic synthetic study of a post-commit, pre-finalization crash in an Agent2Agent (A2A) task invoking a Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool. The study uses the A2A Python SDK 1.2.2, MCP Python SDK 2.3.0, a SQLite effect ledger, and a versioned A2A task store. A merchant process exits after an effect is committed but before the original task is finalized. A matched evaluation comprises 20 pairs (40 runs) comparing operation-keyed downstream idempotency without task reconciliation (policy B) with version-checked reconciliation of the original durable task (policy C). The archive preserves the effect ledger, durable task state, process-exit traces, and separate-process A2A GetTask observations. A prospective adversarial matrix spans four synthetic requests, five receipt conditions, and two reconciliation implementations (40 worker-arm executions, 48 original tasks). In deliberately mismatched wrong-amount and wrong-item cases, a receipt-exists-only worker falsely completed 8\/8 tasks, whereas the intent-bound worker evaluated and refused 8\/8, without producing additional effects. title: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort
abstract: When does a human correction become useful learning, and what establishes better segmentation at matched human effort? This critical narrative review follows feedback through its selection, learner update, and evaluation. It compares active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation using a common mathematical account of target information, predictive error, response predictability, and human work. An exact Bayesian update converts evaluation-label information into expected log-loss improvement; an excess-risk decomposition explains what an approximate learner can lose. Conditional information decompositions separate the roles of selected locations, labels, and displayed context. Empirical comparisons show why response protocols, update mechanisms, and effort denominators matter, distinguishing current-mask refinement from reusable learning and simulated interaction from human evidence. We identify what logs can reveal, what requires independent evaluation, and what remains model-dependent. title: Robota-Embed: Unified VLA Embeddings for Robot In-Context Learning and Evolution
abstract: Retrieving useful context for a robot requires matching its task, execution stage, and the continuation that should follow. We introduce Robota-Embed, to our knowledge the first vision-language-action (VLA) embedding model to jointly encode all three modalities in both current-state queries and recorded future continuations. Predictive retrieval training aligns these endpoints, enabling historical continuations to serve as context at inference time. We construct a multi-source corpus of 1,695,684 cleaned training anchors and introduce Robota-Embed-Bench, with 4,000 queries and a shared 8,000-entry gallery. Robota-Embed achieves 47.33% clip-level and 81.77% episode-level R@1, exceeding action-free Gemini Embedding 2 by 22.09 and 33.47 percentage points. Controlled retrieval studies show that removing native action degrades retrieval more than removing vision. We study two complementary applications. Embed2ICL uses retrieved experience for training-free and training-based policy conditioning, increasing success from 47.0% to 56.3% in DROID-Sim and from 86.4% to 92.8% on the LIBERO difficult subset, while improving task progress on real robots. Embed2Evolve uses execution feedback to

title: XViewRank: Overlap-Conditioned Score Fusion for LLM-Augmented Sparse Retrieval
abstract: Large language models can reduce vocabulary mismatch in sparse retrieval by generating alternative views of a query. Once these views are searched independently, however, their ranked lists may be complementary, redundant, or affected by query drift, making fixed fusion suboptimal. We present XViewRank, a lightweight retrieval-side method for conditionally fusing BM25 results from an original query, a hypothesis view, and a step-back view. For each pooled candidate, XViewRank retains three normalized BM25 scores and three query-level overlaps between the retrieved result sets. A small nonlinear scorer uses the overlaps as context that changes how the view-specific scores are interpreted, without jointly encoding query and passage text. Under a matched-input protocol, XViewRank improves nDCG@10 and MAP numerically over reciprocal rank fusion on both TREC DL 2019 and 2020, with a statistically significant MAP gain on DL19. Additional analyses show that the clearest benefit occurs when the view rankings have low agreement, while the evidence on DL20 is weaker. The results support overlap-conditioned score fusion as a compact retrieval-side alternative to fixed fusion, while also delim

title: LabOPBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Laboratory Decision Making
abstract: Laboratory experiments involve more than following predefined protocols; they require adaptive decision-making as the experimental state changes. Existing scientific benchmarks rarely assess such evidence-based decisions in laboratory settings. Here we present LabOPBench, a multimodal benchmark of 756 expert-authored, independently reviewed questions in organic synthesis and materials science. Each item pairs laboratory evidence with procedural context and an open-ended judgment, evaluated using a question-specific scoring rubric. Eight multimodal models obtain overall normalized scores of 28.8-45.8%, leaving substantial room for improvement. On a controlled 100-question subset, the strongest models outperform undergraduate participants on average but remain below the average performance of PhD participants. Expert analysis of responses from the three leading models identifies Evidence Misreading and Evidence-Decision Conflict as the dominant error patterns. These results reveal that current models still struggle to turn multimodal perception into reliable laboratory decision-making.

title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Leadership for Multilingual and Intercultural Language Education in Developing Countries
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering university governance, teaching, and language education across developing countries, yet ethical-leadership scholarship remains concentrated on well-resourced, digitally mature institutions. This paper reports a PRISMA-informed, PICO-guided literature review examining how ethical AI leadership can be theorized for multilingual and intercultural language education in developing-country higher education, with a conflict-affected higher-education setting in South Asia as an illustrative case. Fifty-six sources met inclusion criteria after a staged identification, screening, and eligibility process conducted by a single reviewer using open academic search engines and publisher platforms rather than subscription-indexed databases. Thematic synthesis identified four recurring barrier domains infrastructural access, institutional governance, socio-cultural capacity, and linguistic/data equity and three leadership theories (transformational, distributed, and ethical leadership) that jointly inform a proposed six-dimension conceptual framework for ethical AI leadership. title: Fake News Detection Using BERT-Based Language Model-With Explainable AI

title: A Discipleship Framework of Godly Leadership for Coaches and Athletes
abstract: There is a systemic lack of deliberate discipleship in Christian athletics, specifically observed in the wrestling program at Trinity Christian Academy. Despite professed faith, coaches and athletes lacked a systematic, theologically viable method for integrating biblical truth into training, competition, and team leadership. This project created and implemented the Game Plan for Godly Leadership handbook, a resource integrating Scripture, mentorship protocols, leadership principles, and assessment tools for the wrestling context. The handbook was developed as part of a strategic plan designed for implementation across two academic years and two wrestling seasons; however, the documented implementation and assessment period occurred from late June through July 28, 2026. During this period, seven participants (two coaches and five athletes) engaged with the framework and completed the documented assessment activities. Descriptive findings indicated positive short-term changes in understanding of godly leadership, intentional discipleship, confidence in leading others, faith integration, and accountability. title: Thinking in Graphs: Neo4j-Backed Exploit-Chain Reasoning for LLM Penetration-Testing Agents
abstract: LLM coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex can drive penetration-testing tools, but they reason about an engagement as a flat list of findings in a context window. Attackers think in graphs: isolated low-severity exposures turn catastrophic once chained through credential capture, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. This gap feeds a common belief that AI agents cannot truly chain exploitation; we argue this describes the flat context window, not the model. We present ChainGraph, a pattern that externalizes exploit-chain reasoning into a Neo4j property graph wired to an off-the-shelf agent via the Model Context Protocol, no bespoke harness. Findings, attack steps, credentials, assets, and tamper-evident evidence receipts are typed nodes with pre/post-condition edges; JSON/Markdown holds documentary memory while Neo4j holds reasoning memory. We formalize five operator questions (next-step inference, entry-to-crown-jewel pathing, combined-severity promotion, evidence provenance, and chokepoint identification) as reusable Cypher and Graph Data Science queries, plus a chain-severity score distinct from per-finding local severity. A cascaded probabilistic framework for stealth-aware MITRE ATT&CK path prediction in active directory adversary emulation
abstract: Abstract Proactive adversary emulation requires anticipating multi-step attack trajectories, yet existing approaches rely on static attack graphs or single-signal models that cannot jointly satisfy coherence, tactical realism, and evasiveness. We propose a cascaded probabilistic framework for MITRE ATT&CK technique-path prediction in Active Directory environments, where exhaustive enumeration is intractable. Its contribution is a three-stage architecture that decouples these objectives instead of blending them. Stage 1, a two-layer unidirectional LSTM trained on observed threat-actor chains, emits a five-candidate pool rather than one technique. Stage 2, an empirical Markov tactic-transition gate, admits only attested transitions, including self-loops and backward moves a strict linear kill chain excludes. Stage 3 re-ranks survivors against a detection-rule corpus, favoring evasive over merely probable techniques. Candidates are masked at inference to Windows-applicable techniques, so outputs are technique chains, not instantiated paths. title: CONTROLLED CONCEPT MUTATION & EVOLUTION AT THE LIMIT Living Concept Civilization — Flagship Research Monograph 04 STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization · 2026 ABSTRACT When does a deliberate alteration of a concept produce new, reproducible inferential power without silently overturning its defining propositions, source rights, or safety constraints? This English-language research monograph develops a hypothesis-led framework for controlled conceptual mutation. It treats mutation not as a biological fact about ideas, but as an auditable transformation over versioned propositions, typed edit operators, contextual invariants, comparison models, and independent tests. The project is organized around a three-coupling of mutation generation, invariant protection, and evidence selection. It examines additive and subtractive changes, explicit negation, analogical transfer, changes of scale, context substitution, composite operators, provenance preservation, permission inheritance, adversarial falsification, unknown-state calibration, negative findings, legal withdrawal, rollback, and multi-generation research succession. The governing research question is whether an edited concept generates a measurable new prediction or capability that survives rigorous baselines and hard rights constraints. All proposed scores require future operational definitions and calibration. STRUCTURE This volume contains 82 chapters with one provisional core equation per chapter and twelve separately paginated methodological research units per chapter. Its physics preface offers 30 distinct domain-conditional mathematical derivation routes accompanied by three-dimensional conceptual geometry; these are educational comparisons, not claims of physical laws governing conceptual evolution. The closing research apparatus comprises 200 independently indexed Research Gates followed by 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Each of these 233 entries includes a distinct physical equation anchor, which remains valid only in its appropriate physical regime and is not presented as experimental evidence for conceptual behavior. SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND RESEARCH ETHICS The book is a research agenda and structured hypothesis collection rather than an account of completed empirical findings. All worked examples, proposed systems, experimental protocols, metrics, derived conceptual indices, and positive predictions are UNVERIFIED until tested. Strong baselines, negative controls, held-out tasks, error attribution, rights checks, reproducibility, and independent successor review are conditions for future validation. No text length, model agreement, or graphical sophistication is claimed as proof of novelty. Public availability does not override consent, privacy, attribution, or cultural governance. OPEN RESEARCH DESIGN The 200 Research Gates are intended as stand-alone, falsifiable investigation prompts. The 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos are not authoritative answers; they are candidates that may be rejected, decomposed, revised, branched, or responsibly retired. The program invites independent critical testing and lawful reinterpretation across researchers, models, institutions, and generations. RESEARCH LINEAGE AND REFERENCE POINTS This volume expands Flagship 04 of Living Concept Civilization: Eighteen Tri-Coupled Flagship Research Programs, v2.0 (2026-10-13), provided as the project's working mother document. Relevant method references include the W3C PROV-O specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/) and the FAIR Guiding Principles (Wilkinson et al., Scientific Data 3, 160018, 2016; https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18). Let meaningful questions be entrusted to the future without requiring the future to preserve today's answers.

title: Settlement and Execution Extension of the Casino Protocol: Payload Generation Architecture, Numerical Integrity Verification, and Boundaries with Real Settlement and On-Chain Execution (Technical Report Series Vol. 3)
abstract: Abstract This technical report presents a strictly bounded operational extension module designed to translate verified computational payloads into structured execution parameters, based on the theoretical pricing models and reference computational architectures of the Casino Protocol (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23325710, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23326052). To eliminate blind reliance on self-reported status strings (calculation_status: "verified"), the architecture enforces robust pre-generation validation, incorporating strict type checks via a dedicated non-negative decimal parser (explicitly rejecting booleans, None, and unhandled structures), non-negative constraints, detection of primary input type and numerical conversion errors, explicit verification of the supported protocol name (Casino Protocol) and version (1.0), structural validation of bank information as dictionaries containing non-empty strings, and independent conservation law verification within a predefined absolute tolerance (\varepsilon = 10^{-4} JPY). title: Climate-driven asymmetric range shifts of montane birds along a subtropical elevational gradient in China
abstract: Species distributions in montane ecosystems are rapidly reorganizing in response to climate change, underscoring the need to understand species redistribution along elevational gradients for effective conservation planning. Although upslope shifts in avian elevational ranges are increasingly documented, the mechanisms underlying these patterns remain uncertain and contentious. Here, we conducted a 64-year resurvey (1957–2020) of bird distributions along a subtropical elevational gradient (500–3099 m a.s.l.) on Mount Emei, China—a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has undergone significant warming and drying. Using a resampling-based protocol to mitigate sampling bias and a null model to control for stochastic and geometric constraints, we quantified elevational range shifts and then examined how climate and functional traits mediated them. Bird species exhibited highly individualistic and asymmetrical range dynamics. Upper limits showed a mean expansion of 213.93 ± 572.47 m, while lower limits contracted by 34.18 ± 504.51 m. Multivariate analyses revealed that temperature and precipitation jointly mediated shift directions—warming promoting upslope movements and reduced precipitation

title: A scoping review of infant body composition (0–24 months) assessed by deuterium dilution
abstract: The deuterium dilution technique is applicable across the 0–24 month age range in diverse resource settings. No structured review has previously mapped the scope of its use in this population. This scoping review was limited to mapping infant body composition studies (0–24 months) using deuterium dilution, describing methodological approaches, identifying contexts of applications, and highlighting evidence gaps. A structured literature search was conducted across four databases with citation tracking, following prisma-ScR guidelines. Twenty-four studies from approximately 18–20 distinct cohorts across six continents were included from 1,078 identified records. Substantial heterogeneity was documented in every protocol element: dose, equilibration time, analytical platform, correction factor for non-aqueous exchange (unreported in approximately one-third of studies), and hydration model. This heterogeneity prevents direct comparison of fat mass and fat-free mass values across studies, precluding meta-analytic synthesis. title: Regenerative tourism through a dual-lens ADO-TCM systematic literature review: a behavioral-structural framework and wellness research agenda
abstract: Regenerative tourism has grown rapidly but remains conceptually diffuse and empirically thin. This review develops a behaviorally specified conceptual framework and proposes wellness tourism as an under-examined demand-side bridge for future inquiry. Following the SPAR-4-SLR protocol, 45 Scopus-indexed articles in ABDC 2025-listed journals were synthesized through an integrated Antecedents–Decisions–Outcomes and Theories–Contexts–Methods (ADO-TCM) framework. Screening agreement was near-perfect (Cohen’s κ = 0.858); extraction was double-coded and reconciled to consensus. The corpus reveals a coherent but lopsided structure: six antecedent families act through mediating mechanisms, chiefly regenerative mindset and experience quality, to shape regenerative behavior and five outcome families. The field is richly theorized through Living Systems Theory but lacks demand-side behavioral theory, concentrates on Global North, supply-side contexts, and relies overwhelmingly on qualitative designs. title: Weighted Blanket Load and Sleep Outcomes During Daytime Napping and Overnight Sleep: Two Randomized Crossover Studies
abstract: Background/Objectives: Weighted blankets provide deep pressure stimulation and may support relaxation, sleep initiation, and sleep continuity. However, the optimal acute blanket load across different sleep contexts remains unclear. This study examined the acute effects of 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets on daytime napping and overnight home sleep in healthy adults. Methods: Two complementary randomized crossover protocols were integrated into one manuscript. In Protocol A, 20 healthy young adults completed four randomized 30-min laboratory nap conditions: control/sham blanket, 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets. In Protocol B, 20 healthy young adults completed four randomized overnight home sleep conditions: personal blanket control, 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets. All conditions were separated by one-week washout intervals. Portable EEG/EOG polysomnography was used to assess nap and sleep architecture. Relaxation state, handgrip strength, blood pressure, heart rate, and skin/ambient temperature were also assessed where applicable. title: Evidence for models of integrated dementia care: a scoping review protocol
abstract: There is a substantial and increasing need for efficient, high quality integrated dementia care to serve our ageing population, but a dearth of literature regarding best practices for development and evaluation of these service models. The goal, therefore, of this scoping review is to systematically examine the literature regarding existing integrated models of dementia care in order to map the current state of the literature. We will also examine how models of integrated dementia care are evaluated, and to what extent they align with best practices for integrated care in a Canadian context. We will conduct a scoping review based on the methods suggested by Arksey and O'Malley (2005) and updated by Levac et al. (2010), using the following databases: MEDLINE, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), PsycINFO and Google Scholar. We will supplement our findings by a systematic search of relevant grey literature. We will include studies that (i) describe a model of integrated care in the health and/or social care sectors, (ii) include an assessment of outcome, and (iii) are published in 2019 or later. title: CATEGORY-BASED PROMPT CONSTRUCTION FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EDUCATION: A PEDAGOGICAL PROMPT ENGINEERING MODEL AND WEB TOOL
abstract: This article proposes a pedagogical model, and a web tool built on it, for constructing prompts by educational material category so that teachers and researchers can work effectively with artificial intelligence (large language models). The relevance of the study stems from the fact that the quality of a generative model's output depends directly on the quality of the instruction, while many educators lack prompt-writing skills. The aim was to develop a solution that produces ready-to-use, structured prompts for eleven types of educational material: lesson plans, research projects, scientific articles, 3D models, multimedia, animation, virtual materials, assessment, didactic games, graphics and software development. A design-based approach was applied, combining prompt engineering principles with the TPACK framework. As a result, a five-part prompt structure (role, task, context, requirements, output format), a set of category-specific parameters, a mechanism for adapting prompts to the target type of AI tool, and a model-assisted prompt refinement step were developed. title: A Model-Agnostic Persistent Memory Infrastructure for Long-Term AI Agents Using Hybrid Retrieval, Scope Isolation, and MCP
abstract: This paper presents a model-agnostic persistent memory infrastructure for AI agents, designed to support long-term information storage and retrieval across sessions, models, and agent frameworks. The proposed architecture explores hybrid retrieval combining semantic search and BM25, Elasticsearch-based memory storage, REST API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces, and mechanisms for memory lifecycle management, deduplication, conflict handling, and scope isolation. The work focuses on the architectural design and implementation of reusable memory infrastructure for AI agents. Empirical performance claims should be interpreted in accordance with the validation methods and experimental evidence reported in the paper.

title: Integrated CAV Agent Architectures with MCP and A2A
abstract: This chapter establishes theoretical foundations and practical frameworks for building unified agent systems that seamlessly integrate the model context protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent protocol (A2A) in connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) applications. Real-world CAV applications demand unified systems combining external capabilities with collaborative reasoning. The chapter covers protocol selection criteria, system architectures for protocol integration, and implementation guidelines for robust systems operating in safety-critical environments. It examines how integrated architectures enable CAVs to access both deterministic external services and collaborative peer intelligence, addressing complex decision-making scenarios requiring both tool integration and multi-agent coordination. The chapter provides comprehensive guidance for building and deploying integrated agent systems in CAV environments.

title: Mapping gender-specific incubators: impact, frameworks and future directions in women's entrepreneurship
abstract: Purpose This article evaluates the empirical and conceptual evidence on the impact of gender-specific business incubators, accelerators, and entrepreneurship support organizations published between 2010 and 2025. It responds to recent calls within the International Journal of Gender and Entrepreneurship (Jones et al., 2025; Woods and Orser, 2026) to strengthen feminist theory building in entrepreneurship research and to scrutinize the institutional structures that support, or constrain, women, girls and gender-diverse founders. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 protocol (Page et al., 2021). Searches across Scopus, Web of Science, Emerald Insight, EBSCO Business Source Complete, and JSTOR yielded 312 records, of which 35 peer-reviewed articles and books and 11 institutional and grey-literature sources (46 sources in total) were retained for thematic synthesis. A descriptive bibliometric overlay was undertaken to identify publication trends, intellectual structure, and geographic coverage. Findings The literature converges on three observations. title: Proposal for the Management of Students' Mental Health Care through Agricultural Projects to Promote Sustainable Social Development
abstract: Mental health care management proposals are relevant because they also include projects aimed at social development. Objective: To propose a management model for student mental health care through agricultural projects that promote sustainable social development in educational institutions. Methodoloy: This propositional article adopts a qualitative approach based on a documentary review of literature on student mental health, educational productive projects, and sustainable development, as well as the systematization of institutional management criteria. Results: Three interconnected components are proposed: participatory planning of agricultural projects focused on well-being, socioemotional support during productive activities, and engagement with the community and local market. The model includes implementation phases, monitoring and evaluation indicators, ethical safeguards, and institutional stakeholders’ responsibilities. Conclusions/Contributions: Agricultural projects can integrate mental health care, practical learning, and community development, strengthening shared responsibility among schools, families, and communities. title: Facilitating Space Data Archives interoperability through standardization in OAIS and related framework
abstract: Introduction: Interoperability among space data archives remains a key challenge in the current context of long term digital preservation and effective information exchange. The complexity is intensified when disparate archive systems - belonging to space agencies or partners - adopt different internal data models and im-plementation approaches, also for historical rea-sons, leading to heterogeneous environment that hinder seamless collaboration. Addressing these barriers necessitates a fundamental re-evaluation of approaches to long-term digital preservation, with a particular focus on fostering cross-agency and interdomain collaboration. Such efforts must encompass both OAIS-conformant and non-conformant repositories, ensuring that the principles of interoperability extend beyond established standards to embrace a broader spectrum of archival practices and technological frameworks. The paper presents an experience aimed at supporting standardization within OAISfamily data archiving interoperability, adopting an iterative prototyping approach. title: Trustworthy electricity theft detection integrating informative missingness learning and certified conformal audits
abstract: This repository contains the official open-source verification framework, neural architecture implementations, and experiment replication suite for the research paper: "Trustworthy electricity theft detection integrating informative missingness learning and certified conformal audits" (Under review at Scientific Reports, Nature Portfolio). Key Components:1. Missingness-Aware Multi-Representation Detector (MAMRD): A compact 0.97M-parameter deep learning architecture integrating selective state-space models (Mamba), zero-sum Laplacian differencing, and context-conditional missingness embeddings.2. Leakage-Free Native-Prevalence Protocol: Standardized evaluation pipelines for the State Grid Corporation of China (SGCC) and ElectricityLoadDiagrams (ECL) benchmarks preventing temporal and customer-level data leakage.3. Certified Conformal Audits: Post-hoc class-conditional conformal prediction routines certifying finite-sample theft recovery guarantees across heterogeneous consumption tiers.4. Baselines: Production implementations of rival architectures (GRU-D, WDCNN, HORLN, Self-Attention, and MSDM).

title: Editorial: Modulating the gut immune microenvironment through nutrients: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential in immune-related gastrointestinal disorders
abstract: Nutrients are increasingly recognized as upstream regulators of the gut immune microenvironment. Dietary components do not simply provide calories or build blocks for host tissues. They determine the substrates available to intestinal epithelial cells, resident microorganisms, and infiltrating immune cells, thereby shaping the molecular conditions under which barrier maintenance, immune tolerance, and inflammatory activation occur. This concept moves beyond the traditional view that diet acts mainly through long term changes in body weight or nutrient deficiency. Instead, dietary carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, micronutrients, and food associated compounds can rapidly modify luminal metabolite pools, oxygen availability, redox state, bile acid composition, and microbial metabolic activity. These local signals directly influence epithelial differentiation, mucus production, tight junction organization, antigen sampling, and the activation state of macrophages, dendritic cells, innate lymphoid cells, and T cells. title: Peer Review Report For: Mapping evidence of postgraduate research supervision experiences at higher education institutions in Africa: A scoping review protocol [version 2; peer review: 4 approved with reservations]
abstract: Background The evolving landscape of the African higher education sector necessitated by global higher education reforms and the need for research informed responses to address contextual challenges is partly dependent on effective postgraduate research supervision. A wide range of postgraduate research supervision models and practices are documented globally. In the African context, the experiences of postgraduate research supervision are not clearly understood from the experiences of all stakeholders. Aim The proposed scoping review aims to map evidence on the range of postgraduate research supervision experiences at higher education institutions in Africa. Methods The methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O’Malley will be used to conduct the review. Relevant articles will be sourced from different electronic data bases namely; ERIC, Web of Science, EbscoHost and Scopus. A combination of search terms and Boolean operators will be used to obtain the relevant articles based on the inclusion criteria stipulated within the Population, Context and Concept (PCC) framework of study identification for this review. title: Beyond Permeability Prediction: Machine Learning for Gas-Separation Membranes from Data Curation to Experimentally Validated Discovery
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is transforming gas-separation membrane research, yet high retrospective accuracy does not necessarily translate into experimentally viable or process-relevant materials. This review reframes the field around the evidence chain required to convert a membrane record into a defensible discovery decision. Across polymers, metal–organic and covalent organic frameworks, mixed-matrix membranes, carbon molecular sieves, and two-dimensional systems, we critically examine data curation, physics-aligned representation, multitask and multi-fidelity learning, uncertainty quantification, inverse design, and prospective validation. We introduce a five-level evidence framework spanning retrospective interpolation, domain-disjoint generalization, physics or simulation confirmation, prospective membrane validation, and deployment-relevant testing. We further propose a contextualized observation unit that binds chemical identity to membrane state, fabrication history, feed composition, operating conditions, time, protocol, and provenance, thereby exposing leakage and structural uncertainty hidden by conventional datasets. title: Cold Exposure-Induced Intestinal Dysfunction: Mechanisms, Animal Models, and Nutritional Intervention Strategies
abstract: Cold exposure is an important environmental stressor that can disrupt physiological homeostasis and induce complex metabolic, immune, oxidative, and gastrointestinal responses. Increasing evidence indicates that the intestine is a sensitive target of cold exposure, yet the underlying mechanisms and their interrelationships remain incompletely understood. This review summarizes and critically evaluates current evidence on cold exposure-induced intestinal dysfunction and adaptation, with emphasis on intestinal barrier integrity, mucus and digestive function, inflammatory and oxidative responses, pyroptosis-related signaling, gut microbiota remodeling, animal models, and potential intervention strategies. Experimental studies in rodents, pigs, poultry, and fish indicate that cold exposure can induce intestinal morphological alterations, epithelial barrier disruption, increased permeability, tight-junction remodeling, mucus and digestive dysfunction, inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and, under specific conditions, inflammasome-associated pyroptosis. Concurrent alterations in gut microbial composition and metabolites may interact with epithelial and immune responses

title: Impact of a Dynamic Visualized Pain Assessment Tool on Pediatric Pain Management: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial
abstract: Effective pediatric pain management relies on accurate assessment; however, current behavioral scales are limited by observer subjectivity and fail to capture dynamic fluctuations. The primary goal of this protocol is to detail the implementation and evaluation of a dynamic visualized pain assessment tool, providing a standardized methodology to transition nursing practice from experience-based estimation to data-driven precision. Using a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial design across five clinical wards, the study enrolled 15 infants and analyzed 45 video segments across three clinical contexts: baseline, acute procedural pain, and postoperative recovery. The system captured high-definition facial video synchronized with bedside physiological monitoring to generate real-time pain trajectory curves and trend-based alerts. Generalized linear mixed models showed that the tool reduced nursing response latency from 15.4 to 6.7 min (P < 0.001) and increased assessment consistency (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]: 0.71-0.93). Unreachable Oracles: Auditing Ground-Truth Derivability in a Synthetic Tool-Drift Benchmark for LLM Agents
abstract: A tool-migration benchmark for LLM agents contains two objects that are easy to conflate: the behaviour under test and the oracle that scores it. This work asks whether the latter is well formed. We operationalize oracle identifiability under declared information rights at the level of the individual item: a ground-truth item is reachable only if its target value and every construction step are derivable, under a declared finite derivation grammar, from the information granted before the method's first call. We implement this criterion as a deterministic offline auditor with typed outcomes. Applied to a self-authored synthetic tool-drift benchmark, the audit finds 50 of 310 argument-pair items unreachable (16.1%), concentrated in two drift families. A separate 45-item required-field audit finds 20 additional unreachable items, reducing strict complete-call retention to zero in two families. Four derivation-grammar configurations reproduce the same 260/10/40 reachable/target-absent/convention-unobservable split. title: Prometheus Platform
abstract: Prometheus is an agentic AI platform that automates the application of model-based systems engineering discipline to the design, licensing, manufacturing, construction, and operation of nuclear power plants and fuel cycle facilities. A single external API gateway accepts natural-language task requests from the Prometheus Platform UI, third-party clients, or the Genesis Mission Platform, and a Workflow Orchestration component resolves each request to either a matched workflow template or a dynamically composed execution plan, which a human reviewer must approve before any agent executes; an Agent Registry organizes registered agents by engineering domain and exposes each through an A2A-conformant Agent Card, admitting only agents with a formally verified encapsulation guarantee, while a paired Model Proxy mediates every agent-to-model call so that underlying model backends can be substituted without modifying the calling agent. title: Modular Quantum Computing with Superconducting Qubits
abstract: Superconducting qubits provide a promising approach to large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing. However, as superconducting quantum processors scale out of the NISQ era, monolithic architectures face severe physical bottlenecks caused by physical wiring density, crosstalk, and constraints on spatial layout. Transitioning toward a modular paradigm—where smaller, independently optimized quantum processing units are dynamically interconnected—offers a highly scalable alternative. Here, we present our work on developing a scalable, modular superconducting quantum processor based on a reconfigurable router architecture. We demonstrate how this design enables efficient quantum operations across independent modules and smooth integration with state-of-the-art quantum optimal control paradigms, together with correlated-error suppression capabilities. These results pave the way for modular quantum computing and offer a promising approach to scaling to larger-scale quantum circuits.

title: A Manifesto for Future Generation Cloud Computing
abstract: Abstract The digital architecture of the twenty-first century is undergoing a tectonic shift from the centralized hyper-scale models of the past decade toward a pervasive, intelligent, and sovereign compute continuum. This manifesto delineates the evolutionary trajectory of cloud computing, conceptualizing it no longer as a mere remote storage or processing utility, but as a living fabric that integrates edge intelligence, quantum-ready protocols, and ethical governance. By synthesizing recent breakthroughs in 6G-enabled communication, serverless orchestration, and green computing mandates, this analysis provides a comprehensive roadmap for a resilient digital ecosystem. The core thesis argues that the future of cloud computing must be "sovereign-by-design," addressing the widening chasm between global economic efficiency and localized digital autonomy. We examine the transition from the "Fifth Utility" to a decentralized infrastructure that balances the radical concentration of power with the democratization of innovation, particularly within the Global South.

title: Holography and Entanglement in Quantum Field Theory
abstract: Quantum field theory (QFT) and general relativity are individually successful but hard to reconcile. The holographic principle, realized concretely in the AdS/CFT correspondence, offers a route to a reconciliation. However, this correspondence is rigorously established only for special, highly supersymmetric string theory setups, and the holographic duals of most QFTs, including QCD, are unknown. Meanwhile, entanglement is central both to the emergence of spacetime in holography and to non-perturbative QFT. This thesis studies both problems in two largely independent parts. Part I asks whether holography can be derived entirely within QFT itself. The central idea is that the Feynman-diagram expansion can be reorganized into a string-theory amplitude. In diagrams with many interaction vertices, particle worldlines effectively cover a two-dimensional surface, which becomes the worldsheet of an emergent string description. Two constructions are presented. In the first, for diagrams with many vertices, the graph data are lifted to a Riemann surface by treating them as a discretization of continuous functions, using discrete exterior calculus. title: Predicting spectral interpolation from classical dynamics: an exact Berry–Robnik→Brody locus, its error budget, and its domain
abstract: The Brody parameter β is routinely fitted to the level spacings of a mixed quantum system and then read as a measure of its classical chaos. A fitted number cannot test the classical picture — it can only describe the spectrum. This paper asks the question the other way round: given only the classical regular fraction ρ_reg, what should β be, and does the spectrum agree? The answer is a parameter-free locus: the Berry–Robnik superposition with the exact GOE gap probability (not the Wigner surmise) projected onto the Brody family in two canonical coordinates, a Kullback–Leibler projection and a log-variance projection. One consequence is immediate and often overlooked — the Brody parameter of a fully chaotic GOE spectrum is not 1 but 0.954 (KL) and 0.969 (log-variance). The locus was tested pointwise, under scoring rules registered before the spectra were computed, on the quantised standard map, a two-harmonic kicked rotor and the Bunimovich mushroom billiard: 16 of 17 mixed cells fall inside the registered tolerance with nothing fitted to the spectra.
