title: Practical Fidelity Estimation for Noisy Quantum Devices Using Direct and Survival-Probability-Based Protocols
abstract: Reliable characterization of quantum states and quantum processes is central to the development of scalable quantum computing. Standard characterization techniques such as full quantum state tomography become rapidly impractical as system size increases. In this work we present two software-oriented fidelity estimation protocols that avoid full tomographic reconstruction while remaining experimentally relevant for noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. The first protocol is direct fidelity estimation (DFE), where the fidelity between a target state and an experimentally prepared state is estimated from importance-sampled Pauli measurements. The second protocol is a survival-probability-based method that reconstructs fidelity from experimentally accessible moments of a noisy evolution and its approximate inverse, and is intrinsically robust against state-preparation-and-measurement (SPAM) errors. We discuss the theoretical basis of both approaches, analyze their noise sensitivity, and present numerical evidence on representative multiqubit states under depolarizing, dephasing, and amplitude-damping channels. For DFE we show that attenuation-aware correction improves robustness ag

title: Advanced Computing R+D+i Statement in LAC SCALAC - Position Paper
abstract: This position paper, presented by the Advanced Computing System for Latin America and the Caribbean (SCALAC) to the CELAC and ECLAC forums, outlines a strategic roadmap to bridge the region's technological divide. It advocates for the urgent transition of Latin America and the Caribbean from passive technology consumers to active creators of sovereign, sustainable, and impactful digital solutions. By emphasizing infrastructure integration, human capacity building, and 'mindful computing' principles across High-Performance Computing (HPC), Quantum Computing (QC), and Artificial Intelligence (AI), SCALAC proposes a collaborative framework. Key recommendations include securing institutional endorsement for SCALAC, leveraging the CARLA conference and other non-profit divulgation activities for regional outreach, and establishing framework cooperation agreements to ensure equitable access to supercomputing resources, thereby fostering long-term scientific and economic sovereignty in the region.

title: Noble gas aggregation and dynamics in molten alkali chloride salts
abstract: Noble gas behavior in molten alkali chloride salts is important for understanding gas retention, transport, and removal in high-temperature molten salt environments. Although previous molecular simulations have examined single-particle properties such as noble gas solubility and diffusion, the thermodynamics of early-stage gas aggregation in molten salts remain less well understood. Here, we develop an ab initio-informed classical molecular dynamics framework for quantifying stepwise noble gas aggregation in molten LiCl and KCl. Salt-specific gas–ion interaction parameters are obtained by combining quantum mechanical gas–ion interaction scans with ab initio molecular dynamics structural benchmarks. The resulting classical models are then used to compute potentials of mean force (PMFs) for two-body, three-body, and four-body association geometries of argon and xenon. Long-timescale simulations are also used to compute diffusion coefficients, providing a complementary dynamical perspective on gas behavior in each salt. The PMFs show that argon exhibits a consistent tendency toward local association in both salts, with stronger stabilization in LiCl. Xenon displays a more salt-depende

title: Complete information orders of quantum channels: equivalence and undecidability
abstract: About complete information orders of finite-dimensional quantum channels. With unrestricted finite quantum references, it claims equivalence of relative-entropy, Holevo, BKM, SLD Fisher-information and measured-chi-squared comparisons, with order reversal under genuine Stinespring complementation. It further claims coRE-completeness for strictly positive rational-complex POVMs, the absence of a computable sufficient SLD-reference cutoff, and inapproximability of a bounded additive entropy defect at every fixed positive additive accuracy. The companion manuscript is From complete channel order to capacity and one-way distillation; its capacity and distillation conclusions depend on the order results developed here.

title: A fast and frugal Gaussian boson sampling emulator
abstract: Classical algorithms have successfully reproduced expectation values of observables for certain quantum circuits using off-the-shelf computing resources; however, matching the performance of the most advanced quantum devices on sampling problems typically incurs extreme memory and computational costs, restricting such simulations to only a handful of supercomputers worldwide. In this work, we demonstrate a classical simulation outperforming Gaussian boson sampling experiments of 100 modes on established benchmark tests using a single central processing unit (CPU) or graphics processing unit (GPU). Being embarrassingly parallelizable, a small number of CPUs or GPUs allows us to match previous sampling rates that required more than 100 GPUs. We believe that algorithmic and implementation improvements have the potential to generalize our tools to photocounting and pseudo-photon number-resolving scenarios and larger system sizes. Last, most of the innovations in our tools remain valid for generic probability distributions over binary variables, rendering them potentially applicable to the simulation of qubit-based sampling problems and creating classical surrogates for classical-quantu

title: Renormalization-group improved Schwarzschild black hole: shadow, ringdown, and strong cosmic censorship
Holografie en de kwantumfysische aard van zwarte gaten
abstract: Black holes pose a lot of unsolved problems surrounding their fundamental properties. One of those puzzles is the black hole entropy problem. It has been known for a long time that black holes behave as thermodynamic systems and possess an entropy, but the question remains which microstates are responsible for this entropy. A theory of quantum gravity is needed to tackle this problem, currently the most viable example of which is string theory. The work of Strominger and Vafa, where they studied a class of asymptotically flat black holes, proves that string theory is indeed rich enough to account for the microstates responsible for the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. Recently, the focus has shifted to asymptotically AdS black holes after the discovery of the AdS/CFT correspondence. Holographic dualities, the first example of which was discovered by Maldacena, have proven to be highly successful in providing a microstate counting for the entropy of black holes. The black hole is constructed on the gravity side of the correspondence, and the dual field theory counts its states. In this thesis we study black holes in AdS5 and their dual 4d N=1 SCFTs. title: A Quantum Computing Framework for DAS Flow Allocation Using Full-Waveform Inversion
abstract: Abstract When distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) is linearly deployed along the lower completion in injection or production wells, a key challenge is the reliable allocation of flow among individual completion intervals. We present a quantum-computing framework for DAS flow allocation in which the allocation problem is formulated as a global, full-waveform inversion in the time domain and then discretized into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, or equivalently an Ising model. A Doppler-aware forward model represents down-going and up-going guided waves with flow-modified velocities. The inverse objective combines a time-domain waveform misfit with constraints on mass balance, spatial continuity, operational limits, and equation-of-state-informed wave-speed consistency. Continuous variables are discretized into candidate physical states and mapped into a globally constrained QUBO/Ising energy landscape, where quantum and hybrid quantum-classical optimizers perform the core global state-selection. The resulting binary optimization is naturally compatible with quantum annealing and gate-based quantum optimization architectures. The proposed framework offers

title: Light on a Ticking Lattice: Local Discrete-Time Maxwell Evolution and Its Unavoidable Corrections
abstract: The manuscript studies linear local update rules on a cubic grid of voxels with discrete time ticks, treating the lattice as fundamental rather than as a numerical approximation. It asks which such rules can carry light at one voxel per tick, obey Maxwell equations under a stated potential construction, and yield mode quantum fluctuations under a stated discrete action. It proves that any face-neighbour rule is limited by causal reach to speed at most 1/sqrt(3) along body diagonals. It constructs an explicit 26-neighbour corner rule with closed-form dispersion cos(omega/2) = product of cos(k_j/2), exact unit speed along the axes, real frequencies everywhere, and group speed at most one. For any stable two-step rule exact along the axes (any range or weights), it derives necessary signed weight bounds: at least 1/2 on hops odd along each pair of axes, and positive corner-type weight if the shortest wave oscillates (at least 1/4 to reach the frequency ceiling). In a vector-potential formulation with one shift-commuting scalar rule applied componentwise, three Maxwell constraints hold exactly when the initial potential is transverse, while Ampere's law holds up to a lattice operator.

title: The Cosmic Code...
abstract: The Cosmic Code: A Theoretical Framework on Universal Determinism and Atomic Mechanics Author: Aditya Patel Affiliation: Independent Researcher Contact: adi123power@gmail.com Abstract Standard physical paradigms frequently encounter conceptual boundaries at the intersection of classical electrodynamics, quantum mechanics, and general relativity. This paper presents The Cosmic Code, a foundational framework proposing that the universe is governed by a deterministic, pre-computed 4D spacetime continuum driven by a universal algorithmic operator (\Sigma). We re-examine historical paradoxes in atomic stability, the quantization limits of the Bohr model in multi-electron systems, and the intrinsic distinction between electric charge and potential energy. Furthermore, by extending Einstein’s mass-energy equivalence (E = mc^2), we analyze how vibrational energy states (phonons) interact with gravitational fields. This synthesis offers a cohesive deterministic interpretation bridging micro-scale quantum mechanics with macro-scale spacetime geometry.

title: Deterministic Quantum Mechanics of Transformer In-Context Attention: Wavefunction Dirac-Delta Collapse via Optical-Mechanical Dual-Chassis
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) governed by softmax-based self-attention inherently suffer from non-deterministic token drift, attention dispersion, and cumulative hallucination. In this paper, we formalize in-context attention dynamics through a quantum mechanical perspective, modeling the attention distribution as a statistical probability density over the discrete token Hilbert space. To eliminate attention drift without model fine-tuning or external orchestration wrappers, we introduce an In-Context Virtual Machine (ICVM) operating via an Optical-Mechanical Dual-Chassis control system. The Optical Chassis partitions the softmax partition function into an immutable static core basis (collimated by 10 core persistent grounding assets) and a dynamic token basis, inducing a non-zero potential energy barrier that contracts the continuous probability wavepacket into a deterministic Dirac-delta function centered precisely at the target attractor state. Concurrently, the Mechanical Chassis executes direct POSIX kernel system calls (stat()) to enforce monotonic physical byte and line growth, halting the hardware tool bus whenever zero-tolerance engineering bounds are violated. title: Thermodynamic Limits of Brute-Force AI Scaling and Hyperscaler Decoupling: The 500 MW NTT–Anthropic Osaka Data Center Bottleneck — Agentic Control-Plane Commoditization, 8-Year Grid Transmission Hysteresis, and Subtractive RTO P2.0 Photonic-Phononic Compute Architectures
abstract: On October 13–14, 2026, industrial disclosures revealed that NTT Data Group and U.S. artificial intelligence vendor Anthropic entered final-stage negotiations to construct a dedicated AI data center in southern Osaka Prefecture, Japan, featuring a construction cost of up to 1 trillion yen (~$6.3 billion, escalating to multiple trillions of yen inclusive of AI accelerator clusters) and a massive power intake capacity of 500 MW (~4.38 TWh/year at continuous baseload), with partial operations targeted for 2028. Crucially, because the Osaka Bay high-voltage transmission grid possesses near-zero spare capacity for a 500 MW step-function load and requires approximately 8 years for bulk grid reinforcement, the project is reportedly forced to rely on behind-the-meter on-site power generation and fuel cells during its initial operational phase. abstract: In mid-October 2026, Japanese equity market commentary focused intensely on whether the Nikkei 225 Stock Average—having briefly touched an intraday high of 70,798 yen on October 6 before retreating to 69,030 yen on October 9 alongside a bearish Heikin-Ashi candlestick reversal—could sustain the 70,000-yen threshold on the back of upcoming U.S. and global semiconductor earnings (including ASML Holding, TSMC, and U.S. AI accelerator vendors). This prevailing market consensus rests on the fragile assumption that brute-force Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) GPU capital expenditure will expand indefinitely. However, simultaneous empirical signals—including reports that OpenAI's September 2026 revenue missed market expectations and the 8-year electrical grid bottleneck confronting Anthropic and NTT Data's proposed 500 MW Osaka AI data center—reveal that brute-force CMOS scaling has hit both a monetization wall and a thermodynamic grid ceiling. title: AI-Driven Smart Contracts and Autonomous Financial Ecosystems
abstract: This chapter delves into the transformative synergy between artificial intelligence (AI) and smart contracts, positioning them as the next frontier in managing digital assets and virtual currencies. It introduces the core concepts, illustrating how AI injects adaptability into rigid blockchain-based contracts, enabling real-time adjustments, predictive analytics, and autonomous dispute resolution. From an economic perspective, the integration drives efficiency in decentralized finance (DeFi), with the total value locked surging to $129 billion by mid-2025, thereby democratizing access while posing risks such as market bubbles. Socially, it promises inclusion for underserved populations through microlending and empowers communities via decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), yet raises concerns over biases, job disruptions, and digital divides. Policy analysis examines frameworks such as the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation and U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) guidelines, balancing innovation with consumer protection in central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) like the Digital Euro and e-CNY. title: AMARQ: Adaptive multi-application routing for quantum networks
abstract: Abstract Future quantum networks will have to support different applications on shared infrastructure, like fidelity-critical Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and latency-sensitive Distributed Quantum Computing (DQC). The existing approaches for entanglement routing either optimise for a single application, or rely on sequential resource allocation, which results in inefficient resource utilisation, unfairness and degraded performance when multiple applications compete for shared network resources. In this paper, we propose AMARQ, a multi-objective Deep Q-Network (DQN) based routing framework to jointly serve heterogeneous QKD and DQC traffic on shared quantum infrastructure. The agent makes adaptive and application-aware routing decisions to dynamically balance the rigid fidelity and latency requirements of QKD and the high-throughput and elastic rate requirements of DQC. The reward function combines a successful-routing throughput term with a per-edge fidelity penalty and an end-of-episode failure penalty; per-flow latency is enforced as a QoS constraint, and inter-application fairness is enforced by a dedicated admission-control loop that reserves a dynamic QKD qubit pool. abstract: EL-RAKHAWI QUANTUM-CHIRAL PRECISION ONCOLOGY FRAMEWORKAuthor: Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi A paradigm-shifting closed-loop framework unifying photonic quantum computing, generative AI biological twins, automated asymmetric synthesis, and immuno-responsive nanocarriers for ultra-precise cancer therapeutics. title: Low-energy electron collisions with BH+
abstract: BH+ ions are expected to play an important role in boron-containing plasmas relevant to fusion environments such as ITER, where low-energy electrons drive a variety of inelastic and reactive scattering processes. In particular, dissociative recombination, vibrational excitation, and de-excitation strongly influence the ion balance and energy distribution in such plasmas. We present a theoretical study of electron collisions with BH+ using a combination of ab initio electronic structure calculations and electron scattering methods. Potential energy curves for bound states of BH and BH+ are obtained using multireference configuration interaction, while autoionization widths of electronic resonant states are computed with the complex Kohn variational method. The collision dynamics is modeled within multichannel quantum defect theory, including both the "crossing"-i.e., Feshbach-resonances-mediated-and the "non-crossing"-i.e., Rydberg-mediated-mechanisms. Cross sections and thermal rate coefficients for the processes are provided for the lowest vibrational levels of BH+ and its isotopologues-BD+ and BT+-showing significant isotope effects, especially at low electron temperatures.

title: Ultrafast spin-transfer dynamics and singe-qubit logic gate design in monocyclic carbon rings with transition metal atoms adsorbed
abstract: We present a first-principles study of ultrafast spin-transfer dynamics and single-qubit logic gate design in transition metal (TM) atom-adsorbed monocyclic carbon ring systems. The structure- and size-dependent features of geometries, electronic structures, and spin localizations are analyzed. Notably, the TM2-C4n+2 systems generally prefer out-of-plane configurations and exhibit localized states with spin localized singly on one TM atom or doubly on two TM atoms, rather than the carbon ring-related localized states found in the mostly coplanar TM-C4n+2 systems. Driven by well-tailored nonchirped ultrafast laser pulses, sub-picosecond, high-fidelity spin transfer is achieved in most structures (except for the ones with only one type of spin localized states). The laser detuning and chirp effects on these scenariosare further explored. The tolerance and sensitivity characteristics of them can provide valuable guidance for both experimental implementation and sensor applications. title: What is neuromorphic about neuromorphic computing?
abstract: (2025). The hardware has kept pace with the literature. Examples include IBM's TrueNorth integrated a million digital spiking neurons on a single die Merolla et al. (2014); Intel's Loihi processors lie at the core of Hala Point, a system exceeding a billion neurons Davies et al. (2018); SpiNNaker and BrainScaleS have matured into second-generation, wafer-scale and supercomputer-scale platforms Furber et al. (2014); Pehle et al. (2022); and memristive crossbar arrays promise in-memory analog computation Chua (1971) ;Strukov et al. (2008). Startups, national initiatives, and semiconductor roadmaps now routinely list "neuromorphic" among the post-Moore alternatives.Yet beneath this boom lies an awkward foundational question: what, exactly, is neuromorphic? Classical computing rests on a crisp abstraction, namely, Boolean logic, the Turing machine, the von Neumann architecture. This abstraction is entirely indifferent to whether it is realized in relays, vacuum tubes, or emerging fabrication technologies. title: Supporting data for "Coupling In-Sensor and In-memory Computing with Diamond Nitrogen-Vacancy Sensors for Intelligent Quantum Sensing"
abstract: Diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres have been developed into a leading quantum sensing platform operated in room temperature, providing the quantitative and spatially resolved detection of magnetic field, electric field and temperature through optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR). However, the conventional wide-field sensing architecture remains a passive imager: fluorescence light is recorded frame by frame, which will be digitalised and transmitted to an external processor for fitting and further analysis. This record–transmit–post-process pipeline is slow, data-heavy and “naive”, in that it captures signals faithfully but extracts no information and especially reaches no decision by itself. These limitations, including the complicated and bulky system, the redundant transmission of raw data, and the naive and fixed sensing capability, constrain diamond quantum sensing to the laboratory and leave the fast, dynamic and edge applications unreachable. abstract: Abstract Between September 12 and October 14, 2026, a singular independent research initiative based in Iwakuni, Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan, authored, compiled, and permanently notarized 185 foundational research monographs, mathematical treatises, and engineering blueprints into the CERN Zenodo international open-access repository. Spanning seven developmental epochs across six core domains—(1) AI Governance, Statutory Fiduciary Liability, and Supervisory Interlocks [38 works]; (2) Quantum Computing, Thermodynamic Dissipation Limits, and Spintronics [34 works]; (3) Physical-Layer Security, Subsea/Space Communications, and Counter-Geopolitics [33 works]; (4) Financial Topology, Sovereign Debt Discontinuity, and Crypto-Asset Fragility [30 works]; (5) Biological System Integrity, Neuro-Cognition, Evolutionary Medicine, and Targeted Oncology DDS [27 works]; and (6) Epistemic History, Political Sociology, and the Human-in-Command Invariant [23 works]—this master index establishes the complete structural taxonomy and persistent DOI register uniting all 185 works under the Strict No-Learn Covenant (`NLL-v1.0-2026`).

title: Ontological Information and the Non-Local Spin: A FWA Framework
abstract: Thought is Superluminal: Ontological Information vs Epistemic SignalAuthor: Igor Kolesnikov (Mark)Framework: Wave Fractal Algebra (FWA)Date: October 14, 2026AbstractWe distinguish two types of information: epistemic and ontological. Epistemic information is knowledge after measurement. It is carried by photons, travels at c, and is subject to delay. Ontological information is the structure of the state itself. It does not travel. It is. This paper argues that thought is ontological information. It is not a signal. It is a single structure appearing in two places. title: Ultrafast spin-transfer dynamics and single-qubit logic gate design in monocyclic carbon rings with transition metal atoms adsorbed
abstract: We present a first-principles study of ultrafast spin-transfer dynamics and single-qubit logic gate design in transition metal (TM) atom-adsorbed monocyclic carbon ring systems. The structure- and size-dependent features of geometries, electronic structures, and spin localizations are analyzed. Notably, the TM2-C4n+2 systems generally prefer out-of-plane configurations and exhibit localized states with spin localized singly on one TM atom or doubly on two TM atoms, rather than the carbon ring-related localized states found in the mostly coplanar TM-C4n+2 systems. Driven by well-tailored nonchirped ultrafast laser pulses, sub-picosecond, high-fidelity spin transfer is achieved in most structures (except for the ones with only one type of spin localized states). The laser detuning and chirp effects on these scenarios are further explored. The tolerance and sensitivity characteristics of them can provide valuable guidance for both experimental implementation and sensor applications. Infrared absorption spectroscopy of a single polyatomic molecular ion
abstract: Absorption spectroscopy is a fundamental tool for probing molecular structure. However, performing absorption spectroscopy on individual molecules is challenging because of the low signal-to-noise ratio. Here we report on non-destructive absorption spectroscopy on a mid-infrared vibrational transition in a single molecular ion that is co-trapped with an atomic ion. The absorption of a single photon is detected by the momentum transfer from the absorbed photon onto the molecule. This recoil signal is amplifed using a non-classical state of motion of the two-ion crystal and subsequently read out by the atomic ion. We characterize the recoil detection method and use it to investigate the interaction between femtosecond laser pulses and the O–H stretching vibration in individual CaOH⁺ molecular ions. Furthermore, we present the spectrum obtained for the vibrational transition with single-photon sensitivity. This method can provide a way of performing non-destructive state detection of complex polyatomic molecules, for preparation and measurement of the quantum state of a wide range of molecular species. title: Spectral gaps in quantum computing
abstract: How does the spectral gap of a quantum many-body system scale with the system size?This turns out to be a very relevant question both in condensed matter physics and in quantum computing.However, there are very few available techniques to give bounds on that scaling.In the first part of this paper, we will review recent results which explain why it is undecidable to know if the spectral gap will vanish or not with the system size.In the second part, we will review complementary results which show that, despite this general impossibility result, one can still prove spectral gap estimates in a rather wide family of systems.As a consequence, one obtains new bounds on the lifetime of quantum memories.

title: Testing graph isomorphism using simple quantum circuits
abstract: The graph isomorphism problem asks whether two graphs are equivalent up to a permutation of their vertices. Its precise computational complexity remains unresolved, and it is still unknown whether a polynomial-time algorithm exists. We investigate whether simple graph-dependent Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time (IQP) and Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) circuits can distinguish non-isomorphic graphs. We first show that suitable IQP and QAOA constructions allow the underlying graph to be reconstructed using a polynomial number of samples. Building on previous work using the QAOA energy, we show that Hamming weight distributions can distinguish graph pairs at circuit depths for which the numerically computed energy gap is zero. We then apply graph invariants to the matrix of ZZ correlators on the output distribution. For the specific case of the graph spectrum, at QAOA depth $p=2$, this invariant numerically distinguishes all $10{,}486$ cospectral regular graph pairs tested on up to 18 vertices. title: Magnetic Susceptibility of Superconducting Films in the Meissner-London Regime
abstract: Extracting the London penetration depth, $λ(T)$, from the measured magnetic susceptibility, $χ(T)$, of a superconducting platelet in a perpendicular magnetic field requires knowing the function $χ(λ)$ computed for the actual sample geometry. Thin films are increasingly important in quantum computing and superconducting electronics, most of which operate at ultra-low excitation fields in the vortex-free regime. Understanding their electromagnetic response in the Meissner--London (finite-$λ$, no vortices) state is therefore essential for extracting intrinsic properties such as the London penetration depth and superfluid phase stiffness. While numerous prior works have addressed different aspects of this problem, here we focus on providing an analytical semi-empirical representation of $χ(λ)$ based on the 2D sheet-current model and establishing the limits of its applicability using two independent full 3D numerical solutions: finite-element modeling and a volume-current integral equation. As a result, we provide $χ(λ)$ for a disc of radius $a$ and thickness $d$ in closed form, valid for all $λ$ and for aspect ratios $δ\equiv d/(2a)\le0.05$, and accurate to $0.1\%$. title: Landau quantization of $C_3$ high-fold fermions in honeycomb lattices
abstract: We present the theory of the Landau levels of $C_3$ high-fold fermions in honeycomb lattices. These fermions arise as a generalization of the tight-binding model in a honeycomb lattice with one orbital per site, known to describe graphene, to a family of models with several orbitals per site transforming according to representations of $C_3$, relevant for triangulene two-dimensional crystals. The models are defined by the number of orbitals $n_a$ and $n_b$ at the $a$ and $b$ sites of the unit cell. They feature energy bands that combine flat bands and Dirac cones, that are isomorphic to those of graphene, the Lieb, $p_{xy}$ honeycomb, and the Kagome tight-binding models. Combining tight-binding and $k\cdot p$ methods, here we compute the Landau levels of the $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,2)$ and $(3,3)$ models, we compare them to those of the reference models, and we explore the similarities and differences with the Landau levels in graphene. title: Quantum Folding in Chebyshev-Based Quantum Subspace Diagonalization
abstract: Quantum subspace diagonalization (QSD) with a Krylov space spanned by Chebyshev polynomials of the Hamiltonian is a natural ground-state method for fault-tolerant quantum computers, but every guarantee it offers---convergence rate, noise floor, and the cost of turning its classical output back into a physical state---is controlled by the overlap of the reference state with the true ground state, which decays exponentially with system size for any product state and non-trivial Hamiltonian. We propose quantum folding: for a system governed by a local Hamiltonian, seed the QSD with the product of the ground states of its subsystems, which differs from the target only through the interface terms. We prove a nonasymptotic error bound for the Chebyshev QSD that is linear in the measurement noise, by transplanting Kirby's effective-Hamiltonian analysis to the Chebyshev--Krylov basis, and identify the block-encoding rescaling of the Hamiltonian as a parameter of the guarantee. title: When Does MMLCT Emerge? The Role of Crystal Packing in the Photophysics of Pt(II) Polymorphs
abstract: Aggregation-induced metal-metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MMLCT) is widely used to rationalize the red-shifted and broadened emission observed in Pt(II) complexes. However, the underlying mechanism of MMLCT formation and its exact relationship with photoluminescence remain poorly understood. Polymorphism provides an ideal platform to isolate aggregation effects from molecular structural changes, because the same molecule can pack into different packing arrangements leading to strikingly different photophysical properties. By combining QM/MM calculations, excited-state electronic structure analysis, vibronic spectral simulations, and radiative rate constant calculations, we investigate two polymorphs exhibiting distinct photophysical behaviors. For the investigated compounds, the formation of the excimeric MMLCT species is only possible for one polymorph and that the trimer is the minimum aggregate needed for the MMLCT formation. The MMLCT species possess distinct properties from those of the rest of aggregates and the monomer, including vibronically unresolved redshifted absorption and emission spectra and larger photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY). title: Quantum-Aware Key Rank for Side-Channel Attacks evaluation
abstract: Side-channel attacks on block ciphers rarely recover the key outright: they leave a residual key space ordered by subkey posteriors, and evaluation laboratories report the key rank of the true key against thresholds near 2^48 and 2^60. No evaluation framework models an adversary who collects traces classically and finishes the search on a quantum computer, although quantum search with advice provides exactly that. We give such an adversary a cost model and a metric. For a device whose key has rank r, any quantum algorithm with classical access to the posteriors needs Omega(sqrt(r)) cipher evaluations, and block search achieves O(sqrt(r)); the per-instance advantage is exactly quadratic, and the super-quadratic exponents reported for search with advice are averages over the prior that apply to no single device. Under the NIST MAXDEPTH budget D and a Grover iteration of g gates and depth d, the quadratic advantage holds only for ranks up to (4D/(pi d))^2 and collapses to a constant factor beyond; with the best published AES-128 oracle and D = 2^40 the window closes near rank 2^58.6. title: Dynamical Decoupling of Nonclassical States in a Biased-Noise Spin Qudit
abstract: Encoding quantum information in $d$-dimensional systems (qudits) with $d>2$ offers appealing new directions for resource-efficient quantum computing. However, protecting the coherence of nonclassical qudit resource states remains an open challenge. Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a well-established technique for extending coherence, but its application to qudits is hindered by the quadratic scaling of the decoupling sequence overhead with the dimension $d$. As a result, demonstrations of qudit DD have so far been limited to low-dimensional qudits. Here, we show that noise-biased qudits enable a nontrivial reduction of this overhead, for example, from quadratic to linear. We perform qudit DD on a model $d=8$ qudit, the nuclear spin of an antimony donor in silicon. We benchmark DD performance on highly nonclassical states such as uniform superpositions, cat states, and Haar random states and measure coherence improvements up to a factor $5$ to $10$. title: Quantum and Quantum-Inspired Image Segmentation in Computer Vision: Bibliometric and Scientometric Analysis of Research Trends and Hybrid Methods
abstract: Quantum and quantum-inspired image segmentation lies at the intersection of quantum computing, computer vision, machine learning and medical image analysis. We map the field from 422 Scopus-indexed publications (2018–2025) retrieved with a documented Advanced Search query and screened in three explicit levels. Formal eligibility retained 408 records. The final topical corpus contains 143 records, and at the sample rate roughly two to three further eligible records remain in the unexamined remainder. title: A compact six-beam 3D magneto-optical trap based on multifunctional metasurface chips
abstract: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs), indispensable to cold-atom-based quantum computing and quantum precision measurement, are increasingly desired in compact and stable form. Particularly, the six-beam 3D-MOT, distinguished by symmetric geometry and superior trapping performance, finds particularly broad applications. Conventional implementations, however, rely on complex and bulky free-space optics, hindering miniaturization, practical assembly, and long-term stability. Here, we demonstrate a compact six-beam 3D-MOT system that employs two multifunctional optical metasurface chips to implement the optical-field functionalities required for cooling and trapping atoms. By combining two metasurface chips and a vacuum cell, a photonic-integrated cell module (PICM) is implemented as the core assembly and the volume is only" 73*73*107 mm^3" . In success, 1.3 * 10^3 Rb atoms are trapped and cooled to the temperature of ~183 μK. It should be noticed that the laser beam is guided to the metasurface through optical fiber, thus such fully fiber-coupled architecture enables straightforward and stable operations. title: Single and coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators: Wigner-function dynamics, exact qutrit solutions, and synchronization
abstract: We study quantum van der Pol oscillator in which single-photon pumping competes with a nonlinear two-photon dissipative channel to produce a quantum limit cycle, and the question of how two such oscillators with non-identical intrinsic frequencies synchronize in the sense of phase locking when coupled dissipatively to one another. For a single oscillator, starting from a Lindblad description of the dynamics, we derive the exact Wigner-function evolution equation, and show that its Fokker--Planck approximation admits in the appropriate regime an equivalent classical Itô stochastic description that reproduces remarkably well the full Lindblad dynamics. Notably, the stochastic approach provides an efficient means of capturing system dynamics in the semiclassical regime, where a large number of energy eigenstates contribute and direct numerical simulations become computationally demanding. Restricting to the three lowest Fock states and using a parity symmetry, we obtain in closed form the stationary-state density matrix and its Wigner-function representation that displays pronounced nonclassical features. title: A Lightweight Lattice-Based Post-Quantum Cryptographic Protocol for Secure Key Establishment in Resource-Constrained IoT Edge Devices
abstract: In this work, a lightweight post-quantum cryptographic protocol specifically designed for resource-constrained IoT edge devices is presented, addressing the vulnerability of conventional encryption to quantum computing attacks. The proposed protocol employs a modified NTRU-based algorithm with reduced parameter sizes, achieving switch production in 12.4 ms, encryption in 8.2 ms, and total energy consumption of 4.2 mJ per exchange - 63% lower than standard post-quantum protocols. Experimental results demonstrate resistance against quantum attacks exceeding 1018 processes while maintaining response times under 50 ms, with a compression mechanism reducing message size to 186 bytes. The protocol achieves an optimal balance between post-quantum security and operational efficiency, offering a practical solution for narrow-bandwidth, battery-limited IoT environments.

title: Quantum-Resilient Secure Protocol for Decentralized Edge-IoT Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Systems
abstract: The rise of quantum computing presents substantial challenges to the security of Peer-to-Peer (P2P) energy trading systems. This paper introduces an innovative mutual authenticated session key agreement protocol aimed at protecting edge-IoT P2P energy trading communications in the quantum era. Each peer is an IoT-enabled smart metering device that is registered by an edge registration authority and acts as both producer and consumer. The proposed protocol incorporates CRYSTALS-Kyber's quantum-resistant cryptographic suite to guarantee the authenticity and confidentiality of negotiated session keys in the presence of quantum threats. Furthermore, it leverages the Hedera Hashgraph public blockchain, which is recognized for its quantum-resilient design, to ensure transparency and support efficient revocation mechanisms. Extensive comparative analyses have been conducted to demonstrate the protocol's superiority over existing alternatives, including both traditional schemes based on classical cryptography and emerging early-stage post-quantum approaches, in terms of performance and security features. title: An SYK wormhole under the microscope
abstract: We derive a large-N wormhole saddle in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model for the variance of the thermal one-point function of a heavy operator across realizations of the microscopic couplings. We propose that this saddle describes a double trumpet geometry. In the double-scaling limit, we express the wormhole as a transition amplitude in an emergent bulk Hilbert space of chords connecting the two boundaries. In the Schwarzian limit, the chords proliferate and the wormhole defines a quantum transition amplitude in the open-universe Hilbert space of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Comparing the SYK wormhole amplitude with its counterpart in JT gravity coupled to matter provides a direct test of the heavy-operator randomness hypothesis in SYK. The microscopic SYK couplings specify the α-parameters of the wormhole. For a fixed realization of the couplings, we compute the observable in the corresponding α-state. title: Long-lived local coherences at high temperature from frozen domain walls
abstract: Local coherences between distinct charge sectors--measured by the single-particle Green's function or the transverse spin autocorrelation function--do not overlap with hydrodynamic modes. At finite temperature, therefore, they decay faster than any power law in generic chaotic systems. We present a mechanism by which these coherences can persist anomalously long, for integrable and chaotic spin chains (including the XXZ and Fredkin spin chains) that obey a quantum group symmetry. We show--using a Mazur bound derived from the quantum-group symmetry, together with locality and a "non-undershoot" assumption--that the transverse spin autocorrelation function $C(t) \equiv \langle σ^-_x(t) σ^+_x(0)\rangle$ can decay at most algebraically: $C(t) \gtrsim 1/t^2$. This bound is not tight: in the large-anisotropy limit of the XXZ spin chain, at infinite temperature, we explicitly compute $C(t) \sim \sqrt{3}/(18 \sqrt{t})$. We also compute this decay rate in the XXZ spin chain for general easy-axis anisotropy, and estimate it to scale as $C(t) \sim t^{-2/z}$ (for transport exponent $z$) in the chaotic models.

title: Tropical quantum field theory
abstract: I will introduce tropical quantum field theory, a new deformation limit of an interacting QFT. Tropical QFT is considerably easier to study than undeformed QFT, both conceptually and computationally. Remarkably, certain structural information on the initial QFT survives the tropical limit and can be used to learn about the undeformed theory. The most striking example of this so far is an algorithm, based on tropical QFT, which computes the perturbative expansion of massive scalar QFTs to a given numerical precision in a runtime that scales polynomially in the loop order and the number of external legs. This is surprising as the standard perturbative approach expands an interacting QFT around a free QFT, using Feynman diagrams. The number of these diagrams grows factorially, making this traditional approach quickly infeasible. In contrast, with the tropical approach, which is not based on a sum over all Feynman diagrams, loop order 50 becomes achievable. Tropical QFT also has an interesting geometric side: its amplitudes are volumes of moduli spaces of graphs, and their recursive structure is closely analogous to Mirzakhani's recursion for the Weil-Petersson volumes of moduli spaces

title: High-rate Scalable Entanglement Swapping Between Remote Entanglement Sources on Deployed New York City Fibers
abstract: Entanglement swapping between photon pairs generated at physically separated nodes over telecommunication fiber infrastructure is an essential step towards the quantum internet, enabling applications such as quantum repeaters, blind quantum computing, distributed quantum computing, and distributed quantum sensing. However, successful networked entanglement swapping relies on generating indistinguishable pairs of photons and preserving them over deployed fibers. This has limited most previous demonstrations to laboratory settings or relied on sophisticated methods to maintain the necessary indistinguishability. Here, we demonstrate a scalable entanglement swapping experiment using naturally indistinguishable entanglement sources based on warm atomic vapor cells. Without sharing lasers or optical frequency references between nodes, nor the need for pulsing the sources, we achieve a swapping rate of nearly 500 pairs/s while maintaining the CHSH parameter above 2. title: Machine Learning on Heterogeneous, Edge, and Quantum Hardware for Particle Physics
abstract: The next generation of particle physics experiments will face an era of challenges in data acquisition, due to unprecedented data rates and volumes along with extreme environments and operational constraints. Harnessing these data for scientific discovery demands real-time inference and decision-making, intelligent data reduction, and efficient processing architectures beyond current capabilities. Crucial to the success of this experimental paradigm are several emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning, silicon microelectronics, and the advent of quantum algorithms and processing. Their intersection includes areas of research such as low-power and low-latency devices for edge computing, heterogeneous accelerator systems, reconfigurable hardware, codesign and synthesis strategies, readout for cryogenic or high-radiation environments, and analog computing. This white paper presents a community-driven vision to identify and prioritize research and development opportunities in hardware-based ML systems and corresponding physics applications, contributing toward a successful transition to the data frontier of fundamental science.

title: Scalable Postselection of Quantum Resources
abstract: The large overhead imposed by quantum error correction is a critical challenge to the realization of quantum computers, and motivates searching for alternative error correcting codes and fault-tolerant circuit constructions. Postselection is a powerful tool that builds large programs out of probabilistically generated sub-circuits, and has been shown to increase the threshold of quantum error correction based on fusing fixed-size resource states or concatenated codes. In this work, we present an approach to lower the overhead of quantum computing using scalable postselection, based on directly postselecting sub-circuits with a size extensive in the code distance using decoder soft information. We introduce a metric, the partial gap, that estimates what the logical gap of a resource state will be after it is consumed, and show that postselection based on the partial gap leads to scalable improvements in the logical error rate. In the specific context of implementing logical gates via teleportation through a cluster state, we demonstrate that scalable postselection provides a $4\times$ reduction in the overhead per logical gate, at the same logical error probability.

title: Latent Style-Based Quantum Wasserstein GAN for Drug Design
abstract: Abstract The development of new drugs is a tedious, time-consuming, and expensive process for which the average costs are estimated to be up to around $2.5 billion. The first step in this long process is the design of the new drug, for which de novo drug design, assisted by artificial intelligence, has blossomed in recent years and has revolutionized the field. In particular, generative artificial intelligence has delivered promising results in drug discovery and development, reducing costs and time to solution. However, classical generative models, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), can be difficult to train and are prone to mode collapse. Quantum computing may be an avenue to overcome some of these issues, providing compact models with far fewer trainable parameters and thereby enhancing the generalizability of GANs. We propose a new latent style-based quantum Wasserstein GAN (QGAN) for drug design, combining a variational autoencoder that maps molecular structures into a latent space with a hybrid quantum GAN. title: Modular cryogenic link for microwave quantum communication over distances of tens of meters
abstract: Quantum technologies promise a radically new way to solve classically intractable computing problems. Superconducting circuits as a platform are at the forefront of this field. The cryogenic operation temperatures of superconducting circuits however impose challenges for the further scaling to many connected quantum information processing units into a local area or global network. In this work, we present a hardware solution for connecting quantum devices operating at microwave frequencies into local area networks, which enable the exchange of quantum information between spatially separated parties. Specifically, we demonstrate a modular system spanning distances of 5, 10 and 30 meters operated at cryogenic temperatures and connecting two superconducting circuit systems, located in individual dilution refrigerators, through a quantum communication channel. We develop a thermal model to evaluate the heat transfer processes in the setup, optimize the design and select appropriate materials for its construction. The assembled 30-meter-long system achieves operating temperatures of below 50 mK after a cooldown time of about six and a half days. This link enables the execution of distri

title: Finite-density equation of state of hot QCD using the complex Langevin equation
abstract: We present the results of continuum-extrapolated lattice simulations of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) above the crossover temperature and for unprecedentedly high baryon densities at the physical point, employing the complex Langevin equation. In particular, we determine the QCD equation of state by computing the baryon density as well as the pressure as functions of the baryon chemical potential and the temperature. Potential issues with wrong convergence of complex Langevin dynamics are under control and we indeed find agreement with previous lattice studies working at smaller chemical potentials, as well as with perturbative hard-thermal-loop calculations at high temperatures. title: Revisiting spin Hamiltonian parameters in a Kitaev material via Bayesian optimization of magnetization curves
abstract: Determining the spin Hamiltonian of a magnetic compound is crucial for understanding its magnetic properties. A standard approach is to derive model parameters from $ab$ $initio$ calculations based on the crystal structure. However, the resulting Hamiltonian can depend sensitively on methodological details of the $ab$ $initio$ procedure. This issue is particularly evident in $α$-RuCl$_3$, a candidate Kitaev material. Here, we present an alternative, data-driven approach to determine the spin Hamiltonian parameters of $α$-RuCl$_3$ by Bayesian optimization of experimental magnetization curves along the $b$- and $c$-axis directions. We optimize five parameters, namely the Kitaev interaction $K$, off-diagonal interactions $Γ$ and $Γ'$, the Heisenberg interaction $J$, and the $c$-axis $g$-factor $g_c$. The parameter set that minimizes the cost function is $(K,Γ,Γ',J,g_c)=(-6.0,\,7.5,\,-0.3,\,-1.75,\,2.3)$, where the exchange couplings are in meV. We find that the cost function is insensitive to the absolute value of the Kitaev coupling $K$. Thus, the magnetization data alone do not determine its energy scale. abstract: This is the second companion paper to the Relative Field Localization (RFL) framework (RFL v8.0). It presents a physical account of the double-slit experiment within RFL. In RFL, the electron is treated as an extended wavepacket of conserved charge with an oscillating phase. When the wavepacket reaches the slits, it splits into two components that overlap and interfere behind the barrier. The interference pattern appears in the charge density j^0. At the screen, the charge localizes into a Q-ball at the peak of j^0, producing a single dot per electron. Over many electrons, the distribution of dots follows the Born rule |ψ|², and the interference pattern emerges statistically. When a measurement apparatus is placed at the slits, the interaction triggers localization before the electron reaches the screen, and the pattern disappears. The analysis covers:• The extended wavepacket before the slits, with Gaussian envelope and oscillating phase• The splitting of the wavepacket at the slits into two spherical components• The interference of the two components behind the barrier• The localization at the screen and the emergence of a single dot• The statistical buildup of the interference p

title: Definiteness as Index: A Minimal Coherent Reading of Quantum Outcomes over Spacetime
abstract: A switch by itself has no fact attached to it. Call one position "occupied" and the other "vacant", but nothing in the switch tells you which convention you chose. A state becomes a fact only through comparison. This paper asks what follows if quantum outcomes are understood the same way. The answer is definiteness as index. An outcome is an occupancy: a yes-or-no distinction from a reference, located at a region of spacetime and relative to the measurement made there. It records that an outcome obtained, not which. Records can be read, but every reading makes a new fact for the reader rather than carrying an old one across. The Ground. Spacetime is typed into two primitives: extension, carrying total orientation, and sequence, carrying causal order and time orientation. Neither contains the other's orientation. The Index. Outcomes are occupancies over this ground. Quantum statistics are unchanged. In the Frauchiger-Renner argument, every link in the chain joins laboratories separated by extension, and the step that fails joins a record to a later, incompatible measurement separated by sequence. title: QUANTUM COHERENCE PRESERVING NANOFABRICATION PROCESS WINDOWS AT THE LIMIT Research Architecture Edition v1.0 | STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization ABSTRACT This research architecture examines a testable and deliberately platform-specific question: under which nanofabrication conditions do deposition, lithography, etching, annealing, bonding, cleaning, and other energy-bearing operations satisfy nanoscale geometric tolerances while also preserving relevant quantum function? The central proposal is to qualify fabrication through joint, conditional observations of process state, surface and interface defects, electrical and thermal behavior, and device-specific measurements of coherence, noise, spectroscopy, or photonic performance. Geometry-only yield and aesthetic micrographs are not accepted as proxies for coherence. The monograph treats process qualification as an observationally defined joint event rather than a product of assumed-independent success probabilities. For superconducting circuits, plausible contributors include dielectric two-level-system losses, Purcell channels, nonequilibrium quasiparticles, magnetic defects, and packaging effects. For silicon spin qubits, charge traps, valley splitting, interface disorder, magnetic noise, and control geometry may require different characterization and validation protocols. The proposed framework does not assume that one recipe or coherence metric generalizes across quantum platforms. RESEARCH DESIGN Five research layers structure the inquiry: (1) fabrication-energy and material-state provenance; (2) joint nanoscale, defect, classical-electrical, and quantum-function metrology; (3) conditional acceptance modeling and uncertainty; (4) wafer, apparatus, operator, and material-lot shift tests; and (5) independent blind reproduction and responsible handover. A particularly important possible outcome is a null result: if mature classical metrology predicts final quantum device failure as well as a quantum-aware model, the more elaborate process-window hypothesis is rejected. SCOPE OF THIS EDITION This architecture edition comprises 82 chapters and 410 individually paginated research sections, 30 introductory physics/statistics derivation plates, 200 Research Gates that specify falsifiable experiments, 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos as provisional and revisable design proposals, and 233 indexed equation signposts combining a physical reference with a separately defined research diagnostic. It includes references to established materials-loss and semiconductor-spin-qubit literature and a clear distinction among known physics, engineering models, and untested hypotheses. IMPORTANT SCIENTIFIC AND EDITORIAL LIMITATIONS This is a research architecture, not a report of experiments newly performed for the book and not an independent certification of coherence-preserving process settings. The 233 signposts are 233 indexed composite expressions, not 233 newly discovered independent physical laws. Physical anchor formulas recur where applicable, and model applicability must be checked in every proposed study. The manuscript has not yet met the separately specified 200,000-word substantive-English target: the current paragraph-level count is approximately 121,000 English words, with methodological scaffolds still requiring independent source-rich development. Therefore the edition should not be advertised as a completed 200K+ research monograph. SOURCE LINEAGE The concept extends the author-provided NANO_QUANTUM_FISSION_18_FRONTIER_RESEARCH_FLAGSHIPS v2.0 architecture and identifies Q3 (swarm assembly of quantum devices), Q7 (AI closed-loop quantum-nanofabrication), and Q8 (stigmergic swarm manufacturing under measurement uncertainty) as conceptual mother frameworks. These chapter references are research lineage pointers and do not validate the proposed cross-domain integration. title: Future Perspectives
abstract: This final chapter closes the book by returning to the four core attributes introduced earlier—namely, integrity, vision, emotional intelligence, and adaptability—and examining how the AI era has reshaped each. It argues that, taken together, the four remain the best available summary of what leadership requires, even though the practices through which each is exercised have been transformed. After taking each attribute in turn, the chapter considers several emerging developments likely to shape the next several years, among them agentic AI systems, advanced robotics, quantum computing, the growing concentration of foundational-model capability, and a widening regulatory environment. It then offers a candid account of what a book of this kind can and cannot do, acknowledging that the specific technologies and incidents it references will date faster than the principles it develops. The chapter closes with a reflection on the leadership vocation itself, what it means to lead well under the uncertainty that technology transitions reliably produce, and the leader’s role in shaping the ethical evolution of AI through the rest of the century.

title: Gate-Based Path integral Quantum Control applied to quantum chemistry
abstract: Abstract The Path integral Quantum Control (PiQC) algorithm was recently introduced as a new approach for computing optimal controls in continuous-time open and closed quantum systems. In this work, we adapt the PiQC algorithm to optimize parametrized quantum circuits and refer to this version of PiQC as the Gate-Based PiQC (GB-PiQC) algorithm. We apply GB-PiQC and the original continuous-time version of PiQC for ground state preparation of electronic structure problems, and benchmark them against the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), optimized using the stan- dard Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (SPSA) optimizer, on a set of standard benchmark molecular Hamiltonians. For a fair comparison, we optimize the hyperparameters of the algorithms for each molecule. We find that both PiQC algorithms exhibit greater robustness than SPSA to variations in the target Hamiltonian induced by changes in interatomic distance, when hyperparameters for both methods are fixed at values tuned near equilibrium. Furthermore, PiQC algorithms also achieve superior performance compared to SPSA in most instances under this fixed- hyperparameter setting, particularly at stretched inte

title: Admissibility of "Raw Neural Data" as Criminal Evidence in Criminal Courts: A Jurisprudential, Legal, and Neuroscientific Analysis
abstract: The growing convergence of neuroscience and criminal law, known as neurolaw, has presented a new challenge regarding the admissibility of "raw neural data" (e.g., EEG signals and brain activity) as criminal evidence in judicial proceedings. This study aims to examine the position of these data within Iran’s criminal evidence system, employing a descriptive-analytical method with an interdisciplinary approach to assess the threefold dimensions of scientific, legal, and jurisprudential aspects of the issue. Research findings indicate that from a scientific perspective, raw neural data lacks the necessary validity to serve as independent and conclusive criminal evidence due to high uncertainty, technical challenges in collection and interpretation, and the existence of an "explanatory gap" between purely biological brain activity and criminal intent. From a legal perspective, mandatory reliance on such data contradicts the principles of fair trial, particularly the right to silence, presumption of innocence, and the right to mental privacy. Finally, from a jurisprudential standpoint, the lack of sufficient certainty regarding this evidence renders it subject to the principle of doubt

title: Four-Dimensional Ultrasound Imaging of the Brain
abstract: Visualizing blood flow in the brain is essential for safe neurosurgery and enables functional imaging of brain activity for neuroscience. Ultrasound can measure these hemodynamics at high resolution with portable hardware, but technical constraints have limited existing work to two-dimensional imaging. A single cross-section cannot capture the three-dimensional organization of vascular networks or the distributed patterns of brain activity across the cortex. This project develops volumetric (3D) and four-dimensional (3D+time) ultrasound methods for real-time acquisition and visualization of cerebral blood flow. This includes a 'freehand' 3D reconstruction method designed around existing intra-operative infrastructure, and a complete 4D imaging system that overcomes the hardware and computational challenges of continuous volumetric acquisition. The system is validated during neurosurgery and in functional experiments with awake participants, providing the first demonstration of 4D functional ultrasound in humans.

abstract: This paper critically examines the 2026 analog cognition and consciousness proposal of Miller, Brincat, and Roy and develops an interdisciplinary theoretical integration with Scretching Digital Relativity Psychology (DRP), Digital Relativity Linguistics (DRL), the Scretching Diagnostic Matrix (SDM), and Dynamic SDM (D-SDM). Drawing on empirical research concerning human traveling theta and alpha brain oscillations and ephaptic neural propagation, the study investigates potential relationships among neural wave dynamics, information integration, cognition, consciousness, linguistic interpretation, and psychological state transitions. Novel theoretical contributions include frame-conditioned cognitive interpretation, a normalized frame-sensitivity measure, hierarchical longitudinal state modeling, and a proposed method for testing the incremental predictive value of neural wave features. The analysis distinguishes experimentally supported neuroscience from speculative mechanisms of semantic computation and phenomenal consciousness. title: Engaging Patient Communities in Intracranial Neuroscience Research
abstract: Patients who participate in intracranial neuroscience research make invaluable contributions to our understanding of the brain, accelerating the development of neurotechnological interventions. Engagement of patients as part of this research presents unique challenges, where study goals can be distant from immediate clinical applications and require specialized domain knowledge. Yet methods for meaningfully integrating patient communities as part of these research efforts are essential, as intracranial neuroscience guides the application of artificial intelligence (AI) for understanding and enhancing human cognition. In order to identify what patients consider meaningful research engagement we interviewed individuals who participated in a study during their Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) surgery and attended a group event where they interacted with our research team. Analysis of semi-structured interviews identified four main themes: interest in science and the future of clinical care, contributing to science to improve lives, connecting with others, and accessibility considerations. title: The Whole Brain as a Typed Causal Grammar: Seven Operator Families, Their Joint Feasibility, and the Conditions That Would Refute Them
abstract: This preprint proposes a typed causal grammar for understanding whole-brain function. Rather than identifying the brain with a single algorithm, the framework organizes endogenous causal transformations into seven candidate operator families: inference, control, parameter learning, retention, structural revision, maintenance, and architectural development.The framework specifies intervention-conditioned causal states, operator composition rules, physical implementation constraints, and conditions governing the joint feasibility of neural computations. It develops formal accounts of finite computational concurrency, functional access, causal operator arbitration, adaptive depth, learning credit assignment, memory preservation, and structural properties of neural information.Mathematical derivations and computational constructions establish conditional results and identify limitations of several previously proposed explanatory laws. title: Toward robust, reproducible, and widely accessible intracranial speech brain-computer interfaces: a comprehensive narrative review of neural mechanisms, hardware, algorithms, evaluation, clinical pathways and future directions
abstract: Intracranial speech brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising route for restoring communication in individuals with severe, chronic, and otherwise irreversible motor and speech impairments who cannot communicate adequately using conventional assistive technologies, but clinical translation remains limited by fragmented and heterogeneous evidence, as well as unresolved design trade-offs across neuroscience, hardware, algorithms, validation methods, and clinical integration. This narrative review synthesizes recent progress across four key domains in intracranial speech neuroprosthetics: i) the neural mechanisms underlying overt, attempted (including silent miming and attempts without observable movement), and imagined speech (speech imagery without an attempt to articulate); ii) decision-oriented hardware comparisons of surgically implanted recording modalities, including microelectrode array (MEA), electrocorticography (ECoG), and stereotactic electroencephalography (SEEG); iii) experimental strategies for cross-subject generalization; and iv) advances in neural decoding, including sequence models, attention-based architectures (e.g., transformers), articulatory intermedia

title: A microelectrode array-organoid interface for probing oscillatory behaviors and network-level functional characteristics in mini-brain models
abstract: The convergence of brain organoids and microelectrode arrays (MEAs) represents a transformative advancement in neuroscience, drug discovery, and the emerging field of organoid intelligence. However, the absence of refined analytical methods for extracting reliable and meaningful data continues to impede its full potential. By shifting from single-unit activity to local field potentials, we uncover the predominance of spatiotemporal slow oscillations, particularly within the delta range (<4 Hz), originating intrinsically from the organoids. Throughout development of the organoids, the intensity of oscillatory activity strongly correlates with neuronal maturity and cellular composition. Moreover, electrical or chemical stimulation can lead to rapid changes in oscillatory behavior. In ischemic stroke models, oxygen-glucose deprivation elicits changes in oscillatory patterns, accompanied by elevated delta-band coherence and increased global efficiency. title: Neurological Basis of Learning Among Persons with Intellectual Disability
abstract: Learning is a complex neurobiological process involving the coordinated functioning of multiple brain systems responsible for attention, perception, memory, executive functioning, emotion and motor activity. Contemporary neuroscience has demonstrated that learning is accompanied by changes in neural connectivity and brain function through mechanisms of neuroplasticity. Understanding these mechanisms is particularly important in the context of persons with intellectual disability. In persons with intellectual disability there are differences in cognitive and adaptive functioning that may influence attention, working memory, executive functioning & language, problem-solving and the acquisition & generalization of new skills. This review examines the neurological basis of learning and considers the relevance of Brain-Based Learning (BBL) as a neuroscience-informed educational framework for learners with intellectual disabilities. A narrative review of peer-reviewed research, systematic reviews, meta-analyses and scholarly books was undertaken. title: The glymphatic connectome: a hypothesis for how metabolic waste accumulation may contribute to preferential network degeneration
abstract: Background Neurodegenerative diseases exhibit selective vulnerability, with preferential involvement of highly connected brain regions. This review explores how glymphatic dysfunction and impaired extracellular waste removal may contribute to network-specific degeneration.Methods Narrative review of 2000–2026 literature (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Google Scholar), integrating connectome neuroscience, network analysis, glymphatic physiology, neurovascular biology, and proteinopathy research.Results Hub regions show greater amyloid-β and tau accumulation, suggesting metabolic demand, vascular regulation, and clearance efficiency shape regional vulnerability. Glymphatic transport patterns resemble pathological deposition patterns, supporting a role for impaired clearance in disease progression. Connectome features—centrality, modularity, resilience—may index cumulative molecular, cellular, and vascular dysfunction.Conclusion The Brain Waste Fingerprint hypothesis proposes neurodegeneration arises from interactions among impaired clearance, vascular dysfunction, protein accumulation, and connectome reorganization. title: Fast-Slow Timescales of Allostatic Dysregulation and Chronic Scar Retention in an In Silico Whole-Brain Drosophila Model
abstract: Allostasis maintains physiological viability under environmental stress, but whether acute load and chronic allostatic 'scars' recover on comparable timescales remains an open question in computational neuroscience. We investigate this fast-slow dynamic using Ethosoma, an in-silico Drosophila-inspired whole-brain agent evaluated via a deterministic headless mirror across solvent and resource-scarce baselines. Our simulations reveal that while acute allostatic load recovers completely to zero across all stress durations under solvent conditions, the underlying slow scar variable exhibits persistent retention (94–96% for durations of 600–900 s). We identify a sharp reversible-to-irreversible critical duration threshold (t* = 142.8 s at native heat forcing u = 1.0) and demonstrate that neuromodulatory compensation displays a degenerate low-load basin under continuous stress. Comparative regime analysis confirms that balanced work-respite cycles permit zero-scar recovery, whereas chronic stress and pharmacological monoamine surges incur irreversible saturation (retaining up to 100% of damage). title: EL-RAKHAWI TOPOLOGICAL-PHENOMENAL CONSCIOUSNESS RESONANCE SYSTEM (TPCRS) An Objective, Mathematically Closed Framework for Mapping and Quantifying Subjective Experience via Causal Neural Geometry
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Topological-Phenomenal Consciousness Resonance System (TPCRS) addresses the "Hard Problem of Consciousness" by providing the first mathematically closed framework for objectively quantifying subjective experience. Current neuroscience relies on unreliable behavioral assessments or statistical correlations that cannot distinguish conscious awareness from unconscious processing. TPCRS bridges this gap through a novel neuro-computational architecture integrating high-density quantum-neuroimaging (OPM-MEG for femtotesla magnetic mapping and fNIRS for hemodynamic tracking) with the El-Rakhawi Riemannian Causal Continuum (RCCA). The system calculates the strictly dimensionless Topological-Phenomenal Consciousness Metric (Φ_TCM), bounded between 0 and 1, using a stable multiplicative formulation: Φ_TCM = I_integrated_norm · [(1 + β·C_causal_norm)/(1 + β)] · (1 - S_neural_entropy_norm). This metric quantifies integrated information, causal feedback strength, and inverted dynamical neural noise, avoiding singularities while capturing the geometric complexity of conscious states. title: Hypothesis-Driven Identification of Neural Algorithms With Dynamical Structure-Preserving Manifolds.
abstract: Neuroscience aims to uncover the algorithms by which the brain builds and manipulates rich internal representations of objects, agents, and places. Existing reverse-engineering frameworks remain ineffective for identifying these algorithms. Here, we present Dynamical Structure-Preserving Manifolds (dSPMs)---a novel multilevel reverse-engineering framework that programs, without training, recurrent neural networks to enable hypothesis-driven identification of the brain's algorithms that generate symbolic, structure-preserving representations of the world around. We apply dSPM to identify an algorithm for physical scene prediction in the dorsomedial frontal cortex (DMFC) of macaques intercepting a ball on a Pong-like virtual gameboard. dSPM better explained DMFC than alternatives, made predictions confirmed in neural data, and revealed an algorithm of DMFC that we term 'manifold-based simulation': perceived initial conditions rapidly collapse neural activity onto a low-dimensional manifold whose geometry encodes a physics-based representation of the scene, supporting far-out predictions without traditional next-step simulation. dSPM supports effective exploration of the computational

title: Socially embedded predictive construction: a model of emotional experience
abstract: The dominant view in affective neuroscience has long held that discrete emotional states are universal, biologically fixed, and implemented in dedicated neural circuits. This ‘basic emotions’ framework faces accumulating challenges from neuroimaging meta-analyses, cross-cultural research, and studies of individual variability, while an alternative account—the theory of constructed emotion—holds that emotional experiences are generated by integrating interoceptive predictions, prior conceptual knowledge, and cultural and linguistic context. This Perspective makes three contributions. First, it distinguishes the following three explananda that the debate routinely conflates: rapid, largely subcortically mediated emotional reactions and expressive behaviour; the conscious experience of feeling; and the linguistic categorisation of that experience. Much of the apparent inconsistency of the neuroimaging literature follows from treating these as one phenomenon. title: Un tour por tu mente
abstract: A free book on human behaviour and neuroscience. A practical journey through neuroscience and everyday psychology to see what is behind your thoughts, emotions, and choices. Discover the biases, manipulation tactics, and brain mechanisms that rule your daily life. A simple guide to better understand yourself and take control of your mind.

title: To build health-promoting cities, we have to study the brain where it lives
From Cancer Dependency Maps to Antiviral Structures: Highlights of Recent Advances in Medicine and Biology — A Research Brief on Frontier Progress, September 2026
abstract: The September 2026 issues of a leading international science journal present a rich harvest of biomedical research. This communication selects 34 original research articles with close relevance to medicine and the medical biosciences, and organizes them into six themes: cancer biology and translational oncology; neuroscience and brain disorders across the lifespan; neuroimmunology; metabolism, ageing and the microbiome; infection, haematology and global health; and broader biological advances that underpin future medicine. For each study we provide a concise summary and brief commentary, aiming to offer clinicians and researchers a panoramic view of current progress.

title: The trade-off between fractal morphology and function of Drosophila neurons
abstract: Studying correlation between structure and function in brain networks has long been a central and compelling topic in neuroscience. Using the FlyWire project's fully digitized Drosophila melanogaster brain map, we analyzed a total number of 125330 3D skeletons of neurons from various functional super-classes and classes. By separating axonal and dendritic arbors of individual neurons we compare several morphological and topological properties, including cable length, fractal dimension, number of nodes, maximum width, and tree height. The fractal dimensions of neurons can reach up to 2.4, with dendritic arbors generally more complex than axonal ones, except in the afferent flow, where the situation is reversed. Correlating fractal dimension with cable length reveals that neurons from the same classes cluster in state space. These clusters densify and separate more clearly as we go deeper down the hierarchical annotation schema, indicating that the brain specializes fractal morphology for distinct functional classes.

title: Spatiotemporal AI-based modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain using Seal
The legible body and the language of cognition
abstract: Neural activity moves the body to act on the world, and the world returns through the body to shape neural activity. Systems neuroscience built tasks to cut this loop, isolating low-dimensional, task-related signals and discarding the rest. Tasks suited cognition as classically conceived: general-purpose machinery between sensation and action, performing latent computations abstracted from specific behaviors. With recording techniques limited to tracking individual neurons and discrete actions, it took tasks to make cognition legible by supplying meaning within a limited but generalizable frame. That constraint has been lifting: brain-wide neural recording and rich video tracking of the body can now read neurons and behavior as two facets of one dynamical system. Together they reveal cognitive primitives - decision variables, expected values, hidden states - distributed not only in brain activity but also in subtle face and body movements long dismissed as noise. Cognition, it turns out, is not confined to higher-order cortex; it surfaces in incidental movements carrying latent variables the brain computes - even ones it never acts on.
