This volume transforms an imaginative conversation about one-way tickets, minimum-cost living, autonomous cities, flight, creative freedom, and civilizational succession into an explicit, testable research program. It studies what makes a digital world worth inhabiting: accessible presence, reliable services, useful energy and computing budgets, human agency, protected exit, privacy, social choice, and long-term continuity. The flagship organizing distinction is fundamental. Immersive interface residency is a legitimate subject for engineering and empirical accessibility research. A hypothetical functional digital person is a different claim. title: THE EL-RAKHAWI THEORY OF NEURAL SOVEREIGNTY AND ALGORITHMIC BIOLOGICAL JUSTICE From Artificial Brain Responsibility to Consciousness Rights in the Digital Twin Era Revised Edition with Derived Data Sovereignty and Multi-Modal Consciousness Triad
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Neural Sovereignty and Algorithmic Biological Justice (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23246018, Revised Edition) establishes the first comprehensive framework for protecting cognitive and biological sovereignty in the AI era, spanning four pillars: (1) Algorithmic Justice & Forensic Neuroscience — governing artificial brain responsibility, fMRI evidence, and pre-crime ethics; (2) Cyber-Medicine & Digital Biology — regulating digital twins, CRISPR-AI, and genomic encryption; (3) BCI & IP — defining neural rights and criminalizing neural hacking; (4) Hybrid Cognition — addressing biocomputers' legal status. Three revolutionary enhancements: (1) **Derived Neuro-Behavioral Data Sovereignty** — closing the loophole where companies claim ownership of patterns derived from users' neural data; (2) **Multi-Modal Consciousness Triad** — requiring integrated information (Phi), goal-directed adaptive behavior, AND self-report correlates simultaneously for legal personhood; (3) **Tiered Sovereign Implementation Protocol** — phased pathway enabling Global South compliance. title: Looking Inside LLMs: Small-World Connectivity as a Signature of Reasoning Performance
abstract: Understanding large language model (LLM) reasoning requires looking beyond behavioral performance to examine how reasoning ability is reflected in internal organization. Inspired by neuroscience findings linking higher intelligence to stronger small-world organization in functional brain networks, we investigate small-world connectivity as a structural signature of LLM reasoning. We construct functional graphs from attention-head activation similarities and find that a higher small-world index (SWI), capturing local clustering and short global paths, consistently correlates with better fluid reasoning performance across models and training checkpoints. Since local clustering is central to small-world organization, we further examine how heads important for model performance connect within and across communities. We find that these heads tend to have a larger share of connection weight within their own communities (high core scores) and a more concentrated weight distribution across communities (low bridge scores). title: Nobel Laureates vs Odam Tili: Optogenetics, Meaning, and the Origin of Language
abstract: This video presents a critical scientific comparison between the 2026 Nobel Prize-winning work on optogenetics and the Odam Tili theory developed by Dr. Mahmudjon Kuchkarov. The Nobel-recognized discoveries associated with Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel established powerful methods for controlling defined neural circuits through light-sensitive ion channels. These advances transformed modern neuroscience by allowing researchers to test causal relationships between neural activity, behavior, memory, perception, and emotion. The central question of this video, however, lies beyond neural control itself: Does identifying or manipulating the neural circuitry associated with a behavior explain how semantic meaning originally emerged? The Odam Tili framework proposes that the origin of meaning should be investigated through the full embodied chain: physical event → perception → bodily response → neural encoding → vocal or motor expression → repetition → stable association → meaning → language. title: Ethical Issues of Modern Neurotechnology
abstract: Abstract Neuroethics has been described as the study of the ethical, legal, and social implications of neuroscience and neurotechnology. There have been concerns over the application of optogenetics for psychiatric conditions in humans, if and when that day occurs. For example, opinions differ on the question of modifying memory and the possible ethical concerns of memory manipulation. There is also some uneasiness about the ethics of experimenting with human brain tissue in the context of cerebral organoids and what some call brain chimeras—transplanted human neural organoids in nonhuman animals. This chapter introduces the NeuroRights Foundation whose goal is to promote research, advocacy, and outreach on neurorights, our right to mental privacy—so that no one decodes our mental activity without our consent. The combination of systemic delivery of microbial opsins and the specific deployment of the opsin ChRmine from outside the skull suggests that optogenetic neuromodulation of nonhuman primates without the need for any intracranial surgery is closer than has previously been the case. title: Trait-relevant movies amplify neuroticism-associated brain responses
abstract: High neuroticism is a risk factor for mental disorders. Understanding whether individuals share a common foundation in brain function underlying neuroticism is therefore an essential goal of neuroscience. We applied Inter-Subject Representational Similarity Analysis on data from 174 Human Connectome Project participants to investigate if their similarity in neuroticism is reflected in their similarity of fMRI-recorded brain activity during movie watching. To test behavioral personality theories that consider trait expression as dependent on situational context, we examined whether brain-trait representational similarity varied between trait-relevant and trait-irrelevant movie scenes (independently rated, N = 86). Higher neuroticism was associated with greater heterogeneity in brain responses, a pattern that was particularly pronounced during trait-relevant scenes. Our study informs dimensional conceptualizations of psychopathology viewing neuroticism as risk factor and extends behavioral personality theories to the level of brain function. Broadly, it highlights the value of naturalistic imaging and underscores the importance of stimulus selection when investigating brain-behavior

title: Optogenetics and Modern Neurotechnology
abstract: Abstract Optogenetics is a transformational technology in neuroscience that allows the control of neural circuits in real time in awake, behaving animals and thus begins the era of causal neuroscience: making it possible to manipulate the brain and record an animal’s response rather than only observing and making inferences. Optogenetics can reproducibly turn on and turn off neural function with cell-specific, millisecond precision commensurate with how the brain works. The new technology includes the insertion into cells of genes that bestow light responsiveness to the proteins they produce (notably, Channelrhodopsins), the means for delivering light deep into living, freely moving animals, the targeting of light-sensitivity only to cells of interest, and ways for evaluating the effects of this optical control on behavior. Optogenetic studies have contributed to our understanding of psychiatric illnesses such as anxiety, depression, addiction, and autism as well as neurodegenerative disease in the form of Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s. Optogenetic research has also revealed a new understanding of normal brain functions. What sets sleep/wake cycles? How do we manage to stay hydrated?

title: The Double Empathy Problem and Social Connections
abstract: This chapter applies a developmental framework to examine how social competence shapes mental health and subjective well-being in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Grounded in the double empathy problem (DEP)—a conceptual model that reframes social difficulties as reciprocal misunderstandings between ASD and non-ASD individuals—we challenge deficit-based conceptions of autism and emphasize the co-constructed nature of communication barriers. We review evidence linking these mutual misattunements to increased risks of loneliness, psychological distress, and suicidality in ASD populations. Drawing on developmental neuroscience and social psychology, we explore how early relational experiences, brain development, and environmental expectations interact to shape long-term communication patterns and social outcomes. Interventions consistent with DEP principles are examined for their capacity to foster mutual empathy, strengthen therapeutic alliances, reduce psychiatric risk, and promote social competence. These interventions span multiple approaches and share a focus on enhancing social understanding through relationship-based, inclusive, and context-sensitive strategies.

title: Profile of Michael N. Shadlen
abstract: Neuroscientist and neurologist Michael N. Shadlen is a world leader in the neurobiology of decision-making, a field of study he helped establish. His research explores higher brain functions-memory retrieval, reasoning, and multitasking, among others-that he theorizes share underlying mechanisms. His work suggests that a holy grail of neuroscience-the "hard problem" of consciousness, or the mechanism(s) by which physical brain operations are translated into lived experiences-could be resolved. Shadlen's Inaugural Article explains what distinguishes conscious from nonconscious thought.

title: The Brain Is Fascinating but Formidable
abstract: Abstract Modern neuroscience arose around 1900 after a ferocious, decades-long debate: was the nervous system made up of discrete, individual neurons, or were neurons contiguous with one another, part of a single enormous network? Ultimately, the scientific world became convinced that the neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, one of the tenets of the so-called neuron doctrine. Another point of contention was the existence of dendritic spines; though many scientists had seen them through their microscopes, they dismissed them as staining artifacts. They were wrong, and proof of the reality of dendritic spines was finally accepted. Now, more than 100 years later, optogenetics uses light to modify the activity of neural circuits. This has led to a paradigm shift from neurons to neural circuits as the new basic unit of inquiry. The chapter also introduces a discussion of the relevance of (nonhuman) animal studies to humans as well as the significance of nonhuman primates in optogenetics research.

title: Optogenetics—Neurotechnology’s New Discovery Tool
abstract: Abstract In the early years of the twenty-first century, a new technology in neuroscience has emerged to unveil the causal relationship between the activity of specific neurons and the behaviors they control; that technology is called optogenetics. Optogenetics is a made-up word: “opto-” refers to proteins that respond to light; “-genetics” refers to the genes that produce these proteins. Optogenetics is a combination of optics and genetics to control well-defined events within specific cells of living tissue, the better to understand the mechanistic origins of those events. This introduction outlines the broad methods used in optogenetics and acquaints the reader with microbes such as archaea that are crucial to optogenetic experiments. The introduction also emphasizes that by both measuring and manipulating a neuron’s pattern of firing action potentials (voltage spikes), optogenetics enables scientists to both “read” and “write” the neural code—the language of the brain. Additionally, this introductory section outlines the roadmap for the rest of the book.

title: Investigation of the Prolonged Impact of Severe Socioeconomic Hardship and Mother's Perceived Social Support on Neurocognitive Development in Young Children in the Rural Ecuadorian Amazon
abstract: Children living in conditions of severe socioeconomic (SES) hardship are at elevated risk for neurocognitive delays, yet most developmental neuroscience research has focused on children in high-income, Western populations, limiting our understanding of diverse developmental contexts. This study examined maternal perceived social support as a potential buffer against the stressors associated with SES hardship on child neurocognitive development in a longitudinal sample of Indigenous families in the rural Ecuadorian Amazon. Twenty-eight children (M age = 28.02 months at T1; 57.6 months at T2) participated in the study completing an assessment of early cognitive ability at T1 and an inhibition task while functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measured cortical activation at T2. A three-level linear mixed model revealed a significant interaction between early cognitive ability and maternal perceived social support on functional activation. Specifically, children of mothers with high social support showed no association between early cognitive ability and cortical activation, while those with low support exhibited atypical patterns (hyper- or hypoactivation), suggesting that incr

title: Diagnostic Criteria for Neurogenic Pulmonary Edema in Neurosurgical Patients: A Systematic Scoping Review of Definitional Heterogeneity
abstract: Protocol for a systematic scoping review mapping the diagnostic criteria and case definitions used for neurogenic pulmonary edema (NPE) in adult neurosurgical patients (subarachnoid hemorrhage, traumatic brain injury, intracerebral hemorrhage, spinal cord injury, hydrocephalus, neurosurgical procedures and seizures in the context of neurosurgical conditions). Studies will be classified as using explicit, partially explicit, implicit or no reported diagnostic criteria, and the frequency of individual diagnostic components will be charted. The review follows PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S and is conducted as a master's thesis in the Postgraduate Programme "Basic and Applied Neurosciences", School of Medicine, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Greece. The original protocol is written in Greek (NPE_Protocol_GR.pdf). An English translation is provided for accessibility (NPE_Protocol_EN.pdf). In case of discrepancy, the Greek version prevails.

title: The Main Line of Emotion Formation: A Benefit–Harm Signal Account
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the nature of emotion and the underlying mechanism of its formation. It proposes that emotion is an individual's instinctive psychological reaction to a benefit-harm signal, representing the core expression of the human drive to seek benefit and avoid harm. The study establishes a clear, two-stage "main line" of emotion formation: The First Stage: The brain evaluates encounters or thoughts ("matters") through cognitive judgment to generate a benefit-harm signal, and determines whether that signal is attended to based on the "importance-weighting" and "importance-following" principles. The Second Stage: The "signal-response system" (a physiological functional structure) reacts instinctively to the attended benefit-harm signal, converting it directly into the corresponding psychological feeling and physiological reaction. Furthermore, the paper highlights that while physiological functional systems act as the execution "transducer" in converting signals to emotional outcomes, the benefit-harm signal itself is the sole direct cause of emotion. The persistence of emotion depends entirely on sustained attention to this signal. By clarifying these mechanisms,

title: A multi-scenario EEG dataset for auditory attention decoding in naturalistic multi-talker environments
abstract: Understanding how the brain selectively follows relevant speech amid competing voices is a central challenge in auditory neuroscience and a key step toward neuro-steered hearing technologies. However, most open-source Electroencephalography (EEG) datasets for Auditory Attention Decoding (AAD) use idealized single-competing-talker paradigms that oversimplify the acoustic, spatial, and semantic structure of everyday communication. To capture this ecological complexity, we introduce the SoundBubble-EEG dataset: a high-density 128-channel EEG resource comprising more than 25 hours of recordings from 30 participants. The paradigm requires listeners to selectively attend to a dynamic target speaker group, a designated "sound bubble", amid competing multi-speaker distractor bubbles across three realistic scenarios: a restaurant, a home TV viewing, and a meeting discussion. By bridging the gap between constrained laboratory protocols and real-world auditory scenes, this dataset enables investigations of multi-talker speech comprehension, neural speech tracking, and cross-scenario generalization. It also provides a benchmark for AAD algorithms under realistic acoustic and semantic variabili

title: Therapeutic Validity in Adaptive Deep Brain Stimulation: Temporal Change, Closed-Loop Intervention, and the Need for Reassessment
abstract: Adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS) is a closed-loop neurotechnology in which recorded neural activity is used to adjust stimulation in response to changing physiological states. In Parkinson’s disease, subthalamic nucleus (STN) beta-band activity is among the principal physiological signals investigated for this purpose. Longitudinal studies, however, indicate that some features of STN beta activity can exhibit both substantial stability and clinically relevant changes associated with postoperative recovery, medication, stimulation, and clinical state. These findings raise a question that predictive performance alone cannot resolve: when does a neural signal remain therapeutically valid as a target for adaptive intervention? This paper argues that predictive validity is not equivalent to therapeutic validity. The distinction is particularly important in aDBS because the intervention is part of the measurement environment: stimulation alters the neural activity from which subsequent measurements and control decisions are derived. A biomarker may therefore remain measurable and predictive while the physiological, clinical, or therapeutic relationship that gives it significance ch

title: CircuitATLAS: Agentic reasoning over a systems neuroscience knowledge graph for target discovery in circuitopathies
abstract: Drug discovery for neurological disease has traditionally centered on the molecules altered by disease. But the molecules that cause pathology are not necessarily the best points from which to reverse it. Here, we ask which otherwise unaltered molecular control points can be engaged to restore pathological neural circuits toward functional states. We present CircuitATLAS, a provenance-grounded systems-neuroscience knowledge graph and agentic framework for target discovery in circuitopathies. It structures literature-derived relationships across diseases, phenotypes, electrophysiology, circuits, brain regions, cell types and molecular effectors, while deliberately excluding direct disease-gene and disease-protein edges to reduce shortcut reasoning. The graph contains 3.83 million nodes and 7.66 million edges, including 5.31 million LLM-extracted relations, and incorporates structured datasets such as the Human Cell Atlas and new multimodal in vivo measurements. We then introduce an agentic workflow that reasons from measurable disease phenotypes through their circuit and cellular substrates to molecular interventions, therapeutic feasibility and clinical constraints. Finally, we int

abstract: Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim, al-Malik, al-Quddus, as-Salam This is dedicated to my friend Fatima, who is the inspiration for this work along with Allah swt. May Allah accept our intentions for a better universe, ameen. title: 人体智能假说 ——基于智慧物质的生命本体与智能层级理论模型
abstract: 现代生命科学、神经科学、意识哲学与人工智能研究仍然存在若干底层理论盲区:生命自主调控的本体主体尚不明确;意识与潜意识的生成机制缺乏统一解释框架;身心重症的发生机理难以实现跨学科自洽;物种智能梯度、人类个体禀赋差异缺少本体层面阐释;人机智能之间存在本体鸿沟;衰老深层机理有待进一步补充。同时,现有主流理论难以统一解释部分临床与社会观察现象,如百岁群体普遍的心念稳态特征、部分肿瘤患者长期带瘤生存、人类依靠信念突破生理极限等。 针对上述跨学科矛盾,本文提出智慧物质本体概念,构建《人体智能假说》理论模型。假说认为,宇宙弥散分布一类具备自主性、自组织性、层级性、载体选择偏好的本源生命智能基质,定义为智慧物质;该基质仅可入驻活体生命系统,无法进驻非生命载体。本文区分控制主体(智慧物质)与肉体执行主体(大脑、器官),人体智能的主体是智慧物质,智慧物质组织了人体的自动化系统,大脑仅作为信号中转接口与执行单元。人类通过DNA获得基础完整但层级有限的智慧物质基底;后天依靠正向心念、学习、行为与信念能量,可吸纳、改良智慧物质,提升智能层级,维持生命稳态。人体不同生理系统对应智慧物质子域团体;疾病划分为外部扰动引发的轻症与智慧物质结构性缺损导致的重症,临床突发危重疾病多为子域损伤累积至临界阈值后的外在表现。 百岁人群、带瘤生存、意志突破生理极限等现象为本假说的现象级佐证,稳定心念与正向行为可修复智慧物质本体,延缓衰老,拓展生命边界。智慧物质主导的生命自动化属于带有原生觉知的生命级自动化,区别于机器程序自动化;潜意识、直觉、灵感属于智慧物质的基础表现。人工智能不具备智慧物质本体、完整生命演化链条与原生觉知,因此无法等价或超越人类本源生物智能。人脑(大脑显意识层面)在显性数据存储与符号运算处理上弱于AI,但AI局限于人类整理完成的符号数据集,难以完成范式级根本突破。需要明确区分大脑显意识算力与智慧物质主导的人体自动化智能系统的信息处理能力:智慧物质驱动的生命自动化系统,持续完成全身约37万亿细胞的实时感知、海量并行调控、动态纠错以及个体全生命周期生命信息沉淀;这套生命自动化系统拥有远超现有AI、面向活体生命的综合并行处理算力,其数据存量、多维度并行处理规模、实时自适应的复杂程度,是现有AI尚无法企及、难以对标复刻的。注:人工智能符号浮点运算指标不能直接与生命本体综合处理能力做简单数值等价换算,两类计算范式存在本质差异。智慧物质驱动人类生成全新概念、底层理论等本源创造,构成人类独有的高阶优势。对爱因斯坦离体大脑切片的解剖研究,因生命终结后智慧物质与肉体解离,标本不再承载生前高阶智慧本体,因此脑组织解剖无法解释质能方程E=mc²这类划时代发现。智慧物质冲破人脑后天逻辑形成的知识禁锢,其内在动力来源于本体意识范畴内生的意志力、坚定性与专注性。 衰老的本体表现为肉体DNA载体承载能力衰减叠加智慧

title: Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Anxiety: Translating Brain–Behavior Models into Scalable Clinical Tools
abstract: Advances in affective and systems neuroscience have clarified how distributed brain networks encode threat processing, generate bodily arousal, and shape cognitive and behavioral features of anxiety disorders. However, this progress has not been systematically translated into patient-facing educational tools or clinical care. Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation (NIPE) extends conventional psychoeducation by incorporating brain-based explanations of symptoms and treatment, while also structuring materials to engage attention, memory, and self-referential processing. Emerging work suggests NIPE may enhance insight, reduce stigma, and improve treatment engagement and adherence. NIPE aims to optimize both the content (what is taught) and structure (how it is delivered) of psychoeducation to engage emotional and motivational aspects of learning. Building on recent NIPE frameworks applied to other psychiatric conditions (e.g., addiction), here we extend this approach to anxiety disorders. We developed two cartoon-based NIPE posters within an anxiety disorders specialty clinic to operationalize core brain–behavior processes in anxiety. title: Dissociable neural oscillations track subjective value under risk and ambiguity
abstract: How the brain values uncertain prospects and translates them into choices is a central question in decision neuroscience. Current accounts propose that decisions under risk and ambiguity share a valuation process that integrates outcome with probability information, with ambiguity additionally requiring evaluation of the uncertainty about the probabilities themselves. Here we used computational modeling to estimate trial-wise subjective value and tested whether it was tracked by shared or distinct neural dynamics under risk and ambiguity. Participants accepted or rejected risky and ambiguous monetary gambles while we recorded neural activity using electroencephalography (Experiment 1) and magnetoencephalography (Experiment 2). Across both experiments, alpha-band (9–14 Hz) activity localized to the precuneus and superior parietal cortex tracked subjective value under both risk and ambiguity. By contrast, delta-band (1–3 Hz) activity localized to the ventromedial prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortices tracked subjective value only under ambiguity. title: Project Sovereign Genesis: The Sugarcane Paradigm: A Manifesto on the Chemically Induced Anthropocene A multi-generational analysis of sucrose-driven metabolic, genetic, and cognitive manipulation, with engineering strategies for an industrialized pivot.
abstract: This comprehensive document functions as an academic-style manifesto exploring the socio-biological history and industrial transformation of sugarcane. It tracks how the 400-year transition from localized, whole-plant chewing to the industrial mass crystallization of sucrose has systematically altered human biology. The manifesto synthesises cutting-edge research across neuroscience, endocrinology, epigenetics, and evolutionary biology to detail how refined sugars drive global weight gain, structural brain decline ("Type 3 Diabetes"), and societal aggression via ancestral survival pathways. Concluding with a bold structural pivot, the document outlines an engineering blueprint to completely divert sugarcane from the human food supply into carbon-negative advanced manufacturing (cellulose nanofibrils, bio-rubbers, and electronics) supported by a passive, self-sustaining biomimetic atmospheric water harvesting system (utilising basalt engines, triskele spiral geometries, and dragonfly wing micro-textures).

title: RESEARCH GATE NEUROSCIENCE AT THE LIMIT Researchable Unknowns, Testable Gates & Cumulative Neural Evidence as Successor-Ready Scientific Infrastructure
abstract: RESEARCH GATE NEUROSCIENCE AT THE LIMIT Researchable Unknowns, Testable Gates & Cumulative Neural Evidence as Successor-Ready Scientific Infrastructure RESEARCH GATE NEUROSCIENCE AT THE LIMIT develops a research architecture for treating unresolved neuroscience questions as durable, testable, and successor-ready scientific objects. Rather than leaving important uncertainties as one-line “future work” statements at the end of papers, the book asks how an unknown can be given enough structure to remain identifiable across experiments, laboratories, devices, models, institutions, and generations of researchers. Its central three-coupling is: Researchable Unknown x Testable Gate x Cumulative Neural Evidence The book proposes the heuristic: RGN = (U_r x G_t x E_c x H_o) / (1 + V_q + C_s + F_f) This relation is a book-defined research scaffold, not a natural law, clinical score, or universally validated metric. title: Dataset for Naturalistic spatial education engages distinct neural processes for mental rotation, cognitive load, and linguistic demands.
abstract: Anonymized fMRI and behavioral data for "Naturalistic spatial education engages distinct neural processes for mental rotation, cognitive load, and linguistic demands." The dataset behaviorNormalized_event_PSC_Content includes individual subject percent signal change for each ROI/network, instructional content coding, and behavior scores. Group_Average_Correlation_Table_FisherTransformed_Labeled contains the group average z-scores between ROIs used for connectivity and network analyses, and logWB_summary_ROI_posonly contains the data for within-between ratio figures. Note, Text Density corresponds to Linguistic Density, Motor corresponds to Premotor, and LBroca corresponds to LIFG in the main text. ABSTRACT: Neuroscience studies typically isolate spatial cognition using simplified tasks targeting a single cognitive process. However, during formal spatial education, the brain rarely performs one cognitive operation at a time. Here, we used fMRI to assess neural systems involved in dynamically processing an educational spatial-visualization lesson. title: SELF-REVISING BCI RESEARCH GRAMMARS AT THE LIMIT Rule Revision, Neural Evidence & Continuity Memory for Versioned, Auditable, Rollback-Capable Brain-Computer Interface Science
abstract: SELF-REVISING BCI RESEARCH GRAMMARS AT THE LIMIT Rule Revision, Neural Evidence & Continuity Memory for Versioned, Auditable, Rollback-Capable Brain-Computer Interface Science SELF-REVISING BCI RESEARCH GRAMMARS AT THE LIMIT develops a research architecture for placing the rules of brain-computer interface science themselves under version control. Instead of treating measurement rules, calibration rules, model-comparison rules, intervention rules, longitudinal baseline rules, and governance rules as static background assumptions, the book asks how those rules can evolve under evidence and failure while preserving comparability, auditability, rights, continuity memory, and a reversible path to earlier versions. Its central three-coupling is: Rule Revision x Neural Evidence x Continuity Memory The book proposes the heuristic: SRG = (R_v x E_n x M_c x A_u) / (1 + R_d + O_p + L_f) This relation is a book-defined research scaffold, not a natural law, clinical score, or universally validated metric. title: Editorial: Socio-legal, ethical, technical and medical considerations on neuroprivacy and brain-machine interaction technologies in the era of A.I.
abstract: The rapid convergence of neurotechnology and artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond the isolation of clinical laboratories and IT factories to become a transformative force capable, in the long-term, of redefining the human experience. In the wake of brain-machine interaction technologies, human and cognitive enhancement and even transhumanism perspectives, this evolution has given rise to the concept of the hybrid mind, a state where biological cognitive systems merge seamlessly with artificial ones, blurring traditional boundaries of identity, agency, autonomy, and consciousness. While these advances offer unprecedented potential to restore sensory and motor functions, they simultaneously challenge our foundational understandings of cognitive liberty, mental integrity, neuroethics and conventional privacy paradigms. This Research Topic, hosted by Frontiers in Human Dynamics -Digital Impacts and cross-listed across seven participating journals, includingFrontiers in Sociology, Neurology, and Neurorobotics, serves as a multidisciplinary research collection that aims to connect different fields and backgrounds with a common frame. title: Spatiotemporal encoding signatures of covert speech revealed by source-localized EEG and fMRI
abstract: Covert speech, the silent production of words without overt articulation, is fundamental to human cognition and a potential target for restoring communication in speech-impaired populations. Yet where, when, and how the human brain represents specific phrase content during covert speech remains largely unresolved. Here, we combine source-localized EEG (n = 57) with fMRI validation in the same cohort (n = 49) to map the encoding of five covert command phrases. Phrase-discriminative activity is concentrated before estimated articulation onset, peaking at 200–400 ms and strongest in the theta band. Cross-modal representational similarity analysis reveals convergent EEG–fMRI phrase representations in left sensorimotor cortex, while phase-lag connectivity identifies left postcentral gyrus as a phrase-sensitive functional hub within a parietal-somatosensory-temporal sequence during the speech planning period. Beyond these group-level signatures, individual-specific encoding patterns substantially exceed group-average effects. These findings provide a temporally precise, cross-validated cortical map of covert speech and identify targets for speech neuroscience and non-invasive brain-compu

title: Neuromorphic Intelligence: Translating Brain Mechanisms into AI Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence has experienced tremendous success over the years. This is despite the fact that conventional deep learning models have shortcomings when it comes to matters of energy efficiency, adaptability, temporal computation, and their alignment with biological processes. The human brain, on the other hand, demonstrates highly efficient, strong, and adaptive intelligence processes via event-driven neural communication and local learning processes. There has since been a growing focus on the concept of neuromorphic intelligence. This involves the use of biological processes for intelligence AI models. This paper presents a systematically arranged review of neuromorphic intelligence and its approaches using biological brain mechanisms such as spiking neural communication, neural coding schemes, and synaptic plasticity. Here, advanced biologically inspired models such as spiking neural networks would be examined with respect to their learning procedures, characteristics, and advantages over artificial neural networks. title: Task structure and construct validity in the neurobiology of trust: A systematic structural synthesis
Attachment-Informed Leadership (AIL): A New Leadership Framework based on Attachment Theory and Social Neuroscience
abstract: Leadership research has catalogued many styles, among them transformational, authentic and servant leadership, but has offered few accounts of the regulatory mechanisms through which leader-follower relationships operate. We propose that attachment, understood through social neuroscience, supplies one such mechanism. Humans regulate environmental demands relationally, and attachment organises this social regulation of a finite bioenergetic budget under challenge. When followers face threat, dependence or uncertainty, this relationship can come to serve attachment functions, and the leader's reliability as a security provider bears on how much of followers' regulatory resources remains available for work. Building on the Social Neuroscience of Human Attachment (SoNeAt), we develop an attachment-informed leadership (AIL) framework spanning social allostasis, attachment and caregiving, predictive regulation and biobehavioural synchrony. We position AIL relative to evolutionary accounts of leadership and derive nine propositions that distinguish attachment processes from exchange, trust and identification, measurable from self-report to physiology and brain activity.

title: The Role of A Surgeon in Restoring the Senses & in Biomedical Engineering
abstract: This review is based on my 2025 Jepson Lecture and outlines my personal journey to restore hearing in people with a severe sensorineural hearing loss. My dream started as a 5-year-old as I told my kindergarten teacher when I grow up 'I want to fix ears' because my father is deaf. The journey resulted in a career in surgery followed by auditory neuroscience, engineering and audiology. While the key stages in the development of the multi-channel cochlear implant are highlighted, their importance in discovering the first restoration of a human sense, and in understanding brain function is presented as well. The discoveries also underpin the development of modern neural interfaces in general that restore human function. And so, a new discipline in biomedical engineering has emerged.

title: The Neurocognitive Architecture of Language: A Psycholinguistic Exploration of the Reciprocal Relationship between the Human Brain and Linguistic Processing
abstract: Language represents one of the most complex cognitive abilities of the human species, emerging from the continuous interaction between biological structures, neural mechanisms, and environmental experiences. This theoretical paper explores the reciprocal relationship between the human brain and linguistic processing from a psycholinguistic perspective. It examines the neurological foundations of language, including classical localization models associated with Broca’s and Wernicke’s areas, as well as contemporary perspectives that emphasize distributed neural networks. The discussion further considers language acquisition, neuroplasticity, bilingualism, and the influence of linguistic experience on cognition, decision-making, and moral interpretation. In addition, the paper explores conceptual connections between contemporary psycholinguistic research and Islamic perspectives on human linguistic capacity, symbolic representation, and cognitive responsibility. By integrating insights from cognitive neuroscience, psycholinguistics, and cultural perspectives, this study argues that language is not merely a communication system but a dynamic cognitive phenomenon that both emerges from

title: Neuro-Protective Criminal Justice: A New Paradigm For Child Criminal Responsibility And Protection
abstract: Contemporary criminal justice systems predominantly assess child criminal responsibility through fixed age thresholds and formal legal capacity while often disregarding neuroscientific evidence concerning brain development, impulse regulation, and limited decision making capacity. This article proposes neuro protective criminal justice that integrates neuroscience, neurolaw, and child centered human rights into criminal law policy. The study aims to examine the conceptual foundation of neuro protective criminal justice, analyze child criminal liability under Indonesian law, and develop a model of neurological protection within the child criminal justice system. This research employs a normative juridical method using statutory, conceptual, and comparative approach. The analysis demonstrates that age based responsibility doesn’t adequately reflect children’s vulnerability to social and structural influences. It argues for a framework that prioritizes rehabilitation, prevention of neurological and psychological harm, and long term developmental well being through restorative justice, therapeutic interventions, and diversion. title: Optogenetics wins the Nobel – one neuroscience breakthrough in a line of technological innovations helping scientists map and control the brain
Environmental Neurotoxicants And Autism Spectrum Disorder: From Toxic Metals And Pesticides To Neuroimmune Dysregulation Narrative Review
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder resulting from interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental factors during critical periods of brain development. Increasing evidence implicates environmental neurotoxicants, particularly toxic metals and pesticides, in ASD risk through oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, blood–brain barrier impairment, epigenetic alterations, and persistent neuroinflammation. Neuroimmune dysregulation, including chronic microglial and astrocyte activation, cytokine imbalance, and altered peripheral immune responses, may contribute to abnormal neuronal development and connectivity. These effects may be amplified by gene–environment interactions, increasing individual susceptibility. This review summarizes epidemiological and experimental evidence linking toxic metals and pesticides to ASD, with emphasis on molecular and neuroimmune mechanisms, emerging biomarkers, and preventive strategies. Despite advances in understanding these pathways, causal relationships and clinical translation remain challenging. Integrating epidemiology, toxicology, molecular neuroscience, and multi-omics approaches may help i

title: Single-cell and network voltage imaging in acute brain slices: an updated guideline
abstract: Membrane potential (or voltage) imaging in acute brain slices is widely used in fundamental and applied neuroscience even in an age characterised by the surge of in-vivo recording. This optical method remarkably increased its ability in providing key information both at the level of single cell and at the level of populations and networks. But, more importantly, technical progresses occurred in the last two decades enlarged the potential pool of voltage imaging users from relatively few specialists to scientists in many fields including those working in industry. This review aims at offering an updated guideline for anyone wishing to perform voltage imaging in brain slices. We analyse the technical and practical aspects to consider in the choice between using an organic voltage sensitive dye (VSD) or a genetically encoded voltage indicator (GEVI). We then examine advantages and disadvantages of using the straightforward approach of wide-field illumination, versus other methods providing higher spatial resolution and optical sectioning. Other choices are analysed in particular for users adopting VSDs who are confronted with the decision of recording from single neurons or from neuro

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF APPLIED NEUROPLASTICITY From Molecular Mechanisms to Human Brain Rewiring A Comprehensive Scientific Framework for Understanding, Measuring, and Harnessing the Brain's Capacity for Transformation
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Doctrine of Applied Neuroplasticity presents a groundbreaking scientific framework bridging molecular neuroscience, cellular dynamics, and systems-level brain reorganization into actionable protocols for cognitive enhancement and neurological rehabilitation. It introduces five foundational pillars: the molecular architecture of synaptic plasticity, cellular structural dynamics including neurogenesis, large-scale neural network reorganization, the novel El-Rakhawi Neuroplasticity Index (ENI) for quantifying individual brain adaptability, and evidence-based clinical protocols. These offer targeted interventions for cognitive enhancement, stroke recovery, psychiatric disorders, cognitive aging, and addiction. Grounded in peer-reviewed studies, this doctrine transforms theoretical neuroplasticity into a practical science, empowering clinicians and individuals to harness the brain's lifelong capacity for rewiring. Released under the Ferial Zayed Humanitarian License, it ensures this transformative knowledge remains accessible to all. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23150402.

title: Biological Psychology, Neuroscience, and Digital Self Representation in DRP and DRL
abstract: This conceptual paper connects biological psychology and neuroscience with Digital Relativity Psychology (DRP) and Digital Relativity Linguistics (DRL) to examine how biological and digital systems represent, transmit, and interpret information. Human neural communication combines continuous electrochemical processes with discrete action potentials and synaptic events, whereas digital systems process information through engineered physical states and computational architectures. Their common dependence on physical signaling provides a useful basis for interface research, but does not imply equivalent organization, cognition, identity, or consciousness. The paper examines brain–computer interfaces, avatars, human digital twins, and digital alter egos as experimental and conceptual tools for investigating agency, body ownership, self-reference, source attribution, identity continuity, and conscious report. It distinguishes established findings in neuroscience and interface research from proposed DRP and DRL extensions, and uses formal illustrations to clarify membrane dynamics, signal sampling, model fidelity, representation, and biological–digital identity relations. title: A Novel Mathematical Framework for Multi-Scale Neural Dynamics: Integrating Stochastic Differential Equations with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: The integration of multi-scale neural dynamics remains a fundamental challenge in computational neuroscience. This paper introduces a novel mathematical framework that integrates stochastic differential equations with graph neural networks to model multi-scale brain dynamics. Our approach treats neural activity, synaptic efficacy, and network topology as co-evolving dynamical variables governed by coupled equations spanning microscopic, mesoscopic, and macroscopic scales. The framework's multi-level architecture combines stochastic differential equations for microscopic neural dynamics with biologically realistic noise; activity-dependent plasticity rules for mesoscopic connectivity evolution; and graph neural networks for macroscopic network property learning. Through rigorous mathematical analysis, we derive stability conditions and identify critical bifurcation points governing cross-scale interactions. We introduce a novel mathematical framework unifying stochastic differential equations with graph neural networks to model hierarchical brain dynamics. title: Integrated Hippocampal Tissue Image Analysis Using Generative and Foundation Models
abstract: Fluorescent immunohistochemistry tissue imaging is an important tool for studying brain structure, neuronal activity, and molecular expression within anatomically defined regions. In hippocampal research, region-specific analysis is particularly important because hippocampal subregions have distinct structural and functional roles in memory, plasticity, and neurological disease. Automated segmentation, semantic identification, and cellular quantification of these tissue images therefore represent important problems in computational neuroscience and biomedical image analysis. Despite advances in deep learning-based biomedical image analysis, automated analysis of hippocampal fluorescent immunohistochemistry images remains challenging. Existing methods primarily focus on generic medical image segmentation, MRI-based hippocampal analysis, or cell-level detection without explicitly modeling hippocampal subregion structure. Consequently, integrated computational frameworks that segment hippocampal subregions, identify them semantically, and quantify cells within anatomically meaningful boundaries remain limited. Limited annotated datasets, heterogeneous staining patterns, low signal-to-

title: How does adolescent neurodevelopment impact substance use? The substance use neuroplasticity and peer (SNAP) model: A novel neurodevelopmental model of adolescent substance use
abstract: Substance use among adolescents age 13-18 remains a significant societal concern, yet contemporary neuroscience models of addiction have been grounded in the chronic, cyclic stage model developed for adult presentations of substance use disorder (SUD). Relative to adults, adolescents exhibit distinct patterns of substance use, and many structural and functional findings garnered from studies of addiction in the adult brain have not been reliably observed or replicated in adolescent samples. Thus, contemporary models of adult addiction do not readily translate to adolescents, resulting in downstream developmental incongruities in how substance use is conceptualized, measured, and treated in this age group. Here, we present a review of the current state of human and preclinical models of neurobiological risk factors and mechanisms specific to substance use in adolescents. Grounded in this literature, we present the Substance use Neuroplasticity And Peer (SNAP) model, a novel neurodevelopmental model of adolescent substance use that captures the differentiated nature of substance use initiation and escalation in this high-need, yet undertreated population.

title: NeuroChrono: Dissociated Neural Encoding with ChronoGate for Brain-to-Video Diffusion
abstract: Reconstructing natural video viewed by a subject from non-invasive neural recordings is a challenging problem at the intersection of computational neuroscience and generative modelling. Existing brain-to-video methods encode multi-modal neural signals (typically fMRI together with EEG or MEG) into a single unified brain latent that conditions a video diffusion model. This unified-latent assumption can entangle two practical decisions: how to preserve complementary semantic-structural and temporal-kinetic evidence from fMRI and EEG, and how strongly each evidence source conditions different denoising stages. We present NeuroChrono , a brain-to-video framework built around two method components. First, a Dissociated Neural Encoder (DNE) instantiates a role-specialized hypothesis by routing fMRI toward semantic and structural heads (the slow stream) and EEG toward temporal-dynamics heads (the fast stream), motivated by their complementary measurement properties and by classic two-stream accounts of visual processing. title: Seeing what students learn: assessing cognitive representations and academic outcomes via EEG image reconstruction
abstract: Abstract Understanding how humans process visual information during learning remains a central challenge in cognitive neuroscience. Traditional approaches typically rely on behavioral observations or indirect neural measures, which limits direct insight into learners' internal cognitive representations. Recent advances in brain--computer interfaces (BCIs) and deep learning have enabled image reconstruction from electroencephalography (EEG), providing a promising pathway to decode latent cognitive states. In this study, we investigate how EEG-based image reconstruction relates to students' learning. While students watched educational videos, we recorded EEG signals and used an image reconstruction model to generate images reflecting their perceived visual representations. We assessed reconstruction quality using semantic similarity between reconstructed and original images. First, we examine whether semantic similarity predicts overall academic performance and find a strong positive association. Second, we evaluate item-level effects and show that questions answered incorrectly correspond to significantly lower semantic similarity than correctly answered questions. Third, we analyze

title: Editorial: Health data science and AI in neuroscience & psychology
abstract: Gao et al. introduced a deep learning framework for health risk assessment in adolescents by developing a combination of a two-dimensional convolutional autoencoder (2DCNN-AE) with multisequence learning and multi-scale asynchronous correlation information extraction techniques. Applied to modelling fMRI data from the Adolescent Risk Behavior (AHRB) dataset, the framework was designed to capture both spatial and time-shifted relationships among brain regions considering limited labelled data. The study demonstrated the promising performance of a deep learning-based approach for understanding and predicting health-related risks in adolescents. The work illustrated the potential of the developed deep learning method in enhancing the precision of health risk assessment and supporting early identification of individuals who may benefit from timely intervention. However, more robust external validation and assessment of generalisability across diverse populations and settings are essential to establish the clinical utility and readiness for real-world implementation.Chalmers et al. developed a study of using deep reinforcement learning to simulate the effect of dendritic spine loss as o

title: Single-Objective Light-Sheet Microscopy Allows Long-Term, High-Resolution In Vivo Brain Imaging of Drosophila
abstract: Abstract In vivo imaging of dynamic subcellular brain structures is key to understanding several phenomena in neuroscience. However, in the fruit fly, its implementation has been hindered by a trade-off among spatial resolution, speed, photobleaching, phototoxicity, and setup complexity required to access specific target regions of the small brain of Drosophila. Here, we present DrosoScope: a single-objective light-sheet microscope customized for in vivo imaging of adult flies and optimized for maximum resolution. With it, we imaged the axonal projections of small lateral ventral neurons (s-LNvs) in intact adult flies. We imaged the plasma membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and dense-core vesicles with high spatial resolution of up to 310 nm, lower photobleaching than confocal microscopy, lower invasiveness and reduced sample-mounting complexity than alternative light-sheet technologies, and without relying on potentially phototoxic pulsed infrared lasers. Furthermore, we implemented active focus stabilization and sample-drift correction. Combined, these features enabled time-lapse brain imaging in living flies for up to 5 h, revealing neuronal plasticity and dynamic mitochondrial

title: Commentary on the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine: Transcending Neuroscience into Next-Generation Pancreatic Cancer Cure and Diabetes Management
abstract: The October 2026 announcement of the Nobel Prize inPhysiology or Medicine awarded to Dr. Karl Deisseroth, Dr.Peter Hegemann, and Dr. Georg Nagel for the developmentof optogenetics marks a historic inflection point in modernmedicine. While initially lauded for illuminating neuralcircuits within the brain, this commentary explores howtheir discovery of light-gated algal ion channels has tran-scended traditional neuroscience. We evaluate its frontierapplications in tackling the dense, therapy-resistant microen-vironment of pancreatic cancer and pioneering autonomous,wireless metabolic control in diabetology

title: Developmental shift from hormonal to neural correlates of psychobehavioral problems among early adolescent boys
abstract: Adolescence begins with puberty and involves dynamic hormonal, neural, and social changes. The early-pubertal testosterone surge, particularly in boys, may shape the amygdala, which regulates emotion and behavior. However, it remains unclear how testosterone- and amygdala-related correlates of psychobehavioral problems differ across early adolescence. Using data from the Tokyo Teen Cohort and its neuroscience extension, we examined associations among salivary testosterone, amygdala volumes, and parent-rated Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) scores at approximately ages 10-11 and 12-13. Participants were 106 boys in wave 1 and 98 boys in wave 2, with 69 contributing complete biological measures at both waves. Wave-specific Poisson models of CBCL internalizing and externalizing scores were adjusted for age, Tanner stage, and intracranial volume. In wave 1, higher testosterone was associated with lower internalizing and externalizing scores (exp(β)= 0.64 and 0.66, both adjusted P < 0.001). In wave 2, testosterone was not significantly related to CBCL scores, whereas smaller right amygdala volume was associated with higher internalizing problems (exp(β)= 0.71, adjusted P < 0.001). Associations between psychological distress symptoms and cognitive function among trauma‐exposed women: Moderating role of the developmental period of trauma exposure
abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and related internalizing symptoms, including anxiety and depression, are associated with emotional-cognitive alterations. These alterations, such as biased attentional processing and reduced emotional inhibition, are thought to contribute to persistent distress. However, these associations may vary across individuals. Developmental neuroscience suggests that the timing of trauma exposure (childhood, adolescence, adulthood) can differentially influence brain development and emotional processing. This study examined whether the developmental period of first trauma moderated the link between internalizing symptoms and emotional-cognitive alterations. Participants were 109 women exposed to interpersonal trauma (age range: 28-53 years) who completed a visual search task assessing attentional biases and an emotional go/no-go task measuring emotional inhibition. Questionnaires evaluated trauma exposure and PTSD, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Groups were based on the developmental period of participants' first trauma exposure: childhood (0-11 years; n = 38), adolescence (12-17 years; n = 32), or adulthood (≥ 18 years; n = 39). title: The Tumor Neuroimmune Niche: A Unifying Framework for Cancer Progression and Its Neuropsychiatric Burden
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer has traditionally been framed as a cell-intrinsic genetic disease and, more recently, as a disorder of the tumor microenvironment (TME). An emerging third view reframes malignancy as a systems-level neuroimmune disorder, in which neurons, glia, immune cells, and tumor cells form a continuously communicating network, the tumor neuroimmune niche. SUMMARY: This review synthesizes evidence that the nervous system actively regulates tumor initiation, proliferation, angiogenesis, invasion, and metastasis through autonomic, sensory, and neuroendocrine inputs, while tumors in turn remodel both peripheral nerves and central circuits. Sympathetic, parasympathetic, and sensory fibers shape the immune compartment, frequently driving T-cell exhaustion, macrophage repolarization, and an immunosuppressive milieu via β-adrenergic and neuropeptide signaling. title: THE PSYCHO-IMMUNOLOGICAL SHIFT THEORY (PIST)
abstract: Background. Psychoneuroimmunology has documented associations between psychological stress, adverse experience in childhood and the onset or course of autoimmune and chronic inflammatory disease. The part played by the expression or suppression of emotion, as a distinct and measurable variable, remains poorly defined and is seldom tested directly. Aim. This thesis presents the Psycho-Immunological Shift Theory (PIST) as a testable theoretical framework. It proposes that sustained, unresolved and poorly expressed emotional load acts, in susceptible people, as a contributory factor that modifies the probability and course of immune dysregulation, through a chain of five links: exposure, neuroendocrine and autonomic activation, a shift towards a low-grade inflammatory profile, disruption of barriers and microbiome, and loss of tolerance. Approach. The work is a theoretical and integrative synthesis. It draws together the literature of immunology, neuroendocrinology, the neuroscience and psychology of emotion, developmental science and the sociology of health. title: When the Brain's "Go Signal" Runs Low: Could Dopamine Explain Why the Mind and Body Slow Down Together? (Video Lay Summary OER)
abstract: This open educational resource (OER) accompanies the video lay summary, When the Brain’s “Go Signal” Runs Low: Could Dopamine Explain Why the Mind and Body Slow Down Together? It translates the complex neuroscience of psychomotor slowing into an accessible narrative, exploring whether reduced dopamine signalling may help explain shared slowing of movement, speech and thinking across Parkinson’s disease, depression and catatonia. title: Biological Psychology, Neuroscience, and Digital Self Representation in DRP and DRL
abstract: This paper connects biological psychology and neuroscience with Digital Relativity Psychology (DRP) and Digital Relativity Linguistics (DRL) to examine biological and digital signaling, self-representation, and human–machine interfaces. Human neural communication combines continuous electrochemical dynamics with discrete spiking events, whereas digital systems process information through engineered physical states; their shared dependence on physical signaling motivates comparison without implying equivalent organization or consciousness. The paper examines brain–computer interfaces, avatars, human digital twins, and alter egos as tools for studying agency, body ownership, source attribution, self-reference, and conscious report. Formal models illustrate membrane dynamics, sampling, model fidelity, and identity relations, while published findings are clearly separated from proposed DRP/DRL experiments. abstract: ABSTRACT Classical materialistic models of neuroscience are used to localize human visual perception and ist representation as imagination within the primary visual cortex (V1) of the occipital lobe. The brain contains, activates and provides the „screen“. However, this model fails to address the hard problem of consciousness and cannot physically explain why the three-dimensional image is experienced immediately and topological in space rather than as a neural equivalent inside the dark skull. This paper proposes a radically reciprocal model: the eye does not only act as a passive camera, but also as an optical projector and transceiver. Based on a mathematical-geometric framework of coherence mechanics — a dual, fractal spatial lattice of circles and squares in permanent fundamental vibration — we postulate that visual experience is a physical hologram manifested directly in space. Through a coherent network of microtubular quantum resonators, neural Hertz clocking (modulated by synaptic glutamate transitions and CaMKII memory complexes) undergoes phase-shift keying of π-electron clouds in microtubules to transform into a biophotonic terahertz reference wave. title: Modelling towards a neurobiological explanation of action semantics: response to de Zubicaray (2026)
abstract: In response to de Zubicaray [2026. Modelling in the midst of a replication crisis for embodied action semantics: a commentary on Carriere et al. (2026). Language, Cognition and Neuroscience, 1–8], we discuss the plausibility of brain-constrained neural networks as a tool for offering a neurobiological explanation of how language and cognition emerge at the level of neural circuits. We argue that the commentary places considerable emphasis on the biological plausibility of computational models being determined by their ability to reproduce empirical effects that remain under debate. In contrast, we suggest that plausibility should be evaluated across multiple complementary dimensions beyond replicability, including neurobiological constraints, cross-model validation, generalisability across linguistic phenomena, and the ability to provide a neuromechanistic explanation thereof. Furthermore, the commentary draws strong conclusions against motor involvement in action semantics while giving limited consideration to substantial evidence of motor engagement, including proposals emphasising individual differences in sensorimotor experience and related cognitive factors. title: Distinct Patterns of Cortical Reorganisation Accompany Behaviour-Specific Development in Freely Behaving Infants
abstract: Abstract A central premise of developmental neuroscience is that mature behaviour emerges through reciprocal interactions between infants’ spontaneous actions, neural activity, and environmental experience. Yet, much human neuroimaging research relies on highly controlled, repetitive paradigms designed to minimize behavioural variability, obscuring the very brain-behaviour dynamics that drive developmental change. Here, we introduce a naturalistic functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) paradigm that exploits, rather than suppresses, natural variability in infants’ behaviour to investigate cortical changes associated with behavioural development. Continuous video coding of spontaneous infant behaviour was combined with finite impulse response (FIR) modelling to estimate behaviour-specific hemodynamic responses associated with reach-to-grasp, hand-to-mouth, and vocalization behaviours while accounting for temporally overlapping hemodynamic responses by treating extraneous behaviours as nuisance regressors. abstract: EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF NEURO-COMPUTATIONAL SOVEREIGNTY: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY This treatise establishes Neuro-Computational Sovereignty, founded by Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi. title: Neurobiological Modulation of Substance Use Without Neurotoxicity: A Conceptual Framework for Non-Damaging Inhibition of Addictive Behaviors
abstract: Substance use disorders represent a complex interaction between neurobiological, behavioral, and environmental factors. Current pharmacological approaches often focus on substitution or aversive mechanisms, frequently accompanied by undesirable neurological or systemic side effects. This conceptual study proposes a non-damaging neurobiological modulation strategy aimed at inhibiting substance use without inducing neurotoxicity or cognitive impairment.The framework integrates principles from neuroplasticity, reward circuit modulation, receptor-level interference, and behavioral conditioning, emphasizing selective pathway inhibition rather than global neurotransmission suppression. By targeting specific neural circuits involved in craving and reinforcement—while preserving executive and emotional functions—this approach seeks to reduce substance-seeking behavior without compromising brain integrity.This paper does not propose a finished pharmacological compound but outlines a biologically plausible and ethically grounded research direction. title: Heterarchy in the Brain: Control as a Spectrum, Not a Chain of Command
abstract: Neuroscience treats the brain as a control hierarchy, with cortical systems governing subcortical mechanisms. We argue that this mistakes a configuration for an architecture. Local asymmetries of influence are real, but control is relational and process-specific; because neural elements constrain one another across concurrent processes, relations can form cycles that resist a stable ranking. Evidence from learned action, cortico-cerebellar and thalamocortical loops, and defensive behavior shows that control changes with practice, task phase, urgency, viability demands, and affordances. Hierarchical order therefore characterizes time-bounded configurations, whereas heterarchy characterizes the architecture's repertoire across occasions. We propose a spectrum of control indexed by dynamical decoupling: how far behavior can depend on history, internal state, and anticipated consequences. The account yields experimentally testable predictions.

title: Artificial Sentience: From Computational Functionalism to Behaviourism?
abstract: I critically examine Jonathan Birch’s account of how brain emulations might create artificial sentience candidates, arguing that his account risks collapsing into a behaviourist account, unless the specific computational processes realised by such emulations are carefully considered. Drawing on examples from computational neuroscience, I show that similar behaviours can arise from vastly different computational processes, thereby undermining the suggestion to focus on behaviourial profiles to determine whether a brain emulation of a sentience candidate is itself a sentience candidate.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF NEURO-ALGORITHMIC SYMBIOSIS LAW The Juridical Architecture for Hybrid Cognitive Personhood, Brain-Computer Integration, and Neuromorphic Computing Governance
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Doctrine of Neuro-Algorithmic Symbiosis Law presents the first comprehensive legal framework governing human-computational integration through brain-computer interfaces. Building upon the Universal Declaration of Neuro-Rights, it introduces fifteen innovations: the Hybrid Cognitive Personhood Doctrine; the Legal Intent Attribution Protocol with Presumption of Neural Innocence acknowledging neuroscience limitations; Neural Causal Forensics distinguishing semantic content from causal patterns; Neural Zero-Knowledge Proofs with biological compensation; the Cognitive Encryption Standard; bio-neuromorphic computing regulation; the Qualified Right to Cognitive Disconnection with medical exceptions; Algorithmic Cognitive Influence Liability; Neuro-Weapons Prohibition; Protection of Minors; Cultural and Religious Accommodation; Anti-Existential Monopoly measures; and a 15-year economic implementation strategy. The doctrine explicitly acknowledges scientific limitations, demographic bias risks, and implementation costs while providing actionable guidance for protecting cognitive sovereignty in the neural-algorithmic age. title: Neuro-Tourism
abstract: The foundations of neuro-tourism and experiential neuroscience represent an emerging interdisciplinary frontier that integrates insights from neuroscience, psychology, tourism studies, and technology to understand and enhance how individuals perceive, experience, and remember travel. At its core, neuro-tourism seeks to apply principles from Neuroscience and Cognitive Psychology to analyze tourists' emotional, cognitive, and sensory responses to destinations, attractions, and experiences, thereby enabling the design of more engaging, meaningful, and memorable journeys. This approach moves beyond traditional tourism research, which often relies on self-reported data and observational methods, by incorporating neuroscientific tools and methodologies such as brain imaging, biometric tracking, and psychophysiological measurements to capture real-time at a deeper, objective level. Experiential neuroscience, a closely related concept, focuses on how the brain processes and encodes lived experiences, emphasizing the role of perception.

High-throughput serial two-photon tomography with BakingTray and BrainSaw
abstract: Abstract Volumetric imaging is increasingly important in fields such as neuroscience, where quantifying structure and mapping features are inherently three-dimensional problems. Block-face serial two-photon tomography (STPT) has emerged as a powerful approach for high-resolution, whole-organ volumetric imaging. STPT avoids complex sample preparation and balances image quality, speed, and scalability. However, STPT remains niche, in part because of the absence of flexible, general-purpose control software. Here we present BakingTray, an open-source software platform for STPT that extends ScanImage. BakingTray’s modular framework accommodates diverse hardware configurations and allows users to build systems customised to their needs. Twelve such systems, which we call ‘BrainSaws’, have been constructed worldwide since 2016, with more under construction, and have so far contributed to 35 research papers. The three systems at the Sainsbury Wellcome Centre alone have acquired over 7,000 samples in a busy multi-user facility. We demonstrate the platform across its core neuroscience applications: electrode track localisation, brain-wide cell counting, and bulk projection mapping. Beyond t

title: Insights on Neuro Tourism in Hospitality 5.0
abstract: Tourism marketers can examine their traveler's brain waves and how different stimuli affect them through using neuroscience in tourism, also referred as “neuro-tourism”. Neuro-tourism allows access to travelers' minds, giving us real-time insight into what they consciously and unconsciously feel. Neuromarketing methods such as brain–computer interface (BCI), eye tracking, galvanic skin reaction have been implemented in neuro-tourism for purposes of designing tourism products and services that increase visitors happiness and experience. Since neuro-tourism is relatively new and there are few studies on the topic, this chapter offered an indepth investigation of peer reviewed journal papers published within neuro-tourism research during the past years in order to highlight possible trends in this line of research and present implications for researchers.

Frontal lead in preterm functional brain maturation
abstract: Understanding how brain maturation unfolds in preterm neonates is critical for both neuroscience and clinical care. Structural MRI suggests that the frontal cortex develop late, yet EEG offers a direct window into functional activity that follows a different trajectory. We analysed 211 EEG recordings from 62 preterm neonates (25-40 weeks postmenstrual age, PMA) using convolutional neural networks trained on single channels to estimate functional brain age (FBA). We introduced the spatial difference in FBA (sd_FBA) metric, which quantifies the relative maturity of each channel compared with all others within a recording. sd_FBA revealed a consistent maturation gradient, frontal regions exhibited the highest sd_FBA, followed by central regions, whereas occipital and temporal regions showed lower values. With increasing PMA, central maturation converged with frontal values, while occipital regions remained significantly lower. Functional maturation in preterm infants follows a clear frontal-occipital gradient, in contrast to structural MRI findings. title: 6th International Mobile Brain-Body Imaging Conference
abstract: The Mobile Brain/Body Imaging (MoBI) Conference brings together researchers from various fields using mobile brain imaging from around the world. Using portable methods such as EEG and fNIRS, MoBI brings neuroscience closer to embodied and naturalistic states that we experience in real life. The 6th International Mobi conference was hosted by the Berlin Brain-Body Imaging Lab at the Technical University of Berlin between August 25-28. We foster scientific communication, networking, and good scientific practices related to MoBI research. All abstracts in this book were reviewed by members of the scientific committee and approved by authors.

title: Neurotechnological toolkit for sales management of intermediary commercial structures in social media
abstract: This article develops an integrative conceptual toolkit for sales management by intermediary commercial structures operating in social media, combining the classical sales process framework with neurotechnological methods of consumer behavior diagnostics. The study employs systematic analysis of prior empirical research, comparative analysis, and conceptual modeling. Intermediary commercial structures increasingly rely on social media not only for product promotion but for the full sales cycle, from prospecting to post-purchase engagement. However, conventional behavioral metrics such as clicks, impressions, and conversion rates fail to capture the underlying cognitive and affective mechanisms driving purchase decisions at each stage of the sales process. At the same time, academic coverage of neuroscience applications in sales management remains substantially narrower than in consumer marketing, and no integrative framework currently links established sales-process stage models with neurotechnological diagnostic methods for the specific context of intermediary commercial structures acting through social media channels. title: International Conference on Cognitive Neuroscience: Abstracts Book
abstract: The International Conference on Cognitive Neuroscience (ICON), established in 1980, has a long-standing tradition of promoting scientific collaboration and interdisciplinary exchange in the field of human cognition. Held in Porto, ICON 2025 brought together an international community of researchers to share new discoveries, ideas, and perspectives on the neural basis of cognition. abstract: The El-Rakhawi Doctrine of Algorithmic Neuro-Hallucination and Cyber-Biological Crime presents the first legal framework addressing the intersection of AI hallucinations, Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs), and generative biology. Authored by Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi, it introduces six innovations to protect cognitive sovereignty. It precisely defines Algorithmic Neuro-Hallucination (ANH) as a neurological divergence causing uncommanded phenomena. It establishes the Crime of Cognitive Assault, utilizing Presumed Negligence with a Statutory Safe Harbor to balance victim protection with innovation. It mandates the Reality Filtering Protocol (MRFP) to intercept false signals, and introduces the Automated Hardware-Level Cognitive Circuit Breaker (AHCCB), a physical safeguard operating independently of user volition. It enforces joint liability for Generative Bio-Hallucination, targeting Algorithmic Fraud. Finally, it anchors protections to the 2021 Chilean Neuro-Rights reform and mandates export controls for open-source neuro-AI. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23108273.

title: Neural efficiency and decision making changes in female basketball players
abstract: This study provides novel evidence for the neural mechanisms underlying sports expertise and training-induced plasticity in female basketball players. By integrating resting-state and task-based EEG, we show that long-term sport-specific training enhances baseline neural efficiency, while targeted visual attention training significantly improves decision-making efficiency in novices. These findings bridge the gap between cognitive neuroscience and applied sports training, highlighting the value of EEG as an objective tool for athlete evaluation and the potential of perceptual-cognitive interventions, such as multiple object tracking, in optimizing athletic performance. The work not only advances theoretical understanding of brain function in sports expertise but also offers practical implications for athlete development, training design, and talent selection.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Sleep Science: Evaluating User Satisfaction of Static and Dynamic Sleep Surfaces at User-Neurophysiological Interface
abstract: Sleep and brain health are inextricably linked.External sleep physiology is the study of how outside environmental cues and observable physical parameters interact with the body's internal sleep-wake cycles.Improving the complex relationship between sleep, brain function and neurological health remains at the frontiers of scientific and technological innovation.An AI-enabled Dynamic Mattress was developed for use within homes after two years of applied research in New Zealand.This study assessed short-term user satisfaction for comparing Static and Dynamic Sleep Surfaces combining full sample of 60 adults (31 Males, 29 Females), aged 30-70 years who tested two mattresses in Auckland and scored them quantitatively on Comfort, Firmness, Temperature, and Overall Satisfaction using the Boston Mattress Satisfaction Questionnaire (BMSQ) developed by the Harvard Medical School with qualitative feedback.Participants rated Dynamic Mattress higher than Static Mattress in terms of Comfort, Firmness, and Overall Satisfaction, with mean differences which were all highly statistically significant (p < 0.001).Temperature received a marginally higher rating which was not statistically significant.

NEURODEGENERATION IN AYURVEDA A CONCEPTUAL REVIEW WITH CONTEMPORARY CORRELATION
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease constitute a growing global health burden. Modern neuroscience attributes neurodegeneration to protein aggregation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation, whereas Ayurveda explains degeneration through derangements of Dosha and depletion of Dhatus. This conceptual review aims to elucidate neurodegeneration through Ayurvedic principles and correlate them with contemporary biomedical mechanisms. Classical Ayurvedic texts and relevant PubMed-indexed literature were reviewed to establish integrative correlations. Neurodegeneration is primarily understood as Mastulunga Majja dhatu kshaya (brain and nervous tissue depletion) with predominant Vata dosha involvement, particularly Prana, Udana, and Vyana Vata, leading to cognitive, speech, and motor impairments. Disturbances of Samana and Apana Vata explain gut–brain axis dysfunction and autonomic manifestations. Secondary involvement of Pitta and Kapha contributes to Dhatupaka (pathological metabolism), neuroinflammation, protein aggregation, and impaired metabolic clearance. The Samprapti of neurodegeneration is best explained through Dhatu
