title: Toward a Post‐Jungian Cosmopsychism: Entropy, Information, and the Inhibitory Dynamics of Consciousness
abstract: Abstract This paper advances a model of the psyche as a thermodynamic–informational organism that modulates entropy to let symbolic life emerge and evolve. Building on Jungian metapsychology, complexity theory, and contemporary predictive‐processing and oscillation neuroscience, I introduce the Acceleration–Expansion–Gravity (AEG) model of psychic dynamics. Acceleration marks entropy spikes and archetypal flooding, Expansion the elaboration of symbolic complexity, and Gravity the integrative forces that restore coherence. Central to these rhythms is the “inhibitory membrane” of consciousness: an explicitly metaphorical construct with physiological anchors, instantiated by oscillatory brain dynamics that regulate the permeability between unconscious potentials and conscious awareness. The model illuminates clinical phenomena such as trauma, psychosis, creativity, and individuation as recurrent cycles of entropy modulation. Framing psyche and cosmos alike as self‐organizing, entropy‐regulating systems, this post‐Jungian cosmopsychism offers both a clinical map of transformation and a cosmological vision of how meaning coheres at the edge of chaos.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI THEORY OF HARMONIC CARDIAC PERCEPTION A PARADIGM SHIFT IN NEUROSCIENCE, PHILOSOPHY OF MIND, AND CRIMINAL JURISPRUDENCE
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Harmonic Cardiac Perception revolutionizes neuroscience, philosophy, and criminal law by dismantling the entrenched neurocentric paradigm. It posits that the heart is not a mere hemodynamic pump, but an autonomous cognitive organ housing the Intrinsic Cardiac Nervous System (ICNS) with ~40,000 neurons. Through ascending vagal afferents (comprising 80-90% of vagal fibers), the heart actively dominates cerebral function, providing the rhythmic temporal scaffolding essential for consciousness and executive cognition. The theory introduces the "El-Rakhawi Equation for Cardiac Intentionality," mathematically formalizing the doctrine of *Mens Rea Cardialis*. This provides a quantifiable, court-admissible metric for assessing criminal intent based on objective cardiac coherence (HRV), replacing subjective legal inference. Philosophically, it establishes "Neurovisceral Monism," transcending Cartesian dualism by framing the mind as an emergent property of the integrated heart-brain axis. Profoundly, it bridges empirical science with ancient theological epistemology, scientifically validating the Quranic assertion that the heart is the true locus of comprehension, mo

title: Toward A Whole-Brain Interface Enabled by High-Resolution Surface Electrophysiology
abstract: The goal of building a whole-brain interface-capable of generating a real-time digital representation of the state of the entire central nervous system-has long been framed as a hardware challenge of recording simultaneously from ever-larger numbers of microelectrodes. Advances in high-resolution neural interfaces now enable electrophysiologic interaction with the human nervous system at spatial and temporal resolutions previously unattainable without disrupting tissue architecture or physiology. These capabilities create new opportunities for mechanistic neuroscience, neuroprosthetics, and precision-guided neurosurgery. With the advent of modern microelectrode array technology, however, the whole-brain interface has also become a data challenge. Rather than pursuing large-scale human brain recording purely through a single device placed in a single patient, we demonstrate here that systematic multi-subject aggregation, across brain regions and behavioral paradigms, in a common anatomical framework, can achieve something functionally similar to a whole-brain interface. Here we present an approach to a functional atlas of the human central nervous system derived from high-resolution

title: FAIRsharing record for: BrainMaps.org
abstract: This FAIRsharing record describes: BrainMaps.org is an interactive, multiresolution digital brain atlas providing access to high-resolution, annotated images of serial brain sections from primate and non-primate species. It integrates these large-scale image datasets with a database that enables users to search, visualize, and retrieve information about brain structures and functions. The resource supports neuroscience and neuroanatomical research through virtual microscopy, brain mapping, 3D visualization, and analysis tools.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF NEURAL REALITY QUANTUM DECOHERENCE AS THE GUARDIAN OF THE BRAIN'S CLASSICAL BORDERS AND THE DOWNFALL OF THE QUANTUM COMPUTER HYPOTHESIS
abstract: "THE EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF NEURAL REALITY" by Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi presents a rigorous quantitative refutation of the quantum brain hypothesis, notably the Orch-OR theory. Through first-principles calculations of quantum decoherence in biological tissue, the treatise demonstrates that decoherence timescales for neural processes range from 10^-13 to 10^-27 seconds. This is many orders of magnitude shorter than the millisecond timescales of neural processing, rendering sustained quantum coherence in the brain physically impossible under physiological conditions. Consequently, the doctrine establishes that cognitive degrees of freedom in the brain must be treated as classical dynamical systems. Far from diminishing the brain's wonder, this conclusion highlights the extraordinary computational power of classical neural networks, refined by evolution. The work provides testable predictions and a robust framework for advancing neuroscience grounded in physical realism rather than quantum mysticism.

title: Educación aumentada
abstract: Augmented Education: Artificial Intelligence, Neuroscience, and New Frontiers of Human Learning explores the transformation of the contemporary educational paradigm resulting from the convergence of intelligent technologies, neuroscience, and pedagogy. The work defines "augmented education" as a human-centered approach aimed at amplifying the cognitive, creative, and self-regulatory capacities of students and educators, preventing indiscriminate automation and technological dependence. Across three chapters, it examines the evolution of digital ecosystems toward adaptive and immersive environments, brain function in digital settings (analyzing neuroplasticity, attention, executive functions, and neuroethics), and the establishment of new pedagogical frontiers focused on challenge-based learning, formative assessment, and digital humanism.

title: Ketamine in psychiatry: a systematic review of clinical applications, safety considerations, and emerging challenges
abstract: Ketamine has progressed from solely being an anesthetic agent to a drug of rising clinical and research interest due to its distinctive pharmacological properties. Its dissociative properties and rapid-acting antidepressant effects have made it a prominent area of investigation across many medical and psychiatric applications. This systematic review examines ketamine’s history, mechanisms of action, clinical uses, and significant challenges. A systematic search of PubMed, SCOPUS, PsycINFO, and other sources, generated peer-reviewed publications that addressed the history of ketamine, its pharmacology, clinical applications, recreational use, safety considerations, and societal consequences. Overall, 106 articles were identified for inclusion in this study. At the receptor level, ketamine is an antagonist of NMDA receptors that triggers a number of downstream effects ranging from heightened glutamate transmission, AMPA receptor activation, increased BDNF expression, synaptogenesis, and mTOR pathway signaling. At the network level, it alters activity within large-scale brain circuits including the default mode network, affecting cognition, mood, and perception. Clinically, ketamine i

title: CRSS: Consistency-regularized semi-supervised spectral unmixing for multicolor fluorescence microscopy images
abstract: Multicolor fluorescence microscopy is a cornerstone of biomedical research, enabling simultaneous visualization of multiple subcellular targets. However, inherent spectral overlap between fluorophores causes pervasive detection-channel crosstalk, which distorts quantitative intensity measurements, generates false co-localization signals, and severely limits multiplexing capacity. Traditional unmixing methods rely on pre-calibrated reference spectra and lack adaptability to variable experimental conditions, while deep learning approaches require costly fully labeled fluorescence datasets. We propose CRSS, a semi-supervised blind spectral unmixing method that jointly models spectral-spatial features via the Global-Local Spectral Attention module, adaptively fuses channel-pair features via the Dynamic Feature Fusion module, and imposes bidirectional consistency constraints on unlabeled data using multiple Gaussian perturbations. The method leverages limited labeled and abundant unlabeled data through dual-path synergistic training combining supervised loss, unsupervised reconstruction loss, and multi-perturbation consistency loss. Trained on 344 U-2 OS images with only 9.7 % labeled d

title: THE GUT–BRAIN CONNECTION: WHERE NUTRITION MEETS NEUROSCIENCE
abstract: You've felt it before. The flutter of nerves before a big presentation. The knot in your stomach when you receive bad news. For most of human history, we treated these sensations as poetic curiosities — the gut somehow 'knowing' what the mind refuses to admit. Ancient writers spoke of bowels of compassion and burning courage. It turns out they were onto something far more literal than they could have imagined.

title: Neurospirituality: Conceptual Foundations, Clinical Relevance, And Current Evidence
abstract: Background: Neurospirituality is an emerging interdisciplinary framework integrating neuroscience, neurology, palliative care, and the medical humanities to address the spiritual and existential dimensions of health. Spirituality refers to meaning-making through connectedness beyond the self, whereas religiosity denotes organized beliefs, rituals, and communities. Objective: To review the conceptual foundations, neuroscientific evidence, and clinical applications of neurospirituality in neurological disorders and palliative care. Methods: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from neuroscience, cognitive science, neurology, palliative care, and spirituality research to examine the neural correlates, clinical relevance, limitations, and future directions of neurospirituality. Results: Current evidence associates spiritual experiences with distributed brain networks, particularly the default mode, salience, and frontoparietal control networks, rather than discrete brain regions. These models are heuristic and suggest that domain-general cognitive processes may contribute to spiritual experiences without implying spirituality-specific neural mechanisms. Clinically, greater spirit

title: Rare earth oxide-based memristors for neuromorphic applications
abstract: Abstract The escalating demands from artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, and wearable electronics are accelerating the rapid exploration of hardware that can deliver low-power, low-latency, and highly integrated information processing that transcends the limitations of conventional von Neumann architecture. To achieve this objective, memristor-based neuromorphic systems are significantly promising to enable the physical convergence of memory and computation. In particular, rare earth-based oxides (REOs) are particularly distinguished by their unique combination of multivalent states, versatile redox behavior, and highly tunable defect kinetics advanced by their specific 4f electronic configuration. These distinctive characteristics render REOs exceptionally promising for regulating resistive switching, stabilizing analog conductance modulation, and realizing synaptic plasticity with enhanced functional versatility. In this work, we review the remarkable progress of REOs-based memristors covering material design, switching mechanisms, synaptic emulation, array integration, and chip-oriented neuromorphic architectures. title: Brain stimulation boosts CSF flow
Ethics of artificial intelligence use in dermatology research and healthcare
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming dermatology at a rapid pace unlike any other clinical specialty, largely because skin disease is diagnosed visually and, therefore, lends itself naturally to image-based machine learning. Convolutional neural networks now correspond with dermatologists in classifying pigmented lesions, teledermatology platforms triage patients across vast distances, and AI-enabled applications are increasingly available on patients’ screens. Yet this rapid uptake has outpaced the ethical and regulatory scaffolding needed to govern it safely. The Indian Council of Medical Research has addressed this gap conscientiously in March 2023 by publishing the Ethical Guidelines for Application of AI in Biomedical Research and Healthcare, India’s first dedicated ethics framework for medical AI. This article examines the ethical dimensions of AI in dermatology research and clinical practice through the lens of these guidelines, drawing on dermatology-specific evidence on algorithmic bias, consent, data privacy, transparency, and accountability, with recommendations for dermatologists, researchers, and ethics committees engaging with this technology.

title: Integrating Agrometeorology, Agronomy and Artificial Intelligence for Climate-Resilient Sustainable Food Production: A Critical Narrative Review
abstract: Climate-resilient food production requires decisions that are meteorologically informed, agronomically plausible and adaptive to rapidly changing conditions. Agrometeorology provides observations and forecasts of weather and climate risk; agronomy translates those risks into crop, soil and management responses; and artificial intelligence can fuse high-volume, heterogeneous data, learn complex relationships and accelerate prediction. These domains are increasingly connected, yet their evidence bases remain partly fragmented. This critical narrative review evaluates how their integration can support sustainable crop production, with particular attention to the chain from environmental observation and prediction to management action and measurable resilience outcomes. Literature published from 1 January 2000 to 8 August 2026 was examined through relevant agricultural, multidisciplinary and biomedical scholarly sources, with supplementary citation searching and verification of bibliographic metadata. The synthesis shows that the strongest case for integration is not a replacement of process knowledge by data-driven prediction, but a division of labour: meteorological models define tim

title: Research advances of magnesium and magnesium alloys worldwide in 2025
abstract: Research on magnesium materials has achieved rapid development in 2025, with a total of 6124 related papers indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, where China contributes 50.89% of the global output, occupying a leading position in international magnesium research. Bibliometric analysis indicates that microstructure evolution, mechanical performance, and corrosion resistance remain the mainstream research focuses of magnesium alloys. Meanwhile, functional magnesium material systems, including biomedical magnesium alloys, hydrogen storage media, and rechargeable magnesium batteries, have witnessed remarkable breakthroughs. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly integrated into magnesium research workflows, supporting multi-performance forecasting, inverse alloy composition design and interpretable property regulation, which provides an innovative paradigm for the customized optimization of magnesium alloy properties. The continuous drop in primary magnesium prices further facilitates scaled industrial deployment of magnesium products. This review systematically summarizes the full spectrum of magnesium research advances in 2025 and

title: Artificial Intelligence–Based Gait Analysis in Neurological Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review
abstract: Background: Gait impairment is a common consequence of neurological disorders, including stroke, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and cerebral palsy. Accurate gait assessment is essential for identifying functional limitations, monitoring recovery, and optimizing rehabilitation interventions. Traditional gait assessment methods may be limited by their dependence on specialized equipment, clinical expertise, and controlled laboratory environments. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision, offers promising opportunities to improve gait analysis through automated movement assessment, pattern recognition, and data-driven clinical decision support. Objective: This systematic review aims to examine the applications of AI-based gait analysis in neurological rehabilitation, focusing on computational approaches, data acquisition technologies, gait assessment outcomes, clinical applications, and challenges affecting clinical implementation. Methods: The review will systematically identify and evaluate relevant studies using predefined eligibility criteria and a reproducible search strategy across appropriate biomedical and engineeri

Non-toxic aryl diazirine photoinitiators
abstract: Photoinitiators offer an energy-saving alternative to thermal initiation, initiating free-radical polymerization through irradiation. Despite their benefits, current photoinitiators face issues of toxicity and solubility. Trifluoromethylphenyl diazirine, an aryl diazirine, is a promising photoinitiator that generates a carbene upon exposure to light. Aryl diazirines exhibit favorable optical and molecular properties, including minimal skin sensitization and liquid miscibility with aqueous and organic resins. Experimental studies demonstrate the ability of aryl diazirines to initiate free-radical polymerization of acrylate monomers, offering several advantages over traditional photoinitiators, such as TPO and BAPO. Aryl diazirines’ unique attributes include low cytotoxicity, prevention of resin shrinkage, and removal of unreacted monomers post-curing. R-group variants enable both UV and visible-light activation, thereby expanding their utility across biomedical and industrial sectors. The study explores the potential of aryl diazirines as photoinitiators for acrylate polymerization, addressing the limitations of current photoinitiators like toxicity and solubility. title: Artificial Intelligence in Bioengineering: Innovations, Challenges, and Future Directions: A Narrative Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming bioengineering, with applications ranging from diagnosis and biomedical imaging to wearable technologies, rehabilitation, biomaterials, biofabrication, and digital twins. This narrative review aims to examine the major innovations, challenges, and future directions of AI-enabled bioengineering, with particular attention to its clinical and translational development. The literature was searched in Scopus and PubMed, with emphasis on systematic reviews and meta-analyses and consideration of other relevant secondary literature across the main bioengineering domains. A total of 57 secondary publications were included in the principal evidence base. The review process was additionally informed by the ANDJ Narrative Review Checklist and an established qualification and scoring methodology applied to the selected secondary literature. The reviewed evidence shows a broad expansion of AI applications and increasing integration of intelligent technologies into bioengineering systems. However, important challenges remain, particularly regarding data quality and representativeness, validation and generalizability, reproducibility, safety, hu

Using informatics to understand pediatric allergic diseases
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent advances in the power, utility, and accessibility of artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled new methods of investigation in the biomedical sciences and opportunities to transform clinical workflows. As allergic conditions are among the most common chronic diseases affecting children, pediatric allergy represents a promising area for AI-augmented informatics methods to support molecular discovery, early identification, risk stratification, treatment customization, and longitudinal monitoring, as reviewed herein. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent pediatric allergy studies have applied informatics and AI methodologies across various data sources, including molecular and multiomic data, structured and unstructured electronic health record data, environmental exposures, diagnostic images, remote monitoring devices, and patient- and clinician-facing AI tools. Primarily still in the research phase, these approaches include biomarker discovery, disease phenotyping, risk stratification, prediction modeling, remote monitoring, and emerging chatbots for allergy education. SUMMARY: Although still relatively nascent within pediatric allergy, AI-augmented informatics shows pro

title: Future Directions in Tiny Machine Learning
abstract: Tiny machine learning (TinyML) represents a transformative frontier in the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), merging machine learning capabilities with ultra-low-power embedded systems to enable real-time inference at the edge. As data generation accelerates across billions of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, the need for intelligent edge computing that operates efficiently without relying on cloud infrastructure has become critical. TinyML addresses this demand by enabling localized AI processing on constrained devices with limited memory, computation, and energy resources. This chapter provides a comprehensive exploration of the cutting-edge advancements and research trends shaping the present and future landscape of TinyML. We begin by analyzing the core technological enablers of TinyML, including the rise of energy-efficient microcontrollers, specialized AI hardware accelerators, and neuromorphic computing platforms that emulate human brain-like functionality. Innovations in model compression techniques—such as pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation—play a central role in shrinking complex deep learning models into formats suitable for resource-constrained

title: AI-Powered Scoring System for Detecting Drug-Drug Interaction Insights from Scientific Literature
abstract: Background and Objective: Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) present major challenges in clinical care, impacting patient safety and therapeutic outcomes. Traditional detection methods, often based on curated databases, may miss newly emerging interactions or require frequent manual updates. Recent advances in natural language processing (NLP) and artificial intelligence (AI) offer novel tools for real-time, automated DDI detection directly from biomedical literature. This study introduces an AI-powered approach to identify DDIs, assign relevance scores to publications, and benchmark performance against conventional databases. Methods: We developed an NLP pipeline incorporating sentence classification to detect safety and interaction-related content, and named entity recognition (NER) to extract drug-drug interaction types, their clinical impact, and patient features. The sentence classification module is based on a BERT architecture fine-tuned from microsoft/BiomedNLP-BiomedBERT-baseuncased-abstract-fulltext, and the NER module uses the open-source model d4data/biomedical-ner-all. A DDI relevance score was designed to quantify each article’s significance based on weighted parameters de

title: Scoping One Health Foresight Collaboration among EU Agencies
abstract: This working paper constitutes the first deliverable under the EFSA contract RTD/2023/OP/0011 – Lot 1 on Foresight on Demand in Science, Technology, Research and Innovation Policy, implemented within the framework of multi-agency foresight on One Health and authorised by the European Commission, DG Research & Innovation, G1 – Common R&I Strategy and Foresight Service. It examines the relevance of the One Health approach for a broad range of European institutions and agencies and argues that One Health has become an increasingly important framework for addressing the complex and interdependent challenges facing the European Union. These challenges include emerging infectious diseases, antimicrobial and antifungal resistance, environmental pollution, climate change, food insecurity, mental health pressures, and widening social inequalities, all of which cut across traditional sectoral and institutional boundaries. The report situates One Health within its broader conceptual and policy context. It shows that the approach has evolved from earlier biomedical understandings centred on zoonotic disease and veterinary-public health cooperation into a wider framework linking human, animal,

title: Multimodal Deep Learning and Knowledge Graph Framework for Early Disease Screening
abstract: Abstract — Traditional artificial intelligence (AI) systems often treat medical images and clinical data separately. However, screening various diseases can facilitate their early detection and prompt clinical action. Decoupled handling of medical images and clinical data could potentially limit AI’s ability to associate patients’ unique risks, abnormal image findings, symptoms, lab results, etc. In this paper, we propose a multimodal deep learning and knowledge graph framework that integrates patients’ chest x‐ray images and relevant structured clinical data from the electronic health records and screens five common thoracic conditions, i.e., atelectasis, cardiomegaly, pulmonary edema, pleural effusion, and pneumonia. Specifically, we plan to employ transfer learning‐based models as the backbones to extract informative embeddings of patients’ chest radiographs, a multilayer perceptron to learn structured clinical data embeddings, and a graph neural network to model patients’ relevant biomedical knowledge embeddings. Then, we propose an availability‐aware gated‐fusion module to integrate embeddings from all modalities and predict patients’ risks of target diseases. Our framework is

title: Landscape of small molecules derived from marine sources and their clinical progression
abstract: 1. Marine organisms have fascinated scientists with their unique and unparalleled biodiversity and therapeutic potential.2. They are known to possess novel bioactive compounds with varied pharmacological properties that encompass anticancer, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, neuroprotective, antiviral, and cardioprotective properties.3. The review is put forth to discuss key advancements in landscapes of small molecules derived from marine sources, along with their clinical status.4. We also identify key challenges in marine drug discovery, such as access to marine organisms, supply chain sustainability, chemical diversity, synthesis complexity, bioavailability optimization, and intellectual property concerns.4. The review also put forth the discussions on improving the drug discovery area from marine sources by considering the advancements in marine biotechnology, artificial intelligence, and interdisciplinary collaborations.5. Redressing these challenges and adopting emerging technologies, the potential of marine biodiversity may be harnessed for biomedical innovation and, in turn, contribute to health and promote environmental sustainability.

title: Metal-Organic Framework-Based Surface Engineering of Biomedical Magnesium Alloys: Types, Electrochemical Behaviour, Corrosion Protection Mechanisms, Biomedical Applications, and Future Challenges
abstract: The biodegradable magnesium (Mg) alloys are found to have some of the most desirable mechanical properties, biodegradability and biological functions, which are beneficial for temporary orthopedic and cardiovascular implants. However, their extremely rapid corrosion rates in physiological environments, hydrogen evolution, localized alkalization, and loss of mechanical integrity early on are great challenges for their clinical translation. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have been the focus of much research in recent years as multifunctional platforms for surface modification to overcome these limitations. The MOF materials offer unique opportunities to enhance their corrosion resistance, bioactivity, antibacterial property, and therapeutic function, because of their highly porous nature, tunable chemical compositions, controlled ion release, and drug loading abilities. This systematic review provides a detailed review of coating of magnesium alloys using MOFs for biomedical applications with the emphasis on MOF of elements such as Zn, Fe, Co, Cu, Zr, Ti, and Ni. In the review, 180 peerreviewed publications from 2016 to 2026 were analysed and discussed, which focused on the structur

title: Instrumentations, Devices, Machines and Their Health Condition Monitoring Techniques Used in Biomedical Engineering: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: The instrumentations, devices, and machines used in biomedical applications have a highly intricate structure that necessitates not just a substantial number of components (i.e., medical imaging machines; medical sensing devices; robotics; wearable devices; and e-Health remote monitoring systems), but also different types of technologies (mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic devices to operate, and electrical and/or electronic devices to control). This intricacy makes them susceptible to breakdowns and malfunctions, which can result in injuries and, in severe cases, fatal accidents. Therefore, developing effective health condition monitoring (HCM) methods is essential for handling fault detection and diagnosis (FDD), fault-tolerant control (FTC), lifecycle estimation (LCE), and prognosis and health management (PHM) in the field of biomedical engineering. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of the contemporary techniques for fault detection, diagnosis, and prognosis in the diversified smart-biomedical systems (SBSs) and their different applications. Ultimately, the goal is to provide a state-of-the-art platform for researchers, doctors (i.e., the operators), maintenanc

title: Age-Reversal
abstract: This perspective discusses emerging regenerative interventions that target biological aging. Over recent decades, scientific advances have expanded understanding of aging as a potentially modifiable biological process. Technologies under investigation include partial cellular reprogramming, senescent cell clearance, artificial-intelligence-driven drug discovery, organ regeneration, and modulation of epigenetic aging clocks. Preclinical studies indicate that aged cells may regain more youthful functional characteristics under specific experimental conditions. For example, inhibition of interleukin-11 signaling initiated in late life extended median lifespan by approximately 20–25% in mice and partial reprogramming has improved tissue function and survival in aged mouse model. Developments in DNA-methylation-based biomarkers now permit estimation of biological age, allowing more efficient assessment of candidate interventions. All reprogramming data to date are preclinical, and human senolytic and IL-11 data are early-phase. Although many findings remain experimental or early translational, they represent a convergence of approaches that may influence future biomedical research. This

title: Writing by proxy: Authentic authorship in the era of AI‐powered communication of scientific knowledge
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping biomedical research as both a key analytical tool and an efficient copyeditor. Large language models and related algorithms can help investigators sift through the ever‐expanding bodies of scientific literature, connect fragmented biological and clinical datasets, and uncover/recognize meaningful patterns buried within complex multidimensional data. Beyond the bench, these tools can improve and refine manuscript architecture and streamline the flow of information by honing the articulation of simple or complex scientific ideas and sharpening the clarity and cadence of scientific information, which ultimately strengthens the writing in publications and grant proposals alike. For researchers working across languages or at early career stages, these tools allow them to express ideas with greater clarity and fluency, ultimately ensuring that intellectual contributions are assessed on the basis of their conceptual merit and experimental validity. However, the growing persuasiveness of AI‐generated writing raises an important concern as to whether persuasive language can create an impression of rigor that is not necessarily matched by ri

title: Landscape and training opportunities in artificial intelligence for biosciences in Latin America: the BiotrAIn project
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining biosciences by enabling the analysis of complex, large-scale biological and medical data. Latin America has demonstrated remarkable potential through studies applying AI to biomedical sciences often using locally generated data and addressing regional needs. However, the integration of AI into research and healthcare in this region faces several structural challenges, including insufficient infrastructure, lack of specialized training, fragmented research systems, and continuously constrained funding. To overcome existing limitations, capacity building at the regional level is crucial. This includes developing localized AI training programs and the reinforcement of a collaborative research framework. Collaboration across institutions and countries, along with engagement from industry and government, is key to fostering an enabling environment for the responsible and effective use of AI. One promising response to these challenges is the BiotrAIn project, a partnership involving EMBL-EBI, the University of Costa Rica, and CABANAnet, with support from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. title: A Perspective on Advanced Wood Manufacturing: A Decision-Centric Framework for Future Research and Education
abstract: For over a century, wood manufacturing has been organized around understanding the material and process and optimizing the product. It established a globally successful industry and enabled efficient production of traditional and engineered wood products. This manufacturing practice is now being challenged by the complexity of resource variability, product diversification, mass customization, and rapid technology integration. This perspective proposes Advanced Wood Manufacturing as a decision-centric smart manufacturing ecosystem that integrates Resource Intelligence, Manufacturing Intelligence, Product Intelligence, and System Intelligence through a unifying Decision Intelligence framework to convert variability into high-value manufacturing decisions. We argue that natural resource variability, while requiring control where necessary for reliable production, can also provide decision-relevant information for adaptive manufacturing and value creation. The product space of wood manufacturing extends far beyond lumber and panels into emerging functional products for energy storage, flexible electronics, and biomedical applications, enabled by artificial intelligence, sensing and dig

title: Engineering reduced graphene oxide hybrid nanocomposites for biomedicine: progress, challenges and emerging opportunities
abstract: Abstract Hybrid nanocomposites based on reduced graphene oxide (rGO) have emerged as a versatile class of multifunctional materials for advanced biomedical applications owing to their exceptional physicochemical properties, tunable surface chemistry, high surface area and improved biocompatibility. This review critically examines recent advances in the design, synthesis, functionalization and biomedical applications of rGO hybrid nanocomposites, emphasizing synergistic integration with polymers, metals, metal oxides, ceramics and biomolecules. The review discusses their applications in drug and gene delivery, cancer therapy, antimicrobial systems, tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, biosensing and bioimaging in detail. rGO hybrids exhibit high drug‐loading capacity, stimuli‐responsive release, enhanced cellular uptake, synergistic chemo‐photothermal effects, broad‐spectrum antibacterial activity, improved mechanical reinforcement and highly sensitive biosensing for real‐time diagnostics. Despite these advances, clinical translation remains constrained by concerns about long‐term toxicity, fabrication scalability and reproducibility, regulatory approval, and the lack of stand

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Music Therapy for Emotion Regulation: A Multi-Level Representation and Dynamic Adaptation Framework
abstract: Systematic quantitative explanations of the multi-level evolution of emotion regulation remain limited in intelligent music-based intervention research. Traditional music interventions also have limited capacity for dynamic and precise emotion regulation. To address this gap, a generative artificial intelligence (GAI) music therapy framework is developed for multi-level emotion representation and dynamic adaptation. Quantitative transmission pathways are examined across physiological response, psychological perception, and cognitive processing. The framework represents the process from acoustic stimulation input to emotional homeostasis output and compares static fixed-music intervention with GAI-driven dynamic music intervention. The multi-level representation model achieves stable fitting performance, with absolute fitting errors across levels maintained within 0.002-0.005. Under the simulation conditions, the overall transmission efficiency of dynamic music intervention is higher than that of static fixed music intervention. At the 180 s intervention point, the difference in transmission efficiency reaches 0.14, while the difference at the physiological level remains within 0.11

title: Intelligent Hydrogel Sensors for Health Monitoring and Therapeutic Intervention: From Material Design to Integrated Diagnosis and Treatment
abstract: Intelligent hydrogel sensors are integrated sensing devices employing stimuli-responsive hydrogels as the core functional sensing layers. Featuring tissue-mimetic mechanical flexibility, superior biocompatibility, and dynamic stimulus responsiveness, they fundamentally resolve the mechanical and biological interfacial mismatch between traditional rigid electronics and soft living tissues, providing new avenues for in situ, real-time, and in vivo physiological monitoring and precise biomedical intervention. This review systematically elaborates the full-scale design logic, multifunctional integration strategies, and cutting-edge biomedical applications of engineered intelligent hydrogel sensors. The material selection principles covering natural, synthetic, and hybrid polymer systems, multi-mode crosslinking strategies for three-dimensional network construction, and functional modification approaches for conductivity, biological recognition, self-healing, adhesion, and antifouling performance are comprehensively summarized. The sensing mechanisms that convert physical deformation and biochemical variations into quantifiable electrical or optical signals are classified and analyzed,

title: Artificial Intelligence Across the Surgical Research Workflow: A Stage-Specific Framework for Benefits, Failure Modes, and Oversight
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, particularly large language models (LLMs), have rapidly integrated into surgical and biomedical research, prompting fundamental questions about their appropriate role. This review presents a stage-specific framework mapping each phase of the surgical research workflow (literature review, data analysis, manuscript preparation, and research synthesis) to the role AI plays, the benefits it provides, the failure modes it introduces, and the oversight it requires. Artificial intelligence-powered query systems are designed to speed literature synthesis across thousands of publications. In data analysis, LLMs paired with statistical environments can perform regression modeling and generate auditable code, while specialized architectures support automated image segmentation and histopathology analysis. Each stage's benefits, however, are matched by characteristic failure modes: LLMs are prone to error and hallucination, reproducibility is threatened by model versioning and run-to-run variability, fabricated citations and paper-mill submissions endanger the integrity of the literature, and over-reliance risks eroding trainee competencies in critical appra

title: From Protein Corona Characterization to Computational and AI-Enabled Approaches: Mapping the Evolution of Nano-Bio Interface Research
abstract: Protein corona formation critically shapes nano-bio interactions by influencing nanoparticle biological identity, cellular uptake, biodistribution, toxicity, and performance in nanomedicine. To characterize the evolution of protein corona research and the emergence of computational approaches, we conducted a comparative bibliometric analysis of records retrieved on July 25, 2026, using the Web of Science Core Collection as the primary database and Scopus and PubMed for external validation. Two complementary corpora were constructed: a general protein corona corpus comprising 1,212 documents published between 2000 and 2025, and an AI-enabled computational protein corona corpus comprising 310 documents published between 2011 and 2025. Bibliometric analyses included global collaboration, publication sources, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, citation bursts, and cross-database consistency. The general corpus showed that protein corona research has evolved from physicochemical characterization and protein adsorption toward biological identity, nanomedicine, drug delivery, and functional interpretation. The computational corpus retained the

title: Molecular Biology and Genetics: Theoretical Models, Numerical Verification and Research Collection (2026)
abstract: This research collection brings together 26 distinct works addressing theoretical, computational and interdisciplinary questions in molecular biology, genetics and related biomedical sciences. The studies investigate biological mechanisms through mathematical formulations, numerical analyses, theoretical modeling and comparisons with previously published experimental findings. The collection covers several research areas, including cellular processes, molecular mechanisms, proteomics, immune responses and radiobiological phenomena. Methodology and Numerical Verification The research employs theoretical frameworks, quantitative calculations and numerical consistency assessments. Where applicable, model-derived results are examined in relation to findings reported in external experimental literature. Numerical verification is distinguished from direct laboratory experimentation. Comparisons with external experimental sources are presented according to the specific evidence available for each study. Theoretical cellular mechanisms and potential clinical implications are discussed as research interpretations rather than direct demonstrations of clinical efficacy. Collection Contents Th

title: Artificial intelligence as a disruptive tool in interdisciplinary research: current trends and emerging applications
Deep-learning for improving prognostication and therapy prediction in breast cancer
abstract: Treatment decisions in early breast cancer depend on accurate prognostication and on therapy-relevant biomarkers, both of which rely largely on examination of routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue. Manual assessment, however, is subject to observer variability and cannot exhaustively quantify tissue features or detect complex morphological associations. Advances in artificial intelligence have therefore prompted the development of computational tools that extract additional information from routine sections. This thesis investigates whether deep learning applied to H&E whole-slide images (WSIs) can improve prognostication beyond established clinicopathological factors and enable inference of therapy-relevant biomarkers in breast cancer. Four studies are presented, addressing (i) the design of a general modeling framework, (ii) the interchangeability of models for assessing an immune biomarker (i.e., tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes), (iii) the inference of molecular alteration from morphology, and (iv) the direct modeling of patient survival. In the first study, we developed a model-agnostic, multiresolution multiple-instance learning (MIL) framework for WSI analysis, th

title: New Competencies for the Digital Doctor
abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping clinical medicine, requiring physicians to develop competencies that extend beyond traditional biomedical expertise into data literacy, algorithm interpretation, prompt design, and interdisciplinary collaboration with technical teams. As predictive models increasingly influence diagnosis, treatment planning, and healthcare system operations, clinicians must understand how algorithms are trained, validated, and deployed, as well as how to recognize bias, uncertainty, and performance limitations. This chapter outlines a progressive framework of expertise ranging from basic clinical users of AI tools to clinician-scientists and clinician-engineers who co-design and evaluate intelligent health systems. It examines how digital professionalism, ethical stewardship, regulatory awareness, and patient communication must evolve in parallel with technical capability. Ultimately, the digital doctor is not defined by programming proficiency but by the ability to interpret machine-generated insight responsibly and integrate it with human judgment to ensure that artificial intelligence strengthens equitable, safe, and patient-centered care.

title: Microfluidics in Biomedical Applications: Fundamental Principles, Fabrication Technologies, Emerging Diagnostic Platforms, Organ-on-Chip Systems, Drug Development and Future Perspectives
abstract: Microfluidics has emerged as an important platform for manipulating and analyzing small volumes of fluids, cells, biomolecules, and particles with high precision. Its ability to control microscale flows and integrate multiple analytical steps has enabled diverse biomedical technologies, including lab-on-a-chip, point-of-care diagnostics, organ-on-chip, and microphysiological systems. This review summarizes the fundamental principles of biomedical microfluidics, including microscale fluid dynamics, laminar flow, diffusion, and key dimensionless parameters, together with major platform formats such as continuous-flow, droplet-based, and digital microfluidics. Recent fabrication approaches, including photolithography, soft lithography, molding, laser-based methods, 3D printing, micromilling, and paper- and lamination-based techniques, are also discussed. The review highlights applications in cancer and liquid biopsy, infectious disease diagnostics, cardiovascular and neurological disorders, organ-on-chip models, drug screening and toxicity testing, pharmaceutical synthesis, drug delivery, single-cell analysis, and regenerative and reproductive medicine. Particular attention is given t

title: Personalized, Data-Rich, and Population-Level Care
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare by enabling integration of genomic sequencing, wearable sensor streams, electronic health records, and environmental exposure data into predictive and preventive clinical systems. These advances support a transition from reactive treatment toward individualized precision health while simultaneously strengthening population-level analytics and public health decision making. Polygenic risk modeling, pharmacogenomics, real-world evidence platforms, and learning health systems illustrate how multimodal biomedical data infrastructures can improve early detection, treatment selection, and disease forecasting. However, these innovations introduce challenges involving algorithmic bias, privacy governance, interoperability, and equitable access to emerging technologies. Responsible deployment of large-scale health data requires transparency, regulatory oversight, and inclusive datasets that reflect diverse populations. The future of medicine will depend on balancing personalization with fairness while ensuring that AI-driven healthcare improves outcomes not only for individuals but also for entire communities through precision public h

title: Pharmaceutical Sales and Marketing: A review
abstract: Healthcare has historically relied on population-based, generalized treatment protocols, often leading to trial-and-error prescribing, delayed diagnoses, and variable treatment outcomes across individuals. A digital twin in healthcare is defined as a dynamic, continuously evolving virtual representation of an individual patient, organ, physiological system, or disease process. It is constructed through the integration of multi-modal biomedical data, including genomic and multi-omics profiles, electronic health records (HER), medical imaging (MRI, CT, ultrasound), real-time physiological signals from wearable and IoT sensors, and behavioral/lifestyle data. Methodology/Approach: This study/review synthesizes current literature and technological frameworks underlying healthcare digital twins, examining the convergence of enabling technologies - artificial intelligence, machine learning, cloud and edge computing, IoT-based sensing, and mechanistic physiological modeling - that make real-time, patient-specific simulation computationally feasible. Significance: Digital twins represent a fundamental shift from reactive, population-averaged medicine toward predictive, preventive, and indiv

title: Operationalizing biological interpretability in health-related visual stimuli using multimodal artificial intelligence as standardized non-human raters
abstract: Abstract Evaluation and assessment research in health communication requires structured, construct-based approaches for interpreting visual materials. This study introduces the Asclepius Biological Interpretability Scale, developed through a two-stage modified Delphi process (a joint image-and-item panel followed by an independent item-only panel) grounded in the Biopsychosocial Model and Visual Literacy Theory, and examines whether multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) systems can reproducibly apply this framework relative to internally generated human reference scores. Six artworks (four health-themed and two controls) were evaluated by three multimodal AI models and four researchers (internal human reference) using a standardized protocol with independent researcher-operated accounts, memory-isolation procedures, repeated assessments over two days, and the final 20-item scale. Because Image Type varied across only six stimuli, health-themed versus control differences were summarized at the image level (Cohen’s d), human–AI differences were summarized descriptively at the rater level, and reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Spearman

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmacovigilance: Current Applications and Future Perspectives
abstract: Pharmacovigilance (PV) is the science and practice of detecting, assessing, understanding, and preventing adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and other medication-related problems. The increasing volume of healthcare data generated through electronic health records, spontaneous reporting systems, biomedical literature, social media platforms, and realworld evidence databases has created significant challenges for traditional pharmacovigilance methods. Artificial Intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), natural language processing (NLP), and large language models (LLMs), has emerged as a transformative technology capable of improving drug safety surveillance. AI-based approaches facilitate automated signal detection, adverse event identification, duplicate report detection, causality assessment, and pharmacovigilance workflow optimization. Recent studies demonstrate that machine-learning models often outperform conventional statistical methods in identifying safety signals while reducing manual workload. Despite these advances, challenges related to data quality, algorithmic bias, interpretability, regulatory acceptance, and ethical concerns remain barriers
authors: Hiten Thakkar, Mansi Vasava, Vankar Padamdas, Pathak Shailly, Dr. Ria Memoria*

title: Beyond Risk: Sexual Health Vulnerability in University Students
abstract: Aim: To examine multilevel sexual-health vulnerability in higher education and distinguish evidence about knowledge, preventive behaviour, service use and infection-related outcomes. Subject and Methods: The authors conducted a structured critical review of a pre-existing 118-reference bibliography, retaining a publication boundary of 25 May 2026. The reference-based evidence map was documented on 8 October 2026. Sources were classified by population, design and relevance; 38 candidate reports received content-level assessment. Source-linked information and the availability of supporting material were recorded. The review was human-led, with artificial intelligence used as an assistive tool. Results: Thirty-three empirical higher-education reports were charted and 85 references retained as context. The mapped reports comprised 18 cross-sectional analyses, six randomised trials, five other intervention evaluations, three qualitative studies and one participatory mixed-methods study. They described gaps between knowledge and practice, uneven testing and vaccine uptake, and barriers involving confidentiality, stigma and service design. Digital interventions had outcome-specific findin

title: Artificial intelligence in healthcare in practice: tools, applications and perspectives for clinicians, researchers and educators — an international educational review
abstract: Abstract Introduction: The digital transformation of healthcare systems has been accompanied, since the early 2020s, by the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), further accelerated by the emergence of generative AI and large language models (LLMs). Beyond broad discussions about the potential of AI, healthcare professionals, researchers, and educators need practical guidance regarding available tools, their applications, performance, limitations, and the conditions required for their responsible use. Objective: To provide an international, critical, and educational synthesis of the major applications of AI in clinical practice, biomedical research, and health sciences education, while examining its potential benefits, limitations, associated risks, and the conditions required for safe and responsible use, particularly in resource limited settings. Methods: A structured narrative review of the literature was conducted using publications indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. The literature search was supplemented by institutional documents from the World Health Organization (WHO), UNESCO, and the European Union, as well as selected sy

title: Proceedings of the 7th National Big Data Health Science Conference
abstract: We are excited to present this proceeding from the 7 th National Big Data Health Science Conference that took place February 12-13 th , 2026 in Columbia, SC.The conference, which is supported in part by NIH, centers on the critical questions and emerging methods in big data health science which are contributing to the present and future of healthcare.The purpose of the conference is to foster multidisciplinary collaboration and serve as a venue for the exchange of new concepts, methods, and findings.The conference aims to bring together researchers from academia, government, and industry to share theoretical, methodological, and substantive knowledge about Big Data in biomedical science and public health.This is the seventh year that the University of South Carolina Big Data Health Science Center (BDHSC) has hosted the National Big Data Health Science Conference.The theme of the 2026 conference was "Unlocking the Power of Big Data in Health: Bridging the Gap Between Discovery and Delivery." title: Explainable Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Precision Laboratory Diagnosis: Integrating Biomarkers, Molecular Profiles, Immunological Signatures, and Clinical Data
abstract: Background: Precision laboratory diagnosis increasingly relies on the interpretation of heterogeneous biological and clinical information. Conventional workflows tend to examine biomarkers, molecular measurements, immunological findings, and clinical characteristics along partly separate analytical pathways. Artificial intelligence (AI) can uncover complex relationships in high-dimensional biomedical data, yet many such systems remain hard to interpret at the point of clinical use. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) renders algorithmic outputs more transparent by identifying the features, modalities, and interactions that shape a prediction. Objective: This manuscript proposes an explainable multimodal AI framework for precision laboratory diagnosis, termed XMAI-PLD, which unites conventional laboratory biomarkers, molecular profiles, immunological signatures, and clinical data within a single analytical architecture. The framework is designed to support, rather than supplant, laboratory expertise and clinical judgement. title: An intelligent systems explanation of type 2 diabetes and a narrative to promote lifestyle change
abstract: Type 2 diabetes is an error in the glycemic control system caused by insulin resistance. Self-organizing control systems use artificial intelligence to monitor and correct how they function and are used in modern applications of robotics. The development of type 2 diabetes is gradual and reversible through lifestyle changes, and this is consistent with insulin resistance being formed through a self-organizing or intelligent control system rather than the traditional control system on which current biomedical control systems are modelled. Lifestyles that induce high levels of glycemic variation would, in an intelligent control system, be detected as excessive oscillation, and an intelligent system can reduce oscillation by reducing the amplification. Insulin resistance represents low amplification in the glycemic control system. Intelligent control system functioning requires a network architecture, so if the glycemic control system is self-organizing, then it should be part of a network system that provides intelligent functioning for other control systems, and error in the glycemic control system would contribute to errors in other control systems and to a state of general network

title: Large language models in healthcare: Mapping the global research landscape through bibliometric and science mapping analyses (2022–2025)
abstract: The rapid emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed healthcare research by enabling advances in clinical decision support, biomedical text mining, medical education, electronic health record analysis, and healthcare communication. Despite the explosive growth of this research area, a comprehensive understanding of its scientific development, intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, and emerging research directions remains limited. This study provides a bibliometric and science mapping analysis of the global research landscape on LLMs in healthcare published between 2022 and 2025. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using publications indexed exclusively in the Scopus database from 2022 to 2025. Data were analyzed using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny for descriptive bibliometric indicators and VOSviewer for science-mapping analyses, including author cocitation, keyword co-occurrence, overlay visualization, and international collaboration networks. Scientific productivity, citation impact, leading journals, authors, institutions, countries, intellectual structure, conceptual evolution, and emerging research frontiers were systematically examined. The

title: Editorial Call for Papers: Special Issue on Case Reports & Clinical Vignettes
abstract: In contemporary clinical medicine and biomedical engineering, large-scale clinical trials and systematic reviews establish standard care protocols, yet individual case reports remain the primary mechanism for detecting novel disease manifestations, unexpected therapeutic outcomes, and early-stage technological innovations at the bedside. This Editorial introduces the Medical Technologies Journal (MTJ) Special Issue dedicated exclusively to Innovative Case Reports & Clinical Vignettes. Derived from the keynote framework "The Epistemological and Pedagogical Value of Case Reports in Clinical Literature: Why and How to Publish," this issue addresses the critical need for structured, peer-reviewed documentation of single-patient observations. The scope encompasses technology-assisted diagnostics, rare pathologies, real-world evaluations of artificial intelligence decision-support tools, biomedical engineering applications, and unexpected clinical complications. To ensure high editorial standards, peer-review integrity, and broad database visibility, this Special Issue bridges bedside clinical observations with scholarly publication to accelerate the adoption of technology-driven patient

title: Advancing Drug Discovery via AI and In Silico Approaches
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly become a paradigm shift in driving in-silico research to provide new solutions to old drug discovery and development challenges. AI facilitates fast design of drugs, precise prediction of drug-target interactions, better Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) profiling and more toxicological screenings by using machine learning, deep learning and generative algorithms. The combination of AI and molecular modeling, simulations, and multi-omics platforms will guarantee accuracy and customization in the development of therapies never previously achieved. Also, AI helps in automation, feature extraction, and natural language processing and may increase the reproducibility and broaden the nature of biomedical research. Although these improvements have been made, several challenges are still present, especially the quality of data, interpretability, ethical concerns, validation systems, and generalizability in non-homogenous populations and in rare diseases. These issues are central to the realization of the potential of AI in precision medicine. Explainable AI, federated learning, quantum computing and regulatory al

Biological Variability and Biomedical Innovation in Personalized Orthodontics: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis
abstract: Background/Objectives: Orthodontic treatment response varies considerably among patients because mechanical loading interacts with individual biological, anatomical, systemic, and behavioral characteristics. Advances in mechanobiology, molecular biomarkers, omics technologies, and artificial intelligence (AI) may support a more personalized approach to treatment. This systematic review (SR) aimed to evaluate human clinical evidence concerning these domains and their potential contribution to predicting orthodontic response, improving clinical decision-making, and reducing adverse effects. Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted through June 2026. Primary studies involving human participants and addressing orthodontic tooth movement (OTM), biological variability, biomarkers, genomics, epigenetics, multi-omics, or AI-supported orthodontics were selected according to predefined eligibility criteria. The review was conducted and reported in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, and heterogeneous evidence was synthesized narratively across four predefined domains. Autonomous AI research agents in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma immunology: from multimodal evidence to experimental validation
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most challenging malignancies due to profound biological heterogeneity, complex stromal organization, and limited responsiveness to current immunotherapies. Recent advances in single-cell sequencing, spatial omics, digital pathology, and multimodal profiling have revealed that PDAC immune states are shaped not only by cellular composition but also by spatial organization, treatment context, and patient-specific evolutionary trajectories. However, the increasing complexity and fragmentation of biomedical evidence create substantial challenges for conventional artificial intelligence (AI) approaches that are typically optimized for predefined analytical tasks. Autonomous AI research agents represent an emerging paradigm that extends beyond predictive modeling by integrating scientific reasoning, retrieval of heterogeneous biomedical knowledge, computational tool orchestration, workflow adaptation, and evidence traceability. In this Review, we examine how agentic AI systems may contribute to PDAC immunology research, from characterization of immune ecosystems and spatial cellular interactions to biomarker discovery, neoantigen

title: Correction: Decoding the mechanisms of acupuncture by neuroimaging: an integrated review from networks to molecules
abstract: With a history spanning millennia, acupuncture is globally utilized for conditions such as chronic low back pain (1), various pain syndromes (2), Alzheimer's disease (3), and functional dyspepsia (4). Despite its clinical application, the biological mechanisms underlying its effects remain incompletely defined. While traditional concepts like "Qi" and "meridians" offer one explanatory framework, a gap persists with modern biomedical understanding (5). Closing this gap through robust mechanistic evidence is essential for acupuncture's integration into contemporary evidence-based medicine.Non-invasive neuroimaging has opened a valuable window into the brain's response to acupuncture (6). Early research focused on identifying activated or deactivated brain regions (7). The field has since progressed towards a systems-level approach, investigating how acupuncture might influence the dynamics of large-scale brain networks and neural circuits (8,9). Yet, interpreting these neuroimaging findings demands careful acknowledgment of their inherent correlational nature and the various confounds present in acupuncture studies.This review provides a comprehensive and critical overview of current

title: Fundamentals, methods, and advances in tribology
Biomedical Signal-to-Image Representations for Artificial Intelligence: A Review
abstract: Biomedical signals such as Electrocardiogram (ECG), Electroencephalogram (EEG), Surface Electromyogram (sEMG), Electromyogram (EMG), Electromyotomogram (EMT), and Photoplethysmography (PPG) are among the most commonly used physiological signals. They provide useful information for diagnosis and monitoring, rehabilitation, and wearable healthcare. However, these signals are not easily analyzed directly because physiological recordings are often non-stationary, nonlinear, noisy, and variable across different subjects and recording instances. This has led to the development of a large number of approaches that transform one-dimensional signals into two-dimensional representations, which can be processed using image-based artificial intelligence. This review discusses spectrograms, scalograms, EMD and Hilbert–Huang representations, recurrence plots, Gramian Angular Fields, and direct image encodings. Their suitability is evaluated with respect to the information they provide and the requirements of downstream learning tasks. The review also compares CNNs, transfer learning, hybrid CNN–recurrent neural networks, and LSTMs, as well as attention networks, Transformers, Vision Transformers

title: Salivary Science in the Lab: A Comprehensive Review of Analytical Platforms and Possibilities
abstract: Saliva is a non-invasive, readily accessible biofluid containing electrolytes, enzymes, proteins, nucleic acids, metabolites, extracellular vesicles, cells, and microorganisms, with growing value in clinical diagnostics and biomedical research. This chapter provides a practical, evidence-based synthesis of laboratory methods for salivary analysis and links platform selection to intended use, specimen type, biological target, expected abundance, matrix behavior, and required analytical performance. Established approaches reviewed include biochemical and enzymatic assays, immunoassays, nucleic acid amplification, proteomics, metabolomics, microbial culture, and sequencing-based microbiome analysis. Emerging technologies, including microfluidic systems, biosensors, CRISPR-based diagnostics, wearable devices, multi-omics integration, and artificial intelligence, are also critically considered. Particular attention is given to pre-analytical variables, including collection method, sampling time, stimulation, diet, oral hygiene, medication use, processing, transport, and storage, as well as to low analyte concentrations, viscosity, oral contamination, matrix interference, and biological

title: Cold Atmospheric Plasma in Biomedicine
abstract: Cold atmospheric plasma has emerged as a promising interdisciplinary technology with rapidly expanding applications in biomedicine and healthcare. This chapter presents a comprehensive overview of the fundamental principles, diagnostic methods, biological interactions, and biomedical applications of cold atmospheric plasma. The historical development of plasma medicine is first discussed, followed by an explanation of key plasma physics concepts. The chapter further explores major plasma generation techniques used in medicine, the experimental and computational methods employed to characterize plasma behaviour. The biological effects of plasma-generated reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, which play a central role in antimicrobial activity, wound healing, tissue regeneration, and cancer therapy. Finally, future perspectives are presented, emphasizing the development of intelligent adaptive plasma systems integrated with advanced diagnostics and artificial intelligence for personalized medical treatment.

title: A comprehensive survey of communication technologies, security frameworks, and intelligent architectures for medical internet of things and quantum-enabled healthcare
abstract: The convergence of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), advanced communication technologies, and biomedical engineering has advanced intelligent, connected healthcare. This comprehensive survey investigates the evolution of IoMT architectures and communication protocols, along with their application across a range of healthcare scenarios. It provides a comparative analysis of short-range and long-range communication technologies, with emphasis on secure, privacy-preserving, and energy-efficient designs tailored for IoMT devices. The review also highlights recent advances in enabling technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and quantum computing, and their growing role in enhancing system intelligence, data security, and diagnostic precision. In addition, the study examines the integration of edge and cloud computing for real-time health monitoring, diagnostics, and decision support. Emerging trends, including AI-enabled IoMT systems, blockchain-based privacy frameworks, and next-generation biomedical sensors, are analyzed in depth. Drawing on over 200 peer-reviewed publications, this work identifies persistent challenges in current IoMT ecosystems, including

title: AI-Driven Plasma Surface Engineering for Advanced Aerospace and Material Applications
abstract: Plasma engineering has become a sophisticated technology for processing surfaces and enhancing functional properties of materials for a wide range of industrial processes. The role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the integration of plasma-based surface engineering and optimization of material properties is explored in this chapter. This emphasizes low temperature and atmospheric plasma processes for coating deposition, surface activation and fabrication of nanostructures. The importance of AI and machine learning for predicting plasma behavior, optimizing process parameters and coating quality is emphasized. Applications such as aerospace, biomedical devices, semiconductor processing and sustainability (CO2 conversion and plasma-assisted catalysis) are discussed. Additionally, experimental diagnostics, numerical simulations, and scalability, process control and industrial integration issues are explored. Finally, future directions towards intelligent and sustainable plasma systems are summarized.

title: Introduction to the Advanced Biophotonics feature issue
abstract: Biophotonics is an interdisciplinary field at the intersection of photonics, biology, and medicine, driving advances in biomedical imaging, sensing, diagnosis, and therapy. With rapid developments in optical imaging, computational optics, artificial intelligence, nanophotonics, and advanced optical instrumentation, this feature issue highlights recent advances that span fundamental research, enabling technologies, and emerging biomedical applications.

title: Innovative Strategies in Modern Drug Discovery and Development
abstract: Pharmaceutical discovery and development continue to be some of the most intricate, financially demanding, and protracted pursuits in the biomedical field, with typical development periods surpassing ten years and failure rates resulting in just a minor percentage of candidates attaining approval. In the last twenty years, a synthesis of computational, biological, and engineering advancements has started to transform this domain. Artificial intelligence and machine learning currently infiltrate almost every phase of the pipeline, from target identification to clinical trial formulation, as deep learning frameworks and generative models facilitate novel molecular design at unparalleled velocity. Structure-oriented and ligand-oriented computer-assisted drug development, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative structure–activity relationship modelling, pharmacophore analysis, as well as virtual and high-throughput screening are evolving in tandem with fragment-based methodologies and DNA-encoded libraries. Simultaneously, multi-omics profiling, systems biology, and network pharmacology are facilitating a comprehensive comprehension of disease biology, whereas C
authors: Sanmay Yadav*, Abhishek Doshi, Sarthak Kole, Mayuri Kore, Sneha Dhekane

title: Artificial intelligence tools for evidence synthesis in the biomedical field: A living rapid review and evidence map
abstract: Evidence synthesis (ES) is costly and time-intensive. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used to automate or semi-automate ES tasks. We conducted a living rapid review of AI tools that automate or semi-automate ES tasks. We searched for published articles and preprints through MEDLINE, Embase, and the Association for Computing Machinery Digital Library from January 1, 2021 through October 15, 2025, supplemented by hand-searching. We included existing reviews to capture evaluations before 2021. Screening was conducted in duplicate at the title/abstract level, with single full-text screening and data extraction verified by a second reviewer. We included 134 studies. Performance varied by task and evaluation approach. Search automation tools showed poor recall (median 17%), although human-in-the-loop approaches improved performance. Tools for identifying randomized controlled trials demonstrated high median recall (98%) and precision (92%). Semi-automated abstract screening tools using active learning reduced screening burden by approximately 50% while maintaining 95% recall. title: Digital and robot-assisted kinesitherapy: A systematic review of clinical efficacy, safety, and translational validity compared to conventional rehabilitation
abstract: The digital transformation of health systems over the past two decades has driven a fundamental shift in kinesitherapy rehabilitation models, with robot-assisted systems, telerehabilitation platforms, virtual and augmented reality, wearable biosensors, and artificial intelligence algorithms creating new clinical paradigms whose efficacy, safety, and applicability in routine clinical practice require rigorous evaluation according to the principles of evidence-based medicine. The purpose of this systematic review was to conduct a critical comparative analysis of the clinical efficacy, safety, and translational validity of digital and robot-assisted rehabilitation models compared to conventional kinesitherapy, and to assess the extent to which technological innovation translates into genuine clinical superiority. Methodologically, the research was designed as a systematic review with critical comparative synthesis, aligned with internationally recognized guidelines for reporting systematic reviews, with research questions structured according to population, intervention, comparison, and outcome; the search was conducted across major biomedical and clinical literature databases for the

title: Трансформация медицинской кибернетики в эпоху искусственного интеллекта: от гомеостаза к персонализированным навигационным системам
abstract: Статья посвящена историческому анализу эволюции кибернетического подхода в биологии и медицине, а также исследованию современных тенденций его конвергенции с технологиями искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) и машинного обучения. Актуальность работы обусловлена необходимостью переосмысления классических кибернетических принципов (обратная связь,гомеостаз, управление) в эпоху цифровой трансформации здравоохранения, перехода к персонализированной и предиктивной медицине,а также появлением новых вызовов, связанных с нелинейностью физиологических систем и интерпретируемостью «черных ящиков»нейросетевых моделей.
