title: Comparative analysis of intelligent predictors using multi-supervised learning models for bioconvective flow of Oldroyd-B nanofluid over a Riga surface in a porous medium
abstract: Efficient control of heat and mass transfer in complex, non-Newtonian fluids is central to improving the energy efficiency of modern thermal management systems, yet such flows remain difficult to model because they couple fluid motion, heat transport, and the swimming behavior of motile microorganisms. Our model describes the thermal bioconvective flow of a non-Newtonian nanofluid containing gyrotactic microorganisms over a porous stretching Riga surface and asks whether artificial intelligence-based predictors can reproduce this behavior more quickly and reliably than purely numerical solutions. The governing equations were first reduced to a system of ordinary differential equations through similarity transformations, then solved with a fourth-order collocation-based boundary value solver. The resulting data set was used to train and compare four supervised machine learning predictors: a long short-term memory network, a nonlinear autoregressive network with exogenous inputs, a random forest regressor, and a support vector regressor. title: Future Trends in Quantum Computing for Medical Research
abstract: The field of quantum computing is also no longer in its infancy but is now being used to transform the healthcare sector with unprecedented computing power; this power can be used to improve machine learning as well as increase the security measures, which will spawn future innovations. The chapter provides an overview of the new environment of quantum-enabled healthcare, especially concentrating on collision points between machine learning and quantum computing to speed up diagnostics, and advancements in tailored healthcare. The quantum-enhanced algorithms would unlock complex biomedical trends that are beyond the capability of classical systems. Simultaneously, quantum cryptography is a security framework capable of providing strong security solutions that are needed to protect sensitive patient data in a healthcare environment that is becoming more digitized. With further development of quantum hardware and algorithms, they are likely to be incorporated in clinical practices, which will bring additional accuracy, efficiency, and ethical practices to medical research and practice. title: Computational Model for Exploration of Microbial Chemotaxis Dynamics on Casson-Maxwell Reactive Fluid in Off-Centered Stagnation Point Flow: A New Frontier in Computational~Intelligence
abstract: Comprehending bioconvection facilitates the modelling of natural processes in aquatic environments and improves the efficacy of systems incorporating microorganism suspensions. It connects biology with fluid dynamics, providing insights into the impact of living creatures on fluid flow behaviour. The current study offers insights into the mechanisms of heat, microorganism and mass transfer in complex fluids, with potential applications in biomedical devices, chemical engineering and industrial processes involving non-Newtonian fluids under the influence of electromagnetic and thermal effects. The off-centered stagnation point flow of a Casson-Maxwell fluid across a spinning disk under the influence of Soret, Dufour and magnetic field is investigated. The Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg fourth-fifth order (RKF-45) method~is~used to numerically solve the reduced ordinary differential equations (ODEs), and an artificial neural network (ANN) is employed to~increase stability and accuracy. The microbial profile decreases as Lewis and Peclet numbers rise. As the Dufour number and radiation parameter increase, the temperature profile rises.

title: Iridium‐Based Nanomaterials: Precise Fabrication, Structural and Electronic Modulation, and Biomedical Applications
abstract: Iridium (Ir), a representative platinum-group metal, possesses unique 5d electronic structure, multiple accessible oxidation states, exceptional chemical stability, and highly tunable coordination chemistry, making it an attractive platform for biomedical nanotechnology. Recent advances in nanomaterial synthesis and interfacial engineering have enabled the development of diverse Ir-based nanomaterials, including coordination complexes, nanoparticles, single-atom nanocatalysts, and metal-organic frameworks, with precisely engineered electronic structures and catalytic properties. Through the rational regulation of valence states, crystal phases, defect structures, and metal-support interfacial interactions, these nanomaterials exhibit remarkable redox activity, enzyme-like catalysis, and responsiveness to external-field stimuli. In this review, we systematically summarize recent advances in the design, fabrication, structural and electronic engineering, physicochemical properties, and biological applications of Ir-based nanomaterials. Particular attention is given to their enzyme-mimetic activities, catalytic mechanisms, and unique bidirectional oxidative-antioxidative regulatory ca

title: Generative AI in Publishing: An Editors' Panel on Ethics and Policies
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping scholarly research faster than journals have developed stable norms for its use. This article presents an edited thematic account of a 2026 Joint Statistical Meetings panel that brought together editorial perspectives from mathematical statistics, data science, biomedical statistics, and general statistical scholarship. The discussion examines journal policies, disclosure, authorship and research integrity, peer-review confidentiality, researcher training, editorial workload, access, and possible future models of scholarly publishing. Panelists shared commitments to human accountability, the protection of confidential submissions, and disclosure of consequential assistance, while offering different recommendations on assistance with research ideas and proofs, disclosure requirements, automated review, and policy enforcement. By distinguishing shared principles from unresolved implementation questions, the article clarifies the choices facing statistical publishing and outlines an agenda for evaluating policies and practices as GenAI evolves. The account seeks to foster continued discussion of GenAI in scientific communication

title: Transparency of Artificial Intelligence Prediction Model Studies in the Biomedical Literature
abstract: This cross-sectional meta-research study will assess transparency in biomedical artificial intelligence diagnostic and prognostic prediction-model studies published from 2010 to 2025. We will examine English-language original research available in the PubMed Central Open Access subset for five indicators: conflict-of-interest disclosure, funding disclosure, protocol registration, data sharing, and code sharing. Automated assessment will be validated through manual review of a sample of articles. We will estimate the prevalence of each indicator, describe changes over time, and examine differences across journals, fields of science, and publication licences.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Prevention and Early Detection of Sexually Transmitted Infections—Review
abstract: Background/Objectives: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) continue to pose a global public health problem, exacerbated by barriers to access, stigma and the limitations of traditional screening models. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a tool with the potential to enhance early detection, risk stratification and personalised counselling. This article critically analyses the current role of AI in STI prevention (encompassing primary and secondary prevention, including early detection), identifying validated applications, limitations and ethical implications. Methods: A narrative review was conducted of the literature published between 2020 and 2026, using biomedical databases, with a focus on original studies, systematic reviews and documents from leading organisations on the applications of machine learning, computer vision and conversational agents in the prevention, diagnosis and surveillance of STIs, including HIV. Results: Machine learning algorithms applied to clinical and behavioural data stratify the individual risk of STIs with satisfactory performance, supporting the recommendation for pre-exposure prophylaxis. title: Nano Robotics in Medicine: Advancements, Applications and Future Prospects
abstract: Nano robotics is a new and emerging discipline that combines nanotechnology and robotics to develop Nano scale robots that can execute specific tasks at atomic, molecular, and cellular levels. The Nano robots, which are usually between 1 and 100 nanometres in size, are intended to function in different biomedical applications such as cancer treatment, targeted drug delivery, surgery, and gene therapy. By means of sophisticated fabrication methods, Nano robots can be made from biocompatible materials with little immune reaction and effective functioning in the body. Medical Nanorobots like respirocytes, microbivores, and clottocytes imitate biological processes to maximize therapeutic benefit. Respirocytes work as artificial RBCs, transporting O2 and CO2with high efficiency, whereas microbivores are used as artificial white blood cells that destroy pathogens with high accuracy. Clottocytes, meanwhile, quickly restore blood clotting, minimizing haemorrhage complications. Sensors, actuators, and on-board computational systems integrated into them provide the ability to navigate autonomously and sense in real-time, enhancing diagnostic efficacy and therapeutic accuracy. title: MediNet: Simplifying Federated and Privacy-Preserving AI Deployment in Healthcare
abstract: MOTIVATION: The application of Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning (DL) in healthcare is increasingly feasible in principle, yet remains inaccessible in practice for most clinical institutions. Beyond the well-known challenge of data privacy regulations that prevent centralization of patient records, two further barriers limit adoption. First, deploying a federated learning infrastructure requires substantial technical expertise: configuring distributed training environments, implementing privacy-preserving mechanisms such as Differential Privacy (DP), and managing secure inter-institutional communication demands specialized knowledge that most healthcare organizations do not possess. Second, designing and configuring DL models (selecting architectures, tuning hyperparameters, interpreting results) currently requires machine learning expertise that clinical professionals, including researchers and physicians, typically lack. Existing federated learning frameworks address the infrastructure problem but impose a steep learning curve that effectively excludes non-specialized users. title: Terahertz Technology – A New Frontier in Oral Cancer Diagnostics
abstract: Background: Terahertz (THz) technology is a promising non-ionizing and non-invasive imaging modality that has gained considerable attention in biomedical diagnostics owing to its ability to differentiate tissues based on water content, dielectric properties, and unique molecular signatures. Recent advances in THz imaging, including near-field, single-pixel, and real-time techniques, have improved spatial resolution, imaging speed, and tissue characterization, facilitating applications in cancer detection and intraoperative tumour margin assessment. Aim: This narrative review aims to provide an overview of the current applications and emerging advances in THz technology, with particular emphasis on its potential applications in oral medicine and dentistry, cancer diagnostics, tissue characterization, and intraoperative guidance. Methods: An extensive narrative review of the available literature was undertaken to summarize the principles, imaging modalities, biomedical applications, and recent technological advances in THz technology, with particular emphasis on applications in oral medicine and dentistry. title: The Changing Role of AI Agents in Science Must be Recognized
abstract: Current editorial guidelines from organizations such as the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) treat generative artificial intelligence (AI) primarily as an administrative assistant or text manipulator, relegating its contributions to footnotes or acknowledgments. This policy framework misinterprets the operational reality of modern biomedical research, where advanced language models function as active intellectual partners capable of logical stress-testing, data synthesis, and hypothesis generation. Conflating operational cognitive contribution with legal and ethical accountability creates unnecessary opacity in scholarly publishing. To resolve this tension, this paper examines four structural credit frameworks—ranging from the institutional status quo to dual-track independent lists and expanded contributor taxonomies. We propose that medical publishing must evolve beyond obsolete binary definitions, establishing transparent attribution models that separate human regulatory liability from the recognition of machine-assisted scientific co-creation.

title: AI algorithms empowered terahertz functional devices design and perception applications
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms have profoundly reshaped scientific research paradigms, providing data-driven, automated, and intelligent solutions to problems traditionally constrained by complexity and inefficiency. Recently, the integration of AI with terahertz (THz) technology has emerged as a highly significant research area. This is because AI algorithms not only facilitate the design of metasurface devices but also assist in the processing of data from THz-related research. We reviewed recent research progress from two major perspectives. 1) Device structural design: AI has been applied in inverse modeling and parameter optimization, substantially improving design efficiency and expanding functional diversity. 2) Practical applications: AI enhances THz data analysis capabilities and imaging quality, enabling more accurate and efficient approaches for non-destructive detection, material identification, and biomedical exploration. We summarized the main advances and controversies, established an integrated framework of device design and application, and highlighted future directions.

title: A Zero‐Dimensional Hybrid Tin Halide with Efficient Near‐Infrared Luminescence for Intelligent Defect Inspection
abstract: ABSTRACT Near‐infrared (NIR) luminescent materials have attracted considerable attention for biomedical imaging and industrial inspection because of their deep penetration capability and strong technical adaptability. Coupling NIR luminescence with deep‐learning algorithms further offers a promising route toward intelligent inspection with enhanced automation and accuracy. Here, we report a 0D, Sn halide (MBI) 2 SnCl 6 (MBI = 2‐methylbenzimidazole), composed of organic MBI + cations and isolated [SnCl 6 ] 2− octahedra, and Sb substitution yields broadband NIR emission with a highest photoluminescence quantum yield of 59.19%. On this basis, subvisible defects on silicon wafer surfaces can be clearly visualized. When integrated with a U‐Net‐based convolutional neural network, the NIR imaging output enables rapid and automated defect identification, allowing accurate discrimination between qualified and defective wafers as well as subclassification of defective samples, with an average accuracy of 90.92% and an average recall of 92.92%. title: Recent advances in dielectric and two-dimensional material-based surface plasmon resonance biosensors for ultrasensitive refractive index sensing and diverse applications
abstract: Advanced biosensors utilizing Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) are becoming powerful label-free optical sensing platforms for the real-time detection of biochemical interactions owing to their incredibly high sensitivity toward refractive index (RI) changes. Conventional metal-based SPR sensors typically suffer from optical losses, large resonance curves, and degraded detection sensitivity. The combination of widespread advances in high-RI dielectric materials and two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials has greatly contributed to the improvement of SPR sensor performance, as a result of improved electromagnetic field confinement, enhanced biomolecular interactions, and higher overall sensing efficiency. This review summarizes the progress in dielectric- and 2D material-based SPR biosensors for both applications: ultrasensitive RI sensing and diverse biomedical, environmental, and chemical sensing. The basic concept of SPR, sensing performance indicators, and the nature of dielectric and 2D materials, multilayer devices, and theoretical modelling strategies are reviewed in detail. title: Interfacial thermodynamics and data-driven design of polymeric nanofluids: Structure–property relationships, spectroscopic insights, and intelligent functional performance
abstract: Polymeric nanofluids have emerged as advanced multifunctional materials with significant potential in thermal management, energy systems, biomedical engineering, advanced manufacturing, and smart-material applications. Their performance is governed by complex interfacial interactions between nanoparticles and polymer matrices, which influence colloidal stability, rheological behavior, thermal transport, electrical conductivity, and long-term durability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamental interfacial science, structure–property relationships, and functional performance mechanisms governing polymeric nanofluids. Particular emphasis is placed on nanoparticle–polymer interactions, surface functionalization strategies, interphase formation, microstructural evolution, rheo-chemical coupling, thermal transport pathways, and electrokinetic phenomena. The review further highlights the application of advanced characterization techniques, especially ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and chemometric analysis, for elucidating molecular interactions and establishing quantitative structure–property correlations. abstract: INTELLIGENT NANOROBOTIC MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT Toward a Civilization of Programmable Matter, Distributed Fabrication, and AI-Guided Micro/Nanoscale Production Intelligent Nanorobotic Manufacturing at the Limit is a large-scale research exploration of what may happen when additive manufacturing, micro/nanorobotics, smart materials, swarm coordination, artificial intelligence, metrology, repair, and governance begin to converge into a single manufacturing architecture. The central question of this book is no longer simply: Can we build smaller robots? It is: Can intelligence, geometry, materials, robotic agency, and distributed fabrication converge into a manufacturing civilization capable of translating intention into verified physical structure? Across 82 chapters, the book examines manufacturing from the level of geometry and material response to actuation, sensing, energy, communication, AI planning, swarm coordination, repair, provenance, authorization, safety, economics, biomedical translation, planetary industry, starship fabrication, and long-term civilization continuity. Precision Nutrition for Gut Health: Bridging Gut Microbiome Science and Ayurvedic Ahara Principles
abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of digestive, metabolic and immune health. Ayurveda has traditionally advocated individualised dietary planning through concepts including Prakriti (constitutional phenotype), Agni (digestive and metabolic capacity), Dosha status, Ahara (diet), and Pathya (wholesome dietary practices) emphasising that dietary recommendations should be tailored according to individual characteristics. This review explores the relationship between gut microbiome science and precision nutrition and examines their conceptual convergence with Ayurvedic dietary principles. Current evidence indicates that the gut microbiome significantly influences nutrient metabolism, dietary responses, and disease susceptibility, supporting personalised nutritional strategies. Studies investigating associations between constitutional phenotypes and gut microbial profiles have provided insights into integrating Ayurvedic concepts with contemporary microbiome science. title: The Translational Gap in Neonatal Sepsis Prediction: A Scoping Review of Prospective Artificial Intelligence Validations in the NICU
abstract: Background and Clinical Context Neonatal sepsis remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among premature infants in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). Because the clinical signs of sepsis in premature infants are often subtle and non-specific, diagnosis is frequently delayed, leading to rapid deterioration. In recent years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as highly promising tools to predict sepsis hours or even days before clinical onset by analyzing continuous physiological data (such as heart rate variability) and electronic health records. However, a critical "translational gap" exists. The current scientific literature is overwhelmed with retrospective, in silico models trained on historical databases (like MIMIC-III) that have never been tested on real patients. Despite the technological hype, very few algorithms have successfully transitioned from the computer science laboratory to bedside implementation in the NICU. title: Nanostructure-integrated electrochemical devices for biomedical applications
abstract: Nanostructured device-integrated electrochemical biosensing is advancing clinical and healthcare platforms for the rapid, sensitive, and cost-effective detection of clinically important viruses, bacteria, biomarkers, and other biomolecules in precision medicine. These biosensors exploit the unique properties of functionalized nanostructures including high surface area, tunable electrochemical behavior, and efficient signal transduction to achieve improved analytical performance compared with conventional sensor technologies. In particular, the incorporating of nanostructured materials such as metal nanoparticles and graphene-based materials can offer enhance sensitivity, faster response times, and greater adaptability to a wide range of biomarker targets, including viral and bacterial pathogens. Furthermore, the integration of advanced data processing and artificial intelligence (AI) enables signal denoising, feature extraction, pattern recognition, and predictive modeling, thereby expanding the capabilities of these biosensing platforms. title: Artificial Intelligence in the Diagnosis of Oral Potentially Malignant Disorders: A Critical Narrative Review of Diagnostic Validity, Prognostic Value and Translational Readiness
abstract: Oral potentially malignant disorders carry a variable but clinically meaningful risk of progression to oral squamous cell carcinoma, and their recognition depends on visual examination and on histological grading of epithelial dysplasia, both of which are subjective and unevenly available. Artificial intelligence has been proposed as a means of standardising detection, triaging lesions in settings without specialists, and estimating the risk of malignant transformation. This critical narrative review examines whether the published evidence supports these expectations. Peer-reviewed literature published between January 2000 and 27 July 2026 was identified through structured searches of biomedical and multidisciplinary scholarly indexes, supplemented by citation searching, and was appraised for study design, reference standard, validation strategy, calibration, reporting quality and clinical applicability. title: AI-Optimized Microneedle Platforms for Precision Occular Drug Delivery System
abstract: ABSTRACT: Ocular diseases are considered a primary cause of visual handicaps, and their management is often constrained by the eye's anatomical and physiological barriers. Traditional ocular drug delivery approaches — eye drops, ointments, systemic, periocular, and intravitreal injections — are commonly characterized by reduced bioavailability, rapid drug clearance, poor tissue penetration, and poor compliance. Microneedle (MN)-based ocular drug delivery systems have been proposed as a minimally invasive approach to overcome such limitations and have been demonstrated to enable targeted delivery to anterior and posterior ocular tissues. Dissolving, coated, hollow, bio-inspired, and cryo-microneedles have each been demonstrated to enhance bioavailability and sustain drug release while reducing dose frequency. Continuous improvements in material science, microfabrication, and biomedical engineering of ocular microneedles, along with the increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) for microneedle design, formulation, drug release, computational modeling, and personalized therapy, have enabled such devices to offer a substantial improvement in terms of safety, precision, and therape

title: The application value of artificial intelligence in medical imaging: foundations, progress, and challenges
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming medical imaging, reshaping the field as it does everyday life. As imaging data grow in complexity and clinical workloads continue to rise, AI has become increasingly essential for improving diagnostic efficiency and precision. However, despite these technical advances, the clinical adoption of AI in medical imaging remains fragmented, with limited generalizability, insufficient interpretability, and unclear clinical responsibility. In this review, we critically examine the evolution of AI in medical imaging, with a particular focus on its functional roles across the imaging workflow and its actual contributions to contemporary clinical needs. We systematically analyze current application paradigms, identify methodological and translational bottlenecks, and discuss emerging strategies to improve model robustness, interpretability, and clinical integration. In addition, we identify key barriers to the practical implementation of AI in medical imaging, including challenges related to cross-domain generalizability, data privacy issues and regulatory compliance. title: A blockchain-based non-fungible tokens framework for ownership and intellectual property preserving with controlled access to medical datasets
abstract: Abstract The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced data analytics techniques across biomedical research, diagnostics and personalized medicine has established high-quality medical datasets as foundational resources. However, a significant impediment to progress is the reluctance of data owners to share these valuable resources because existing infrastructures provide no reliable guarantee of ownership or intellectual property preservation, in addition to the control over unauthorized usage. Consequently, vast quantities of recorded, high-potential data remain unused within private repositories. To overcome this barrier, a blockchain-based framework leveraging Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) is introduced in this paper to preserve ownership of medical datasets. The general workflow involves minting an NFT representing the dataset (stored encrypted off-chain), allowing users to request time-limited access via a smart contract. Access is granted using ephemeral decryption keys, enforcing fine-grained and revocable control. title: Artificial intelligence driven multimodal medical image segmentation algorithm: applied research and clinical verification
abstract: Abstract Multimodal medical imaging—comprising CT, MRI, and PET—is fundamental to modern diagnosis, lesion localization, and treatment planning. The accuracy and speed of segmenting these modalities directly affect clinical decisions. To overcome limitations in cross-modal integration, sensitivity to small lesions, generalization, and workflow compatibility, we propose AMIS-Net, an AI-driven segmentation network. Built on an encoder-decoder backbone, AMIS-Net incorporates a Dual Attention Module (DAM) for adaptive feature recalibration and a Small Object Capture (SOC) module for multi-scale feature extraction. A hybrid loss function balances pixel-wise training to address severe class imbalance. Extensive validation on CHAOS, Synapse, and a proprietary clinical dataset shows that AMIS-Net consistently outperforms U-Net, ResUNet, and STUNet. On Synapse, it achieves a Dice of 83.17% and HD95 of 20.89 mm, with per-organ Dice scores ranging from 74.85% (esophagus) to 94.21% (liver). abstract: Deep learning has made significant advancements in medical data analysis, which has made it possible to advance the diagnostics process, prognostication, and therapeutic care through new methods. However, the usability of artificial neural networks in common clinical practice is still hindered by their excessive computational, memory, and power requirements, which do not make them applicable to the resource-stressed conditions of a portable imaging device, a wearable sensor, or an edge-computing system. The limitations are dealt with in this chapter by discussing ways of making medical neural networks more efficient. The question of interest is model-compression methods such as pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, and neural architecture search, aimed at reducing the computational cost while preserving diagnostic quality. Also, the chapter argues for improvements in training time, which include transfer learning, self-supervised learning, and few-shot learning, which alleviate the challenges posed by small labeled medical datasets. title: The Next Language of Biology May Not Be Human
abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how cancer biology is read, searched, modeled, and turned into hypotheses. But scientific AI does not meet biology directly. Much of what it learns has already passed through English, abstracts, pathway labels, database entries, and text-mined relations. New foundation models create a second translation problem. They can learn from molecular structures, single-cell profiles, perturbation data, and clinical trajectories without first converting those relations into human-readable explanations. This could expand biological and biomedical discovery, but it also changes the burden of proof. If a model proposes a target, biomarker, stratification, or perturbation that is reproducible but only partly interpretable, what evidence should be required before researchers or clinicians act on it? We argue that interpretability is not only an engineering problem. It is a translation problem. When the internal language of a model is difficult to read, the external evidence must become stronger: clear provenance, experimental challenge, cross-population validation, reproducibility, and accountable human judgment.

title: Inferring the Landscapes of Mutation and Recombination in the Common Marmoset ( Callithrix jacchus ) in the Presence of Twinning and Hematopoietic Chimerism
abstract: ABSTRACT The common marmoset ( Callithrix jacchus ) is one of the most commonly used nonhuman primate models in biomedical research. Yet, the population genomics of the species remains relatively poorly characterized, despite the critical importance of this knowledge in many areas of research including genome‐wide association studies, models of polygenic risk scores, and scans for the targets of selection. This neglect owes, at least in part, to two biological peculiarities related to the reproductive mode of the species—frequent twinning and sibling chimerism—which are likely to affect standard population genetic approaches relying on assumptions underlying the Wright–Fisher model. Using high‐quality population genomic data, we here infer the rates and landscapes of mutation and recombination—two fundamental processes dictating the levels and patterns of genetic variability—in the presence of these biological features, and discuss our findings in light of recent work in primates. Our results suggest that, while the species exhibits relatively low neutral mutation rates, rates of recombination are in the range of those observed in other anthropoids. title: Denario Project: Deep Knowledge Artificial Intelligence Agents for Scientific Discovery
abstract: We present , an Artificial Intelligence (AI) multiagent system designed to serve as a scientific research assistant. can perform many different tasks, such as generating ideas, checking the literature, developing research plans, writing and executing code, making plots, and drafting a scientific paper. The system has a modular architecture, allowing it to handle specific tasks, such as generating an idea or carrying out near end-to-end scientific analysis using as a deep-research backend (end-to-end except for the novelty assessment, which is intentionally left for the user to inspect). In this work, we describe in detail and its modules, and illustrate its capabilities by presenting multiple AI-generated papers generated by it in many different scientific disciplines such as astrophysics, biology, biophysics, biomedical informatics, chemistry, material science, mathematical physics, medicine, neuroscience, and planetary science. can also produce work that combines ideas from different disciplines, which we illustrate with a single ( N = 1 ) example: a paper that applies methods from quantum physics and machine learning to astrophysical data. title: Internet of things-enabled biomedical engineering: current applications, challenges, and emerging directions
abstract: The internet of medical things (IoMT) is a structured integrative review of the internet of things (IoT) that focuses on the medical field, specifically on the integration of physiological sensors, medical devices, communication networks, and the clinical information systems to monitor and track patients' health and conditions continuously, and use data to support medical treatment. Through July 2026, a reproducible search and evidence audit of PubMed/MEDLINE, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, publisher/digital object identifier (DOI) records, and authoritative regulatory and standards repositories was conducted. The final evidence base consisted of 65 distinct sources that were assessed using a set of explicit eligibility criteria and evidence weighting. Wearable atrial-fibrillation screening, remote monitoring, digital inhalers and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), and connected hospital infrastructure were shown to be clinically significant in large-scale studies, but such benefits were only seen if there was confirmatory pathway, workflow integration, data quality and persistent engagement. title: Explainable machine learning assisted terahertz metamaterial absorber for multi-cancer cell biosensing
abstract: This work presents a terahertz (THz) metamaterial absorber (MMA) for sensitive detection of dielectric variations associated with skin, blood, cervical, and breast cancer cells. The proposed absorber operates within the 6.2–7.2 THz frequency range and exhibits five distinct absorption resonances with a maximum absorption of 99.99%, achieved through effective impedance matching and strong electromagnetic field confinement. Key resonance frequencies (notably at 6.499 THz and 7.015 THz) are strategically positioned within relative terahertz atmospheric transmission windows, mitigating atmospheric attenuation and supporting stable biosensing performance in indoor environments. The proposed biosensor demonstrates excellent sensing characteristics, achieving a maximum refractive-index sensitivity of 1139.0 GHz/RIU (1.139 THz/RIU), a quality factor of 136.3, and a figure of merit of 22.33 RIU −1 . Distinct resonance shifts are observed for normal and malignant skin, blood, cervical, and breast cancer cells, indicating the potential of the sensor for multi-cancer discrimination. title: Patient-Specific Implant Design: Current Evidence for Artificial Intelligence, Imaging and Computational Planning—A Systematic Review of the Biomedical-Indexed Literature
abstract: Background and objectives: Patient-specific skeletal implants are designed through a pipeline of imaging, computational planning and, increasingly, artificial intelligence. Each pillar has its own validation literature, but no review has asked what evidence supports each one in implant design itself. We mapped that evidence from the biomedical-indexed literature in this paper. Methods: A systematic review was conducted under a protocol committed before retrieval (PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, SWiM). MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Crossref and OpenAlex were searched on 2 and 3 September 2026 for primary studies from 2015 onwards applying artificial intelligence, an evaluated imaging pipeline or computational planning to an implant whose geometry derives from the individual patient’s anatomy. Engineering indexes were unavailable, so this review maps biomedical-indexed literature, and a bounded probe was used to estimate what that omits. Two artificial intelligence screeners from different vendors screened every record; every clinical study was appraised twice, independently, by assessors from different vendors. title: Leon Kass's Conception of Human Dignity: An Integrated Philosophical Framework for Contemporary Bioethics
abstract: Abstract The concept of human dignity has acquired renewed philosophical significance in the light of rapid developments in biotechnology, genetic engineering, artificial intelligence, reproductive medicine and end-of-life care. While such scientific innovations offer unprecedented benefits, they can provoke reductive interpretations of the human person, encouraging the view that human beings are primarily biological organisms or technological objects. This article examined Leon Kass's conception of human dignity as an integrated philosophical framework for engaging these contemporary bioethical challenges. Drawing upon philosophical analysis and critical evaluation, the study argued that Kass's conception of human dignity is grounded on the intrinsic nature of the human person and not on autonomy, utility or social recognition. Furthermore, Kass's bioethical vision incorporated philosophical anthropology, scientific reflection and moral reasoning as a way of defending the uniqueness of human life against technological reductionism. title: Integrated Systems for Self-Powered Sensing and Closed-Loop Therapy
abstract: Abstract The convergence of artificial intelligence and biomedicine is creating opportunities for smart sensing systems in precision medicine. Conventional sensors, however, remain dependent on external power sources. Short battery life, difficult replacement, and potential biological risks limit their use in implantable, wearable, and long-term monitoring applications. Self-powered smart sensing systems offer a promising alternative. These devices harvest ambient energy from mechanical, thermal, chemical, or biological sources and convert it directly into electricity. The result is an integrated sense-and-power unit. This paradigm provides a direction for next-generation medical devices. In this review, we summarized recent progress in the field by focusing on two key healthcare applications. The first is the ultrasensitive detection of biomarkers for early cancer diagnosis. The second is the construction of intelligent closed-loop wound management systems that combine real-time monitoring with precise treatment. We discussed the working mechanisms, core materials, and system architectures of these devices. We also identify current challenges and outline future research directions

title: Reducing Clinician Annotation Fatigue in Open-Set Federated Learning: A Client-Adaptive Vision-Language Gatekeeper
abstract: PURPOSE: Federated learning enables breast-imaging sites to jointly train mammography artificial intelligence (AI) without sharing images, but radiologists at each site must still annotate selected images during active-learning rounds. We developed and evaluated a client-adaptive vision-language gatekeeper that withholds radiopaque artifact-containing images considered unsuitable for a breast-density annotation objective and quantified its effect on annotation time, queue quality, and label reliability. METHODS: In this retrospective, scanner-partitioned study, we used FedEMBED, derived from the public Emory Breast Imaging Dataset (222,700 training and 65,891 test images; four scanners; artifact prevalence 4.8%-13.1% per scanner). PromptGate adapted a biomedical vision-language model with site-specific learnable prompts and classified each image as relevant in-distribution (ID) or irrelevant out-of-distribution (OOD) using the class with the highest softmax probability. abstract: This study is embedded in a systematic review that evaluates artificial intelligence, robotics and digital technologies across the coffee value chain against the three Industry 5.0 pillars: human-centricity, sustainability and resilience (host review; protocol registered at DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/K86WV). The host review screens 7,436 deduplicated records (N₁) retrieved on 28 September 2026 from Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection and IEEE Xplore, published 2011–2026. Only 15% of the studies identified by Scherbakov et al. were actual reviews conducted with LLM support. Ambient AI Medical Scribe Development: A Research Framework for Clinical Data and Clinical Documentation
abstract: Clinical encounters generate large amounts of information through conversations between patients, physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals. Symptoms, medical histories, medications, observations, diagnostic reasoning, treatment decisions, and follow-up instructions are often communicated verbally before becoming part of a structured medical record. Ambient AI Medical Scribe Development focuses on the technologies required to transform these conversations into structured clinical documentation while maintaining clinical context, data quality, privacy, and human oversight. For researchers in artificial intelligence, biomedical informatics, healthcare data science, and software engineering, ambient medical scribing represents a multidisciplinary research problem. It combines speech recognition, natural language processing, clinical terminology, information extraction, generative models, healthcare interoperability, and evaluation methodologies. title: Following the Traces of Tesla's Creativity: From Tesla's Resonant Coil to Bioresonant Integrative Medicine
abstract: Tesla's visions and inventions realized in his controlled altered states of consciousness contributed to his legendary aura as the greatest inventor in the history of electrical engineering at the end of 19th century, and what makes him fascinating is his unusual mental control of his creative visions, with significant quantum-holographic transpersonal creative–educational implications (including limits of Artificial Intelligence). At the beginning of the 20th century, Tesla's previously almost mythical scientific reputation and intuition began to darken, but he has still fascinated contemporaries by self-healing with HF currents, which subsequently led not only to the foundations of today's physical electrotherapy, but also represented inspiration for biomedical research and development of the field of bioresonant medicine, contributing also to the rapid development of nowadays integrative medicine (including transpersonal psychology) – with additional hints for reorientation to ecologically holistic subtle actions for solutions of the global risk society.

title: Comparing Small-Angle X-ray Scattering Approaches for Quantifying Magnetic-Field-Induced Orientation of Superparamagnetic Iron Oxide Nanoparticles
abstract: Abstract The magnetic-field-induced orientation of superparamagnetic multicore iron oxide nanoparticles, exemplified by ferucarbotran (Resovist), was quantified by small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). Scattering patterns were recorded as a function of magnetic field strength and particle concentration and analyzed using the Maier–Saupe orientational distribution function, originally introduced for nematic liquid crystals. This analysis yielded the second-order orientational order parameter, which was compared with values obtained from a circular-function approach and a model-free evaluation. The close agreement between the different procedures demonstrates that SAXS provides a reliable basis for quantifying field-induced orientational order in dispersions of multicore iron oxide nanoparticles. Beyond its relevance for colloid and nanomaterials research, this method comparison may also be useful for biomedical applications of magnetic nanoparticles, for which reproducible characterization and standardized analysis protocols are essential. title: Traditional and modern education systems in Ayurveda education: a critical integrative review
abstract: The evolution of Āyurveda education reflects a shift from an ancient, philosophically grounded educational model to a contemporary, institutionalized, competency-based one. Historically, Āyurveda was transmitted through the Gurukul system, a personalized, residential pedagogical model combining textual study with hands-on clinical training, emphasizing moral discipline ( Dharma ) and the Guru-Śiṣya Paramparā (teacher-disciple lineage). Learning was structured around the Trividha Jñānopāya (three-fold means of knowledge) and the cognitive sequence of Śravaṇa (listening), Manana (reflection), and Nididhyāsana (internalization). Colonial administrative frameworks and subsequent modernization transitioned Āyurveda education into a structured, time-bound, standardized university system. Today, under the governance of the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and guided by the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, Āyurveda education employs Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME), integrating digital technologies, Simulation-Based Learning (SBL), and objective assessment tools such as the Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE). title: Disseny i desenvolupament d'un sistema optomecànic de caracterització per a imatge polarimètrica
abstract: [ES] Este Trabajo de Fin de Grado propondrá el diseño y desarrollo de un sistema de caracterización óptica hermético a la luz para la medida de propiedades polarimétricas, que se desarrollará en el ARTORG Center for Biomedical Engineering Research dentro del grupo AIMI (Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging). Los sistemas polarimétricos requieren un alto nivel de precisión para garantizar una medida fiable del vector de Stokes y un correcto funcionamiento global. Dado que los componentes ópticos comerciales, como polarizadores y láminas retardadoras, pueden presentar desviaciones respecto a sus especificaciones nominales, resulta esencial realizar una caracterización previa y precisa antes de su integración en el sistema. Para dar respuesta a esta necesidad, se diseñará un recinto compacto y modular que proporcione condiciones de medida controladas. El sistema integrará un conjunto de componentes optomecánicos montados sobre una plataforma con desplazamiento lateral, permitiendo dos configuraciones de medida. El diseño se centrará en la repetibilidad del posicionamiento, la robustez mecánica y la facilidad de uso, manteniendo al mismo tiempo una estricta estanqueidad a la luz.

title: Integration of case taking and repertorisation in individualised homoeopathic practice: principles, clinical applications, evidence, challenges, and future perspectives—a narrative review
abstract: Individualised homoeopathic clinical practice is traditionally described as a sequential process involving comprehensive case taking, qualitative symptom evaluation, construction of an individualised symptom totality, repertorial analysis, and verification against Materia Medica. Although these components are frequently discussed as separate procedures, their methodological relationship is better understood as an interconnected and iterative process of clinical reasoning. Objective To synthesize and critically examine the historical foundations, conceptual principles, clinical workflow, empirical evidence, methodological challenges, patient-safety considerations, and emerging digital and artificial intelligence applications relevant to the integration of case taking and repertorisation in individualised homoeopathic practice. Methods A structured narrative review was undertaken using classical homoeopathic literature, contemporary biomedical publications, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, safety literature, methodological guidance, and international frameworks for artificial intelligence in health. title: Effectiveness of an Artificial Intelligence Health Education Accurately Linking System (AI-HEALS) for the intervention of chronic kidney disease: a randomised controlled trial protocol
abstract: Introduction Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health challenge with high morbidity and socioeconomic burden. Despite medical advances, long-term prognosis remains poor, highlighting the need for sustained self-management and health education. Traditional face-to-face care is limited by inefficient follow-up and insufficient attention to psychosocial and behavioural determinants, making it inadequate for long-term support. Artificial intelligence and mobile health offer personalised sustainable health education interventions. Accordingly, we developed the Artificial Intelligence Health Education Accurately Linking System (AI-HEALS) to support CKD self-management. Methods and analysis This is a single-centre, randomised, assessor-blinded, parallel-group controlled trial. A total of 74 adults with stages 1–5 CKD will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either the control group, receiving standard care or the intervention group, receiving standard care plus the AI-HEALS programme for 3 months. title: Network Biology: Current Status, Applications, Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Network biology provides a systems-level framework for understanding how interactions among molecular components, cells, microbial communities, tissues, and organs generate biological function and disease phenotypes. Recent advances in multiomics, single-cell and spatial profiling, network inference, organoid and organ-on-chip technologies, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence have shifted the field from static molecular maps toward dynamic, multiscale, and predictive network models. Major branches include molecular interaction networks, intracellular regulatory networks, single-cell and multicellular networks, microbial networks, disease networks, and interorgan interaction networks. Experimental and computational approaches are compared with respect to network reconstruction, causal validation, and cross-scale integration. Biomedical applications span disease classification, biomarker discovery, therapeutic-target identification, drug-response prediction, regenerative medicine, and precision healthcare. Fostering Clinical Pharmacology and Drug Development in India: A Perspective From SAC‐ACCP
abstract: Since its inception in 2006, the South Asian College, Affiliate of the American College of Clinical Pharmacology (SAC-ACCP), headquartered in Mumbai, India, has fostered the discipline, emphasizing education, training and dialogue across academia, regulators, and industry. The 2026 Annual Conference, themed "Think Global Act Local," covered topics ranging from Artificial Intelligence in healthcare to the Genome India project and multi‑regional clinical trials, reflecting India's strategic maturation as it moves decisively from participation to co-leadership in global drug development. This Commentary highlights the proceedings of this summit, celebrating India's emergence as a globally visible leader in biomedical research and drug development at a key milestone of the 20th Anniversary of SAC-ACCP.

title: The emerging role of large language models in oncology care delivery: A bibliometric and thematic analysis.
abstract: 759 Background: Large language models (LLMs) and generative artificial intelligence (AI) are rapidly transforming oncology care delivery through applications in clinical decision support, patient communication, documentation, and workflow optimization. We performed a bibliometric analysis to evaluate global research trends in LLMs and generative AI for oncology care delivery and quality improvement. Methods: A bibliometric analysis was conducted using PubMed. Publications evaluating LLMs or generative AI in oncology care delivery, quality improvement, clinical workflows, patient communication, survivorship, symptom management, and decision support were identified. Bibliographic data were exported and analyzed using VOSviewer. Co-authorship, organizational collaboration, and keyword co-occurrence networks were constructed. Overlay visualization was used to identify emerging research themes. Results: Approximately 400 publications were identified. Co-authorship analysis demonstrated a collaborative but fragmented research landscape, comprising 59 authors organized into 14 collaboration clusters (total link strength [TLS]=478). Choroid plexus pathophysiology and artificial intelligence in hydrocephalus: Toward mechanism-informed diagnosis and therapy
abstract: Hydrocephalus is a clinically and biologically heterogeneous disorder caused by disturbed cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics; however, current diagnostic and prognostic tools rely predominantly on coarse imaging indices and subjective clinical assessments. Growing evidence identifies the choroid plexus (ChP)—the primary site of CSF production and a key blood–CSF barrier—as a central hub in hydrocephalus pathogenesis, integrating ion transport, barrier integrity, and neuroimmune signaling. Concurrently, artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the analysis of multimodal biomedical data, including neuroimaging, clinical variables, physiological signals, CSF biomarkers, and omics profiles, offering opportunities to transition from descriptive assessments of ventriculomegaly toward mechanistic, quantitative disease models. In this review, we summarize ChP anatomy, transport physiology, and omics-defined cellular heterogeneity, discussing how ChP dysfunction contributes to hydrocephalus etiologies through hypersecretion, barrier breakdown, and inflammatory remodeling. title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Advances in Analytical Chemistry: Methods, Applications, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping analytical chemistry by changing how instrumental measurements are processed, interpreted, optimized, and translated into chemical decisions. Modern analytical platforms generate high-dimensional spectra, chromatograms, mass spectra, images, and sensor signals in volumes that can exceed the practical capacity of conventional univariate or manually supervised workflows. This integrative review examines AI-driven advances across spectroscopy, chromatography, mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), chemical sensors, imaging, and analytical method development. The review adopts a structured narrative design using purposive sampling of peer-reviewed reviews, primary methodological literature, and regulatory guidance identified through targeted searches of major biomedical and chemistry literature sources and official regulatory repositories. Evidence was thematically coded into four domains: data enhancement, predictive modelling, analytical-method optimization, and decision support. Microphysiological Systems Integrating Bioprinting, Organoids, Organ‐on‐a‐Chip, and AI: Next Generation Platforms for Pharmaceutical Development
abstract: Microphysiological systems (MPS) have emerged as transformative in vitro platforms to address the long-standing bottlenecks of conventional preclinical models, including poor physiological relevance inherent to 2D cultures, as well as species incompatibility and ethical constraints associated with animal models, thereby improving clinical predictability and redefining modern pharmaceutical development. This review highlights the innovative convergence of bioprinting, organoids, organ-on-a-chip (OoC), and artificial intelligence (AI) as a next-generation MPS framework, enabling precision reconstruction of human tissue microenvironments with unprecedented fidelity. Bioprinting delivers spatially defined 3D architectures; organoids recapitulate organ-specific heterogeneity; OoC integrates dynamic physiological cues; and AI enables intelligent fabrication optimization, real-time monitoring, and predictive drug-response modeling. Their synergistic integration overcomes the inherent limitations of single-technology systems. Inteligencia artificial multimodal en cardiología: síntesis crítica del rendimiento diagnóstico y la aplicabilidad clínica
abstract: The article critically examines the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence systems in the analysis of cardiovascular imaging and biomedical signals, taking into account both validation conditions and methodological limitations that hinder clinical applicability. Findings indicate that image-based studies achieve high accuracy in echocardiographic segmentation, although performance is constrained by poor image quality, small sample sizes, and limited external validation. Signal-based studies report strong performance across multiple applications, yet with variable specificity and notable declines when evaluated in external cohorts. Overall, the evidence suggests meaningful diagnostic potential, albeit conditioned by sample heterogeneity, overfitting, selection bias, reliance on incomplete metrics, and regulatory shortcomings. Such limitations underscore the need for rigorous prospective and external validation, along with continuous monitoring, prior to clinical implementation.

title: Multifunctional Hydroxyapatite: Recent Progress and Future Prospects in Biomedicine and Materials Science
abstract: One of the most studied biomaterials for biomedical applications is hydroxyapatite (HAp), a bioactive ceramic (Ca-P) with structural and compositional similarity to the mineral phase of human bones and teeth. HAp is investigated for various applications, such as bone regeneration, dental implants, tissue engineering, implant coatings, and controlled drug delivery systems, due to its excellent biocompatibility, osteoconductivity, and ability to accommodate ionic substitutions. This review accounts for an extensive overview of crystal chemistry, structure–property relationship, mechanical properties, and biological activity of HAp. The focus is given to the effect of ionic substitutions, microstructural characteristics, and processing parameters on the physicochemical and biomedical behavior of HAp-based materials. The review also covers the latest developments on composite biomaterials, additive manufacturing, multifunctional coatings, and nanostructured HAp systems for future healthcare applications. Furthermore, a processing–structure–property–performance (PSPP) framework is suggested for setting up correlations between material design, functional properties, and clinical performa

Development of Smart Surface Texturing Techniques Using Ai-Driven Laser Machining for Enhanced Tribological Performance
abstract: An approach to increase the tribological performance of engineering materials via the development of smart surface texturing techniques using artificial intelligence (AI)-driven laser machining is presented in this study. However, existing surface texturing approaches largely rely on trial-and-error methods and lack adaptive optimization and predictive design capabilities. This study integrates AI-based texture design with precision laser surface texturing (LST) to develop optimized surface patterns on AISI 316 L stainless steel and Ti 6Al 4V alloy substrates. This deep learning model was used to train the generation of ten unique texture geometries, each of which was subsequently fabricated using a nanosecond pulsed fiber laser system. Tribological testing using a ballon-disk tribometer under dry sliding conditions revealed significant improvements, including up to 35% reduction in the coefficient of friction and up to 48% reduction in wear volume compared to untextured surfaces. Data analysis confirmed that key texture parameters, such as dimple spacing, cut depth, and aspect ratio, were major factors that improved the surface performance. title: Synergistic engineering of organoids and organ-on-a-chip systems through microengineering and sensor integration for advanced biomedical research
abstract: Microphysiological systems, including organoids, organ-on-a-chip (OoC) platforms, and their integrated forms, are increasingly used to model human physiology in vitro. Organoids contribute self-organized cellular diversity and tissue architecture, whereas OoC platforms provide controlled geometry, perfusion, mechanical cues, and access to real-time measurements. Their integration into organoid-on-a-chip and multi-tissue systems can improve physiological relevance for efficacy evaluation, quality control, mechanistic studies, and personalized medicine. This review examines organoid generation, organ-specific OoC models, hybrid systems, 3D bioprinting, acoustic bioassembly, and sensor integration. It also discusses the principal barriers to translation, including scalability, reproducibility, standardization, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence and multi-omics data. Together, these advances position synergistically engineered microphysiological systems as promising translational tools, provided that performance is validated against standardized, reproducible, and clinically relevant benchmarks.

title: Reorienting Healthcare from Disease-Centered to People-Centered Care
abstract: Healthcare is entering an era of extraordinary scientific and technological progress. Advances in biomedical sciences, digital health, artificial intelligence, precision medicine, genomics, and novel therapeutics are transforming the diagnosis and management of disease. Yet, amid this rapid evolution, the fundamental purpose of healthcare remains unchanged: to promote health, prevent disease, relieve suffering, prolong healthy life, and preserve human dignity. The central challenge for health systems is therefore not simply to develop more sophisticated interventions, but to ensure that scientific progress translates into care that is accessible, affordable, equitable, safe, effective, and responsive to the needs of people. Universal health coverage requires access to essential health services without financial hardship, while strong primary health care provides the foundation for achieving this objective.¹,² This principle has particular relevance for Pakistan. Wearable IoMT Biosensors for the Surveillance and Early Detection of Lassa Fever in Resource-Constrained Environments: A Systematic Technical Review
abstract: Lassa fever remains a dangerous threat in West Africa, carrying a high death rate and posing a severe risk of spreading within healthcare facilities. Pinning down a diagnosis currently relies on centralized lab tests like RT-PCR, which are too expensive and take too long to help rural, under-resourced clinics when every hour counts. This systematic technical review analyzes biomedical and engineering literature from PubMed and IEEE Xplore (2021–2026) to evaluate how wearable bioelectronics, edge artificial intelligence (AI), and the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) can be combined for real-time, remote disease tracking. The literature shows that running optimized machine learning models, specifically Random Forest ensembles, directly on low-power microchips like the RISC-V-based ESP32-C3 mini drops wireless radio use by up to 88%. This extends wearable battery life to 14–21 days on a small 300 mAh charge. By cross-analyzing core temperature, movement, and vital signs, these systems achieve a 91.4% diagnostic sensitivity. title: Throw-Ins in Soccer: Current Insights, Tactical Relevance, and Practical Recommendations for Practitioners. A Systematic Review
abstract: This study was designed as a systematic review to identify, critically appraise and synthesise the available evidence concerning throw-ins in association football. The scope of the review was deliberately broad because the existing literature does not treat the throw-in as a single, homogeneous performance variable. Instead, the evidence addresses complementary dimensions ranging from the regulatory and biomechanical constraints of the action to its temporal management, offensive organisation, defensive responses and contribution to subsequent attacking outcomes. Accordingly, the review sought to integrate these dimensions within a single evidence framework while maintaining clear distinctions between technical, tactical, contextual and outcome-related findings. The review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 statement (PRISMA 2020; Page et al., 2021), and the identification and reporting of information sources and electronic search procedures were additionally guided by the PRISMA extension for searches (PRISMA-S; Rethlefsen et al., 2021).[KS6.1][DP6.2][Á6.3] The review was structured around an adapted Populati

title: Stimuli-Responsive Polymeric Nanoparticles for Targeted and Controlled Drug Delivery: From Molecular Design to Clinical Translation: A Review
abstract: Background: Stimuli-responsive polymeric nanoparticles (PNPs) have emerged as smart drug delivery systems capable of releasing therapeutic agents selectively in response to physiological or external stimuli. Recent advances in polymer engineering, surface functionalization, and multi-stimuli responsiveness have expanded their biomedical applications.Objective: This review aims to summarize recent developments (2023–2025) in stimuli-responsive PNPs, focusing on their design strategies, therapeutic applications, performance improvements, and challenges associated with clinical translation.Methods: Recent studies investigating stimuli-responsive PNPs were analyzed with emphasis on polymer composition, surface modification techniques, multi-stimuli architectures, and their applications in cancer therapy, gene therapy, immunotherapy, infectious diseases, and metabolic disorders.Results: The reviewed studies demonstrated significant improvements in drug stability, controlled release kinetics, targeting efficiency, and biocompatibility of PNP systems. title: Integrating Nanotechnology and Artificial Intelligence for Next Generation Breast Cancer Management: A Scoping Review
abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and its clinical management continues to be complicated by substantial tumor heterogeneity. Two technological forces are reshaping the therapeutic and diagnostic landscape of this disease: nanotechnology and artificial intelligence (AI). Nanomedicine has matured into a versatile platform for targeted drug delivery, diagnostics, and theranostics, while AI provides the computational capacity required to interpret complex biomedical datasets, forecast clinical outcomes, and tailor therapeutic strategies to individual patients. For much of their development, these two fields progressed largely independently; their recent convergence, however, has begun to define a distinct frontier in oncology research. This review examines the intersection of AI and nanotechnology across the breast cancer care continuum, beginning with AI-guided rational design and high-throughput screening of nanocarrier platforms, including lipid-based, polymeric, and inorganic systems, and how computational approaches accelerate their development and optimization. The contribution of AI to nanodiagnostics is then discussed, with attention

title: Research on the Technical Bottlenecks, Regulatory Frameworks of Global Medical AI Industry Implementation and the Supporting System of Biomedical Engineering Discipline
abstract: The escalating integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into healthcare presents transformative potential, yet its widespread global implementation is significantly impeded by multifaceted technical bottlenecks. This research systematically identifies and categorizes these primary obstacles, including data bias, model interpretability, robustness, computational demands, and interoperability issues, which collectively hinder the transition from research to clinical practice. Concurrently, an in-depth analysis of existing global regulatory frameworks, such as those established by the FDA and EMA, reveals their evolving but often insufficient capacity to address the unique complexities of medical AI, particularly concerning validation, bias mitigation, and transparency. The study posits that the biomedical engineering discipline is uniquely positioned to bridge this gap by developing critical supporting systems. This includes advancing explainable AI (XAI) methodologies, establishing robust validation tools and interoperability standards, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration to translate ethical principles into practical engineering solutions. title: Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Medicine, Biomolecular Design, and Drug Discovery: From Computational Performance to Translational Evidence
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly evaluated not only for technical performance but also for its ability to improve biomedical research and clinical care. This narrative review examines recent evidence across clinical medicine, biomolecular design, and drug discovery, focusing on the transition from computational capability to clinically or biologically meaningful outcomes. In clinical medicine, randomized and prospective studies suggest that AI-assisted systems can improve selected diagnostic and decision-making tasks, although effects on workflow, sustained use, and patient outcomes are variable. In biomolecular research, structure prediction and generative design have progressed to experimentally validated binders, antibodies, and other engineered molecules, but biological activity, developability, and safety still require empirical confirmation. In drug discovery, AI can accelerate target identification, molecular generation, and candidate prioritization, and early clinical studies provide proof of concept; however, whether these approaches improve overall development success remains uncertain. title: Advances in Multimodal Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: Data Integration, Foundation Models, and Clinical Applications—A Narrative Review
abstract: Background/Objectives: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in radiology to combine medical images with radiology reports, clinical narratives, structured health records, laboratory measurements, and other patient data. These systems may support more context-aware interpretation, reporting, and clinical decision-making than unimodal approaches. This narrative review examines recent technical and clinical advances in multimodal radiology AI and identifies barriers to responsible implementation. Methods: Relevant biomedical and technical literature was identified through targeted searches of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, Scopus, arXiv, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar. A documented screening process identified 111 reviewed publications from 1154 records. Study selection and data extraction were conducted by one reviewer without independent verification. Original research, reviews, and commentaries, including selected preprints, were synthesized thematically. title: Mapping The Intellectual Structure of AI in Tuberculosis Research: A Keyword Co-occurrence and Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly essential in global tuberculosis (TB) control, offering advances in diagnostic accuracy, drug-resistance prediction, treatment monitoring, and public health decision-making. As research activity accelerates, a structured bibliometric assessment is necessary to map scientific progress and highlight emerging directions. This study conducted a bibliometric analysis using data retrieved from Scopus, from which 57 articles were included after rigorous cleaning and screening. Citation metrics were computed using Publish or Perish, while VOSviewer was employed to visualize keyword co-occurrence networks. Citation impact was evaluated using total local citation score (TLCS) and total global citation score (TGCS). Findings show that annual publication output remained low until 2023 but increased sharply from 2023 to 2025, reflecting rapid global expansion of AI-related TB research. The Indian Journal of Tuberculosis and the International Journal of Biomedical Imaging emerged as influential journals, with the latter demonstrating the highest TGCS, underscoring its broad international impact.
