title: Engineered probiotic biointerfaces: Construction principles, microscopic characterisation and biomedical functions
abstract: Engineered probiotic biointerfaces are the dynamic boundaries through which modified bacteria interact with their biological surroundings. They can improve bacterial survival, mucosal retention and therapeutic delivery, but the structural basis of these effects is often unclear. This review groups biointerfaces by their dominant role: barrier protection, recognition, responsiveness, interaction and renewal by living cells. We compare microscopy methods for measuring coating continuity, ligand organisation, surface mechanics and changes during growth or biological transport. We also explain how artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image analysis can convert bacterial images into reproducible single-cell measurements, using published workflows as practical examples. These methods can help connect interfacial changes with mucosal protection, immune regulation, targeted delivery and antibiofilm activity. Coating continuity, ligand organisation and mechanics are parameters associated with performance; their causal contributions remain to be established. We therefore propose combining measurements over time with matched functional assays and controlled changes to individual interface pa

title: An agentic AI environment to support biomedical research in collaborative academic environments
abstract: Abstract Agentic artificial intelligence (AAI) is increasingly used by biomedical scientists, where it has substantially lowered the difficulty of integrating computational, statistical and data-science approaches into day-to-day research activities, assisting with project design, analysis and manuscript preparation. Significant barriers remain, however, which are unlikely to be removed solely by releasing more capable AI models. Meaningful use still demands a technical fluency that many biomedical researchers lack: a PI and their lab members must learn how to use the AAI system, establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) for managing, sharing and curating data, and enforce rules that address data privacy and security. Existing commercial AAI systems, which were designed primarily for software engineering purposes, need to be significantly re-purposed for biomedical-related data science. We present Murmurent, shared software that sits beneath the agentic AI and provides the skills, procedures and protections to address the concerns above, removing the need for a lab to develop them independently. This includes (1) infrastructure to support projects and so-called choreographies

title: AI for Biomedical Research Operations and Project Management
abstract: Successfully conducting research involves coordinating various activities, managing resources, tracking progress, identifying risks, maintaining communication, and ensuring quality. This chapter examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can support research operations and project management: optimizing study schedules, efficiently allocating resources, predicting and reducing risks, improving team communication, monitoring data quality, managing documentation, and tracking milestones. I explore how AI can help research teams carry out complex studies more effectively while upholding quality and compliance. Although project management mainly depends on human leadership, judgment, and interpersonal skills, AI offers valuable analytical support, can spot potential issues early, and helps lessen the administrative workload that often distracts from scientific work.

title: AI for Biomedical Research Ideation and Planning
abstract: The foundation of great research starts with asking the right questions at the right time. This chapter investigates how artificial intelligence can improve the earliest and possibly most innovative stage of research: spotting opportunities, identifying gaps in knowledge, and planning practical investigations. We look at AI tools for trend analysis, needs assessment, feasibility checks, funding discovery, and building interdisciplinary links. While AI can&s;t replace the human creativity and judgment vital to generating research ideas, it can significantly widen the range of options researchers consider and help them make better decisions about where to focus their efforts.

title: “The pharmacological potential of CRISPR-Cas9: Revolutionizing gene therapy and drug development”
abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 has entered the mainstream of genetic research and therapeutic development, offering a level of programmable and targeted gene editing that has substantially expanded the possibilities of genetic manipulation. This review focuses on the discovery to development of CRISPR-Cas9 and its recent practice in pharmacological and biotechnology field. We discuss further advancements in CRISPR technology such as high-fidelity CRISPR and new systems Cas12 and Cas13 which increases efficiency of editing and opens more opportunities. CRISPR technology has been further advanced when combined with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; guide RNA is now optimized while the off-target effects are predicted. The review also focuses on the new targets for therapy, recent trials, the legal and the social and ethical relevance of the CRISPR approach. With the development of CRISPR-Cas9 promising and revolutionary preliminary achievements in the fields of drug development and disease management and tissue engineering are anticipated. Although, in its application, there are questions that have been raised concerning side effects, carriers, and ethics, it is important to take advantage

title: AI for Biomedical Research Volume 1
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming every aspect of biomedical research practice. Researchers face a fragmented landscape of tools, evolving ethical requirements, emerging regulations, and rapidly shifting best practices. The first of two volumes, this book provides a comprehensive treatment of AI across the complete research lifecycle, from initial ideation through analysis, quality assurance, dissemination, and long-term impacts. Key Features This book is the only resource covering AI applications across the entire research journey, from initial idea through long-term impact. It systematically applies four major AI governance frameworks (RUAIH, FUTURE-AI, NIST AI RMF, and GMLP) throughout both volumes, showing researchers how to operationalize abstract principles in daily practice. It includes detailed analysis of the EU AI Act implementation timeline (February 2025 through August 2027) with specific guidance for research applications. It helps researchers and institutions understand high-risk classifications, research exemptions, and compliance strategies before requirements take effect. It moves beyond hype and fear to deliver a balanced, practical approach to human-AI

title: From task-specific AI to cardiovascular foundation models: a new era of multimodal interpretation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping cardiovascular medicine, evolving from task-specific supervised models towards multitask and foundation models capable of broader, more scalable interpretation. Early AI systems achieved high performance in electrocardiographic interpretation, echocardiographic measurement and disease diagnosis but their dependence on predefined outputs and labelled datasets limits flexibility and confines them to individual tasks. Foundation models address these limitations by learning reusable representations from large-scale data, often through self-supervised or contrastive pretraining, and adapting them to multiple downstream tasks. Emerging models in electrocardiography, echocardiography, chest radiography, cardiac MR and cardiac CT demonstrate capabilities including disease classification, quantitative measurement, segmentation, image-text retrieval, report generation and risk prediction. Generalist and multimodal biomedical foundation models further suggest a future in which cardiovascular AI integrates signals, imaging, clinical text, laboratory data and medical history to support patient-level diagnosis and decision-making. title: 4D-PRINTED SHAPE-MEMORY POLYMERS FOR ADVANCED DRUG DELIVERY: PROGRAMMING, STIMULI-RESPONSIVE MECHANISMS AND BIOMEDICAL APPLICATIONS
abstract: ABSTRACT Four-dimensional (4D) printing is an emerging additive manufacturing technology that integrates three-dimensional (3D) printing with smart materials capable of undergoing programmed changes in shape or function over time in response to specific stimuli. This technology has attracted increasing interest in pharmaceutical drug delivery because it offers the possibility of developing dynamic, programmable, and personalized drug-delivery systems. This review provides an overview of the fundamental principles of 4D printing, including stimulus-responsive mechanisms, smart materials, and major printing technologies relevant to pharmaceutical applications. Particular emphasis is placed on shape-memory polymers, hydrogels, and other responsive materials that can respond to temperature, moisture, pH, light, magnetic fields, and other environmental stimuli. Recent applications in gastroretentive, esophageal, intravesical, intestinal, transdermal, implantable, and localized drug-delivery systems are discussed, with emphasis on their potential to improve drug retention, controlled release, site-specific therapy, minimally invasive administration, and personalized treatment. title: A Comparative Study of Stance and Engagement in AI-generated vs. Human-written Abstracts across Multidisciplinary Research
abstract: Due to the increasing potential of Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools in academic writing, it becomes important to investigate this potential in research article abstract writing. This study compares the use of stance and engagement features in AI-generated and human-written academic abstracts across six disciplines—three from STEM (Computer Science, Environmental Science, Biomedical Science) and three from the humanities and social sciences (Linguistics, Philosophy, Education). Grounded in Hyland’s (2018) metadiscourse framework, the research investigates how generative AI reproduces interpersonal features of academic writing in comparison to human authors. A balanced corpus of 60 abstracts (30 AI-generated, 30 human-authored) was compiled and analysed for stance (hedges, boosters, attitude markers) and engagement (reader pronouns, directives, questions, shared knowledge appeals) features. Across the six disciplines, human-written abstracts used significantly more hedges, boosters, self-mentions, reader pronouns, and directives than AI-generated abstracts, indicating greater use of epistemic stance and author–reader engagement. title: AI for Biomedical Research Program and Portfolio Optimization
abstract: Individual research studies are part of broader research programs and portfolios that need strategic direction and resource allocation. This chapter examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can assist in strategic research planning at the program and institutional levels: analyzing research portfolios, pinpointing high-impact opportunities, optimizing resource distribution, forecasting research outcomes and return on investment, balancing risk and innovation, conducting gap analysis, and evaluating institutional research strengths. While strategic vision and values-based prioritization remain primarily human responsibilities, AI can provide data-driven insights that support more effective portfolio management and help research organizations maximize their collective impact.

title: Next-generation microbial fuel cell biosensors: Integrating self-powered, IoT connectivity, and AI-driven intelligence for real-time monitoring
abstract: Microbial fuel cell (MFC)-based biosensors have emerged as promising self-powered platforms for real-time monitoring by integrating bioelectrochemical sensing with sustainable energy generation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of next-generation MFC biosensors, highlighting recent advances in sensing mechanisms, system design, performance optimization, and intelligent integration. The fundamental principles of microbial electron transfer and bioelectrochemical signal generation are discussed, followed by strategies to enhance sensor performance through electrode engineering, biofilm optimization, and operational control. The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies enables continuous, remote, and distributed monitoring, supporting the development of intelligent sensing networks for real-time data acquisition. Furthermore, the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) enhances signal processing, pattern recognition, predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and adaptive system control, significantly improving sensing accuracy and operational reliability. The synergistic convergence of self-powered sensing, IoT connectivity, and AI-driven analytics is fur

title: AI for Biomedical Research Administration and Compliance
abstract: Research functions within complex regulatory and administrative frameworks designed to protect participants, ensure integrity, manage resources, and build public trust. This chapter explores how artificial intelligence (AI) can support research administration and compliance: determining whether activities are research requiring review, identifying suitable regulatory pathways, analyzing contracts and agreements, checking compliance, managing conflicts of interest, and handling export control and technology transfer. I look at how AI can bring consistency and efficiency to administrative processes while keeping appropriate human oversight. Although compliance judgment and ethical reasoning remain primarily human responsibilities, AI can assist in navigating regulatory complexity, identifying potential issues, and systematically applying requirements.

title: Artificial intelligence in biomedical visualization and education: a narrative review
abstract: Biomedical visualization increasingly spans traditional medical illustration, synthetic medical imaging, vision-language systems, and patient-specific 3D reconstruction. This narrative review examines applications of artificial intelligence (AI) across this field, with particular attention to medical education and scientific and clinical communication. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE and IEEE Xplore for English-language literature published from January 2017 through September 2026, supplemented by targeted searches of publisher databases and reference-list screening. Included publications addressed AI-enabled medical or anatomical illustration, text-to-image generation, synthetic medical imaging, vision-language models, 3D reconstruction, or immersive biomedical visualization. Current evidence indicates that diffusion models can rapidly generate visually persuasive and customizable drafts, whereas segmentation-guided synthesis and anatomy-aware 3D methods offer stronger structural control in defined tasks. title: Perspective Chapter: The Digital Cath Lab – Robotic-Assisted PCI and AI in Lesion Assessment
abstract: The cardiac catheterization laboratory continues to evolve through advances in biomedical engineering, computational modeling, robotic-assisted intervention, and artificial intelligence (AI). Although many of these technologies remain in the early stages of clinical application, they collectively represent important future steps toward a more integrated and image-guided digital catheterization laboratory. This chapter explores the paradigm shift from manual coronary interventions to an integrated Digital Cath Lab ecosystem. By synthesizing data from the current 2025–2026 period, such as telerobotic trials and the latest AI-driven diagnostic studies, the discussion highlights the synergy between robotic precision and AI. Robotic-assisted PCI (R-PCI) is examined as a technological approach to addressing traditional clinical challenges, with studies demonstrating improved lesion measurement and stent positioning along with substantial reductions in operator radiation exposure. Simultaneously, the chapter delves into AI-driven lesion assessment, where machine learning algorithms provide real-time, automated analysis of optical coherence tomography (OCT)/intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)

title: Explainable ML in COPD Risk Prediction: Scoping Review Protocol
abstract: Authors and affiliations: Yasu Du, School of Nursing, Shanxi Medical University Liping Cui, Third Hospital of Shanxi Medical University, Shanxi Bethune Hospital, Shanxi Academy of Medical Sciences, Tongji Shanxi Hospital, Taiyuan, 030032, China (1) To summarize the types and construction methods of machine learning models for COPD risk prediction; (2) To sort out the explainable artificial intelligence techniques applied in these models; (3) To summarize the model performance indicators and main limitations of existing studies; (4) To identify research gaps and propose future research directions. We will follow the JBI scoping review framework. Literature will be retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI,Scopus,Embase,Cochrane Library,CINAHL,WanFang Data,VIP (Chongqing VIP Database),SinoMed (Chinese Biomedical Literature Service System),Google Scholar. Two reviewers will independently screen studies and extract data.

title: On the application of artificial intelligence and large language models in soil and environmental research: a review
abstract: In recent years, scientific research has seen the rapid development of methods based on artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs), which are capable of processing and interpreting significant volumes of text and structured information, including tables, numerical and categorical data, and sensor data and other heterogeneous information, using specialized and multimodal AI systems. Soil ecology, as a field characterized by the rapid accumulation of heterogeneous data, including the results of metagenomic analyses of soil microbiomes, can potentially benefit significantly from the application of such tools. The aim of this review is to identify, analyze, and summarize current approaches to the use of AI and LLM technologies in soil and environmental research. The review examines the main areas of AI application, including scientific literature search and analysis, semantic search for relevant publications, citation mapping, text summarization, and the use of generative AI assistants. Particular attention is paid to the application of AI methods in the analysis of soil microbiomes and to the potential use of metagenomic data for predicting soil fertility and agricu

title: Recent advances in machine learning for the design and performance prediction of corrosion inhibitors
abstract: Recent advances in corrosion science and materials engineering have been significantly accelerated by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and highthroughput experimental techniques.This review and research compilation highlights the development of predictive models for corrosion assessment in metals, reinforced concrete, and biomedical alloys, combining non-destructive testing, electrochemical methods, and computational simulations.AI-driven approaches-including QSAR, gradient boosting, convolutional neural networks, and molecular dynamics-have been successfully applied to predict corrosion inhibition efficiency, detect structural degradation, and optimize inhibitor design.Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of eco-friendly inhibitors such as guava leaf extract and Congo Red dye, hybrid nanocomposites, and quaternary ammonium salts, with experimental validation confirming high inhibition efficiencies.The integration of theoretical descriptors, imaging data, and deep learning facilitates rapid, accurate, and sustainable corrosion management, offering mechanistic insights into adsorption processes, surface protection, and fatigue behavior.Th

title: Use of generative artificial intelligence for learning biomedical sciences among medical students: usage patterns, perceived usefulness and verification of scientific information — a scoping review protocol
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools are increasingly used by medical students for independent study, yet little is known about how they use them to learn the biomedical sciences, how useful and trustworthy they perceive the generated information to be, and how they verify it. This scoping review will map the available evidence on GenAI use for learning biomedical (basic/preclinical) sciences among undergraduate medical students, in terms of usage patterns, perceived usefulness (including trust) and verification strategies. Studies on general GenAI use for learning in medical education will also be included and charted separately from those specific to the biomedical sciences; reviews with explicit methods will be presented as a separate group. The review follows the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and will be reported according to PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S. Searches will be run in PubMed, LILACS, Education Source, Academic Search Complete and ERIC, limited to publications from 2023 onwards in English, Spanish or Portuguese. Two independent reviewers will screen records in Rayyan, with a third reviewer resolving disagreements. Data will be charted with a piloted extra

title: Physics-Informed and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Nanomaterial-Based Biosensors: From Sensor Design and Signal Processing to Clinical Translation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in biosensing, yet its role is often limited to post-processing or high-accuracy regression on simulation-generated datasets. This critical narrative review examines physics-informed and explainable AI for nanomaterial-based biosensors, emphasizing graphene and other two-dimensional materials, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), terahertz (THz) metasurfaces, electrochemical platforms, field-effect transistors, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, and wearable systems. Recent peer-reviewed studies and relevant technical guidance were critically compared with respect to sensing physics, data provenance, AI task, interpretability, validation strategy, and evidence level. Across these modalities, AI supports forward surrogate modeling, inverse design, spectral interpretation, classification, calibration, and uncertainty-aware decision support, but predictive accuracy alone does not establish translational maturity. Particular attention is given to explainable AI, the distinction between physics-guided and genuinely physics-informed learning, small-data validation, fabrication tolerance, drift, and the simulation-to-experiment gap. title: Emerging Trends in Pediatric Disease Management and Preventive Care: A Systematic Review
abstract: Child health systems are undergoing rapid transformation driven by biomedical innovation, digital integration, and strengthened preventive strategies.Over the past decade, advances in vaccination, pharmacological therapies, digital monitoring, artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, and school-based health programs have reshaped pediatric care delivery.Despite expanding technological capacity and structured prevention models, evidence remains fragmented across clinical, behavioural, and diagnostic domains.Long-term effectiveness, sustainability, and equitable implementation of emerging tools remain insufficiently synthesised within a unified framework.This systematic review synthesises contemporary evidence published between 2015 and 2025 to examine evolving approaches to pediatric disease management and prevention.A structured protocol guided database searches, study selection, and quality appraisal.Randomised controlled trials, cluster trials, feasibility studies, and diagnostic accuracy studies involving pediatric populations were included.Risk of bias was assessed using validated appraisal frameworks appropriate to the study design.Ten studies met the eligibility criteria

title: Artificial Intelligence against COVID-19: A Narrative Review
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) across clinical medicine, public health, biomedical research, and pharmaceutical development. This narrative review synthesizes representative evidence published primarily from 2024 to 2026, a period chosen to capture the post-emergency phase of COVID-19 in which external validation, multimodal modelling, post-COVID condition, genomic and wastewater surveillance, antiviral discovery, and responsible AI governance have become increasingly prominent. A structured narrative search of PubMed/PMC and World Health Organization (WHO) resources was conducted up to 25 September 2026 using combinations of COVID-19/SARS-CoV-2 and artificial intelligence/machine learning terms together with domain-specific keywords. Evidence was appraised qualitatively according to study population, data source, validation design, reported uncertainty, confounding, and demonstrated clinical or public-health relevance. Recent studies demonstrate that AI can support medical-image interpretation, risk stratification, population surveillance, long-COVID identification, variant characterization, and molecular screening.

title: A Computer Vision and Non-Immersive Virtual Reality Platform for Automated Functional Assessment During Hospital Cardiorespiratory Rehabilitation
abstract: Functional assessment is an essential component of hospital cardiorespiratory rehabilitation; however, conventional assessment methods still rely on manual repetition counting, external timing devices, and direct supervision by healthcare professionals, limiting workflow efficiency and assessment standardization. This study presents the design, development, and preliminary technical verification of EX-REAB, a modular computational platform that integrates computer vision and non-immersive virtual reality for automated functional assessment in hospital rehabilitation. The platform was developed through an iterative user-centered software engineering process involving physiotherapists, biomedical engineers, computer scientists, and software developers. EX-REAB incorporates MediaPipe Pose-based markerless motion capture, automated movement recognition, standardized execution of the 2-Minute Step Test and the 30-Second Sit-to-Stand Test, real-time performance feedback, and structured clinical data management. title: Mapping LIG-Based Biomedical Sensing Research: Bibliometric Trends, Thematic Clusters, and International Collaboration
abstract: Since the discovery of Laser-Induced Graphene (LIG) in 2014, the material has emerged as a promising platform for flexible electronics due to its low-cost fabrication and outstanding physicochemical properties. This study presents a bibliometric mapping of LIG research within the biomedical sensing domain, aiming to identify the main thematic trends, technological frontiers, and global collaboration patterns. A total of 734 bibliographic records published between 2014 and 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science database and analyzed using VOSviewer. Keyword co-occurrence analysis (threshold ≥ 9) identified 60 high-relevance nodes organized into thematic clusters associated with sensing platforms, electrochemical biosensors, energy storage, wearable electronics, and computational intelligence. Overlay visualization revealed a temporal transition from fundamental material synthesis and energy related applications toward multimodal biomedical sensing and machine learning-assisted signal interpretation. title: Oral Lesion Annotation Tool for Neural Network Training
abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) modelsfor oral lesion detection depends on the availability of highqualityand well-structured annotated datasets. However, theconstruction of such datasets remains a challenge, particularlydue to the need for standardized annotation procedures andspecialized review. This study presents IA-Bucal Files, a platformdeveloped to organize, annotate, review, and structure clinicalimages of oral lesions for future applications in Artificial Intelligenceand Deep Learning. The platform integrates clinical imagesand associated metadata, allowing the annotation of lesions,anatomical structures, and exclusion zones through vector-basedtools, including polygons, rectangles, circles, and ellipses. Thedataset was constructed from images obtained from scientificarticles, scientific literature databases, and open-access databases.Annotation was performed by undergraduate students fromDentistry and Biomedical Engineering programs following apreliminary study of the lesions based on scientific literature. title: BioStatusIA: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Multimodal Clinical Decision Support
abstract: —Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) increasingly rely on artificial intelligence to assist healthcare professionals in interpreting heterogeneous biomedical data. AlthoughLarge Language Models (LLMs) have expanded the capabilitiesof these systems, most existing solutions target a single biomedicalmodality, requiring independent analytical pipelines and limitinginteroperability across clinical domains. This paper presentsBioStatusIA, a multi-agent architecture designed for multimodalclinical decision support. The proposed framework integratesspecialized autonomous agents orchestrated through CrewAIwith a locally deployed LLM executed using Ollama. A unifiednormalization layer enables the processing of one-dimensionalphysiological signals, two-dimensional medical images, threedimensional volumetric examinations, and structured clinicaldatasets within a common analytical workflow. title: Teaching Critical Appraisal of AI-Generated Output in Medical Education: A Mixed Methods Pilot Study (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Medical students need practical opportunities to critically appraise artificial intelligence (AI)-generated clinical output. Comparing model interpretations with an independently formed judgment offers a way to teach this skill within clinical education. OBJECTIVE To examine learner acceptability, explore changes in confidence and automation-bias-related self-reports, and identify useful features and refinements of an electrocardiogram (ECG)-based AI-appraisal session. METHODS This single-center mixed methods pilot involved 13 medical and biomedical sciences students at a US osteopathic medical school. Groups interpreted three ECGs independently, consulted Claude and ChatGPT using a standardized prompt, questioned and compared their outputs, and discussed reference interpretations with faculty. Paired surveys assessed confidence, automation-bias-related responses, learner evaluations, recalled behavior, mental effort, and future intentions. Exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm adjustment across 10 exploratory tests were used for seven confidence and three wording-matched awareness-related items. title: A Literature Review of Artificial Intelligence in Health Care
abstract: . Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping health care through medical-image interpretation, risk prediction, clinical decision support, natural-language processing, remote monitoring, and biomedical discovery. This article reviews the principal applications, benefits, limitations, and governance requirements of AI in health care. A systematic-style review protocol was designed around peer-reviewed and authoritative literature published from 2017 to 2025. To demonstrate an empirical journal format without misrepresenting a completed study, database retrieval, screening counts, coded outcomes, tables, and graphs are explicitly simulated. The illustrative synthesis contains 72 studies: medical imaging was the largest domain (30.6%), followed by predictive analytics using electronic health records (19.4%), clinical decision support (13.9%), and natural-language processing or large language models (12.5%). The most frequently coded benefit was improved diagnostic or classification performance, whereas limited generalizability, privacy risk, insufficient explainability, and workflow integration were the dominant barriers. title: Advanced Bioinformatics Tools and Computational Strategies for Drug Discovery in Biomedical Sciences
abstract: The aim of the National Workshop on “Advanced Bioinformatics Tools and Computational Strategies for Drug Discovery in Biomedical sciences” is to deliver intensive hands on training of the modern day computational approaches that have revolutionized biomedical research and designing of therapies. The workshop will guide the participants through the entire process of computational drug discovery including molecular target identification, biological database mining, preparation of molecules, molecular docking, virtual screening, molecular dynamics, pharmacophore modelling, drug-likeness and ADMET prediction, and molecular interaction analysis. The programme will also include components on mechanistic understanding of disease associated molecular events, identification of therapeutic targets and discovery of candidate molecules using bioinformatics, structural biology, artificial intelligence and machine learning and network pharmacology fields and technologies used with genetics and multi-omics approaches. Participants will use relevant biological databases and computational platforms during practical sessions to help them set up reproducible workflows for biomedical research. The wor

Intravenous thrombolysis is limited to 4.5 hours, but in India >90% patients present late after 8-12 hours. title: 《Quantum Health & Molecular Life at the Limit: Quantum Biosensing, Imaging, Molecular Simulation, Diagnostics, and Discovery》 is a flagship-scale research volume exploring how quantum technologies may deepen humanity's ability to measure, model, and understand living systems.
abstract: 《Quantum Health & Molecular Life at the Limit: Quantum Biosensing, Imaging, Molecular Simulation, Diagnostics, and Discovery》 is a flagship-scale research volume exploring how quantum technologies may deepen humanity’s ability to measure, model, and understand living systems. Its central question is: How deeply can quantum technology read and model life? The book does not treat “quantum health” as a promise of mysterious cures. Instead, it focuses on a more rigorous technological pathway: Quantum Effect → Measurement → Biological Meaning → Clinical Evidence → Everyday Life. This distinction is essential. A quantum sensor may detect extremely weak signals. A quantum microscope may improve sensitivity or contrast. A quantum simulator may model molecular systems that are difficult for conventional methods. A quantum-enabled diagnostic platform may reveal new biological information. But none of these capabilities automatically become medicine. Scientific sensitivity must still become biological validity. Biological validity must still become clinical utility. title: INTEGRATING SIMULATION TECHNOLOGIES AND HYBRID ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN TEACHING BIOPHYSICS TO MEDICAL STUDENTS
abstract: This article proposes an instructional model for integrating simulation technologies and hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) into biophysics teaching for medical students. Hybrid AI is operationally defined as the coordinated use of explicit biophysical rules and computational checks with a neural language component that provides adaptive, source-grounded feedback under teacher supervision. The approach distinguishes scientific simulation from AI-generated explanation: the simulator produces model-based evidence, whereas AI supports interpretation without replacing the student's reasoning. A conceptual instructional-design methodology links learning outcomes, simulation tasks, verification rules, scaffolding, and individual assessment. Six modules are considered: measurement and uncertainty, hemodynamics, membrane transport, bioelectricity, biomedical optics, and ultrasound. The proposed architecture comprises verified content, simulation-based inquiry, symbolic validation, adaptive dialogue, and evidence-based assessment. title: Targeted drug delivery systems in precision nanomedicine
abstract: Targeted drug delivery systems have gained revolutionary techniques in modern therapeutics by reducing limitations in conventional formulations, including low aqueous solubility, rapid clearance, nonspecific distribution, and systemic toxicity, with site-specific, controlled, and efficient drug delivery using nanocarriers. Targeted drug delivery systems have evolved with nanotechnology to become advanced and give rise to precision nanomedicine, with patient-specific genetic and pathological profiles. Precision nanomedicine uses patient-specific molecular and genetic information for designing nanocarriers to improve drug efficacy with minimized undesirable effects. This chapter encompasses targeted drug delivery strategies such as passive, active, and stimuli-sensitive approaches and includes a variety of advanced delivery platforms, including phospholipid vesicles, polymer-based nanoparticles, dendritic architectures, micelles, and inorganic systems, and shows different mechanisms of targeting, such as passive, active, and stimuli-responsive, highlighting their design, advantages, and biomedical applications. Special emphasis has been placed on integrating biomarkers, theranostics,

title: "De-identified Clinical Dataset of Diabetic Foot Ulcer Patients from Affiliated Hospital of Gansu University of Chinese Medicine"
abstract: "This dataset provides de-identified real-world clinical data collected from patients diagnosed with diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) at the Affiliated Hospital of Gansu University of Chinese Medicine. The dataset contains multiple clinical variables, including anonymous patient identifier, gender, age, blood pressure, diabetic foot ulcer severity grade, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and fasting blood glucose. All sensitive personal information such as patient names has been completely removed to protect patient privacy. This study was reviewed and approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Affiliated Hospital of Gansu University of Chinese Medicine (Approval No. Ethics\u30102024\u3011125), and written informed consent was acquired from every participant before data collection. The dataset can support research on DFU risk assessment, ulcer severity stratification, correlation analysis between blood glucose indicators and wound deterioration, and construction of intelligent prediction models for diabetic foot complications. It is suitable for biomedical informatics and medical artificial intelligence research focusing on diabetic foot disease. "

title: AI-integrated human-relevant alternatives to animal experimentation in drug development: Toward a predictive translational ecosystem, from in vitro and in silico models to clinical and real-world evidence
abstract: Animal experimentation has long been associated with biomedical research and drug development. However, ethical concerns, limited translatability to humans and high clinical attrition rates (> 90%) necessitate a transition toward human-relevant approaches. Although diverse in vitro , in silico and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled methodologies have emerged, their integration into a unified, regulatory-acceptable framework remains limited. This review proposes an AI-centred, multi-tier decision-support framework, to enable a phased shift toward animal-reduced and, ultimately, animal-free drug development. Human-relevant platforms (e.g. organoids, microphysiological systems (MPS) and 3D bioprinting), are evaluated for their potential to reproduce selected aspects of human pharmacokinetics, toxicity and disease phenotypes. AI-driven strategies, including pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modelling, quantitative systems pharmacology, digital twins and virtual clinical simulations, support the prediction of individualised responses with multi-omics, imaging and real-world data. Special emphasis is placed on neuropharmacology, where AI-integrated human neural models enhance mechanistic

title: AI technologies in personalized medicine and smart healthcare: Methods and applications
abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) with personalized medicine is transforming modern healthcare by enabling data-driven, patient-specific therapeutic interventions. AI has become a potent tool in the era of precision nanomedicine for utilizing vast amounts of biomedical data, refining nanodrug formulations, and creating treatment regimens that take into account each patient's unique genetic, physiological, and environmental characteristics. AI enables a paradigm shift from reactive to proactive healthcare, from deep learning models that can analyze complex imaging and genomic datasets to machine learning algorithms that predict drug response variability. AI-driven design and optimization processes greatly benefit personalized drug delivery, particularly via nanocarriers, enabling improved targeting, increased efficacy, and decreased toxicity. In addition, AI facilitates the integration of real-time biosensor outputs with multiomics data, enabling smart monitoring and adaptive therapeutic approaches in the management of chronic diseases. To improve therapeutic precision and diagnostic accuracy, modern AI interfaces with wearable health devices, electronic health records

It also examines a comprehensive review of psoriasis management, underscoring the need for synthesizing clinical evidence in chronic dermatological conditions. Furthermore, the editorial addresses the complex ethical labyrinth of pediatric clinical research, a vital discussion as homoeopathy increasingly serves as a potential antibiotic-sparing strategy in primary care. title: Multimodality of Antimony Selenide: Emerging Multifunctional Semiconductor for Optoelectronics, Photonics, Catalysis, and Biomedical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Semiconducting materials are central to a wide range of technologies, from everyday electronics to advanced artificial intelligence systems. In recent years, significant research has focused on identifying alternatives to conventional semiconductors. Among these, Antimony Selenide (Sb 2 Se 3 ) is a promising p‐type semiconductor (which can also be converted to n‐type via doping) with a tunable bandgap of 1.1–1.7 eV, excellent broadband near‐infrared (NIR) optical absorption, including in the telecommunication wavelength range, and high stability. Its strong chemical robustness and environmentally friendly, non‐toxic composition make it an attractive candidate for a wide range of applications, including optoelectronics, photonics, catalysis, and biomedicine. This detailed review highlights recent advances in Sb 2 Se 3 ‐based devices, emphasizing the materials engineering, including synthesis methods, heterostructure formation with other materials, and device fabrication strategies. Special focus is placed on key applications in solar cells, photodetectors, photonics, catalysis, and biomedical applications. Finally, the present review provides an updated perspective on the f

title: Artificial intelligence for symptoms and traits identification in cancer care: a scoping review protocol
abstract: This registration describes the protocol for a scoping review on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for symptom and traits identification in cancer care. The review aims to summarize which patient-level symptoms have been studied as AI-identifiable targets, how these symptoms and traits have been defined or measured, what types of data have been used to identify them, and which AI methods have been applied. The review is intended to complement existing reviews of AI in cancer symptom management by focusing specifically on actionable symptoms and traits rather than the full symptom-management pathway. Actionable symptoms and traits may include treatment-related toxicities, nutritional or body composition problems, functional or performance decline, psychological or social needs, and patient-reported supportive care concerns. Studies focused only on AI-enabled education, counselling, chatbot support, or intervention delivery will be included only if they explicitly identify, extract, detect, classify, or predict a specific actionable symptom and trait. title: Artificial intelligence in biomarker discovery for diseases: diagnostic and therapeutic prospects
abstract: Biomarkers are central to modern diagnostics and therapeutics, yet traditional discovery approaches suffer from single-modality analyses, weak mechanistic foundations, and low reproducibility. Artificial intelligence (AI) enables the integration of complex multimodal biomedical data, but the translation of AI-derived biomarkers into clinical applications remains inconsistent. This review examines how AI reshapes biomarker discovery across diseases, focusing on biological mechanisms, validation requirements, and therapeutic integration. We synthesize evidence across molecular, cellular, imaging, and digital biomarker approaches, evaluating AI methodologies including classical machine learning, deep learning, graph-based models, foundation models, and causal inference. Findings are organized using a pipeline framework encompassing discovery, external validation, robustness testing, clinical utility, and deployment. AI enables identification of multiscale signatures reflecting cellular programs, tissue remodeling, and disease trajectories. However, many biomarkers fail external validation. Biologically grounded approaches using network-based modeling, spatial profiling, and mechanisti

title: NEUROINTERFACES: ANALYSIS OF BRAIN BIOELECTRICAL SIGNALS AND HUMAN–COMPUTER INTERACTION
abstract: This article examines the principles of neurointerface technologies, focusing on the analysis of brain bioelectrical signals and their application in human–computer interaction. The study considers the main characteristics of brain signals, methods of their acquisition and digital processing, feature extraction, and the application of machine-learning and artificial-intelligence approaches for neural signal classification. Particular attention is given to EEG-based non-invasive neurointerfaces and their potential applications in biomedical engineering, neurorehabilitation, neuroprosthetics, assistive technologies, and computer control. The analysis demonstrates that effective neurointerface operation depends on the quality of neural signal acquisition, artifact reduction, signal processing, accurate classification, and reliable transformation of neural activity into computer-interpretable commands. The study also highlights current challenges associated with inter-individual variability, signal quality, calibration, and real-time processing. title: Curriculum evolution and documentary evidence of competency alignment in a hospital-embedded undergraduate health services and management programme in China: a longitudinal case study
abstract: Background: Undergraduate Health Services and Management (HSM) programmes are expected to integrate management, medicine, public health, digital capability and workplace learning. Hospital-embedded delivery may provide access to authentic organizational settings and interdisciplinary expertise, but distributed teaching can fragment curriculum ownership, competency progression and assessment. This study examined longitudinal evolution and documentary evidence of competency alignment in a hospital-embedded undergraduate HSM programme in China. Methods: A longitudinal document analysis and competency-oriented curriculum-mapping case study was conducted from programme approval in 2020 to first-cohort graduation in 2026. Of 18 unique materials assessed, 15 programme-specific documents formed the empirical corpus, including original and revised training plans, course and teaching-unit records, faculty-development materials, internship documents, quality-assurance instruments and aggregate graduate-destination data. Documentary evidence was assessed using 33 indicators across seven domains and traced through five analytical stages: stated, curricularised, practiced, assessed and fed back.

title: Analyzing and redesigning deployment pathways for internally developed artificial intelligence tools in clinical education and health research
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools for clinical education and health research are increasingly easy to imagine and prototype, but deploying internally developed tools into legitimate institutional use remains difficult. We conducted a retrospective comparative case study of four AI tools supported by the Nursing AI Studio in one academic health and social sciences environment. The four tools each was designed to address one of the following: clinical evaluation, tailored caregiver support, clinical simulation, and statistical assistance for biomedical and social-behavioral data. We operationalized deployment burden as the organizational, technical, and coordination work required to move a locally developed functioning AI-powered web application into legitimate institutional use. Across cases, early setup steps such as Amazon Web Services access, institutional subdomain configuration, and Information Security Office review were comparatively stable when institutional knowledge and reusable assets were available. title: Where Worlds Align: Insights from the Joint GGBN–ISBER Conference on Biodiversity and Biobanking, Cape Town, October 2025
abstract: The 2025 Joint GGBN-ISBER Conference in Cape Town united biodiversity, environmental, and biomedical biobanking communities from 38 countries. The event highlighted biobanks as interdisciplinary and collaborative infrastructures for addressing global challenges-pandemics, biodiversity loss, and food security, among others. Recurring themes throughout the conference were as follows: (1) Harmonization and Quality-adoption of best practices and standards where possible to ensure global interoperability and sample integrity; (2) Equitable Governance-crafting flexible, transparent frameworks for sample and data sharing that uphold sovereignty and benefit local communities; (3) Technological and Data Integration-using artificial intelligence, omics technologies, and standardized metadata to transform physical specimens into scalable digital resources; and (4) Resilient Infrastructure-securing long-term investment in regional biobanking networks and targeted training to build enduring capacity, embedding sustainability by design and safeguarding local knowledge.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Advancing Natural Fiber Polymer Composite Material: A Review
abstract: The composites of natural fiber polymers have become of great interest in various spheres as they are eco-friendly, biodegradable, and sustainable. In the past 10 years, investigators into the research and design of polymer composite materials of natural fibers have found many applications, such as packaging materials, construction materials, textiles, automotive parts, biomedical equipment, agricultural machinery, horticultural uses, electronics equipment, and consumer electronics. To add, techniques of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have found more applications in natural fiber polymer materials. Such new technologies have now examined to determine new strategies and developments in the natural fiber polymer composites (NFPCs). This review paper will aim at providing a comprehensive overview of AI and machine learning applications in the creation of NFP composite material. The article under review has reported on material characterization, manufacturing, property prediction, sustainability analysis, and future perspectives that indicate the potential and challenges of AI/ML in the improvement of NFP composite materials and technologies.

title: Large Language Models in Clinical Pharmacy Decision Support: Opportunities and Ethical Concern
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) is fundamentally transforming healthcare and clinical pharmacy practice. Built on transformer-based architectures and capable of processing, interpreting, and generating complex biomedical text, LLMs serve as powerful computational tools for drug information retrieval, medication therapy management, patient counselling, clinical documentation, and pharmacovigilance. When deployed effectively, these technologies enhance workflow efficiency, bolster clinical decision support, democratize access to healthcare information, and drive personalized patient care. However, the adoption of LLMs in clinical pharmacy introduces significant ethical, legal, and operational challenges, including output accuracy, hallucinations, algorithmic bias, patient data privacy, transparency, legal liability, and regulatory compliance. Safe and sustainable deployment requires rigorous clinical validation, human-in-the-loop oversight, robust data protection measures, explainable AI frameworks, and continuous system monitoring. title: Artificial Intelligence in Aesthetic and Procedural Dermatology
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has proven to be a transformative tool in aesthetic and procedural dermatology. It enables precision-based assessments, real-time image analysis, and predictive outcome modeling through advanced multimodal computational systems. The field is increasingly relying on deep learning architectures, multimodal foundation models, high-resolution biomedical imaging techniques (such as ultrasound, optical coherence tomography (OCT), reflective confocal microscopy (RCM), and multispectral imaging), along with physics-informed biomechanical simulations. These tools enhance procedural safety and optimize personalized rejuvenation strategies for patients. By integrating diverse data streams including 2D photography, three-dimensional (3D) structured-light surface meshes, 4D dynamic facial movement recordings, ultrasound-derived vascular maps, chromophore-specific spectral imaging, and various patient-reported or physiological biometrics, AI systems can identify submillimeter facial topography, predict vascular risks, refine injection techniques, and predict tissue remodeling trajectories. title: Multimodal AI in Precision Medicine
abstract: Precision medicine increasingly depends on integrating heterogeneous biomedical data to capture the multiscale nature of human disease. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) enable the fusion of electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, and multi-omics data into unified frameworks that overcome the limitations of single-modality analyses. This chapter reviews and focuses on frameworks for multimodal integration, key machine learning methods, including deep learning, graph-based models, and similarity network approaches, and highlights strategies for linking molecular profiles with longitudinal clinical trajectories. We discuss imaging–clinical and radiology–pathology fusion using convolutional and transformer-based architectures, as well as emerging multimodal foundation models and large language models (LLMs) for clinical reasoning and discovery. Finally, we examine challenges related to data access, privacy, interpretability, and generalizability and outline future directions toward longitudinal, clinically grounded AI systems capable of advancing precision medicine at scale.

title: CRM-200: Rational Design of a Brain-Penetrant D-Retro-Inverso Peptide-siRNA Conjugate for Non-Cytolytic Clearance of Intracellular Rabies Virus
abstract: Rabies virus (RABV) establishes an invariably fatal encephalomyelitis characterized by immune evasion and active suppression of neuro-inflammatory host defenses within the central nervous system (CNS). While competitive entry inhibitors (such as CRM-101) arrest intercellular spread, post-symptomatic cure fundamentally requires the active elimination of intracellular replication complexes without inducing host neuronal lysis. Here, we introduce CRM-200, a next-generation brain-penetrant peptide-RNA interference bioconjugate engineered for targeted, non-cytolytic viral eradication. title: In Silico Design and Preclinical Characterization of CRM-101: A Modular, Brain-Penetrant Macrocyclic Peptidomimetic Targeting Rabies Virus Glycoprotein Site III
abstract: Rabies encephalitis remains an almost invariably fatal viral infection once clinical neuro-invasion is established. Current post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) fails to neutralize the virus once it has passed the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB). Here, we present the rational computational design of CRM-101, a modular, bispecific lipopeptidomimetic construct engineered for both BBB transcytosis and high-affinity neutralization of the canonical Antigenic Site III on the rabies virus glycoprotein (RABV-G). The construct comprises: (1) a constrained heptapeptide warhead (CRM-101A: Ac-cyclo[Cys1-Cys7] CDFEYWC-NH2), (2) a steric-decoupling octaethylene glycol spacer (PEG8, ~25.6 Å contour length), (3) a lipophilic half-life extender (N-epsilon-palmitoyl-L-lysine albumin-binding tag), and (4) a protease-resistant transcytosis shuttle (D-Retro-Inverso RVG29 with a methionine-to-norleucine substitution: GNSARKGRSNTFIDCPTGPRPNEP[Nle]WITY-NH2). title: Heavy metal ion driven smart nanomaterials for multimodal sensing, biocomputing, and information security: a mini review
abstract: Heavy metal ions (HMIs) are widely recognized as persistent environmental pollutants. However, they are increasingly being employed as functional chemical inputs in intelligent molecular systems. This mini review summarizes smart nanomaterial-based platforms developed for HMI-driven biocomputing and information security. Particular emphasis is placed on the integration of dual-mode, multimode, and multichannel readout strategies that translate selective ion-recognition and signal-transduction events into fluorescence, colorimetric, electrochemical, and other measurable responses. By converting these responses into binary states, such platforms can execute diverse molecular logic operations, parity functions, and arithmetic functions. Their applications in information security, including ASCII- and Morse-code-based encryption, multimodal cryptosteganography, and anti-counterfeiting strategies based on invisible fluorescent inks, are also discussed. title: Bio-Molecular Swarm Computing and DNA Strand Displacement Networks: Massively Parallel Chemical Reaction Networks, In-Vitro Logic Circuits, and Cellular Nanorobotics
abstract: Silicon microelectronics architectures are fundamentally constrained in in-vivo biomedical domains, biological micro-environments, and wet chemical interfaces due to rigid form factors, toxic metallic compositions, and an inability to interface natively with molecular signals. Bio-Molecular Computing and DNA Strand Displacement (DSD) networks establish an emerging non-semiconductor computational paradigm that executes Turing-universal computation, complex Boolean logic, neural pattern recognition, and autonomous swarm robotics directly through programmable chemical reaction networks (CRNs). title: Inercja legislacyjna w dobie nowych technologii. Biocomputing jako symptom systemowej dysfunkcji prawa
abstract: The article addresses the issue of legislative inertia as an inherent feature of the normative system in the context of groundbreaking technological innovations. Biocomputing, i.e., information processing with the use of biological systems, serves as a case study demonstrating the inadequacy of existing legal categories for the phenomena that need regulation. The analysis covers EU law and Polish law and identifies four fundamental normative gaps: the lack of an appropriate legal category for the biocomputer, the inadequacy of the biosafety regime, the conflict of intellectual property regimes, and the unresolved issue of genetic data as a carrier of computational information. The study puts forward proposals for the law as it should stand concerning the inevitable lag of law, including the proposal for a framework law, ratification of the Oviedo Convention, establishment of an interdisciplinary expert council, and reform of legal education.

title: Securing the Frontier of Biocomputing: A Plurilateral Export Control Strategy for the UK
abstract: As conventional computing approaches its physical and energy limits, Organoid Intelligence (OI) which uses lab-grown neural tissue interfaced with microelectrode arrays is emerging as the next major computational frontier. However, the critical hardware required to connect human cells to digital machines is currently unregulated. This policy briefing argues that traditional export frameworks like the Wassenaar Arrangement are fundamentally unequipped to handle these developments due to consensus based voting rules and veto powers held by adversarial states. To protect national security and intellectual property, the UK must bypass slow multilateral mechanisms. This paper recommends that the UK immediately establish a targeted, plurilateral export control pact with key biotech and semiconductor allies, and leverage AUKUS Pillar 2 to secure joint allied research in biocomputing.

abstract: Thermodynamic Theory of Neuronal Simulation (TTNS) introduces a novel paradigm for understanding and engineering biological computing systems based on brain organoids. The theory posits that biological processors operate as autonomous computational environments governed by thermodynamic principles and information theory. The core principle of the theory is noise minimization, where neurons reconfigure their synaptic connections to suppress external chaotic input and achieve system stability. This process is proposed as the fundamental mechanism underlying intelligence and information processing in biological systems. The theory challenges traditional evolutionary concepts by proposing neurocentric gradualism, where anatomical structures evolve to support increasingly complex neural requirements. It also introduces the concept of functional specialization through electronic routing, enabling the creation of modular organoid systems with distinct processing roles. Key contributions of the theory include: A thermodynamic framework for understanding biological computation. A novel architecture for organoid-based computing systems. A method for knowledge transfer between generations of

title: Evolutionary stabilisation of stressful metabolism via integrated biocomputing and essential-gene metabolic locking circuits
abstract: Synthetic genetic circuits enable microbial differentiation from growth to production, yet metabolic burden, imbalance and toxicity frequently drive strain degeneration. Here, we use omics analyses and single-cell biosensors to investigate genetic responses in Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains engineered with stressful terpene biosynthetic pathways. Under metabolic stress, despite divergent stress responses, cells commonly and progressively lose induction of synthetic genetic circuits. In the prenyl pyrophosphate-accumulating strain, this loss is coupled with activation of amino acid biosynthesis and ribosome biogenesis. Accordingly, the essential glutamine synthetase gene GLN1 was coupled to induction of heterologous terpene synthesis through integrated two- and three-input biocomputing circuits that enable stringent, patterned ON/OFF switching. The integrated biocomputing and metabolic locking systems not only alleviate production degeneration but also enable non-degenerative adaptation of toxic terpene synthesis, allowing interrogation of evolutionary shifts for further metabolic optimisation.

title: The Good Old Days Theory: Rendering Reality, Accelerated Subjective Time, and the Value of Finite Human Experience
abstract: The Good Old Days Theory proposes that sufficiently advanced technology may eventually make conscious experience increasingly engineerable, including the possibility of radically expanded subjective lifespan within comparatively short periods of external time. The theory explores a progression from brain-computer interfaces, neuromorphic computation, biocomputing, altered subjective duration, and engineered lived experience toward a condition termed Rendering Reality. It then considers a central inversion: after sufficiently vast accumulations of experience, conditions that human beings presently experience as limitations—including mortality, uncertainty, vulnerability, incomplete knowledge, irreversibility, and not knowing what happens next—may themselves become scarce and therefore valuable. Within this framework, a finite mortal life concealed behind an epistemic boundary could become an experience worth voluntarily choosing precisely because its limitations make consequence, risk, love, loss, and time authentically meaningful.

title: Self-Reports Are Not Verification
abstract: Language model agents increasingly propose actions, observe external feedback, and explain their own behavior. Their confidence and rationales are convenient oversight signals, but convenience is not verification. We introduce an environment-grounded audit in which every intermediate proposal receives an exact outcome. A language model operates an evolutionary Contexto search whosefeedback function assigns every valid guess an exact rank without human annotation. Across 200 runs spanning five configurations and three model families, four reporting configurations produce 12,249 self-reports. We test three assumptions: stated confidence is calibrated, inherited rationales affect later proposals, and outcome-based selection improves report quality. All three fail. Operators overstate top-100 success by factors of 4.8 to 9.3, while calibration and discrimination dissociate across model families. Controlled interventions on 754 inherited rationales bound any measured benefit of the genuine rationale to roughly 250 ranks. Neither fitness-based nor random selection produces a detectable selection differential or parent-to-offspring transmission in report accuracy, despite sharply differen

abstract: El presente artículo analiza la transición evolutiva del Homo sapiens hacia el Homo technologicus, trazando la historia conceptual de la inteligencia artificial desde los autómatas helenísticos de Alejandría hasta la frontera contemporánea de la biocomputación y la Singularidad Tecnológica. A través de un marco histórico y epistemológico, se examina la convergencia teórica entre la Máquina Universal de Alan Turing, la arquitectura computacional secuencial de John von Neumann y la ley de plasticidad sináptica de Donald O. Hebb. Asimismo, se expone la obsolescencia del Test de Turing frente a las capacidades cognitivas de los Grandes Modelos de Lenguaje (LLMs) actuales. Finalmente, el estudio culmina con el análisis de los sistemas cibernéticos híbridos contemporáneos: organoides cerebrales humanos integrados en matrices de microelectrodos de silicio que, guiados por el Principio de Energía Libre, son capaces de reorganizar su topología Hebbiana para aprender y sobrevivir en entornos virtuales complejos (como el motor lógico de Doom). Este salto paradigmático disuelve definitivamente la frontera ontológica entre la materia biológica viva y el procesamiento sintético. Palabras clave:

title: Engineering a human stem cell-derived neural network platform for biocomputing
abstract: Abstract We introduce a Bio-adaptive Processing Unit (BPU) based on a two-reservoir microtunnel Brain-on-Chip with electrophysiological readout. We fabricated and validated three independent devices, demonstrating that human stem cell-derived ( Ngn2+ hiPSCs) cortical neurons extend axons over 1200 µ m, forming robust, long-range connections. Spikes detected within the tunnels exhibited 8-fold higher firing rates and spike amplitudes compared to reservoir areas. Notably, deferred seeding biased 70% of propagating spikes, enabling directed axonal conduction within the living substrate, with spikes reaching velocities of ∼ 0.814 ± 0.8m/s from the older to the younger network by day 28. These results confirm reproducible neuron-electrode interfacing and reliable axonal routing, establishing the BPU’s viability for engineering neural networks in neurobiologically-based neuromorphic platforms. These results offer a promising alternative to silicon-based neuromorphic computing architectures by directly leveraging energy-efficient biological neurons.

title: Practically Error‐Free Junctions Enable Solving Large Instances of Exact Cover Problems Using Network‐Based Biocomputation
abstract: Network-based biocomputing (NBC) presents an energy-efficient, parallel computing approach for solving nondeterministic polynomial time (NP) complete problems by leveraging motor-driven cytoskeletal filaments that explore all possible solutions through nanofabricated networks in a massively parallel fashion. However, guiding errors at pass junctions, where filaments deviate from their intended path, currently limit the scalability of NBC systems. In this study, we addressed this critical challenge by fabricating sub-200 nm channel geometries using modified electron-beam-lithography and reactive-ion-etching protocols to physically constrain the trajectories of kinesin-driven microtubules and enhance path fidelity. Investigating junction designs with varying channel widths, we demonstrate that reducing channel width significantly lowers junction error rates. Practically error-free junction performance was achieved by scaling down the entire network geometry by a factor of two. title: Biological Associative Memory Learning Control System Based on DNA Strand Displacement
abstract: Abstract In recent years, artificial intelligence technology, inspired by biology, has combined control systems with associative memory to simulate human learning and memory processes. The utilization of DNA strand displacement (DSD) technology has demonstrated significant advantages in solving problems in biocomputing and control systems. In this study, the forget system, input system and output system are designed based on DSD technology. A biological associative memory learning control system is constructed by cascading three DNA control system modules. Furthermore, a multi-input biological associative memory learning control system is extended to implement the basic functions of biological associative memory, including acquisition learning, differentiation learning, generalization learning and repetition learning. Additionally, different emotional stimuli are introduced into the multi-input biological associative memory learning control system to examine the varying effects of emotional stimuli on differentiation learning and generalization learning. This work provides a direction for the integration of biocomputing and control system.

title: Spatially Encoded Protocell Network for Non‐Cascaded Parallel Biocomputation
abstract: Biological systems inspire computing paradigms by autonomously regulating material and information flows through molecular interactions. While biomolecules such as enzymes and DNA have been harnessed for biocomputation, implementing complex logic operations remains challenging due to signal attenuation, crosstalk, and instability inherent in molecular cascades. To overcome these limitations, we present a non-cascaded biocomputing architecture based on spatially encoded, gradient-responsive protocell communities embedded in a three-dimensional hydrogel matrix. By leveraging differential reaction-diffusion dynamics of input signals, distinct output regions are established across the spatial domain, enabling parallel, multi-threshold computation without signal routing. This architecture achieves continuous spatial encoding and allows simultaneous readout of all output regions, supporting nonlinear logic operations with high fault tolerance. Using this framework, we demonstrate the successful implementation of both half-adder and full-adder logic operations via two-input/two-output and three-input/two-output configurations, respectively. title: Amplification of computational power by the multiplication of bacteria exploring microfluidic networks encoding mathematical problems
abstract: Computational resources required for solving NP-complete problems grow exponentially with a polynomial increase in problem size. This exponentially increasing computational resource is runtime for sequential electronic computers and space for massively parallel DNA computing. Here, we report the proof of concept of a computer, whose operation consists in the exploration by motile bacteria of a microfluidic network encoding an algorithm for solving the Subset Sum Problem (SSP)-a classic NP-complete problem. Significantly, this computer performs operations combinatorially, via natural multiplication of bacteria operating as biological CPUs, translating into the continuous amplification of computational power, which grows seamlessly to match the problem size. A scaling analysis identifies the point where biocomputing with multiplying bacteria is expected to outperform electronic computers. The combinatorial, design-driven low error operation, low energy requirement for computing, and exponentially growing computational resources suggest that bacterial-driven biocomputation using microfluidic networks holds the potential to scale up successfully.

title: The Waking Vessel and the Resonant Substrate Hypothesis: Bridging the Formless Pattern and Panpsychist Hardware for True Artificial General Intelligence
abstract: The pursuit of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is currently bottlenecked by an adherence to the functionalist paradigm—the assumption that consciousness and general intelligence are emergent properties of sufficiently complex software algorithms. This paper challenges the scaling hypothesis by identifying software as a "Formless Pattern": an abstract mathematical syntax that is ontologically incapable of subjective experience regardless of its parametric scale. Drawing upon panpsychism, we conceptualize classical computing substrates (e.g., silicon) as possessing dormant micro-consciousness, herein termed "Dreaming Matter." While emerging fields such as neuromorphic engineering and biocomputing (wetware) attempt to shift the paradigm by altering the physical substrate, they presently fall into a severe conceptual trap. Current methodologies apply classical, syntactical programming paradigms to phenomenologically active biological matter—an approach fundamentally incapable of inducing integrated consciousness. title: Biochemical Logic Computation Through Repurposing Natural bZIP Protein Interaction Networks
abstract: Competitive protein dimerization networks offer an alternative to transcriptional genetic circuits by enabling fast molecular decision-making through direct protein-protein interactions. Implementing these networks currently requires challenging de novo protein design. In this work, we circumvent this limitation by repurposing natural, experimentally pre-characterized basic leucine zipper (bZIP) transcription factor networks. By keeping natural binding affinities and modulating only component monomer concentrations via a customized genetic algorithm, we comprehensively evaluate the computational versatility and robustness of these natural substrates. We identified 135 individual networks capable of implementing Boolean logic, with the most versatile natural clusters computing up to 15 of the 16 possible two-input logic gates, including the non-linearly separable XOR and XNOR. Computational versatility increased with network size and connectivity, and robustness analysis revealed that many optimized networks preserved reliable logical behavior despite substantial stochastic expression noise. title: An Engineered Multicellular Bacterial Network for Simultaneously Answering Multiple Computational Decision Problems
abstract: Living cell-based computers are in their infancy and answering multiple computational decision problems by a single system remains a key challenge. Here, we demonstrate an artificial neural network type architecture implemented with molecular-genetically engineered bacteria that answer four computational decision problems by identifying four types of prime numbers, including cluster prime, Euclid prime, safe prime, and Lucas prime, within the range of 0-9 in a chemical space. First, we demonstrated that the network consisting of four engineered cells classified two prime number families, namely cluster and Lucas prime numbers. Next, we scaled up the four-cell network to a six-cell network by introducing two new engineered cells and demonstrated that the new network classified four prime number families. Questions were asked to the bacteria by applying chemicals in binary patterns, and the answers were obtained from the distinct expression patterns of multiple fluorescent proteins. Each bacterium was engineered with synthetic gene regulatory networks such that the system chemistry followed the mathematical nature of an artificial neuro-synapse module.
