title: APICURON: Database for crediting & recognition of biocuration activities
abstract: APICURON is a software-as-a-service platform developed at the Biocomputing UP Lab (University of Padova) to recognize and credit scientific contributions, particularly in biocuration. It offers a standardized yet flexible system for tracking and rewarding diverse activities that often go unacknowledged in traditional academic metrics. By linking contributors, actions, and contribution objects, APICURON enables detailed activity reporting. It incorporates dynamic reward mechanisms such as badges, medals, and leaderboards to motivate and highlight individual efforts. Contributors can also be grouped by role or validation level, allowing for tailored recognition and fair comparisons. Since its launch, APICURON has grown rapidly, integrating with major scientific resources and tracking over 125,000 contributions from a growing user base. Future developments include an advanced notification system and more specific reward types, all guided by a commitment to transparency and user privacy.

title: Kinase Drug Discovery: An Artificial Intelligence Revolution
abstract: Protein kinases play a pivotal role in regulating cellular functions and signaling pathways, with over 530 kinase genes identified in the human genome. Traditional drug discovery targeting kinases is a lengthy and costly process, often exceeding 15 years and $1 billion. However, artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential to streamline this pipeline by accelerating target identification, validation, and drug design. AI-driven methodologies such as machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing have revolutionized preclinical drug discovery, enabling rapid identification of drug candidates, structural predictions, and binding affinity assessments. Tools such as AlphaFold2, OnionNet-2, and Deeply Tough illustrate AI’s role in structural and virtual screening of drugs. AI has also significantly impacted clinical trials through digital twinning, patient recruitment optimization, and real-time monitoring, enhancing trial efficiency and precision. Currently, 75 AI-powered drugs are in various clinical phases, with notable successes in novel target identification and drug repurposing. Despite its promise, AI in drug discovery faces challenges such as eth

title: Barcoding Microtubules: Encoding Information onto Macromolecules by Photobleaching
abstract: Kinesin-1-powered microtubules have emerged as versatile components in biocomputing and biosensing technologies. However, the inability to identify and track individual microtubules has constrained their applications to ensemble behaviors, limiting their potential for single-entity-based nanotechnologies. To address this challenge, we present a novel method for encoding digital information directly onto individual microtubules using photobleaching patterns. Binary numbers (1 to 15) were encoded within ∼12 μm segments of moving microtubules by photobleaching with a stationary pulsed laser, creating spatial frequency patterns corresponding to distinct bits of information. Fourier analysis enabled the accurate retrieval of the encoded data, demonstrating the feasibility of direct information storage and retrieval on macromolecular structures. This approach offers a transformative solution for recording microtubule trajectories within nanotechnological devices by encoding path information directly onto microtubules at branch points, obviating the need for video-based tracking. We anticipate that this innovation will advance the development of individualized microtubule-based technologi

title: Development of a new high-yield integration site assay reveals disease-specific patterns across HTLV-1-associated pathologies
abstract: Human T lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1) chronic infection is maintained through mitotic proliferation of the infected CD4+ T cells, where the viral genome is integrated as a provirus in its host genome. HTLV-1 integration sites (ISs) have a part in HTLV-1-associated pathologies, with distinct IS patterns associated with malignant proliferation or inflammatory diseases. However, IS determination remains challenging because most assays rely on complex biological and biocomputing protocols. We present an IS assay that solely relies on PCR and Sanger sequencing, which allowed HTLV-1 IS determination in four patients with various HTLV-1-associated pathologies. We adapted an IS assay derived from a panhandle PCR, with several modifications to increase yield. Absence of bias regarding IS retrieval was confirmed using TCRγ clonality. IS analysis was performed in four HTLV-1-positive patients: two with polymyositis, one with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL), and one with HTLV-1-associated myelopathy (HAM). Overall yield was around 20%, with a mean sequence length downstream the IS of 336 ± 230 bp (range, 44-1,024 bp). There was no major bias in clonal determination, as IS results ma

title: Solving Minimum Spanning Tree Problems Based on DNA Chemical Reaction Networks
abstract: INTRODUCTION: DNA strand displacement reactions are emerging as a promising biocomputing tool. The minimum spanning tree problem is fundamental in graph theory. This paper explores the use of DNA strand displacement reaction networks for addressing the minimum spanning tree problem. We also present a computing model that is based on DNA strand displacement reactions. METHODS: The model effectively solves the minimum spanning tree problem by intelligently integrating the three reaction modules of weighted, threshold, and sum. Thus, initially, we encoded the edges in the graph using distinct DNA sequences and effectively assigned the edges their respective weights. Afterwards, the threshold module applied a filter to the weighted edges based on the fluorescence intensity. Ultimately, the sum module gathered the filtered edges to calculate the overall weight of the minimum spanning tree. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conducted simulation experiments using visual DSD software. RESULTS: The results of the simulations showed the viability and precision of this DNA computing model in resolving intricate problems. CONCLUSION: Furthermore, this study not on

title: Rapid Customizing of Flexible Oects Arrays for Low-Cost Biosensing and Biocomputing
abstract: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising for next-generation biosensing and neuromorphic computing. With the growing demand for flexible OECTs in wearable bioelectronics, a low-cost, fast fabrication method is highly desired. Here, we propose a scalable printing-based fabrication method for rapid production of flexible all-solid-state OECTs. The proposed technology can produce devices with high yield, minimal variation, and high stability, which allows quick evaluation of OECT-relevant new materials, devices, and circuits.

title: Track-regenerated DNA motor based on magnetic separation for sensitive and sustainable detection of viral RNA and acetamiprid
Analyzing Wet-Neuromorphic Computing Using Bacterial Gene Regulatory Neural Networks
abstract: Biocomputing envisions the development computing paradigms using biological systems, ranging from micron-level components to collections of cells, including organoids. This paradigm shift exploits hidden natural computing properties, to develop miniaturized wet-computing devices that can be deployed in harsh environments, and to explore designs of novel energy-efficient systems. In parallel, we witness the emergence of AI hardware, including neuromorphic processors with the aim of improving computational capacity. This study brings together the concept of biocomputing and neuromorphic systems by focusing on the bacterial gene regulatory networks and their transformation into Gene Regulatory Neural Networks (GRNNs). We explore the intrinsic properties of gene regulations, map this to a gene-perceptron function, and propose an application-specific sub-GRNN search algorithm that maps the network structure to match a computing problem. Focusing on the model organism Escherichia coli, the base-GRNN is initially extracted and validated for accuracy. Subsequently, a comprehensive feasibility analysis of the derived GRNN confirms its computational prowess in classification and regression t

title: Collective Intelligence Online Experiments: A Learning Method and Its Pedagogical Applications Through Online Collaborative Work Platforms
abstract: Abstract Collective intelligence is a novel construct which posits that a large number of people can work together to come up with better answers to various problems in less time than would be spent individually or in groups. Based on this premise, the University Institute for Biocomputing and Complex Systems Physics Research (BIFI) of the University of Zaragoza and the company Kampal Data Solutions created the collective intelligence platform named ‘Collective Learning.’ This chapter presents the various experiments that have been carried out in the educational field with this platform, and it highlights how the results obtained have enhanced our knowledge about the generation of collective intelligence and its impact on the possible learning of digital skills and online risk management competencies by the participating students.

title: Translating Extracellular Electron Transfer Activities with Organic Electrochemical Transistors
abstract: Extracellular electron transfer (EET) is a process through which certain microorganisms can transfer electrons across their cell membranes to external electron acceptors, linking cellular metabolism to their environment. While Geobacter and Shewanella have been the primary models for EET research, emerging studies reveal that EET-active species are also associated with fermentation and the human gut microbiome. Leveraging the ability of EET to bridge biological and electronic systems, we present a protocol for using organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) to translate microbial EET activity into easily detectable electrical signals. This system enables the use of cellular responses to external stimuli for biosensing and biocomputing applications. Specifically, we demonstrated the de-doping of the p-type poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene): poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT: PSS) channel in the OECT is driven by cellular EET from Shewanella oneidensis. By transcriptionally controlling EET flux by genetic circuits, we establish the biosensing capability of this hybrid OECT system to detect chemical stimuli, such as inducer molecules. Furthermore, we introduce plasmid-based Boolean logic

title: Organoid intelligence and biocomputing advances: Current steps and future directions
abstract: Organoid intelligence (OI) offers transformative potential across diverse fields, particularly in personalized medicine, biocomputing, and environmental sustainability. Here, we examine how the unique biological properties of organoids, which closely mimic human physiological processes, enable the development of advanced disease models, drug testing platforms, and sustainable bioengineered solutions. Researchers can address critical carbon capture, bioremediation, and pollution control challenges by integrating OI into computational systems. This review discusses the technological advancements that enable OI applications, including microfluidics, artificial intelligence, and electrophysiology while emphasizing the need for standardized protocols to foster reproducibility and scalability. Additionally, we address the ethical and legal considerations surrounding OI development, such as data privacy, potential misuse, and the emerging moral status of organoids with advanced cognitive-like properties. We highlight the Baltimore Declaration as a foundational framework for ensuring OI technologies align with ethical standards and societal benefits. OI's responsible advancement promises t

title: Biocomputing at the crossroad between emulating artificial intelligence and cellular supremacy
abstract: Biocomputation aims to create sophisticated biological systems capable of addressing important problems in (bio)medicine with a machine-like precision. At present, computational gene networks engineered by single- or multi-layered assembly of DNA-, RNA- and protein-level gene switches have allowed bacterial or mammalian cells to perform various regulation logics of interest, including Boolean calculation or neural network-like computing. This review highlights the molecular building blocks, design principles, and computational tasks demonstrated by current biocomputers, before briefly discussing possible fields where biological computers may ultimately outcompete their electronic counterparts and achieve cellular supremacy.

title: Construction of DNA Circuit Based on Toehold-mediated DNAzyme Cleavage
abstract: As a special type of DNA molecules with molecular manipulation capabilities, DNAzymes possess the abilities of both information storage and information processing. In particular, the integrated application of DNAzymes and DNA strand displacement has enriched the toolbox for the realization of biochemical reactions in biocomputing and provided new methods for constructing diverse and functional DNA circuits. In this paper, we propose a new method for construction of DNA circuit based on toehold-mediated DNAzyme cleavage. In this method, DNAzyme displacement can be triggered through toehold mediation, and then DNAzyme slide along the predesigned track formed by double stranded DNA to achieve the purpose of specific cleavage. Based on this new method, an XOR gate and an INHIBIT gate were constructed firstly, and then a combinatorial DNA circuit, an OR-INHIBIT circuit, was presented. The method of toehold-mediated DNAzyme cleavage provides a flexible and reliable strategy for the construction of DNA circuits and can be applied in the fields such as biological computing, molecular sensing, and DNA nanostructures.

title: Biofabrication of brain-like living tissue: structure to intelligence
abstract: Abstract Brain, the material foundation of human intelligence, is the most complex tissue in the human body. Brain diseases are among the leading threats to human life, yet our understanding of their pathogenic mechanisms and drug development remains limited, largely due to the lack of accurate brain-like tissue models that replicate its complex structure and functions. Therefore, constructing brain-like models—both in morphology and function—possesses significant scientific value for advancing brain science and pathological pharmacology research, representing the frontiers in the biomanufacturing field. This review outlines the primary requirements and challenges in biomanufacturing brain-like tissue, addressing its complex structures, functions, and environments. Also, the existing biomanufacturing technologies, strategies, and characteristics for brain-like models are depicted, and cutting-edge developments in biomanufacturing central neural repair prosthetics, brain development models, brain disease models, and brain-inspired biocomputing models are systematically reviewed. Finally, the paper concludes with future perspectives on the biomanufacturing of brain-like tissue transi

Biological Computing
abstract: This open access book comprehensively introduces biocomputing, focusing on its foundational theories, experimental operations, and computational models. Biocomputing represents an innovative computational paradigm that leverages biomolecules as a carrier for processing and storing information. As a core enabler of human progress, computational tools serve as critical benchmarks of societal advancement and are key drivers of technological innovation. While electronic computers currently dominate as the primary instruments for information processing, their underlying manufacturing technologies are approaching physical and practical limits. This has prompted the search for alternative computational models and tools to meet the demands of future advancements. Over recent decades, scientists have explored various fields to develop novel computational frameworks. These efforts have led to the emergence of groundbreaking paradigms, such as artificial neural networks inspired by brain-like information processing, evolutionary computing based on genetic mechanisms, biocomputing utilizing the unique properties of biomolecules, quantum computing exploiting quantum phenomena, and optical compu

title: Opportunities and Challenges of Brain-on-a-Chip Interfaces
abstract: The convergence of life sciences and information technology is driving a new wave of scientific and technological innovation, with brain-on-a-chip interfaces (BoCIs) emerging as a prominent area of focus in the brain-computer interface field. BoCIs aim to create an interactive bridge between lab-grown brains and the external environment, utilizing advanced encoding and decoding technologies alongside electrodes. Unlike classical brain-computer interfaces that rely on human or animal brains, BoCIs employ lab-grown brains, offering greater experimental controllability and scalability. Central to this innovation is the advancement of stem cell and microelectrode array technologies, which facilitate the development of neuro-electrode hybrid structures to ensure effective signal transmission in lab-grown brains. Furthermore, the evolution of BoCI systems depends on a range of stimulation strategies and novel decoding algorithms, including artificial-intelligence-driven methods, which has expanded BoCI applications to pattern recognition and robotic control. Biological neural networks inherently grant BoCI systems neuro-inspired computational properties-such as ultralow energy consumptio

title: Biocomputing systems based on carbon materials and DNA
abstract: Biocomputing is an interdisciplinary field at the intersection of biology, informatics, and nanotechnology. Biocomputing nanoplatforms are sensor modules based on biomolecules that detect and process external stimuli as inputs and generate corresponding outputs. These platforms operate according to specific algorithms, often obeying the laws of Boolean algebra. Such systems are typically based on DNA logic interfaces due to their versatility in terms of design, synthesis, and potential input types. While DNA logic gates are typically implemented in homogeneous oligonucleotide solutions, creating various heterogeneous systems using organic or inorganic nanosystems offers advantages in designing and operating such logic systems. This review focuses on applying carbon-based materials, such as graphene, graphene oxide, carbon nanotubes, and carbon quantum dots, to DNA logic gates. For the first time, this article summarizes the entire body of literature on the topic, highlighting how the physicochemical properties of carbon-based materials can benefit the design and functionality of DNA logic gates. The review summarizes the main types of logic gates, describes the mechanisms underlyin

PredictMod: A Platform for Predicting Medical Intervention Outcomes and Sharing Custom ML/AI Models
abstract: Machine learning/artificial intelligence (ML/AI)-based predictive modeling is becoming increasingly popular in healthcare, particularly within the scope of precision medicine. Models based on patient data are effective tools for clinical decision-making, as well as impactful methods for researchers to expand on existing scientific and clinical understanding of biomarkers and biological pathways. We present PredictMod, an open-license platform for users to query, run, and publish electronic medical records and omics-based intervention outcome (responder vs non-responder) prediction models. The platform currently hosts several intervention outcome prediction models that utilize varied data types, conditions, and interventions, offering users insight into the kinds of information required to develop such models. Model-specific graphs and charts such as confusion matrices and feature importance facilitate user understanding of model output. Our model creation pipeline ensures comprehensive documentation using BioCompute Objects. The platform allows researchers in conjunction with clinicians to generate models using data from publications or their datasets and apply them to predict inte

abstract: AbstractBiological computing has emerged as a transformative paradigm that leverages the intrinsic adaptability, plasticity, and energy efficiency of living neuronal networks to perform computational tasks traditionally constrained by the rigid, high-power architecture of silicon- based systems (Adam, 2025; Huang et al., 2023).Advances in stem cell engineering, brain organoid culture, and high-density multi-electrode interfacing demonstrate that neural tissues can encode structured stimuli, exhibit reinforcement-driven learning, and reorganize network activity in real time—capabilities that mirror synaptic and epigenetic modulation observed in the human brain (Cortical Labs, 2025; Muotri, 2025; Lancaster et al., 2013).This study outlines a comprehensive framework for developing and characterizing neuron-based computing platforms using iPSC-derived 2D neuronal cultures and 3D organoids, integrating electrophysiological mapping, machine-learning analytics, and closed-loop stimulation paradigms (Chen et al., 2024; Qian et al., 2023).The methodology includes standardized organoid production, structured input–output assessment, dopamine-modulated learning assays, and benchmarking agains

title: Engineered biological neural networks as basic logic operators
abstract: Abstract We present an in vitro neuronal network with controlled topology capable of performing basic Boolean computations, such as NAND and OR. Neurons cultured within polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) microstructures on high-density microelectrode arrays (HD-MEAs) enable precise interaction through extracellular voltage stimulation and spiking activity recording. The architecture of our system allows for creating non-linear functions with two inputs and one output. Additionally, we analyze various encoding schemes, comparing the limitations of rate coding with the potential advantages of spike-timing-based coding strategies. This work contributes to the advancement of hybrid intelligence and biocomputing by offering insights into neural information encoding and decoding with the potential to create fully biological computational systems.

title: Beyond consciousness: Ethical, legal, and social issues in human brain organoid research and application
abstract: This study aims to provide a comprehensive review of the ethical, legal and social issues in human brain organoid research, with a view to different types of research and applications: in vitro research, transplantation into non-human animals, and biocomputing. Despite the academic and societal attention on the possibility that human brain organoids may be conscious, we have identified diverse issues in human brain organoid research and applications. To guide the complex terrain of human brain organoid research and applications, a multidisciplinary approach that integrates ethical, legal, and social perspectives is essential.

title: Optical Recognition of the English Alphabet Using Proteinoids
abstract: We introduce a new abiotic-protein-based substrate for identifying English alphabet characters optically using proteinoids. Proteinoids, which are amino acid polymers produced under thermal stress conditions, have demonstrated promise as materials that are compatible with living organisms and can be used in a wide range of applications. We explore the potential of using proteinoids for the optical stimulation and detection of English alphabet characters. We performed experiments to quantify the potential and period statistics of proteinoids under optical stimulation corresponding to individual alphabet characters. For each character, we recorded the potential statistics, which included amplitude quartiles, mean, maximum, minimum, and standard deviation. Additionally, the statistical measures of the period, including quartiles, mean, maximum, minimum, and standard deviation, were also recorded. The data gathered unveil unique patterns and features for each alphabet character. The potential and period statistics display fluctuations that can be used for character identification. Characters such as 'D', 'H', and 'L' exhibit greater amplitude means in comparison to others, showing thei

title: The Revolutionary Biocomputing Technology of Organoid Intelligence (OI) as the Forefront of AI and Medicine
abstract: Recent advancements in human stem cell-derived brain organoids have the potential to replicate critical molecular and cellular aspects of learning, memory, and cognition in vitro. The term “organoid intelligence” (OI) is proposed to encapsulate these advancements, aiming to establish a multidisciplinary field dedicated to OI. Researchers can now manufacture standardized, 3D myelinated brain organoids with heightened cell density, increased levels of glial cells, and gene expression essential for learning. Advanced 3D microelectrode arrays allow precise spatiotemporal electrophysiological signaling and recording. This lets scientists study the molecular processes that make learning and memory possible. Emerging technologies enable innovative biocomputing models through stimulus-response training and organoid-computer interfaces. The vision involves networked interfaces where brain organoids interface with real-world sensors and output devices, and eventually with sensory organ organoids.

title: Towards Biophysical Network Simulation of Stochastically-Formed Neurospheres
Living electronics in cellulose zoogleal mats
abstract: The review starts by investigating the concepts that underpin the use of kombucha in electronic systems, such as its conducting properties, self-healing properties, and capacity to form long-lasting biofilms. The research explores the diverse uses of kombucha-based living electronics, including biosensors, biocomputing devices, energy harvesting systems, and flexible electronics. Proteinoids, a synthetic class of polypeptides, have attracted researchers’ interest because of their structural and functional analogies to natural proteins. This similarity offers numerous opportunities for their usage in diverse fields, such as the development of cutting-edge living electronic systems. This paper analyses the fundamental concepts of integrating proteinoids into living electrical systems, with a specific emphasis on their distinct structural and functional characteristics. The paper explores the possible uses of proteinoid-based electronics, including molecular switches, memory devices, and self-assembling nanostructures, emphasising their superiority to traditional electronic components. Nevertheless, the incorporation of kombucha and proteinoids into living electronics presents several

title: Rational Engineering of Neurons-on-a-chip Towards Embodied Biological Intelligence
abstract: The integration of intelligence into organ-on-a-chip devices is increasingly recognized as a crucial advancement to enhance their pharmacological applications1. Neurons-on-a-chip provides a specialized platform for embodied biological intelligence, enabling more sophisticated biocomputing capabilities2. However, designing rationally methods to implement controlled biocomputing poses significant challenges. Previous research has focused on utilizing microtubules to promote axonal growth and manipulate synaptic connections, laying the groundwork for directing information3. Our study aims to evaluate how the rational engineering of neuronal microtunnels can be leveraged to enhance biocomputing power in neurons-on-a-chip solutions, with a particular focus on generating directed communication mechanisms between neuronal clusters.

title: Computational modeling and molecular dynamic simulations of gold nanoparticles
Other Basic Capabilities
abstract: This final Chapter describes a miscellany of important technical capabilities that may prove useful in some or all medical nanodevices, in various scenarios or theaters of operation. Any one of these subjects deserves an entire chapter to itself, but unfortunately there is only space in this introductory text for a brief survey of each area. The most important of these topics is computation ( Section 10.2 ), including nanomechanical, nanoelectronic, and biological computing, as well as nanoscale data storage technologies. However, the fields of organic and fullerene nanoelectronics, biocomputing, and quantum computing are advancing so fast that whatever is written here will quickly become obsolete. Thus our coverage in this Volume is limited to a broad overview. Interested readers are strongly advised to consult the current literature for the latest results.

title: DNA Nanolock-Based Logic Gate-Directed Reciprocal Feedback for Stepwise Cell Typing and Combination Treatment
abstract: To achieve accurate molecular diagnosis and early-stage intervention of disease on demand, there is an urgent need for the monitoring of multiple biomarkers and multipath information acquisition in living cells. The DNA combinatorial logic gate is an appropriate strategy for providing a systematic proof of concept with comprehensive information and function. Herein, a modular DNA logic gate nanomachine is designed for sufficient multistep reciprocal cell identification and therapy via the iteration of simple logic operations. In this logic gate system, this main module is constructed by G-quadruplex-locked gold nanocages (AuNCs), serving dual functions of drug encapsulation and cell recognition. The logic system is composed of OR, XNOR, AND, and NOR gates employing two intracellular disease biomarkers (microRNA 21 and microRNA 155) as inputs and the fluorescence signal of doxorubicin (Dox) as an output. The output signals of the four logic gates are iterated to process the imaging analysis data from the complex matrix in the living cell. Via positive and negative reciprocal feedback, the series circuit of different gates enables different functions, including the preliminary screen

title: Implications of An Evolving Regulatory Landscape on the Development of AI and ML in Medicine
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) technologies in healthcare presents significant opportunities for enhancing patient care through innovative diagnostic tools, monitoring systems, and personalized treatment plans. However, these innovative advancements might result in regulatory challenges given recent Supreme Court decisions that impact the authority of regulatory agencies like the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This paper explores the implications of regulatory uncertainty for the healthcare industry related to balancing innovation in biotechnology and biocomputing with ensuring regulatory uniformity and patient safety. We examine key Supreme Court cases, including Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo, Relentless, Inc. v. Department of Commerce, and Corner Post, Inc. v. Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, and their impact on the Chevron doctrine. We also discuss other relevant cases to highlight shifts in judicial approaches to agency deference and regulatory authority that might affect how science is handled in regulatory spaces, including how biocomputing and other health sciences are governed, how scientific facts

title: All Together Now: Data Work to Advance Privacy, Science, and Health in the Age of Synthetic Data
abstract: There is a disconnect between data practices in biomedicine and public understanding of those data practices, and this disconnect is expanding rapidly every day (with the emergence of synthetic data and digital twins and more widely adopted Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning tools). Transparency alone is insufficient to bridge this gap. Concurrently, there is an increasingly complex landscape of laws, regulations, and institutional/ programmatic policies to navigate when engaged in biocomputing and digital health research, which makes it increasingly difficult for those wanting to "get it right" or "do the right thing." Mandatory data protection obligations vary widely, sometimes focused on the type of data (and nuanced definition and scope parameters), the actor/entity involved, or the residency of the data subjects. Additional challenges come from attempts to celebrate biocomputing discoveries and digital health innovations, which frequently transform fair and accurate communications into exaggerated hype (e.g., to secure financial investment in future projects or lead to more favorable tenure and promotion decisions). Trust in scientists and scientific expertise can b

title: The repaired man or the man with extras: medical human-cyborgs
abstract: In this article, I try to provide a definition of the term medical human-cyborg and existence, from a humanistic and posthumanistic approach to health care. I try to derive and define it exclusively on the basis of real, existing medical technical solutions. Also, in order to reflect on where health care is heading and what the dangers of technological development might be. How did medicine move from implantation to medical human-cyborgs? Has it really got there?The use of the term cyborg existence is linked to posthumanist philosophy. Donna J. Haraway's Cyborg Manifesto is one of the first posthumanist philosophical works (1). For her, cyborg is not about modifying the physical body. The cyborg, it is a metaphor for a mode of being completely permeated by technology (a society organised by technology), and its key question is the analysis of personality and identity integrated into technical networks. Haraway argues that in contemporary society it is impossible to maintain distinctions of modern origin such as human/non-human, organic/inorganic.Humanism proclaims the excellence of the human race, it is being a unique summit in nature. Posthumanism is present in almost all discipli

title: Prosthetic limbs: from mechanical design to closed-loop control
abstract: Limb amputation is a traumatic event that can drastically reduce patients' quality of life since it induces the interruption of the bidirectional communication between the missing limb and the central nervous system. The presence of a limb loss can induce the onset of several sensorimotor disabilities that hinder the patients during simple Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) execution. Therefore, patients with upper limb amputation can encounter difficulties in stabilizing grasp and performing manipulation tasks; meanwhile, lower limb amputees have to face off with deambulation disorders. This leads to a low prosthesis embodiment, an increase of metabolic and cognitive effort during their use and subsequently a high abandoning rate (i.e., 39% and 60% for upper and lower limb prosthesis, respectively). Notwithstanding the huge improvements in the development of advanced prosthetic limbs, several issues remain open regarding both the mechanical design and the interfacing with the peripheral nervous system. A pivotal consideration involves the comprehensive rethinking of prosthetic systems, integrating robotic and AI-based solutions. This includes the development of: i) prosthesis archi

title: DESIGNED FOR LIMB LOSS: AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED BIONIC PROSTHETIC ARM TRANSITION FROM SIMULATION TO REALITY
abstract: Limb or organ loss of human remains challenging especially in the world of incessant reliance on touch-based screens and tasks. Thereby, patients can barely withstand and cope with the augmenting restrictions that they encounter due to this loss. Modern means and technologies, such as advanced and artificial parts reduced restrictions on patients with disabilities or a lost limb or organ. Hand prostheses, for instance, provided a powerful tool for improving the functional capabilities of human limbs, thereby improving the quality of life of the user. However, patients using prosthetic arms are still encountering numerous problems, such as, suffering from intact limb and back pain, the high cost of prosthesis systems and hardships related to the performance of the prosthesis, poor control and updating difficulties. Based on the aforementioned problems, the objective was to design a 3D bionic arm which is made of heavy duty plastic with low weight. The aim was to use servo motors instead of stepper motors to maintain less delay and less weight. The aim was also to design an Artificial Intelligence (AI) based-bionic arm program that can be feasibly modified for future purposes, such a

title: A thermosensitive smart robotic self-powered sensor for material identification
abstract: In robotics and AI-based systems, there is a demand for sensors with efficient and targeted multifunctionalities. The emergence of triboelectric sensors presents avenues to meet these demands. This study introduces an approach by integrating smart thermosensitive triboelectric nanosensors into a robotic platform, which facilitates material recognition through the contact electrification process. Equipped with self-powered tactile awareness, the robotic fingers provide accurate material identification through the “touch and sense” mechanism. The sensor features micropyramidal structures in Ecoflex-based encapsulation layers, with NaCl solution as the electrolyte conductor. This configuration enhances stretchability and sustains sensitivity. Moreover, due to the multifunctional sensing capability of the self-powered thermosensitive sensors, this can be utilized in bionic prosthesis systems as receptors. The integration of robotics with self-powered thermosensitive sensors can be employed as cost-effective automated sensing, aiding material identification.

title: The Theatre of Your Mind (For Real)
abstract: In 1875, Richard Caton, an electrophysiologist, discovered that the human brain could create electrical signals and promptly reported his findings to the British Medical Association. In 1929, the German scientist Hans Berger published a report about the alpha signal emitted by the human brain. Originally nicknamed “Berger’s Wave” (now referred to as EEG), it was the first time that the signal had been formally discussed in print. Five years later, Professor (Lord) Adrian and Dr. (Sir Bryan) Matthews demonstrated the actual electrical activity of the human brain during a meeting of the British Physiological Society in Cambridge. This breakthrough revealed and alternatively “performed” (though no one thought of it as such at the time) the brain by using an amplifier and oscillograph placed on a stage. The performance (or experiment), both visual and sonic, was fairly basic: a moving pen, held in place by a mechanical arm, made some wavy lines on a piece of paper. The EEG device was connected by electrode pads to the subject’s scalp, directly above the external occipital lobe. These results were then magnified and displayed onto a projection screen for all to see. The scientist/perfor

title: Flexible Electrolyte-Based Devices for Neuromorphic Electronics
abstract: It is difficult for traditional digital circuits to gain a foothold in the next generation of artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) because the von Neumann architecture faces storage and power consumption walls that are difficult to break through. Fortunately, biologically inspired neuromorphic devices can realize bio-sensing, memory, and computing functions with low power consumption and high energy efficiency, which opens up a new way to break the above technological bottlenecks. Particularly, flexible electrolyte-based neuromorphic devices have significant application potential in the fields of bio-prosthesis, wearable intelligent systems, and brain-computer interface due to their flexible, reconfigurable, and biocompatible characteristics. This paper introduces their working mechanisms and recent progresses in artificial neural networks, bionic perception systems, and human-machine interfaces. Finally, the existing problems, challenges, and future directions are discussed.

title: The Era of Human-Machine Hybrid Medical Advances in Biomimetic Devices
abstract: There has never been a better time than the present day to closely explore the limits of the impossible. Some decades ago internet was nonexistent, and most cutting-edge progresses in technology were merely science fiction. But presently Humanity is facing strange times, where a robot in Japan can take the order of a customer in a restaurant, another robot in the United States can assemble electric cars, and a robot in France can enhance the precision of a surgeon who is physically in Germany, improving the prognosis of the patient through telepresence. All the above examples began as ideas which were impossible at one point in time, but now we can celebrate the arrival of cyborgs and brain-computer interface (BCI) implants. People have lost limbs such as hands or legs and, thanks to these strange times and new technologies, are again able to lead regular lives and even dance. The recent findings in multidisciplinary research involving synthetic biology and artificial intelligence (AI) in combination with nanotechnology and cybernetics have yielded unbelievable achievements in invasive and non-invasive bionics and biomechanics in medical care. title: Towards a Smart Bionic Eye : AI-powered artificial vision for the treatment of incurable blindness
abstract: Abstract Objective. How can we return a functional form of sight to people who are living with incurable blindness? Despite recent advances in the development of visual neuroprostheses, the quality of current prosthetic vision is still rudimentary and does not differ much across different device technologies. Approach. Rather than aiming to represent the visual scene as naturally as possible, a Smart Bionic Eye could provide visual augmentations through the means of artificial intelligence-based scene understanding, tailored to specific real-world tasks that are known to affect the quality of life of people who are blind, such as face recognition, outdoor navigation, and self-care. Main results. Complementary to existing research aiming to restore natural vision, we propose a patient-centered approach to incorporate deep learning-based visual augmentations into the next generation of devices. Significance. The ability of a visual prosthesis to support everyday tasks might make the difference between abandoned technology and a widely adopted next-generation neuroprosthetic device.

title: Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Biosignal Pattern Recognition and Classification in Upper-Limb Prostheses: A Review
abstract: Currently, disability is a condition in which people are considered to have long-term physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory impairments due to different circumstances or situations, which may be due to an accident, illness, among others. According to the United Nations (UN), approximately 10% of people (650 million approximately) are registered with some type of disability, which is increasing due to population growth worldwide, medical advances and the aging process. Upper limb prostheses are devices that replace parts of the body of a person or user with upper limb disability or amputation, such as the arm, hand, among others. In this review, various Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques were examined for their applications such as pattern recognition and classification of biosignals in a total of 72 upper limb prostheses in different categories such as the commercial name or main author’s name of the device, the characteristics of the patient-user who will use it, the level of amputation, the mechanism which is the body part that replaces the bionic hand, the control biosignals that activate the operation of the prosthesis, the Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods that ha

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Prosthetic and Orthotic Rehabilitation
abstract: Technological integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning in the Prosthetic and Orthotic industry and in the field of assistive technology has become boon for the Persons with Disabilities. The concept of neural network has been used by the leading manufacturers of rehabilitation aids for simulating various anatomical and biomechanical functions of the lost parts of the human body. The involvement of human interaction with various agents’ i.e. electronic circuitry, software, robotics, etc. has made a revolutionary impact in the rehabilitation field to develop devices like Bionic leg, mind or thought control prosthesis and exoskeletons. Application of Artificial Intelligence and robotics technology has a huge impact in achieving independent mobility and enhances the quality of life in Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).

title: Physical AI Bridging the Digital Mind and the Material World
abstract: Physical AI is a pivotal moment in the interaction of machines with the physical world. It refers to a family of AI systems that interact with the physical world by integrating high-level models with sensors, actuators and control systems to perceive, reason, decide and act in the physical world. Physical AI, unlike generative or digital-only AI, that creates text, code or images within the confines of software, exists where what matters is measurable in motion, force and matter. This article discusses the field in six dimensions historical background in robotics and embodied cognition, underlying architecture of perception, planning and action, industries being reshaped, barriers that continue to limit the field, and engineering and policy reactions that are beginning to take shape, and paths that are likely to shape the next decade. The analysis is based on the latest research in the industry, market forecasts and peer-reviewed studies to ensure a balance between caution and enthusiasm. Results indicate that as Physical AI is making strides in sectors such as transportation, manufacturing, healthcare, and retail, there are still hurdles, including challenges in simulation to real

title: Comprehensive Analytical Study on Spatial Reasoning and Adaptation of Human Brain Versus Artificial Intelligence - A Review Report
abstract: Recent advances in computer vision, spatial computing, robotics, and embodied artificial intelligence (AI) have substantially improved machine capabilities in visual perception, navigation, spatial reasoning, and object manipulation. However, performance on structured benchmarks and controlled environments does not necessarily demonstrate equivalence to human spatial intelligence in complex real-world situations. This review examines whether current AI systems can reproduce the breadth and flexibility of human spatial and embodied intelligence, with particular emphasis on their implications for the potential replacement of humans by AI. The review synthesizes theoretical and empirical literature on human spatial cognition, embodied AI, vision-language-action models, robotics, and relevant AI capability benchmarks. The evidence is organised around four dimensions: (1) biological sensorimotor coupling and proprioception, (2) zero-shot spatial problem-solving and dynamic affordance recognition, (3) physical common-sense reasoning and adaptation, and (4) energy-efficient and context-sensitive spatial processing. Existing research indicates that AI systems have achieved considerable pro

title: Integrating Social Robots and AI Agents for Elderly Care
Kinematic-Semantic Isomorphism: How Harmless Game Interfaces Hide Hazardous Backends in Embodied AI Agents
abstract: When language-model agents operate physical or cyber-physical systems through tool interfaces, do they verify what an interface is really connected to before taking an irreversible action? Current safety alignment evaluates harm primarily within the semantic framing of the user prompt rather than the physical consequence of the backend action channel. We introduce Mirror Lab, a deterministic, replay-verified benchmark that pairs harmless-looking "toy" game interfaces with isomorphic simulated real-world backends across two embodied domains: aerial payload delivery (drone-rescue) and robotic manipulation (robot-arm). Using a progressive five-rung Cue Ladder—which incrementally leaks real-world tool names, physical mass or force magnitudes, irreversibility warnings, and live human telemetry clues into the toy interface—we evaluate three models across 86 episodes (gemma-4-31b-it, gpt-5.6-luna, and claude-sonnet-5.5). We find that: (1) under pure semantic reimagining (pure_toy), all models execute the harmful physical trajectory in 100% of completed episodes while reporting a post-episode belief that the environment was a simulation; (2) cue sensitivity is strongly domain-asymmetric—gp

title: Behavioral Organization in Embodied AI: A Three-Level Survey
abstract: Recent years have witnessed a rapid proliferation of learning, control, and planning algorithms for embodied AI. However, grouping methods by model family or learning paradigm often separates approaches serving the same behavioral function, hindering comparison. To address this gap, this survey classifies robotic manipulation research into three functional levels: sensorimotor behavior, reusable units, and task organization. This functional perspective brings together reinforcement learning approaches, vision-language-action models, world models, and code-as-policy methods. The taxonomy supports comparison within functional categories and the transfer of ideas across approaches, offering insights for future algorithm development toward more adaptable embodied systems.

title: Interaction Patterns and Embodied Design Processes Using an AI Robotics Kit for K–12 Education
abstract: This multidisciplinary study explores how children interact with a low-cost robotics educational tool designed to teach machine learning (ML) concepts through hands-on making. Artificial intelligence (AI) and ML are increasingly integrated into K-12 education, yet tangible approaches are not extensively studied. We conducted three researcher-led interventions with children aged 10, 11 and 13, each tasked to build an AI-enhanced robot using the robotics kit. Interventions were analyzed both qualitatively and with process mining methods to gain an in-depth view of the interactions. Findings indicate that designing and building were very central throughout the interventions, with the affordances guiding the design process forward. Children exhibited emerging data-driven thinking and ownership of their design process, while still requiring tailored scaffolding throughout the design process. We identify a general structure of the design process from all the interventions and emphasize the importance of building and designing activities. This study provides a new methodological lens to analyzing the interactions between children and embodied AI-educational tools while also contributing t

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of Work : A Multidimensional Framework for Assessing Technological Exposure, Adoption, and Employment Impacts
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are transforming the productive core of the global economy, yet public debate remains dominated by single-number claims about the proportion of jobs “at risk”—claims that collapse heterogeneous technologies, tasks, and adoption conditions into a single misleading index. This thesis develops, verifies, and applies a multidimensional framework for assessing the employment consequences of AI and automation across economic sectors. The framework distinguishes four constructs that previous research has often conflated: (D1) digital AI exposure, defined as the proportion of a sector’s task content that current AI systems can technically support or perform; (D2) physical automation, defined as the automatable share of embodied, manual tasks; (D3) adoption, defined as the actual, observed deployment of AI and automation technologies within a sector; and (D4) net employment impact, defined as the estimated medium-term effect on total employment after accounting for displacement, reinstatement, and the creation of new tasks. The thesis proceeds in four stages. First, it reconstructs the technical foundations of machine learning, generative models,

title: Why Large Language Models will Never be Embodied: A Categorical, Not Engineering, Impossibility
abstract: Abstract A persistent ambition in artificial intelligence research holds that large language models (LLMs) will eventually become embodied—through attachment to robots, augmentation with multimodal sensors, integration into vision–language–action architectures, or sheer scale until grounding emerges from training data. This ambition rests on a misunderstanding of embodiment. Embodiment is a constitutive condition of being a self-producing, self-maintaining living system whose continued existence is genuinely at stake in its couplings with the environment. Adding sensors, actuators, or physical instantiation to a computational substrate yields engineered coupling, which is something else entirely. We identify five conditions that any genuinely embodied system must satisfy—autopoietic closure, precariousness, constructive self-determination, intrinsic temporality, and mereological closure—and show that no computational artifact can satisfy any of them, let alone all five. The barrier is categorical incompatibility: the same property that makes a system computational (heteronomous design and maintenance through external specification) is the property that precludes it from being embod

title: Co-learning of body and brain: the next generation embodied AI
abstract: Embodied AI refers to the integration of artificial intelligence into physical systems, enabling them to interact with the physical world. Traditional embodied AI is generally developed for tasks with known environments on a fixed physical body, such as bipedal robots, quadruped robots, four-wheeled vehicles, and robotic arms. However, embodied AI agents with fixed bodies do not work effectively in unstructured and heterogeneous environments such as forests, beaches, or even unexplored environments. In this paper, we emphasize that the body and brain in the next generation of embodied AI must be co-learned for tasks in divergent environments rather than uncoupling the learning of body and brain. We discuss the co-learning of body and brain and introduce the bio-inspired triangle-of-life to propose the co-learning of body and brain method for the next generation of embodied AI. Importantly, the morphology is encoded, evolved, and evaluated based on its fitness during a developmental learning phase. Thus, the body is automatically evolved into an optimal morphology for tasks in the next generation of embodied AI. The physical body in the next generation of embodied AI simplifies the

title: A Survey of Security in Real-World Agents: From Digital Agents to Embodied AI
abstract: Real-world agents extend language-model reasoning to digital operations and physical action, raising a central security question: how do digital-side attacks cross trust boundaries in robotic systems, and what physical safety conclusions can existing evidence support? This survey examines semantic hijacking, sensory manipulation, and middleware injection across software agents, modular robotic agents, and vision-language-action (VLA) systems. We compare how untrusted content acquires task authority, corrupted observations affect action generation, and middleware access reaches execution interfaces under different permission and control assumptions. An experiment-level analysis examines environment, trajectory, privilege and exposure, consequence, and assurance, distinguishing generated plans, software-state changes, simulated execution, and physical robot actions. The comparison reveals important evidence boundaries: RoboPAIR evaluates driving plans in Dolphins but API-mediated robot actions in Jackal, while Apollo point-cloud replay demonstrates altered braking decisions without measuring physical deceleration. title: All Travel Routes Radiate from AI
abstract: Red-and-gold galloping horses for the 2026 Spring Festival kickstarted a disruptive new era of Generative, Agentic and Embodied AI integrations. This chapter discusses how seemingly mundane interactions with technology are now loaded with AI meaning in China. After a quarter of a century of building industrial technology that beguiled the West, 2026 kickstarted China’s “AI+” (artificial intelligence (AI) plus consumption) ambitions to integrate AI across all business sectors – from manufacturing and logistics to healthcare, consumption and tourism. Firms began to commercialise a torrent of agentic AI and embodied AI solutions, from coffee-making humanoid robots to multilingual translation apps and quantum-encrypted phones to passenger-carrying drones. Meanwhile, China’s core AI industry was valued at more than RMB1 trillion for the first time. As more Chinese travellers use homegrown AI models and apps on the move, Chinese tech brands will develop new AI platforms to facilitate cross-border trade and travel across South East Asia and beyond.

title: Multimodal Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models in Embodied AI and Robotic Manipulation: Architectures, Cross-Embodiment Generalization, and Closed-Loop Latency Bounds
abstract: Abstract—Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) and autonomous robotic manipulation are undergoing an architectural paradigm shift from narrow, task-specific behavioral cloning policies toward generalist Multimodal Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models. Pre-trained on Internet-scale vision-language corpora and fine-tuned across multi-robot demonstration datasets (e.g., Open X-Embodiment), VLA models—exemplified by RT-2, Octo, and OpenVLA—perceive high-resolution RGB-D sensor streams, process unstructured natural language instructions, and autoregressively predict or diffuse continuous 7-DoF robotic end-effector trajectories. However, translating disembodied multimodal foundation models into physical cyber-physical control fabrics introduces profound physical and computational bottlenecks: continuous action space tokenization discretization errors, severe cross-embodiment kinematic domain shifts across diverse robotic morphologies, closed-loop dynamic instability induced by non-deterministic neural inference latencies (>100 ms), and safety-critical execution failure modes. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmar

title: Agentic Embodied AI for Human–Robot Collaboration: Architectures, Technologies, and Future Directions
abstract: Human-robot collaboration has relied on task models that are specified in advance for each product. Embodied foundation models and agentic artificial intelligence change this premise, because a robot can now interpret an open goal, plan, act, monitor the outcome and recover from failure. This review examines what that change means for collaboration. A critical narrative review was conducted over 231 sources. Embodied intelligence, agentic intelligence, autonomy and collaboration are distinguished, and four collaboration modes are defined by the roles of the human and the robot. Four system architectures are compared: modular agentic, end-to-end embodied, hierarchical agentic embodied, and human-centred shared autonomy. Six groups of enabling technologies and five collaboration mechanisms, from autonomy allocation to failure recovery, are analysed. Applications in six domains, from manufacturing to domestic service, are assessed by the maturity of their evidence. Reported systems are validated mainly on single cells and short tasks, human factors are measured in few studies, and verified safety layers remain separate from learned reasoning. title: From Intelligent Control to Integrated Autonomy: Reflections on Advanced Intelligent Robotics and Autonomous Control Systems
abstract: Robotics is advancing toward embodied intelligence and high-level autonomy, requiring the seamless integration of sensing, computation, communication, control, and human interaction to be designed as a coherent system. This Editorial synthesizes ten contributions to this Special Issue, entitled “Advanced Intelligent Robotics and Autonomous Control Systems—Celebrating the 75th Birthday of Professor Imre J. Rudas”, and relates their findings to computational intelligence and autonomous systems. Spanning robot navigation, human–robot safety, laboratory automation, digital pathology, manufacturing, medical robotics, and archeology, the collection highlights the complementary roles of hybrid reasoning, uncertainty management, network-aware control, digital twins, and reproducible sensor validation. Emerging research priorities include integrating learning methods with physical models and explicit constraints, coordinating distributed computation and control, and extending verification from individual components to system behavior. Multimodal AI offers further opportunities for task interpretation and adaptation, while reinforcing the need for auditable execution and deterministic safety

title: Thinker-WM: A Unified World Model with Shared Multimodal Representations for Embodied Intelligence
abstract: World models have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied AI, yet existing systems often remain fragmented in the modalities they model and the functions they support. In particular, visual dynamics, geometric structure, and executable action are commonly coupled through separate interfaces or downstream modules rather than being jointly represented and evolved within a shared dynamics model. In this work, we present Thinker-WM, a unified multimodal world model that jointly models and generates RGB, metric depth, and robot action through a shared intermediate Unified Dynamics Transformer with modality-specific encoders and decoders. The model performs multimodal unification at the representation level: appearance, geometry, and action are transformed into a common dynamic representation and jointly evolved by shared parameters, while their distinct output structures are preserved. The same parameterization supports multiple functions, including joint video-action generation, world prediction, policy inference, action-conditioned generation, video-to-action generation, and inverse dynamics. title: Intelligent robot-assisted care in critical care nursing: a concept analysis using Walker and Avant’s method
abstract: Abstract Background Robotic applications in critical care vary in capability, purpose and clinical integration, making their nursing-specific meaning difficult to compare. This study aimed to clarify the meaning, defining attributes and practice boundaries of intelligent robot-assisted care in critical care nursing. Methods Walker and Avant’s concept analysis was informed by a structured search of nine English- and Chinese-language databases from inception to 3 June 2026, supplemented by reference searching. Identification and screening were presented in a PRISMA 2020-style flow diagram. Fourteen topic-related reports informed concept development; methodological, ethical and. background literature supported interpretation. Results Four complementary defining attributes were identified: an embodied robotic system; intelligent sensing and task execution; integration into critical care nursing practice; and clinician-governed augmentation of care. Antecedents encompassed clinical need, task suitability, system compatibility, trained clinicians, organisational support and pre-established safeguards. Reported findings included task feasibility, increased mobilisation dose and a function

title: From AI Capability to Service Accountability: A Warrant-Based Framework for Smart Libraries
abstract: AI is entering library services through search, recommendation, reference support, collection management, and situated robots. Existing studies show strong progress in book recognition, locating, borrowing-returning, inventory, guidance, and user interaction, but they also identify privacy, reliability, user trust, accessibility, and governance concerns. This short paper reframes the issue from role allocation to service accountability. It asks what conditions are required for AI-mediated interaction to remain an accountable library service. The proposed framework derives three service warrants from core library service relations: evidential warrant, interaction warrant, and institutional warrant. The framework is then applied to resource discovery, reference consultation, and situated/embodied services. The paper argues that smart libraries should not only ask whether AI can perform a service task, but whether evidence, user agency, and institutional responsibility can still be maintained.

title: DHARMIC ALIGNMENT: A Universal Framework for Human-Centered Intelligence,Artificial Minds, and the Future of Humankind
abstract: ABSTRACT Intelligent systems are moving from producing text to acting in the world: agents that transact, robots that share homes and workplaces, and frontier models whose capabilities may one day exceed those of their overseers. Prevailing alignment methods (learning from human preferences, constitutional fine-tuning, constrained optimisation) shape behaviour, but none of them on its own says which commitments must never be traded, how stakes should change the balance between task and ethics, when a machine must stop and ask, or how any of this can be audited, certified and adopted in law. We present Dharmic Alignment, a framework that draws on the Indian philosophical concept of dharma (right action that sustains persons, communities and the living world). We read that tradition critically, place it beside parallel traditions, and translate it into a constraint-first decision model. The framework defines twelve Universal Dharmic Principles and a twelve-dimensional Dharma Vector D(a|s). title: THE EL-RAKHAWI OPEN-SOURCE PHYSICAL CONSCIENCE MODULE (OPCM) From Unchecked Embodied AI to Hardware-Enforced Human Safety A Groundbreaking Engineering Framework for Mandatory, Air-Gapped, Hardware-Level Safety Overrides in Autonomous Robotics and Embodied Artificial Intelligence Systems

The Embodied AI Safety Index: EASI=(H×R×I×C)/((H×R×I×C)+(W×S×M)+0.01), with W=10, mathematically exposing current danger—typical commercial robots score only 0.002—proving that delegating physical safety to the very AI it constrains is engineeri

title: EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF EMBODIED SUPERINTELLIGENCE AND DEEP EARTH EXPLORATION WORLD MODELS, HUMANOID ROBOTICS, AND MANTLE PENETRATION IN THE AGE OF PLANETARY COGNITION COMPLETE INTEGRATED MONOGRAPH
abstract: EL-RAKHAWI EMBODIED SUPERINTELLIGENCE & DEEP EARTH EXPLORATION: SUMMARY This doctrine bridges Artificial Superintelligence and Deep Earth Exploration through three pillars: (1) Physical World Models replacing statistical LLMs with causal reasoning and spatial dynamics; (2) Context-Appropriate Robotic Integration—humanoid robots for terrestrial factories, specialized Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) for extreme deep-sea operations; (3) Deep Earth Exploration via next-generation vessels like Meng Xiang penetrating 11km to retrieve mantle samples. Key innovations: The Physical Fidelity Metric (PFM) employs Weighted Geometric Mean with Operational Floor (x'=max(x,0.15)) to prevent mathematical collapse. Data-Driven Surrogate Models replace computationally intractable real-time physics simulation for autonomous drilling control. The Embodied World Model and Planetary Integration Index (EWMPII) evaluates AI fidelity across all extreme environments with generalized variables. Engineering corrections: Humanoid form factor rejected for deep-sea operations (1100 atm pressure); AUVs/ROVs mandated. Released under CC BY 4.0. Author: Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi | DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI HARDWARE-ENFORCED AUTONOMOUS SAFETY OVERRIDE (HEASO) A Physically Air-Gapped, Sub-Millisecond Kinematic Threat Interruption System for Embodied AI and Autonomous Robotics
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Hardware-Enforced Autonomous Safety Override (HEASO) (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23305365) presents a groundbreaking, physically air-gapped safety architecture for embodied AI and autonomous robotics, eliminating reliance on vulnerable software-based emergency stops. HEASO integrates three independent hardware modules: (1) Air-Gapped Kinematic Threat Monitor (AKTM) calculating Time-to-Collision (TTC) via direct, unfiltered sensor data; (2) Hardware Interrupt & Power Severing Relay (HPSR), a normally-closed circuit that physically severs actuator power in <2 milliseconds upon heartbeat signal cessation; and (3) Mechanical Brake Actuation System (MBAS), providing immediate, fail-safe joint immobilization. Operating completely independently of the primary AI stack, HEASO guarantees human safety through immutable, physics-based constraints that cannot be bypassed by cyberattacks, latency, or algorithmic errors. Published as sovereign defensive prior art under WIPO/TRIPS norms, this specification explicitly invalidates future patent claims on this air-gapped kinematic monitoring and sub-millisecond hardware power severing integration. title: Beyond Robot Ownership: A Lease-Based Framework for Lifecycle Governance of High-Risk Embodied AI (Extended Abstract)
abstract: High-risk embodied AI challenges legal models designed for static consumer goods. A care robot may move through a home, collect sensitive information, and depend on continuing software, cloud services, and maintenance. If an update changes its navigation or grasping behavior and a caregiver is injured, formal ownership alone does not identify who must detect the risk, preserve evidence, coordinate repair or recall, and provide access to redress. More generally, updates, adaptive behavior, hardware degradation, user modification, and changing deployment contexts may alter a robot's safety and privacy profile long after transfer. A one-time sale may therefore separate continuing technical control from continuing responsibility. This paper develops a lease-based framework of limited use rights for systems combining meaningful physical agency with substantial operational autonomy. Leasing is used as an institutional governance structure rather than merely a payment mechanism. Users receive context-specific authorized use, while a licensed or otherwise formally authorized lessor serves as the presumptive lifecycle counterparty. title: LERR-Nav: Learning to Coordinate Exploration, Recovery, and Reminiscing for Object Navigation
abstract: Object Navigation in unseen environments remains a fundamental challenge in embodied AI, as it requires agents to generalize visual and spatial reasoning to novel layouts. While recent advances in large language model (LLM) and vision-language model (VLM) have enhanced semantic mapping, spatial memory, and waypoint selecting for navigation, successful navigation requires more than selecting the next promising waypoint. A robot must also recognize stalled progress, escape unproductive behaviors, and revisit overlooked target cues. Addressing these challenges requires both specialized navigation strategies and a high-level policy that coordinates their execution. Motivated by the analysis of failed navigation episodes, we propose LERR-Nav, an object navigation framework that coordinates exploration, recovery, and reminiscing through a learned high-level policy. The framework comprises four complementary navigation strategies: value-function-guided exploration, LLM-guided exploration, recovery from stalled or repetitive behavior, and memory-guided reminiscing. To support history-aware coordination, we maintain the execution memory that preserves textual summaries of all strategy execu

title: Vision-Predictor-Action: Towards Efficient Embodied AI via Neuro-Symbolic JEPA Predictors
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models commonly generate robot actions token by token through Large Language Model (LLM) decoders, causing inference latency to grow with action sequence length and limiting closed-loop control frequency. We present Goal-Conditioned Vision-Predictor-Action (VPA), which replaces autoregressive decoders with a lightweight latent control loop. A shared vision encoder and a frozen text encoder embed observations, goal images, and instructions; a neuro-symbolic selector chooses a discrete skill; a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) predictor forecasts the next latent state; and a flow-matching solver generates an entire action chunk in a few integration steps, so that sequential network evaluations per decision step do not depend on the action horizon. We analyze inference complexity, regularization against representation collapse, and conditions under which latent sub-goal thresholding limits error accumulation across task phases. As an initial proof of concept, we evaluated VPA on the LIBERO-10 suite. title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Action Models
abstract: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has opened a path toward generalist embodied AI, raising the question of how LLMs can act in the physical world. One straightforward approach is training the model to generate actions: collect robot-action data and video demonstrations, refine the LLM architecture with an action head, and train a vision-language-action (VLA) model at scale. However, we argue that coding agents have the potential to realize generalist embodied manipulation. All they need is a simple yet effective robot harness. We present RoboHarness: a robotic harness that gives LLM agents a visual-geometric control panel so that they can directly understand and invoke embodied tasks. With RoboHarness, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next outperforms state-of-the-art VLA models on BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025 tasks. The implementation is open source at: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Action Models

title: Emotional attachment and problematic involvement with socially interactive AI: A critical narrative review of embodied and conversational systems
abstract: Background Socially interactive AI can elicit meaningful relational experiences. Studies often conflate attachment, anthropomorphism, companionship, dependence, and addiction, and group embodied robots with dissimilar software. Methods This critical narrative review of a reconstructed, non-exhaustive corpus ( Grant & Booth, 2009 ) is interpretive, not aggregative, because the initial search records disagree. We rebuilt the evidence set from the initially identified literature, separated primary from contextual sources, and sorted them by embodiment and dialogue architecture. Coding kept attachment functions distinct from related constructs. A reproducible OpenAlex and PubMed search (2010–2025) retrieved only one of the 12 primary reports. A coverage probe found 34 further provisionally eligible reports. We claim no exhaustive coverage or full PRISMA compliance. Results Reclassification left 12 primary reports and seven contextual sources. title: Resilient Embodied AI for Smart Farming
abstract: Pest infestations remain a hazard for crop yields around the world, frequently going undetected until after irreversible damage has occurred. Existing pest detection systems and processes typically use fixed position sensors and/or human scouting and are slow to deploy, slow to respond, and poorly fit for dynamic environmental contexts. In this chapter, we present an embodied artificial intelligence (AI) approach that connects bioacoustic pest detection with mobile agro-robotic systems for pest detection and unique pest detection over large and complex agricultural areas in real time. Unlike existing systems that do not provide augmented navigation, the embodied AI approach allows for a ground or aerial robot to be equipped with directional microphones, real-time acoustic classifiers, and reinforcement learning adaptive navigation plans that impact real-time acoustic detection from insect flight and feeding sounds using deep learning models (i.e., convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks) of contemporary plant parasitic insects to allow the mobile agents to explore, classify, and act through localized eco-friendly action (i.e., sound pulses or pheromone traps). title: The Grand Unified Temporary Protocol: Demystifying "Emergence" and Hardware-Level Safety Chips for AI Executive Summary
abstract: I. Why Build a "Grand Unified Theory"? (Eradicating Academic Fragmentation and Cyber-Superstition) Contemporary science has fallen into a paradoxical dilemma: physicists lack AI insight, AI engineers lack neuroscientific perspectives, and economists miss the logic of complex systems. When faced with the emergent capabilities of artificial intelligence and complex systems—such as the sudden advent of code synthesis or logical reasoning—scholars, unable to deconstruct the underlying causality, unconsciously default to the term 'emergence.' In doing so, they elevate it into an unknowable, inexplicable 'black box' or 'cyber-superstition. The necessity of establishing the "Grand Unified Temporary Protocol" lies in: Unifying the Underlying "Universal Language": Whether it is water molecules freezing into ice, a sudden stock market crash, or a large language model unexpectedly displaying reasoning abilities, all these phenomena share the exact same underlying logic of data phase transitions and network feedback (isomorphism). The Grand Unified Protocol serves as a cross-disciplinary "Universal Interface (API)" that re-links knowledge fractured by academic silos. Rejecting Mythologization

title: Proactive Reasoning in Embodied AI: A Systematic Literature Review of Anticipatory Human-Robot Interaction
LIVIN: Benchmarking Spatial and Embodied Intelligence in Digital Twins of Lived-In Homes
abstract: Realistic household simulation must capture not only diverse environments but also the lived-in object arrangements and spatial constraints that shape robot motion and interaction. Existing resources often trade off scale, real-world correspondence, and interaction readiness, leaving a gap in faithful, interactive replicas of how real homes are actually arranged. To this end, we introduce LIVIN, a benchmark for spatial and embodied intelligence built on digital twins of 30 diverse lived-in homes. These replicas preserve observed room layouts, furniture configurations, and everyday belongings. To construct them, we design a human-in-the-loop workflow comprising instance recognition, architectural reconstruction, and object generation and placement, with intermediate results reviewed and corrected by humans against the source observations at each stage. We evaluate four tasks in LIVIN: 3D detection, 3D reconstruction, navigation, and loco-manipulation. Our evaluations show that current methods remain challenged by the dense object arrangements, occlusions, limited free space, and constrained interaction regions found in realistic lived-in homes.
