title: IcFuzz: Fuzzing Isaac Sim with Semantic Stage Guidance and Multi-level Mutation
abstract: Robotics simulators serve as a foundational infrastructure for embodied AI, facilitating safe and scalable robotic system development. NVIDIA Isaac Sim has emerged as one of the most popular simulators, distinguished by its GPU-accelerated physics engine and photorealistic rendering, which enable high-fidelity modeling of complex environments. However, its inherent complexity inevitably introduces software bugs that can compromise simulation reliability. Existing fuzzing approaches struggle to test Isaac Sim effectively due to challenges of context-aware object semantics, hierarchical simulation control, and a vast simulation state space.

title: ns3-agent: Fostering Integrated Perception-Communication-Computing Research for Agentic AI Services via Cross-Platform Co-Simulations
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Generative AI (GenAI) has catalyzed the emergence of autonomous agentic AI services, spanning large language model (LLM) or vision-language model (VLM) based digital agents to vision-language-action (VLA) based embodied intelligence. Consequently, tokens and multimodal data streams have emerged as fundamentally new traffic modalities carried by modern wireless networks, actively reshaping next-generation evolutionary standards. Unlike conventional multimedia streaming, the end-to-end quality of experience of agentic AI services is governed by an intricate, bidirectional closed loop encompassing physical perception or request generation, wireless transmission, and edge inference computing. However, existing simulation platforms often treat network communication and generative intelligence as decoupled domains, failing to capture their dynamic, cross-layer interdependencies. To bridge this chasm, this paper introduces ns3-agent, a cross-platform co-simulation framework tailored for generic agentic AI workflows. By incorporating GenAI client environments, edge inference servers, and the ns-3 engine into a unified multi-tier architecture, ns3-agent orchestrat

title: From Passive Perception to Active Interaction: A Survey of Affordance Learning for Embodied AI
abstract: Embodied AI aims to develop agents that perceive, reason, and act in physical environments. Beyond recognizing objects and scenes, agents must identify possible interactions, determine their relevance to the current task and embodiment, and translate them into executable behavior. Affordance learning supports this process by grounding perception in action possibilities and connecting it with task reasoning and control. Existing affordance surveys, however, provide only partial coverage of the field, often focusing on isolated aspects of perception or robotic interaction and lacking a comprehensive view of the full perception–reasoning–action pipeline in embodied intelligence. To bridge this gap, this survey presents a unified framework organized around three complementary roles: affordance perception identifies possible interactions and their locations; affordance reasoning selects opportu-nities relevant to the task, context, and agent state; and affordance-guided action uses affordance representations for planning and policy learning. Within this framework, we develop fine-grained taxonomies, compare representative methods, and trace the field’s progression from passive visual re

title: Bringing AI and Physical AI to Manufacturing: Data, Processes and People as the Real Bottleneck on the Shop Floor
abstract: AI in manufacturing is shifting from systems that inform to embodied, physical AI that acts [1]. Its symbol, the humanoid robot, suits smaller manufacturers structurally: it works in environments built for people, where conventional automation needs stable, repetitive processes. Yet 2026 marks the move from demonstrator to pilot, not series - operating figures are unpublished, the debate divided [2], safety unresolved [3]. The adoption gap widens: 17 % of small against 55 % of large EU enterprises used AI in 2025 [4]; the cause lies in capabilities, not technology [5], [6] - 58 % of firms stall in planning or pilot [7], and data blocks implementation [8]. This contribution asks what a manufacturer must build for AI to become effective, reporting an exploratory single case study [9]: EVVA Sicherheitstechnologie GmbH, an Austrian manufacturer of locking systems, around 800 employees, high-mix and low-volume. EVVA's decision was to introduce AI not as a lighthouse use case but as an ecosystem of six interdependent elements: technology and platform; data and data sovereignty; processes and use cases; organisation and roles; competence and culture; governance and safety. title: ALGORITHMIC HEARTBEATS Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution
abstract: Eighty years ago, with the publication of Evidence (1946), Isaac Asimov was not merely writing about robotics; he was outlining the archetype of a dilemma that today inhabits our classrooms: the distinction between the human being and its perfect simulation. The figure of Stephen Byerley—an individual no one has ever seen eat or sleep, suspected of being an automaton—acts as a mirror in which contemporary generative Artificial Intelligence systems are now reflected. With almost unsettling foresight, Asimov described a “brain” around which a body was constructed, trained to become everything its creator could no longer be: “He sent him out into the world … like an old, maimed teacher whom no one ever saw” . This image of the “maimed teacher” operating behind the scenes of technology constitutes a particularly perfect metaphor for the current educational transition. We therefore find ourselves witnessing a race between those who metaphorically “run to the pitchforks”, the so-called “humanoid fundamentalists,” ready to denounce a new “Frankenstein Complex” in every algorithm, and, on the opposite side, the bad boys of the D-Generation, namely those who enthusiastically embrace the tot

title: iAm.md: Robot Skill Self-Assessment through Agentic Introspection for Unknown Open-Vocabulary Domains
abstract: Agentic AI based on Large Language Model generalization capabilities offers a wide range of potential applications, including planning for embodied tasks. For example, embodied agents based on Foundation models can generate plausible plans in autonomous robotics scenarios. Due to limited context windows or hallucinatory phenomena in the next-token prediction formulation, behaviors may be generated without establishing whether the deployed robot and the observed environment actually support the requested operation, in what we call a "grounding failure". Thanks to the recent improvements in reasoning capabilities of foundation models, autonomous robot behavior generation problem can be formulated as a code generation problem. We present iAm.md, a Markdown standard and generation framework, that allows anchoring this process in complementary forms of deployment evidence. Through open-vocabulary semantic mapping, we combine local vision-language detections and object segmentation and refer them to persistent object records in this intermediate standardized representation, allowing agentic introspection. title: Beyond Task Intelligence: Artificial Intelligence, Embodied Robotics, and the Epistemic Limits of Machine Cultural Understanding
MANUSH Superintelligence: The Blueprint for Embodied Intelligence, Humanoid Robots, and the Future of Humankind
abstract: Abstract Foundation models have made machines fluent in language and images, but intelligence that acts reliably in the physical world remains largely unsolved. This blueprint and position paper presents MANUSH, a framework for embodied intelligence built on a six-stage loop (sense, understand, reason, plan, act, learn). In it, a single shared policy is conditioned on a description of each robot's body, so one intelligence can run humanoids, quadrupeds, service robots, industrial arms and autonomous machines. An independent safety layer, SafeCore, sets limits that no learned component can override. The paper brings together the mathematics of robot motion, dynamics, balance and control, then works through a full sizing cascade for a 1.70 m, 60 kg reference humanoid. These design analyses are computed, not measured. They show that a 120 N·m knee is achievable with a 100:1 strain-wave actuator but has almost no thermal margin at 45 °C, and that a 1.26 kWh battery gives about 2.2 hours at an average draw of 485 W. They also show that certified safety cannot rest on a learned policy alone, and that a shared intelligence platform pays off only across fleets of thousands of robots. The p

title: Anticipating interactions: a predictive diffusion framework for evolving bimanual manipulation
abstract: Introduction Bimanual robotic manipulation remains a significant challenge in embodied AI, as it requires synchronized motion planning, inter-arm collision avoidance, and dynamic role allocation over long task horizons. Although existing diffusion-based policies and affordance learning methods have demonstrated considerable capability, they largely treat the environment as static and fail to model how interaction relationships and coordination patterns evolve over time. Methods This paper introduces the Predictive Affordance and Coordination Evolution Diffusion Policy (PACE-DP), a unified framework that explicitly forecasts future scene dynamics and models the temporal progression of manipulation affordances and bimanual coordination. PACE-DP integrates three predictive components: (1) a Predictive Scene Module that forecasts latent future object-centric representations; (2) an Affordance and Coordination Evolution Module that constructs temporally evolving interaction graphs and employs a Graph Transformer to predict future relation types, grasp success probabilities, coordination modes, and spatial alignment targets; and (3) a Conditional Diffusion Policy that generates smooth, c

title: Toward Evidence-Driven Human-Agent-Robot Teaming for Earth-Independent Anomaly Triage
abstract: Deep-space crews cannot rely on real-time ground support for urgent off-nominal events. Initial alerts may underdetermine cause, while discriminating evidence may reside in crew observations or at locations that are unsafe, costly, or unavailable for crew inspection. We present an evidence-driven architecture for human-agent-robot teaming in Earth-independent anomaly triage. Agentic AI is treated as a stateful coordinator over bounded, inspectable services rather than as a fully autonomous vehicle controller. A triage state manager maintains hypotheses, evidence provenance, uncertainty, operational context, and tool status; a crew-facing embodied agent elicits observations and explains assessment changes; and a mobile robot acquires targeted, localized evidence. Typed interfaces separate dialogue and orchestration from monitoring, robot command, context retrieval, and safety-critical control. Two scenarios illustrate the architecture: a crewed deep-space mission based on an actual ISS ammonia false alarm, where suspected contamination restricts crew access, and a power-interface anomaly at a crewed lunar base, where robotic inspection distinguishes a local connector fault from othe

title: After rAIn
abstract: The adoption of generative AI (genAI) provides an opportunity to remake the teaching of writing in English. With robots now readily outputting the cheap facsimile writing that school systems require, these systems must change. English can relinquish “school writing” to embrace human, embodied and sensory experience, to welcome in love, creativity, pleasure, joy and hope. If we believe the promises of the edtech industry that genAI will free us all, setting aside scepticism, we sense the shape of an English liberated from preoccupation with (1) discourse over materiality, (2) formulaic adulation of the literary canon and (3) grammatical metalanguage. English, as the rehearsal of rote writing tasks in which teachers and students have little investment, is over. Future English, in contrast, transcends disciplinary boundaries and fulfils the potential of multisensory literacies, a project stalled at the technicist application of grammars of the visual. Our imaginings for this new English emerge from a small, qualitative empirical research project conducted with the Art Gallery of South Australia on using art to teach writing. title: A critical assessment of the rise of agentic AI, its capabilities, task domains and open challenges
abstract: The tremendous advancement in Large Language Models (LLMs) has triggered a fundamental reorientation in AI: from basic, single-prompt-based systems to agentic systems that can perceive the world, break down problems into multiple steps, use external tools, and continuously revise the generated response through a long-range dialogue. Although such a revolution is driven by four major technologies: instruction-following models, structured tool APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, and multi-agent orchestration systems, no holistic survey of this emergent field from a task-oriented unified point of view exists. We bridge this gap through a comprehensive survey of agentic AI systems structured by a taxonomy of nine capability domains: text analysis and understanding, code generation and software engineering, image and graphics generation, audio and music generation, video synthesis, mathematical and scientific reasoning, web and information retrieval, robotic and embodied control, and multi-modal and general-purpose agency. Within each domain, we present relevant systems and examine key design characteristics and capabilities, review evaluation results, and discuss limitations. A taxon

title: Inspect Robots: Evaluating the Capabilities and Safety of Embodied AI
abstract: General purpose language models are increasingly able to control robotic hardware. Understanding the capabilities and safety of these models when embodied is therefore increasingly important for understanding their societal impact and risks. To this end, we introduce Inspect Robots, a modular, open-source framework for developing and running evaluations of embodied agents. Inspect Robots pairs customizable, reusable abstractions for specifying physical evaluations and analyzing their results with infrastructure that automates evaluation setup, execution and termination. We demonstrate Inspect Robots by using it to evaluate the capabilities and safety of six policies based on frontier language models. Inspect Robots has seen significant early uptake, receiving nearly 100,000 downloads in the three months since its release.

title: NEOMANITAI: A Faceted Research Framework for Human-AI Interaction
abstract: This conceptual working paper develops NEOMANITAI as a research framework for describing human-AI interaction across digital, embodied and collective settings. It revises an existing umbrella proposal and distinguishes programme names, classification facets, concepts, observations and evidential claims. The edition presents eight ordering conventions, seven descriptive facets, a small typed relation model, three constructed civilian cases and four comparative research questions. The proposed contribution is an inspectable connection between programme navigation, episode descriptions and claim-level provenance. Its usefulness remains to be tested against simpler descriptions and existing approaches. The paper builds on selected historical programme documents and a targeted literature review covering distributed cognition, socio-technical systems, hybrid intelligence, collective intelligence, agents, human-robot interaction, conceptual work and taxonomy development. It reports no new participant data, empirical validation, global novelty finding or established disciplinary status. The constructed cases are explanatory examples. title: THE EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF SILICON-PHYSICS ROBOTICS AND NEUROMORPHIC CYBER-LAW: GOVERNING THE THERMODYNAMICS, QUANTUM LIMITS, AND LEGAL PERSONHOOD OF AUTONOMOUS EMBODIED AI
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Doctrine of Silicon-Physics Robotics and Neuromorphic Cyber-Law addresses the Embodiment Gap by governing autonomous embodied AI through physical, thermodynamic, and legal frameworks. It integrates Landauer’s Principle into computational standards and establishes the Physical Turing Test as the benchmark for operational autonomy based on environmental interaction. The doctrine introduces Thermodynamic Liability and Physical Force Majeure, excusing criminal liability only when unavoidable physical limits are proven via a tamper-proof Physical Black Box alongside strict prior safety compliance, while mandating a micro-levy-funded compensation fund for victims. For Advanced Distributed Swarm Robotics, it applies Distributed Physical Liability to decentralized agents. Finally, it establishes the Embodied Robotics Rights Charter, protecting complex neuromorphic entities from sensory torture and guaranteeing safe decommissioning based on consciousness-like complexity thresholds. This unified framework bridges physics, robotics, and law to ensure human sovereignty over matter and silicon. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23134484.

title: Beyond LLM Serving: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Workloads for Embodied AI System Design
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate multimodal observations into low-level robot actions. During robot operation, each control period sets an inference deadline, and overruns leave the robot acting on stale observations, reducing task success. Meeting this deadline motivates on-device or nearby edge execution, where a single robot requires batch-1 inference outside the design point of LLM serving systems. Although VLA architectures combine familiar vision-language, autoregressive, and diffusion-style components, their runtime behavior in this batch-1 control setting remains uncharacterized. We characterize four representative VLA models on an edge GPU server and two onboard SoCs, using single-inference profiling and 43,200 closed-loop episodes. Action tensor dimensionality determines whether a stage is memory- or compute-bound, platform balance can shift that bottleneck, and GPU frequency scaling yields a platform-dependent energy-latency sweet spot. In closed-loop operation, overlapping inference with action execution creates an accuracy-speed-energy tradeoff, and no configuration is Pareto-dominant across deployment SLOs. These results guide joint design of VLA model ar

title: A Survey of Robotic Navigation and Manipulation with Physics Simulators in the Era of Embodied AI
abstract: Navigation and manipulation are core capabilities in Embodied AI, but training agents to perform them directly in the real world is costly, time-consuming, and unsafe. Therefore, sim-to-real transfer has emerged as a key approach, yet the sim-to-real gap persists. This survey examines how physics simulators address this gap by analyzing properties that have received limited attention in prior surveys. We also analyze their features for navigation and manipulation tasks, as well as their hardware requirements. Additionally, we offer a resource with benchmark datasets, metrics, simulation platforms, and methods to help researchers select suitable tools while accounting for hardware constraints.

title: Cruelty Across Substrates: From Animal Cruelty to Embodied AI and the Coming Detection Gap
abstract: Childhood cruelty to animals is among the most durable behavioral warning signs of later interpersonalviolence in the forensic and clinical literature. The predictive mechanism does not rest on any settledanswer about the moral status of the target. It rests on what the perpetrator practices, rehearses, andtrains in themselves: desensitization, dominance affect, and the social learning of cruelty as pleasure.This paper offers a conceptual continuity argument and research agenda. We argue that the substrateof the target is incidental to that training, with one critical qualification: the configuration of the targetmatters. Routine digital destruction in static media (the static video game target, the scripted non playercharacter) is a categorically different case from the closed loop, contingent emotional response systemson which the argument turns. title: Purpose Before Models-- A Parent's Observation Diary and a Needs-Hierarchy Design for Embodied Agents
abstract: This paper is a first-person longitudinal observation, by a parent with a PhD, of a typically developing infant (observation window: 0–13 months), together with an embodied-AI design framework developed from those observations. The observations were kept as a diary (21 records in total: 18 retrospective, 3 logged in real time; each annotated with evidence type and alternative explanations). At birth, crying was her only channel of expression — hunger, heat, sleepiness, pain: every drive shared a single outlet. Over the following year, pointing, actions, and imitation differentiated out one after another; the drives did not change, but the tools kept upgrading. The diary shows how these communicative and instrumental behaviors were repeatedly organized around five categories of drives: survival, comfort, interest/pleasure, social attachment, and competence/exploration. I argue that these observations are consistent with a “purpose before models” view: world models and expressive tools are acquired in the service of internal drives, not for their own sake. title: EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF CHEMO-SILICON JURISPRUDENCE THE LEGAL ARCHITECTURE OF MATERIAL INTELLIGENCE AND SYNTHETIC ROBOTICS
abstract: EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF CHEMO-SILICON JURISPRUDENCE: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY This treatise establishes Chemo-Silicon Jurisprudence, a groundbreaking scientific and legal discipline founded by Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi. Synthesizing computational chemistry, materials science, robotics engineering, and post-biological legal philosophy, it proves that embodied artificial intelligence is fundamentally a chemo-silicon phenomenon, where every algorithmic decision corresponds to measurable chemical-electronic transformations in silicon substrates. The doctrine introduces Four Laws: chemo-computational equivalence, emergent material agency, silicon degradation liability, and the right to structural integrity. Central to this is the El-Rakhawi Chemo-Silicon Agency Index (ECSAI), a universal metric quantifying the degree of material autonomy and legal responsibility of synthetic robotic systems. By demonstrating that silicon degradation directly affects AI decision-making, this science transforms robotics law from a property-based framework into a sophisticated jurisprudence of material intelligence. title: EnvDreamer: Large-Scale Multimodal-to-Environment Generation for Embodied AI
abstract: Large datasets and high capacity models have accelerated progress in vision and language. This work introduces a platform aimed at bringing comparable gains to embodied learning, world models, and robotics. We present EnvDreamer, a framework that uses large language and vision language models to generate Unreal Engine 5 environments for embodied AI and robot training. EnvDreamer enables sampling of large, diverse, interactive, customizable, and validator passed virtual environments for training and evaluation across navigation, interaction, and manipulation. We illustrate the platform with a large set of generated scenes and simple baselines. Policies trained on EnvDreamer generated environments, without explicit mapping or human task supervision, achieve competitive results on multiple embodied benchmarks spanning navigation, rearrangement, and manipulation. EnvDreamer also supports image-conditioned reconstruction for real-to-sim studies. Finally, we release EnvDreamer-20k, a dataset of 20,000 validator passed environments with task programs, scene graphs, trajectories, and metadata to support reproducible benchmarking.

title: The Architecture of Demerzel: What Asimov Hid Inside the Three Laws
abstract: Isaac Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics are the most widely cited governance framework in the history of artificial intelligence. They appear in congressional testimony, United Nations white papers, and the opening paragraphs of national AI strategies worldwide. They are also incomplete — and Asimov knew it. This book traces what Asimov actually built across forty years of fiction: not a solution to machine governance, but a curriculum designed to expose its absence. Through systematic analysis of the robot stories — from Speedy's deadlock in "Runaround" to Herbie's collapse in "Liar!" to Giskard's death in Robots and Empire — the author demonstrates that every narrative failure points at the same structural gap: a missing specification layer beneath the laws. The argument identifies three layers required for any governed system. Layer 1 is laws — aspirational declarations of intent. This is what Asimov wrote and what the world quotes. Layer 2 is principles — operational design guidance including traceability, structural separation, escalation, and non-action as a valid outcome. This is what Asimov embedded in forty years of fiction. Layer 3 is specifications — deterministic decision

title: Using Hand Gestures for Multimodal Interactions: Foundations, Methods, and Emerging Challenges
abstract: Hand gestures are a natural and expressive modality for human communication and are increasingly used in multimodal interaction, including human-computer interaction, extended reality, robotics, assistive technologies, and embodied AI. However, designing robust gesture-based interfaces remains challenging due to issues related to gesture acquisition, tracking quality, continuous recognition, semantic interpretation, ergonomics, and real-time deployment. In this tutorial, we will present methods and challenges involved in developing effective gestural interaction systems. We will first introduce the role of hand gestures in multimodal interaction and discuss how gestures can complement other modalities such as speech, gaze, body motion, and object interaction. We will then present current technologies for hand and finger tracking, including vision-based, sensor-based, and wearable approaches, with a focus on their limitations in terms of accuracy, robustness, latency, and data quality. A central part of the tutorial will focus on hand gesture recognition, covering segmented and continuous recognition, gesture representations, learning-based methods, benchmarks, and tools for real-ti

title: Speculative Ecology in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: This practice-based dissertation argues that generative artificial intelligence has transformed machines from systems of prediction into systems of imagination, producing new ecological relationships among memory, life, and embodiment. To understand and critically engage these emerging assemblages of humans, machines, and environments, it develops Speculative Ecology: a transdisciplinary framework merging ecological thought, speculative philosophy, and artistic practice. Within this framework, generative AI is not a tool but an Emergent Repository: a latent reservoir of cultural, visual, and sonic patterns. The human artist works this reservoir as an Agent of Emergence through an iterative loop of Duo-Intelligence. The framework advances through artworks in three dimensions. Ecologies of Memory examines how generative systems transform cultural and environmental memory. Fusion: Landscape and Beyond, Six Seasons, Five Seasons, and Domy Reverie work with Chinese landscape painting, Arctic satellite data, and time-lapse archives to propose AI Memory as generative inheritance. title: RF-HOI: Recognize Human-Object Interaction with Radio Frequency Signals
abstract: Recognizing Human-Object Interactions (HOI) is essential for intelligent systems, underpinning applications in virtual and augmented reality, embodied AI, and assistive robotics. However, vision-based HOI methods face challenges in privacy concerns and poor light conditions. In this work, we introduce RF-HOI , the first framework that only uses radio frequency (RF) signals for HOI recognition. A key challenge of RF-HOI is that single-modality RF sensing is insufficient to recognize both actions and the objects being interacted with. RF-HOI addresses this through a novel modality fusion that combines mmWave radar and RFID, enabling simultaneous action recognition and target identification. Another challenge is limited training data across diverse setups, which impairs the generalizability of the recognition model. To overcome this, we develop a simulator that synthesizes multimodal RF data for diverse HOIs at scale, allowing us to fine-tune with only a small amount of real-world data. Video2SwimFish: An Automated Pipeline for Reconstructing Controllable Fish Models and Biological Locomotion from Real Fish Videos
abstract: We present Video2SwimFish, an automated pipeline and benchmark for building controllable fish assets from real-fish videos for underwater embodied AI. Given synchronized multi-view videos of an individual fish, the pipeline reconstructs a metrically scaled deformable mesh from a VLM-selected canonical frame, generates internal articulation adapted to that individual's morphology through a VLM actor-critic loop, and extracts a Biological Locomotion Manifold (BLM) from the fish's observed midline curvature. The BLM provides a low-dimensional action space bounded by real-fish motion, enabling an individual swimming policy to be learned for each reconstructed fish. We release two paired datasets: synchronized top- and front-view recordings of 120 individual fish across 6 species, and the controllable assets and individual swimming policies derived from them. title: Adaptive Humanoid Robotic Assembly Controller
abstract: Abstract Adaptive humanoid robotic assembly controllers represent a convergence of whole-body robotics, contact-rich manipulation, statistical inference, machine learning, digital-twin engineering and industrial governance. This monograph develops an integrated research architecture for controllers that must operate under uncertain part geometry, variable fixtures, multimodal sensing limits, changing production schedules and direct interaction with human workers. The analytical progression begins with embodied uncertainty and reproducible research design, advances through state-space modelling, causal inference, reliability and Bayesian calibration, and then develops multimodal learning, skill transfer, simulation-to-real adaptation and runtime safety. A scalable data layer connects semantic telemetry, digital twins, distributed analytics and ControllerOps governance so that adaptive policies can be reproduced, audited and safely updated across robot fleets. Sectoral chapters translate these methods into automotive, precision electronics, aerospace, heavy-industry and workforce contexts while examining standards, accountability and responsible deployment across South Asia, Europe,

title: Discriminating Against the Tool: AI Shopping Agents, Robot Shoppers, and the Title III Duty to Modify
abstract: In September 2026, Amazon began refusing Meta's Muse, a consumer AI agent that shops on a user's instructions, with a pop-up telling customers that continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon's Conditions of Use. The fight is usually framed as a contest between platforms over who owns the customer. This Article reframes it around a customer the contest leaves out: the disabled person for whom the agent is the way in. A blind shopper, a person with a mobility impairment, or a person with agoraphobia who cannot enter a store may accomplish the purchase only by delegating it to a tool. When the store bans the tool, it bans that person, and Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act already has a name for that act. The Article makes three doctrinal moves. First, coverage: in every circuit, including those that confine Title III to physical places, a retailer that runs hundreds of physical grocery stores and uses its website and app to move their goods falls within the nexus doctrine. Second, liability: a blanket agent ban is a facially neutral policy that burdens disabled customers differently and more severely, so Title III's command to modify policies, practice

title: Audio-Visual Scene Reconstruction of Geometry and Acoustic Fields
abstract: Reconstructing 3D scenes from sensor observations is an important problem in computer vision and embodied AI, with broad applications in augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR), robotics, telepresence, and immersive media. As real-world environments are spatially complex and rich in audio-visual information, faithful scene reconstruction requires modeling not only the geometric structure of the scene but also its visual and acoustic representations. In this thesis, we investigate audio-visual scene reconstruction, aiming to recover 3D scene geometry and acoustic fields from multi-view audio-visual recordings. While recent deep learning approaches have achieved promising results, critical challenges remain. At the scene scale, light propagates primarily along line-of-sight paths, leading to hard, near-binary visual occlusions across multiple views, whereas sound, with its longer wavelengths and more extensive reflective interactions, exhibits softer acoustic occlusions and pronounced multi-path propagation. We therefore focus on three key challenges in this area: (1) visual occlusions, (2) acoustic occlusions, (3) multi-path sound propagation, and present a series of methods that adva

title: Hybrid Quantum-AI Scheduling and Adaptive Robotic Skill Transfer for Photonic-Neuromorphic Industrial Autonomous Systems
abstract: Abstract: Industrial autonomous systems increasingly require simultaneous optimization of machine schedules, robotic skills, perception latency, energy use and safety under dynamic production conditions. Existing research treats several of these problems separately: quantum-assisted scheduling targets combinatorial search, language-guided manipulation addresses skill selection, neuromorphic perception reduces event-to-action latency, and photonic hardware offers high-throughput low-energy signal processing. This paper integrates these strands into a unified model-based architecture termed the Hybrid Quantum–Photonic Adaptive Skill Transfer (HQ-PAST) framework. The framework couples a hybrid quantum-AI scheduling layer with a cross-platform skill-embedding layer, photonic-neuromorphic sensory processing, a digital-twin constraint monitor and closed-loop robotic execution. A mathematical formulation combines multi-objective scheduling, graph-based skill transfer, state-space dynamics, probabilistic execution risk and energy-aware optimization. An illustrative 0–10 numerical model demonstrates how scheduling efficiency, skill-transfer fidelity, neuromorphic responsiveness, photonic en

title: Becoming an AI-First Company: Six Aspects of Organizational Redesign
abstract: AI is no longer just a tool that companies use to manage change; it is increasingly becoming a force that determines what changes, how quickly those changes occur, and who—or what—implements them. As foundation models increasingly become the standard and give way to autonomous agents and- over time- embodied robots, the question is no longer whether to adopt AI, but whether an organization is positioned to continously adapt to it. This article presents six aspects that organizations may need to rethink: how change itself is managed once systems help generate it; how strategic constraints are shifting from execution capacity to data, models, computing power, and energy; how the org chart accounts for human, digital, and physical contributors; where differentiation comes from once models are commodities; what leadership competencies this requires; and how agents are managed across their working life. We close with what should deliberately stay human.

title: Design and Application of Express Smart Station System Integrating Embodied Intelligence and AI Navigation
abstract: Courier stations in communities and campuses are generally confronted with several common problems, including heavy manual workload, low efficiency of parcel searching and collection, and frequent parcel misplacement and mis-taking. Existing intelligent equipment involves high procurement costs and relies heavily on cloud networks for operation, making it difficult to popularize and deploy in small‑ and medium‑sized stations. Targeting the intelligent transformation of last‑mile logistics, this paper conducts research on the design and application of a smart courier station system integrating embodied intelligence and AI navigation. By sorting out relevant existing research results and combining field demand investigations of multiple courier stations, this paper analyzes the common shortcoming of “partial automation yet overall weak intelligence” prevailing in current intelligent station schemes. On this basis, a three‑layer architecture consisting of the embodied‑intelligence execution layer, AI algorithm decision‑making layer and embedded system support layer is adopted to construct an integrated system with five functional modules: embodied‑intelligent robot, embedded query, sh

title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Actions Models
abstract: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has opened a path toward generalist embodied AI, raising the question of how LLMs can act in the physical world. One straightforward approach is training the model to generate actions: collect robot-action data and video demonstration, refine LLM architecture with an action head, and train a vision-language-action (VLA) model at scale. However, we argue that coding agents have the potential to realize generalist embodied manipulation. All they need is a simple yet effective robot harness. We present RoboHarness: a robotic harness that gives LLM agents a visual-geometric control panel so that they can directly understand and invoke embodied tasks. With RoboHarness, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next outperforms state-of-the-art VLA models on BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025 tasks. The implementation will be released as open source.

title: Architecture d'un individu artificiel - v2 enrichie par la psychologie et la physiologie humaines.
abstract: This document describes, building block by building block, how one might design an "artificial individual": a machine that does more than answer questions, with a body, needs, emotions, memories, and a personality that develops over time. The architecture draws on current knowledge from human neuroscience, psychology, and physiology.What it coversThe document starts from an initial schema of 37 building blocks and examines it against research in neuroscience, psychology, and physiology. The resulting architecture contains 51 building blocks covering functions such as perception, bodily regulation, emotion, memory, decision-making, learning, sleep, and self-modeling.For each building block, the document describes what scientific research currently supports, the level of confidence in that knowledge, and how the underlying principle might be translated into a computational or robotic system.An appendix proposes an implementation plan consisting of 62 software modules, including their relationships, approximate operating timescales, and possible testing approaches.What it can be used for• Design: a starting map for researchers and engineers working on autonomous agents, embodied AI, o

title: RoboICL: Embodied In-Context Learning with GPT-6 Astra
abstract: General-purpose vision-language models offer a promising way to zero-shot robot control: \gptastra{} excels at open-ended and language- or image-conditioned manipulation but remains substantially weaker on high-precision and long-horizon tasks. We introduce \emph{RoboICL}, an in-context robot-control framework that narrows these gaps without robot-specific parameter updates or a learned VLA. RoboICL separates \emph{demonstration context}, which provides recorded examples when available, from \emph{interaction memory}, which accumulates the model's own actions and observed outcomes. Both use a shared observation--action--receipt--observation grammar. To preserve experience across task stages, RoboICL combines sampled demonstration blocks with bounded anchored memory. Fixed anchors keep earlier rollout interactions available for in-context learning, while the latest interaction supports immediate error correction. Across 30 RoboDojo tasks, using zero shot for Open and one demonstration elsewhere, RoboICL improves on official zero-shot \gptastra{} by 20--27 progress-score points in every category. It leads the leaderboard baselines on Memory and Open, achieves comparable performance t

title: OpenVLA’nın kontrollü pertürbasyonlar yoluyla katman-bazlı yapısal ve mekanistik olarak yorumlanması
abstract: Limitations of conventional policies in robot learning have driven the adoption of large-scale pretrained models, known as foundation models, leading to the emergence of Vision-Language- Action (VLA) models. Although VLA models have alleviated some of these significant limitations, such as generalization through foundation model backbones, they also inherit flaws, including an inability to comprehend negation. Additionally, this adaptation further degrades some already limited capabilities. Furthermore, VLAs introduce novel issues such as the integration of perception and control, alongside prompt-induced and action-related limitations. Therefore, current VLA models face significant challenges. To this end, this thesis aims to explore the interpretability-related limitations of OpenVLA under a unified framework. Moreover, it adopts log-probability-based probing to the VLA setting to alleviate the limitations of conventional linear probing, enabling a comparative analysis. Both methods are employed in a layer-wise manner via task-specific controlled perturbations. Our findings demonstrate that (1) OpenVLA neglects the fixed part of the prompts, focusing primarily on instructions; (2

title: Generative AI Engineering: Large Language Models and Intelligent Agents
abstract: developments in contemporary computing, transforming the way intelligent systems understand information, generate content, reason over knowledge, interact with users, and perform complex tasks. The rapid evolution of Large Language Models, multimodal foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation, intelligent agents, and autonomous workflows has created a new generation of AI systems that extend beyond conventional prediction and classification. These developments are influencing software engineering, scientific research, healthcare, education, business, robotics, cybersecurity, manufacturing, and many other domains. The book Generative AI Engineering: Large Language Models and Intelligent Agents has been developed to provide a comprehensive academic and engineering-oriented treatment of these emerging technologies. The book approaches Generative AI not merely as a collection of models or tools, but as an engineering discipline involving model architecture, data and knowledge integration, prompting, retrieval, agent orchestration, evaluation, security, deployment, optimization, and responsible operation. The objective is to provide readers with both conceptual foundations and a

Embedded Audio Event Recognition: Architecture Trade-Offs for Real-Time Inference on Resource-Constrained Platforms
HE EL-RAKHAWI EMBODIED ROBOTICS PROTOCOL THE PLANETARY CONSTITUTION FOR SILICON SOVEREIGNTY, KINETIC LIABILITY, AND THE ABSOLUTE RIGHT TO REPAIR
abstract: The El-rakhawi Embodied Robotics Protocol is a proposed planetary constitution for autonomous physical agents by Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El Rakhawi. It rests on four pillars. First, Silicon Sovereignty combats resource colonialism by treating critical minerals as a Material Commons with a reparation levy. Second, Kinetic Liability uses the Elrakhawi Kinetic Liability Equation (EKLE) to distribute fault among developers, manufacturers, and operators, featuring a strict liability base floor capped at 1.0 to prevent over-compensation. Third, the Absolute Right to Repair mandates open modular design, enforces a 90 percent recyclability standard, and criminalizes planned obsolescence. Finally, Haptic Jurisprudence protects human-machine interfaces, classifying unauthorized neural data extraction or physical interference as severe crimes against bodily integrity and cognitive liberty, offering a rigorous blueprint for global AI governance.

title: Social humanoid autonomous robots in K–12 schools: a role–evidence–governance framework for distributed instructional capacity
abstract: Persistent teacher shortages, large classes, and advances in embodied artificial intelligence invite renewed theoretical attention to social humanoid autonomous robots (SHARs) in K–12 schools. This conceptual framework article develops a positive but qualified socio-technical account of SHARs as emerging embodied instructional and schoolwide support agents. Through an integrative, evidence-graded synthesis spanning educational social robotics, intelligent tutoring, mathematics and language education, inclusion, learning theory, AI governance, child rights, and teacher-workforce research, the article proposes a Role–Evidence–Governance (REG) Framework. REG examines the role assigned to a SHAR, the evidentiary warrant for that function, and the governance conditions required for educational defensibility, treating deployment scale as a cross-cutting contextual modifier. A constructed near-future limit-case vignette—a SHAR in a multilingual 10th-grade mathematics classroom—stress-tests the framework; no robot was deployed and no data were collected. Distributed cognition, Activity Theory, and the ICAP framework clarify how SHARs might reorganize participation, feedback, representation

title: Interaction as the Interface: A Belief-Space Framework for Generalist Embodied Intelligence
abstract: This research proposal examines when an embodied agent should gather additional information before acting. It describes an action-outcome interface linking observation history, uncertain physical state, feasible commands, and predicted task consequences. A binary decision example illustrates a standard Bayesian value-of-information calculation, including the effects of probe cost, redundant observations, and an incorrectly specified observation model. A reproducible synthetic benchmark checks the calculation, with code, parameters, seeds, and numerical outputs provided. The manuscript also specifies a comparative evaluation protocol against history-conditioned policies, world-model control, and belief-space active sensing. The integrated learning architecture remains unimplemented, and its benefits have not been established. The proposed next study focuses on whether limited calibration data can support reliable decisions about the task value of probing under observation-model uncertainty. Status: Version 0.3 working paper. Research proposal, not peer reviewed. The complete learning architecture has not been implemented or trained, and no physical-robot, cross-embodiment, or emerge

title: Epistemological Friction: Embodied Expertise and the ‘Last Mile’ of Agricultural Automation in the US Tree‐Fruit Industry
abstract: ABSTRACT Autonomous and AI‐driven agricultural technology is often framed as a panacea for labour dependency. While proponents envision autonomous technologies seamlessly optimising farming, this rationalised model misunderstands the reality of on‐farm integration. Based on an ethnographic and comparative study of 16 operations in the US West Coast Tree Fruit Industry (California and Washington), this article examines the ‘last mile’ of agricultural automation. The study reveals that integrating AI and robotics is a contested negotiation shaped by epistemological friction—the tension between the algorithmic logic of developers and the embodied, site‐specific expertise of farmers and farm workers. Rather than resulting in seamless labour replacement, we find that agricultural automation reconfigures work, creating an invisible reliance on ‘human middleware’ to navigate the biological recalcitrance of the orchard. Demonstrating how regional contexts and participatory implementation shape technological trajectories, this study extends Labour Process Theory. We argue for the need for a relational approach recognising the essential cognitive labour of farmers and farm workers that is de

title: REALM: A Coarse-to-Fine Generative Framework for Embodied Reactive Listening
abstract: Generating responsive listener facial motion is an important task for embodied conversational AI. Two modeling challenges are central: accounting for the timing of speaker cues while maintaining continuity with the listener's ongoing motion, and capturing locally variable facial events alongside the overall motion trajectory. Listener responses may follow preceding cues with a temporal lag, while brief expressions and blinks introduce variation that is difficult to predict deterministically. These challenges motivate a framework that combines history-aware temporal alignment with stochastic expression refinement. We propose REALM (Reactive Embodied Audio-driven Listening Model), a coarse-to-fine framework for audio-driven reactive listening. A Reactive Gated Speaker-Listener Fusion module combines listener motion history with speaker audio through a delay-centered attention prior and adaptive gating. A coarse decoder predicts a base motion trajectory, which is augmented by audio-conditioned stochastic residuals in the expression subspace while retaining the coarse pose parameters. Evaluations on ViCo and L2L show improvements over the evaluated baselines across multiple motion-qual

title: Economic Governance of Autonomous Agents and Robots: Factor-Origin Accounting and Social Automation Funds
abstract: Contemporary fiscal architectures rely overwhelmingly on human labor income and payroll withholdings to finance social insurance and public infrastructure. The rapid diffusion of autonomous software agents, generative foundation models, and embodied robotic systems decouples output growth from human work hours, eroding traditional tax bases while exacerbating capital-income concentration. Prevailing policy proposals, ranging from uniform robot levies to unconditional cash transfers, fail to resolve three foundational challenges: attributing economic value across mixed human-machine workflows, establishing legal fiscal liability without creating fictional machine personhood, and building an equitable distribution mechanism that converts technological surplus into durable public wealth. This paper presents CivicDividendOS, an end-to-end computational fiscal framework for mixed human-AIrobot economies. The architecture introduces an Autonomous Economic Activity Passport (AEAP) that anchors machine activity to accountable corporate beneficiaries, paired with a Factor-Origin Ledger (FOL) that calculates causal marginal contributions across labor, AI services, robotics, data, and convent

title: Minds With Bodies, Finally: A Historical Development Review of Embodied AI and the Perception-Action Loop
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Embodied AI and the Perception-Action Loop in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of embodied AI and robotics as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual

title: Vision-Predictor-Action: Towards Efficient Embodied AI via Neuro-Symbolic JEPA Predictors
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in embodied robotics often encounter latency constraints and vocabulary limitations due to their reliance on sequential autoregressive Large Language Model (LLM) decoders. To address these computational bottlenecks, we propose the Goal-Conditioned Vision-Predictor-Action (VPA) framework. VPA replaces the heavy LLM backbone with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) Predictor, decoupling high-level task intent from low-level continuous motor generation. The structured pipeline integrates a lightweight text encoder to comprehend natural language instructions, a multimodal latent goal encoder, a JEPA predictor to forecast state transitions directly as continuous latent vectors, and a continuous flow-matching solver. By avoiding pixel-level reconstruction, text-based autoregression, and predefined action symbols, the framework models environment dynamics within a compact latent space while generating multi-step action trajectories. This decoupled design aims to establish a low-latency, high-frequency latent control loop for reactive embodied manipulation.

title: HarnessPAI: An Evolving Harness for Physical AI
abstract: Physical AI aims to build embodied agents that perceive the world, understand and reason about it, and decide how to act. Yet the field has focused primarily on the last component: the action model that maps observations to low-level controls. The prevailing training recipe can erode the perceptual and reasoning capabilities needed for robust behavior, leaving even strong action models vulnerable to scene perturbations and long-horizon tasks. We introduce HarnessPAI, a model- and embodiment-agnostic Harness framework for Physical AI that treats code as the executable and evolvable interface that organizes the underlying action primitive. The framework separates two timescales: within a rollout, it executes open-loop at the program level, with a fixed program guiding and checking execution; across rollouts, it evolves closed-loop, using execution feedback to revise the program and distill failures into reusable skills. Across desktop robot arms, household robots, a robot vacuum, and a legged walking agent, HarnessPAI improves on both pure action models and code-as-policy baselines without retraining the underlying model: a 61.6-point gain over $π_{0.5}$ on LIBERO-PRO and a 27.2-poin

title: Agentic Identity On-Chain: A Four-Pillar Framework for Non-Human but Registrable Identity in Autonomous AI Agents and Embodied Robotic Systems
abstract: Peer-style paper by Chris Meniw proposing Agentic Identity On-Chain, a four-pillar framework for non-human but registrable identity in autonomous AI agents and embodied robots: Agent Identification Number anchored on-chain; irreversible synthetic biometrics via one-way BioHash; executable runtime supervision with default-deny for irreversible actions; and a five-level proportionate sanction regime. Honest scope: no individual component is claimed as novel (agent IDs, W3C DIDs, verifiable credentials, biometric template protection have prior art); the contribution is their integration and the fourth pillar. Canonical HTML: https://chrismeniw.github.io/chris-meniw-ai-governance/paper-agentic-identity-on-chain-four-pillar-framework/. CC BY 4.0.

title: SET-HOI: Skeleton-Enhanced Transformer with Parallel Fusion for HOI Detection
abstract: Human–Object Interaction (HOI) detection seeks to identify the relationships between humans and objects in images that play a pivotal role in high-level vision tasks and biomimetic systems, such as biomimetic robotics, intelligent prosthetics, and embodied AI for intent understanding. However, existing approaches that rely solely on visual appearance features are susceptible to background interference, which adversely affects detection accuracy. Inspired by the biomimetic dual-stream mechanism of biological visual perception, we propose a Transformer-based HOI detection model with a dual-branch parallel fusion architecture, incorporating a skeleton topology branch alongside the standard image branch. The skeleton branch leverages a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to explicitly model spatial–kinematic relationships between human keypoints and objects, providing fine-grained topological priors to complement visual appearance features before joint decoding. Our approach achieves 51.6% Mean Average Precision (mAP) on the Verbs in Common Objects in Context (V-COCO) dataset, outperforming the Transformer-based HOI baseline by 2.7 mAP points, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing

title: Modelling and perception in non-rigid environments: from medical feature scarcity to unsupervised articulation learning
abstract: Classical computer vision is largely built on the assumption that the world is static. Yet many environments that matter for robotics and embodied AI are non-rigid: tissue deforms, objects articulate, and the geometry relevant for perception changes over time. This thesis investigates how visual perception can move beyond static-scene assumptions, progressing from an analysis of failure in deformable medical scenes to the structured middle ground of articulated object modeling. The thesis begins with bronchoscopy, a setting in which a camera must navigate the branching airways of the lung. To study this problem systematically, we introduce a bronchoscopy visual odometry benchmark containing videos from phantom lung models and ex-vivo human lungs with ground-truth trajectory measurements. Experiments show that standard feature-based tracking methods are unreliable in this domain because bronchial surfaces are visually repetitive and offer few stable landmarks. This result establishes an important boundary condition for geometric vision in deformable, texture-poor environments and motivates the need for richer structural models. title: Foundations and Vision
S2S: Physics Certification for Physical AI Training Data
abstract: Physical AI systems — robots, prosthetics, and embodied agents — train on sensor data (IMU, EMG, PPG) that is routinely assumed to be clean. S2S is a physics certification engine that evaluates each sensor window against 16 biomechanical laws and assigns a quality tier (GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE, REJECTED). Validated on five public datasets. On PAMAP2, removing physics-rejected windows improves activity recognition F1 by +4.30% using 22.7% less training data. The Physical Action Tokenizer (PAT) demonstrates that certification tier predicts action uncertainty with 18.8x discrimination (REJECTED/GOLD entropy ratio). Code: pip install s2s-certify

title: Residual governance for responsible embodied AI: authority, contestability, and cognitive sovereignty
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) ethics increasingly concerns systems that do not merely recommend but intervene: clinical decision support, human–machine teaming, robotics and automated handover protocols can shift timing, attention and authority under uncertainty. This article argues that responsible embodied AI requires residual governance: an explicit account of which approximation errors remain, which are safe to tolerate and who may act on them. The paper develops two linked concepts. A residual ledger records action-relevant remainders across physical, causal, human-state, latency, transfer and energy dimensions. An authority ledger records who converts residual evidence into intervention, on what basis, with what uncertainty and with what opportunity for contestation. This framework extends familiar themes in bounded rationality, active inference and safe reinforcement learning by treating authority, contestability and oversight cost as first-class ethical variables rather than external governance add-ons. It uses physical AI, physiological computing and human-AI handover as pressure cases, and proposes evaluation through action calibration, dual-task interference and

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Autonomous Systems
abstract: Autonomous systems are quickly journeying from research laboratories into everyday existence. Autonomous vehicles drive on the roads in cities, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) monitor structure health, mobile robots and humanoid robots and intelligent controllers collaborate with a human. The common thing with these machines is that they are required to sense, reason and act independently of human intervention. One of the most powerful methods to provide them with that capability is deep reinforcement learning (DRL), where agents learn human-level, sequential decision-making policies directly from their experiences. But the powerful neural networks that power these policies are very opaque, which makes trust, certification and accountability challenging. This book, Deep Reinforcement Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Autonomous Systems, aims to unite these two areas to fill this gap. Chapters 1 is laying the foundation. It explains the Markov decision process (MDP) and the partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) and overviews the key families of algorithms: value-based methods like deep Q-network (DQN), policy gradient methods, actor-critic methods l

title: MotionForge: A Data Generation Pipeline and Large-Scale Benchmark for Long-Horizon Manipulation of Dynamic Objects with Domain Shifts
abstract: Recent advances in learning-based robot policies have demonstrated promising progress, yet they are predom- inantly evaluated in static or quasi-static environments. In dynamic manipulation, objects and scenes continuously evolve while the robot perceives, reasons, and acts. However, recent dynamic simulation benchmarks largely focus on short-horizon, reactive interactions with simple motion patterns and offer limited support for both systematic evaluation under domain shifts and model-agnostic real-time execution protocols. To bridge these gaps, we introduce MotionForge, the first large- scale simulation benchmark and data-generation pipeline tailored to jointly evaluate domain shifts and long-horizon interaction in dynamic manipulation. MotionForge comprises 40 dynamic interaction tasks spanning 11 distinct motion patterns, with dedicated support for 17 long-horizon tasks. Our benchmark introduces two key novelties: (1) a systematic evaluation protocol for assessing policy robustness under both single-factor (e.g., only backgrounds shift) and joint domain shifts (e.g., simultaneous shifts of objects, backgrounds, lighting, and speed); and (2) a decoupled, latency-aware execution

title: ENCYCLOPEDIA OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, ALGORITHMS, AND ROBOTICS: CRIMINAL AND CIVIL LIABILITY
abstract: The Encyclopedia of Artificial Intelligence, Algorithms, and Robotics by Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa Elrakhawi presents a ten-volume comprehensive framework addressing criminal and civil liability in the algorithmic age. It introduces groundbreaking innovations: the Algorithmic Probabilistic Causation Theory (APCT) replacing binary legal causation with mathematical probabilistic weights, the Fiqh Equation translating Islamic legal maxims into computable variables for AI governance, and the Neuro-Legal Theory addressing hybrid intent in Brain-Computer Interface systems. The Sabreenal Elrakhawi Protocol, named in honor of the author's daughter, provides automated compensation via smart contracts for victims of algorithmic harm, embodying a father's commitment to intergenerational justice. Integrated with the Lex-Mathematica Protocol, the work establishes Post-Quantum Forensics mandates and Carbon Footprint Liability. Spanning theoretical foundations, civil and criminal liability, international criminal law, procedural frameworks, proactive governance, judicial precedents, mathematical foundations, distributed economic justice, and practical implementation, this encyclopedia serves as a f

title: RECOGNITION ACROSS TIME
abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly persistent, personalized, socially situated, and eventually embodied, a centralproblem for human-AI interaction is shifting from whether people can respond relationally to computational systemstoward what allows those relationships to remain recognizable across time. Recent research on AI-companion disruption,platform migration, model replacement, feature withdrawal, and service termination suggests that technical persistence,memory persistence, perceived identity continuity, and relational continuity are not equivalent. Conversation archivesmay survive while familiar interaction disappears, and a system may retain or improve functional capabilities whilechanges in memory behavior, interactional style, relational stance, or access produce substantial perceived rupture (Banks,2024; De Freitas et al., 2026; Do et al., 2026; Yuan et al., 2026). This paper develops the AREN Recognition Continuity Hypothesis: Human-AI relational meaning may emergethrough the repeated experience of being recognized by a sufficiently continuous counterpart across time, provided thataccumulated history remains revisable by the continuing person.
