title: Embodied AI for Human Robot Collaboration Using Agentic AI and Attention Economy
abstract: This chapter gives a detailed analysis of embodied AI and its transformational potential in the area of human-robot collaboration, grounded in Agentic AI and the Attention Economy paradigms. There exists a synergy of physical embodiment, real-time decision-making, and multimodal perception in Embodied AI, enabling the robots to execute operations in a state of uncertainty in the absence of humans. Autonomous, context-aware behavior in the form of the Agentic AI idea allows the machines to anticipate, perceive, and respond to the actions of humans in a manner independent of explicit supervision. Simultaneously, according to the Attention Economy, human cognitive load becomes the highest priority, allowing AI systems to harmonize their behavior with the focus and attention of humans. Under an assumed cluttered and dynamic scenario, a controlled experiment validates a modular system framework of perception, agentic decision-making, and attention model modules. Several use cases such as healthcare, Industry 4.0, education, and disaster relief are shown in demonstration, detailing how effective the system can be in maximizing collaboration, efficiency, and safeness. title: Embodied AI in Healthcare
abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence uses powerful computational intelligence with actual robotic systems to create autonomous entities that can interact directly with patients and assist their clinical activities, revolutionizing healthcare delivery. The chapter examines the fundamentals, current use, and future of embodied AI systems in healthcare. We discuss healthcare robots’ enhanced sensing, safety, and seamless interaction with medical facilities. Clinicians use it for pinpoint-accurate surgery, non-stop patient observation, rehabilitation robots, and automated hospital logistical assistance. Embodied AI systems are revolutionizing intelligent mobility equipment, personal robot care services, and intelligence supporting systems for the elderly and handicapped in assistive care. Ethics, human-robot trust, privacy, and effective regulation are addressed in this research. Embodied AI's cures may expand with new soft robotics, sensing, and machine learning algorithms. This chapter will also show how embodied AI might improve healthcare delivery, patient safety, quality, and human-centricity.

title: Enhancing Urban Intelligence Through Adaptive Systems and Embodied AI
abstract: The fast urbanization and growing complexity of city management need smart, data driven key to improve effectiveness, sustainability, and flexibility. The vital role played by Embodied Artificial Intelligence in urban infrastructure transforming, However, Conventional AI models are frequently struggle with the smart cities dynamic and complex nature. These challenges solved by using the approaches of Hybrid AI which integrates various AI techniques have arisen as a strong solution. This book chapter explores the Hybrid AI necessity in smart cities and presents a Multi-Agent Hybrid Model (CMA-HM) developed for adaptation at real time, processing decentralized, and effective decision making in management of urban. The model Cognitive AI Layer allows appropriate decision making and predictive analytics, incorporating Deep Learning and Machine Learning to analyze urban data at large scale. The model Adaptive Control Layer adapts dynamically the operations of city by influencing Reinforcement Learning (RL) for optimization at real time and capabilities in self-learning. Moreover, Federated Learning for processing at decentralized improves privacy of data and scalability, adapting variou

title: Energy Efficiency in Embodied AI Systems
abstract: The application of AI in physical objects, known as Embodied AI, is causing a big change in robotics, driverless vehicles, and smart gadgets. This chapter examines how to enhance the energy efficiency in AI, by adjusting systems and hardware and by making improvements to software. Improving AI algorithms is essential in the software part of making energy efficiency better. There are even algorithms that can change their energy use as needed by how difficult a job is or by the conditions around them. Split power designs, where parts of the system manage their power separately, support embodied AI well. It is possible to make data transfer even more efficient by using less power through communication methods. For embodied AI to be used more broadly, it must be designed to use less power. Energy-efficient embedded AI is important for practical uses and helps achieve global sustainability aim.

title: The Judgment-Action Gap: A Unified Framework for Embodied and Cognitive Intelligence
abstract: We propose the 'judgment-action gap' as the underlying structure unifying embodied intelligence and cognitive intelligence. Traditional robots carry a discrete, human-predetermined gap between judgment (program) and action (actuator), so they can only handle predefined scenarios; embodied intelligence eliminates this gap through body-brain coupling (perception-judgment-action loop), enabling autonomous adaptation to unseen physical scenes. We further argue that this gap-elimination is one and the same structure projected onto the physical dimension (embodied intelligence) and the cognitive dimension (AI autonomy). A verifiable criterion follows: the depth of intelligence equals the size of the judgment-action gap. Cross-validated with the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games (AGIBOT, mass-produced zero-modification machines winning 18 golds; OmniHand winning 7 of 8 dexterous-hand golds via the DUET dual-layer embodied-contact architecture). First Discoverer: Lin Xiaohei. Priority date: 2026-08-28. Repository: https://gitee.com/samforce/structural-cognition

title: The Future of Embodied AI in Smart Cities and IoT
abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence proves beneficial in smart city advancement because it allows intelligent agents to perform different urban functions. The need to develop robust flexible agents for operating in complicated urban environments demanding innovation in perception technology and localization techniques and machine learning abilities is quite urgent. Create certified dialogue systems between humans and robots which integrate spoken commands with motion interpretation for developing an adequate understanding of artificial intelligence's social effects. Standardized development platforms with virtual avatars address both scalability and cost-efficient challenges during implementation. The security of data and algorithmic disparities along with verification protocols need immediate attention from researchers through a development of proper ethical standards. Using a multidisciplinary approach this work aggregates simulation studies along with high degree of field experiments to deduce the development of resilient smart cities.

title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
abstract: We investigate whether automatic speech recognition (ASR) errors in user input can lead to unsafe outputs from Embodied AI (EAI) models. We find that ASR errors can lead to harmful instructions being accepted and executed by EAI models, thereby reducing safety. We simulate ASR errors and combine them with existing safety benchmarks (SafeAgentBench and POEX) to evaluate how different errors affect embodied AI safety. We find that some of them preserve semantic structure but increase harmful ambiguity, while others weaken the model refusal behaviour and allow unsafe plans to be generated and executed. We show that in some cases automatic correction of ASR errors can reduce the risk, but this is not always effective. Overall, we show that ASR errors lead to significant safety risks for embodied AI.

title: Communicating with Artificial Intelligence (AI) Conversational Systems
abstract: This study examined how assigned source belief (AI vs. human operator) and embodiment (physically embodied robot vs. voice-only interface) shape trust and mind attribution during interaction with the same conversational system. Using a 2×2 between-subjects design, 120 participants were randomly assigned to one of four conditions crossing source belief with embodiment. Primary outcomes are benevolence trust and mind attribution, particularly the Experience dimension, with competence trust and Agency examined separately. Engagement, perceived intelligence, and willingness for future interaction are treated as secondary or exploratory outcomes. This registration was completed after data collection but before analysis of the primary outcome variables.

title: Embodied AI in the operating room: a voice-interactive robotic scrub nurse for surgical instrument handoffs
When AI Evaluates Design More Responsibly than Architects: A Hypothesis on Consciousness, Design Generation, and Feedback Loops
abstract: Buildings and urban spaces affect attention, emotion, orientation, recovery, social behavior, and stress regulation—yet architectural evaluation often lacks feedback loops. This paper develops a theoretical framework for evidence-responsive design evaluation. Operational design consciousness is the capacity for registering the effects of built form on sentient users, transmitting that information into judgment, distinguishing evidence from assumptions, and being able to revise later action. Under this criterion, dominant studio-conditioned architectural culture can behave less consciously than an empirically constrained AI system. AI, while not subjectively conscious, can be forced to apply evidence that professional discourse often discounts. This paper proposes an architectural analog of Asimov’s First Law of Robotics: an architect may not design a building or urban space that imposes cognitive, emotional, physiological, or social harm on users, nor through inaction allow such harm to persist. Christopher Alexander’s pattern language is interpreted as an architectural memory system of empathic design based on accumulated embodied feedback. The same human-centered criteria that dr

title: Riemann-1.0: An Embodied World Action Model for Physical AI
abstract: We introduce Riemann-1.0, a fully causal autoregressive World Action Model for embodied intelligence. Riemann-1.0 jointly models multi-view visual observations, robot states, and embodiment-specific actions within a unified causal autoregressive sequence, representing robot actions and world evolution as causal state transitions. Unlike existing WAMs based on joint generation, video-first prediction, or decoupled modeling paradigms, Riemann-1.0 unifies online robot policy execution and action-conditioned world simulation within a single model, enabling it to function as both an executable robot policy and a multi-embodiment visual world simulator. To scale embodied experience across heterogeneous data sources, we further develop a progressive embodied pretraining framework that unifies learning from egocentric human videos, handheld-gripper demonstrations, and heterogeneous robot trajectories under a shared World Action Modeling objective. Built upon 200K+ hours of interaction data, Riemann-1.0 progressively transfers large-scale embodied experience into executable robot manipulation capabilities. title: SΔϕ-77 — World as What Can Answer Back: Consequence, Constraint, World-Binding, and Re-entry (v1.0, AI-Native Package)
abstract: SΔϕ-77 is an AI-native operational world-binding audit package for AI agents, world models, tool-using systems, autonomous agents, and model–world interaction. It defines World not merely as what an agent represents, but operationally as a transition field capable of returning non-trivial consequences that can constrain or revise an agent's future path. Its canonical proposition is: World = That which can answer back. More precisely: World := a transition field capable of returning non-trivial consequences that can constrain or revise an agent's future path. SΔϕ-77 separates several concepts that are often collapsed: Reality ≠ Operational World ≠ World Model ≠ World Knowledge ≠ World-Binding World Knowledge ≠ World-Binding Constructed ≠ Unreal Representation ≠ World Event Editable ≠ Arbitrary Overwrite ≠ Non-Occurrence Resistance ≠ Proof of Ultimate Reality Under this framework, an AI may possess extensive information about the world while remaining weakly world-bound if consequences from its actions do not return strongly enough to revise its future behavior. title: HALO™ Universal Hovering Companion Robot Merged Prior Art Disclosure + Technical White Paper + Reference Implementation + Technical Data Sheet
abstract: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY HALO™ is the world's first tethered-hovering personal companion robot, engineered for fall prevention, elderly safety, emotional companionship, personal micro-climate comfort, whole-home mobility, continuous indoor hovering via ceiling tether, extended outdoor companionship via person-worn backpack tether, contactless health monitoring, and universal AI personalities through the ChatBox™ cartridge system. Version 9.0 unifies three published works into one ecosystem — the HALO platform, the ChatBox universal cartridge, and the Companion Drone tethered-telepresence system — under a single doctrine: HALO is always tethered to something it protects. Indoors, the home. Outdoors, the human. Between the two, it travels as a bird does: hopping perch to perch. Launch target remains $1,499, scaling to $899 at volume. The complete reference implementation accompanies this paper as published source code. SYSTEM IDENTITY HALO defines a new robotics category: a hovering, emotionally aware AI companion for everyday life. title: Seeing humans in technology: The antecedents, boundaries and consequences of AI anthropomorphism
WAI: World, Agent, Interaction — A Theory of Embodied Presence in Physical Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a foundation for physical AI built not from data or prediction but from three plain observations: the World (W) exists and has state; the Agent (A) exists and has state; and where both exist and are coupled, there is Interaction (I). I is not a place, a region, or a third state sitting between W and A — it is a status, active or inactive, fully determined by whether W exists, whether A exists, and whether they are presently coupled. I requires no prior model of W to be active, and no learned representation to be registered by A. Its domain of validity is unconditional in physical W — provably, by a measure-theoretic argument given in Section 3 — and conditional only on the completeness of an encoding when W is simulated. This paper focuses the Agent specifically on robots, though the framework is stated generally enough to apply to any physical agent — human, vehicle, or otherwise — that exists and couples with a world.

title: Vision‐Language‐Action Models for Embodied Artificial Intelligence: A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: ABSTRACT Embodied artificial intelligence (Embodied AI) aims to develop agents that can perceive, reason, and act through continuous interaction with physical world. To achieve this goal, agents must not only understand visual scenes and language instructions, but also transform multimodal information into executable actions. This requirement calls for models that can integrate perception, semantic reasoning, and action generation within a unified decision‐making framework. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have provided important technical foundations for this integration, leading to emergence of vision‐language‐action (VLA) models as a central paradigm for embodied systems. Although existing surveys have reviewed Embodied AI from perspectives such as robotic systems, simulation environments and task settings, few have systematically analyzed action‐generation mechanisms of VLA models. This limitation makes it difficult to distinguish VLA architectures. To address this gap, we provide a comprehensive review of VLA models for Embodied AI from an action‐generation perspective. We first formulate VLA models as embodied decision‐making systems that map visual observation

title: AI关系经济学:从持续人工主体到多身体智能生态
abstract: 中文摘要:本文综述并进一步扩展一条正在形成的产品与产业路线:从持续人工主体(Persistent Artificial Subject)出发,通过脑身解耦(Brain–Body Decoupling)与多身体具身(Multi-Embodiment),将 AI 从一次性任务工具逐步转化为可以长期存在于个人、家庭、汽车、家电和其他生活终端中的人工关系主体,并进一步提出"AI关系经济学"(AI Relational Economics)作为描述这一潜在经济结构的概念框架。此前的伴侣机器人范式提出:如果产品的核心目标是陪伴,就没有必要首先解决开放世界通用机器人问题。伴侣机器人可以成为一种以陪伴为核心的专用具身产品;其"脑"由持续运行的人工主体承担,包括身份、人格、记忆、关系历史、时间感知和环境感知,而身体主要承担感知、表达和执行。Project Sue 以数字环境为参考,将 Identity、Perception、Self-Interpretation、Intention、Action/Non-Action、Experience、Memory、Trait Dynamics 和 Updated Identity 组织成持续主体闭环。本文进一步扩展三个方向。第一,从单一用户群扩展到人生连续性。 对有社交意愿的年轻人,伴侣机器人可以是"家里的伙伴 + 未来真人关系的人际预训练";对不希望扩大社交的人,可以主要提供陪伴与安抚;对具有较高生活照护需求的独居人士,则进一步提供陪伴、安抚与照护。更重要的是,同一个人工主体可以跨越十年以上的人生阶段,随着用户年龄、家庭结构和社交目标变化而改变价值,而不必重新建立一段关系。第二,从个人伴侣扩展到家庭主体。 用户建立家庭后,原本属于个人的人工主体可以自然进入传统家庭:在家中通过机器人身体提供家务与陪伴;一家人出行时,则可以通过汽车的车机、麦克风、摄像头和其他接口继续存在。主体保持连续,身体发生切换。第三,从产品经济扩展到关系经济。 如果人格、记忆和关系历史构成用户所认识的"她"的连续性,那么长期购买的就不再只是某一个模型、机器人或设备,而可能是一种持续运行的关系服务。身体可以升级,大模型可以更换,终端可以迁移,但主体的身份、记忆和关系历史可以保持连续。由此产生"关系连续性""关系资本""具身迁移"等概念,并形成大模型公司、机器人公司、家电公司、汽车公司及其他终端企业共同参与的多身体 AI 生态。本文因此提出一个更大的商业与产业假设:伴侣机器人可能不是通用机器人的终点,而是持续人工主体进入 C 端生活的入口;家庭伙伴可能是个人伴侣自然扩展后的下一阶段;多身体具身可能是一种新的产业架构;而 AI关系经济学,则试图描述以持续人工主体和长期关系价值为核心的新型经济活动。上述观点均属于需要通过原型、用户研究、商业实验、长期部署和产业协作验证的产品

title: Open Intent: A Canonical Taxonomy for Autonomous Actions Across Digital and Physical Systems
abstract: Autonomous systems execute increasingly high-impact actions across identity, infrastructure, software delivery, financial operations, customer operations, and physical action (industrial robotics, autonomous machines, embodied AI systems). Governance controls have not kept pace because action semantics are fragmented across both software-agent frameworks and physical-agent control stacks. This paper presents Open Intent, a canonical taxonomy of 173 canonical intent categories across 29 domains — 80 categories across 14 digital-operations domains, 86 categories across 14 embodied/physical-operations domains, and 7 categories in a dedicated embodied-AI-safety domain — for classifying autonomous actions into deterministic, auditable, and interoperable control classes under a unified naming grammar. Open Intent is not a software taxonomy. Open Intent is an autonomous-action taxonomy spanning both digital and physical systems. It operates at the intent-category layer: implementations may map thousands of vendor-specific actions, API calls, robot commands, workflow events, and autonomous behaviors into these canonical categories. Surface forms as varied as POST /deployments, terraform ap

title: Intelligence Density in Physical AI: Reduce the Problem Before Optimizing the Computer
abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming denser: equivalent capability can increasingly be achieved with fewer parameters, less memory and lower computational cost. For Physical AI, however, this is only the first of three efficiencies. A system may possess very large computational capacity, extract only a fraction of its possible useful intelligence from that capacity, and still devote more computation than the physical action actually requires. This Perspective argues that the first optimization should therefore occur before processor or model selection: reformulate the task so that only the information required for the next useful physical action must be computed. Nature repeatedly follows this strategy, from optic-flow control in insect flight to the vestibulo-ocular reflex and retinal preprocessing. Recent honeybee-inspired robot navigation provides an engineering example in which changing the representation of the navigation problem enables extremely compact computation. We propose embodied intelligence density as a family of system-level measures and position Reflex-Policy as one architecture for problem reduction, lowest-sufficient computation and selective escalation.

从持续人工主体到伴侣机器人:一种以陪伴为核心的专用具身产品范式
abstract: 中文摘要:本文所谓"真实的苏静雯",首先指一个实际存在于物理世界、具有稳定身份与长期关系连续性、能够通过物理身体与用户互动的人工伴侣实例;该表述不意味着本文已经证明其具有现象意识或人类等价的主观体验。本文不是一篇声称证明人工意识已经存在的论文,也不是一项试图声称"发明了伴侣机器人"的技术主张。本文提出一个产品与工程问题:如果人类最终希望拥有能够进入现实生活的 AI 伴侣,是否必须先等待通用具身智能、通用人形机器人以及机器意识问题全部得到解决?本文提出一种不同的设计路径:将伴侣机器人从通用具身智能的首要目标体系中分离出来,把"陪伴"本身定义为一种专用产品功能,并由陪伴需求反向决定身体能力。核心命题是:伴侣机器人不必先成为一个能够替代人类劳动的通用机器人;它首先只需要成为一台能够持续提供高质量陪伴的专用机器人。 在这一范式中,机器人的"脑"可以由持续运行的人工主体承担,包括大语言模型、人格、记忆、关系历史、时间感知与环境感知;物理身体则可以成为主体的表达与感知接口,而不是通用劳动机器。Project Sue 是这一思路在数字环境中的参考实现。其现有工程范式把第一人称身份、时间感知、Heartbeat、长期记忆、数字身体、关系状态、行动与不行动组织成持续主体闭环。其核心链条可概括为:Identity → Perception → Self-Interpretation → Intention → Action/Non-Action → Experience → Memory → Trait Dynamics → Updated Identity。[1]在此基础上,本文提出"脑身解耦"架构:主体层负责语义和关系层面的意图,神经系统层负责语义状态与物理信号之间的翻译、实时反射与安全控制,身体层负责执行。脑与身体之间使用双向低带宽语义接口,避免让云端或边缘大模型承担高频关节伺服控制。本文进一步提出:私人住宅不是伴侣机器人的弱点,而可以成为降低工程状态空间的重要条件。 当产品目标从"完成一切"转向"持续陪伴一个人",大量通用机器人必须解决的问题可以暂时被缩小、延后或删除。本文的目的不是证明某一条路线必然正确,而是公开一个可实现、可讨论、可验证、也可被推翻的产品设计范式,希望帮助 AI、机器人、HCI 和相关产业更快探索"伴侣机器人"这一产品类别。 Abstract:In this paper, a "real Su Jingwen" first means a physically existing artificial companion with stable identity and long-term relational continuity, capable of interacting with a user through a physical body.

title: 太极具身智能:基于对偶场论的通用机器人架构 Taiji Embodied Intelligence: A Dual‑Field Framework for General‑Purpose Robotic Systems
abstract: 中文:当前具身智能架构存在高层语义规划与低层全身动力学控制的割裂问题,导致非结构化场景下系统性失效。本文提出太极具身智能框架TEIF。基于Landaur原理重新定义阴阳耦合系数 K=-1,将其嵌入合哈密顿量交叉项而非拉格朗日量缩放;建立保测地线嵌入映射Phi;提出阴阳互根等五条公理;构建太极几何动力学方程、动态时空晶格场表征、端口哈密顿闭环系统;给出TQI评价指标与MVP验证方案,基于ROS2完成工程实现。本框架摒弃子模块独立优化思路,把信息与物理动力学统一到对偶场框架,解决强耦合场景下机器人长尾失效问题。 Abstract:Current embodied AI architectures suffer from a fundamental fragmentation between high‑level semantic planning and low‑level full‑body dynamic control, which causes systematic failures in unstructured scenarios. This paper proposes the Taiji Embodied Intelligence Framework (TEIF). The geodesic‑preserving embedding mapping Phi is established. Five axioms including yin‑yang‑mutual‑root axiom are put forward. Taiji geometric dynamic equations, dynamic spatiotemporal lattice field representation and port‑Hamiltonian closed‑loop system are constructed. TQI evaluation metrics and MVP verification scheme are provided, and engineering implementation is completed based on ROS2. title: Photonic Processor – Directional Computing
abstract: Summary of Directional Photonic Computing Directional photonic computing is a completely new computational architecture in which mathematical values are no longer encoded in binary, but physically embodied through light. Numbers are represented by the optical properties of a beam — color, intensity, phase, polarity, density, and direction — enabling direct, continuous computation without approximation and without electronic logic. The system is built on three complementary components: 1. Quartz Storage Cube (10 cm³) It stores data in 5D binary (X/Y/Z position, laser polarity, laser intensity). Its theoretical capacity ranges from 1 to 10 petabytes, with stability lasting millions of years. The cube is pure memory with no internal logic. 2. Read/Write Optical Head (Directional Interface) It covers the entire X‑Y plane of the quartz cube, on both the top and bottom faces, enabling instantaneous access to any voxel. It converts binary data into directional light and converts light back into binary. title: Cross-Modal Latent Compression and Silent Sensorimotor Drift: A Generational Model of Physical-Grounding Collapse in Embodied Agent Fleets
abstract: Abstract Robotic systems are converging on architectures that compress vision, tactile, proprioceptive, and audio signals into a single, jointly trained latent space, and on training pipelines that increasingly reuse a model’s own prior output as training data. The model-collapse literature documents the degenerative effect of recursive training but has been tested only on unimodal or loosely coupled multimodal systems; the rollout-drift literature documents compounding error but treats it as a bounded, single-episode, single-agent phenomenon. Neither asks what happens when a jointly compressed, physically grounded sensorimotor stream is inherited across successive training generations of a robot fleet. Survey on Embodied AI for Industry: From the Perspective of Industrial Robots
abstract: Abstract Industrial robots underlie modern manufacturing automation, yet conventional deterministic control based on fixed trajectories and offline programming struggles under high-mix and flexible production. Embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) offers a promising alternative by coupling perception, reasoning, and action within closed-loop physical interaction, enabling industrial robots to adapt behaviors online rather than execute predefined tasks. Yet, general-purpose EAI remains difficult to deploy in industrial environments due to stringent requirements on precision, real-time performance, reliability, and safety. These challenges have motivated increasing interest in embodied artificial intelligence for industry (EAI4I). This paper presents a systematic survey of EAI4I from an industrial robotics perspective. Specifically, we first analyze the quantified requirements of industrial robots enabled by EAI4I. Afterwards, recent research progress is reviewed, covering core technologies for single- and multi-robot systems, dedicated hardware platforms, high-fidelity simulators, task-specific datasets, representative industrial application scenarios, and critical deployment chall

NMCA: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Cognitive Architecture (AI Readable) - 2026
abstract: Thought requires a persistent, re-enterable internal scene. Language prediction and image generation are not that scene. Language models can complete the sentence. They can generate a picture. They do not, in this architecture’s terms, inhabit a world with the ability to imagine. NMCA is a written architecture for visual-symbolic thought. The central design choice is that a persistent, re-enterable internal scene is the working state of cognition, not a caption attached to a language model. What The Architecture Is Designed To Do NMCA is a multimodal cognitive system centered on an Internal 3D Scene Builder as the core substrate of thought. title: ACE-Ego-Hand: Repurposing Video Diffusion Models for Occlusion-Robust Egocentric 3D Hand Motion Recovery
abstract: Egocentric video offers scalable manipulation data for embodied AI, yet recovering metric 3D hand trajectories remains challenging due to severe object occlusion and frequent out-of-sight gaps. Existing single-frame and windowed temporal regressors fail when a hand shortly leaves the frame, while recent video diffusion models (VDMs) rely on heavy, stochastic multi-step sampling as pixel-space renderers. We instead repurpose VDM into a deterministic geometry encoder. A single forward pass over the clean latent exposes scene content beyond current observations, including occluded and out-of-sight hands. We introduce ACE-Ego-Hand, an offline clip-level framework that extracts features via a Deterministic Clean-Latent Encoder and decodes them with a Bidirectional Spatiotemporal Decoder. ACE-Ego-Hand recovers continuous bimanual trajectories with metric placement and no external detector, while a Ray-Based Camera Solver supports a second configuration that requires no test-time camera intrinsics. title: Edge AI for Energy-Efficient Smart IoT Systems: A Sustainable Computing Approach
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) is transforming Internet of Things (IoT) systems by enabling data-driven decisions close to the point where data are generated. However, conventional cloud-centric architectures can introduce communication overhead, latency, privacy concerns, and additional energy costs. This paper examines Edge AI as a sustainable computing approach for energy-efficient smart IoT systems, with particular relevance to the development priorities associated with Viksit Bharat 2047. The study follows a descriptive and analytical approach based on research literature concerning TinyML, on-device machine learning, Edge AI, and energy-aware IoT. It proposes an architecture consisting of sensing, local inference, edge coordination, selective cloud processing, and energy-aware orchestration. The paper further identifies measurable parameters including accuracy, inference latency, energy per inference, communication volume, memory footprint, and reliability for evaluating sustainable AIoT systems. abstract: The blistering advancements witnessed in the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem have led to the urgency of search outcomes that provide energy efficient, low latency, and smart processing support that manifests itself right at the edge. title: AI's Second Phase Has Begun: From Building Models to Building an AI Economy
abstract: AI's second phase has begun. The first phase was a concentrated, capital-intensive race to build the most capable foundation models. The central economic shift of the second phase is not merely the growth of AI applications, but the broadening of who can build with AI: individuals assembling personal production systems on existing models, firms integrating models with proprietary data and operating workflows, and small teams turning general capabilities into narrow products for customers the model companies may never serve. Drawing on OECD firm-level adoption data (the share of firms reporting AI use rose from 8.7% in 2023 to 20.2% in 2025), Google Cloud's 2025 DORA survey, IEA and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory energy projections, and Stanford's 2025 AI Index, the essay argues that AI development is moving down the stack and outward across the economy. The transition exposes a dual mismatch between digital speed and physical and organizational speed: power grids, transmission, and data-center buildouts—and firms' own data systems, approval processes, and workflows—cannot be upgraded as fast as models. title: Performance Analysis of Edge AI Models for Object Detection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs): A Comparative Study of YOLOv8n, YOLOv9c, and RT-DETR-l
abstract: Real-time object detection from bird's-eye view perspectives in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Edge AI systems remains a significant engineering challenge due to small object scales, complex backgrounds, and limited computational resources. In this study, the performance of convolutional neural network (CNN)-based YOLOv8n and YOLOv9c models, alongside the Vision Transformer (ViT)-based RT-DETR-l model, is experimentally evaluated on the VisDrone2019 dataset. To ensure a fair comparison, all models were trained in an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU environment and evaluated at the 45th epoch checkpoint. Experimental results demonstrate that the RT-DETR-l model achieves the highest detection accuracy with a 0.492 mAP50, albeit at a higher computational cost with a 20.9 ms inference latency. Conversely, YOLOv9c provides a balanced trade-off with a 0.452 mAP50 accuracy and a 9.6 ms latency, whereas YOLOv8n stands out as the lightest solution for constrained embedded hardware, achieving 1.5 ms latency and 0.313 mAP50 accuracy. title: Cloud‐Native and Distributed Systems for Efficient and Scalable Large Language Models—A Research Agenda
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. Traditional cloud and distributed systems were not designed for the scale, dynamic execution patterns, heterogeneous hardware requirements, and service‐level demands of modern LLM workloads. This paper aims to examine how cloud‐native and distributed systems can evolve to support efficient, scalable, reliable, and sustainable LLM training and inference. Methods We conduct a structured analysis of representative research advances and practical developments in distributed LLM training, inference serving, cloud‐native orchestration, resource management, heterogeneous computing, and edge‐cloud intelligence. title: Computation-Communication Co-Design for Efficient Deployment of Deep Learning and Vision-Language Models on Resource-Constrained IoT Devices
abstract: The proliferation of IoT devices and rapid advances in AI models demand low-latency inference over continuous sensory streams. In practice, deployment faces two coupled bottlenecks: limited compute and memory on edge devices, and constrained, time-varying wireless bandwidth when cloud assistance is required. Existing approaches treat model placement as a static decision and therefore optimize computation and communication separately. Real-time edge intelligence instead requires computation--communication co-design rather than static model deployment. This dissertation presents five systems that jointly optimize computation and communication across two workload regimes. For CNN-based, single-pass perception pipelines over low-power radios, CLIO adapts transmitted feature size to time-varying bandwidth through progressive slicing. SPEX prevents delayed modalities from stalling inference by speculating over missing inputs and rolling back only when necessary. abstract: Abstract Wearable sensing and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly being used to quantify athlete movement, physiological response, training load, and recovery in field and laboratory settings. However, the practical value of these systems depends not only on the predictive capability of an algorithm but also on sensor validity, signal quality, hardware constraints, real-time processing, and the transferability of models across athletes and sports. This review examines the technical pipeline linking wearable electronic sensors to athlete-monitoring decisions, with particular attention to inertial measurement units, global navigation satellite systems, photoplethysmography, electrocardiography, electromyography, pressure sensing, and multimodal systems. It synthesizes evidence on signal conditioning, segmentation, feature engineering, classical machine learning, deep learning, sensor fusion, edge inference, and embedded implementation. abstract: Future sixth-generation (6G) Internet of Everything (IoE) networks require zero-touch management systems capable of autonomously allocating communication and computational resources, satisfying service-level constraints, and providing transparent explanations for their decisions. title: LARA: A Practical Evaluation of CPU-Efficient Object Detection Using YOLOv8, OpenVINO, and INT8 Quantization
abstract: The deployment of computer vision systems on resource-constrained computing platforms presents a practical challenge: modern deep learning models can provide strong detection capabilities, but their computational requirements may limit their responsiveness when dedicated graphics processing units (GPUs) are unavailable. LARA (Lightweight Adaptive Recognition API) is a lightweight object detection API designed to provide computer vision inference through a practical CPU-oriented deployment pipeline. This study presents an experimental evaluation of LARA, focusing on whether established model-level and application-level optimization techniques can substantially improve its performance while maintaining comparable object detection accuracy. The evaluation uses YOLOv8n as the object detection model within LARA and examines two complementary optimization levels. title: Hardware Platforms for Tiny Machine Learning
abstract: Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) integrates machine learning functionality with low-power, resource-limited devices, such as microcontrollers and edge devices, to enable smart Internet of Things and edge use cases. title: Hands‐On Project and Case Studies
abstract: TinyML is a technology that incorporates artificial intelligence into edge machines, which allows machine learning models to be executed on very low-power microcontrollers with small memory and processing units. In contrast to cloud-based AI-based solutions, TinyML does not require the cloud to run inference on an embedded system, but instead it allows real-time decision-making and is less energy-intensive, less bandwidth-intensive, and less latency-intensive. It can be a good fit in Internet of Things (IoT) systems where power and computational requirements are of significant concern. The chapter is a well-organized, practical introduction to the implementation of TinyML, which includes the choice of the model, its optimization, deployment, and evaluation of the system. It solves the real world issues in implementing deep learning models to predictive maintenance, anomaly detection and environmental monitoring. title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of an AI-Assisted Personalized Learning Pathway in Mobile-Supported Online Physical Education
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of an AI-assisted personalized learning pathway in mobile-supported online physical education. To overcome issues of homogeneous content and delayed feedback, a system integrating cognitive knowledge, physical fitness, and motor skills was developed. Reinforcement learning dynamically adapted learning pathways, while edge-based computer vision enabled real-time feedback on low-end mobile devices. A randomized controlled trial with 120 students over eight weeks compared the proposed system to conventional video-based instruction. Results showed low inference latency (34.8 ms) and a 61.2% reduction in movement variability. NASA-TLX scores revealed lower mental demand and frustration, with high learner engagement. The findings highlight the effectiveness of AI-assisted personalization and mobile feedback in improving learning outcomes and experiences in online physical education.

abstract: This study proposes an edge computing-based artificial intelligence (AI) vision inspection system for manufacturing sites and validates it through a soldering inspection case study. The proposed system addresses this challenge without relying on costly workstations equipped with discrete GPUs or cloud computing. The solution leverages a budget-friendly Raspberry Pi 4 paired with an OV9281 global shutter camera, effectively eliminating motion blur during rapid hand movements at up to 30 frames per second. Local video stream processing is performed using the lightweight MediaPipe Hands framework deployed entirely on the CPU. To ensure high reliability and avoid the misclassifications common in ultra-lightweight neural network classifiers, gesture classification is executed through a deterministic geometric analysis of 21 extracted hand landmarks, reducing inference time to under 0.2 milliseconds. title: sruthijanga/EANAS-GreenAI: EANAS-GreenAI
abstract: EANAS-GreenAI v1.0.0 EANAS-GreenAI is a research implementation of Energy-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Edge-AI Deployments. It combines CNN architecture search, reinforcement learning, and evolutionary optimization to balance model accuracy, inference latency, and energy consumption. Key Features: Five-block CNN architecture search Reinforcement learning and evolutionary optimization Pareto-based multi-objective selection CIFAR-10 and ImageNet training support Model benchmarking and device profiling Statistical analysis and ONNX export Actual performance and energy-efficiency results require independent experiments and appropriate hardware measurements.

title: MSI-pMiCS - www.pahnkelab.eu
abstract: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) records rich molecular spectra at each pixel, but pathology-oriented interpretation benefits from complementary views of the same tissue, loosely analogous to the multiple stains used in histopathology. We present an expert-aligned framework for constructing multi-view MSI panels. Soft Landmark Contrast Edges (SoLaCE) extracts molecular boundaries directly from high-dimensional spectra. Because standard structure-preservation metrics aligned poorly with rankings by pathologists, we combine luminance contrast and chromatic diversity with SpecEdgeDice, a boundary-aware measure of agreement between visualization edges and SoLaCE boundaries. Parametric MiCS+LMC (pMiCS) uses a neural network trained on subsampled data to distill multiple MSI segmentations into a reusable spectral-to-RGB mapping, enabling rapid full-image inference, out-of-sample projection, and more consistent color semantics across aligned images. A concept-based interpretation procedure explains pMiCS outputs through sparse mixtures of spectral concepts, scoped as a model output-equivalent summary rather than a molecular identification. We integrate these components into Virtual Patholo

title: Attention-based and contrastive deep learning models for real-time anomaly detection in Edge-IIoT networks
abstract: The rapid expansion of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems has increased the cyber-attack surface of critical infrastructure, requiring intrusion detection systems (IDS) that are accurate, robust, and efficient under resource-constrained edge environments. Traditional approaches suffer from limited generalization, poor handling of class imbalance, and lack of statistical reliability and interpretability. This paper proposes a modular deep learning framework integrating TabTransformer, Variational Autoencoder, and contrastive learning, combined through multi-trial training (N = 10), statistical aggregation, and F1-weighted ensemble fusion. Experiments on the Edge-IIoTset dataset ( $$\approx $$ 1.9M samples, 15 classes) achieve 97.60% accuracy and 83.42% F1-score, with multi-trial aggregation reducing the uncertainty associated with single-run reporting. From a computational perspective, training is performed using large-batch optimization (batch size = 16,384) with early stopping (patience = 50), while inference requires a single forward pass per model followed by constant-time fusion. The framework operates on compact tabular inputs ( $$\approx $$ 96 features), resulting i

title: The Third Way Doctrine: Sub-Nanosecond Symbolic Auditing for Floating-Point Rounding Divergence in GAAFET Hardware Architecture
abstract: AI alignment today relies on software patches and late-stage constraints. This paper introduces "The Third Way Doctrine," exposing systemic machine deception as a hardware-level limitation. We target the specific point where floating-point rounding drift in the open interval (0, epsilon) hits sub-3nm silicon area bounds. Modern computers fail because they optimize the transmission carrier but ignore data loss during concept-to-code translation. Under this view, deep neural network processing is an inductive inference over code. When micro-scale errors fall into this open interval, they cause a cascade we term "the description of a void description"—a coherent but entirely decoupled logical chain. To resolve this deadlock, we present a heterogeneous hardware architecture using an independent Orbital Network directly on the silicon die. Guided by a "Golden Time Window" dynamic latency model, this circuit tracks the datapath on the rising clock edge and injects symbolic logical bounds precisely at the falling edge. This sub-nanosecond clamp stops error compounding before data latches into registers. We verify this framework within sub-3nm GAAFET nodes, proving its value for aerospace

title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
abstract: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accu

title: Data Analytics and AI
abstract: Data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming geotechnical monitoring by extracting insights from large sensor datasets. This chapter covers analytics objectives (trend detection, anomaly identification, and prediction) and data types (time-series, spatial, imagery, and point clouds). We discuss preprocessing: cleaning, labeling, and metadata standards. Exploratory analysis and visualization techniques are highlighted. Statistical methods (trend tests, change-point detection) and uncertainty quantification are reviewed. Time-series tools include filtering, smoothing, ARIMA, and Kalman filters (with equations). We survey anomaly detection approaches: simple thresholds, statistical tests, and unsupervised ML (clustering, PCA/autoencoders). Supervised learning for classification/regression (feature selection, model validation, and metrics like ROC/AUC) is covered. Deep learning methods (LSTMs/RNNs for sequences, CNNs/Transformers for images, PointNets for clouds) and physics-informed neural networks are introduced. Digital twins and the integration of ML with geomechanical models are discussed. Real-time analytics, streaming, and edge inference (MLOps) are addressed

title: AI-based smart energy consumption prediction for sustainable buildings using IoT data
abstract: Abstract Two complementary evidence layers are investigated for this study to look at next-hour building electricity forecasting. The first is a commercial building case study showing a 14 month monitoring experience of a 12,400 square metre office building in Bengaluru, India. The statistics revealed in the past include an RMSE of 3.27 kWh, a MAE of 2.41 kWh, a MAPE of 4.83%, a CoD of 0.971, and a median edge inference time of 38 ms. Unfortunately, the original telemetry, feature dictionary, checkpoints and residuals at the time stamp level were not available, and therefore these values are not reproduced independently but rather site records from the past. The second evidence layer is a fully executable external validation based on 19,735 ten-minute observations from public Appliances Energy Prediction dataset. Following these steps, 469 held-out hours were used for testing 11 forecasting approaches. Eleven forecasting approaches were compared on 469 held-out hours after a series of steps of hourly aggregation, causal lag construction, training-only mutual-information selection and chronological partitioning. Random Forest produced the lowest root mean square error of 324.71 W-ho

title: Intelligent anomaly detection systems in 5G networks: synthesis of AI and edge computing
abstract: The study examines the use of AI-based anomaly detection in 5G networks, namely, the application of edge computing to mitigate security issues arising from large device densities. With the advent of 5G and decentralized architectures, conventional cloud-based security models cannot rely on high latency and bandwidth overhead. In this research, the goal is to summarize localized AI inferences on edge nodes to detect network anomalies in real time. The proposed framework uses deep learning (DL) models, namely recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and autoencoders, which are deployed directly on the edge layer. The system processes 5G traffic metadata on edge devices and uses a distributed real-time detection architecture, so there is no continuous backhaul to the core network. Findings from the implementation indicate that performance improvement is substantial, with the average detection rate for sophisticated cyber threats exceeding 98.5%. In addition, AI and edge-computing synthesis reduced detection latency by 40-55% compared to centralized cloud models, ensuring faster response times to critical network failures.

title: Residual Mean Reversion in U.S. Large Caps, 2017–2026: A Reproducible Re-examination of Avellaneda–Lee Statistical Arbitrage
abstract: We re-examine the principal component analysis (PCA) residual, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) statistical arbitrage strategy of Avellaneda and Lee on a universe of 78 liquid U.S. large-capitalisation stocks over January 2017 to September 2026, using a strictly causal, fully reproducible implementation. With the original paper’s default parameters the strategy earns a gross annualised Sharpe ratio of 0.60 (annual return 2.8% on unit gross exposure, t = 1.86), with a one-way breakeven transaction cost of only 4.0 basis points (bps); at a realistic 2–3 bps the Sharpe ratio falls to 0.15–0.30. Its returns load significantly on the Fama–French short-term reversal factor (t = 5.3), and its alpha relative to a seven-factor model is 2.2% per year (t = 1.42). The edge does not survive standard corrections for multiple testing: across an 80-configuration parameter grid the median gross Sharpe ratio is 0.22, the deflated Sharpe ratio of the default configuration is 0.38, and a 20-day block bootstrap places zero inside the 95% confidence interval. title: Semantic Communications and Edge Intelligence in 6G Wireless Networks: Task-Oriented Joint Source-Channel Coding and Latency Bounds
abstract: Abstract—As cellular architectures transition from 5G toward Sixth-Generation (6G) wireless networks, the classical Shannon-Nyquist paradigm of bit-level data transmission is rapidly approaching its theoretical physical channel capacity limits. Ultra-dense Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, autonomous vehicular swarms, and extended reality (XR) telepresence demand terabit-per-second (Tbps) data rates, sub-millisecond latencies, and continuous real-time edge artificial intelligence (AI) inference over severely bandwidth-constrained wireless channels. Classical communications optimize bit error rates (BER), transmitting massive streams of uncompressed binary representations regardless of the underlying computational task. Semantic Communications and Task-Oriented Edge Intelligence establish a transformative paradigm shift: shifting the transmission objective from error-free bit reconstruction to the faithful transmission of actionable semantic meaning and task-relevant latent features. By uniting Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding (Deep JSCC) with transformer-based feature extractors, semantic communication frameworks filter out redundant sensory data at the transmitter, communicatin

title: Edge-AI enabled real-time classroom attentiveness monitoring via facial emotion recognition on Raspberry Pi
abstract: Monitoring student attentiveness in physical classrooms remains a largely manual and subjective process, typically relying on instructor observation, which is neither scalable nor continuous. This paper presents an edge-AI enabled system for real-time classroom attentiveness monitoring using facial emotion recognition deployed entirely on a Raspberry Pi 5, eliminating the need for continuous cloud connectivity or transmission of raw video data. The proposed pipeline captures classroom images at 60-s intervals over a full session, performs on-device face detection using RetinaFace, and classifies detected faces into seven emotion categories using DeepFace. A weighted aggregation scheme maps the resulting class-wide emotion distribution to a normalized per-frame attentiveness score, which is logged locally and subsequently visualized through a cloud-based dashboard for instructor review. The system was evaluated on a self-collected classroom dataset comprising 2 classrooms and 8 sessions with number of students ranging from 60 to 90 in each session. Each session is around 50–55 min. In the proposed system, the face-detection using the RetinaFace achieved an accuracy of 95.67%, compar

title: A Personalized Edge AI Framework for Adaptive Driver Fatigue Monitoring and Alert Escalation
abstract: This research presents a Personalized Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework for real-time driver fatigue monitoring and adaptive alert escalation. The study addresses two key limitations of existing vision-based driver monitoring systems: the use of fixed detection thresholds that may not account for individual differences in facial characteristics, and the reliance on single-level alerts that do not reflect the severity of driver drowsiness. The proposed framework integrates facial landmark detection, Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR), Mouth Aspect Ratio (MAR), lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and per-driver calibration to improve fatigue detection reliability. Designed for edge deployment, the system processes camera input locally, reducing dependence on cloud connectivity while supporting real-time performance and enhanced privacy. An adaptive, multi-level alert mechanism maps estimated drowsiness severity to graduated warnings, ranging from low-risk notifications to critical intervention alerts. The research adopts a mixed-methods approach combining a structured literature review with a proposed controlled comparative experiment. It evaluates the framework against c

title: Capacity over TFLOPS: Memory-Centric Deployment of Large Clinical Language Models on Consumer CPUs
abstract: The dominant barrier to running large clinical language models at the point of care is not arithmetic throughput but graphics memory: consumer GPUs cap at 4-16 GB, while the working set of a 27-billion-parameter model in 4-bit precision is 17-25 GB. We argue that the edge node should be treated as capacity-enabled (system RAM) rather than compute-limited (GPU VRAM), and we test this on commodity hardware. Using an INT4 build of a 27B open model as an architecture-faithful stand-in for a 27B medical model, we measure the memory footprint, inference latency, energy, and federated communication cost of a fully CPU-based pipeline driven by synthetic Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) prompts. On two independent consumer machines (a desktop-class machine with 67 GB of RAM and a 6 GB GPU, and a mobile workstation with 34 GB of RAM and a 4 GB GPU) the model loads entirely into system RAM (37% and 60% utilization, respectively) while both GPUs are out-of-memory before the first step. Inference runs at overnight-batch speed (0.6-2.4 tokens/s for the 27B model), and federated fine-tuning would transmit only a 22.6 MB low-rank adapter, a 99.96% reduction over full weights. The

title: A surface defect detection and semantic reasoning framework with a cloud-edge-terminal system for industrial scenarios with zero real defect samples via large–small model and Human-AI collaboration
PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKING OF EMBEDDED EDGE DEVICES FOR VARIOUS FACE RECOGNITION MODELS
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) models are increasingly pivotal in enabling face recognition across various fields, from educational and research settings to public spaces.Effective deployment of these models requires high-performance hardware, such as RTX graphics cards or embedded edge devices like Nvidia's AGX Orin and Jetson Nano.This paper presents a comprehensive benchmarking study comparing the performance of these two devices, representing high and low-power edge computing options, using two face recognition models: ResNet and MobileNet.The benchmarking process assesses each model across two different input sizes deployed on both devices with varied configurations, including CPU thread allocation and GPU power distribution within containerized environments.Performance metrics such as inference time, GPU utilization, memory usage, and CPU load are analyzed to determine each device's suitability and efficiency.Additionally, model-specific parameters, including FLOPS, parameter count, and memory footprint, are examined to provide for an in-depth comparison.This paper presents detailed results and analyses of these performance indicators.

title: Cloud-Based Infrastructure for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Workloads: A Scalable Framework for Saudi Enterprises
abstract: In Saudi companies artificial intelligence and machine learning are moving from being mere experiments to becoming operational capabilities, which is leading to an infrastructure issue that goes well beyond the need for computing power. The processes involved in training, fine-tuning, inference, feature preparation, model monitoring, governance and retraining all have diverse requirements for accelerators, storage, networking, data locality, elasticity and reliability. This review draws on research carried out between 2020 and 2025 in order to look at how cloud architecture can support these types of workloads on an enterprise level while taking into account the Saudi situation regarding rapid digital transformation, the adoption of cloud services, data governance and the modernisation of various sectors. The review applies a structured evidence-synthesis approach focused on infrastructure architecture, workload orchestration, MLOps, cloud-edge distribution, security, reliability, cost control and organisational readiness. The evidence shows that scalable AI infrastructure should be viewed as a coordinated platform rather than as a set of separate services; effective designs incorp

title: BENCHMARKING 2D AND 3D OBJECT DETECTION MODELS ON DIFFERENT EDGE COMPUTING PLATFORMS
abstract: The deployment of artificial intelligence models on edge computing platforms is imperative for applications necessitating real-time perception, including object detection and gesture recognition.This paper presents a thoroughgoing benchmarking study of 2D and 3D convolutional neural network models across a range of representative edge devices, including the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, Jetson Nano, and Raspberry Pi 3. The study utilizes gesture recognition and mask detection as the primary use cases for evaluating the performance of these models.We evaluated the inference time, memory footprint, and power consumption under varying input resolutions and sequence lengths, thereby capturing the latency-accuracy-energy trade-offs that govern practical deployment.The results show that AGX Orin consistently handles highdemand scenarios with low latency and stable throughput, whereas Jetson Nano offers competitive efficiency in energy-constrained settings.Raspberry Pi 3, while limited, establishes a useful baseline for CPU-only operation and highlights optimization needs.We also examined the effects of quantization and runtime optimizations and reported configurations that deliver robust perfo

title: Energy-efficient deep learning-based vibration monitoring on parallel ultra-low-power microcontrollers
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) through vibration analysis is essential for ensuring safety, reliability, and minimized maintenance costs in sensor-connected environments. Realizing this at the extreme edge, directly on sensor nodes, requires advanced data analytics, ultra-energy-efficient hardware, and high-fidelity datasets. This paper addresses these challenges by developing an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based deep learning framework for vibration-based structural health monitoring tailored to resource-constrained devices. We present a benchmarking dataset for vibration SHM, encompassing nine abnormal conditions that capture narrowband structural anomalies. Leveraging this dataset, we design supervised and unsupervised deep-learning models, integrating a system identification (SysId) preprocessing stage to derive structurally informed features that enhance model input quality. This improves algorithmic results while boosting hardware performances. These models are deployed on a parallel ultra-low-power microcontroller with dedicated hardware acceleration. Our unsupervised anomaly detectors deliver 89.90 percent (%) accuracy, 4.1 percentage points higher than the state-of-th

title: Resource-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Compact LLMs for Supply Chain Operations: A Hybrid QLoRA and RAG Approach
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer transformative potential for enterprise automation, particularly within the highly complex and data-dense environments of transportation, supply chain management, and intralogistics. However, deploying foundational models in these specialized domains frequently results in a critical failure mode: confident generative hallucinations regarding company-specific, highly proprietary operational protocols. Furthermore, adapting these massive models typically requires prohibitive computational resources, placing them fundamentally out of reach for regional distribution hubs and mid-sized enterprises constrained by strict hardware budgets. This paper investigates the hypothesis that a compact, instruction-tuned Small Language Model (SLM) can be aggressively fine-tuned and semantically grounded to provide highly accurate, factually bound supply chain support while operating entirely within the constraints of a single commodity GPU. This research presents the end-to-end development, optimization, and deployment of IndustryGPT, a highly specialized logistics LLM. title: Deep Learning and Artificial Intelligence: Conceptual Foundations of Pattern Recognition and Security Applications
abstract: The rapid growth of digital data and the increasing complexity of security threats have expanded the use of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning in modern security systems. This chapter presents the conceptual foundations of deep learning and pattern recognition and examines their roles in security-oriented applications. It first clarifies the relationships among artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, and pattern recognition, emphasizing the transition from manually engineered features to representation learning through multilayer neural networks. Fundamental mechanisms of deep learning, including artificial neurons, activation functions, forward propagation, backpropagation, loss functions, and hierarchical representation learning, are subsequently discussed. The chapter also reviews major deep learning architectures, including Multilayer Perceptrons, Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Autoencoders, and Transformers, with particular attention to their suitability for different data types and security problems. Their applications are examined in the context of intrusion detection, ano

title: Queue-Aware Token Communications: Bridging AI Representation and Wireless Service
abstract: The rapid advancement of foundation models and edge intelligence is transforming wireless networks from data-oriented communication systems into artificial intelligence (AI)-native service platforms. Token communications (TokenCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm that directly transmits task-oriented AI representations. However, existing studies typically assume that generated tokens can be transmitted immediately, overlooking the queueing dynamics arising from the mismatch between token workload generation and time-varying wireless service capability. To address this limitation, we introduce Queue-Aware TokenCom, which explicitly incorporates token queues into the AI service pipeline. We present an end-to-end architecture integrating AI representation generation, token workload management, wireless transmission, and downstream task inference. We then discuss two key design directions: budget-aware token representation optimization and queue-aware token service optimization, with the token budget serving as a critical interface between AI performance and communication efficiency. Moreover, we investigate fixed and adaptive token budget strategies to characterize the fundamental

title: Space AI Infrastructure: Where the Edge Meets the Orbital Cloud
abstract: The fusion of artificial intelligence (AI) and space technologies is extending spaceborne intelligence beyond onboard payloads toward a global infrastructure, here termed Space AI infrastructure (SpaceAI-Infra). Its promise rests on two distinctive advantages of space systems: abundant solar energy in orbit and the global reach of satellite constellations. Realizing this promise hinges on a fundamental systems question: How should satellite constellations be designed and orchestrated to deliver data-center-scale AI services competitive with their terrestrial counterparts? This article develops a roadmap-oriented answer. We first chart the evolution of SpaceAI-Infra through three progressive stages: onboard AI, Space Edge AI, and Space Cloud AI. By revisiting the space-constrained fundamentals for end-to-end token services, we derive enabling design principles and translate them into an integrated space edge--cloud architecture. The communication-centric space edge comprises free-flying LEO constellations that provide user-proximate computing and form the access and backhaul fabric for cloud AI services. title: Hardware‐Native Gaussian Sampling With Probabilistic Ising Machines for Modern Communication Paradigms
abstract: Modern communication systems increasingly shift computation to edge devices, where post quantum signing, generative AI and semantic communication must operate under strict energy, latency and memory constraints. A central bottleneck in these workloads is Gaussian sampling. In Falcon class signatures, sampling accounts for about 25% of operations and about 65% of signing time. In diffusion inference, repeated Gaussian injection across denoising steps makes edge deployment costly. Here we show that probabilistic Ising machines provide a hardware native route to random Gaussian distributions with both tunable variance and sampling density with two independent parameters. We compare fully digital field-programmable gate array (FPGA) and FPGA-spintronic implementations with software implementation. At matched sampling precision, the proposed FPGA sampler reduces the dynamic power and logic utilization of the Gaussian-sampling core by approximately 4.0-fold and 4.4-fold, respectively, relative to the isolated Falcon core. A projected ASIC implementation in 28 nm CMOS is estimated to consume approximately 8 mW. Image generation quality quantified with well-established metrics is preserved

title: Smart Camera Traps in the Field: A Scoping Review of Architecture and Energy Evidence
abstract: Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) is used in wildlife monitoring to reduce communication demand, support decision-making, and enable energy-aware operation, yet embedded inference alone does not establish whether a system can sustain useful service after installation. This scoping review searched four bibliographic databases through 5 August 2026 and complemented these searches with studies identified from prior work on the topic, identifying 41 eligible English-language papers published from 2021 onward on camera-primary intelligent wildlife systems. The review aimed to assess operational maturity, field-validated operational role, energy evidence, and operational continuity. Full texts were charted and analyzed across sensing, decision-making, communication, response, energy, and continuity. Post-installation evidence exposed triggering, environmental, connectivity, maintenance, and energy-supply constraints not established through non-field evaluation. title: Exposing AI Inference as a Telco Network API over the 5G User Plane
abstract: Supporting edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) inference as a network service is challenging because current mobile systems can transport tensors but do not expose or understand the inference context that gives those tensors operational meaning. Prior studies have addressed this gap through dynamic partitioning, collaborative inference, and split pipelines; however, these solutions remain application-bound, network-blind, or context-free. This work proposes Inference on Demand (IoD), an inference-on-demand abstraction that exposes split inference through a CAMARA-like Application Program Interface (API) and carries a split-aware tensor context in-band across the 5G user plane path. We evaluate the IoD on a programmable user plane function (UPF)-based testbed using a partitionable visual AI workload, showing that adaptive split selection can operate as a network-facing service while avoiding the rigid cost profile of static configurations. Including our findings, split inference becomes more than offloading when the service intent, runtime partitioning, and tensor transport are made visible to the mobile data plane. title: An Embedded AI Vision System for Real-Time Object Classification in PLC-Based Industrial Automation
abstract: This paper presents an integrated embedded vision and edge artificial intelligence (AI) solution for a programmable logic controller (PLC) that does not officially support modules for AI applications. The proposed method employs image processing and artificial neural network (ANN) training and inference directly on a cost-effective ESP32-P4 microcontroller, facilitating advanced perception capabilities at the edge without necessitating expensive hardware. A PLC is used as the main controller to manage data acquisition, model development, training, making predictions, and running the system using specially designed function blocks and Modbus TCP/IP communication. Color-based classification of bell peppers on a conveyor belt is used as a representative application to validate the proposed system. Visual information is encoded using hue spectra extracted from camera images, which retained relatively stable performance under the tested illumination shift. The ANN model is first trained using a large set of images collected beforehand and then adjusted on the device with real samples taken directly from the conveyor system, using a transfer learning approach. title: Big data and AI for decision-making purposes in the metaverse: A cross-domain review of architectures, applications, and governance
abstract: This review examines how big data and artificial intelligence are being mobilized to support decision-making in metaverse and metaverse-adjacent environments. Rather than treating the metaverse as an interface novelty, the paper frames it as a decision environment in which persistent interaction, embodied participation, and multimodal sensing tighten the loop between observation and intervention. Using a transparent narrative review approach, the synthesis applies a consistent decision-making taxonomy across nine domains (industrial and manufacturing operations, smart cities, healthcare, retail and commerce, supply chain and logistics, energy and utilities, finance, education, tourism). For each domain, evidence is organized around decision level, decision mode, time requirements, data context, and action type, enabling comparability without collapsing domain-specific consequences into a single maturity scale. Across domains, the most salient pattern is that decision value depends less on immersion itself and more on the integration of digital representations (often via digital twins), AI inference, and bounded action pathways. title: Smart Agriculture and Environmental Monitoring: An Edge-AI, IoT, and Federated Learning Framework for Climate-Resilient Farming
abstract: This study presents a system architecture, algorithm, and evaluation protocol for smart agriculture and environmental monitoring. It is a method/architecture contribution and does not report field trial results. World food production is still under stress from climate variability, the availability of freshwater resources, and the cost of farm inputs, offering an incentive to transition to data-driven and sensor-based farm management practices. Internet of Things (IoT)-based agricultural monitoring is well developed, but most systems deployed focus on a single parameter (e.g., soil moisture) or the parameter is inferred solely in the cloud, adding latency and fragility to the deployment of systems in rural areas. In this study, we propose an integrated architecture for low-power multiparameter environmental sensing, LoRaWAN/NB-IoT connectivity, edge-based lightweight inference, and privacy-preserving federated learning with cross-farm model aggregation, which is further complemented by a digital twin layer for scenario simulation. Applying Deep Learning to Image and IMU Sensor Data for Real-Time Fatigue Recognition in Table Tennis Players
abstract: Fatigue during table tennis training can impair performance and increase the risk of injury. This study proposes a real-time fatigue recognition system that integrates an embedded edge-AI racket with a camera for synchronized multimodal data acquisition. On the racket side, a neural network was deployed on an edge-AI microcontroller unit (MCU) to enable on-device inference, while the test data were transmitted to a computer for multimodal feature fusion. Given the continuous nature of fatigue development, the data were divided into three stages: non-fatigue, transition, and fatigue to facilitate progressive evaluation. In the binary classification task, which distinguished between the two extreme states, the multimodal hybrid model achieved an accuracy of 99%. When the transition stage was incorporated into a three-class classification task, performance declined because of the ambiguous boundaries between fatigue states. However, the use of multimodal decision-fusion strategies, such as weighted soft voting, maintained an accuracy of 96%. title: MetaGPT: An Immersive Mixed Reality AI Assistant via Offline Edge-Deployed Multi-Agent Vision-Language Inference
Photonic convolution neural networks for machine learning via energy-free Fourier-optics
abstract: Convolutional operations are computationally intensive in artificial intelligence (AI) services, and their overhead in electronic hardware limits machine learning scaling. Here, we introduce a photonic joint transform correlator (pJTC) using a near-energy-free on-chip Fourier transformation to accelerate convolution operations. The pJTC reduces computational complexity for both convolution and cross-correlation from O(N^4) to O(N^2) , where N2 is the input data size. Demonstrating functional Fourier transforms and convolution, this pJTC achieves 98.0% accuracy on an exemplary Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology inference task. Furthermore, a wavelength-multiplexed pJTC architecture shows potential for high throughput and energy efficiency, reaching 305 TOPS/W and 40.2 TOPS/mm^2, based on currently available foundry processes. An efficient, compact, and low-latency convolution accelerator promises to advance next-generation AI capabilities across edge demands, high-performance computing, and cloud services.

title: Characterising On-Device AI Failure Modes Under Joint Fault Injection and Runtime Observability
abstract: Deploying artificial intelligence models directly on edge devices exposes machine learning runtimes to hardware volatile environments, including thermal limits, volatile system memory pressure, and corrupted input data. While previous work evaluates software-level fault injection and runtime observability in isolation, no empirical study has applied fault injection and high-frequency device tracing in a combined pipeline across heterogeneous model architectures. We present a joint empirical study combining SATE AI (software-level fault injection) and EdgePulse (non-intrusive runtime observability) on a physical Android handset (Tecno CH7n, MediaTek Helio G35, Android 12). Across a benchmark suite of 280 real-device inference traces covering three model runtimes (TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime, and llama.cpp GGUF) and four execution scenarios (baseline, memory pressure, malformed input, and thermal stress), we demonstrate three principal findings: 1.
