title: Integrated Feasibility Assessment of Edge, Cloud, and Hybrid AI-as-a-Service Architectures for Face Recognition
abstract: Deploying face recognition as a service requires evidence beyond recognition accuracy because architecture affects latency, scalability, cost, and biometric-data exposure. This study evaluates Edge, Cloud, and Hybrid architectures through an integrated technical, techno-economic, and regulatory-readiness framework. EdgeCloudSim experiments modeled 100–500 connected devices using an infrastructure-level workload abstraction structurally mapped to published face-recognition pipelines, while explicitly distinguishing this abstraction from direct neural-inference benchmarking. The technical screening thresholds were treated as scenario-specific engineering gates and evaluated through threshold sensitivity analysis. A five-year comparative cash-flow model applied the same modeled avoided operating-cost benefit to all architectures. At 500 devices, Hybrid produced 2.2066 s processing time, 16.736% failed tasks, and 0.1355 s total latency; its failure rate was lower than Edge (27.797%) and Cloud (22.137%). Under the common economic-benefit scenario, Edge and Cloud generated negative NPVs of IDR 982.50 million and IDR 247.25 million, respectively, whereas Hybrid generated an NPV of IDR 958

title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
abstract: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model genera

title: EdgePulse: A Runtime Observability Framework for Quantized Large Language Models on Consumer Edge Devices
abstract: On-device AI execution lacks unified runtime observability across mobile platforms. Existing tools focus on isolated model profiling or single-engine metrics and give no synchronized view of memory, thermal state, battery draw, and inference latency during real workloads. We present EdgePulse, an open-source runtime observability framework for on-device AI. EdgePulse captures structured InferenceTrace telemetry on Android (Kotlin) and iOS (Swift) via native platform channels: resident memory via Debug.getPss(), OS thermal state via PowerManager.currentThermalStatus, battery current draw via BatteryManager.CURRENT_NOW, CPU utilization from /proc/stat, and per-inference latency. We evaluate EdgePulse through a real-device empirical study on a physical Tecno CH7n (MediaTek Helio G35, 4 GB RAM, Android 12, API 31) across three runtimes: TFLite (MobileNet-V3-Small), ONNX Runtime (ResNet18), and GGUF/llama.cpp (TinyLlama 1.1B Q4). Analyzing 90 baseline traces and 60 sustained-load traces reveals: baseline mean latency varied 12× across runtimes (148 ms to 1,779 ms); sustained MobileNet inference over 15 minutes showed no degradation; sustained TinyLlama decoding produced a +16.5% latency

title: Stochastic Modeling and Resource Dimensioning of Multi-Cellular Edge Intelligent Systems
abstract: Edge intelligence enables the execution of AI inference tasks on computing platforms at the network edge, typically co-located with or near the radio access network rather than in centralized clouds or on mobile devices. This approach is particularly well suited for data analytics of low-latency and resource-constrained applications, where large data volumes and stringent latency constraints require tight integration of wireless access and on-site computational resources. However, the performance and cost-efficiency of such systems fundamentally depend on the joint dimensioning of wireless and computational resources prior to deployment, specially amid spatial and temporal uncertainties. Prior works largely emphasize run-time resource allocation or employ simplified network models that decouple radio access from computing infrastructure, overlooking end-to-end correlations in large-scale deployments. This paper introduces a unified stochastic framework for dimensioning multi-cellular edge-intelligent systems. We model network topology via a Poisson point process to capture randomness in user and base-station locations, incorporating inter-cell interference, distance-proportional fr

title: Predictive Maintenance for Bird Feeder Motors via Time-Series Current Analysis
abstract: Automated outdoor electronic device systems have been deployed widely for their high efficiency. However, environmental vulnerabilities could be a severe issue. To be more specific, high humidity outdoors causes feed agglomeration, therefore leading to fatal problems like mechanical jamming and motor burnout. According to current techniques, although deep learning model achieves the high accuracy of diagnosis, the heavy load is not suitable for a low-cost edge artificial intelligence (AI) controller. At the same time, traditional signal processing methods based on threshold values can easily cause false alarms in a noisy environment. This paper adopts lightweight sensorless predictive maintenance method, combining it with the motor current characteristic analysis (MCSA) and random forest classifier, and extracting the variance and peak amplitude features via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) in the frequency domain. The result shows that by this method, the accuracy on the test data is up to 96.80%, which is superior to the standard deep neural network (89.30%) and maintains an extremely low inference latency, which is suitable for edge AI deployment.

title: Edge AI-Enabled Smart Textiles for Real-Time Healthcare Monitoring
abstract: Smart textiles, flexible electronics and Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) are enabling wearable healthcare systems to evolve from basic sensing platforms to smart decision-making ecosystems. In this chapter we discuss the design and implementation of AI-enabled e-textiles for continuous physiological monitoring, real-time analytics and personalized health interventions. Particular focus is given to TinyML and Edge AI frameworks that allow inference on devices, thereby reducing latency, improving privacy and reducing reliance on cloud infrastructure. The chapter discusses applications such as heart rate monitoring, electrocardiogram analysis, respiratory assessment, stress detection, activity recognition, and management of chronic diseases. In this chapter, we provide a comprehensive roadmap for researchers, engineers and healthcare practitioners who want to develop next-generation intelligent textile systems that can deliver ubiquitous, personalized and real-time healthcare services

title: CrashSenseAI: latency-aware edge AI system for real-time traffic accident detection and notification
abstract: Road accidents remain a critical public safety issue, where detection often depends on witnesses calling authorities, leading to delays of several minutes before police and ambulances are dispatched. This study presents CrashSenseAI (CSAI), an Edge artificial intelligence (Edge AI) accident detection and notification system built on You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) and YOLOv12 models. Using a labeled dataset of accident and non-accident images, we trained Nano, Small, and Medium variants with batch sizes of 16 and 32 to evaluate accuracy–latency trade-offs. Results show YOLOv12n achieved the lowest inference latency (3.6–3.7 ms) with high precision (0.89), while YOLOv8s provided the best balance of accuracy and efficiency (Recall 0.85, Precision 0.90, mean average precision (mAP) at an Intersection over Union threshold of 0.5 (mAP@0.5 = 0.89) and mAP@0.5–0.95 = 0.70) at 4.8–5.0 ms. Larger variants improved mAP@0.5 scores (up to 0.90) but incurred higher latency (11–14 ms). A Scientific Hypothesis on the Lion's Roar Vocal Practice for Lower-Jiao Coldness: A First-Person Cognitive Archive and Its Spontaneous Convergence with Neurophenomenology
abstract: Functional symptoms related to "lower-jiao coldness" (e.g., primary dysmenorrhea, chronic pelvic pain) present a therapeutic challenge due to the limitations of reductionist approaches. This paper proposes a testable hypothesis: traditional Lion's Roar vocalization induces synergistic contraction of the diaphragm, abdominal wall, and pelvic floor muscles, producing rhythmic visceral massage to improve microcirculation and reset central set-points. Crucially, this paper transcends a conventional medical hypothesis. It presents a first-person cognitive archive and a radical meta-methodology: the hypothesis was not generated within a traditional academic institution, but was spontaneously formulated by an independent Chinese non-medical researcher, relying on first-person interoception, Eastern holistic cognition, and AI-assisted collaboration. We document the authentic cognitive evolution: the AI initially failed to retrieve literature on neurophenomenology, interoceptive active inference, and embodied cognition—the very frontiers of modern neuroscience. title: iBTEC: A tiny deep learning approach for indoor temperature and occupancy prediction in Smart Buildings
abstract: Maintaining thermal comfort while ensuring energy efficiency is a critical challenge in modern buildings. Smart Buildings (SBs) address this issue by integrating interconnected sensors and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to automate systems such as heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC), lighting, and water heating. However, achieving optimal HVAC control demands precise predictive modeling to effectively balance occupant comfort and energy consumption. In response, this paper introduces the Intelligent Building Thermal-Energy Controller (iBTEC), an innovative solution utilizing a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) enhanced by modern pruning techniques. The proposed iBTEC simultaneously predicts indoor temperature and occupancy, treating temperature prediction as a regression problem and occupancy prediction as a classification problem. To facilitate efficient deployment at the network edge and align with the principles of Green AI, this work employs two pruning strategies aimed at producing a lightweight model suitable for resource-constrained environments. These pruning techniques are justified as a means to make the approach greener, reducing computational overhea

title: Protecting CPU AI On Edge TEEs: WebAssembly's Promise and Practical Challenges
abstract: AI models on edge hardware contain important intellectual property (IP), but an adversary can steal it when they achieve root access. Trusted Execution Environments (TEE) like Arm TrustZone protect against these Operating System (OS) level attacks. However, they are challenging to use. More precisely, it is difficult to run unaltered applications inside a TEE. This work presents a solution that allows the execution of unaltered AI models, compiled to WebAssembly, on the WebAssembly Micro Runtime (WAMR) in OP-TEE for Arm TrustZone. Additionally, this work provides an AI model distributor that encrypts the WebAssembly binary and places the encryption key in one of the device's fuses. This way, only the WAMR Trusted Application (TA) in OP-TEE can decrypt and execute the AI model. A thorough evaluation of our solution shows that it incurs an additional overhead of 22% in comparison to an application manually ported to OP-TEE, while also facilitating the execution of unaltered AI models with an additional inference latency of 6% without significant porting effort. Overall, there is a pressing need to safeguard the IP of AI models and this work shows that there is a real promise in WebAs

title: RAPID-DNN: Reliability-Aware Partitioning for Robust DNN Inference Deployment on Edge AI
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) deployed on heterogeneous edge accelerators are increasingly exposed to runtime hardware faults. Tight power and resource budgets push these platforms toward aggressive voltage scaling and limit the use of hardware fault mitigation, while process variation, thermal stress, and device aging raise fault rates further. The resulting transient bit level corruptions propagate through inference and can sharply reduce prediction accuracy. Existing DNN partitioning frameworks optimize latency and energy under fault free assumptions, so their deployment strategies often fail to sustain reliable inference in realistic operating conditions. This paper presents RAPID DNN, a reliability aware partitioning framework that adds runtime reliability as a third optimization objective alongside latency and energy. RAPID DNN first characterizes layer wise reliability through systematic fault injection in the weight and activation domains to identify vulnerability critical layers. The resulting sensitivity profile guides a three objective NSGA II optimizer that jointly minimizes inference latency, energy consumption, and expected fault induced accuracy degradation. We evaluat

title: EcoTrust-Net: A Causal, Explainable, and Energy-Aware Graph Transformer and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Intelligent Network Traffic Prediction and Optimization
abstract: The increasing complexity of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems, Software-Defined Networking (SDN), edge intelligence, cloud-native infrastructures, and Internet of Things (IoT) environments has intensified the need for intelligent network traffic prediction and optimization capable of supporting low latency, high throughput, cyber-resilience, explainability, and energy-efficient operation. Existing approaches often address traffic prediction, routing optimization, explainability, or energy efficiency independently, resulting in limited topology awareness, weak causal interpretation, and reduced adaptability in highly dynamic communication environments. To address these limitations, this study proposes EcoTrust-Net, a causal, explainable, and energy-aware framework that integrates Graph Transformer-based topologyaware traffic prediction, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for adaptive routing and congestion control, Structural Causal Modeling (SCM) for causal inference and counterfactual reasoning, SHAP- and attention-based explainability, and multi-objective energy-aware optimization within a unified architecture. title: AI-Enabled Sustainable Precision Farming Using Raspberry Pi and Coral Edge TPU with Cloud-Based Model Training
abstract: Precision Agriculture requires intelligent, adaptable and efficient technology that is capable of making decisions in agriculture at the right time, based on the condition of the plants and the environment. This paper proposes the development of an AI-based sustainable precision farming system based on computer vision, cloud based model training, Raspberry Pi, Coral Edge TPU and the Internet of Things (IoT) sensing. The proposed architecture's sensing layer, edge processing layer, cloud intelligence layer, and application layer enables a complete data processing pipeline from the field to real time decision support. Crop photos are collected for AI condition classification and agricultural conditions such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity and light intensity are collected by built-in sensors. After the above preprocessing, normalisation, image resizing and augmentation, the dataset is divided into training, validation and test sets. The trained deep learning models in a cloud environment are then quantized and converted to be optimized for the edge, following this step. Following this step, the trained deep learning models are quantized and converted for optimization on edge.

title: AI-Driven Threat Detection Architecture
abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital infrastructure, spanning cloud computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), edge networks, and mobile platforms, has dramatically expanded the attack surface available to cybercriminals. Traditional signature-based intrusion detection systems, while effective against known threats, are fundamentally inadequate in the face of zero-day exploits, advanced persistent threats (APTs), encrypted malicious traffic, and evolving ransomware campaigns. This chapter presents a comprehensive examination of AI-driven threat detection architectures as the next-generation response to these escalating cybersecurity challenges. It explores the full spectrum of the threat landscape, encompassing DDoS attacks, botnets, APTs, and cloud-specific vulnerabilities, before detailing the layered architectural framework through which AI-based detection systems operate, from raw data collection at the network and endpoint layer, through preprocessing and feature extraction, to model inference and automated response. A range of machine learning and deep learning methodologies is evaluated, including supervised classifiers such as decision trees, random forests, k-nearest neighbors

title: Cost-Aware and Self-Validating Multi-Agent Engineering of Computer-Vision Pipelines: An Optimization-Based Framework with Applications to Remote-Sensing Image Analysis
abstract: Remote-sensing image analysis increasingly requires workflows that combine heterogeneous sensors, geospatial preprocessing, deep-learning models, uncertainty estimation, and domain-specific quality control. Conventional computer-vision pipelines are commonly designed manually, making them expensive to develop, difficult to reproduce, and inflexible when sensor quality or task requirements change. Recent agentic-AI systems have demonstrated the feasibility of automatically planning and executing computer-vision and AutoML workflows, but computational cost, geospatial validity, recovery behavior, and provenance remain insufficiently integrated. This paper proposes COSA-CV, a Cost-aware and Self-validating Agentic Computer-Vision framework for automated engineering of remote-sensing image-analysis pipelines. COSA-CV consists of specialized agents for task interpretation, dataset auditing, remote-sensing context analysis, pipeline planning, model and tool routing, image preprocessing, inference, post-processing, validation, error diagnosis, recovery, uncertainty estimation, cost monitoring, and report generation. title: Computational intelligence enabled hardware software co design for energy efficient Edge Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Abstract Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) facilitates efficient and high-speed inference by making use of its ability to process data in-device without depending on an external server. Despite its promising possibilities, its deployment still faces many obstacles due to limited computing capacity, memory size, power consumption, and the variety of hardware platforms used at the edge. Thus, this article provides structured narrative review of the latest breakthroughs achieved in the development of energy-efficient Edge AI, focusing specifically on hardware-software co-design practices aimed at improving inference quality. The analysis involves studying state-of-the-art Edge AI hardware infrastructures based on microcontrollers, FPGAs, GPUs, NPUs, ASICs, and some new architectures that utilize in-memory computing, as well as applying various techniques for improving software performance such as model compression, quantization, pruning, neuromorphic computing and techniques applied during compiling, executing, and allocating workloads. title: An Edge-Intelligent Framework for Multi-Class Ocular Disease Detection using Optimized Transfer Learning Models
abstract: Millions of people worldwide lose vision to conditions that, if caught early, are treatable, yet specialized eye care remains out of reach for many low-resource regions. This work presents an edge-deployed AI framework built to classify multiple eye diseases directly on embedded hardware, closing that access gap. Eight deep learning architectures were benchmarked on a public fundus image dataset spanning four categories (normal, cataract, glaucoma, and diabetic retinopathy): VGG16, ResNet-50, Inception V3, DenseNet-169, ConvNeXt, Vision Transformer, Swin Transformer, and a CNN-Transformer hybrid (HybridVisionNet). DenseNet-169 achieved the highest test accuracy with 97.16%, ahead of ConvNeXt (96.21%), ViT (95.02%), HybridVisionNet (94.79%), Swin Transformer (92.56%), Inception V3 (90.52%), ResNet-50 (89.73%), and VGG16 (89.26%). This model was then ported to an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and optimized with TensorRT using FP16/INT8 quantization. abstract: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Ambient Cognitive Intelligence and Sovereign Distributed Systems (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23205028) unifies 43 AI/IoT/NLP domains into a sovereign cognitive ecosystem. abstract: Context & Educational Focus: This open educational resource provides an analytical and systems-level foundation in industrial energy and resource efficiency for advanced undergraduate and pre-university engineering curricula. It addresses the operational imperative of eliminating hidden energy dissipation, material scrap, and thermal inefficiencies while maintaining production throughput and product quality. title: Deployment of Optimised Brain Tumour Segmentation Model on ZCU104 FPGA Using Xilinx Vitis AI
abstract: Brain tumour segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging requires accurate delineation of sub-regions under clinical constraints on computational resources. Deploying deep segmentation networks on edge hardware demands model optimisation that preserves accuracy while reducing complexity. This paper presents the deployment of a pruned RAAGR2-Net brain tumour segmentation model on the Xilinx ZCU104 FPGA using the Vitis AI 3.0 toolchain. The model was optimised through sensitivity-guided channel pruning, which suppresses channels identified as redundant while maintaining segmentation stability. The pruned model was trained and evaluated on the BraTS 2019 dataset. At a pruning ratio of 0.1, the pruned model achieved Dice scores of 0.8578, 0.8131, and 0.8635 for tumour core, enhancing tumour, and whole tumour respectively, compared to 0.8169, 0.7896, and 0.8424 for the base model. The deployment further serves as a verification step, confirming that suppressed channels do not contribute to inference on hardware before structural removal is applied. title: Comparative evaluation of artificial intelligence-integrated and conventional camera traps for small mammal monitoring
abstract: Context Conventional camera traps generate vast amounts of non-target images that makes edge artificial intelligence (AI) cameras a promising solution for real-time species detection. However, the real-world effectiveness of these systems depends heavily on how models generalise from training to unpredictable field conditions. Aims We test whether within-distribution validation accuracy predicts field deployment performance for edge-deployed object detection models by examining how training-dataset background composition affects field generalisation for small mammal detection, and compare AI-integrated and conventional camera-trap detection outcomes under matched field conditions. Methods We conducted a field-based comparison between an AI-integrated camera system (MaixCAM-Pro running YOLOv11n) and a conventional trail camera (Hawkray HC-900A) for small mammal monitoring. Three object-detection models were evaluated based on training datasets with different background compositions: heterogeneous varied backgrounds (Model A), uniform white backgrounds (Model B) and a combined dataset integrating both (Model C). Practical Research on a BERT-Based Domain Knowledge Question Answering System
abstract: Domain knowledge question answering (QA) systems face practical constraints in offline operation, data sovereignty, and long-term invocation costs. Current mainstream approaches tend to adopt large-scale generative models; however, this paper argues that for domain-specific tasks, the majority of parameters in large models encode general-purpose linguistic knowledge, while the effective parameters actually serving the target domain constitute a negligible proportion, resulting in significant model redundancy. Focusing on marine domain knowledge services and building upon edge-side large language model (LLM) experiments, this work returns to a discriminative architecture, adopting a "text classification + preset answers" paradigm using bert-base-chinese with approximately 102M parameters to build an offline-deployable QA system. Initial experiments on domestic ARM development boards compared Ollama CPU inference with RKLLM NPU inference, revealing limitations of edge-side LLMs in latency, hallucination, and resource consumption, which motivated the shift to the BERT classification approach. title: Resource-aware residential load forecasting: A cross-platform evaluation on embedded edge devices
abstract: This work presents a systematic, deployment-oriented evaluation of residential power demand forecasting models on resource-constrained embedded edge devices. In comparison to previous work, this study jointly analyzes forecasting performance, memory footprint, inference latency, and directly measured on-device energy consumption. A unified experimental pipeline is introduced, including data preprocessing, model training, validation, conversion and quantization, platform-specific deployment, and high-resolution oscilloscope-based energy measurement under controlled conditions. Four representative forecasting approaches, including autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), feed-forward neural networks (FFNN), convolutional neural networks (CNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), are systematically evaluated across varying model architectures, depths, and quantization levels on multiple embedded platforms, including Arduino UNO R4 WiFi, ESP32, and Google Coral Micro. The results demonstrate that forecasting accuracy is strongly influenced by dataset characteristics rather than model complexity alone. title: Artificial Intelligence in Additive Manufacturing: A Critical Review of Methods, Applications and Industrial Challenges
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) has grown from a rapid-prototyping tool into a legitimate production technology, yet its broader industrial adoption continues to be constrained by process variability, stochastic defect formation, and the near-impossibility of mapping complex Process Structure Property (PSP) relationships through conventional experimental methods. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as the primary technical response to these constraints, offering data-driven pathways to optimize parameters, detect anomalies in real time, and reduce development lead times substantially. This review examines AI integration across the complete AM workflow: generative design and topology optimization in the pre-processing stage; surrogate modeling, Bayesian optimization, and reinforcement learning (RL) during the build stage; convolutional neural network (CNN)-based in-situ monitoring and sensor fusion for quality assurance; and AI-enhanced Digital Twins (DTs) for post-process certification. title: DETERMINISTIC AI FOR SOVEREIGN DEVELOPMENT, The Sub-Saharan Case: When the Grid, the Cloud, and the Connectivity Are All Foreign
abstract: The World Bank's 2026 Africa's Pulse reports that Sub-Saharan Africa's growth held at 4.1%in 2025 and is projected at 4.3% in 2026, despite mounting debt service burdens, limitedfiscal space, and high energy and transport costs. It identifies artificial intelligence as anopportunity for productivity and job creation, but notes that adoption remains uneven. The binding constraints it names are connectivity, energy cost, fiscal space, and public sector capability. This paper examines whether deterministic edge AI — specifically the ST-T1024 architecture— addresses these four constraints by construction rather than by investment. We compare the resource requirements of cloud-based stochastic AI against deterministic embedded inference across four dimensions: energy, connectivity, fiscal cost, and sovereignty. We find that the four constraints named by the World Bank are structurally bypassed by thearchitecture, not mitigated by it. We state the claim precisely: deterministic edge AI does not require the enablers that theWorld Bank identifies as missing. title: EDGE AI: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence in Edge Computing
abstract: Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) combines edge computing and AI to process data in real time while lowering latency, improving privacy, and making use of available resources.In sectors including healthcare, smart manufacturing, and the Internet of Things (IoT), Edge AI improves operational efficiency by processing data closer to the source.Large Language Models (LLMs) have been optimized for edge devices, inference performance has been increased, and issues with model size, energy consumption, and unstable network settings have been addressed.An overview of Edge AI's current status is given in this paper, along with a discussion of its revolutionary effects and potential future research areas.Important advancements include frameworks for optimizing AI models according to edge computing constraints and architectural considerations for combining generative AI (GenAI) with edge-cloud computing.In vital applications like the Internet of Vehicles, where real-time processing is essential for efficiency and safety, Edge AI has shown notable advancements.Edge AI is anticipated to be crucial in developing intelligent systems and guaranteeing quick, safe, and effective decision-making

title: BARE-AI: Bit-Flip Attack Resilience in AI Hardware through Built-in Performance Monitors
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are integral to many safety critical systems, yet they remain highly vulnerable to bit-flip attacks (BFAs), where a few memory level perturbations can drastically degrade accuracy. Existing defenses incur significant hardware overhead, depend on retraining, or fail against targeted flips. We propose BARE-AI, a runtime framework that detects, localizes, and mitigates BFAs during inference. BARE-AI introduces AI Performance Counters (APCs), lightweight hardware monitors in the accelerator datapath that capture per-layer activation statistics such as sparsity, entropy, kurtosis, and spectral shift. These are analyzed by the Predictive Unit for Layer Security Evaluation (PULSE), a compact detector trained offline as an ensemble of classifiers and realized on-chip as a small neural engine. For explainability and recovery, BARE-AI introduces an Activation Shift Index (ASI) for layer level fault localization and a z-score based repair that resets anomalous weights toward clean layer statistics. title: A Framework for Accelerating Transformer Inference on RISC-V for Edge AI
abstract: This work presents a framework for accelerating transformer-based language models (LMs) on resource-constrained IoT devices. The framework targets compact LMs: BERT-Tiny (B-Ty), MobileBERT (M-Bt), MiniLM (M-Lm), Electra (E-Lt) and DeBERTa (D-Bt) -- selected for their architectural diversity and use in edge inference scenarios. The proposed flow derives lightweight instruction set extensions tailored to the non-obvious computational patterns of these models. In addition, a custom instruction is introduced to accelerate the address generation stage of batch matrix multiplication, achieving a performance improvement of 15.39--21.74% with modest ASIC overheads of 6.79% in area and 2.33% in power. To further enhance performance without incurring additional processor core hardware cost, an optional compiler-directed loop unrolling strategy is employed, trading increased code size for overall reduced execution time. Evaluation on the Synopsys trv32p3f RISC-V core demonstrates inference speedups of up to 2.19x, and FPGA implementation on the AMD Zynq UltraScale+ ZCU102 shows a 32.94% area overhead at 75 MHz, whereas the ASIC implementation using the TSMC 28 nm library incurs a 21.08% area

title: Machine learning for fault detection, diagnosis, anomaly detection and failure prediction in industrial electric motors and fans: protocol for an AI-assisted systematic review of openly accessible studies with real-time or field elements
abstract: This project registers the protocol of an AI-assisted systematic review prepared for a master's thesis (Information Technologies, LBTU) on predictive maintenance of industrial devices. Purpose: To map how openly accessible primary studies published 2015–2026 develop, train, validate and deploy machine-learning models for fault detection, fault diagnosis, anomaly detection and failure prediction in industrial electric motors and fans, when the models run in real time, on embedded/edge or IoT systems, with a digital twin, or on field data from machines in operation. Methods: Searches of OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and arXiv (titles/abstracts; search strings validated with known-item recall and sampled precision), plus review-based citation searching. Title/abstract screening by an AI model in two independent passes with adjudication, checked against the author's blinded decisions (percent agreement, Cohen's kappa, PABAK). Full-text eligibility and data extraction from legal open-access full texts, with every judgement anchored to a quoted text snippet. abstract: This deliverable describes the User-centric Security Trust Function designed and implemented in the context of SAFE-6G Work Package 4 (Task 4.3). The Security Trust Function contributes to the broader SAFE-6G trustworthiness management framework delivering an adaptive, security control plane that addresses identity sovereignty, continuous authentication, fine-grained authorisation, zero-trust policy enforcement, and immutable audit trails in dynamic 6G and metaverse environments. Following the WP4 layered reference model, the Local AI Agent serves as the security intelligence component, continuously monitoring cluster telemetry and executing a multi-stage machine learning inference pipeline to assess edge infrastructure viability. In coordination with the Cognitive Coordinator, it dynamically recommends an operational security trust flavour (low, mid, high), balancing requested security guarantees against real-time continuum operational capacity. title: Deliverable D4.7: User-centric Reliability Function
abstract: his deliverable presents the design, implementation and evaluation of the Reliability Trust Function (TF) within the SAFE-6G cognitive trustworthiness framework. The Reliability TF ensures predictable, stable and user-aligned service behaviour across the edge-cloud continuum, with particular emphasis on QoE-critical applications such as real-time video streaming and immersive media. The Reliability TF leverages a multi-layer monitoring framework that collects telemetry from physical servers, virtualisation layers and application components. This telemetry enables the TF to detect anomalies, anticipate reliability degradation and enforce corrective actions aligned with user-centric trust requirements. title: A lightweight pose-guided fusion approach for accurate safety helmet compliance monitoring on edge devices
abstract: This paper presents an AI framework employing automated visual analysis to verify personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance in complex construction and industrial settings. Within the framework of engineering automation, robust semantic modeling of worker safety configurations is essential for enabling real-time hazard monitoring and data-driven risk management. In such environments, lightweight architectures are crucial for low-latency inference and efficient deployment on resource-constrained edge computing devices. However, existing studies rely on standalone object detection, leading to unreliable PPE verification, or use computationally heavy models that limit real-time performance. The proposed framework performs helmet detection and human pose estimation within a unified YOLO11-based architecture using a shared backbone. A spatial consistency mechanism aligns head keypoints with helmet regions to verify correct PPE usage. Experimental results on the Construction Personal Protective Equipment (CPPE) dataset achieve an F1-score of 0.961 at 110.7 frames per second (FPS), maintaining both accuracy and efficiency. title: A Low-Power, Self-Sustained Acoustic Node for Always-On Voice-Command Detection and Recognition Based on Triboelectric Nanogenerators and Edge Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Always-on voice-command recognition is important for smart-home control and human-machine interaction, but continuous acoustic sensing, edge inference, and wireless transmission can rapidly drain batteries. Here, we report a low-power, self-sustained acoustic node for always-on voice-command detection and recognition that integrates triboelectric acoustic wake-up and sensing, hierarchical edge artificial intelligence (edge AI), on-demand Bluetooth transmission, photovoltaic energy harvesting and energy storage. Rather than keeping all modules continuously active, the system reduces energy consumption through module-level power optimization and system-level event-driven control of module operating time. It remains in near-zero-power monitoring until acoustic activity crosses a preset threshold, then enters a low-power stage for wake-word screening. Command recognition and Bluetooth transmission are activated only after wake-word confirmation. The system achieved real-time accuracies of 96.0% for wake-word screening and 95.64% for 11-class command-word recognition on the microcontroller. title: Future of edge AI in biodiversity monitoring
abstract: Abstract Many ecological decisions are slowed by the gap between collecting and analysing biodiversity information. Edge computing moves data processing closer to the sensor, with edge artificial intelligence (AI) using AI models for data processing and selective data transfer. edge AI extends the scope of biodiversity monitoring by complementing retrospective ecological analysis with real‐time sensing, enabling responsive and adaptive decision‐making. However, the adoption of edge AI systems in ecological research remains fragmented because deploying efficient and reliable systems is complex. Edge hardware, on‐device AI models and network configuration are tightly linked, such that optimising any one component shapes the performance and feasibility of the others, demanding holistic system design. For the uptake of edge AI in biodiversity monitoring, it is essential to understand the design trade‐offs, performance constraints and implementation challenges faced by current systems. Here, we analyse 82 studies published between 2017 and 2025 that use edge AI systems for biodiversity monitoring across acoustic, vision‐based, tracking and multi‐modal sensing. abstract: Distributed farm environments require monitoring systems that can operate with limited power, intermittent connectivity, and minimal human supervision. Small-animal intrusion is particularly difficult to detect because targets are small, fast-moving, and frequently occluded by vegetation, soil structures, or low-light conditions. This paper presents a demonstration-scale solar-powered monitoring system that integrates photovoltaic energy harvesting, lithium-ion storage, passive infrared (PIR) motion triggering, camera activation, YOLOv8n edge detection, event logging, and deterrence using floodlight and speaker modules. The system is designed as an event-driven pipeline in which image capture and visual inference are activated only after a motion event, reducing unnecessary computation relative to continuous video analysis. A custom five-class dataset covering rat, mouse, squirrel, chipmunk, and mole was used to fine-tune the prototype detector. Under constrained proof-of-concept conditions, the five-class model achieved an mAP@0.5 of 0.81, an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.54, a mean retained-detection confidence of approximately 0.81, and about 22 FPS on a Raspberry Pi 4B. abstract: This chapter presents a comprehensive framework for Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence in Construction 6.0, outlining how Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, and predictive risk modeling integrate to enhance safety and risk management across the project lifecycle. NLP unlocks insights from near-miss reports, daily logs, and incident narratives, transforming unstructured text into structured risk intelligence linked to Building Information Modeling/Digital Twin environments. title: Agentic Design Space Exploration for Joint Hardware Configuration Selection and Mapping of AI Inference Workloads on Heterogeneous Edge SoCs
abstract: Modern edge Systems-on-Chip (SoCs) integrate heterogeneous processing units (PUs) such as CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, each with distinct performance and energy characteristics. Deploying AI inference workloads on them under real-time latency and energy constraints requires jointly mapping workloads to PUs and configuring each PU (e.g., selecting the number of active cores and the operating frequency). This joint space grows combinatorially, making exhaustive search infeasible. Most prior work on design space exploration (DSE) applies black-box optimization (BBO) such as evolutionary search, where each evaluation returns only aggregate metrics such as latency and energy. Recent LLM-guided DSE relies on the same sparse feedback. We observe that this limits its efficiency: it offers no insight into the design space or the reasons a design choice performs the way it does, and it leaves the reasoning abilities of LLMs largely unused. We present TraceDSE, an agentic DSE flow that performs joint workload mapping and PU configuration selection for AI inference on heterogeneous SoCs. title: ST-T1024 Microcontroller Implementation Guide — Version 2.1 : Programming the Deterministic AI Standard on ARM, RISC-V, and Beyond
abstract: ST-T1024 is a deterministic AI inference architecture for embedded and edge hardware. This guide provides a practical, step-by-step path to implementing ST-T1024 on a microcontroller or microprocessor — ARM, RISC-V, or otherwise. The core insight: ST-T1024 eliminates floating-point multipliers, stochastic sampling, andlarge DRAM arrays. This dramatically reduces silicon and firmware complexity, making itaccessible to any competent embedded engineer.

title: An Edge-First Multimodal Asset Management Studio and Retrieval Engine for Heterogeneous AI-Generated Media
abstract: AI-generated image collections combine visual content with heterogeneous provenance such as prompts, model parameters, and workflow graphs. Managing these collections locally requires coordinated metadata extraction, responsive browsing, and retrieval without mandatory remote inference. We present Berry AI Studio, an edge-first asset management system built with Vue, Tauri, Rust, SQLite, and ONNX Runtime. Berry integrates format-specific metadata parsing with raw-payload retention, generation-aware cancellation of queued thumbnail work, a persistent multi-tier thumbnail manifest, cursor pagination, and local image-text retrieval. We evaluate these mechanisms in five independent repetitions on a pinned source revision. With 50,000 catalog records, the median warm first-page database call was 285.3 ms; at offset 40,000, keyset pagination reduced median raw-query latency from 57.9 to 0.46 ms. A controlled browser harness recorded a 0.3 ms median-of-run P95 update time during virtualized scrolling, while cancellation prevented all 1,200 stale speculative decodes in the tested trace. abstract: Resource-constrained edge devices increasingly require local AI inference while providing limited memory, storage, compute capability, and operating-system support. This paper presents a cartridge-oriented architecture in which model-specific inference information is packaged as a compact, validated artifact executed by a reusable native inference engine. Unlike conventional deployments that embed models within a general-purpose inference runtime, the proposed approach establishes an explicit deployment boundary between the reusable execution engine and replaceable AI cartridges. A prototype was implemented as a bare-metal system and evaluated using QEMU RISC-V and ARM Cortex-M3 targets. The experiments demonstrate independent artifact replacement, loader-level validation, execution of multiple operator structures, and byte-identical cartridge portability across the two architectures. The results provide evidence that a model-specific deployment artifact can be separated from a reusable native execution engine without requiring a general-purpose operating system or interpreter. title: CyTReX: Explainable AI-Based Cybersecurity Threat Reasoning Framework for DER Networks
abstract: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) environments rely on network communication protocols to coordinate control commands, measurements, and device states across edge assets and cloud systems. Edge anomaly detection systems (ADS) monitor this traffic to identify deviations from normal communication behavior, flagging suspicious flows for further investigation. When the ADS flags abnormal network traffic, a single attack label is often insufficient for operational response: the label reports the detector's selected class but does not expose alternative threat interpretations that may warrant investigation. This paper presents Cybersecurity Threat Reasoning with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (CyTReX), an evidence-grounded threat reasoning framework for DER security that transforms network-level anomaly alerts into ranked, analyst-facing threat hypotheses designed to support Security Operations Center (SOC) triage and investigation. CyTReX constrains large language model (LLM) reasoning through a structured evidence packet, defined as a consolidated record of detection outputs, model explanations, and cyber threat intelligence (CTI) context. abstract: In an age of hyperconnectivity, emotional disconnection has paradoxically surged, intensifying mental health issues globally. The Voice of Care (VoC) system was conceived as a cutting-edge, privacy-first voice assistant, engineered to address the growing epidemic of loneliness and digital burnout. Unlike conventional artificial intelligence (AI) systems, VoC operates fully offline on a dual-node Raspberry Pi architecture, combining edge computing, advanced speech-to-text (STT), natural language processing (NLP), and text-to-speech (TTS) technologies. Leveraging models like Whisper, LLaMA, and Piper, the system ensures that emotionally intelligent interactions are delivered with high responsiveness (<1.2-s latency) while safeguarding personal data from cloud-based vulnerabilities. The personalized voice synthesis capability, built using fine-tuned ONNX models, enables VoC to replicate the voice of a loved one, fostering emotional familiarity and comfort. title: Edge-Based Fruit Quality Assessment Using an AI-Driven Electronic Nose
abstract: Abstract Ensuring food safety and minimizing waste remain key challenges across domestic and industrial contexts. This paper presents a smart fruit spoilage detection system that combines advanced gas sensing with deep learning for real-time monitoring and automated decision-making. The system employs an electronic nose (E-nose) with nine gas sensors to identify early indicators of fruit spoilage, thereby improving hygiene and reducing health risks. To achieve accurate and efficient classification, three deep learning models Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM) and hybrid CNN-LSTM architectures were evaluated. The LSTM achieved the best results with 97.03% accuracy, a 2.57 MB model size,and an inference time of 133.2 ms. To overcome the constraints of edge computing, several model compression techniques were explored. Among them, the knowledge distillation approach achieved the best trade-off, reducing the model size by 78.3% while incurring only a 0.71% accuracy loss. AI-Powered Multimodal Human Attention Analytics with Adaptive Learning Intervention for Online Education
abstract: The shift to online education has removed the non-verbal cues, such as gaze, posture and facial expression, that teachers use to judge whether students are engaged. Existing engagement detectors mostly rely on a single modality and send raw video to central servers, which causes accuracy problems and serious privacy risks under regulations such as the GDPR. This paper proposes an edge-computed, privacy-preserving multimodal framework that runs entirely in the learner’s browser. The system extracts 468 three-dimensional facial landmarks with MediaPipe, derives the Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) and head-pose Euler angles with OpenCV’s solvePnP, and fuses these cues with gaze estimates and learning-platform interaction logs using a Cross-Attention Transformer. A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent then selects real-time pedagogical interventions based on estimated cognitive load. Only anonymous numeric feature vectors are processed, and no video leaves the device. In a simulated evaluation built on the DAiSEE and MPIIGaze datasets, the proposed model reaches 71.8% accuracy and a macro F1-score of 0.69 for four-level engagement recognition, outperforming CNN and LSTM baselines. title: A Token Service Interface for AI-Native RANs
abstract: Generative and embodied AI services exchange token streams within continuing inference and control loops. Their communication requirements depend on each token set's purpose, useful timing, and execution context. This article organizes these properties into service, temporal, and stateful semantics and proposes a token service interface (TSI) between applications, radio access networks (RANs), and edge runtimes. TSI binds delivery requirements, readiness forecasts, and execution-state references to each schedulable token set, specifying field ownership, versioned updates, and admission feedback. A drone inspection case study over a decoupled RAN illustrates importance-aware radio allocation, advance preparation for timely delivery, and selective state migration that balances interruption against forwarding delay.

title: A Hybrid Single-Shot Vision-AI and Geospatial Framework for Multimodal Infrastructure Degradation Mapping in Urban Networks
abstract: Conventional transportation infrastructure inspection is often labor-intensive, time-consuming, and limited to individual asset types, reducing the efficiency of large-scale infrastructure management. This study proposes a hybrid Vision-AI and geospatial framework for automated multimodal infrastructure deterioration detection and digital asset monitoring. The framework integrates a YOLO-based object detection model, edge computing, geospatial synchronization, and a Digital Twin Web-GIS platform to detect, localize, and visualize infrastructure defects in real time. Experimental evaluation under multiple environmental conditions demonstrated stable detection performance, achieving 95.1% Precision, 94.3% Recall, 94.7% F1-score, and 96.4% mAP@0.5 under daylight conditions while maintaining reliable accuracy under shadowed, wet, and low-light environments. Edge deployment on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano also provided low-latency inference suitable for real-time field applications. title: BITEWISE: AI-POWERED NUTRITION, MEAL LOGGING AND CALORIE TRACKING PLATFORM
abstract: BiteWise is an AI-powered nutrition, meal logging, and real-time calorie tracking platform designed to streamline personal health monitoring by eliminating tedious manual entries. The system features a modern, decoupled architecture integrating a Next.js and React frontend with a high-performance Python FastAPI backend service. [1] Core System Workflow Image Upload & Validation: The application accepts JPG, JPEG, and PNG image uploads up to 5 MB, performing automatic data boundary and file-format validation before inference. Computer Vision Inference: The application utilizes a compact, pretrained YOLOv8s object detection model optimized for rapid edge deployment. The model processes 640×640 image inputs to localize and classify target foods across 12 distinct culinary classes with an approximate inference latency of just 42 ms per image. Nutrition Mapping & Calculation: A dedicated foodDatabase mapping layer bridges the visual classifier and nutritional data. It translates categorical class predictions into quantitative calorie, protein, carbohydrate, and fat metrics based on standardized serving size assumptions. title: A Zero-Shot Multi-Scope Life Cycle Assessment Framework for Machine Learning: Unifying Carbon, Water, and Network Footprints
abstract: Machine learning workloads now consume a significant and increasing percentage of global data centers energy. To overcome this problem, researchers and developers of new AI applications and pipelines are forced to use post hoc techniques and approaches to power telemetry to measure the actual power consumption during model executions. However, these approaches present a crucial and structural problem. Profiling a model requires running it first, which means we waste energy trying to measure its models’ energy’s draw. Furthermore, these tools and approaches are affected by ambient cloud virtualization noise rather than the actual algorithmic efficiencies. We propose a zero-shot, multiscope Life Cycle Analysis (LCA) framework that bypasses the actual physical execution of a model by recursively traversing a Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) and extracting topological depth of the tree-based ensembles. The engine maps the graph-level arithmetic intensity to physical hardware saturation ceiling via dynamically rooflining modeling and profiling. title: Performance–Energy Evaluation of Distributed Nanopore Basecalling for Mobile Edge Health Systems
abstract: Nanopore sequencing enables portable genomic analysis in field and mobile healthcare settings (e.g., rural areas), but real-time base-calling remains computationally demanding on low-power edge platforms. This paper investigates performance-energy trade-offs of distributed genomic basecalling on a Kubernetes-orchestrated cluster of NVIDIA Jetson Nano devices with node- and batch-level parallelism. Three basecalling models—SACall, RODAN, and Chiron—were evaluated across different batch sizes and power modes for throughput, energy consumption, resource utilization, and scalability. Experimental results show that SACall provides the best overall balance between throughput, scalability, and power efficiency, while RODAN achieves the highest throughput for small workloads and Chiron demonstrates near-linear scaling at the cost of high GPU utilization. The results confirm the feasibility of energy-efficient genomic inference on mobile edge infrastructures and highlight the importance of jointly optimizing AI workloads, power usage, and distributed execution in resource-constrained health applications.

title: Generative AI-powered multimodal physiological sensors for personalized edge health monitoring
abstract: This study focuses on personalized edge inference for multi-source physiological time-series signals instead of imaging data. The main contribution is a lightweight model for personalized, calibrated prediction that integrates a generative prior and flexible latent structures for denoising and imputation for short segments of ECG/PPG followed by prediction. Supporting components include federated learning, privacy-preservation mechanisms, and TinyML. Experiments were performed using the public MIMIC-III Waveform Database. The analyzed dataset comprised 10,282 patients and 22,317 patient-disjoint, record-level windows for binary (abnormal/risk) event classification. Positive labels were assigned to the physiological abnormality window intervals, and negative labels were assigned to the stable, non-event interval classes. Separating the data for training, validation, and testing was performed at the patient level using a disjoint 70%/15%/15% split of the patient datasets (7,197/1,542/1,543 patients), with approximately 30% positive-class examples, and ensured that no windows occurred across multiple partitions. title: EDGEMIND: LATENCY–ACCURACY–ENERGY OPTIMIZATION OF AI INFERENCE ACROSS CLOUD, EDGE, AND TINYML ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: Artificial intelligence inference is increasingly moving away from centralized cloud infrastructure toward edge devices and ultra-low-power microcontrollers. This shift can reduce network delay and support applications that must respond locally, but it also introduces strict limits on memory, compute capability, and energy. Most model-development workflows still emphasize predictive accuracy, while deployment decisions are often made using latency or hardware cost alone. EdgeMind proposes a unified evaluation framework that treats accuracy, latency, memory footprint, model size, and energy per inference as a multi-objective optimization problem. The study compares cloud, edge, and TinyML deployment levels and evaluates the effect of INT8 quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation. MLPerf Tiny is used as the main methodological reference because its benchmark framework explicitly evaluates model quality and single-stream inference latency and provides optional energy benchmarking. title: ZTA-Q: an Open-source RISC-V Platform for Accurate Quantized CNN Inference
abstract: Low-precision inference is widely adopted in edge AI to reduce computational cost and memory footprint. However, existing open-source accelerator platforms provide limited end-to-end support for CNNs following the standard TensorFlow Lite integer inference scheme. This paper presents ZTA-Q, an open-source RISC-V-based platform that enables accurate deployment of TensorFlow Lite INT8 models. In addition to extending operator support, ZTA-Q provides a configurable post-processing datapath for studying how circuit-level approximations, including reduced multiplier precision, shared shift scaling, and simplified rounding, affect model accuracy. The proposed system is implemented on a Digilent Arty A7-100T FPGA and operates at 83.3 MHz. Evaluations on representative CNN models show that with LUT, register, and DSP overheads of 26.3%, 12.6%, and 150%, respectively, ZTA-Q limits the degradation in both top-1 and top-5 accuracy to within 0.25 percentage points.

title: ECO AI-OPT: MULTI-OBJECTIVE OPTIMIZATION OF AI MODELS FOR ACCURACY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, LATENCY, AND CARBON-AWARE COMPUTING
abstract: The rapid deployment of artificial intelligence on cloud, mobile and edge platforms has made computational efficiency an important research concern. Traditional model evaluation often emphasizes predictive accuracy while reporting computational cost only as a secondary consideration. EcoAI-Opt proposes a multi-objective optimization framework that evaluates accuracy, inference latency, memory footprint, energy consumption and estimated carbon impact together. The framework compares a baseline floating-point model against pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation and combined optimization strategies. CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST are proposed as reproducible image-classification workloads, while MLPerf Tiny provides a standardized reference for low-power inference benchmarking. The central decision problem is formulated in two practical ways: maximize accuracy under an energy budget, or minimize energy while maintaining a predefined accuracy threshold. The framework also introduces an EcoAI composite score for ranking models, while retaining the raw measurements so that the score does not hide important trade-offs. title: First-in-human evaluation of real-time pixel-level AI-assisted anatomical segmentation in neurosurgery: pituitary surgery as an exemplar
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Precise anatomical navigation is fundamental to safe endoscopic pituitary surgery, a high-stakes procedure characterised by a challenging learning curve. While traditional navigation systems often rely on workflow-disrupting probes or static preoperative imaging, advancements in computer vision AI (CVAI) now enable dynamic, real-time pixel-level anatomical segmentation directly from live surgical video. Our group has previously conducted a series of preclinical human-computer interaction studies to refine the system's design, alongside digital and high-fidelity physical simulations demonstrating the potential benefit of AI assistance in improving surgical performance, training, and safety. Building on this foundation, the current study represents a first-in-human evaluation of real-time pixel-level CVAI anatomical segmentation in the neurosurgical operating room - assessing feasibility, human factors and clinical outcomes, while iteratively improving the system. METHOD: Guided by the DECIDE-AI and IDEAL frameworks, this single-centre evaluation comprises an initial proof-of-concept of CVAI anatomical segmentation in endoscopic transsphenoidal pituitary surgery. title: Post-Training Quantization of Autoregressive Weather Models
abstract: Advancements in high-resolution numerical weather prediction (NWP) and data assimilation (DA) have shaped the developments in deep learning (DL) architectures emulating atmospheric dynamics. Emulators for weather forecasting exhibit forecast quality comparable to physics based models at forecast horizon scaling from few days to subseasonal time scales. The emulators are driven by hardware-accelerated matrix multiplication in autoregressive inferences, significantly reducing the computation time and resources required for NWP. Optimization of the matrix multiplication processes in GPU architectures provides opportunities to scale towards high-resolution domain, and offers implementation of out of the box solutions. Post-training quantization (PTQ) has been demonstrated across multiple DL architectures to accelerate and increase the number of computations in unit time while consuming less power, enabling applications on edge hardware. In this study, we investigate the effect of PTQ on pre-trained AI emulators for global-scale weather forecasting. title: AI for rural healthcare: Transforming villages of India through intelligent and predictive systems
abstract: Rural healthcare systems face persistent shortages of trained personnel, diagnostic infrastructure, continuous monitoring capability and rapid referral pathways. This paper extends a Python-based artificial-intelligence framework for rural healthcare into a portable multimodal screening architecture termed the Quantum Suitcase. The name denotes a compact field-deployable health-monitoring platform; it does not imply that unvalidated “quantum resonance” measurements can diagnose disease. The system prioritizes non-invasive, needle-free first-line screening using physiological signals that can be measured through established physical principles: photoplethysmography and pulse oximetry, electrocardiography, oscillometric blood pressure, infrared thermometry, respiratory monitoring, digital auscultation and camera-based observation. Optional point-of-care laboratory tests may be added when clinically required, but the initial screening workflow is designed to operate without routine venipuncture. title: Review of Deployable Endogenous Security Technologies for Smart Grids
abstract: The smart grid is a critical infrastructure in the modern energy system that couples cyberspace with physical operation processes, and it has become a key pillar of national energy security. With the widespread use of massive heterogeneous devices such as distributed energy resources, energy storage systems, and smart meters, the "cloud—network—edge—terminal" collaborative architecture has become the mainstream paradigm. However, the continuous evolution of attack techniques has led to increasingly frequent cyberattacks targeting Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, intelligent terminals, and communication networks. The inherent lag of conventional ″patch-and-block″ passive defense techniques and their dependence on prior knowledge cause difficulty in effectively countering security threats deeply embedded in system architectures and operational processes. AI-IoT architectures for dairy welfare assessment: multimodal monitoring, deployment constraints, and the emerging role of digital twins
abstract: The intensification of dairy production has increased the need for continuous, transparent, and scientifically grounded animal welfare assessment. Artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) are rapidly expanding the sensing, data-processing, and analytical capabilities available to precision livestock farming; however, much of the existing literature remains task-specific, modality-centered, and weakly connected to deployment realities. Many studies report promising performance for isolated tasks such as lameness detection, feeding behavior recognition, or disease-risk prediction, yet fewer studies examine how sensing architecture, data flow, compute placement, uncertainty handling, and human decision workflows jointly determine whether AI-enabled welfare assessment is operationally reliable. This review provides a system-oriented and deployment-aware synthesis of AI-IoT applications for dairy welfare assessment. Welfare is treated as a dynamic and partially observable system state shaped by interactions among behavior, physiology, environment, and management. Lightweight explainable AI for real-time resource allocation in heterogeneous edge computing networks
abstract: Heterogeneous edge networks put computing close to users and sensors, but with strict latency, energy and reliability requirements, resource managers need to decide where workloads execute, where to allocate radio resources and compute resources, and when to move the workload to another node. Learning-based policies are able to adjust to varying demand, but they have been hard to audit and can be too complex to explain or infer by resource-limited devices. This review brings together the basic concepts of edge computing technologies, optimization-based allocation, reinforcement learning approaches, explainable AI and efficient inference research. It marks a gap in co-design: Allocation performance, explanation fidelity, and explanation cost are frequently considered a separate and isolated concern. We present an explainable resource-allocation architecture, including a non-blocking explain path and a fast control path, which is light weight. Edge-Based Real-Time Medical Image Processing and Classification Using a Lightweight Explainable Deep Learning Framework
abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly improved medical image processing applications in healthcare. Still, there are difficulties in deploying deep learning in the field due to high computational overhead, latency, and limited explainability. To address the stated challenges, the framework under discussion comprises two stages: image preprocessing and a lightweight CNN with depth-wise separable convolutions for effective feature extraction and classification. Grad-CAM and saliency map visualizations provide a visual explanation of the output. This framework is intended for edge deployment and may be used on platforms such as the Raspberry Pi 4, the Jetson Nano, and TinyML. Moreover, the design is aimed at ensuring real-time operation on resource-constrained edge devices while preserving the patients' data privacy. Experimental validation was performed on benchmark medical image datasets typically used in healthcare image classification research. Results indicate that the lightweight model demonstrates comparable classification quality (~90–91% accuracy) but has fewer parameters (2.1M parameters, 0.6 GFLOPs) and faster inference time (~95 ms). title: Machine-Verifiable Legal Transactions and Quantum-Secure Cryptographic Agility for Trusted AI-Native 6G Digital Infrastructure
abstract: Abstract AI-native sixth-generation (6G) infrastructure will increasingly execute network, commercial and public-service actions through autonomous agents distributed across terminals, edges and clouds. Yet a conventional digital signature can authenticate a message without proving that the message was produced under an authorized legal rule, an admissible machine decision, a valid model state, or a quantum-resilient cryptographic configuration. This paper develops a model-based architecture for machine-verifiable legal transactions coupled with cryptographic agility in AI-native 6G environments. The proposed MVLT-QSA6G framework represents legal obligations as signed policy graphs; binds AI decisions to verifiable inference evidence and network context; selects post-quantum or hybrid cryptographic suites through an agility orchestrator; and commits execution evidence to a tamper-evident audit graph. title: Edge AI Empowering Real-Time Decision-Making and Autonomous Defense Operations in Smart Warfare
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence edge computing, and autonomous systems is transforming the nature of modern warfare. Traditional defense operations, which relied heavily on centralized command structures and human decision-making, are increasingly being augmented by intelligent systems capable of sensing, analyzing, and responding to dynamic battlefield conditions in real time. Among these technologies, Edge AI has emerged as a critical enabler of smart warfare by allowing data processing and AI inference to occur directly on deployed platforms rather than relying on distant cloud infrastructures. This chapter explores the role of Edge AI in defense operations, with particular emphasis on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), autonomous surveillance systems and intelligent reconnaissance platforms. It further examines the use of Edge AI for applications such as target recognition, battlefield situational awareness, autonomous navigation, mission execution, and decentralized decision-making.

title: Lightweight Edge-AI Model for Real-Time Sorghum Disease Detection on Resource-Constrained Mobile Devices
abstract: Lightweight Edge-AI Model for Real-Time Sorghum Disease Detection on Resource-Constrained Mobile Devices presents an efficient artificial intelligence approach for identifying sorghum diseases directly on mobile and edge-computing platforms. The study focuses on developing a lightweight machine learning model capable of performing rapid and accurate disease detection while operating under limited computational resources, memory, and power constraints. Computer vision and deep learning techniques are used to analyse sorghum leaf images and distinguish healthy plants from diseased conditions. Model optimization strategies are considered to reduce computational complexity and improve inference speed without substantially compromising detection performance. The proposed approach supports real-time, on-device disease diagnosis, reducing dependence on cloud connectivity and enabling timely intervention in agricultural environments. The work highlights the potential of Edge AI and mobile computing to make intelligent crop monitoring more accessible, practical, and scalable, particularly for farmers and agricultural users operating in resource-constrained settings.

title: A 1-Byte Deterministic Acoustic Interface for Ultra-Low-Latency Edge Computing: Hardware-Native Phonetic Encoding via 2KB On-Chip L1 SRAM
abstract: Contemporary deep neural speech architectures rely heavily on extensive subword tokenizers (e.g., Byte-Pair Encoding) and multi-byte Unicode International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) representations. These conventional pipelines impose substantial DRAM bus contention, multi-megabyte memory footprints, and non-deterministic inference latencies exceeding 300 ms, rendering them unsuitable for resource-constrained edge microcontrollers (MCUs) and hard real-time reflex control in robotics. This paper proposes AI-IPA, a hardware-native, 1-byte deterministic acoustic interface architecture operating over a strictly closed vocabulary of fewer than 50 symbols (exactly 47 symbols). By mathematically formulating the bio-articulatory mechanics of the Hunminjeongeum matrix, the proposed system completely eliminates external rendering libraries, multi-byte font engines, and off-chip memory dependencies, executing entirely within an allocated 2KB on-chip L1 SRAM address space (0x000–0x800). title: Decentralizing Intelligence: Edge AI, Sovereign Data, and the Resurgence of Tech Jobs
abstract: Decentralizing Intelligence: Edge AI, Sovereign Data, and the Resurgence of Tech Jobs Abstract & Overview: September 2026 ABSTRACT The rapid acceleration of artificial intelligence has historically favored a centralized paradigm characterized by massive hyper-scale cloud deployments, monopolistic data aggregations, and soaring energy costs. However, physical grid constraints, high inference latency, and strict enterprise data governance demands are forcing a structural rotation toward decentralized edge intelligence. This technical dispatch examines how high-compression data formats, solid-state miniaturization, and unified LLM-driven orchestration enable application-infrastructure proximity at the edge. Furthermore, it explores the deployment of Small Language Models (SLMs) with precise guardrails for deterministic, repetitive tasks across stateful industrial IoT systems—such as automated traffic controllers, food processing plants, and paint manufacturing lines. Finally, it analyzes how the decentralization of enterprise data and edge infrastructure is driving a robust multi-year economic recovery and employment expansion for engineering, security, and compliance professionals. title: Energy-efficient GW detection with adaptive expert layers an adaptive expert-driven AI for GW detection
abstract: In this paper we propose an Adaptive Hierarchical Mixture of Experts (HMoE) model for energy-efficient, real-time gravitational-wave (GW) detection. The model organises specialized expert subnetworks that focus on different time–frequency characteristics of the GW strain data, and a lightweight gating network that dynamically selects only the most relevant experts for each input. This dynamic expert selection reduces redundant computation and allows the architecture to balance detection accuracy, latency, and power consumption according to signal complexity. To further improve efficiency, the HMoE framework is combined with model-compression techniques, including pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation, so that most of the inference can be executed with low-precision, low-cost operations while preserving detection performance. The model is trained and evaluated on real LIGO and Virgo datasets from the Gravitational Wave Open Science Center, containing a variety of compact binary coalescence events and realistic non-stationary noise. title: HAR-ASIC: A Configurable Edge-AI Human Activity Recognition Circuit for Ultra-Low Power Wearable Devices
abstract: We present an application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) using digital hardware design to maximise energy-efficiency of human activity recognition (HAR) in autonomous wearable devices. The HAR-ASIC was designed in 22 nm technology and includes a battery of configurable, hardware-optimised feature extraction functions along with a decision tree ensemble classifier, thus serving as an edge AI device for local sensor data processing. We validate the HAR-ASIC based on post-layout process data with five HAR datasets and show the design scalability for configurations to maximise energy saving and others to maximise recognition performance. We show that feature extraction often requires up to 100 times more energy than the classification function. Our configuration analysis shows that feature extraction energy consumption can be reduced by factors of two to five, with at most 3% loss in F1-score, depending on the dataset. Across all datasets, feature extraction and classification energy was between 64 and 678 nJ per inference for Pareto-optimal configurations using sliding window buffers of up to 512 samples. title: Edge AI-Driven Traffic Management for Urban Air Mobility
abstract: Cloud-centric Air Traffic Management architectures are poorly suited to Urban Air Mobility, where dense, three-dimensional flight paths require conflict-resolution decisions within tens of milliseconds. This chapter proposes a four-layer, edge-native reference architecture combining Deep Reinforcement Learning for adaptive route optimization, Federated Learning for privacy-preserving collaboration across operators, TinyML for onboard inference under strict power budgets, and 6G-enabled Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks for multi-tier connectivity. Each layer is specified in terms of its inputs, algorithmic choices, and hardware placement, and the design rationale linking the architecture to the latency, privacy, and energy constraints of urban airspace is set out in full. The chapter further defines a complete evaluation methodology by which the architecture should be validated. The contribution is architectural rather than empirical: the framework is offered as a design and evaluation foundation, not a validated system.

abstract: Abstract The increasing global demand for tabletop and board games is placing growing pressure on manufacturers to adopt efficient, scalable production solutions. This paper presents an automated assembly approach that leverages state of the art computer vision and AI based object detection to enable real time identification of game box components for robotic pick and place operations. An industrial imaging setup combined with an edge AI device enables continuous image acquisition and low latency processing of conveyor belt data. To address the detection of standardized packaging elements, a custom dataset was created and formulated as a two-class object detection task. In addition to conventional axis aligned bounding boxes, the study investigates the use of Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB) to better capture object pose and alignment, which is particularly relevant for precise robotic grasping and placement. Multiple YOLO model families were trained and evaluated in nano, small, and medium configurations to analyze the tradeoff between detection accuracy and inference speed required to sustain production rates of up to 80 units per minute.
