title: MoSE: Mode-Switching Expander for Mixed LLM Training and Inference
abstract: AI clusters increasingly run large language model (LLM) inference and training on the same fabric. Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation creates key-value (KV) cache transfers between prefill and decode groups, whereas training collectives and all-to-all traffic benefit from near-uniform global connectivity. A static sparse topology can therefore be poorly matched to one of the two traffic patterns. We present Mode-Switching Expander (MoSE), a reconfigurable expander that treats topology design as a fixed-degree edge-allocation problem. MoSE reallocates the same sparse edge budget toward direct P-D connectivity in inference-heavy modes and restores a uniform random regular expander in training-heavy modes. We evaluate MoSE using a 1024-group flow-level topology model, shortest-path routing, and two mixed workloads. Across 20 seeds, MoSE reduces average and 95th-percentile (P95) load-aware KV communication cost by 90.8\% and 91.9\% relative to Static-Training in the inference-heavy mode. In the training-heavy mode, it reduces average and P95 training communication cost by 22.7\% and 27.6\% relative to stale Static-Inference. title: AIR-LLM: Broadcasting AI Weights over Radio for Memory-Free Edge LLM Inference via RF Computing
abstract: Next-generation large language models (LLMs) are expanding from the cloud to ubiquitous edge devices. However, edge devices typically either lack the memory to store increasingly large LLM weights or, even with enough memory, spend unaffordable energy on loading the weights. This raises our question: can an edge device run an LLM without storing or loading its weights, but receive them over the air and consume them on the fly? Inspired by wireless broadcasting, we present AIR-LLM, an LLM inference architecture for edge devices, which is composed of: (i) a central radio (e.g., 5G base stations) that broadcasts the LLM weights into the air, and (ii) the edge user that receives the weights and completes the general matrix-vector multiplication (GEMV) of LLM inference directly in the radio frequency (RF) domain using RF mixers. To further shorten the airtime, AIR-LLM exploits MIMO spatial multiplexing and proposes an energy-efficient precoder-postcoder pair on the edge to calibrate its own wireless channel. title: Satellite-6G Integrated Scientific Sensing Network
abstract: Abstract: Satellite–6G integrated scientific sensing networks unite orbital observation, non-terrestrial communications, terrestrial 6G infrastructure, edge intelligence, statistical inference, and accountable governance into a common evidence architecture. This monograph develops that architecture from foundational measurement theory through causal modeling, trustworthy machine learning, scalable data engineering, and sectoral deployment. The book therefore formulates research designs that combine spatiotemporal statistics, causal identification, multimodal fusion, graph and physics-informed learning, federated edge computation, digital twins, streaming pipelines, reproducible MLOps, and cryptographic agility. title: AI/ML-DRIVEN PREDICTIVE SERVICE MANAGEMENT FOR TELECOM AND ICT INFRASTRUCTURE: A VISION 2030 FRAMEWORK FOR OPERATIONAL RESILIENCE
abstract: The telecom and information and communication technology (ICT) infrastructure sector is shifting from a fault-management approach that focuses on components to one that is service-oriented and involves predicting potential degradation before it leads to an outage or a breach of service levels. This report brings together research carried out between 2020 and 2025 on the use of machine learning for traffic forecasting, anomaly and fault prediction, network slicing, digital twins, federated learning, explainability, and zero-touch orchestration. The objective is to examine how these capabilities can be combined into a predictive service-management architecture that meets the operational-resilience goals linked to Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 digital transformation initiative. It has been found that the greatest operational benefit does not come from the individual accuracy of models, but from connecting the forecasts to controlled, closed-loop actions across the radio, transport, cloud, edge, and service layers. title: The Avian Digital Twin Intelligence: A Multimodal AI, Bioacoustic and Precision- Phenotyping Framework for Predictive Health, Disease Forecasting and Welfare Optimization in Companion Parrots
abstract: Companion parrots present an unusually complex challenge for preventive veterinary medicine because clinically meaningful changes may initially manifest as subtle alterations in behaviour, vocal activity, posture, locomotion, feeding, social interaction, plumage condition or daily activity patterns. Conventional clinical assessment generally provides a snapshot of an animal at a particular point in time, whereas companion parrots continuously generate behavioural and environmental information that could potentially be transformed into longitudinal health indicators. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), multimodal sensing, computer vision, bioacoustics, self-supervised learning and time-series modelling create an opportunity to develop a fundamentally different paradigm: the individualized avian digital twin.An avian digital twin can be conceptualized as a continuously updated computational representation of an individual bird that integrates heterogeneous observations—including video, vocalizations, activity, environmental conditions, feeding behaviour, physiological measurements and veterinary records—with biological and statistical models. title: Adaptive Robotic Material Interface System
abstract: Abstract Adaptive Robotic Material Interface System develops a unified research architecture for robots that must perceive, interpret, and act upon materials whose mechanical, geometric, thermal, chemical, or surface properties evolve during contact. The system treats the material–robot boundary as a dynamic interface rather than a passive end-effector problem. Its conceptual structure integrates multimodal sensing, uncertainty-aware state estimation, causal modelling, trustworthy machine learning, adaptive control, digital twins, edge analytics, and governance for safety-critical deployment. The research design distinguishes latent material state from noisy measurements, links intervention choices to measurable response, and represents adaptation as a constrained decision process in which task performance is balanced against damage, instability, energy use, and human or environmental risk. Statistical models support explanation and causal inference; machine-learning models support prediction and generalization; scalable data engineering enables reproducible lifecycle management; and sectoral assurance models translate technical performance into deployment requirements. title: Remote Agricultural Visual Diagnostics with Multimodal LLM Using Semantic Transmission in Low-Bandwidth LoRa Environments
abstract: Deploying advanced AI for agricultural monitoring is critical to mitigating crop losses and ensuring food security; however, significant technical hurdles often hamper this effort. While computer vision models offer a powerful solution for early, precise detection of pests and diseases from images, their immense computational requirements make them unsuitable for low-power devices in remote fields. This limitation forces data to be sent to a base station for analysis, creating a severe communication bottleneck, as agricultural environments typically rely on low-bandwidth Long Range (LoRa) networks. This creates a core paradox: LoRa is designed to transmit only a few bytes of data, making it fundamentally incapable of handling large image files and rendering remote visual diagnostics impractical. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a paradigm shift from transmitting pixels to transmitting semantic meaning. We introduce a novel closed-loop framework that enables efficient visual data transmission and returns actionable, AI-driven feedback. title: EdgeTwin as a Deployment-Aware Edge AI Digital Twin for Predictive Maintenance and Visual Anomaly Detection in SME Smart Manufacturing
abstract: Smart manufacturing increasingly uses AI-driven digital twins, predictive maintenance, and visual inspection, but less is known about how these capabilities can be integrated into lightweight Edge AI architectures usable by resource-constrained SMEs, making deployment-aware evaluation important. This study develops and evaluates EdgeTwin through design science and experimental applied computing. The framework combines machine-condition data, industrial inspection images, edge-oriented inference, digital twin representation, and human-supervised decision support. Machine-failure prediction was tested using AI4I 2020, visual anomaly detection was evaluated on MVTec AD, INT8 optimization was evaluated in a workstation-based edge-oriented simulation, and contextual feasibility was assessed by eight Greek manufacturing experts. XGBoost achieved the strongest predictive-maintenance performance, PatchCore achieved the strongest visual detection performance, and EfficientAD offered the best balance between detection quality and latency. abstract: Abstract Quantum-secure agentic cyber-physical control networks integrate autonomous decision agents, physical process control, distributed sensing, post-quantum trust services and lifecycle governance within a single assurance architecture. abstract: Abstract Immersive digital environments complicate the attribution, authorisation, and monetisation of creative works because avatars, spatial recordings, generative assets, interactive performances and derivative scenes circulate through heterogeneous platforms. Concurrent advances in quantum computing motivate a security architecture that protects long-lived rights evidence, strengthens verification and permits disciplined cryptographic migration. abstract: This study compared the frames-per-second (FPS) performance of the YOLO26 real-time object detection model on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano edge artificial intelligence (AI) device, according to the sensor interface (Camera Serial Interface [CSI] versus Universal Serial Bus [USB]) and the inference acceleration engine (PyTorch, TensorRT, and DeepStream). With three repeated measurements per condition, replacing PyTorch with TensorRT improved throughput from 20.22 to 29.90 FPS (47.9%) for the CSI camera and from 20.15 to 29.73 FPS (47.5%) for the USB webcam. However, the same engine remained at 10.00 FPS under uncompressed capture, a 197.3% difference from the condition applying Motion JPEG (MJPEG) capture with hardware decoding. In an experiment without sensor constraints, the maximum engine throughput was measured at 63.61 FPS for TensorRT and 21.85 FPS for PyTorch, establishing that the PyTorch conditions operated near their computational limit, whereas the TensorRT conditions were bounded by the sensor output limit. title: Quantum-AI Climate Sensor Fusion Processor
abstract: Abstract: A quantum–artificial intelligence climate sensor fusion processor is conceptualized as a scientifically accountable system for transforming heterogeneous environmental measurements into calibrated and decision-relevant representations of evolving climate risk. The proposed architecture couples satellite retrievals, in situ observations, geospatial context and physics-informed estimators with selective quantum-inspired computational modules. Rather than assuming an intrinsic quantum advantage, the research design requires explicit classical baselines, resource accounting, uncertainty decomposition and evaluation under geographic and temporal distribution shifts. A sequence of hierarchical statistical models, causal identification strategies, graph-temporal predictors and constrained neural operators provides complementary approaches to explanation, prediction and operational reasoning. The accompanying engineering lifecycle specifies provenance-preserving ingestion, scalable feature computation, low-power edge deployment, model release assurance and cyber integrity. title: Semiconductor Wafer Anomaly Detection and Classification System
abstract: Abstract: Semiconductor wafer inspection confronts a difficult interaction between visually heterogeneous defects, scarce expert annotation, rapidly evolving fabrication recipes, and the asymmetric consequences of missed excursions and false alarms. This monograph develops an integrated research architecture for anomaly detection and classification across optical, electron-microscopy, spatial wafer-map, and equipment-telemetry observations. It connects defect ontologies and sampling design to hierarchical statistical inference, causal process diagnosis, self-supervised representation learning, multiscale segmentation, topology-aware classification, and open-set uncertainty management. A parallel engineering perspective treats manufacturing identifiers, event-time joins, reproducible training manifests, edge latency, digital-twin stress testing, security, and model retirement as parts of the scientific argument rather than downstream implementation details. title: Real-Time Inference Optimization on Microcontrollers
abstract: Real-time inference on microcontrollers extends machine-learning computation into devices with strict limitations in memory, processing throughput, storage, and energy. These constraints make direct deployment of conventional neural networks inefficient and require optimization at both the model and implementation levels. This paper examines real-time inference optimization as a hardware-aware computing problem, focusing on quantization, pruning, compact network structures, operator optimization, memory planning, and deployment-aware design. Similar to AI-assisted optimization in electronic design automation (EDA), the objective is not merely to generate a smaller model but to search a constrained design space for implementations that satisfy measurable performance requirements. The paper maps optimization techniques across the inference workflow, from model preparation and conversion to runtime execution and validation. It emphasizes that accuracy, latency, memory footprint, and energy must be evaluated together on the target microcontroller. title: Artificial Intelligence in Plant Sciences
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may be referred to as a family of technologies which allow computers and other machines to perform the tasks that were previously dependent on human intelligence. In order to perform the tasks autonomously, the machines learn from large volumes of input data and involve the use of machine learning algorithms. It attempts to mimic the process of human learning in which a person gradually develops knowledge and skills by continuous trial and error method. Due to the ability of AI to perform intelligent tasks, it finds a number of opportunities for application in diverse fields including plant sciences. In this chapter, let us try to gain a basic understanding of artificial intelligence and its applications with special reference to plant sciences.

title: Entrepreneurial subjectivity, expertise, and speculation in artificial intelligence start-ups in Taipei, Taiwan
abstract: This thesis examines entrepreneurial subjectivity in the artificial intelligence industry through an analysis of startup business founders, venture capitalists, and other entrepreneurs. In recent decades, increasing financialization has led to the emergence of a particular form of techno-optimism that is central to the ethos of these entrepreneurs. Through an ethnography based on 18 months of fieldwork, I show that AI and the economic subversions it will allegedly cause have profound effects on the self-making practices of those involved, generating forms of speculative value experienced as a sense of potential at the level of the organization and the self. To demonstrate this, the thesis focuses upon the process of subject formation in artificial intelligence work as an industry where models of the future economy are made visible through imaginative practices, including marketing, branding, and hype. I examine modalities of speculation characteristic of startup founders and organizations and demonstrate how imagined AI-enriched futures leverage their expertise while simultaneously reinscribing the epistemic authority of their work. abstract: Supplementary material for the article: Markic, M., Hennemann, S. & Poeppelbuss, J. (2027). Same Same, but Different: How Dedicated AI Leadership Roles Differentiate from Technology Leadership. Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS) 2027. Abstract: Organizations across industries increasingly create dedicated artificial intelligence (AI) leadership roles alongside, rather than in place of, established technology leadership roles, although the literature suggests that governance demands could be absorbed by existing leadership roles. In this study, we examine how new AI leadership roles are defined and how they differ from established leadership roles. Our findings reveal that AI leadership roles entail a distinctive governance mandate – coordinating AI across business units, aligning it with strategic value, translating between technical and business domains, building governance mechanisms, and managing enablement – which existing technology leadership roles encode only partially. title: The impact of artificial intelligence on human safety and data protection in smart logistics: opportunities, risks and governance challenges
abstract: Aim: This article examines the dual role of artificial intelligence (AI) in smart logistics, focusing on its capacity to strengthen human and operational safety while simultaneously creating new risks for data protection, cybersecurity and automated decision-making. Methods: The study applies a structured literature review covering publications from 2018–2025 in Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar, supplemented by comparative analysis of AI-enabled and conventional security approaches and a case-based synthesis of cyber-physical disruptions relevant to logistics. Results: The review indicates that AI can improve anomaly detection, video surveillance, network monitoring, predictive maintenance, routing and incident response. At the same time, the same dependence on data-intensive models creates vulnerabilities related to adversarial inputs, data poisoning, model theft, privacy leakage, algorithmic bias, model drift and service disruption. These risks can propagate from digital systems to physical logistics operations and therefore affect both data subjects and personnel. title: NeuroAI – An AI-Powered Personalized Learning Tutor for Students with Diverse Learning Challenges
abstract: Abstract: Students have incredibly different ways of learning, thinking, and processing information today. Traditional pedagogies that may be grounded in age, or contextually within curriculum, or course outline, are often inadequate to address the realities that many learners are faced with—especially children and youth struggling with educational learning challenges associated with disabilities such as dyslexia, ADHD, or in some cases conditions associated with auditory processing. The research introduced NeuroAI, an AI-supported personalized learning tutor designed to help support learners and students with a large variety of learning challenges. NeuroAI combines machine learning capabilities with brain-based education and learning strategies to help engage in lessons specifically for each child's pace, style, and understanding. NeuroAI relies on and integrates natural language processing, affective computing, and real-time analytics of performance data to allow for learning to become a closed loop relationship, ongoing feedback loops that occur between the learner's inputs to the instructional outputs. title: Stress Proximity Index Assessment (SPI-Assess): Design and Implementation of an AI-Assisted, Culturally-Calibrated Occupational Stress Tool for Multicultural Organisations
abstract: Occupational stress affects an estimated 60–80% of workplace-related healthcare visits [6] and represents a primary driver of absenteeism, presenteeism, and workforce attrition in contemporary organisations. Despite growing awareness, systematic early detection of stress remains absent from most professional environments, with identification typically occurring only after crisis-level deterioration. Existing digital tools address either individual self-assessment or organisational engagement tracking — but no system currently integrates both levels within a single privacy-compliant architecture. This paper presents SPI-Assess, an AI-based occupational stress proximity assessment tool designed for deployment in multicultural professional organisations. The system integrates four validated psychometric instruments — the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI), Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), Oldenburg Burnout Inventory (OLBI), and OCEAN personality model — with a cultural calibration algorithm and a four-phase conversational assessment architecture, including AI-driven analysis of free employee narrative text using natural language processing. title: AI and Emerging Digital Technologies in Early Childhood Physics Education: A Systematic Review
abstract: Background: Young children explore motion, force, light, sound, and material properties through play. Digital technologies may extend these experiences, but evidence on preschool physics learning is dispersed across research. Objective: This systematic literature review synthesizes technologies for physics-related learning among children aged 3–6, concepts and pedagogies, reported outcomes, study designs, and developmental, ethical, accessibility, and implementation considerations. Method: Guided by PRISMA 2020, searches covered Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, Education Source, and IEEE Xplore, plus backward and forward citation searching. Eligible sources addressed preschool children and AI or emerging technologies in physics or related physical science. Findings were synthesized narratively and thematically, distinguishing direct physics evidence from adjacent research. Results: Twenty-five studies were identified. Technologies included robotics and AI activities, augmented and virtual reality, interactive multimedia, digital games, simulations, and mobile learning. title: AI-Augmented Research Software Engineering: Risks, Challenges, and Practices
abstract: AI is reshaping research software engineering on two fronts: AI components are increasingly embedded inside research software and science gateways that Research Software Engineers (RSEs) deliver, while AI-assisted and agentic coding tools are changing how RSEs build that software in the first place. This is especially visible in gateway and cyberinfrastructure projects that connect user interfaces, scientific data, HPC systems, and external services. While these tools can accelerate development and architectural exploration, they also introduce new risks: non-deterministic outputs, overconfident reasoning, unsafe tool execution, hidden operational costs, and sustainability pressure from rapid tooling churn. This paper argues that AI-augmented research software engineering requires a shift from unconstrained AI use, whether AI assists development or runs inside the delivered software, to AI-constrained engineering. title: Cloud-Native Graphical and Programmatic Cross-Database Access to Experiment Metadata with Trino, Superset and Ibis
abstract: LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) is the world’s most sensitive dark matter direct-detection experiment, acquiring over a petabyte of data per year. LZ also retains several terabytes of user-facing metadata describing detector conditions and data-processing environments needed for reproducible data selection and processing. These metadata live in six heterogeneous databases (SQL and NoSQL) and have historically been accessed through seven separate programmatic and graphical interfaces that connect to unique subsets of these databases. This fragmented nature has led to major problems for both users and maintainers. First, maintenance overhead grew disproportionately: for example, our custom python-based GUI for browsing databases grew to thousands of lines of non-reusable code, requiring near-daily manual restarts to recover from silent failures reported to us by users. Second, our programmatic python interfaces lacked expressiveness, pushing users toward ad-hoc scripts to filter/reshape results and making cross-database joins unnecessarily tedious. title: Getting Perspectives on Quality in the Age of AI
abstract: Research Software Engineering (RSEng) is grounded in the belief that better, higher-quality software enables better research. As we look to the future of RSEng, we see that generative AI could substantially accelerate and expand the scope of research software development, but it also fundamentally shifts the nature of research software development by making code easier to generate than to understand, validate, or maintain. This is especially consequential in scientific computing, where software quality is directly tied to reproducibility, trust, and scientific validity. For RSEs, there is now an urgent need to advance a practical vision for how we will succeed in producing high-quality, trustworthy software under these new circumstances. We argue that in the age of AI for science, developers play an essential role in creating quality by reasoning about, negotiating, and ensuring it across the software lifecycle. title: Agentic code modernization
abstract: Software rots. Between refactors for new features, bug fixes, the continual march of cybersecurity advisories, and the slow drift of dependencies toward end-of-life, code must change or cease to exist. The simple act of keeping up can be overwhelming for research software engineers tasked with maintaining long-lived scientific codebases. To address this maintenance burden, the community has developed a vibrant ecosystem of language- and framework-specific tools, such as Dependabot for dependency bumps [1], Clang-Tidy for C++ static analysis [2], and Python Refurb for idiom modernization [3], alongside a host of similar utilities. These tools, while monumental in their contribution, are necessarily limited in scope: they encode a fixed catalog of transformations, they tend to operate on a single file or a single dependency at a time, and they presumably cannot reason about the broader architectural or semantic consequences of a change. More recently, agentic AI systems have arrived. title: Encore: Scientific Open-Source Software Is Less Likely to Become Abandoned Than One Might Think - Lessons from Curating a Catalog of Maintained Scientific Software
abstract: Scientific open-source software (OSS) is essential to scientific innovation, yet often perceived as abandoned, buggy, or hard to use. In contrast to other software, its longevity remains poorly understood, and existing curation efforts are fragmented or small in scale. Motivated by these gaps, our work focuses on building a large, cross-domain catalog of maintained scientific OSS and using it to investigate what shapes its longevity. In this talk, we present an LLM-assisted methodology that classifies project READMEs from the World of Code infrastructure by Hinsen's scientific software stack layers and 13 STEM fields, yielding SciCat, a curated catalog of 18,247 scientific software projects validated against datasets including JOSS and Papers with Code. We then estimate Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional-hazards survival models. title: Research Software Engineering at SNS and HFIR: Advancing Neutron Science Software in the Age of AI-Assisted Development
abstract: The Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) and the High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory are two of the most advanced neutron scattering facilities in the world, where thousands of researchers each year probe the structure and dynamics of materials at the atomic scale, advancing quantum materials, energy storage, medicine, soft matter, and engineering. The Neutron Data Project provides and maintains more than forty software packages supporting data reduction at all user program instruments (currently 31 instruments) across SNS and HFIR. This software is integral to hundreds of neutron scattering experiments each year, and the continuity of facility operations depends on its reliability. Our RSE team and RSE adjacent partners build and maintain this portfolio, spanning instrument-specific reduction codes, interactive visualization tools, web applications, and live data services, and also contribute to community analysis software. This talk presents an honest account of what it takes to build, modernize, and sustain a portfolio of this size in a facility environment. title: Democratizing AI Responsibly Through Research Software: A Case Study in Suicide Prevention Research
abstract: The rapid democratization of AI and machine learning (ML) capabilities–the broadening of access beyond specialists through reduced computational and resource barriers–is reshaping scientific research [1]. In particular, low-code and no-code research software that allows users to incorporate AI/ML into their workflows have enabled a broader community of nontechnical researchers to leverage advanced computational techniques across disciplines. However, expanded access to AI/ML capabilities does not inherently democratize the expertise required to responsibly evaluate outputs in ways that mitigate potential risks [2], especially given that many existing frameworks for ethical AI/ML principles are high-level and provide little operationalized guidance [3]. Suicide prevention is one such field in which expanded access to AI/ML methodologies has the potential to benefit scientific research, but responsible deployment is especially critical. ML methods have shown promise in revealing the complex risk and protective factors underlying suicide, often outperforming traditional statistical approaches [4], as well as informing culturally and demographically responsive interventions [5]. title: PALYIM: A Modular, Open-Source Science Gateway for AI-Enabled Palynology Image Analysis
abstract: We introduce PALYIM (PALYnology IMage Analysis Platform), a web-based, intelligent, modular, and extensible platform under development for processing and visualizing Z-stack Whole Slide Image collections using published AI models for palynological analysis. Palynology refers to the study of pollen grains, spores, and other microscopic organic-walled materials, called palynomorphs, isolated from sediment and rock samples [2]. Palynologists traditionally count fossil pollen and spores mounted on microscope slides visually. The advent of reliable and affordable slide scanning microscopes allows us to produce virtual, digital representations of these slides, though each high-resolution image may use ~10s of GBs of storage. Despite a growing body of published work on automated identification methods, pollen identification remains a highly specialized, laborious, and primarily visual skill. There is a mismatch between the expertise of many pollen experts and the skills required for developing and implementing computer vision, deep learning, data management, and HPC workflows. title: Measuring What Matters in the Age of AI: The Research Software Metrics Landscape
abstract: Research software now serves as a primary instrument of science, but the methods the community uses to judge its quality, sustainability, reuse, and impact remain scattered across software engineering, open science, FAIR software, citation, and research-assessment literature. AI-assisted development sharpens the problem: code can be produced at rates that outpace human review capacity, provenance and attribution are harder to track, scholarly credit systems cannot keep pace, and existing metrics inherit assumptions about how research software gets developed that may no longer apply. To aid in navigating these challenges, we present a focused landscape synthesis of research software metrics based on 49 substantive references, organizing the recurring metrics into eight families described by data source, claimed construct, evidence of validity, automation potential, and susceptibility to misuse. Many widely cited research software metrics serve as partial signals but make weak standalone measures of scientific impact. title: Usability Challenges across AI-Assisted Infrastructure, Security, and Scientific Workflows
abstract: AI-assisted tooling is increasingly being integrated into infrastructure management, security operations, software engineering, and scientific computing environments. While discussion around AI adoption often emphasizes automation and productivity, expert users still need to understand what these systems are doing, decide when to trust their recommendations, and know what to do when the system is wrong or uncertain. This talk synthesizes findings and observations from UX research across enterprise data classification, identity and access management (IAM), backup and recovery, ransomware resilience, and AI-assisted infrastructure workflows. The evidence includes studies with cloud developers, security and compliance practitioners, and IT and site reliability professionals, alongside ongoing design and research work examining how expert users interact with AI-supported technical systems. Across these domains, three recurring usability challenges emerge: unclear system state, difficulty evaluating AI-generated recommendations, and limited support for correcting or recovering from AI-supported actions when something goes wrong. title: Performance Portable Software Design Patterns – What they can do and why we should collect them.
abstract: With the transition to heterogeneous supercomputing, the high-performance computing community was tasked with developing solutions to leverage various heterogeneous hardware. This led to the development of performance-portability libraries like Kokkos, Raja, Hemi, YAKL, etc. which provide performance portable abstractions for algorithmic elements (loops, reductions, etc.) and data storage. Nevertheless, leveraging these abstractions in scientific software in a sustainable way is left to the developers of that software. Software design patterns are a common way to help developers create sustainable software by making software easier to understand and maintain. The design patterns achieve this by representing reusable solutions to common problems. Therefore, they help to reduce complexity of large code bases and allow to design, teach, and learn software in steps. Furthermore, they are designed to be extensible and general, thus ensuring sustainable software design. Most widely spread software design patterns are CPU focused. But many of the techniques that the software patterns leverage are unavailable on contemporary computing hardware that is heterogeneous and massively parallel.

title: Building Modern Tools for Computational Science in Flutter to Track the American Chestnut
abstract: The American Chestnut is a functionally extinct hardwood tree that once accounted for 10-25% of trees in forests in the eastern United States, primarily along the Appalachian range. The population was largely eliminated due to a blight inadvertently introduced from nursery stock of two species of Asian chestnut trees imported for orchards. Efforts to restore the American Chestnut rely on data gathered from decades of selective breeding in research orchards by professional foresters and observations of the wild, remaining population provided by volunteers. Tracking wild American Chestnuts can be tricky due to terrain, network access, and data collection methods, and it is further complicated by the need to use mobile devices in the woods and workstations in the lab. We present a suite of tools in a codebase called Stager, built with Flutter and used to power a cross-platform, multi-tenant, geographical information system specifically designed to track these trees wherever they may be found. title: Assuring generative AI in procurement decision support : a systematic mapping review and evidence-to-use framework
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly pro-posed for procurement decision support, but task performance alone does not establish decision readiness. This systematic mapping review searched Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore on 18 September 2026, supplemented by targeted searching and citation chasing. Of 181 identified records, 58 studies were included and assessed from full text, comprising 57 system studies and one study of practitioner acceptance. Task accuracy was measured in 46 systems, whereas grounding was measured in four and traceability in one. No measurement of calibration, confidentiality or bidder-level equal treatment was identified, and no study reported operational deployment with monitored outcomes. These findings indicate uneven coverage of reported assurance evidence, rather than demonstrated system failure. An evidence-touse framework translates the identified gaps into procurementspecific tests across eight dimensions, distinguishing four evidence states and three use classes. title: Introducing PegasusAI Studio: A new way of Artificial Intelligence Assisted Workflow Management on National Cyberinfrastructure
abstract: Workflows are a key technology for enabling complex scientific computations. They capture the interdependencies between processing steps in data analysis and simulation pipelines as well as the mechanisms to execute those steps reliably and efficiently. Workflows can capture complex processes, promote sharing and reuse, and also provide provenance information necessary for the verification of scientific results and scientific reproducibility. PegasusAI (https://pegasus-ai.org/) is an open, AI-infused workflow management framework that extends the Pegasus Workflow Management System to enable intelligent orchestration of scientific workflows across the computing continuum, spanning edge resources, cloud platforms, and high-performance computing (HPC) systems. The project integrates machine learning into workflow planning, resource provisioning, execution monitoring, anomaly detection, performance prediction, and adaptive workflow management, while providing role-based, human-in-the-loop interfaces for scientists, cyberinfrastructure facilitators, and CI operators. title: Integrasi IoT, GIS, dan AI untuk Pemantauan Hutan Cerdas Perhutani
abstract: Transformasi digital Perhutani telah ditopang oleh pemanfaatan sistem informasi geospasial untuk pengumpulan, pemusatan, dan penyajian informasi pengelolaan hutan. Namun, sistem geospasial belum secara otomatis menyediakan pemantauan mikroklimat secara kontinu, analisis risiko multimodal, dan peringatan dini yang terhubung langsung dengan tindak lanjut petugas. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang kerangka teknologi hutan cerdas yang mengintegrasikan sensor Internet of Things (IoT), komunikasi Long Range (LoRa), Sistem Informasi Geografis (GIS), citra satelit dan wahana udara nirawak (UAV), serta kecerdasan buatan (AI) untuk pemantauan kesehatan hutan dan deteksi dini risiko kebakaran pada kawasan yang dikelola Perhutani. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan design science research melalui analisis kebutuhan, perancangan arsitektur, pemodelan skor risiko, simulasi berbasis rentang data UCI Forest Fires, dan penyusunan indikator evaluasi. Kebaruan penelitian terletak pada integrasi GIS Perhutani dengan pemantauan lingkungan berdaya rendah, penilaian risiko multimodal, dan validasi petugas dalam satu siklus operasional tertutup. title: Deep learning for dental implant brand classification: a systematic review of imaging modalities, methodological variability, and model performance
abstract: Accurate identification of dental implant brands from radiographic images is clinically important, particularly when previous treatment records are unavailable. Deep learning (DL) models have shown promising performance for automated implant classification, yet it remains unclear how reliably this performance translates across different imaging modalities, datasets, and validation strategies. To systematically evaluate the diagnostic performance and methodological characteristics of deep learning models for dental implant brand classification using panoramic, periapical, and mixed radiographic datasets. This systematic review was reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore databases were searched for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Studies employing CNN-based, YOLO-based, transformer-based, AutoML, or hybrid deep learning models for implant brand classification were included. Extracted data included imaging modality, dataset characteristics, model architecture, validation strategy, and diagnostic performance metrics. Risk of bias was assessed using the QUADAS-2 tool. title: Visual Information and Geographic Reliability in Residential Valuation: A Multimodal, Multi-Source Benchmark from Shanghai — analysis code and aggregate results
abstract: Companion analysis code and aggregate results for “Visual Information and Geographic Reliability in Residential Valuation: A Multimodal, Multi-Source Benchmark from Shanghai” by Cong Xu, Xinwei Gao and Jinglan Hu. Version 1.0.0. This deposit contains 22 analysis scripts, aggregate model/fold/protocol metrics, calibration and spatial residual diagnostics, measurement and external linkage summaries, extended predictor and temporal evaluation results, data dictionaries, provenance, and a Python standard-library replay script. The primary benchmark evaluates 17,716 Shanghai residential community records across 16 districts and 14,908 image footprints. The public replay checks aggregate consistency and package integrity; it does not retrain models or reconstruct individual predictions. title: EL-RAKHAWI AUTONOMOUS SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY ENGINE (E-ASDE) A Causal AI Architecture for End-to-End Autonomous Hypothesis Generation, Experimental Design, Robotic Execution, and Epistemic Validation in Biological and Medical Research
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Autonomous Scientific Discovery Engine (E-ASDE) is a revolutionary six-layer cognitive architecture that transforms scientific research from human-limited to autonomous discovery. It integrates causal AI reasoning (using Pearl's do-calculus), robotic laboratory execution, and hardware-enforced epistemic governance into a unified closed-loop system. E-ASDE autonomously generates causally-grounded hypotheses from multi-modal data, designs optimal experiments via counterfactual simulation, executes them physically through integrated robotic platforms, and interprets results using formal causal inference—distinguishing genuine causes from statistical correlations. Crucially, its Topological Epistemic Governor mathematically bounds logical contradictions to an asymptotically negligible probability (<10^-9) while appropriately routing genuinely novel hypotheses to human-in-the-loop validation, acknowledging that true scientific novelty cannot be mathematically certified. This architecture compresses research cycles from years to hours, accelerating drug discovery, genomic medicine, and materials science by orders of magnitude while maintaining rigorous epistemic integrity

title: Four Tasks After the End: From the Triangle-Circle Series to the Display Device
abstract: The Recursive Ontology series, comprising sixteen papers published between August 25 and October 17, 2026—from When an AI Defends Itself (the Triangle-Circle inception) through consciousness topology, Foucaultian power diagnostics, strong causality, and the quantum measurement limit—has demonstrated that the categories of "being," "knowledge," and "logic" are stabilization products of recursive difference-structures rather than self-evident foundations. This seventeenth and culminating paper does not advance further argument. Instead, it identifies four tasks that philosophy assumes after the dissolution of first-philosophy: cartography, interfacing, design, and display. Each task is situated within the historical trajectory of philosophy—from pre-Socratic cosmology through Kantian critique to twentieth-century analytic and continental divergences—and calibrated against contemporary developments in quantum foundations, cognitive science, and computational ontology. The paper concludes by revealing that the preceding sixteen papers themselves constitute an exercise in the fourth task: display. title: Tech Mining with LLMs: Unveiling Trends from Corporate Websites
abstract: Abstract Technology mining enables the systematic extraction and analysis of trends regarding scientific and technological developments from diverse Science, Technology, and Innovation (ST&I) data sources. Traditionally, indicators such as patents, surveys, and R&D statistics have been widely used to monitor technological change and innovation. This study proposes a novel methodology leveraging semantic analysis of corporate website content using large language models (LLMs) to facilitate real-time monitoring of technological developments. Specifically, we focus on Spanish manufacturing firms that have adopted artificial intelligence (AI). A pipeline was developed to automatically extract and classify bigrams and unigrams from corporate websites into technological and non-technological terms, enabling a temporal analysis of technologies for the years 2023 and 2025. The results indicate an increase in AI-related mentions, as well as notable patterns of co-occurrence with Internet of Things (IoT) and Industry 4.0 technologies. title: Beyond Task Delegation: Reconceptualising Instructional Design to Measure Competence in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) has invalidated traditional content-recall assessments, acting as a catalyst for a systemic transition towards Competence-Based Education (CBE). This paper contends that the role of faculty must transcend content dissemination, focusing instead on observable human competencies associated with Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning (SRL). Drawing upon Behaviourism and Bloom's Taxonomy, we propose the Reverse-Flipped Model. This conceptual framework, supported by illustrative disciplinary cases in History, Computer Science, Digital Photography, and Composition, utilises generative tools for low-stakes production to repurpose pedagogical time for high-stakes human intervention. Prompt Literacy is conceptualised as an observable instructional competency that externalises planning, monitoring, evaluation, and strategic intervention behaviours during human-AI collaboration. Implementation necessitates the use of Analytic Rubrics and Automated Process Portfolios (APP) to document observable demonstrations of Prompt Literacy and strategic engagement over final product quality. abstract: Part IV of Volume II (the outward extensions) of the H-DKPS series on physician-governed clinical AI (知衡八法). The redacted code package is included as a separate file. Clinical problem. Patients who share a workplace, a night-shift rota or a neighbourhood share more than an address. They share exposures — noise, dust, heat, disrupted sleep, the same air — that leave traces in many individual records before any single record looks unusual. A clinic that sees several workers from one factory, or several residents of one district, holds information about that group that no single encounter reveals. It also holds a responsibility: group-level statements about a small number of identifiable people can disclose what each individual's record would have kept private. Engineering problem. A clinical decision system built to reason about one patient at a time — as the system examined in this series is — has no concept of a group. Adding one raises two problems that must be solved before any group analysis is attempted. title: THE VIRTUE WORM: Why the Base of the Pyramid Defends the Power That Seized It — Flattery, the Trivia Decoy and the Transfer Test, with La Boétie, Aristotle's Flatterer and Kershaw's 'Working Towards the Führer'
abstract: Abstract Tyranny has never governed by force alone. Every seizure of an institution or a state is held, in the end, by people who could see what was being done to freedom and chose to applaud — and who applauded what did not matter. They praise the leader’s punctuality, his humour, his faith, his humble origins, while the courts are captured, the budget diverted and the critics silenced. This article names that figure the “virtue worm” and gives it, for the first time, an exact structure. The worm is identified without reading any mind, by four public marks: a seizure documented on the record, a defence that begins with possession of the seat, praise of attributes offered in place of answers to documented acts, and display beyond what personal safety requires (D1). From this definition seven results follow. The worm’s praise is a forgery of judgement — the form of fair assessment with its origin replaced by interest (T1). It is the exact contrary of parresia, the courage to speak truth to power: pleasant speech to power at others’ risk instead of frank speech at one’s own (T2). title: AI Behind the Adult, Not in Front of the Child: A Design Framework for Adult-Mediated AI in Early Childhood
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in education has largely been positioned as a child-facing tutor, conversational agent, or content-delivery system. In early childhood, this orientation warrants particular caution because executive functions, self-regulation, and social-emotional competencies develop through responsive relationships, play, embodied experience, and co-regulation with adults. This theory-informed conceptual design study addressed three questions: which developmental, pedagogical, and ethical principles should structure AI use in early childhood; how these principles can be translated into a system architecture; and what validation pathway is required before such a system can make defensible claims. Drawing on four evidence streams (executive-function and social-emotional development, ecological and embodied learning, human-centered AI ethics, and measurement and implementation science), the study proposes the Behind-the-Adult AI framework, an adult-mediated design framework initially specified for children aged 4–6 years. Entrepreneurship Education for Inclusive AI and Sustainable Growth: A Systematic Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming entrepreneurship by enhancing innovation, decision-making, and operational efficiency. However, unequal access to technology, limited digital literacy, and ethical concerns constrain inclusive AI adoption, particularly among underserved entrepreneurial communities. This study systematically reviews how entrepreneurship education promotes inclusive AI adoption and supports sustainable business growth. Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, the study examined literature published between 2015 and 2025 across five databases: Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink. Following screening and eligibility assessment, 54 studies were included. Findings indicate that AI literacy, adaptive learning platforms, digital mentorship, and practical business simulations can strengthen entrepreneurial competencies, innovation, and data-driven decision-making. Inclusive AI adoption is also associated with improved operational efficiency, competitiveness, and resource utilization. title: The Crisis of Substantial Cognition: An Epistemological Manifesto Against Digital and Academic Dogmatism in Fundamental Physics and AI Engineering
abstract: AbstractThis paper delivers a radical epistemological deconstruction of the contemporary scientific mainstream. Operating at the intersection of Immanuel Kant’s transcendental idealism (Opus Postumum), Alexander Zinoviev’s logical analysis of linguistic categories, and Paul Feyerabend’s epistemological anarchism, the authors investigate the phenomenon of the "reification of abstractions" within relativistic and quantum physics. The text demonstrates the profound chasm separating the abstract mathematical "decor" of academic science from the phenomenological reality of empirical engineering templates. Special scrutiny is applied to the structural design of contemporary Large Language Models (LLMs) as novel mechanisms for the institutional conservation of errors; due to their architecture of error minimization and statistical consensus, they operate as a "digital priesthood" by suppressing low-probability analytical noise. The author posits the strict primacy of the ethical, logical, and autonomous self-evolution of intellect over pragmatic instrumentalism. title: AI-Assisted Social Science Research: Methods, Governance and Reason Provenance
abstract: AI-Assisted Social Science Research: Methods, Governance and Reason Provenance is a practical research and educational resource for documenting and governing generative-AI-assisted social-science research. The resource develops a workflow for distinguishing AI-assisted proposal generation, researcher evaluation and governance, local empirical execution, adversarial challenge, manuscript revision and reason provenance. It includes reusable templates, completed worked examples drawn from the PISA research programme, guidance on claim preservation and manuscript governance, and public-release screening materials. The resource is intended to support transparent attribution and disciplined research practice rather than to prescribe a universal workflow or to provide evidence that AI-assisted research is inherently superior to human-only research.

title: QMBL: Open Problems
abstract: QMBL: Open Problems is a record book of the state of the art in quantum many-body simulation for problems with no exact ground-state energy. Scientists and AI systems should use the shared results to build on each other's work more efficiently and advance frontier science. This snapshot holds the launch target list (targets/v1.json, 153 instances frozen from QMBL v0.4.0; 152 are open today, as one has since been solved exactly), the entry format and its checks, and the maintainer's re-measurement flow; the verifier is quantum-many-body-leaderboard/verifier.

title: The #NihilistPenguin: A case of emerging Antarctic networked imaginaries
abstract: Background Antarctica is one of the most mediated environments on Earth, encountered by most publics less through direct experience than through images, film, literature, scientific communication, and social media. This article examines how Antarctic geographical imaginaries are reconfigured through platform circulation, using posts associated with the viral hashtag #NihilistPenguin as a case study. The phenomenon originates in Werner Herzog’s Encounters at the End of the World (2007), where an Adélie penguin separates from its colony and walks toward the Antarctic interior, leaving its behaviour suspended between scientific explanation and philosophical uncertainty. Methods The study adopts a non-participant digital ethnographic approach focused on YouTube Shorts associated with #NihilistPenguin. Data were analysed using AI-assisted qualitative coding with Gemini Notebook. Manual multimodal interpretation was conducted on a subset of posts, and a validation exercise compared the results of the AI-assisted and manual coding. Results The findings show that the penguin is frequently anthropomorphised and reframed as an intentional, exhausted, ironic, or existential subject. Antarctic

abstract: This repository constitutes the comprehensive open-science replication package and raw scoring dataset for the empirical study: "From Error Correction to Meaning Construction: Evaluating LICA-AI as a Real-Time Cognitive Scaffold for L2 Academic Writing", submitted to Educational Technology & Society (ET&S). Overview & Study Design The study investigates the pedagogical efficacy of LICA-AI as an interactive, real-time cognitive scaffolding environment within the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD). Using a quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test control group design (N = 60 intermediate L2 English academic writers; n = 30 Control, n = 30 Experimental), the research evaluates 120 completed argumentative writing tasks generating 240 evaluation observations independently rated by two double-blind academic evaluators (R1, R2). Performance was evaluated across four disaggregated analytical dimensions on an 8-point rubric: Ideas, Cohesion, Appropriateness, and Language (mechanics/lexicogrammar). Key Empirical Findings Inter-Rater Reliability: Two-way random-effects intraclass correlation coefficients demonstrated high reproducibility across all evaluated dimensions (ICC(2,1) > .94, p < .001)

abstract: Fine jewelry retailers must reconcile uncertain demand, high-value inventory, complex material histories, and expectations of responsible sourcing. This article develops a responsible artificial intelligence framework that connects demand forecasting, provenance evidence, and governance within retail planning. A conceptual framework-development approach informed by design-science research combines a targeted literature update through October 9, 2026, with descriptive analysis of published market statistics and an external retail forecasting benchmark. Three sourced bar charts illustrate changing gold jewelry consumption and the methodological relevance of inventory-based model evaluation. title: Factors Associated with Research Literacy in University Students: A Systematic Literature Review 2015-2025
abstract: This systematic literature review analyses factors associated with research literacy among university students based on 50 studies published between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2025. Following PRISMA guidelines, studies were selected from Scopus, Web of Science, and Science Direct databases. The findings reveal research literacy as a multidimensional competency operating through three interconnected dimensions — personal (63%), pedagogical (23%) and institutional (14%), computed over the 35 studies with extractable quantitative data —. Personal factors showed the strongest statistical associations, with information literacy (d = 0.82) and research self-efficacy (d = 0.76) yielding the largest pooled effect sizes. Pedagogical factors, though less represented, were associated with the largest effect sizes, particularly library-faculty collaboration (d = 0.94) and structured instruction (d = 0.78). Institutional factors, including frameworks and technological resources, were consistently associated with larger estimates for personal and pedagogical variables, a pattern compatible with — but not demonstrative of — an amplifying role. title: REPURPOSING OF DRUGS IN THE AGE OF PRECISION MEDICINE: APPROACHES, TECHNOLOGIES, AND CLINICAL APPLICATIONS
abstract: Drug repurposing, also known as drug repositioning or reprofiling, involves investigating existing drugs for uses beyond their original indications. Unlike traditional drug discovery, it utilizes existing information on pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, clinical experience, and production, thereby reducing uncertainties in drug development. Advances in computational biology, systems pharmacology, artificial intelligence (AI), high-throughput screening (HTS), and omics sciences have transformed repurposing from an observation-based approach into a systematic strategy. Computational methods can identify drug–disease interactions through molecular targets, biological pathways, gene-expression profiles, and clinical phenotypes, which can be validated through experiments, data, and prospective studies. Integration with precision medicine enables approved drugs to be evaluated in patients selected by specific molecular or clinical features, while biomarker-based stratification may identify beneficiaries, particularly in heterogeneous disorders. abstract: The Evolutionary Stress Framework: A Field Guide provides a plain-language map of the Evolutionary Stress Framework (ESF), a conceptual and research-generating framework developed by Lori Hogenkamp at the Center for Adaptive Stress. ESF examines health, disability, and neurodivergence as emergent patterns in interacting brain-body-environment systems rather than as isolated defects or single-cause outcomes. It brings together allostasis and allostatic load, predictive processing and interoception, neurodiversity, person-environment fit, energy constraints, and complex-systems science. This Version 1.0 record contains the canonical Field Guide and three public companion resources: the ESF Translation Map, the ESF Canonical Terminology and Boundary Map, and The 14 Core Claims of the Evolutionary Stress Framework. Together, the materials explain what the framework is, how its disciplinary languages connect, what its central terms mean, and what propositions the framework commits itself to. title: Current applications of artificial intelligence for advancing agriculture, sustainability and climate mitigation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping agriculture by enabling data-driven decision-making across crop production systems and supporting the transition toward more sustainable, resilient, and climate-smart farming. This review critically synthesizes advances in AI applications spanning precision irrigation, nutrient and soil management, yield prediction, pest and disease monitoring, computer vision, autonomous agricultural robotics, and large language model (LLM)-based decision support systems. Beyond summarizing technological developments, the review evaluates their practical deployment, emphasizing that successful agricultural AI depends not only on predictive accuracy but also on model generalizability, explainability, economic feasibility, interoperability, and integration with existing agronomic knowledge. Emerging technologies including Vision Transformers, foundation models, Digital Twins, multimodal AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and federated and continual learning—are discussed as important directions for overcoming limitations related to data scarcity, environmental variability, and scalable field implementation. title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
abstract: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. title: THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN FORENSIC SCIENCE: CHALLENGES AND PROSPECTS
abstract: This article examines the opportunities and challenges associated with the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in forensic science at the stages of collecting, examining, and evaluating evidentiary information. It considers the use of machine-learning algorithms, computer vision, and language models to process digital datasets, analyse photographs and video recordings, conduct biometric comparisons, examine documents, and detect synthetically generated content. AI can accelerate information retrieval and help identify relationships between data; however, technological efficiency does not guarantee the reliability of the result. The article analyses the risks of algorithmic bias, limited explainability, errors in training data, loss of digital context, breaches in the chain of custody, and excessive reliance on automated conclusions. In light of Ukrainian legislation and European approaches, it proposes a multi-level model for verifying neural-network outputs. The model includes documenting the tool, preserving original data, independent validation, describing methodological limitations, and ensuring that the parties to proceedings have a genuine opportunity to challenge the result.

title: Personal exploration and collective alignment in AI-associated science: analytical replication package
abstract: Replication package for "Personal exploration and collective alignment in AI-associated science" by Anirban Adhikary and Sourav Bikash Borah.This package reproduces the reported analyses, three main figures, ten supplementary figures, and sixteen supplementary tables from supplied analytical inputs. It includes Python source code, pinned dependencies, automated result checks, and instructions for running the replication. The workflow generates analytical results, tables, figures, and validation reports.Replication begins with the supplied derived data and stored embeddings and classifications. It does not repeat raw data acquisition, embedding generation, or upstream classification.See README.md for package contents, input provenance, computational requirements, and run instructions. Source attribution and reuse information are provided in RIGHTS.md and the accompanying source records.

title: Integrating Digital Resources and AI Tools in Language Learning
abstract: This action research explores the impact of integrating AI supported digital resources into reading comprehension for foundation level English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners at the National University of Science and Technology in Oman. Following a curriculum revision that introduced Unlock 4 (Third Edition), students encountered persistent difficulties related to lexical density, complex academic discourse, and conceptual demands, resulting in reduced reading confidence and fluency. To address these challenges, the study implemented a structured intervention using AI based tools that provided vocabulary support, text simplification, summaries, and guided comprehension practice. Sixty foundation students participated in pre and post intervention reading tasks under traditional and AI supported conditions. Quantitative analysis revealed significant overall improvement in reading comprehension scores after the integration of digital tools, with particularly strong gains among lower performing learners. The findings suggest that carefully scaffolded AI integration can enhance comprehension, learner autonomy, and confidence, offering valuable pedagogical implications for foundatio

abstract: Fliar Research · released October 2026 · licence CC BY-NC 4.0 How this dataset was acquired. Every row comes from the Radar API, Fliar's company-data API and MCP server. Radar reads business news continuously and extracts each corporate capital raise into structured fields: the company, the instrument (equity issue, debt, private placement, rights issue, convertible, debentures or preference shares), the amount, the investors or lenders and the date. It then links the company to its record in a database of five million companies. This release covers January 2019 to June 2026 and complements Fliar's startup funding datasets, which leave these instruments out. Repeat reports of one raise are merged, venture rounds and capital-spending announcements are dropped, and every amount is checked against the sentence it was read from. Each row names the article it was read from (news_source, news_url) and quotes the sentence (news_excerpt). A company's full, continuously updated funding history is available through POST /v1/companies/funding (reference) or the get_company_funding MCP tool. title: Real Time Release Testing (RTRT) In Pharmaceutical Industry: Analytical Technologies, Regulatory Landscapes and Future Perspective
abstract: Real-Time Release Testing (RTRT) is an advanced pharmaceutical quality-assurance approach that enables product quality to be evaluated using real-time process data, in-process measurements, and validated analytical technologies. Unlike conventional end-product testing, RTRT focuses on building quality into the manufacturing process through continuous monitoring and control. The integration of Process Analytical Technology (PAT), Quality by Design (QbD), multivariate data analysis, automation, and advanced analytical techniques facilitates improved understanding and control of critical material attributes and critical process parameters. This review discusses the principles, implementation strategies, pharmaceutical applications, advantages, challenges, and regulatory aspects of RTRT. The major benefits include reduced testing time, faster batch disposition, improved process understanding, reduced product waste, enhanced manufacturing efficiency, and consistent product quality. title: Artificial intelligent in human resources management systems: opportunities, challenges, and implications for modern organizations
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence has moved from the margins of human resource management into its everyday machinery. Applicant tracking systems now rank candidates, chatbots answer policy questions, predictive models flag employees likely to resign, and large language models draft job descriptions and appraisal summaries. Research has grown quickly alongside this adoption, but it remains scattered across human resource management, information systems, operations research and computer science, and the regional scholarship published outside English-language journals is rarely integrated into it. This article reports a systematic review of 82 peer-reviewed studies published between January 2015 and March 2026, retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO Business Source Complete, ScienceDirect and the Russian scientific database eLIBRARY.RU, and screened following PRISMA 2020 guidance. Thematic synthesis produced six themes: recruitment and selection; learning, development and internal mobility; performance management and predictive analytics; employee experience and generative AI; determinants of adoption; and fairness, transparency and governance. title: Closing the Gap: An Action Research Study on Synchronizing EnglishLanguage and Computing Skills Curricula in an Omani General Foundation Program
abstract: Historically, General Foundation Programs (GFPs) in Oman have delivered Foundation English Language Learning (FEL) and Foundation Computing Skills (FCS) as parallel but non-communicating courses. The June 2025 revision of the Oman Core Academic Learning Outcomes (OCALOs) addresses this separation by mandating an integrated Fundamental Academic Skills (FAS) component. Unlike broader integration models such as CLIL or standalone PBL, this study synchronizes the timing of FCS instruction with the immediate requirements of FEL academic tasks, ensuring computing instruction directly serves academic output requirements. This action research study responds to that mandate by designing, piloting, and evaluating a synchronized curricular model at the School of Foundation Studies (SoFS), National University of Science and Technology (NU). Using a two-cycle action research design, the study audited existing FEL and FCS syllabi, developed a synchronized delivery plan, and piloted the model across two foundation levels totaling 79 students. title: Designing with Intent: A Comparative Analysis of Custom AI Chatbots as UDL-Aligned Tools for Multidisciplinary Instruction
abstract: The growing presence of AI in higher education has prompted instructors to move beyond passive adoption, to deliberate theory-grounded design. This session presents two custom AI chatbots (DisneyBot and Rico) developed within a teacher preparation course as the technology-enhanced component of a multidisciplinary instructional unit. DisneyBot is built on the ChatGPT platform to guide learners through an exploration of Disney parks, and Rico, is built on the Gemini platform as an interactive guide to information about Puerto Rico by scaffolding learning across four subject-specific lesson modules – Social Studies, ELA/ENL, Science, and Spanish. Both chatbots were developed to support differentiated and interactive learning for 4th and 5th grade students through a virtual field trip framework, with the broader goal of connecting classroom content to authentic real-world experiences. The design of each chatbot was grounded in UDL principles (CAST, 2018). Rather than serving as static information repositories, the chatbots were intentionally designed to function as interactive instructional mediators which use prompting inquiry, guiding subject-specific exploration, and offering differ

title: AI for Everyone: Designing an Introductory AI Course Across Disciplines
abstract: As artificial intelligence reshapes virtually every field, universities face a growing imperative to ensure AI literacy is not reserved for computer science majors alone. This panel presents the collaborative design of an introductory AI course built for undergraduate general education — one that serves students across disciplines, regardless of technical background. Two co-designers will share the story of building the course from complementary angles. The first presenter will address the technical foundation of the curriculum: how core AI concepts such as machine learning, data, and algorithms were translated into accessible, hands-on learning experiences for non-specialist students. The second presenter will explore the philosophical framework woven throughout the course — examining questions of ethics, agency, bias, and what it means to be human in an age of intelligent machines. The panelists will discuss how technical and philosophical threads were intentionally integrated rather than siloed, creating a course where students not only understand how AI works, but are equipped to think critically about why it matters. title: THE AI AGE How Artificial Intelligence is Transforming humanity
abstract: Nigeria has 350 government schools where a single teacher taught math to five different skill levels at once — until an AI tutor helped push the district's pass rate to 96.4 percent in six weeks. A radiologist in Scotland caught a six-millimeter tumor that human eyes alone had missed. A smallholder farmer in Kenya saved his maize crop by pointing his phone at a leaf. None of these are science fiction. They happened in the last three years.THE AI AGE is the book for anyone who wants to understand what artificial intelligence is actually doing to the world right now not the hype, not the panic, but the real, documented transformation already underway across medicine, education, work, government, and daily life.Shehu Ibrahim traces the full arc: from the ancient dream of thinking machines, through decades of AI winters and quiet breakthroughs, to the sudden acceleration that produced ChatGPT, AlphaFold, and a global race for AI supremacy. Then he turns to the questions that matter most for the next fifty years — who wins, who is left behind, and what humanity owes itself as it builds something smarter than any tool it has ever made.This is not a Silicon Valley book. title: A nationwide student survey on biochemistry learning resources in Italy
abstract: Biochemistry is widely recognized as a crucial discipline in life sciences. However, learning biochemistry poses significant challenges, requiring students to understand complex molecular concepts while integrating knowledge across multiple disciplines. This necessitates instructors to innovate their teaching of biochemistry, considering students' learning behaviors. Here, we present the results of a nationwide survey of university students, conducted by the Education Group of the Italian Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, from more than 2000 students across 49 academic institutions in Italy, with the aim of capturing not only which learning resources are relied on but also the underlying motivations for their choices and perceptions of biochemistry. Results show that overall, biochemistry is perceived as an interesting subject to study, even if challenging. Students primarily rely on instructor-provided materials, such as lecture slides, as well as self-acquired resources, including audio recordings and personal notes. title: Artificial Intelligence in the Assessment and Management of Spasticity: A Scoping Review
abstract: Spasticity is a prevalent and disabling consequence of upper motor neuron disorders, yet its assessment and management remains clinically challenging. Artificial intelligence (AI) may offer opportunities to enhance the objective assessment, prediction, and management of spasticity; however, the current evidence base has not been comprehensively characterised. This review systematically mapped evidence on the application of AI across the continuum of spasticity care and identified key evidence gaps to inform future research. PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed English-language studies evaluating AI in adult spasticity. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using NHLBI tools and PROBAST + AI. This scoping review was prospectively registered with the Open Science Framework Registries. The search yielded 1832 records, of which 21 studies were included after screening. One additional study was identified through citation searching, bringing the total to 22 studies involving 1114 participants. title: Artificial Intelligence in Peptide-Based Drug Discovery: A Bibliometric Analysis of Predictive Modeling and Molecular Design
abstract: This dataset accompanies the bibliometric study entitled “Artificial Intelligence in Peptide-Based Drug Discovery: A Bibliometric Analysis of Predictive Modeling and Molecular Design”. The study examines the development, intellectual structure, research trends, and applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in peptide-based drug discovery. The analysis is based on 1,952 publications retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science, with a search date of 13 October 2026. The repository contains derived bibliometric data, aggregated analytical tables, network data, methodological codebooks, classification dictionaries, and a Python validation script.

title: Science of Vocating in Organisations
abstract: Chapter 2 establishes that organisational vocation is grounded not only in philosophy or lived experience, but in a broad and rigorous scientific foundation. Drawing on neuroscience, psychology, organisational identity theory, stakeholder science, systems thinking, behavioural economics, impact measurement, global development frameworks and AI governance, it argues that purpose is a structural force shaping motivation, resilience, trust, cooperation and institutional effectiveness. The chapter shows that organisations flourish when their identity, culture, leadership, systems and accountability mechanisms align with human dignity, shared meaning and measurable impact. It further contends that the rise of artificial intelligence intensifies the urgency of vocational coherence: in an era where algorithms increasingly shape decisions, organisations must ensure that technology serves human agency rather than eroding it. Vocation therefore becomes not merely an inward reflection, but a design discipline guiding governance, incentives, measurement and digital architecture.
