title: How Charting is Changing: Insights for Interprofessional Communication Curriculum
abstract: With the shift to electronic health records (EHR's), patients have gained increasing real-time access to their medical charts. This poses challenges for new providers, including adapting to broader audiences for their charting and attending to newly embedded AI inputs and alerts. However, health care curriculum has been slow to incorporate these new technologies into student training, especially training for interprofessional communication. This experience report will share findings from three focus groups with health science faculty. The focus group conversations investigated instructor perspectives on how emerging technologies—including patient documentation— are impacting clinical practice and how these technologies might best be integrated into curriculum. Next, I discuss how these findings have informed curriculum design in interprofessional communication, including how I revised a traditional telephone group activity to attend to multiple modes of communication. I end with recommendations for technical communication researchers to collaborate on charting pedagogies in the health sciences.

title: Mapping the Research Landscape of Artificial Intelligence and Lifelong Learning: A Scientometric Analysis Using ScientoPy
abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and lifelong learning has attracted growing educational, computational, and policy attention, yet its intellectual structure has not been mapped systematically. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the AI-lifelong learning literature indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection between 2014 and 2024. Records retrieved from both databases (N = 347) were merged and duplicated in ScientoPy, yielding 259 unique documents. Research momentum was quantified with three time-normalized indicators, average growth rate (AGR), average documents per year (ADY), and percentage of documents published in the last years (PDLY), across six analytical dimensions. Output grew from one document in 2014 to 116 in 2024; across the five principal document types (n = 220), 70.5% of records appeared in 2023-2024. Conference papers (41.3%) and journal articles (38.2%) predominated, with articles expanding fastest (AGR = 21.5; PDLY = 71.7%). Education & Educational Research recorded the highest normalized momentum among subject categories (AGR = 7.0; PDLY = 89.5%). Performance of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms in prediction of breast cancer distant metastasis via imaging: a systematic review and meta‑analysis
abstract: Distant metastasis is a major cause of breast cancer mortality. Early prediction may support risk-adapted surveillance and treatment planning. We evaluated imaging-based machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models for predicting future distant metastasis in patients without baseline metastatic disease. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and supplementary Google Scholar searches were performed through June 2025. Eligible studies evaluated imaging-based AI prediction models and reported quantitative performance. The primary outcome was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST + AI. Random-effects meta-analysis, exploratory subgroup analyses, and univariable meta-regression were performed. Nine studies contributed 43 model evaluations. The pooled model-level AUC was 0.80 (95% CI: 0.77–0.84). A secondary analysis restricted to the best-performing model from each study yielded an AUC of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.83–0.95). CT-based models were associated with higher AUCs than MRI-based models (0.83 vs. 0.71), and models incorporating clinicopathological features had higher AUCs than imaging-only models (0.91 vs. 0.74). title: Comment on egusphere-2026-5661
abstract: Abstract. Compound flooding (CoMF) has emerged as a critical natural hazard for coastal and estuarine regions, where interacting fluvial, pluvial, groundwater, tidal, and storm surge processes generate non-linear amplification effects that challenge conventional single driver flood risk assessments. Yet, despite major advances in compound flood science, integrated literature reviews that link multivariate hazard dynamics, modelling approaches, risk management, and climate adaptation strategies remain limited. This systematic review synthesises three decades of research on CoMF in Cork Harbour and Catchment (CHC), a highly dynamic coastal-estuarine system increasingly exposed to climate change. Following PRISMA guidelines, 503 documents were screened across Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and grey literature sources, identifying 59 peer-reviewed articles and 28 technical reports and policy documents published between 1991 and 2025. This review provides two key contributions of international importance. title: Fairness, Trust and Understanding As Preconditions and Predictors for Industry 5.0 AI Adoption
abstract: Background Workplace adoption of AI technologies depends, not only on technical performance, but also on whether people perceive these systems as fair, trustworthy, and understandable. Existing research utilises varied definitions for these concepts, impeding our understanding of how these factors contribute to AI adoption. Additionally, these concepts are often explored separately, yet in practice they interact. It is hypothesised that perceptions of fairness shape trust, and understanding mediates both. However, there is no shared conceptual framework that clarifies how these dimensions influence sustainable adoption. Research Approach A systematic review and meta-analysis was undertaken to collate definitions of fairness, trust, and understanding, and to aggregate findings across the literature. Drawing on interdisciplinary research from computer science,philosophy of technology, human-computer interaction, and ELSA research, the work develops a preliminary integrative framework. The approach combines conceptual analysis with synthesis of empirical insights from studies on user perceptions, transparency practices, and socio-technical alignment. title: The Evolution of Crime Analysis and Criminal Justice
abstract: Chapter 1 traces the long arc of crime solving from ancient civilizations to modern intelligence-driven policing. It begins with early justice systems such as the Code of Hammurabi, where punishment and social order outweighed investigative rigor, and moves through Greek, Roman, and medieval practices shaped by divine judgment and communal enforcement. The chapter highlights the emergence of early detectives such as Vidocq, whose use of informants and undercover work laid the groundwork for modern intelligence methods. It then examines the rise of formal policing under Sir Robert Peel, the development of forensic science, from fingerprinting to DNA, and the parallel growth of intelligence analysis through OSINT, HUMINT, SIGINT, and fusion centers. Chapter 1 concludes with an overview of contemporary crime analysis tools, including predictive analytics, GIS mapping, biometrics, and AI driven digital forensics, emphasizing how centuries of innovation have shaped today&s;s data-driven approach to criminal justice

Digital transformation and artificial intelligence in organic supply chains: A systematic review with insights from South Tamil Nadu
abstract: Organic agriculture is growing rapidly in India, yet organic supply chains remain structurally fragmented, particularly in smallholder-dominated regions such as South Tamil Nadu. Digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) offer promising solutions to persistent challenges, including inadequate cold-chain infrastructure, limited traceability, intermediary-dependent marketing and certification workflow inefficiencies. This systematic review draws on evidence from 30 peer-reviewed and institutional publications. These sources were identified through a PRISMA-compliant search of Scopus, Elsevier, Taylor & Francis, Web of Science, IEEE, MDPI, Wiley, FAO, and government databases. The findings indicate that AI-enabled precision farming, machine learning-based demand forecasting, Internet of Things-enabled cold-chain monitoring, and blockchain-supported traceability improve production efficiency, market access and organic supply chain transparency. title: Artificial intelligence empowering the diagnosis and treatment of rotator cuff tears
abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being developed for image acquisition, quantitative tissue assessment, diagnosis, and clinical prediction in rotator cuff tears. The breadth of this literature and its methodological limitations have not been integrated across the complete care pathway. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 5, 2026 for English-language original studies applying AI to rotator cuff-related reconstruction, segmentation or quantitative imaging, diagnosis or classification, anatomical measurement, or prognosis. Two reviewers screened reports and extracted study, data, model, validation, reference standard, and performance characteristics. Diagnostic accuracy studies were assessed with QUADAS-2 and prediction-model studies with PROBAST. Because clinical tasks, modalities, models, reference standards, and reported metrics were not sufficiently comparable, evidence was synthesized narratively rather than pooled statistically. title: rbaa-validation: Back-Test of Risk-Based Attention Allocation (RBAA) on Real Open Data — Eurostat AI Adoption and 284,807 Real Transactions
abstract: Abstract:This software package is an empirical companion to the article "Cognitive Optimisation of SME Decision-Making through Risk-Based Allocation of Managerial Attention" (Administrative Sciences, MDPI). Its self-contained Google Colab notebook validates the risk-based attention allocation (RBAA) rule with real, openly licensed data in two parts. Part A documents the context from Eurostat (isoc_eb_ai). In 2025, 55.0% of large EU enterprises used AI, compared with 20.0% of all enterprises. Part B is a counterfactual back-test on 284,807 real card transactions with confirmed fraud outcomes (ULB/Worldline, ODbL). An AI model trained on earlier data supplies calibrated error probabilities. RBAA is then compared, in euros and under the same managerial attention budget, with amount-based approval limits, random spot checks and an AI-score alert queue. title: Technostress in the age of digital transformation and AI: A bibliometric–systematic literature review for HRM research
abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are reshaping human resource management through algorithmic recruitment, automated evaluation, predictive analytics, and generative tools. While these systems improve efficiency, they also intensify technostress through opacity, surveillance, reduced control, and digitally intensified work arrangements. Responding to a fragmented literature spanning both AI-enabled and broader digital work systems, this study provides a B-SLR that maps technostress in digital transformation while identifying AI-specific stressors as a key emerging stream for HRM research. Drawing on 194 Scopus-indexed articles, we combine performance analysis and science mapping to identify publication trends, dominant themes, and intellectual structures. The review shows how AI-specific stressors extend established technostress mechanisms and shift attention toward transparency, control, fairness, and responsible HRM design. We conclude with actionable implications for researchers and practitioners aiming to design more transparent, responsible, and sustainable digital and AI-enabled HRM systems.

title: Nursing leadership and performance metrics in artificial intelligence integrated gastrointestinal surgical care: A narrative review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into gastrointestinal and complex surgical care, yet its practical impact on nursing work remains insufficiently defined.This narrative review examines how nursing leadership can support the safe use of AI across perioperative pathways and how its effects can be evaluated through measurable nursing-sensitive outcomes.Literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, with emphasis on peer-reviewed studies, systematic reviews, guidelines, consensus statements, and implementation frameworks relevant to gastrointestinal surgery, perioperative nursing, clinical decision support, and AI.The review focuses on preoperative assessment, intraoperative coordination, postoperative surveillance, and discharge planning in high-acuity surgical settings.Particular attention is given to workflow efficiency, response times, early recognition of complications, risk-stratified care, documentation quality, interdisciplinary communication, cognitive workload, and patient safety.The proposed framework is intended as a practical, non-validated structure for future evaluation rather than as an established measurement instrume

title: Machine Learning in Hand Pathology Diagnosis: A Narrative Review of Current Insights
abstract: Machine learning (ML), a subset of artificial intelligence (AI), is revolutionizing health care. Given the intricate anatomy and functional complexity of the hand, AI applications in hand pathology are gaining prominence, particularly in the diagnosis of fractures, nerve injuries, and musculoskeletal disorders. This review summarizes ML advancements in hand pathology diagnosis, enhancing clinical history analysis, examination findings interpretation, and imaging assessment. A systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1901 to March 2025 was conducted, focusing on ML applications in diagnosing hand fractures, tendon injuries, and nerve compressions. The inclusion criteria encompassed original research, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and observational studies that demonstrated the use of AI in diagnostic imaging, preoperative assessment, or postoperative management. Studies that did not involve AI-driven diagnostic applications or lacked sufficient methodological transparency were excluded. title: From Anthropomorphism to Trust: Unpacking the Role of Authenticity in Generative AI and Large Language Models—A Structured Literature Review and Future Research Agenda
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has changed the conditions under which users encounter and evaluate machine-produced communication. In systems based on large language models, conversational output is no longer merely functional; it can be fluent, context-aware, and socially legible, inviting judgments that extend beyond usefulness, accuracy, or efficiency. Yet the literature still tends to treat anthropomorphism, perceived authenticity, and trust as largely separate constructs, without sufficiently explaining how human-like cues become credible in the eyes of users and how this credibility shapes trust. To address this problem, the present structured literature review synthesizes recent research on anthropomorphism, authenticity-related evaluations, and trust in AI-mediated interaction, with particular attention to conversational AI, generative AI, and LLM-based systems. A structured search in the Web of Science Core Collection identified 655 records; after duplicate removal, screening, and eligibility assessment, 96 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis. title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases
abstract: Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated work

title: Data Management Plan for Project titled: Sexualised Deepfake Violence on Reddit: Understanding Creation, Consumption, and Policing Prevention
abstract: Sexualised deepfake violence against women and girls (VAWG) is a rapidly emerging form of image-based sexual abuse (IBSA). Deepfake technology uses deep learning–based artificial intelligence (AI) to generate realistic but entirely fabricated sexualised images, videos, or audio. While technical research on detection has expanded significantly, socio-legal and social science research examining how deepfake abuse is understood, normalised, and legitimised within online communities remains limited. There is seldom investigation of the everyday sense-making practices through which deepfake creation and consumption are justified, minimised, or contested within more mainstream online environments, representing a significant empirical and methodological gap for policing and prevention-focused responses. This project is designed as a pilot study to address that gap by developing and testing a scalable methodology for analysing deepfake-related discourse. The pilot focuses on Reddit, which has been identified as a key site for deepfake-related discussion, offering relative anonymity, fewer constraints on text length, and suitability for exploratory qualitative analysis (Gamage et al., 2022)

title: Neutral by Design: More Than a Century of Hidden Bias in Classification Systems
abstract: Classification systems often present themselves as neutral tools while carrying the hierarchies of the people who design them. This paper follows that pattern across three settings. In nineteenth-century ethnology, Frederick Douglass and W.E.B. Du Bois exposed race science as prejudice dressed in method, years before Franz Boas made similar arguments with the authority of the academy behind him. In late-twentieth-century American English, Jane Hill showed how Mock Spanish passed off a racist stereotype as friendly humor. In current AI practice, cultural labels in persona schemas draw stereotyped behavior out of language models, a finding supported by independent studies and by counterfactual audits of the MatrAIx framework. The same mechanism recurs in all three: the category is built by those with power, framed as neutral, completed by its audience, denied by its users, and cited as its own proof. Because corrections layered on top of a label have repeatedly failed, the paper argues for removing cultural labels and describing situations instead, and offers six recommendations for the designers, engineers, researchers, and product managers who build and use persona systems.

Multi-Criteria Decision-Making in Construction Management: A Bibliometric Analysis of the Integration of MCDM, BIM, and Artificial Intelligence (2015–2025)
abstract: The construction industry faces growing challenges that require better decision-making frameworks. Combining Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) with digital tools like Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a promising way forward. Yet their integration remains fragmented across research efforts, revealing a significant gap in theory and practice. As a result, their potential remains underutilized, limiting the development of flexible, data-driven decision-making tools for complex construction projects. This study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to map the development and structure of the MCDM-BIM-AI connection in construction management from 2015 to 2025. Using a PRISMA-compliant protocol, we analyzed 253 peer-reviewed articles from the Scopus database. Our approach combines performance analysis with science mapping through keyword co-occurrence networks and thematic evolution analysis across three time periods: 2015-2018, 2019-2021, 2022-2025, along with a country-level co-authorship network analysis. title: From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology
abstract: Two paradigms now drive the life sciences. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high-dimensional datasets of modern biology. Each has delivered major advances on its own. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry. In this review we propose a three-part taxonomy of integration strategies, namely AI-accelerated mechanistic modeling, mechanism-informed AI, and hybrid models spanning one-directional sequential coupling and bidirectional iterative systems, and we survey their applications in systems and synthetic biology, pharmacology and drug discovery, epidemiology, and neuroscience. We then examine seven challenges that stand in the way: interpretability, data sparsity, causality, identifiability, computational scale, multimodal integration, and validation and generalization, and we close with a view of biological digital twins, causal discovery engines, and automated science. title: CodeGrade: An AI-Augmented Automated Code Grading and Mentoring Platform Integrating Multi-Dimensional Evaluation, Socratic Tutoring, and Gamified Arena Mechanics
abstract: Traditional automated code evaluation systems in Computer Science (CS) education predominantly rely on deterministic input-output string matching. While effective for assessing basic execution correctness, classical autograders fail to evaluate code readability, structural logic, algorithmic efficiency, and Big-O asymptotic complexity. Furthermore, students receive cryptic error tracebacks without pedagogical guidance, leading to reduced engagement and persistent anti-patterns. To overcome these constraints, this paper presents CodeGrade, an end-to-end AI-augmented code evaluation and mentoring platform. CodeGrade integrates a Web-based Microsoft Monaco VS Code editing engine, an isolated dual-sandbox execution environment (Judge0 containerized runner), and a Large Language Model (Groq Llama 3.3 70B) into a unified microservices architecture. The platform introduces a multi-dimensional 60/20/20 Grading Matrix that balances functional correctness (60%), AI structural logic quality (20%), and Big-O asymptotic complexity alignment (20%). Additionally, CodeGrade incorporates an AI-powered Socratic Logic Tutor enforcing strict zero-code-leakage constraints, a Monaco Line-by-Line Refacto

title: Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery and Development: Current Advances and Future Perspectives
abstract: Developing a new medicine takes years of research and requires many decisions along the way. Researchers must identify a promising biological target, find or design a suitable compound, test its safety, and determine whether it benefits patients. Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to support each of these steps. Machine-learning systems can analyse large biological and chemical datasets, while newer generative models can suggest molecules for further study. AI can also help predict drug properties, identify possible new uses for existing medicines, and improve aspects of clinical-trial planning. These developments are encouraging, but they need to be viewed realistically. A computer-generated prediction is only a starting point: it must be tested in the laboratory and, ultimately, in people. AI systems can also be affected by incomplete or biased data, may not work well on unfamiliar problems, and can be difficult to interpret. This review discusses how AI is being used across drug discovery and development, what its current strengths and limitations are, and what will be needed for its responsible use. title: Reframing Hybrid Feedback in Japanese University EFL Writing: Complementary Roles of Peer Feedback and Generative AI
abstract: The present classroom-based exploratory study re-examines hybrid feedback in a Japanese university EFL writing course for science majors. Thirty-six students used both peer feedback and ChatGPT-based feedback during a 12-week semester. Drawing on end-of-course questionnaires and a focused analysis of drafts, peer comments, AI feedback, and revisions, the study asked how students perceived the roles of peer and AI feedback and what pedagogical implications follow for hybrid feedback design. The findings suggested a complementary rather than competitive relationship. Peer feedback primarily supported content development, organization, reader awareness, and collaborative engagement, whereas generative AI primarily supported grammar, wording, and immediate local revision. When combined, the two sources appeared to encourage iterative revision and confidence; however, some students also experienced overload and difficulty prioritizing multiple comments. The paper argues that the value of hybrid feedback lies not in replacing human interaction with AI but in assigning distinct pedagogical roles to different feedback sources. title: Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence in the Development of Gastro-Retentive Drug Delivery Systems: Current Advances & Future Prospectives
abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) into pharmaceutical sciences is reshaping the development of advanced drug delivery systems. Traditional gastroprotective drug delivery systems (GRDDS) are designed to prolong the residence time of oral dosage forms in the stomach to enhance bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy for drugs with narrow absorption windows. However, conventional formulation development often relies on empirical optimization, which is time-consuming and resource-intensive. AI and ML bring a data-driven paradigm to this complex landscape by enabling computational modeling, predictive analytics, and intelligent optimization of formulation parameters. These technologies can analyze multidimensional datasets to identify patterns and relationships between formulation components, physiological variables, and release kinetics that would be challenging to discern using traditional methods. AI-assisted models such as artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and Bayesian optimization have demonstrated significant potential in predicting drug release profiles, selecting optimal polymer systems, and simulating gastric behavior.

title: Bridging the Computational Gap in the Social Sciences: Dual Innovations in Pedagogy and Assessment
abstract: In a world increasingly dominated by data, graduates in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) fields are in high demand. This focus often obscures the fact that a significant portion of digital data is social in nature, generated through human–computer interactions. Consequently, experts trained in the social sciences should be equally sought after, yet this is not consistently the case. A contributing factor is the tendency for social and political science departments to adhere to traditional disciplinary boundaries, inadvertently marginalizing their graduates from a growing number of data-centric professions. This paper argues that this gap can and should be addressed. We present a pedagogical project initiated at the University of Bologna, centered on a tailored data literacy and social computing course designed for Political Science students. This study evaluates a dual-case pedagogical investigation evaluating two complementary but empirically independent educational initiatives—conducted across distinct courses, student cohorts, and academic years—unified under an overarching conceptual framework for social science data literacy. title: AI Tools for Literature Review vs Dissertation Literature Review Writing Services: An Honest Comparison (2026)
abstract: Key Takeaways AI tools for literature review speed up searching, mapping, screening and summarising, but they do not write a critical synthesis for you, and every source they surface still needs checking. This guide compares 16 tools by literature review stage, with free plans and starting prices checked on each provider's website in September 2026. Literature review writing services offer human synthesis, subject expertise and structure at a higher cost, and must be used within your university's academic integrity rules. A literature review is a critical analysis and synthesis of existing literature related to a dissertation topic. However, its core "confrontational" philosophy—continuously seeking chemical small molecules (drugs) for "blockade," "suppression," and "poisoning," along with tumor resection, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy—inevitably harms innocent cells while attacking targets, producing systemic toxic side effects that severely affect patients' quality of life. Moreover, drug resistance, toxic side effects, and "treating symptoms without addressing root causes" have become increasingly prominent. title: Thyroid storm and cardiac arrest: a scoping review of case presentations
abstract: Abstract Background Thyroid storm complicated by cardiac arrest is infrequently reported. Although established guidance addresses thyroid storm and cardiac arrest separately, evidence specific to their combined presentation is limited. This scoping review maps the clinical characteristics, reported management and outcomes of published cases and identifies gaps in clinical documentation. Clinical features, treatment chronology, source-attributed mechanisms and outcomes were summarized descriptively. Results Seventy-six publications described 78 patients. abstract: Data and code that reproduce the two exploratory analyses in Jagtap (2026), "The Safety Net Was Not Built for This: Institutional Mismatch and AI-Driven Labor Market Change," National High School Journal of Science. Analysis 1 links AI Occupational Exposure (AIOE) scores to May 2021 BLS median wages for 667 occupations (r = 0.518, R² = 0.269). title: From Science Fiction to Science Faction: Interrogating Posthuman Assemblage in Bollywood Science Fiction Film Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya
abstract: In an era marked by ever-increasing integration of humans with artificial intelligence (AI), popular culture predominantly Bollywood, functions as a reflective canvas that shapes and mirrors society’s growing reliance on technology. In this context, Bollywood Science fiction film Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya emerges as a significant cultural text that portrays the intricacies of human-AI relationship. The study contextualizes film within the framework of Posthumanism. The study draws from Posthumanist theorist, Stefan Herbrechter’s concept of “Science faction” along with Rosi Braidotti’s posthumanist philosophy, while incorporating the foundational concepts of film theorists, Rosie Thomas’ moral universe and Ranjani Mazumdar’s techno-urbanism. It provides a methodological bridge to examine shifting and evolving paradigms of human-machine relationships within Indian cinema. Employing close textual analysis, the paper argues that the film presents human-AI interaction not as a distant fantasy but as an imminent “Science Factional” appraisal of a near-future reality. title: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence in organic supply chains: A systematic review with insights from South Tamil Nadu
abstract: Organic agriculture is growing rapidly in India, yet organic supply chains remain structurally fragmented, particularly in smallholder-dominated regions such as South Tamil Nadu. Digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) offer promising solutions to persistent challenges, including inadequate cold-chain infrastructure, limited traceability, intermediary-dependent marketing and certification workflow inefficiencies. This systematic review draws on evidence from 30 peer-reviewed and institutional publications. These sources were identified through a PRISMA-compliant search of Scopus, Elsevier, Taylor & Francis, Web of Science, IEEE, MDPI, Wiley, FAO, and government databases. The findings indicate that AI-enabled precision farming, machine learning-based demand forecasting, Internet of Things-enabled cold-chain monitoring, and blockchain-supported traceability improve production efficiency, market access and organic supply chain transparency. title: SmartTwin AI: An Explainable Predictive-Maintenance Decision-Support Framework for Smart Manufacturing
abstract: This research presents SmartTwin AI, a software-based framework for predictive maintenance in smart manufacturing. The study explores how machine-learning models can use industrial sensor measurements to identify potential machine failures and support maintenance decisions. Experiments were conducted using the AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance dataset, which contains 10,000 records of machine operating conditions. Three machine-learning models were evaluated: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting. The evaluation included precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and confusion matrices. A threshold-tuning experiment was also performed to improve the detection of potential failures. The results show that the Random Forest model achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.9653. After threshold tuning, the model achieved a recall of 79.41% on the test set, demonstrating a potential approach for identifying machines that may require maintenance. This work combines concepts from Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Engineering and Technology. title: Dialectics of Knowledge
Learning Sciences Foundations for Engineering Education: A Framework for Epistemological Articulation Across Paradigms
abstract: Educational research explains learning through three major traditions—behaviorism, cognitivism, and the situative perspective—yet typically deploys them as rival options rather than complementary levels of analysis. This article argues that the fragmentation is not a matter of preference but an unresolved epistemological problem: the three paradigms operate on qualitatively distinct epistemic objects—observable behavior, the internal architecture of knowledge and its acquisition and transfer, and the structurally distributed conditions that determine what counts as knowing in a disciplinary community—and therefore generate questions, instruments, and validity criteria that are not mutually substitutable. On this basis, we develop a conceptual synthesis that does not unify the paradigms but specifies the conditions under which each—together with its contemporary extensions (Cognitive Load Theory, self-regulated learning, Self-Determination Theory, and the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning)—is methodologically productive. Bibliographic records were obtained from Scopus (n = 27) and Web of Science Core Collection (n = 16) on 16 October 2026. The combined dataset contains 43 source records, including 13 duplicates. title: AI/ICT-Related talent alignment and regional high-tech employment growth: evidence from European regions
abstract: Digital recruiting demand can expand faster than a region’s science-and-technology talent base, but the relationship between this relative pressure and high-tech employment remains unclear. Using the reported balanced panel of European NUTS-2 regions for 2020–2024, we construct a signed index from standardized ICT-specialist advertisement demand and human resources in science and technology (HRST). The outcome is the percentage-point change in the regional high-tech employment share. Lagged mismatch is positively associated with subsequent share growth, with a negative squared term indicating a concave fitted association. A separate interaction specification shows positive associations for ICT demand and HRST and a positive interaction. These results describe conditional regional associations; the ICT indicator is not an AI-specific vacancy measure, and the employment-share outcome does not establish absolute job creation.

title: Factors associated with generative AI chatbot acceptance among medical students with prior academic use: a cross-sectional study based on an extended technology acceptance model
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots are becoming increasingly embedded in medical education, providing students with on-demand support for learning, clinical reasoning, and academic tasks. However, the psychological and technological factors that shape medical students’ acceptance of these tools remain insufficiently understood. This study examined acceptance among medical students with prior academic use of GenAI chatbots by extending the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to include AI literacy (AIL) and perceived security and privacy (PSP), and by examining their associations with perceived ease of use (PEOU), perceived usefulness (PU), attitude toward using GenAI (ATG), and behavioral intention to use GenAI (BIG). A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among medical students at Hormozgan University of Medical Sciences (HUMS), Iran, between May and June 2026. Eligibility required prior academic use of a GenAI chatbot. Data were collected using a structured, self-administered questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). title: Factors influencing nursing educators’ behavioral intention to adopt artificial intelligence in teaching: A cross-sectional study from Morocco
abstract: Purpose: Educators are central to the successful integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in health sciences education, yet evidence from North African contexts remains scarce. This study examined the factors associated with nursing educators' behavioral intention to adopt AI in their teaching practices in Laayoune, Morocco. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 108 nursing educators (response rate: 90.8%) between June and July 2025. A French-language, self-administered questionnaire based on the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology measured behavioral intention and ten individual, technological, and organizational dimensions (45 items; Cronbach's α = 0.835–0.983). Behavioral intention, the canonical acceptance outcome in both models, was analyzed as a continuous variable using independent-samples t-tests with effect sizes, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression with backward elimination, bootstrap confidence intervals, and a logistic sensitivity analysis. title: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and IoT for Waste Classification and Intelligent Waste Management: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review
abstract: The rapid growth of urban populations and consumption patterns has significantly increased the volume and complexity of municipal waste streams, including recyclable, organic, hazardous, and electronic waste. Traditional waste management approaches such as manual sorting and fixed collection schedules struggle to handle the diversity and scale of modern waste systems efficiently. Consequently, recent research has explored artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision, and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to automate waste classification and enable intelligent monitoring and management of waste infrastructures. However, the rapidly expanding literature in this domain is fragmented across different datasets, sensing platforms, and experimental settings, making it difficult to obtain a comprehensive understanding of current technological progress. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic literature review using the PRISMA methodology, analyzing 50 rigorously selected peer-reviewed studies on automated waste classification and intelligent waste management systems. title: Equipping the next generation: addressing the unmet need for artificial intelligence education at research performing organizations
abstract: BACKGROUND: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools into higher education is rapidly accelerating, yet the educational ecosystem appears largely unprepared for the scale and speed of adoption. Our recent international survey of over 1,200 university students and postdoctoral fellows in the medical and life sciences found that while more than 80% had used GenAI tools, the vast majority had received no formal training, and many were unaware of any institutional policies governing their use. This gap between adoption and institutional preparedness may pose risks to research integrity if left unaddressed. MAIN BODY: Existing research supports a coordinated, evidence-informed approach to AI education in research performing organizations (RPOs), grounded in principles of research integrity, equity, and critical engagement with technology. First, GenAI literacy must be embedded as a core competency in scientific and clinical education, equipping students to critically evaluate tool outputs, recognize hallucination and bias, and understand the distinction between AI-generated inaccuracy and deliberate research misconduct. Second, traditional frameworks for acade

title: Modelo predictivo de las metas de aproximación al dominio: un análisis con IA
abstract: The objective of this study was to use artificial intelligence (AI) to predict mastery-approach goals in secondary school students based on variables from the PISA 2018 database. The sample consisted of 339,560 participants from 60 countries. Machine learning was used with the Super Learner mega-algorithm with 14 candidate algorithms. In addition, deep learning was used with a neural network with 107 parameters. The analyses showed that students’ perceived parental emotional support, competitiveness, purpose in life, self-efficacy, and knowledge of intercultural communication were predictors of mastery-approach goals in secondary school students. This research contributes to the study of factors that influence mastery-approach goals in secondary school students, with analysis models that advance the development of the science of AI-based predictive education.

title: From Physique Concerns to Pan-Appearance Anxiety in the Digital Age:A Dual-Database Bibliometric Analysis of Health-Related Research (2006–2026)
abstract: 1. Background In recent years, the escalating global burden of appearance-related distress has transformed social physique anxiety into a multidimensional public health challenge. Although the rapid expansion of digital environments significantly exacerbates appearance vulnerabilities and the volume of academic literature has grown substantially, a comprehensive quantitative mapping of the field's evolutionary trajectory remains lacking. Previous reviews were often limited to a single database, which may result in a biased representation of global trends and fail to capture the core theoretical transition from specific "physique anxiety" (focusing strictly on adiposity and muscularity) to broader "social appearance anxiety" (encompassing global aesthetic evaluations like facial features and skin tone). 2. Objective This project aims to systematically visualize the knowledge structure, spatiotemporal distribution, and developmental trends of social physique anxiety research by integrating literature from the past two decades (January 1, 2006, to August 15, 2026). Specific objectives include: Mapping and evaluating the global collaboration networks among authors, institutions, and co

title: Pratiques et enjeux de l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle pour l’histoire et la mémoire
abstract: Cette journée d’étude s’inscrit dans le contexte du projet de recherche européen AI Remembers, qui explore la manière dont les techniques d’apprentissage profond et d’intelligence artificielle dialoguent avec l’histoire, le souvenir collectif et la mémoire. L’intégration rapide de l’IA dans l’univers mémoriel soulève des questions cruciales : comment ces outils transforment-ils l’interprétation des sources ? Quel est leur impact sur l’accès du public à l’Histoire ? Comment préserver la critique des sources à l’ère des modèles génératifs ? La journée réunit des spécialistes issus de l’histoire, de l’informatique, des sciences humaines etsociales, ainsi que des professionnels des musées, des mémoriaux et des archives. Elle vise à offrir aux participants une vision à la fois concrète et critique des transformations en cours, en articulant recherche fondamentale, retours d’expérience et réflexion éthique.

title: Machine learning models for childhood obesity risk assessment: design, validation, and reporting practices. A systematic review protocol
abstract: Systematic review, reported with PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S, of machine-learning models that classify or predict overweight or obesity in children and adolescents. It describes designs (prospective or cross-sectional), the use of anthropometric predictors, validation, calibration, and risk of bias with PROBAST+AI. The protocol was registered after the searches were run (15 October 2026; PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science) and before screening of the results, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment.

title: AI for Poststroke Epilepsy: Scoping Review of Imaging-Based Prediction Models and Implications for African Settings
abstract: Background: Poststroke seizures (PSS) and poststroke epilepsy (PSE) are important neurological complications associated with poorer functional recovery, increased mortality, and reduced quality of life after stroke. Neuroimaging plays a central role in identifying patients at increased risk, and recent advances in AI have enabled the development of imaging-based prediction models that may improve individualized risk stratification. However, the current evidence remains fragmented, and the extent to which these approaches are applicable to African health care settings is unclear. Objective: This scoping review aimed to chart the existing global evidence on the development of imaging-based prediction models that can help in predicting PSS and PSE, especially AI-based ones. The purpose was to look into the imaging techniques, computational algorithms, and validation methodologies used and the representation of African populations. Methods: This scoping review was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological framework, and the results were presented based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) f

title: A bioinspired conceptual framework for adaptive university press management
abstract: University presses face converging pressures from scholarly quality, peer-review integrity, reviewer scarcity, Open Science, artificial intelligence, international visibility, and economic sustainability. This article proposes Epigenetic Editorial Intelligence, a bioinspired conceptual framework that represents stable institutional rules as Editorial DNA and models operational adaptation through epigenetic regulation, an Artificial Immune System, organizational memory, human–AI collaboration, and multiobjective optimization. Nine operational indicators are formalized and aggregated into a Global Editorial Intelligence Index (GEII). Internal model behavior is examined through paired synthetic ablations that disable one mechanism at a time, using 200 Monte Carlo repetitions, common random-number streams, 95% confidence intervals, alternative weighting schemes and 1000 Dirichlet weight perturbations. Results are interpreted as structural-consistency diagnostics rather than empirical validation. This work provides a reproducible conceptual and mathematical foundation for subsequent implementation and testing with real editorial records.

title: Reframing education 5.0 through capability theory: A framework for human-centered digital learning
abstract: Industry 5.0 has reoriented technology-driven transformation around human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience, complementing rather than replacing Industry 4.0, with direct implications for education. Existing accounts of the resulting “Education 5.0” paradigm remain largely descriptive, synthesising a dispersed literature without an explicit theoretical mechanism or a transparent, auditable procedure for deriving the constructs they propose. This paper addresses both gaps. First, it anchors the Education 4.0-to-5.0 transition within the capability approach, using capability expansion, not technology adoption, as the mechanism linking Industry 5.0’s human-centric, sustainable, and resilient logic to curricular practice, and specifies the boundary conditions under which the framework should, and should not, be expected to hold. Second, it derives an integrative five-pillar curriculum framework - human-centric pedagogy, resilient and lifelong learning ecosystems, sustainability-embedded curricula, well-being and leadership development, and creativity through human–AI co-creation - through an explicit three-step synthesis procedure that traces each pillar to recurring literatur

title: Harnessing oxidative stress: Novel therapeutics in pediatric brain cancer
Integrating artificial intelligence and data science in environmental geotechnics: a review
abstract: Environmental geotechnics plays a critical role in the development of sustainable and resilient infrastructure systems, while addressing global challenges, such as climate change and resource depletion. This review paper explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and data science (DS) within environmental geotechnics, and their potential to advance the field while supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). By leveraging diverse data sources, including sensors, satellites, laboratory testing and case-history projects, AI-driven and data-centric approaches can support evidence-based decision making for the design, construction and maintenance of climate-resilient infrastructure. The integration of AI and DS enables engineers to efficiently interpret complex datasets, anticipate risks, optimise resource use and respond proactively to evolving ground conditions throughout infrastructure lifecycles. These capabilities contribute to enhanced risk mitigation, environmental protection and sustainable infrastructure development. The synergy between AI–DS and environmental geotechnics directly supports key SDGs, including clean water (SDG 6), industry,

title: How Do Real Operational Shapes Reorganize Inference, Meaning, and Scientific Reality? Belief-Model Operational Dynamics, Physical Transitions, Speed, Brandom and Wolfendale, AI, Xenoscience, and Autonomous Science
Controlled Evidence Mapping of Digitally Enabled Climate-Smart Tourism: From Fragmented Applications to Integrated Destination Climate Intelligence
abstract: This study maps the knowledge structure of AI-enabled climate-smart tourism and examines how artificial intelligence, digital twins, the Internet of Things, remote sensing, predictive analytics, and climate services support adaptation, mitigation, and destination resilience. A systematic evidence-mapping design was combined with controlled bibliometric science mapping. Following PRISMA 2020 and SPAR-4-SLR, 77 records were screened, yielding 50 eligible publications available through June 2026. Analyses included concept co-occurrence, temporal overlay, technology–function cross-tabulation, climate-relevance coding, and evidence-maturity assessment. Publication activity increased after 2023, with planning and governance dominating the literature. Only 11 studies explicitly addressed climate risk, adaptation, weather, or resilience, while outcome-level evaluation remained limited. The findings reveal a sensing-to-action gap, as observation, prediction, simulation, implementation, and learning are rarely integrated. The study conceptualizes AI-enabled climate-smart tourism as an outcome-oriented destination capability and proposes a six-stage climate-intelligence cycle connecting sensi

title: Network Geometry of Neural Processing Components for Interpretable AI in Sparse Neuromorphic Dendritic Circuits
abstract: Neuromorphic AI increasingly draws on sparse dendritic computation, yet a network-science framework linking sub-neuronal circuit organization to function remains underdeveloped. Here we introduce the neural processing component (NPC) paradigm, representing synapses, dendrites, somata and axons as network elements whose sparse topology shapes computation. We implement this paradigm in a dendritic reservoir-based network for trajectory detection, demonstrating in device-informed simulations that real-time motion trajectories can be detected through fixed NPC design rather than training. Using hyperbolic network geometry, we reveal that NPC neuromorphic circuits with dendrites possess latent hierarchical and modular organization that is not visible from circuit diagrams alone. We further show that this geometric representation identifies vulnerable modules and critical routing nodes that can be selectively redesigned, reducing detection error under router-node failure by 50.9%. These results establish NPC network geometry as a method for circuit-level interpretability androbustness-oriented design of sparse neuromorphic AI.

title: Employee responses to workplace AI across cultural contexts: a systematic review of explicitly AI-framed evidence
abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI), generative AI and large language models is reshaping how work is organised and how employees engage with emerging technologies. Yet the role of culture in these responses remains poorly understood and is often inferred from contextual proxies rather than measured directly. This systematic review synthesises empirical journal studies of explicitly AI-framed technologies in workplace and professional settings, with particular attention to directly measured cultural values and culturally situated conditions. Following PRISMA 2020, searches of Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO via EBSCOhost and PubMed identified 910 records. A complete re-screening during revision of an updated title-distinct set of 691 records yielded 13 eligible studies. The evidence base was small, heterogeneous and methodologically uneven. Only four studies directly examined named cultural-value constructs, while the remainder represented culture through national context, organisational culture, professional culture or locally grounded frameworks. Across studies, employee responses ranged from acceptance, trust and optimism to uncertainty, perceived threat, autono

title: Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Financial Fraud Detection: A Bibliometric Analysis of Scientific Development and Future Directions
abstract: This study examines the development and intellectual structure of artificial intelligence (AI)-based financial fraud detection through a bibliometric analysis of 2200 Scopus- and Web of Science-indexed journal articles published between 1992 and 2026. The literature has expanded rapidly, with 89.6% of publications appearing since 2018 and an annual growth rate of 29.4%. Research is concentrated in Computer Science and Engineering, whereas Business and Economics account for 9.2% of classified publications. Credit card and payment fraud constitutes the largest research domain (32.0%), followed by banking, loan, and transaction fraud (14.3%), insurance fraud (12.2%), and accounting and financial statement fraud (9.9%). Neural networks and deep learning, ensemble and boosting methods, and classical supervised classifiers are the dominant methodological families. The field has progressively shifted from traditional data-mining and classical machine-learning approaches toward deep learning, ensemble methods, graph neural networks, and explainable AI. Science mapping shows that the intellectual structure remains strongly centered on payment fraud, while accounting and insurance fraud form

title: Explicit teaching of AI literacy in allied health professions education: a scoping review
abstract: This scoping review will map what has been reported about the explicit teaching of artificial intelligence (AI) literacy in pre-registration (entry-level) education, at undergraduate or postgraduate level, for 11 allied health professions: occupational therapy, physiotherapy, paramedicine, medical imaging and radiation sciences, speech pathology, dietetics, social work, podiatry, exercise physiology, audiology and orthoptics. Teaching content will be coded against four domains: ethical and safe use; documentation, privacy and regulatory compliance; critical appraisal of AI tools; and work readiness for AI-enabled practice. Recent reviews of AI in health professions education are dominated by medicine and nursing, or focus on students’ own use of AI tools rather than on what they are taught. The review follows JBI scoping review methodology and will be reported using PRISMA-ScR. Sources published from 2022 will be identified through MEDLINE, CINAHL, Embase, ERIC, Education Source, Scopus, grey literature and citation searching. A secondary objective is a dated scan of Australian regulator guidance, accreditation standards and professional association competency standards for referen

title: AutoCare AI: An AI-Assisted Vehicle Service Management System
abstract: Independent garages commonly manage repairs with paper job cards, verbal estimates and memory, so the accuracy and efficiency of their service cannot be measured. This paper presents AutoCare AI, a zero-cost web application built with Flutter and Firebase that digitises the garage workflow from walk-in to invoice, estimates a job's fault category, labour time and cost from the customer's free-text complaint using Google Gemini (with a keyword-rule engine for offline demonstration), suggests the least-busy suitable mechanic, predicts each vehicle's next periodic service and records manual, AI and actual outcomes on every job. The study follows a design-science approach with secondary, quantitative data: 31,236 owner complaints from the public NHTSA complaints database, labelled into seven of the application's fault categories and split into 24,988 training and 6,248 test records. A TF-IDF and Logistic Regression classifier reached 90.6 % accuracy (macro-F1 0.907), significantly above an 80 % target (exact binomial p ≈ 1.09 × 10⁻¹¹⁵), whereas the application's keyword rules reached only 57.6 %. title: Atrial cardiomyopathy: from knowledge gaps to clinical impact
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) is increasingly recognised as an underlying atrial substrate contributing to atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), and cardio-embolic stroke. However, diagnostic criteria, disease thresholds, and targeted treatment strategies remain poorly defined. OBJECTIVE: To describe the rationale, structure, and translational strategy of the EmbRACE (Electro-Molecular Basis and the theRapeutic management of Atrial Cardiomyopathy, fibrillation and associated outcomEs) network, a national consortium established to address key knowledge gaps in AtCM. METHODS: EmbRACE integrates mechanistic research, computational modelling, clinical trials, and implementation science within seven interconnected work packages. Human atrial tissue biobanking and deep phenotyping (WP1) enable molecular profiling of candidate pathways (WP2), which are validated in experimental models (WP3). Computational modelling and artificial intelligence (WP4) integrate multimodal clinical and biological data to derive composite AtCM phenotypes and severity frameworks. title: Leveraging Large Language Model Token Probabilities for Literature Review Abstract Filtering
abstract: Grasping the latest knowledge in any field has become increasingly challenging given the rapid pace of modern publishing. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly embedding models and large language models (LLMs), provide promising tools to aid researchers in the filtration and identification of the most relevant literature. However, there is little practical guidance on how to incorporate LLMs into literature reviews, and there are not yet direct comparisons of embedding models versus generative approaches. In this work, we compare these methods using small local LLMs for literature screening on both a simple dataset containing distinct categories and a more complex example with abstracts obtained from the Web of Science. We find that embedding models perform strongly for simple, well-separated queries due to their robustness and computational efficiency. For more complex filtering tasks, generative approaches based on token probabilities can achieve competitive or superior performance, but only when properly calibrated and when token-level outputs are interpreted as continuous scores rather than binary decisions. However, we show these methods are highly sens

title: Beyond Editing Code: Uses for AI Tools in Scientific Work
abstract: Critical research advancements require usable, reliable software products—including AI tooling—for high performance data and computing work. To improve AI systems we must understand scientists’ and engineers’ needs and define design best practices for building interfaces that facilitate collaboration between scientists and AI tools across ecosystems. Ensuring the long-term usability and utility of scientific software products and AI systems for communities protects critical investments, supports high quality research, and reduces end user challenges. This talk will present findings from our semi-structured interview study investigating how scientists and engineers use AI tools for their research work. We recruited from universities and national labs, seeking perspectives from multiple disciplines. Looking beyond common use of AI tools for coding tasks, we sought to understand the varied ways AI is or could be adopted in scientific settings. Our interviews investigated how users determine the utility of AI tools, the concerns they have about adoption, and expectations for agentic tooling in research infrastructures. In this talk, we discuss opportunities for AI tooling in science an

title: Intellectual property in design-driven industries: A bibliometric and thematic analysis (2000–2025) with insights for the Jewellery Industry
abstract: This study aims to systematically examine the intellectual property (IP) research in design-driven industries through a bibliometric and thematic analysis of publications from 2000 to 2025, and further derives implications for the jewellery industry. With the rapid development of the creative economy and digital transformation, IP protection has become an important pillar for innovation and market competitiveness in design-intensive industries. However, current research lacks a systematic and holistic review of this interdisciplinary field, and evidence specific to the jewellery remains limited. To fill this gap, a bibliometric and thematic analysis was conducted based on 359 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. Descriptive statistics were processed using Microsoft Excel, while publication trends, global research patterns, thematic structures, and emerging research frontiers were analyzed using CiteSpace and VOSviewer. The findings indicate that intellectual property research in design-driven industries has maintained continuous growth and gradually formed an interdisciplinary integration trend. Among the valid publications, "Law" is the domi

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Stock Market Prediction: A Systematic Literature Review of Methods, Emerging Paradigms, Reproducibility, and Evaluation Gaps (2016-2026)

Emergence and development of observation practices in AI-assisted plant adaptation learning
abstract: Observation is a fundamental scientific practice in science learning, particularly for understanding gradual biological phenomena such as plant adaptation. Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, limited research has examined how AI-supported tools influence students' observation practices during authentic scientific inquiry. This study investigates the emergence and development of students' observation practices during plant adaptation learning supported by an AI-based identifier. A six-week mixed-methods exploratory study was conducted with 84 middle school students. Learning activities were organised into four phases: orientation, initial observation, AI-assisted identification, and re-observation and validation. Data were collected through observation sheets, students' observation notes, reflective journals, group discussions, and records of AI use. Quantitative analysis revealed significant differences in observation orientations across learning phases (Friedman test, p < .001), indicating changes in observation practices over time. Qualitative findings showed that students initially relied on AI-generated cues to guide their observatio

title: Emerging Trends in Image Processing, Computer Vision, Security, Cloud and Mobile Computing
Charting the Trajectory of Artificial Intelligence Agents in Air Traffic Control
abstract: The aim of the study was to chart the evolution and the current research landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) agents within the domain of air traffic control. Using bibliometric analysis, the study identified major research trends and gaps and provided a consolidated reference for researchers. The analysis included 58 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. The findings showed that the earliest publication in the dataset appeared in 1998 and that research output increased noticeably after 2022. Publication output peaked in 2025, with 16 articles, indicating growing scholarly interest in AI agents for air traffic control. Citation analysis identified Agogino and Tumer’s (2012) article as the most influential publication, with 68 citations. The article introduced a multi-agent approach to air traffic flow management. Brittain and Wei’s (2022) article ranked second, with 54 citations, highlighting the increasing role of reinforcement learning. At the country level, the United States had the highest total citation count, followed by China, France, England, and Spain. By examining AI agents as a distinct research topic, the study provides a focused overview

Emerging Trends in Artificial Intelligence and Applications
Artificial Intelligence Agents and Consumer Behavior: A Bibliometric Analysis of an Emerging Research Field
abstract: Recent dynamic advances in AI technologies have brought about profound transformations in the marketing paradigm and in consumer behavior and interactions. At the heart of this transformation, the relationship between AI agents and consumer behavior stands out as a timely area calling for in-depth investigation in the literature. This study constitutes a bibliometric analysis undertaken to reveal the intellectual accumulation of knowledge in this conceptual domain and to examine the evolution of the literature systematically. To this end, 438 articles indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database between 2020 and 2026 were subjected to a comprehensive examination. The research first conducted a performance analysis to resolve the quantitative structure of the field, mapping annual publication distributions, the most prolific authors, the most highly cited studies, leading countries, and institutional collaborations. It then carried out citation, co-citation, and co-occurence analyses using science mapping techniques in order to structure the intellectual framework of the field. The findings show that the AI agent literature emerging in the context of consumer behavior is following a

title: "Educational intervention can rewire village social networks" Logical Review & Gap Analysis
abstract: This Technical Report applies the Section Zero framework (v2.0) to Papamichalis, Forastiere, Airoldi & Christakis, Educational intervention can rewire village social networks, Nature (2026), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-11154-7. It identifies seven logical gaps not raised by the authors or referees: (G1) the intervention is an unmeasured delivery bundle, with no data on health workers' conduct or recipients' uptake; (G2) outcomes are self-reported nominations; (G3) the low/high dosage cut-off is derived from the outcome data; (G4) baseline degree differs across dosage arms and change depends strongly on baseline; (G5) neighbour subgroups are selected on degree; (G6) "overall structural stability" rests on a single non-significant test; (G7) mediation assumptions are not stated. Claims are rated for reliability on the principle of direct evidence in the paper and peer review file, with a ceiling of Medium–High for a social-science study. Overall: Low–Medium; the core finding is Medium; mechanism and policy implications are unverified. This report does not replace Nature's peer review. title: Emerging Trends in Artificial Intelligence, Computational Intelligence, and Social Networks
Nucleic Acid Therapeutics in an Age of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming how scientific hypotheses are formulated, tested, and applied. Nucleic acid therapeutics can benefit from emerging opportunities but will also face new challenges. AI lowers the barrier to hypothesis generation, increasing the emphasis on critical evaluation, rigorous experimental testing, and expert judgement. The goal of this perspective is to begin that discussion, with an emphasis on basic and applied research at the interface of nucleic acid science and medicine.

title: RAIISE: Resilient Agricultural Intelligence, Informatics, and Systems Education
abstract: Natural hazard events cost U.S. farmers more than $20.3 billion in crop and rangeland losses in 2024, with $9.4 billion uninsured. Atmospheric modeling, risk assessment, and AI-driven decision support can reduce these losses, but food and agricultural sciences education has not kept pace. Farm security depends on a trained workforce that can put natural hazard intelligence and decision support to work for American farm families. RAIISE (Resilient Agricultural Intelligence, Informatics, and Systems Education) addresses this gap through a Collaborative Grant Type 1 (CG1) partnership between Louisiana State University (LSU), the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR), and the LSU AgCenter. RAIISE will equip the next generation of agricultural professionals with competencies and leadership needed to protect American farm families from natural hazard losses, strengthen rural prosperity, and advance national food security. RAIISE pursues three objectives: 1) developing a curricular pathway of new and enhanced undergraduate and graduate courses using NCAR's atmospheric modeling infrastructure and LSU AgCenter Model Farm data; 2) advancing student career readiness through coursewo

title: The illusion of outsourcing learning: A learner-centered perspective on AI in education
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (genAI) is rapidly transforming education, but not the cognitive mechanisms through which humans learn. However, genAI’s effects on learning are often discussed in terms of technological capabilities rather than the cognitive processes through which learning occurs. In this paper, I build on learner-centered accounts for evaluating genAI in education. Through an educational psychology and cognitive science lens, I argue that technologies can influence learning only insofar as they support or interfere with learners’ active cognitive processing. This perspective is particularly important because genAI can increasingly perform cognitive operations on learners’ behalf, such as generating explanations, organizing information, and solving problems. Such capabilities may indeed increase efficiency, but they may also deprive learners of cognitive activities essential for learning. Therefore, the key question for genAI in education is not whether genAI improves learning, but whether the cognitive operations delegated to genAI are operations that learners need to perform themselves for the intended learning to occur. The same genAI function may therefore s

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HEALTHCARE: ITS POTENTIALS AND RISKS
abstract: Artificial intelligence has moved from science fiction into the clinic with remarkable speed. Machine learning systems now read medical scans, flag sepsis before symptoms declare themselves, draft clinical notes, and coach patients through their smartphones. This article examines the promise and the peril of this transformation in narrative form, and then applies the lens to a single, vivid case: the intertwined epidemics of sleep deprivation and migraine in young adults, where wearable sensors and predictive algorithms are beginning to change how these conditions are detected, studied, and managed. The evidence suggests that AI's greatest near-term contribution is not replacing clinicians but extending their reach — while its greatest dangers, including algorithmic bias, opaque decision making, data privacy erosion, and over-reliance, demand deliberate governance. The article argues that the future of medical AI will be decided less by the sophistication of the algorithms than by the wisdom of the humans who deploy them.

title: Supporting MSME Innovation: An Adviser’s Manual Developed for the Philippine Department of Science and Technology
abstract: This Productivity Insights publication outlines four practical AI strategies specifically crafted for small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises: (1) predictive maintenance and AI-based visual inspection for quality control, (2) integration through digital twins and cyber-physical production systems, (3) human-in-the-loop operations, and (4) collaboration through federated learning. Each strategy comes with simple implementation guidelines and a brief business justification. The report also includes a readiness check method and a 90-day roadmap aimed at achieving tangible results. The main goal of this publication is to assist factory leaders in transitioning from isolated trials to scalable applications. It focuses on measurable outcomes like reduced downtime, increased productivity, enhanced energy efficiency, and improved overall equipment effectiveness. It also stresses the importance of governance frameworks and human involvement to ensure clear, actionable, and people-centered technology adoption.

title: AI and IoT in Engineering, Life Science, and Healthcare
Assessment of utilization of ChatGPT on Medical Research Paper Writing Practices amongst University students in Lahore, Pakistan
abstract: Background :The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in academic applications has transformed medical research writing. ChatGPT is an AI-based language model that has been introduced by Open AI. It is been commonly used for literature review, manuscript organization, and writing research papers and articles. Objective: To assess utilization of ChatGPT on medical research writing practices among university students. Method: An analytical cross- sectional study conducted among university student of The University of Lahore and Rashid Latif Khan University. The study participants were split into 3 groups on the basis of their enrolled degree programs; MBBS, BDS and Allied health sciences (undergraduate, graduate and post-graduate students). Duration of study was from January 2025 to June 2025. Descriptive statistics, frequencies, percentages, and cross-tabulations were employed to summarize the demographic features. For inferential testing, statistical tests were used to investigate the relationship between the question variable utilization of ChatGPT and Chi-square (?²) tests were used to detect relationships between categorical variables.
