title: Open Science in an Age of Nationalised Scientific Purpose
abstract: As AI and other digital technologies become strategic assets, governments are recasting the purpose of science around national competitiveness and security. Nanditha Mathew and Luc Soete argue that this “nationalisation of scientific purpose”, visible in both the US and Europe, erodes the institutional autonomy, openness and international collaboration on which scientific leadership depends. The challenge is not to insulate science from national priorities, but to stop the pursuit of strategic advantage from undermining the openness that makes scientific progress possible. For a full article, please click here.

title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE UPSTAGING PREDICTION OF DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
abstract: Background: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) may be upstaged to invasive carcinoma after surgical excision. Predicting upstaging before surgery may help guide treatment planning. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based imaging has been investigated for this purpose, but its overall performance remains unclear. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of AI-based systems for predicting DCIS upstaging to invasive carcinoma. Materials and Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA 2020 and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261516994). PubMed, Scopus, EBSCOhost, ProQuest, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based imaging models for DCIS upstaging were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were calculated using a bivariate random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Results: Six studies involving 701 participants were included. Pooled sensitivity was 0.77 (95% CI, 0.57–0.89) and specificity was 0.78 (95% CI, 0.64–0.87), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 84.0% and 90.6%, respectively). The pooled log diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) was 2.15 (95% CI, 1.64–2.65). The SROC analysis

title: The effects of the arts and arts therapies on mental health outcomes of children and young people: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background There is growing evidence on the positive effects of the arts and arts therapies for mental health (MH) outcomes. This review aims to fill a research gap by establishing the evidence on the effects of arts-based interventions on selected MH outcomes for children and young people (CYP). Methods Our systematic review and meta-analysis included randomised controlled trials with CYP aged 5–24 years receiving any type of arts-based intervention. Five databases (CINAHL, Embase.com, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between 1/1/2005 and 18/5/2025. Two reviewers independently screened all records and assessed risk-of-bias using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB2) and certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). Data were initially extracted using the AI-assisted review tool Elicit and independently verified by two reviewers. All data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis, and effect estimates for MH outcomes are summarised as Standardised Mean Differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). title: Leveraging Large Language Model Token Probabilities for Literature Review Abstract Filtering
abstract: Grasping the latest knowledge in any field has become increasingly challenging given the rapid pace of modern publishing. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly embedding models and large language models (LLMs), provide promising tools to aid researchers in the filtration and identification of the most relevant literature. However, there is little practical guidance on how to incorporate LLMs into literature reviews, and there are not yet direct comparisons of embedding models versus generative approaches. In this work, we compare these methods using small local LLMs for literature screening on both a simple dataset containing distinct categories and a more complex example with abstracts obtained from the Web of Science. We find that embedding models perform strongly for simple, well-separated queries due to their robustness and computational efficiency. For more complex filtering tasks, generative approaches based on token probabilities can achieve competitive or superior performance, but only when properly calibrated and when token-level outputs are interpreted as continuous scores rather than binary decisions. However, we show these methods are highly sens

title: Replication materials: Generative AI use in geometry learning and pre-service mathematics teachers' readiness to teach with AI
abstract: Replication materials for the article "Generative AI use in geometry learning and pre-service mathematics teachers' readiness to teach with AI" (submitted to the International Journal of Mathematical Education in Science and Technology). The study used PLS-SEM, MICOM and PLS-MGA with survey data from 297 pre-service mathematics teachers at two public teacher-education universities (group E, n = 203; group W, n = 94). Participants did not consent to the public release of individual responses, so individual-level data are not shared. The package provides aggregate data (item correlation matrices for the full sample and each group, item and dimension descriptives, aggregated sample characteristics), the Python analysis code, a script that reproduces all PLS-SEM point estimates from the shared correlation matrices, and the complete numerical results behind Tables 1 and 2 and Figures 1 and 2. See README.md for details.

title: A parity-selected endpoint theorem for the regular dodecahedron
abstract: This note gives two precise answers associated with Fuchs Conjecture 3.2. The imported bare endpoint-angle condition is false: exactly the two proper face diagonals per initial face and vertex are additional paths and have graph distance two. An explicitly adopted parity-selected convention has a complete unbounded endpoint-exclusion proof through double-pentagon germ symmetry, a physical edge-midpoint half-turn, and a unique-common-neighbor argument. The convention is a supported disambiguation, not an authenticated author correction or uniquely compelled printed reading. The midpoint and refolding mechanisms are credited to Athreya–Aulicino–Hooper and Troubetzkoy. Alper Ferudun's current contemporaneous preprint, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23267641, contains both the formulation distinction and endpoint theorem, and the public face-word type correction. title: AI Consciousness and the Law: Towards an AI Consciousness Legal Protocol
abstract: Artificial intelligence has not been shown to be conscious, yet the question has moved from philosophy into legislation and corporate research. Some legislatures have begun to answer it by declaration, while developers now study model welfare and the internal states of their systems. This paper argues that law can neither wait for science to settle the question nor settle it by decree. It proposes an AI Consciousness Legal Protocol: a ten-article instrument that sets the technical and legal parameters to be met before law recognises the consciousness of an AI system, entrusts that finding to an independent recognition body, and fixes the rules that govern AI in the meantime. The paper distinguishes the dictionary, scientific and spiritual meanings of consciousness, and separates the contextual awareness that AI systems already display from the valenced experience and self-directed decision that would alter legal relations. Drawing on the indicator-property method of Butlin, Long and co-authors (2023), it proposes seven legal parameters (independent evidence, valenced experience, persistent self, volition, understanding of consequences, absence of engineered mimicry, and reproducibi

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in the Food Industry: Transforming Food Quality, Production, and Sustainable Food Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming the food industry by enabling data driven approaches to food quality assessment, safety management, product development, processing, packaging, storage, and supply chain operations. The growing availability of data from sensors, imaging systems, analytical instruments, and digital production platforms has created new opportunities for machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and predictive analytics across the food chain. This chapter reviews the current applications of these technologies in food systems, with particular emphasis on quality and safety assessment, formulation and product development, process optimization, intelligent packaging, shelf life prediction, logistics, and supply chain management. The potential contribution of AI to sustainable food systems is also discussed, including food loss and waste reduction, resource optimization, and circular food production. In addition, emerging applications of generative AI are examined in areas such as food innovation, sensory and consumer research, and research support. Despite these opportunities, challenges related to data quality, model validation, interpret

title: Wearable Lower-Limb Exoskeletons for Motor Recovery in Chronic Stroke: A Scoping Review of Clinical Evidence and Research Gaps
abstract: This scoping review will map the clinical evidence on wearable, powered lower-limb exoskeleton training for motor recovery in adults with chronic stroke (≥6 months after onset). It follows the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and will be reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Rationale: Robot-assisted gait training is established in stroke rehabilitation, but the evidence on wearable exoskeletons is scattered. Studies differ widely in device type, recovery phase and training protocol, and evidence specific to the chronic phase is limited and often pooled with acute or subacute data. Evidence from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) also appears sparse. Objectives: To identify (1) which wearable exoskeletons and control strategies have been studied (fixed trajectory, assist-as-needed, adaptive or AI-based); (2) the training protocols and comparators used; (3) the outcome measures used and their ICF domains; (4) reported safety, feasibility and adherence; (5) where the studies were conducted, including how much evidence comes from LMICs; and (6) gaps in populations, devices, protocols, outcomes and settings. title: Generative AI in Construction Safety: A Systematic Literature Review of Methods, Evidence, Deployment Gaps, and Future Directions
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly being explored for construction safety; however, its maturity and practical reliability remain unclear. This study systematically reviews GenAI applications in construction safety and assesses whether existing evidence supports reliable, source-grounded, human-supervised, and deployable applications. The review followed a predefined protocol and PRISMA 2020. Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched in May 2026 for studies published from 2019 to August 2026. After duplicate removal and screening, sixty-five studies were included. Data on GenAI methods, safety applications, validation, deployment, and limitations were extracted and synthesized thematically. Six application areas were identified: safety knowledge retrieval and decision support; incident report analysis and risk prediction; multimodal hazard reasoning; synthetic data generation; worker-centered training, communication and behavior support; and generative optimization, monitoring, and safety control. Several studies provided proof-of-concept evidence using historical datasets, simulations, laboratory experiments, or expert assessment

title: Strategic Creativity for Leaders(hip)
abstract: This book explores how creativity is being redefined in the age of artificial intelligence (AI) and information overload. Tracing the evolution from Drucker’s knowledge worker to Florida’s creative class, it examines how generative AI (GenAI) reshapes work, decision-making, and measurement. Drawing on major psychological thinkers such as Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, Teresa Amabile, Daniel Kahneman, and Herbert Simon, it connects creativity research with cognitive science and behavioral decision theory. By combining management theory, creativity studies, and historical insight, the book reveals what remains uniquely human in a world increasingly shaped by algorithms. Readers will gain a nuanced understanding of creativity as a dynamic human capacity rather than a vague buzzword or mystical gift. The book clarifies key distinctions – between abilities, skills, and competencies; between Big-C and little-c creativities; and between algorithmic novelty and human originality rooted in intention and cultural meaning. It integrates major psychological traditions, from Guilford and Torrance to Boden and Sawyer, while critically engaging with contemporary definitions such as those proposed by Pr

title: "Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning"- Logical Review & Gap Analysis
abstract: Independent logical review of Guan et al., "Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning" (Nature, 2026; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-11126-x), which introduces probabilistic bias correction (PBC) for week 3–4 forecasts. Using the Section Zero minimal scientific validation framework (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19485885), the report summarizes the paper's reasoning chain and main claims, and lists the limitations acknowledged by the authors and the referee points only partly resolved. It then identifies six additional gaps not raised in the paper or its Peer Review File: precipitation scoring with zero-inflated data; attribution of skill to the input model versus observation-only information; event-conditioned flood evaluation; non-uniform test periods and multiple testing; calibration and decision value; the quantitative role of isotonic projection. The gaps serve as the basis for assigning an evidence-based reliability level to each claim. Pure mathematical proofs fall outside the framework's scope. The reviewer is not a domain specialist, and no code or data were re-run. This report is not a substitute for formal peer review. Keywords subseasonal forecasting;

title: Enhancing Retrofit Design for Office Buildings in Indonesia’s Hot-Humid Climates: Exploring Energy and Comfort Trade-Offs through Multi-Objective Optimisation Framework
abstract: The building and construction sector is responsible for approximately 34% of total final energy use and contributes about 37% of energy-related carbon dioxide emissions worldwide (United Nations Environment Programme, 2024). Although new buildings can be constructed to high energy performance standards, around 75% of today’s buildings are expected to remain in use in 2050. Most existing buildings do not comply with contemporary energy performance standards. Therefore, energy retrofitting the existing buildings offers significant opportunities to reduce global energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. However, the retrofit process is inherently complex due to the wide array of potential energy-efficient measures, conflicting optimisation objectives, and the multifaceted nature of assessing building performance. To address these challenges, simulation-based multi-objective optimisation (MOO) has been identified as a promising methodological approach, allowing for the simultaneous evaluation of various retrofit measures based on conflicting objectives (Attia et al., 2013). In the context of Indonesia, a densely populated country facing rapid construction growth and increasing e

title: Brain-based digital twins for skilled interceptive movements: computational frameworks for neural-kinematic integration
abstract: Human motor imagery provides a window on how the brain plans and refines movement, but its integration into digital-twin technology for real-time skill improvement remains limited. This thesis addresses that gap by formalising a brain-based digital twin (BB-DT) for cricket batting motor imagery that fuses electro encephalography with synchronised kinematic data to model, predict and provide feedback on skilled interceptive actions. The thesis develops a four-layer neuro-kinematic architecture spanning signal processing, synthetic-data augmentation, personalised neural mass modelling and closed-loop intervention. It specifies validation criteria - representational fidelity, identifiability and tractability - for judging when a brain-based twin is theoretically sound, and treats synthetic EEG as a theory-guided instrument for hypothesis testing rather than a simple data surrogate. Methodologically, the research combines consumer-grade 14-channel EEG, expert-validated cricket-stroke videos, kinematic capture, and a matched-filter signal-processing pipeline. Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinf

title: Next-Generation Marketing in Global Medical Tourism with Augmented, Virtual, and Mixed Reality Technologies, and Turkey
abstract: This study aims to reveal the role of Extended Reality (XR) technologies in marketing of medical tourism destinations and building patient trust. Medical tourism is a sector containing high risk and uncertainty by its nature. In this context, technologies like Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR) and Mixed Reality (MR) offer important opportunities to reduce risk perception of tourists and provide assurance. The study handles potential of Turkey in this field and suggests usage of digital tools like Blockchain and Digital Twin for sustainable competitive advantage. It is concluded that technological integration is necessary to increase value added in the sector and maximize revenue per patient.

title: A digital twin system for retail inventory & sales management : From conceptual architecture to a functional AI-enhanced prototype
abstract: Effective inventory and sales management is crucial in the physical retail stores, directly impacting operational efficiency, customer satisfaction and cost. Integration of Digital Twin technology along with AI and RFID offers significant potential for optimise these functions. While a considerable amount of research has concentrated on Digital Twin development for supply chain management, its application in integrated and privacy-conscious retail & sales management systems is still remains a developing area. Thus, this thesis focuses on designing and developing a conceptual Digital Twin system to address this gap. The thesis begins with a comparative analysis of current inventory management systems as a foundational study. It then presents a conceptual DT architecture that integrates RFID and simulated Point of Sale (POS) data for a physical retail store. The core contribution of the thesis is the functional DT prototype validated using simulated data and demonstrated in a Unity-based 3D virtual environment. In addition, the system integrates simulated AI models (SMA, WMA, and LR) to reflect demand forecasting and automated inventory alerts. The findings of the research revealed t

title: Pros and Cons of AI Humanoid Robots in Human Life
abstract: About This Book Pros and Cons of AI Humanoid Robots in Human Life is a comprehensive technical examination of the most transformative technology of our era. As Boston Dynamics, Tesla, Figure AI, and Unitree deploy AI-powered humanoid robots into real-world environments, the engineering decisions being made today will shape human society for decades. This book provides an evidence-based, dual-perspective analysis across 15 chapters and 8 parts: Parts I–V (Chapters 1–12): The technical foundations — Physical AI, ROS 2, digital twins, NVIDIA Isaac, and Vision-Language-Action systems Part VI (Chapter 13): The genuine benefits — healthcare, manufacturing, hazardous environments, elderly care Part VII (Chapter 14): The real risks — safety, security vulnerabilities, economic displacement, autonomy failures Part VIII (Chapter 15): Ethics, policy frameworks, and a path forward No advocacy. title: Cyclical Force Generation for Triboelectric Nanogenerators: A Review of Mechatronic Approaches, Challenges and Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) convert low-frequency and irregular mechanical energy into electrical energy for self-powered sensors, wearable electronics, Internet-of-Things devices and distributed energy systems. Although major advances have been made in triboelectric materials, surface engineering and device architectures, the mechanical excitation applied during TENG testing remains an important source of experimental variability. Manual tapping, pressing and sliding can introduce uncontrolled changes in force, displacement, velocity, frequency, contact area and waveform, making comparison between experiments difficult. This review examines cyclical force generation as a controllable subsystem for TENG characterization. Linear actuators, servo systems, electrodynamic shakers, cam-follower and crank-slider mechanisms, electromechanical testing machines and tribometers are compared in terms of force/displacement control, frequency, repeatability, cost and suitability. The review also summarizes the mechanical parameters that should be measured together with electrical output and presents a conceptual closed-loop cyclical force generator (CFG) incorporating an actua

title: Recent advancements in AI-assisted tool path generation for CNC machining
Uma Plataforma Experimental para Digital Twins sobre LoRaWAN Aplicada a Aquicultura
abstract: Resumo: O crescimento da Internet das Coisas (IoT) tem impulsionado o uso de Gêmeos Digitais (Digital Twins) como representações virtuais de sistemas físicos, cuja qualidade depende diretamente da camada de comunicação responsável pela coleta de dados. Redes LoRaWAN, adequadas a esse cenário por seu baixo consumo energético e longo alcance, ainda carecem de plataformas experimentais que permitam investigar sistematicamente sua integração com Digital Twins. Este artigo apresenta uma plataforma experimental para investigação de Digital Twins sobre LoRaWAN, composta por infraestrutura de sensoriamento IoT, um gateway já implantado, um banco de dados de séries temporais e uma camada de visualização, projetada para suportar múltiplos estudos de caso. Como primeiro estudo, a plataforma é aplicada ao trade-off entre consumo energético e qualidade de atualização de Digital Twins em um cenário de aquicultura, no qual o Digital Twin representa o estado da qualidade de água de um tanque de piscicultura. Como contribuições, apresenta-se um protótipo de dashboard e diretrizes iniciais de parâmetros LoRaWAN em aplicações orientadas a Digital Twin.

title: Communication and Intelligent Technologies Enabling the Evolution of Smart Grids: From Unidirectional Power Systems to Autonomous Bidirectional Networks
abstract: The transition from conventional power systems to Smart Grids is driven by the increasing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs), battery energy storage systems (BESS), electric vehicles (EVs), and power-electronic interfaces, together with growing requirements for flexibility, reliability, resilience, and efficiency. This transformation requires more than infrastructure digitalization: it depends on the coordinated development of communication, digital information, analytical, and operational capabilities. This paper reviews these technological layers and discusses how their integration enables the evolution from unidirectional and weakly observable networks toward bidirectional, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous power systems. Communication technologies are examined across wide-, field-, neighborhood-, and home-area networks, while intelligent technologies include state estimation, forecasting, optimization, artificial intelligence, machine learning, digital twins, ADMS, and DERMS. A capability-driven framework relates these technologies to successive grid generations. The analysis indicates that autonomy emerges from functional integration, with communications en

title: From Notebook to Control Room: Reproducible MLOps for Accelerator Digital Twins
abstract: Scientific user facilities like the Linac Coherent Light Source (LCLS), the world’s brightest X-ray free-electron laser at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, require rapid, continuous control adjustments to maximize beam time and experimental throughput. Machine Learning (ML) surrogate models can help operators navigate complex parameter spaces, but only if those models can be deployed reliably and updated without disrupting operations. How do you reliably and sustainably move ML models from various researchers’ training environments into a facility production system? In this talk, we present a reproducible MLOps framework that addresses this challenge in the context of digital twin deployments for online accelerator control. We discuss how we standardized the Kubernetes-based deployment of digital twins and ML inference services by prioritizing reproducibility across environments through container-based packaging, rigorous model versioning and experiment tracking integrated into the deployment pipeline, minimal boilerplate templates so domain scientists can onboard models without DevOps expertise, and flexible configuration to adapt across diverse control scenarios. title: DESIGNING RESILIENT ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS THROUGH AI-DRIVEN DEPENDENCY MAPPING AND IMPACT ANALYSIS
abstract: Enterprise systems are now often spread across a range of hidden technical and organizational dependencies; technical debt can accumulate, configurations can change, and failures can propagate. Redundancy or post-incident recovery alone is not enough for resilience design; such environments require continuously updated dependency knowledge and credible impact analysis before, during, and after change. This review considers peer-reviewed journal literature published between 2015 and 2024 that is relevant to the dependency mapping and impact analysis of resilient enterprise systems using AI. The studies included in the review are grouped around microservice architecture, process mining, digital twins, graph learning, anomaly detection, explainable artificial intelligence and resilience measurement, as well as AIOps. Based on the literature, it is shown that AI-based mapping can increase observability of runtime relations, aid in change-risk prioritization, and aid in failure localization with architectural models and operational telemetry. There are still gaps in causal validation, cross-layer dependency representation, data quality, explainability and evaluation against real enterpr

title: CONTEXT-AWARE DIGITAL TWIN ARCHITECTURES FOR REAL-TIME TRANSPORTATION AND WAREHOUSE OPTIMIZATION IN CLOUD-NATIVE SUPPLY CHAIN PLATFORMS
abstract: Context-aware digital twins are emerging as enabling architectures for coordinating responses to disruptions across inventory, warehouse, and transportation operations in cloud-based supply-chain platforms. They are important because they can be used to link continually evolving operational representations with optimization services that are able to react to traffic conditions, order arrivals, equipment status, changes in inventory, and facility constraints. This article reviews peer-reviewed journal literature on digital supply-chain twins, warehouse intelligence, dynamic vehicle routing, Internet of Things-enabled logistics, microservice architectures, and computational modelling. Some studies indicate that digital-twin approaches can improve visibility, scenario evaluation, and decision coordination in specific settings, but there is very little evidence of fully integrated real-time optimization of transportation and warehouse operations. Closed-loop orchestration has not been a primary focus of existing implementations, which tend to focus on warehouse simulation or monitoring, route adjustment, or resilience analysis across logistics domains. Geographies of simulation: Representational asymmetries in planetary computing. The case of Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
abstract: The ambition to model the Earth at a 1:1 scale through planetary computing presents a challenge that transcends technical constraints. At planetary scale, this challenge becomes an epistemological dilemma: the tension between metric fidelity and morphological coherence. This article analyzes Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 not merely as a commercial product, but as a critical exponent of the Earth-as-interface paradigm, sustained by a distributed infrastructure of massive geospatial data and cloud computing. Employing an inverse geography methodology grounded in expert-based geographic evaluation, the study systematically assesses the system’s integrity across diverse landscape typologies and observation scales. The findings show that the simulation operates under a regime of selective realism: while achieving high levels of atmospheric and orographic plausibility at macro scales, it consistently breaks down at complex biophysical interfaces, such as fluvial networks and coastal environments, due to a functional decoupling between terrestrial and atmospheric processes. The article concludes that Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 represents a shift from the simulation of environmental

title: A Review of Human-Centric Construction Manufacturing: Current Practices and Research Opportunities
abstract: Abstract The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on-site. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Human-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems. Despite growing interest in human-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology-driven. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future re

Biomimetic Retinal Sensor Architecture and CUDA Digital Twin for Objective Evaluation of Display Temporal Dithering (FRC) and Cortical Mach Band Load
abstract: Conventional display metrology relies on stationary CMOS frame cameras or single-point photodiodes to evaluate display flicker and spatial image quality. While suitable for characterizing deep Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM) luminance dips, stationary camera sensors fundamentally fail to capture the neuro-ophthalmic load induced by sub-LSB Temporal Frame Rate Control (FRC) dithering and bit-depth quantization banding. A conventional camera sensor integrates photons linearly over a fixed exposure window on a static pixel grid. Conversely, the human visual system processes light through dual parallel retinal pathways (Parvocellular sustained integration and Magnocellular transient differentiation) coupled with horizontal-cell lateral inhibition during continuous oculomotor motion [1, 2, 3]. This paper presents two contributions to display metrology and visual ergonomics: A hardware specification for a Biomimetic Retinal Sensor (Mixed-Signal CMOS-MEMS ASIC) incorporating parallel Parvocellular (P) and Magnocellular (M) analog pixel branches, an on-chip Center-Surround lateral inhibition grid, and an active MEMS oculomotor smooth-pursuit optical stage [8, 9]. title: “Quality by Design (QbD)-Driven Development of Advanced Wound Therapeutics: From Risk-Based Formulation Design to Clinically Translatable Smart Wound Systems”
abstract: Chronic wound management represents one of the most significant unmet clinical and economic challenges in contemporary healthcare, with an annual global burden exceeding USD 22 billion and disproportionately poor clinical translation rates for advanced wound therapeutics despite substantial research investment.Quality by Design (QbD), formalised through ICH Q8 (R2), Q9, and Q10, offers a rigorous, prospective framework for wound formulation development by systematically linking material attributes and process parameters to patient-relevant quality outcomes.This narrative review critically evaluates the application of QbD principles encompassing the Quality Target Product Profile (QTPP), Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs), Critical Material Attributes (CMAs), Critical Process Parameters (CPPs), risk assessment methodologies, and Design of Experiments (DoE) strategies across the principal advanced wound therapeutic platforms: lipid nanocarriers, polymeric nanoparticles, hydrogels, electrospun scaffolds, biopolymeric films, and stimulus-responsive smart dressings.Published evidence demonstrates that DoE-based Response Surface Methodology (RSM) consistently delivers 20-40% improvements

title: Physics-constrained generative digital twin for early leakage detection in nitrogen accumulators in governor control systems at hydroelectric power plants
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen pre-charge loss in hydropower governor accumulators is a slow but critical degradation process that weakens hydraulic energy storage, reduces pressure-retention time, increases pump cycling, and accelerates thermal–mechanical stress. Conventional pressure-threshold SCADA alarms can miss the early stage because oil pressure may remain inside the operating band while waveform dynamics deteriorate. This paper proposes a SCADA-calibrated physics-constrained generative digital twin for early nitrogen leakage diagnosis. Limited anonymized field-SCADA observations are used only as calibration anchors for pressure set-points, pump-ON duration, pump-OFF retention, temperature range, and the fast-rise/slow-decay waveform; they are not presented as a complete labeled leakage dataset. The evaluation uses 80,000 physics-constrained synthetic training records and 20,000 independently generated synthetic test records per run, balanced across eight degradation months. Train and test records are produced with disjoint seeds and no shared cycles or residual draws. title: Circles through Natural Numbers
abstract: This paper introduces Prime-Diameter Circles (PDCs)—a geometric framework that unifies prime generation, distribution, and classical number-theoretic conjectures. By defining circles whose diameters are bounded by prime coordinates, PDCs reveal profound symmetries: primality reflection, parity constraints, and digital index restrictions. These properties naturally encode twin primes, prime gaps, and arithmetic progressions, while offering geometric restatements of celebrated conjectures. Extending the framework, Factor-Finder Circles provide geometric divisibility and primality tests, bridging continuous geometry with discrete number theory. Together, these constructions demonstrate that primes, often studied through analytic or algebraic lenses, can be elegantly characterised through circle symmetries—opening new pathways for visualising, approximating, and testing primality. This work highlights the profound mathematical unity achieved when prime theory is reframed through geometry.

title: Serviceability-oriented multimodal data integration for prescriptive road-tunnel maintenance digital twins
abstract: Road tunnels are indispensable components of transport networks, providing critical connections while operating continuously under demanding environmental, geological, and hydrogeological conditions. Their large dimensions, confined geometry, and uninterrupted operation make comprehensive inspection challenging. Full-face inspection technologies such as light detection and ranging (LiDAR) can rapidly capture high-resolution surface data; however, the resulting digital models are often descriptive rather than explanatory or instructive. This limitation is critical because seemingly minor defects may indicate latent deterioration and, if untreated, can lead to severe safety and operational consequences. With advances in artificial intelligence, particularly large language models (LLMs) and robotic inspection platforms, tunnel inspection is expected to move beyond defect detection towards knowledge-driven diagnosis and decision support. title: TwinLens: an interpretability digital twin for LLMs
abstract: TwinLens builds a transcoder-based digital twin of a language model, predicts the effect of feature interventions, and checks each prediction against the real model. Across 8,064 interventions on GPT-2 small (56 prompts), the linear twin that attribution graphs describe ranks real effects poorly (Spearman rho 0.20). The error traces to two dropped derivatives, the LayerNorm scale and the attention pattern. Restoring both keeps the graph exactly linear and raises rho to 0.53, matching the nonlinear replacement model (0.52), and cuts catastrophic misses from 2.2% to 0.05%. The fix replicates on Qwen3-0.6B (2,304 edits). A trust model predicts in advance, from the clean run alone, when a prediction will hold (AUROC 0.93).

title: TwinVFI-PPO: Uncertainty-Aware Joint Bitrate Adaptation and Frame Interpolation for Neural Video Streaming
abstract: Adaptive bitrate (ABR) control and client-side video frame interpolation (VFI) are usually optimized as separate modules, even though they compete for the same playback, bandwidth, and compute budgets and jointly determine rendered quality. We present TwinVFI-PPO, an uncertainty-aware framework that selects bitrate and VFI mode as a unified action. A probabilistic network digital twin estimates short-horizon throughput distributions, a motion-confidence VFI branch predicts restoration gain and tail latency, and a feasibility-aware PPO policy suppresses bitrate–mode combinations that cannot satisfy the available presentation budget. The resulting controller optimizes encoded quality, rebuffering, temporal variation, interpolation latency, and uncertainty within a single sequential decision process. On Vimeo90K and UCF101, the proposed VFI branch reaches 36.17/0.986 and 38.29/0.975 PSNR/SSIM at 53 ms for 720p inference. Across FCC+Norway, OBOE, and Live no-loss replays, TwinVFI-PPO obtains average QoElin and QoElog scores of 47.72 and 46.86, outperforming PPO-ABR by 3.29% and 2.72%. abstract: Logistics 5.0 indicates the combination of Industry 5.0’s important principles such as human-centricity, resiliency, and sustainability with the advanced digital capabilities of Logistics 4.0. While a growing number of developed countries are starting to adopt AI, digital twins, collaborative robots, and human-machine decision-making systems, there is still only limited evidence available regarding Logistics 5.0 implementation in India. The purpose of this study is to find out the main technological, financial, human, infrastructural, regulatory, organizational, cultural, and sustainability hurdles on the way to Logistics 5.0 implementation in Indian logistics. title: Counterfactual Federated Digital Twins for Causal Fault Localization, Remaining-Life Uncertainty Quantification, and Prescriptive Maintenance of Utility-Scale Solar Farms
abstract: This repository provides the MATLAB R2023b implementation of a physics-guided hierarchical federated digital-twin framework for utility-scale photovoltaic farms using the BR-PVGen dataset. The eight-stage pipeline integrates data quality control, temporal synchronization, physical-reference calibration, federated residual learning, plant-specific personalization, controlled synthetic fault localization, censoring-aware survival forecasting, and simulation-based maintenance optimization. The package includes executable MATLAB scripts, validation utilities, statistical auditing, and reproducibility documentation. Observed power-prediction performance is distinguished from synthetic fault, degradation, and maintenance outcomes.

title: FinTwin: a point-in-time system-dynamics digital twin for corporate liquidity stress testing
abstract: FinTwin turns a company's SEC XBRL filings into a calibrated stock-and-flow (system-dynamics) model of its finances and stress-tests it with Monte Carlo simulation. Every parameter is estimated from point-in-time filings, so backtests are free of look-ahead and restatement bias. This archive contains the Python reference engine, the point-in-time XBRL pipeline, the research experiments and statistics, the scripts that generate every table, figure and number in the accompanying paper, the TypeScript browser engine and dashboard, and data snapshots. Main results (paper in docs/paper): frozen before COVID-19, the twin ranks 2020-21 cash burn of 333 S&P 500 non-financial companies better than the Altman, Ohlson and Zmijewski scores, but a trailing free-cash-flow margin ranks it better still, and no fundamentals-based predictor ranks the shock-induced part of the burn. Fed the revenue that actually followed, the twin identifies where a margin pass-through rule misjudges cash flow (incremental correlation 0.30 across 2,661 firm-years, positive in every year 2014-2023), and its revenue forecasts beat a seasonal random walk and exponential smoothing. abstract: This study examines the effect of government tax reforms on the performance of small businesses in North-West Nigeria, with small business performance positioned as the central dependent variable grounded in both global and contextual evidence. abstract: Reconstructive plastic surgery has evolved from relatively simple techniques of wound closure and skin replacement into a multidisciplinary field capable of restoring increasingly complex anatomy and function. Skin grafts and local or regional flaps remain indispensable because they are reliable, accessible and clinically established, while microsurgery has expanded the ability to transfer vascularized tissue to defects created by trauma, burns, cancer, congenital anomalies and other conditions. At the same time, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine have introduced a different objective: rather than merely replacing missing tissue, the field increasingly seeks to recreate biological environments that support regeneration, vascularization, innervation and long-term functional integration. This narrative review examines that transition and integrates conventional reconstructive surgery with contemporary advances in biomaterials, stem-cell-based therapies, tissue-engineered skin, vascular and nerve engineering, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, digital surgical planning, artificial intelligence (AI), robotic microsurgery and emerging digital-twin concepts. NANOROBOT-ENHANCED DIGITAL TWINS OF BRAIN STATE AT THE LIMIT A multiscale, uncertainty-aware research atlas on microrobotic observations, neural inverse problems, active model discrimination and the limits of computational brain twins. This research monograph asks whether additional microscale observations or strictly bounded reversible experiments can distinguish competing neural-state models that explain conventional measurements equally well. The twin is explicitly defined as a versioned scientific belief, not a digital person, a mind reader or a clinically validated instrument. Its objective is not maximum model complexity but improved identifiability, calibrated prediction under new conditions and faithful retention of failed hypotheses. The work develops five layers: multiscale neural and microenvironment state representation; posterior equivalence and prior sensitivity; non-clinical safe experimental design; frozen-version forking, rollback and reference ancestry; and blind prospective validation against classical state-space systems and independently specified alternatives. Its research architecture includes 30 distinct mathematical derivation plates linked to later chapters, 82 chapters with five independently paginated research sections apiece, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 revisable Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger identifies existing support for brain modeling, latent neural dynamics, experiment design and preclinical microrobot tracking while preventing those sources from being mistaken for evidence of the proposed integrated system. Key research questions include: Can two equally accurate virtual brains be separated by a small, permissible observation? How can the effect of a measurement itself be separated from neural change? When does a prior dominate the inferred brain state? Can the model predict unseen function rather than reconstruct a training signal? Can another laboratory reproduce a rejected twin and safely return to an earlier version? SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND LIMITATIONS This is a forward-looking, non-clinical research synthesis and experimental hypothesis architecture. It provides no personal medical advice, patient-specific interpretations or instruction to deliver neural interventions. Existing murine microrobot tracking and virtual-brain modeling studies do not establish autonomous neural nanorobot readout, human safety, privacy-sensitive mind inference or therapeutic efficacy. Proposed formulas, experiments, research gates and answer embryos are not newly validated biological laws or executed experiments. The work keeps independent safety vetoes, privacy, external reproducibility and explicit model retirement as first-class constraints. Research questions remain open to refutation, correction and reconstruction by future human and AI researchers.

abstract: Abstract Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent chronic disorder with marked clinical heterogeneity and divergent outcomes. Current pathophysiological models fail to fully account for inter-individual variation in progression toward steatohepatitis and systemic multimorbidity. This Perspective posits the mitochondrion as an integrative functional hub where genomic predisposition, epigenomic plasticity, and bioenergetic signaling converge to shape the disease's longitudinal trajectory. We synthesize evidence from the mitonuclear interactome—the co-evolutionary and functional coordination between nuclear and mitochondrial genomes, hepatic epigenomic remodeling, and circulating mitochondrial metabotypes to propose a unified systems biology framework: the MASLD-Mitochondrial Digital Twin (MASLD-MDT). This multiscale platform integrates high-resolution biological data—including single-cell mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) heteroplasmy, NAD+ redox dynamics, and the systemic efflux of mitochondrial-derived peptides (MDPs)—to simulate individualized disease kinetics. Circles through Natural Numbers
abstract: This paper introduces Prime-Diameter Circles (PDCs)—a geometric framework that unifies prime generation, distribution, and classical number-theoretic conjectures. By defining circles whose diameters are bounded by prime coordinates, PDCs reveal profound symmetries: primality reflection, parity constraints, and digital index restrictions. These properties naturally encode twin primes, prime gaps, and arithmetic progressions, while offering geometric restatements of celebrated conjectures. Extending the framework, Factor-Finder Circles provide geometric divisibility and primality tests, bridging continuous geometry with discrete number theory. Together, these constructions demonstrate that primes, often studied through analytic or algebraic lenses, can be elegantly characterised through circle symmetries—opening new pathways for visualising, approximating, and testing primality. This work highlights the profound mathematical unity achieved when prime theory is reframed through geometry.

abstract: The General Foundation Program (GFP) serves as the primary gateway for Omani students entering higher education, focusing on the development of academic and soft skills essential for national development. However, traditional assessment methods, primarily static grades, fail to capture the complexity of a student’s journey or their readiness for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR). This research proposes a Student Digital Twin (SDT) framework—a dynamic, data-driven virtual profile that mirrors a student's academic performance, learning behavior, and digital skill acquisition in real-time. By utilizing a qualitative conceptual synthesis, this paper outlines a four-layer architecture designed to provide personalized pedagogical support. The model explicitly aligns GFP learning outcomes with the strategic goals of Oman Vision 2040, transforming the foundation year into a predictive, high-tech engine for national competitiveness.

title: AI-driven whole-life costing for decision-ready UK public building retrofits
abstract: Abstract Public-sector building retrofits in the United Kingdom require decisions that balance whole-life cost, carbon reduction, service continuity and auditability under limited data and constrained capital budgets. This paper develops a decision-ready whole-life costing (WLC) workflow that integrates environmental, social and governance (ESG) priorities with uncertainty-aware artificial intelligence (AI) for public-building retrofit appraisal. The workflow combines national non-domestic Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) and Display Energy Certificate (DEC) data, Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme (PSDS) delivery evidence and stakeholder inputs to construct a scenario library of public-building archetypes, retrofit actions and appraisal constraints. Stakeholder priorities from interviews, a questionnaire and a co-design workshop are translated into transparent weights using fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (F-AHP). These weights parameterise a reinforcement learning (RL) planner, while a Bayesian convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (BCNN–LSTM) surrogate provides uncertainty-bounded energy, carbon and cost trajectories for repeated policy evaluation. title: Probabilistic Digital Twin Framework for Climate-Resilient Offshore Infrastructure under Coupled Corrosion–Fatigue Degradation and Environmental Uncertainty
abstract: Offshore assets deteriorate through mechanisms that reinforce one another: corrosion removes section and raises the local stress, the elevated stress accelerates fatigue, and fatigue damage exposes fresh metal to the marine environment. Deterministic integrity assessment cannot represent that feedback or the environmental variability that drives it. This paper presents a physics-informed probabilistic digital twin for offshore infrastructure in which coupled corrosion–fatigue degradation modelling, Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, sequential Bayesian data assimilation and a physics-constrained neural surrogate are combined within a single lifecycle assessment loop. The degradation state is a bounded composite index of corrosion penetration, Miner fatigue damage, cumulative environmental exposure and an interaction component, with the stress-amplification coupling regularised so that no governing relation becomes singular as failure is approached. title: AI-Driven Digital Twin Frameworks for Predictive Maintenance and Closed-Loop Remote Control in Smart Factories: A Structured Review
abstract: The increasing connectivity of industrial machines has changed maintenance from a largely schedule-driven activity into a continuous, data-driven process. Digital Twin (DT) technology supports this transition by providing a dynamic virtual representation of a physical asset that is continually updated using operational data. When artificial intelligence (AI) is embedded within the twin, the resulting system can move beyond visualization to support fault identification, anomaly detection, degradation assessment, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, and maintenance decision-making. This paper presents a structured review of AI-enabled digital twin approaches for predictive maintenance in smart manufacturing, examined end-to-end across physical sensing, data acquisition, communication, twin synchronization, intelligent analytics, maintenance decision-making, and remote corrective control. abstract: Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Digital Twins require persistent geospatial infrastructures that connect semantic, spatial, temporal, environmental, road-reference, and 3D urban information across simulation and visualization. abstract: This paper addresses the problem of optimizing inventory management and warehousing logistics for locomotive depots under conditions of information deficiency and uncertainty regarding the condition of rolling stock. As traditional planned-preventive maintenance strategies have exhausted their efficiency, organizing an effective repair infrastructure requires rational resource allocation and optimal stocking of critical units. abstract: Abstract In structural health monitoring, full-field response sensing and monitoring are essential to establish a digital twin model. However, directly measuring all required structural loads and responses is costly and impractical. Simultaneous estimations of structural loads and responses are consequently developed, which is, however, an ill-posed problem. This paper aims to address the ill-posed nature of the simultaneous estimation of load and response from insufficient observations, which is realized by reducing the dimension of unknown loads via principal component analysis to derive the equivalent system functions. First, a set of force basis vectors is calculated from the structural impulse responses in a single time step to replace the original load vector. Subsequently, a reduced equivalent system model is obtained with sufficient controllability on the original system model. Then, the equivalent loads and full-field responses can be simultaneously estimated by the Kalman-type joint input-state estimation filters. abstract: Motivated by Industry 4.0, digital twin (DT) technology has emerged as a pivotal enabler of intelligent transformation in the construction industry, addressing challenges such as fragmented management and limited decision support. However, its practical adoption remains early and is constrained by multiple interdependent barriers. Existing studies often examine these barriers in isolation, overlooking their perceived interrelationships and relative influence pathways. To address this gap, we identify 28 barrier factors through a structured literature review and expert consultation, categorizing them into technical, personnel, organizational, policy, industry, and economic subsystems. We then hypothesize linkages among these barriers and develop a system dynamics model to simulate their relative influence on subsystem-level barrier accumulation. Simulation results show that technical, personnel, and industry barriers exert the strongest influence on DT implementation. abstract: Food microbiology is moving from episodic, laboratory-centered testing toward connected systems that can detect, interpret, and anticipate microbial hazards across food production and distribution. This transition is being driven by the convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), biosensors, computer vision, spectroscopy, predictive microbiology, Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure, and digital-twin concepts. The value of these technologies lies not in replacing reference microbiological methods, but in shortening the interval between sampling, evidence generation, risk interpretation, and corrective action. AI can extract patterns from images, spectral fingerprints, sensor signals, molecular data, and environmental measurements; biosensors can convert biological recognition into rapidly measurable signals; and connected monitoring architectures can place these outputs within dynamic process and supply-chain contexts. title: Hydro Digital Twins for Coastal Governance: A Scoping Review of Objectives, Data Characteristics, and Maturity
abstract: Coastal zones and their connected freshwater and marine systems are among the environments most acutely exposed to accelerating climate hazards. European policy has responded by placing Digital Twin (DT) infrastructures at the centre of its climate adaptation and ocean governance agenda: Destination Earth for the Earth system, and the European Digital Twin of the Ocean (EDITO) for the marine and coastal domain. This scoping review defines and evaluates Hydro Digital Twins (HDTs), encompassing Digital Twins of the Ocean (DTOs), coastal-zone DTs, and freshwater-system DTs, as instruments for coastal management, water territory governance, and climate adaptation decision support. Conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR, the review screened 231 records (January 2020 to September 2025) and retained 21 studies, each coded against a thirteen-parameter framework organised on a governance axis and a data-centric axis. Governance objectives consistently outweigh technical motivations: risk reduction dominates (7/21 studies, 33%), followed by environmental monitoring (5/21 studies, 24%) and coastal management (4/21 studies, 19%). title: Artificial Intelligence for Smart Grid and Renewable Energy Management: A Review of Techniques, Applications, and Future Directions
abstract: Intermittent renewable generation, volatile loads, and concerns over grid stability have become defining features of modern power systems. Addressing these challenges with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) is attracting growing attention, including through better forecasting, automated demand response, optimized energy storage, and smart grid fault detection. This paper highlights the various AI-based techniques developed across the smart grid landscape, ranging from solar and wind forecasting to short-term load forecasting, demand-side management, electricity price forecasting, energy storage and battery management, grid resilience, and digital twins. It offers an overview of recently published work, including the major approaches, namely deep learning (LSTM and Transformer models), explainable AI, multi-agent systems, reinforcement learning, and federated learning, together with their strengths and limitations. The paper also presents a conceptual three-layer framework comprising edge sensing, federated forecasting and control, and explainable operator support at the distribution-utility level; the framework is not validated empirically. title: Multi-scale integration of smart technologies for climate-resilient urban road infrastructure: a systematic literature review and conceptual framework
abstract: Purpose Urban road infrastructure (roads, bridges, pavement and drainage systems) is increasingly vulnerable to climate change impacts, such as extreme weather events, flooding and heat stress, threatening its structural integrity and long-term functionality. This systematic literature review investigates how smart technologies can enhance the climate resilience of urban road systems. Design/methodology/approach A four-phase systematic literature review was conducted, beginning with the selection of 78 key studies from 1,684 Scopus-indexed publications. This was followed by bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and qualitative content analysis with NVivo. The review employed an inductive approach, focusing on identifying technological applications, integration patterns, challenges and frameworks through systematic content analysis. Findings Through systematic content analysis, the review identified seven core technologies, including Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Building Information Modelling (BIM), Digital Twin (DT) systems, the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD) and Remote Sensing (RS). title: Semantic and Uncertainty-Aware Synchronization for Edge-Cloud Digital Twin
abstract: This dataset accompanies the paper Semantic and Uncertainty-Aware Synchronization for Edge-Cloud Digital Twins. It brings together synchronization evaluation data, a Python reference implementation, and technical documentation for the proposed framework. The data_record archive contains CSV evaluation data covering synchronization frequency, edge–cloud consistency, communication volume, uncertainty coverage, ablation results, and trigger attribution. The scheduler_alg.rar archive provides the Python synchronization scheduler and supporting evaluation scripts. The separately uploaded Word document describes the semantic-event taxonomy, probe-mapping scheme, mathematical definitions, and data organization. These materials support interpretation of the reported results, verification of aggregate calculations, and further development of semantic and uncertainty-aware synchronization methods.

title: A Review of Virtual Power Plant Technology and Practice Development in China: Progress, Challenges, and Outlook
abstract: As an important vehicle for resource integration in the construction of new power systems, the virtual power plant (VPP) has moved from the demonstration and pilot stage into a critical transition period of standardized construction and market-oriented operation. This paper systematically reviews the technological development trajectory and the practical progress of VPPs in China. At the technical level, key advances are reviewed across three core domains: resource perception and adjustable potential assessment; optimal dispatch and control strategies (covering centralized, distributed, and reinforcement learning-based methods); and cloud–edge–terminal platform architecture and information security. At the practical level, the paper traces the policy evolution from the early demand response pilots to the 2025 Guiding Opinions on Accelerating the Development of Virtual Power Plants, surveys grid-led and third-party-aggregator demonstration projects, and analyzes business models and pathways for participation in electricity markets. On this basis, the key challenges facing Chinese VPPs in technical standardization, market access, regulatory frameworks, and data security are analyzed,

INTEGRATED COST-SCHEDULE AND PROCUREMENT ANALYTICS FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPPLY CHAINS IN SAUDI MEGA-PROJECTS: ENHANCING FORECASTING AND PROJECT DELIVERY UNDER VISION 2030
abstract: Saudi mega-projects operate through dense networks of designers, contractors, manufacturers, logistics providers and specialist suppliers, so cost and schedule performance cannot be governed effectively as separate reporting streams. Procurement commitments shape the timing and price of resources; schedule changes alter purchasing priorities and logistics demand; and commercial variations feed back into forecast completion cost. This review develops an integrated framework for cost-schedule and procurement analytics in construction supply chains, with particular relevance to Saudi Arabias Vision 2030 delivery environment. Thirty peer-reviewed studies published from 2020 to 2025 were synthesised across artificial intelligence in construction management, project cost prediction, schedule forecasting, construction supply-chain modelling, resilience and digital-twin-enabled control. The evidence indicates that predictive value emerges when cost, schedule and procurement records share consistent identifiers, timestamps and decision horizons. Hyper-Realistic Digital Twin of a Coach: Development and Evaluation of a Sports Training Simulator
abstract: Thanks to advances in the field of computer graphics and natural language processing, it is increasingly possible to create multimedia applications that use a hyper-realistic avatar as the main element of the communication interface with the user. However, major challenges remain, especially when the avatar is required to simulate the appearance and behavior of a real person. This work describes the methodology and tools necessary to create a hyper-realistic avatar that simulates the appearance and behavior of a real person. The methods and tools have been tested by developing a new application that simulates the sports training process. The design of the new application is based on the hypothesis that a digital system that hyper-realistically simulates real training can offer similar benefits to the real one and, therefore, be used to complement real training sessions and thus facilitating the continued performance of the exercise. In this work, a complete sports training simulator has been developed with special emphasis on simulating the coach's real appearance, his way of moving and speaking, as well as a personalized exercise routine generator. A Hybrid System Integrating SLAM and TLS for Efficient Spatial Data Acquisition
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid TLS (Terrestrial Laser Scanning)—SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) framework for spatial data acquisition that integrates mobile laser scanning (Hovermap) with high-precision terrestrial laser scanning (RIEGL TLS). The proposed approach combines the efficiency of SLAM-based data capture with the geometric reliability of TLS reference measurements, enabling fast and accurate generation of spatial datasets that support decision-making in architecture, urban planning, facility management, and digital transformation workflows. A key contribution of the study is a structured workflow for acquisition and processing, including TLS reference loop design, segmented SLAM data acquisition, and a dual-level validation strategy. The framework additionally incorporates partial measurement redundancy, enabling internal self-verification of data consistency and improving robustness against potential measurement errors and SLAM drift. The proposed workflow was validated in a continuously operating public building, demonstrating that high-quality spatial data can be acquired without disrupting building functionality. title: A comprehensive review of underground CO2 storage and associated risks
abstract: Geological carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) storage has emerged as one of the most promising technologies for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and achieving global carbon neutrality. This review provides a comprehensive overview of CO 2 geological storage with emphasis on storage formations, trapping mechanisms, storage capacity assessment methods, monitoring techniques, risk assessment, mitigation strategies, and the key factors governing long-term storage security. Major geological storage formations—deep saline aquifers, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, unmineable coal seams, and basalt formations—are compared in terms of storage capacity, injectivity, containment, and technological maturity; and the fundamental CO 2 trapping mechanisms (structural, residual, solubility, and mineral trapping) are examined together with their contributions to long-term storage permanence. Storage-capacity assessment methods are critically evaluated within the Carbon Sequestration Leadership Forum (CSLF) Theoretical–Effective–Practical–Matched Capacity framework, including the volumetric equations used for saline aquifers and depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs and their associated sources of uncertainty. Current and Future Applicability of Complex In Vitro Models to Biotransformation Studies
abstract: This paragraph examines the evolution of drug research models to assess biotransformation issues, tracing the transition from traditional 1930s-era in vivo animal studies and simple in vitro systems (such as liver microsomes and hepatocytes) to advanced Complex in vitro Models (CIVMs) and Microphysiological Systems (MPS). While traditional models offer robustness, they lack the 3D structure, longevity, and multiorgan interactions necessary for accurate physiological prediction. The rise of CIVMs—including 2D+ co-cultures, 3D liver spheroids, and organ-on-chip (OoC) technology—represents a significant shift toward better simulating human physiology. Although the majority of CIVMs are based on hepatic systems, they are also applied to other organs (gut, lungs, kidney, and the blood-brain barrier) and multiorgan-chips to study complex cycles like entero-hepatic metabolism. Despite challenges such as high costs, low throughput, and technical complexities like non-specific binding, CIVMs offer improved human translatability and support 3R initiatives. title: AI-Based Decision-Making Framework for Climate Change-Induced Flood Risk Management and Urban Resilience
abstract: Climate change has intensified the frequency and severity of urban flooding, creating unprecedented challenges for municipalities worldwide. This study develops an AI-based decision-making framework that integrates machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and geospatial analytics to enhance urban flood risk management and resilience planning. The framework employs ensemble machine learning algorithms including Random Forest, XG Boost, and Cat Boost for flood susceptibility mapping, coupled with SHAP-based interpretability to decode model predictions and translate them into actionable policy insights at administrative scales. A city-scale digital twin component enables real-time flood impact simulation and cascading infrastructure disruption analysis, while a multi-criteria decision support module prioritizes adaptation investments based on economic risk assessment and equity considerations. The framework was validated using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SAR data and hydrological records across diverse urban environments, demonstrating superior predictive performance with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values exceeding 0.95 for ensemble models. It rejects the idea that a twin is a true factory copy and instead treats every twin as a versioned, decision-conditioned belief with a calibration date, validity domain, competing models, residual sentinels, and reset conditions. Calibration discrepancy and twin families: Separate parameter inference model inadequacy and measurement error while preserving competing explanations. Residual sentinels and predictive control: Detect drift select active calibration bound control abstain hand over and reset. Portability replay and successor governance: Transfer process intent count maintenance burden preserve failed twins and enable replacement or retirement. Minimum demonstrator Two competing twins fit the same historical deposition or etch data but encode different hidden-state or discrepancy mechanisms. A low-risk, preregistered perturbation is selected for information gain and executed on witness structures. Both twins predict an unseen batch and hidden maintenance transition. Residual sentinels must detect invalidity, calibrated uncertainty must cover errors, and control authority must demote or abstain before unsafe action. A third party then replays calibration, model fission, reset, and the final decision. Central deliverable The Fissionable Foundry Twin binds physical assets, state graphs, wafer and material genealogy, sensors, references, multiscale models, calibration data, discrepancies, competing branches, forecasts, residuals, drift sentinels, authority tiers, controls, handovers, terminal function, failures, resources, resets, and successor choices. Another team must be able to reproduce, refute, fork, reset, simplify, replace, or retire the twin.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Optimization of Multiphase Chemical Processes for Energy-Efficient and Sustainable Manufacturing
abstract: There are many industrial chemical manufacturing processes that involve multi-phase chemistry, such as gas–liquid, liquid–liquid, gas–solid, solid–liquid and three-phase systems, and these are among the most energy-intensive and complex unit processes to optimise, due to the complex, nonlinear and often unmeasurable interfacial phenomena. The hydrodynamic, thermal and mass transfer coupling involved in these systems are difficult to model with traditional first-principles or empirical optimization approaches and make it challenging to progress towards industrially relevant scales and energy efficient, sustainable manufacturing targets. This narrative review aims to collect and condense the surge of literature on the application of machine learning (ML) algorithms for optimizing multiphase chemical processes, which spans from classic statistical process control (SPC) to advanced data-driven, hybrid and physics-informed learning algorithms. title: Digital Twins In Drug Discovery, Development, And Personalized Therapeutics
abstract: DTs are well-established in the fields of aerospace and manufacturing engineering; however, their application in drug discovery and healthcare is rather poorly explored and lacks consensus on the definition. The present review synthesizes information from various sources throughout the stages of drug discovery and highlights the difference between the dynamic evolving digital patient twin (DPT) and the traditional predictive static model. The present review utilizes the classic digital twin architecture (physical, virtual parts, and data interface), which is applied to the DPT framework. Moreover, the DPT framework is extended by the examples of molecular, cellular, and organ on chip models, virtual patient cohorts, and simulated clinical trials. The scope of generative AI technologies, including generative adversarial network (GAN), variational autoencoder, transformer, restricted Boltzmann machine, and graph neural network, is included. Generative AI distinguishes genuine DT from conventional approaches owing to the fact that it provides for continuous and personalized simulation of a patient’s health path. abstract: This thesis consists of a theoretical and a practical section. The theoretical section presents the fundamental characteristics and importance of Building Information Modeling (BIM), along with the basics of using Autodesk Revit. The practical section focuses on assessing the condition of a reinforced concrete bridge in Sremska Mitrovica. A three-dimensional model (digital twin) of the bridge was developed, where all identified defects and damages were modeled using parametric elements (families) and classified by type, location, and dimensions. This enabled automatic generation of graphical documentation (plans, sections, and details) and tabular reports containing all relevant parameters. This approach facilitates more efficient decision-making regarding the type and scope of required rehabilitation works, while also providing a model suitable for continuous monitoring of the structure’s condition.

Quantitative metabolism: data and mechanism as dual engines for a continuous, computable, and adaptive health framework
abstract: Abstract Metabolism is a dynamic, multiscale system, yet metabolic medicine still relies largely on static, threshold-based measurements that poorly capture longitudinal heterogeneity and early state transitions. We propose an operational framework for quantitative metabolism that integrates high-resolution measurements with mechanistically constrained computational models to represent metabolic states, predict trajectories, and guide intervention. The framework comprises four interconnected layers: multi-omics, defining individual molecular fingerprints; physiological and behavioral dynamics, capturing time-resolved exposures and proximal responses; phenotypic function, representing integrated organ- and system-level consequences; and adaptive metabolic regulation, extending toward digital twins and model-guided interventions such as digital therapeutics (DtX). Four sequential validation stages—quantifiable representation, predictive trajectory, operable intervention, and adaptive regulation—define the evidence required to advance from measurement to closed-loop clinical application. An IoT digital twin framework for smart waste and energy management optimazation in Maiduguri
abstract: The rapid pace of urban development in cities like Maiduguri, Nigeria, brings significant operational challenges to municipal waste collection and energy distribution. This study presents a six-layer Digital Twin (DT) architectural framework designed for resource-constrained urban environments that integrates resilient Internet of Things (IoT) sensing, machine learning (ML) forecasting, and agent-based co-simulation. During a six-month pilot deployment, data was obtained from 10 smart waste bins with ultrasonic sensors, servo actuators, and GSM modules, and 3 distribution-node energy meters. To predict bin fill levels and energy demand without future information data leakage, time-series forecasting models including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using 5-fold rolling-origin cross-validation. The LSTM model gave the best predictive accuracy (R²=0.92, RMSE = 4.8%). The forecasted horizons were fed into an AnyLogic agent-based simulation with Ant Colony Optimisation (ACO) for dynamic collection vehicle routing.
