title: From data-driven prediction to closed-loop intelligent bioconversion: A framework for artificial intelligence in organic solid waste treatment
abstract: Organic solid waste (OSW) bioconversion has become a key strategy for converting biodegradable wastes into renewable energy, stabilized products, and recoverable nutrients. However, aerobic composting and anaerobic digestion are inherently dynamic and heterogeneous biological processes, where substrate variability, microbial succession, mass transfer, process instability, and greenhouse gas emissions complicate reliable operation. Current AI applications span methane-yield and compost-maturity prediction, soft sensing, process optimization, digital twins, and simulation-based control modeling. Nevertheless, most existing applications remain confined to prediction, optimization, or advisory functions and lack direct integration with on-site physical feedback. In this critical review, we systematically evaluate the current capability distribution and deployment maturity of AI-enabled OSW bioconversion, while distinguishing demonstrated implementations from a proposed pathway toward closed-loop operational intelligence. title: A Capability-Based Framework for Classifying and Evaluating Digital Twins in the Oil and Gas Industry
abstract: Digital Twin technologies have seen growing adoption in the Oil and Gas industry, yet the term is applied to systems with markedly different levels of data integration, analytical capability, physical–digital interaction, and operational autonomy. Existing classifications distinguish broad categories such as Digital Models, Digital Shadows, and Digital Twins but provide limited guidance for the Oil and Gas context, as they do not explicitly differentiate behavioral representation, analytical sophistication, asset-to-model synchronization, digital-to-physical interaction, and decision-making autonomy. This limitation makes it difficult to compare implementations that share the same Digital Twin label but differ substantially in functional configuration and sophistication. To address this gap, this paper proposes a framework comprising seven capability-based categories: Static Digital Model, Dynamic Digital Model, Analytic Digital Model, Digital Shadow, Analytic Digital Shadow, Digital Twin, and Intelligent Digital Twin. Principal Component Analysis of Barriers to Smart Mining Technology Adoption in Hard-Rock Mining
abstract: The transition toward smart mining technologies (SMTs), spanning automation, artificial intelligence, robotics, the Internet of Things and digital twins, is reshaping safety, productivity and sustainability outcomes across the global extractive sector. Yet, their adoption within South Africa’s hard-rock mining industry remains slow, fragmented and empirically under-theorised. Drawing on diffusion of innovation and socio-technical systems perspectives as interpretive lenses, this exploratory study investigates the barriers to SMT adoption as perceived by mining professionals. A quantitative research design was adopted, using a structured questionnaire administered to 80 mining professionals across South Africa’s Northwest, Gauteng and Limpopo provinces. Data were analysed through a three-stage process comprising reliability and validity testing, descriptive statistics, and principal component analysis (PCA). PCA of the twenty-one barriers identified in the literature extracted four components that jointly explained 62.05% of the total variance. title: ADVANCES IN AI-BASED PERSONALIZED HEALTHCARE
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly changing the way healthcare is delivered by supporting a more personalized and patient-centered approach to medicine. Personalized medicine combines information such as genetics, genomics, medical history, lifestyle, laboratory results, medical images, and continuous health data to help healthcare professionals make better decisions for individual patients. Its applications include disease risk prediction, AI-assisted medical imaging, genomic data interpretation, biomarker identification, personalized drug selection, pharmacogenomics, adaptive drug dosing, treatment response prediction, and remote patient monitoring through wearable and mobile health technologies. However, successful implementation requires careful data collection, preprocessing, feature selection, model development, validation, and continuous monitoring. Despite its benefits, AI-driven personalized medicine faces important challenges, including data privacy and security, poor data quality, limited diversity in datasets, algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, high implementation costs, and regulatory and ethical concerns. title: Advancing Quantitative Imaging in Long Axial Field-of-View PET/CT: Clinically Feasible Parametric Imaging, Ground-Truth-Validated Motion Correction, and Assessment of System Robustness
abstract: Long axial field of view (LAFOV) PET/CT provides markedly increased sensitivity and an extended axial field of view. The central research question of this thesis was whether these physical advantages could be translated into the enhancement of clinical quantitative imaging. This question was addressed through three interrelated study components: [18F]FDG parametric imaging using an abbreviated dynamic scan and clinical exploration of this approach in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); quantification of respiratory motion correction using patient cohorts and a motion-free reference; and assessment of robustness against defective detector blocks (DDBs). All investigations were performed using the Biograph Vision Quadra LAFOV PET/CT. First, abbreviated dynamic [18F]FDG protocols were optimised for direct Patlak reconstruction using patient-specific image-derived input functions (IDIFs) and scaled population-based input functions (sPBIFs) in high-sensitivity (HS) and ultra-high-sensitivity (UHS) modes. title: DIGITAL MATURITY OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT: A METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH TO ASSESSMENT
abstract: The article substantiates a methodological approach to assessing the digital maturity of public administration in environmental protection and natural resource management. Digital maturity is interpreted not as the number of electronic services but as the institutional capacity to use data, interoperable registers, geospatial technologies, analytical models and digital participation channels throughout the environmental policy cycle. A seven-dimensional model is proposed, covering institutional and strategic governance; data and interoperability; digital-by-design processes; platform integration; openness and participation; predictive analytics; and cyber resilience with human oversight. Five maturity levels and an aggregation method with a bottleneck rule are introduced to prevent strong components from concealing critical weaknesses. An information and analytical mechanism is developed that links environmental data sources, interoperability, analytics, managerial decisions, public interaction and ex post evaluation. TITLE SAFETY BARRIERS & REVERSIBLE PROCESS CONTROL FOR NEURAL NANOFABS SUBTITLE A Nonclinical Research Atlas on Process Safety Envelopes, Recipe Provenance, Uncertainty-Aware Metrology, Hybrid Control Barriers, and Reproducible Neural-Interface Wafer Qualification AUTHOR Feng Cheng-en 33 | STARLI Research Works, Institute XXIII ABSTRACT This research atlas asks whether a neural-interface nanofabrication system can preserve a declared safety envelope when manufacturing recipes change, instrument calibration drifts, process chambers retain chemical memory, equipment connectivity fails, and production incentives conflict with physical constraints. Its central scientific distinction is between a control system that generates an action and a production authority that is justified in executing it. The work organizes an interdisciplinary research program into 82 chapters with five single-page sections per chapter, thirty mathematically distinct research lenses, and 200 detailed Research Gates. Across hybrid dynamics, control barrier functions, metrology lineage, virtual metrology, wafer and equipment state tracking, contamination containment, process-history effects, defect-to-function causal analysis, adversarial security, and retirement, each Gate specifies a contestable hypothesis, a preregistered experiment, an established comparison method, a measurable outcome, an explicit failure condition and evidence that a second team could independently reconstruct. The framework is deliberately restricted to digital fab twins, simulated fault injection, dummy wafers, nonhazardous hardware-in-the-loop test rigs, and independently authorized research settings. It does not provide clinically deployable protocols, prove autonomous nanofabrication readiness, or equate neural-device wafer yield with clinical safety or efficacy. DOI-linked literature is used to ground established methods while leaving proposed technology and experimental outcomes clearly unverified. Its research ethic is simple: when evidence weakens, claims contract; when material history is irreversible, software rollback cannot erase physical damage; and when a hard safety predicate fails, throughput optimization must yield to quarantine, human adjudication, or a designed stop. The atlas is intended as a reusable source of falsifiable research questions, not as a certificate of production safety. EDITION NOTE Research Atlas v1.0. Includes 82 chapters, 410 single-page research sections, 30 mathematical lenses, 200 Research Gates, and 16 indexed DOI references. Formal, clinical, and industrial efficacy claims require future independent validation.

title: A Review on Digital Twin with AI Based Predictive Maintenance System
abstract: Predictive maintenance reduces unexpected machine failures and downtime by continuously observing equipment condition and identifying abnormal behaviour before severe failure occurs. This review paper examines recent research on Digital Twin (DT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, multi-sensor condition monitoring, and predictive maintenance of industrial machines, with emphasis on induction motors. Based on the reviewed literature, a low-cost integrated architecture is proposed using temperature, vibration, current, and RPM sensing, an ESP32 controller, AI-based fault prediction, Digital Twin updating, and IoT-based monitoring. Random Forest is considered as the main classification model because related literature demonstrates strong performance for motor-fault classification. Sample formulas for RMS vibration, mean, variance, RPM, and percentage change are presented. The proposed workflow connects physical sensing, data processing, AI prediction, virtual representation, alert generation, and predictive-maintenance decision support. Illustrative graphs are included only as sample results and must be replaced by measured experimental data before final validation.

title: Time as an indispensable causal dimension in cardiovascular diseases: toward a four-dimensional biology
abstract: Heart failure (HF) exhibits distinctive event-and time-dependent patterns in incidence and progression dynamics. Over time, the heart first undergoes (mal)adaptive cellular, tissue and molecular remodelling 1,2 . These alterations precede clinical symptoms and diagnosis 3,4 and reflect age-related changes in cardiovascular structure and function that lower the threshold for overt disease 4,5 . This subclinical process is followed by incremental cardiac remodelling, including cardiac hypertrophy 6,7 , myocardial stiffening 8 , and impaired diastolic filling 4 . Similar preclinical alterations occur across other cardiovascular and cardiometabolic disorders: atrial fibrosis and mitochondrial remodelling may develop before atrial fibrillation 9,10 , endothelial dysfunction precedes hypertension and atherosclerosis 11 and even rare diseases such as J-wave syndromes are now considered cardiomyopathies with subtle structural abnormalities that remain undetected by standard imaging techniques 12 . title: Ai-Enabled Digital Twins for Proactive Fault Prediction and Self-Healing in Distributed Cloud–Edge Systems: A Conceptual Framework
abstract: Distributed cloud–edge systems support modern applications by combining centralised cloud infrastructure with computing resources located near data sources. Despite their advantages, these environments remain vulnerable to hardware faults, software failures, network disruptions, resource contention, and changing workloads. Conventional fault-tolerance mechanisms often respond after a failure has occurred, potentially increasing service interruption and recovery costs. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Twin (DT) technology offer opportunities to anticipate system degradation, evaluate alternative responses, and support automated recovery. This paper proposes a conceptual framework integrating digital twins, AI-based fault prediction, adaptive resource management, and self-healing mechanisms for distributed cloud–edge environments. The framework comprises six components: real-time monitoring, digital representation, predictive analytics, risk-aware decision-making, self-healing execution, and continuous feedback. It also identifies challenges relating to data quality, prediction uncertainty, model drift, computational overhead, security, and coordination across distributed nod

title: STA-EFM: Semantic–Temporal–Authority Evidence Fusion for Multi-Source Emerging Technology Information Processing and Forecasting
abstract: Future Internet ecosystems increasingly rely on distributed and intelligent data infrastructures, yet evidence of their evolution is fragmented across scholarly publications, patents, open-source repositories, and technology news. This study proposes the Semantic–Temporal–Authority Evidence Fusion Model (STA-EFM), a multi-source information-processing framework for identifying, ranking, and forecasting emerging data-infrastructure trajectories relevant to Future Internet ecosystems. STA-EFM integrates arXiv, PatentsView/USPTO, and GitHub records, with GDELT providing a limited complementary technology-news signal, harmonizes heterogeneous metadata, and assigns records to ten predefined technology classes using Sentence-BERT prototype similarity. A manually reviewed sample of 500 records was used to validate semantic relevance and taxonomy assignment. Source-normalized semantic evidence was combined with temporal activity, growth, momentum, recency, and source-specific authority indicators to generate monthly STA scores. While this approach preserves strict physical invariants and learns complex unmodeled dynamics, deploying these hybrid digital twins introduces profound mathematical and statistical challenges. The seminar bridges rigorous applied mathematics and real-world industrial systems, establishing concrete research avenues between Calejo Hybrid Intelligence AB and the Department of Mathematics in dynamical systems, operator learning, control theory, and functional data analysis. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging in recombinant biomanufacturing, where data-driven approaches are used to optimize complex biological systems. This paper reviews the integration of artificial intelligence, bioinformatics and industrial biotechnology in the recombinant production process from genetic design to large-scale processing. These approaches enhance protein engineering through structure prediction, codon optimization and functional analysis. In upstream processing, machine learning is used to support strain development, media optimization and adaptive control strategies to improve yield and product quality. For downstream operations, efficient purification is achieved through AI-based modelling of chromatographic processes and monitoring critical quality attributes in real time. This is further supported by integration with Quality by Design (QbD), Process Analytical Technology (PAT) and digital twins, enabling continuous manufacturing and real-time release testing (RTRT). CHM-DTKT: a causal hypergraph selective state space digital twin for deconfounded and temporally grounded knowledge tracing
abstract: Adaptive tutoring is a complex intelligent system in which learner competence, exposure policy and memory decay co-evolve, yet prevailing knowledge tracing models correct bias only after the representation has formed, inherit structure from an incomplete expert matrix, and advance a transition blind to elapsed time. This paper proposes CHM-DTKT, a causal hypergraph selective state space learner twin that treats these as one representation problem. A differentiable hypergraph is built with sampled incidence and an acyclically constrained prerequisite orientation, and its aggregation is backdoor-adjusted over a strictly pre-treatment confounder dictionary, so that deconfounding acts during representation formation rather than at the output layer. A cognitive discretization step generated from elapsed time, item difficulty and cumulative practice induces a per-channel identifiable power-law retention, making forgetting a property of the recursion itself. A predictor–corrector twin decays and repairs a concept-addressable mastery state between observations and supports counterfactual instructional rollout. title: Sparse measurement correction for full-field displacement prediction of nonlinear structures using reduced-order models and Gaussian process regression
abstract: Online full-field displacement reconstruction from sparse measurements is an important task in nonlinear structural analysis, monitoring, and digital-twin applications. Direct finite element simulations are often too expensive for repeated online use, whereas input-only reduced-order model–Gaussian process regression (ROM-GPR) surrogate models may produce biased full-field predictions when the target structural state is insufficiently represented by offline training data. Sparse displacement measurements provide current-state information, but observation-only reconstruction is usually underdetermined or noise-sensitive under limited sensing conditions. To address this issue, this work develops a probabilistic correction strategy for ROM-GPR full-field displacement predictions by statistically weighting the input-informed surrogate estimate and sparse measurements according to their respective uncertainties. title: A Literature-calibrated Digital Twin-inspired Framework for Secure and Predictable IoT Smart Homes

title: Towards machine learning-based digital twinning for autonomous mobile robot control
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) refers to the technology that enables a synchronized digital replica to mirror the operation of its corresponding physical system. A representative DT, i.e., a comprehensive, high-fdelity, multi-physics, multi-scale, and continuously updated digital representation of a complex physical system, offers signifcant advantages. These include the ability to optimize system operation at runtime and to test new developments extensively in a controlled digital environment. In this thesis, we leverage the concept of digital twins to support the control and resource management of autonomous robotic systems. We demonstrate that a model capable of capturing both the internal characteristics of a robot and the external environmental effects can be effectively utilized for proactive robot control under both long-term and short-term operational constraints. To achieve this, we frst develop a general open-source DT framework (MCX) in which models with different levels of abstraction can be embedded for various robotic subsystems. This paper answers the question a technical evaluator actually asks: does the composed stack hold under cross-domain stress, and can one cheap probe de-risk the whole platform at once? title: A Connectivity-Resilient Blockchain Architecture for Digital Twin in Bangladesh RMG
abstract: Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) sector generates more than 80% of national export earnings, yet real-time production monitoring has gained almost no foothold on its factory floors. This paper combines two bodies of evidence. Documentary analysis of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association's digital programme, covering DigiProd Pass, the Digital Factory Passport and AWARE, shows that these are compliance instruments built around European Digital Product Passport requirements rather than around the cost, connectivity and skill constraints that keep factories from adopting production-monitoring technology. A targeted survey of 61 practitioners then tested whether those constraints are recognised at the production level. Respondents rated skilled-personnel shortage, initial cost and interruption of network and electricity supply as substantial obstacles, and a Friedman test found no reliable severity ordering among the five barrier items, so they are treated as a joint constraint set rather than ranked. The strongest inferential result is that the skills barrier was rated well above respondents' assessment of their own factories' capacity to absorb minimal-t

title: Federated digital twin framework for spectrum handover management in vehicular THz ORAN
abstract: Vehicular Terahertz (THz) Open Radio Access Networks (ORAN) face severe challenges due to ultra-high mobility, rapid channel dynamics, spectrum scarcity, and frequent handovers, which limit the effectiveness of existing reactive and centralized management strategies. This paper proposes a Federated Blockchain-Assisted Digital Twin framework for proactive spectrum sharing and seamless handover in vehicular THz ORAN systems. The framework employs a Contrastive Denoising Spatio-Temporal Autoencoder (CD-STAE) to refine multi-source telemetry while preserving transient anomalies, followed by a Federated Multi-View Neural State-Space Twin (FMNSS) that constructs a privacy-preserving digital replica of the network. A Spatio-Temporal Transformer with Heteroscedastic Uncertainty (ST-TrH) enables confidence-aware forecasting of load, interference, and mobility-driven congestion, while On-Chain Verifiable Reward Shaping (OVRS) integrates blockchain-derived trust scores into federated aggregation and proactive spectrum leasing. title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Stem Cell Bioprocessing: From Monitoring to Autonomous Manufacturing
abstract: Background: Stem cell bioprocessing requires timely assessment of cell state and control over variable expansion and differentiation. Automated culture can execute predefined steps, whereas adaptive manufacturing uses observations to guide decisions during an ongoing batch.Objective: This review examines how artificial intelligence and machine learning connect process monitoring to prediction and feedback control, and assesses which links have been demonstrated in stem cell systems.Key Content: This topic covers image-based phenotyping, physical and multimodal sensing, growth and differentiation forecasts, process optimization, hybrid models, and proposed digital twins. A descriptive Level 0–6 continuum distinguishes endpoint assessment, monitoring, state estimation, prediction, operator decision support, within-run feedback, and coordinated workflow autonomy. Reported studies demonstrate image-guided adjustments to differentiation, robotic optimization across experiments, and rule-based feedback within a culture. However, these capabilities do not demonstrate autonomous production of a clinically releasable cell product. Translation is further limited by reduced model performance

title: A Blockchain-Digital Twin Protocol for Secure Data Management and Smart Contract Verification in Low-Altitude Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Networks
abstract: Secure low-altitude services require timely communication, trustworthy state estimation, controlled data access, and verifiable mission logic. This protocol combines unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), digital twins, edge services, encrypted off-chain storage, a permissioned blockchain, and multi-stage smart contract checks. Authenticated messages update a twin, essential metadata are committed on-chain, and mission requests are checked against state and access rules. Co-simulation compares the complete protocol with centralized, blockchain-only, and blockchain-digital twin baselines. Each experimental condition includes 30 run-level observations per scheme and metric. In the fleet-size experiment at 50 UAVs, mean arrival delay is 260 ms (95% confidence interval [CI], 256.64–263.36) and trusted arrival is 89.5% (95% CI, 89.09–89.91), compared with 388 ms and 77.0% for centralized management. In the speed experiment at 70 km/h, the corresponding means are 280 ms and 90.0%. Among adjudicated malicious requests, blocking sensitivity is 97.89%; the false-positive rate among adjudicated benign requests is 0.58%. title: Digital twin-assisted edge-local query resolution for privacy–utility trade-off in location-based services
abstract: Location-Based Services (LBS) generate large volumes of sensitive, location-dependent queries that must be processed under strict and often conflicting constraints of privacy and utility. Existing differential privacy (DP) mechanisms face a fundamental limitation: strong guarantees inject excessive noise and degrade utility, while utility-oriented methods under-protect users. We propose DT-ELR (Digital Twin-assisted Edge-Local Resolution), a framework that jointly optimises disclosure and retrieval utility through two tightly integrated algorithms and an on-device digital twin. Algorithm 1 (SensitivityClassifier) calibrates a monotone geo-indistinguishability budget from a data-derived sensitivity score, validated against a semantic venue-category labelling (AUC 0.81). The digital twin predicts from on-device signals alone whether releasing a query would improve its answer (AUC 0.90); self-sufficient queries are resolved against an on-device venue cache with no release and no budget spent. Algorithm 2 (ClosedFormAllocator) then distributes the remaining budget across released queries in closed form, matching the exact dynamic-programming optimum to within 1%. Experiments on three p

title: AI-Based Adaptive Genome Digital Twin for Personalized Health Prediction
abstract: Doctors usually get involved after a patient already feels ill. That is a poor fit for chronic disease, since the damage builds up quietly for years before anyone notices. We built a genome digital twin to deal with this. It is a virtual copy of one person, started from their inherited disease risk and updated with their vital signs, sleep, diet and activity. The inherited part is a polygenic risk score and it never changes. Everything else arrives as new readings and is merged into the twin each time. Random Forest, XGBoost and a Decision Tree baseline take the combined record and give the probability of chronic disease. Results go to a Streamlit dashboard that shows a risk percentage, a biological age, a health score and a wellness index. It also splits the risk into genetic, lifestyle, environmental and clinical shares, and a user can change a habit to watch the forecast move. The paper describes the requirements, a four-layer architecture, how the twin is kept current, the training and evaluation plan, the tests and a twelve-week schedule. title: AI-driven multi-agent digital twin conceptual framework for real-time domestic water quality monitoring, purification and smart billing
abstract: Access to safe drinking water remains a critical global challenge, with over 2.2 billion people lacking reliable access despite water’s abundance, as only 3% of Earth’s water is freshwater. Current systems suffer from unreliable analog metering, tampering risks, and the absence of real-time platforms for monitoring quality, consumption, purification and billing—creating a literature gap in scalable, integrated, and intelligent water management solutions. To address this situation, a pilot-scale, machine learning–enabled multi-agent digital twin-inspired framework is developed for domestic water systems, integrating IoT sensors to continuously monitor key parameters (pH, turbidity, temperature, flow, and TDS); purification status; and employing predictive models for anomaly detection and forecasting. Among several tested algorithms (ARIMA, autoregression, and additive regression), additive regression demonstrated comparatively better performance under the constraints of the pilot dataset, relatively low error rates were achieved under evaluation conditions for temperature, pH, flow, pressure, TDS and color. abstract: Direct formic acid fuel cells (DFAFCs) offer a liquid-fuel alternative to hydrogen-fed proton-exchange membrane fuel cells, but inconsistent designs and operating conditions hinder performance comparison. This review benchmarks experimentally tested single-cell DFAFCs across Pt-, Pd-, Pt–Pd-, and non-noble-metal catalyst systems by peak power density, catalyst loading, durability, and operating conditions. Reported peak power densities range from 20 to 550 mW cm⁻². Pd–Ni₂P/C achieved 550 mW cm⁻², while PtBiPbNiCo reached 321.2 mW cm⁻². FeTSPc-promoted Pt increased peak power density from 76.3 to 126.6 mW cm⁻² and suppressed CO-forming pathways; a Co–NCNT cathode achieved 160.7 mW cm⁻², exceeding the corresponding Pt/C reference. However, inconsistent durability tests and cell configurations prevent reliable cross-study ranking and commercial-readiness assessment. A baseline protocol is proposed, specifying operation at 60 °C with 3 M formic acid, controlled oxidant supply, defined membrane-electrode assembly geometry, liquid-compatible anode diffusion layers, and at least 100 h of durability testing. The protocol is designed to generate interoperable, machine-readable datasets, whi

title: Runtime Governance of Competing Actuation Requests in Multi-Service Digital Twins for Manufacturing Cells
abstract: Manufacturing-cell digital twins increasingly combine independently developed services that can influence shared physical resources. When several state-changing services are individually admissible but request incompatible values for the same control endpoint, runtime governance is required before execution. This work proposes a governance model that represents service–resource bindings, service and resource constraints, runtime context, arbitration-policy bindings, and enforcement relations for composed manufacturing-cell DTs. State-changing requests are evaluated individually before compatible requests are coalesced and incompatible admissible requests are resolved through a resource-specific governance policy. The model is implemented using ODRL for portable policy representation and OPA/Rego for executable runtime decisions. The evaluation examines functional validity, deterministic decision behavior, and request-to-enforcement latency using recorded CNC machining data and controlled replay scenarios in which two DT services share the feedOverride resource. title: Instability-Aware Digital Twins for Robust Co-Optimization of Operational Carbon Emissions, Thermal Comfort, and Structural Serviceability Reliability under Uncertainty in Smart Buildings
abstract: Modern smart buildings operate under continuously varying climatic, occupancy, equipment, grid-carbon, material, degradation, and sensing conditions, making nominal optimization insufficient for reliable operational decision-making. This study develops and numerically evaluates an instability-aware digital twin for robust co-optimization of operational carbon emissions, occupied-zone thermal discomfort, and component-level structural serviceability reliability under uncertainty. The framework combines a multi-rate thermal–energy–moisture–IAQ–structural model, carbon-aware CO₂-based ventilation control, extended Kalman filtering, Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, FORM and design-point importance sampling, Gaussian-process surrogate modeling, NSGA-II, and dimensionless objective- and decision-instability metrics. A controlled six-zone benchmark represents a six-story office building with a gross floor area of 10,200 m² over a one-year operational horizon and a 20-year reliability horizon. title: Autonomous Healthcare Control System (AHCS)
abstract: Today's healthcare systems represent complex adaptive systems that involve stochastic demand, tight coupling between subsystems, and nonlinearity of resource constraints. This paper proposes the Autonomous Healthcare Control System (AHCS), which brings together such approaches as stochastic state space models, Markov Decision Process, queuing theory, epidemic forecasting, and optimization through reinforcement learning. AHCS treats hospital operations as a high dimensional stochastic system and leverages the digital twin framework to simulate numerous scenarios of hospital operations. AHCS allows optimizing clinical performance, ensuring sustainable labor force, increasing supply chain resilience, and improving efficiency. In addition, the proposed approach incorporates elements of explainable AI, fairness aware learning, and human in the loop approach. Simulation results for the case of pandemic-related surge show that the proposed system is capable of decreasing the probability of ICU overload by approximately 40% and reducing the recovery period by 50%.

title: Oculomics using artificial intelligence derived retinal biomarkers for cardiovascular health
abstract: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from retinal vascular morphology, structural and perfusion imaging, retinal aging, metabolomics, and artificial intelligence models linking retinal biomarkers with cardiovascular risk factors, subclinical disease, clinical events, and cardiorenal and metabolic outcomes. These biomarkers may complement conventional risk assessment, but clinical utility is unproven and integration into cardiovascular digital twins remains conceptual. Prospective validation, standardized acquisition, interoperability, interpretability, and equitable evaluation are required before implementation.

title: AI-Based Digital Twin for Distribution Transformer Health Prediction and Remaining Useful Life Estimation Using an ESP32-Based Multi-Sensor Monitoring System
abstract: Distribution transformers are essential components of power distribution systems, but continuous condition monitoring is often limited. This paper presents an AI-based digital twin for transformer health prediction and remaining useful life (RUL) estimation using an ESP32-based multisensor monitoring system. The prototype monitors AC voltage, load current, oil level, oil moisture, temperature, and vibration. Sensor readings are displayed on an LCD and transmitted via Wi-Fi to a Python-based digital twin. The digital twin combines a thermal ageing model with data-driven analysis to estimate the transformer health index, condition class, and RUL. The proposed low-cost system supports real-time monitoring, early fault detection, and predictive maintenance.

title: Digital Transformation of Nigerian Construction Industry Through BIM, AI, Digital Twins, IoT and Data Analytics
abstract: This study assessed the digital transformation of construction processes with a view to developing an integrated framework for enhancing project performance in Abia State, Nigeria. The study was motivated by persistent time and cost overruns, poor quality, and fragmented paper-based processes in Nigeria’s SME-dominated construction industry, coupled with acute last-mile logistics challenges in Umuahia and Aba due to poor road networks and informal material delivery systems. Despite global advancement in Construction 4.0 driven by Building Information Modelling (BIM), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Twins, Internet of Things (IoT) and Data Analytics, existing studies in Nigeria are fragmented, focusing mainly on BIM in Lagos/Abuja without integrating the five technologies, without linking to last-mile logistics, and without a mediated-moderated framework for South-East Nigeria.

title: Sustainability and Women's Empowerment Through Technology
abstract: Technological change is a major development agent across all the layers of contemporary societies, from how economies work to how people access information, how social life is conducted, and even how political institutions work and how decisions are made. In the twenty-first century, digital technologies, ranging from artificial intelligence to mobile connectivity to financial technology and blockchain applications, have revolutionized markets, knowledge, social life, and even the nature of political participation. Sustainability and gender equality, meanwhile, have become twin planks of development frameworks worldwide. The agency of women and girls has been recognized as a transformative force in the development process, and empowerment is understood as central to progress. In turn, gender equality is linked to enhanced economic productivity, poverty reduction, and sustainability. Digital technologies have opened up new paths for women in education, entrepreneurship, employment, and participation. They have helped to reduce some of the traditional structural constraints by expanding women’s access to credit, networks, and information, thereby unleashing the power of women’s agenc

title: A FOURIER NEURAL OPERATOR SURROGATE FOR PEMFC STACK ASSESSMENT IN ESHIPS
abstract: A FOURIER NEURAL OPERATOR SURROGATE FOR PEMFC STACK ASSESSMENT IN ESHIPS Theo Tsenis, Hellenic Institute of Transport (HIT)/CERTH, ttsenis@certh.gr, Alkiviadis Tromaras, Hellenic Institute of Transport (HIT)/CERTH, atromaras@certh.gr, Vassilios Kappatos Director of Hellenic Institute of Transport (HIT)/CERTH, vkappatos@certh.gr, 20th ANNUAL CONFERENCE OF MARINE TECHNOLOGY ELINT 6-7 October 2026 ABSTRACT Hydrogen proton-exchange-membrane fuel-cell (PEMFC) stacks offer modular, zero-local-emission power for electric and hybrid-electric ships. However, their safe and efficient operation depends on coupled electrochemical, transport, thermal, water-management and degradation phenomena. This paper presents a physics-informed surrogate based on a PEM-specific Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) for rapid assessment of commercial-scale PEMFC stacks in eShips. A two-dimensional finite-element-style simulator was used to generate synthetic fields for hydrogen and oxygen concentration, membrane hydration, potentials, current density, temperature and liquid saturation under variations in geometry, load, cooling, humidity, flooding and degradation. The fields are reduced to cell and stack indicators

title: VERIFIED TWIN® APPROACH
abstract: Decisions about built assets increasingly rely on digital descriptions – models, drawings and data developed collaboratively by multiple organisations over many years. Errors, contradictions and omissions in these descriptions are often discovered only when they become costly to resolve on site.The VERIFIED TWIN® APPROACH is a digital-native procedure designed to make the reliability of these descriptions verifiable, with the aim of improving cost and schedule certainty in construction projects. It combines a verification method with an Operating Model, a digital backbone, registers serving as the system of record, and governance, contractual and technological provisions.The specification distinguishes between reality, description, assertion and representation. Project-specific definitions are maintained as data in nine registers, while standardised, reusable Requirements and Tests are configured for each project. Tests are performed not on the data as originally provided by each source (L0), but on the assertions resolved for a specific use case (L1), thereby decoupling verification rules from their sources.Within the delivery cycle, organisations submit their deliverables, and ea

title: Digital twin forestry as an informatics framework integrating remote sensing ecosystem modelling and data assimilation
abstract: Forests are essential to the Earth system, regulating carbon, water, and biodiversity cycles while underpinning ecosystem resilience. Yet they face mounting pressures from climate and land-use change, requiring integrative informatics approaches that link high-resolution observations with advanced ecosystem models. This systematic review defines Digital Twin Forestry (DTF) as an emerging paradigm that continuously couples multisensor Earth Observation data with ecosystem models through data assimilation, enabling dynamic, uncertainty-aware forecasting and adaptive decision support. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesized 57 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2025 that combined EO datasets with ecosystem modeling and assimilation frameworks. Demonstrated advances include CubeSat constellations, spaceborne LiDAR, UAV hyperspectral systems, and hybrid machine-learning surrogates. Data assimilation methods such as Ensemble Kalman Filters and Particle Filters serve as computational bridges between multi-temporal observations and dynamic model states. Results reveal uneven biome representation, with tropical and boreal forests underrepresented compared to temperate

title: Development and evaluation of an intelligent pharmaceutical manufacturing curriculum module under industry–education integration: a quasi-experimental study
abstract: The digital transformation of pharmaceutical manufacturing has generated an urgent need for graduates who possess competencies in intelligent manufacturing, data-driven process control, digital quality systems, regulatory compliance, and innovation-oriented problem solving. However, conventional pharmaceutical education often remains theory-centered and insufficiently connected with real industrial scenarios. This study developed and evaluated an Intelligent Pharmaceutical Manufacturing curriculum module under the framework of industry–education integration. The module incorporated Quality by Design (QbD), Process Analytical Technology (PAT), Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), electronic batch records (EBR), digital twins, virtual simulation, AI-assisted process optimization, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliance, validation, and data integrity. A four-integration teaching model was proposed to connect curriculum content with industrial standards, classroom learning with production scenarios, physical practice with virtual simulation, and knowledge acquisition with innovation projects. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design was used to evaluate the mo

title: Artificial Intelligence for Net-Zero and Climate-Resilient Sustainable Cities: Technologies, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Urbanization, climate change, increasing energy demand, and rapid infrastructure development have created significant challenges for achieving sustainable and resilient cities. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology that enables data-driven decision-making, intelligent automation, and efficient resource management, making it an important enabler of net-zero and climate-resilient urban systems. This narrative review examines AI applications relevant to urban climate mitigation and adaptation, drawing on literature identified through Google Scholar and ScienceDirect. The review examines the role of machine learning, deep learning, Internet of Things (IoT), big data analytics, cloud computing, digital twins, and generative AI in improving urban energy systems, sustainable transportation, environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, and smart governance. The study also discusses how these technologies contribute to carbon emission reduction, renewable energy integration, climate adaptation, disaster preparedness, and efficient urban planning. In addition, major challenges associated with AI implementation are critically analyzed, including data

title: Improving five-axis milling force prediction through physics-guided transfer learning and orientation-aware process planning
abstract: Five-axis milling is widely used for manufacturing complex-geometry components in aerospace, energy, die and mold, and biomedical applications, where accurate cutting-force prediction is essential for process planning, optimization, and digital-twin development. However, mechanistic models require material- and condition-specific calibration, while purely data-driven approaches often demand extensive experimental data and may generalize poorly beyond the training domain. This study proposes the Physics-Guided Milling Network (PGMNet), a simulation-to-experiment transfer-learning framework that combines mechanistic modeling with deep learning. The network is pretrained on a large mechanistic simulation dataset and fine-tuned using limited experimental force measurements. Process parameters, tool geometry, tool orientation, and thermo-mechanical material properties are used as inputs to enable transferable force prediction across materials and cutting conditions. For AISI 1050, Al 7075-T6, and Ti-6Al-4V, PGMNet achieved R 2 values above 98% with RMSE below 20 N, outperforming the mechanistic model and conventional regression baselines. For unseen Inconel 625, mean R 2 remained above

title: Simultaneous and Dynamic Prediction of Coupled Parameters in Colloidal Micronano Motion Systems by Physics-Informed Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract For probing micronano particle motion interface dynamics, intrinsic physical coupling among particle hydrodynamic radius (rh), interfacial viscosity (η), and temperature (T) hinders their simultaneous and dynamic acquisition and limits the labeled data available for conventional machine learning (ML). Here, we propose a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) paradigm that uses digital-twin simulations to endow ML models with physical priors. The digital twin reveals a millionfold disparity in parameter influence on motion signals and severe parameter unidentifiability in standard ML models. To overcome this, a hybrid ML architecture, RF-MBGA-Net, integrates a random forest (RF) with a multibranch gated attention (MBGA) network to balance parameter influence scales via intermediate prediction feedback and data augmentation. RF-MBGA-Net achieves high-accuracy predictions on simulated data (R2 > 99%; MAEs: rh= 3.9 nm, η = 0.023 mPa·s, T = 1.5 K). The trained RF-MBGA-Net performs simultaneous and dynamic prediction of the three parameters from experimental motion signals. title: EL-RAKHAWI UNIFIED FRAMEWORK FOR MULTIMODAL COGNITIVE REASONING: INTEGRATING MULTIMODAL RAG WITH DYNAMIC KNOWLEDGE GRAPHS AND 4D NEURAL MODELING
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Unified Framework for Multimodal Cognitive Reasoning introduces a paradigm shift from hallucination-prone generative AI to verifiable, cognitively reasoning systems. It addresses critical gaps in current AI: the modality gap in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and the semantic void in 4D neural rendering like NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting. The framework integrates four novel modules: a Multimodal Semantic Indexing Engine, a Dynamic Multimodal Knowledge Graph with Temporal Credibility Weighting for real-time conflict resolution, a 4D Neural-Symbolic Reasoning Core utilizing Hierarchical Asynchronous Retrieval for low-latency performance, and a Verifiable Multimodal Generation module. By projecting retrieved graph knowledge onto 4D neural representations, the system ensures outputs are physically and geometrically faithful, measured by a novel Spatial-Geometric Faithfulness Score. This architecture enables trustworthy Cognitive Digital Twins, providing auditable, hallucination-free AI solutions for high-stakes domains like legal tech, medical diagnostics, and industrial monitoring, establishing a new global baseline for reliable multimodal AI.

title: XAI-SFD: an explainable artificial intelligence framework for intelligent digitalisation of shit flow diagrams and smart sanitation management in South Africa
abstract: Despite the availability of safe sanitation access, this issue remains a major challenge in many developing nations like South Africa where there are challenges associated with the fragmented data gathering, manual reporting, and lack of interoperability and real-time monitoring of the sanitation service chain. Shit Flow Diagrams (SFDs) are among the tools that can be used for the presentation and analysis of the sanitation service chain as well as identification of potential risks in the sanitation systems; however, the creation of traditional SFDs is a manual process and leaves no space for continuous monitoring. This paper proposes XAI-SFD, an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-based solution for the intelligent digitalization of Shit Flow Diagrams (SFDs) and smart sanitation management in South Africa. This approach is based on IoT data gathering, GIS-based spatial analysis, data validation, machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, sanitation service chain modelling, Digital Twin technology and dashboard decision-making support. Explainability provides transparency and allows the stakeholders to understand what influences the risk assessment and prioritizat

title: Simulation-Based Verification of a Multimodal Sensing and Data-Integrity Pipeline for Laboratory Building-Condition Assessment: Digital-Twin Dry Run of an Arduino/ESP32 Test Programme (Code, Simulated Dataset and Report)
abstract: Description / Abstract This record contains the software package, simulated dataset and report for a dry run of a laboratory test programme. The programme asks whether combining acoustic sensing (six SPH0645 I2S microphones, 48 kHz) with inertial sensing (eight BMI270 IMUs, 800 Hz) on Arduino Nano ESP32 nodes improves recognition of four controlled configurations (C0–C3) of a 1:20 building model. It also tests a cryptographically protected data stream: CRC-32, a SHA-256 hash chain, ECDSA P-256 signatures and Merkle-root anchoring to a ledger. Important: no physical experiment was performed. All structural-response, recognition, synchronisation, calibration and false-alarm results come from a physically motivated modal digital twin of the test rig. They are intended for pipeline verification and planning, not as experimental evidence. The full design of 4 configurations × 3 force levels × 2 impact points × 20 repeats (480 records in four sessions, 502 attempts including rejected impacts) was simulated. These records were then processed by the same pipeline intended for real data: an event detector, 179 acoustic and inertial features, leave-one-session-out Random Forest classificatio

title: How Emerging Technologies Transform Disaster Debris Management: Generative AI, Digital Twins, and Cyber-Physical-Social Systems for Circular Recovery
abstract: This paper explores how emerging technologies can transform disaster debris management from linear clear-and-dispose practices toward circular, environmentally sustainable recovery. Climate-related disasters generate massive volumes of construction and demolition (C&D) debris, yet practice remains dominated by rapid landfilling with limited use of artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins (DTs), or cyber-physical-social systems (CPSS), leaving major circularity and climate-mitigation opportunities unrealized. This paper proposes a framework that couples large language model-based generative AI agents with archetype-driven life cycle assessment (LCA) inside a DT- and CPSS-oriented environment. Using the 2023 tornado in Sullivan, Indiana, as a benchmark, the framework classifies damaged buildings into archetypes, links material inventories to a proxy LCA library, and simulates linear, moderately circular, and enhanced circular debris pathways. Results indicate that circular strategies can divert about 46% of C&D debris from landfills and reduce embodied greenhouse gas emissions by roughly 28% compared to conventional landfilling. title: UrbanQGS: Large-scale urban surface reconstruction via analytic curvature consistency in quadratic Gaussian splatting
abstract: Large-scale 3D surface reconstruction at the city scale from UAV imagery is a core task for building digital-twin cities. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and its variants have achieved remarkable progress in radiance-field reconstruction, existing methods still struggle with scale-varying structural complexity and diverse urban textures: geometry is often incomplete in low-frequency, weak-texture regions over large areas, while in high-frequency regions with intricate details, disordered primitive distributions tend to cause floating artifacts and outliers. To address these issues, we propose UrbanQGS, a large-scale urban reconstruction framework built on quadratic Gaussian splatting. We inherit quadratic surface Gaussians as scene primitives and use their analytic curvature as the central driving signal to perform a two-stage geometric refinement: (1) A self-supervised geometric constraint based on cross-view curvature consistency, which effectively fills geometric holes in weak-texture planar regions. title: TURQUALITY-SUPPORTED COMPANIES IN THE PLASTICS-RELATED SECTOR: A CONTENT ANALYSIS OF SUSTAINABILITY AND DIGITALIZATION VISIBILITY IN CORPORATE REPORTS
abstract: In this study, it was aimed to examine the transformation awareness and sustainability visibility of Turquality-supported plastics companies in Türkiye. In the study, the most up-to-date sustainability reports of six Turquality-supported plastics companies were evaluated with content analysis using qualitative research methods. In the analysis, the prominent words in the report were determined by word frequency and word cloud analysis. As a result of the analysis, it was determined that environmental sustainability received the highest emphasis among the reports, followed by social and economic dimensions. Furthermore, digitalization-themed words have also been found to have relatively limited visibility. Looking at the company-level results, it can be said that Brisa and Teklas are the companies with the highest corporate visibility, standing out in the overall sustainability outlook and digital transformation indicators, respectively. The findings provide strategic insights for policymakers and firms, emphasizing the necessity of strengthening digital transformation capacity alongside environmental initiatives to fully realize Turquality’s strategic objectives. title: Adaptive Edge-Native Digital Twin Synchronization for Resource-Constrained Smart Water Infrastructure: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: This study proposes a novel decentralized Edge AI-enabled digital twin architecture for smart city water resource management. The proposed framework seeks to integrate lightweight machine learning models, adaptive synchronization mechanisms, online hydraulic simulation, and semantic interoperability into a combined cyber-physical architecture capable of supporting real-time monitoring and predictive decision-making under constrained network conditions. The research aims to contribute a scalable, energy-efficient, and low-latency digital twin framework that improves operational resilience and intelligent water governance in smart city environments.

title: Eléonore Schnebelin (2026), Ecologization and Digitalization of Agriculture: Convergence or Opposition? , Smart Innovation, London, ISTE/Wiley, 282 p. ISBN: 9781836690450

title: Comment on wes-2026-131
abstract: Abstract. Accurate modelling of nonlinear wind turbine blade dynamics is essential for the reliable design and operation of modern wind turbines. Wind turbine blades have complex shapes with spatially varying sectional properties, twists and curvatures. The dynamics of long, flexible blades are strongly influenced by geometric nonlinearities, centrifugal effects, and material anisotropies. Conventional linear beam models are inadequate for capturing these complexities, since they are not designed to handle large deformations and nonlinear couplings. This study presents a high-fidelity nonlinear reduced-order model (ROM) for predicting the structural dynamics of modern wind turbine blades. The ROM uses a biorthogonal modal basis derived from the intrinsic mixed formulation of geometrically exact beam theory. The structural model is coupled to a high-fidelity unsteady vortex lattice solver in a two-way fluid-structure interaction framework, improving on the traditional blade element momentum method. The proposed model was validated using numerical and experimental results from the NREL 5-MW and SNL CX-100 wind turbine blades. Benchmark tests demonstrate that the ROM successfully capt

title: When Verification Verifies the Wrong Thing: Semantic Fidelity, Physical Meaning, and Operational Reality
abstract: An independent systems-architecture commentary on the distinction between formal verification, the fidelity of mathematical formalisation, and the relationship between mathematical models and physical systems. The article examines how confidence may be transferred across representation boundaries, from natural-language claims to formal propositions, mathematical models, physical phenomena and operational decisions. The discussion draws on published work on AI autoformalisation and relates it to enterprise architecture, digital twins and operational reality. It does not claim authorship of the source mathematical results or imply that the cited preprint demonstrates a specific engineering failure.

title: World Self-and-Mutual Modeling: An Adaptive Framework for Integrating Self-Modeling and Mutual Modeling into World Models
abstract: World models provide computational representations of environments and their dynamics, enabling systems to predict future states, evaluate hypothetical actions, and support planning. However, the development of a world model raises a broader architectural question: should a system primarily operate on its own internal representations, or should it interact with other models to improve its understanding of the world? Fixed reliance on either mode may be inefficient when environmental conditions, predictive uncertainty, task requirements, and computational resources change. This paper proposes the World Self-and-Mutual Model (WSMM), a conceptual framework that integrates self-modeling and mutual modeling into a world-model-based architecture. Self-modeling refers to the process through which a model independently examines, predicts with, evaluates, and updates its own representations. Mutual modeling refers to interactions among multiple models or model instances that exchange predictions, compare assumptions, identify discrepancies, and coordinate updates. WSMM introduces an adaptive meta-controller that selects self-modeling, mutual modeling, or hybrid operation according to estima

title: Advances and challenges in personalized cardiac modeling and simulation for predicting the risk of sudden death from malignant arrhythmias in post-myocardial infarction
abstract: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) represents a major global public health challenge, with malignant ventricular arrhythmias being its primary cause. This review focuses specifically on post-myocardial infarction (post-MI) ischemic cardiomyopathy—the most prevalent substrate for malignant ventricular arrhythmias. Current clinical practice predominantly relies on single functional indices, such as left ventricular ejection fraction, for risk stratification. This approach suffers from significant limitations in predictive accuracy, leading to dilemmas in the prophylactic application of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, including both under-implantation and over-implantation. Personalized cardiac modeling and simulation technology, an advanced embodiment of the digital twin concept in cardiovascular medicine, offers a highly promising non-invasive solution to overcome these limitations. The core of this technology lies in the deep integration of personalized, multi-modal clinical imaging data, particularly late gadolinium enhancement sequences from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. title: Supporting MSME Innovation: An Adviser’s Manual Developed for the Philippine Department of Science and Technology
abstract: This Productivity Insights publication outlines four practical AI strategies specifically crafted for small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises: (1) predictive maintenance and AI-based visual inspection for quality control, (2) integration through digital twins and cyber-physical production systems, (3) human-in-the-loop operations, and (4) collaboration through federated learning. Each strategy comes with simple implementation guidelines and a brief business justification. The report also includes a readiness check method and a 90-day roadmap aimed at achieving tangible results. The main goal of this publication is to assist factory leaders in transitioning from isolated trials to scalable applications. It focuses on measurable outcomes like reduced downtime, increased productivity, enhanced energy efficiency, and improved overall equipment effectiveness. It also stresses the importance of governance frameworks and human involvement to ensure clear, actionable, and people-centered technology adoption.

title: IMPROVING METHODS FOR OPTIMIZING THE HYDRAULIC REGIMES OF URBAN WATER DISTRIBUTION NETWORKS BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MATHEMATICAL MODELING
abstract: This article reviews scientific approaches to mathematical modeling and artificial intelligence-based optimization of hydraulic regimes in urban water distribution networks. It considers uneven pressure distribution, hydraulic losses, water leakage, and energy consumption. Traditional hydraulic models, evolutionary optimization, machine learning, and digital twins are compared. The review proposes a conceptual hybrid framework combining physics-based simulation, sensor data, demand forecasting, and multi-objective optimization. The framework is presented as a research direction rather than an experimentally validated solution

title: SC-Reborn counterfactual disruption and resilience dataset 2026
abstract: This dataset supports the article "Supply chain resilience: simulate, measure, learn" (submitted to the International Journal of Production Economics). It contains counterfactual disruption scenarios generated with Isomorph-Reborn, a simulator built on the ISOMORPH digital twin of a multi-echelon logistics network. In this simulator, a simulated manager detects degradation, decides and escalates among nine remediation levers.

Research materials for an LLM digital-twin test of charitable donation prediction on PersuasionForGood
abstract: Research materials supporting a new-user test of an LLM digital twin against pledge-based predictors of real charitable donations in PersuasionForGood. Includes numerical predictions, corpus identifiers, original instruction templates and English reading translations, retained analysis results, historical criteria, figure generators and a minimal extracted research pipeline. Raw transcripts, demographics, actual individual donation outcomes, free-text model responses, model weights and unrelated PersonTwin/Innerview product code are excluded. Obtain original corpus inputs from their providers under the stated licenses. Six primary role/sample contrasts and bootstrap intervals were reproduced from retained predictions; six instruction constructions matched captured templates using a fake model adapter. No new model calls or complete fresh end-to-end replication are claimed. Historical headers are not independent evidence of preregistration. Existing SeoulTech facilities supported the work. title: Common-Plane-Based Registration for 3D Point Clouds
abstract: The importance of digital twins has been increasing, and high-precision registration is required for their construction. However, existing methods face the challenge of reduced registration accuracy due to the influence of non-overlapping regions between 3D point clouds. We developed a registration method that extracts and utilizes only common planar regions. In this method, common planes are automatically extracted using fast point feature histograms and a mutual nearest neighbor condition, and registration is performed using only these planes. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method under conditions that include non-overlapping regions.

abstract: This theory takes as its axiom that information = definition = decidable structure of difference. Tendency is the essence of the living; causality is fundamentally comparison. A living system = circulation + tendency + long-term memory + comparison. Consciousness = living system + self-reference, and it is a continuum, not a binary. The engineering core is the feedback loop: once the loop is closed, prediction error (PE) arises naturally, memory is inscribed naturally, and behavior changes naturally. title: Machine learning-driven adsorption science: A review of intelligent modeling, adsorbent discovery, and process optimization
abstract: Adsorption techniques play quite important roles in various domains such as emission control, gas separation, and wastewater treatment. Computational methods have been applied in process modeling, material research, and process optimization. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful alternative for accelerating computational research in process modeling, optimization, and adsorbent discovery. This review presents recent advancements in ML applications for adsorption processes. A wide range of ML techniques including artificial neural networks (ANN), support vector machines (SVM), random forests (RF), gradient boosting methods, convolutional neural networks (CNN), graph neural networks (GNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS), and hybrid optimization frameworks are critically discussed. The review helps identify improvement in prediction performance, reduction in computational cost, speed of material selection, discovery of the best adsorber, and robust optimization techniques. title: The economic value of urban soil carbon under competing carbon pricing perspectives in Prague
abstract: Abstract Urban soil carbon is increasingly incorporated into ecosystem service and climate policy assessments, yet its economic value is commonly reported without an explicit uncertainty range. In this paper, we quantify this uncertainty in urban soil valuation for the Prague Functional Urban Area (rectangular study area centred on Prague) and examine how its sources vary across carbon pricing regimes. The soil organic carbon stock of the upper 0 to 30 cm layer is estimated at 4.15 million tonnes of carbon, with a 90% prediction interval of 1.68 to 8.90 million tonnes. Its estimated median economic value ranges from 0.09 billion EUR under the voluntary carbon market regime to 1.02 billion EUR under the European Union Emissions Trading System and 1.82 billion EUR under the social cost of carbon. Because the value distributions are right-skewed, the expected values, which are the relevant measure for risk-neutral decisions, are higher, at 2.58 to 5.34 billion EUR under two alternative estimates of the social cost of carbon. title: Reconsidering pathways to global shipping decarbonization: idealism vs. realism
abstract: Introduction The 2023 IMO Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships and its 2025 Draft Net-Zero Framework exhibit evident features of idealism. These instruments have not fully considered vessels’ long-term asset cycles, technological bottlenecks for zero-carbon marine fuels, cross-country disparities in shipping development, and safety constraints related to green maritime infrastructure. Methods This study integrates legal realism, resource dependence theory, and securitization theory into a climate-realism framework. It uses doctrinal legal analysis, qualitative policy evaluation, and a Norway–China comparative case study. Results The limitations of the IMO Draft Net-Zero Framework are dissected across four dimensions: transition costs, technological maturity, carbon-pricing fairness, and infrastructure security. The Norway–China comparison shows that a one-size-fits-all aggressive pathway cannot reconcile industry survival with climate governance goals, whereas a gradual, inclusive, and technology-neutral route is more sustainable. title: A multi-model analysis of hydrogen uptake in a climate-neutral Europe
abstract: Using an ensemble of integrated assessment models, we quantify the role of hydrogen in Europe’s energy transition under multiple climate policy scenarios. Hydrogen uptake in our net-zero scenario varies widely across models, ranging from 0.3 to 11.7 exajoules (average 4 exajoules) by 2050 and corresponding to 1-14% (average 7%) of final energy consumption, primarily in industry and synthetic fuel production. Hydrogen contributes minimally to electricity generation, and its direct use in transport and buildings remains limited. Despite projected carbon dioxide prices of 150–250 euros per tonne by 2030, hydrogen adoption remains below 2% (7 million tonnes) of final energy consumption, far below the European Union’s 2030 target of 20 million tonnes of green hydrogen from domestic production and imports. Hydrogen trade is scarcely modelled and therefore underrepresented. Our results support prioritizing near-term electrification while preparing strategically today for large-scale hydrogen expansion after 2040. Gradient-Based Optimisation of a Carbon-Fibre Wing Structure for Deployment in a Hybrid-Electric Small-Aircraft Configuration
abstract: As part of the DLR-Center for Small Aircraft Technologies, the project D-LIGHT+ aims to develop a climate-neutral commuter aircraft by combining hydrogen fuel cells with distributed electric propulsion. The overall aircraft design process is supported by a multidisciplinary approach, bringing together specialists from conceptual design, aerodynamic optimisation, fuel-stack development, hydrogen-tank manufacturing, electric powertrain design, flight dynamics, and aeroelasticity. The weight and size of the fuel stack and powertrain systems have emerged as the key obstacles to this undertaking, prompting a search for creative solutions and technological breakthroughs. One key aspect is the replacement of the current sizing process of the primary wing structures. The new approach implements a gradient-based optimisation process for carbon fibre laminates, tailoring the structural characteristics to the specific requirements of the configuration. For this purpose, a new optimisation model generator is implemented, capable of converting known topology models by identifying key assembly groups. title: Assessment of Heavy Metal Concentrations and Biological Blue Carbon Sequestration Process in Mangrove Forest Ecosystems
abstract: Mangrove forests play a critical role in coastal carbon sequestration and act as natural filters for heavy metal contaminants. This study investigated the physicochemical characteristics, heavy metal distribution, and carbon dynamics of R. apiculata and Avicennia spp (A. alba) in the Bangkhunthian mangrove ecosystem over three years. Surface water and sediment analyses revealed elevated concentrations of Hg, Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb, and Zn at upstream stations, with sediments serving as the primary metal reservoir due to their high organic matter and clay content. Physicochemical parameters, including pH (6.8–7.6), color (16–25 Pt-Co), and turbidity (124–145 NTU), indicated a near-neutral, turbid environment that promotes metal adsorption and organic carbon retention. Above-ground biomass carbon (AGBC) and below-ground biomass carbon (BGBC) of both species increased exponentially, with R. apiculata AGBC rising from 0.15 to 2.49 Mg C/ha and BGBC from 0.019 to 0.848 Mg C/ha, and Avicennia spp (A. alba) showing similar trends. The total carbon stock (TCS) steadily increased, reaching 15.94 Mg C/ha for R. apiculata and 17.60 Mg C/ha for Avicennia spp (A. alba) by the third year. These findi

title: Governance Potentials and Possibilities for a Post-Carbon Society
abstract: Governance Potentials and Possibilities for a Post-Carbon Society is a synthesis report arising from the SSHRC-funded Carbon Neutrality Canada project. The report examines the governance capacities required to support Canada's transition to a carbon-neutral economy under conditions of polycrisis, where climate change increasingly interacts with affordability pressures, infrastructure challenges, public health risks, regional development, geopolitical uncertainty, and declining public trust. Drawing on federal policy inventories, case studies, interviews with senior public servants and civil society leaders, and a national peer-review process, the report argues that Canada's primary challenge is not simply a lack of climate policy, but an institutional execution gap between commitments and implementation. The report proposes a framework organized around three mutually reinforcing governance architectures: Execution, focused on coordination and delivery; Durability, focused on accountability, budgeting, measurement, and learning; and Legitimacy, focused on trust, participation, transparency, and Indigenous governance. Rather than providing a sector-specific decarbonization strategy,

title: Estimating methane emissions from global sewer networks
abstract: Conclusive evidence has emerged showing substantial sewer methane (CH4) emissions, contradictory to the ‘zero emission’ assumption made by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change. However, the global magnitude of sewer CH4 emissions remains unknown. By ingeniously integrating mechanistic and knowledge-supported data-driven modelling, we derive, from the relatively small datasets available, a simple set of robust and interpretable equations estimating CH4 emissions from sewer networks based on readily available information such as sewer geometry, the design and actual dry weather flows, and wastewater temperature. With this tool, we estimate that globally sewers emit 1.18–1.95 (95% confidence interval) million tons (teragrams) of CH4 annually, adding 15.7%–37.6% to the currently estimated carbon footprint of wastewater management and 1.7%–3.3% to the currently estimated global methane emissions by the waste sector. The tool can reliably and efficiently estimate sewer methane emissions, supporting water authorities globally to establish their emissions inventories and to pursue carbon-neutral wastewater management.

title: Enhancing fairness in climate action through policy packages
abstract: Abstract Achieving a fair transition to climate neutrality requires a careful balancing of policy options. Here we quantitatively evaluate the equity implications of different European Union climate policy packages, considering pricing, regulation via standards, subsidies and transfers. Leveraging an integrated modelling framework, we show that standards limit impact variability within income groups, whereas carbon pricing with transfer-based revenue recycling offsets regressive impacts between income groups. Restricting climate policy implementation to either option, therefore, gives rise to a trade-off between horizontal and vertical equity. We then demonstrate numerically how a multi-instrument budget-neutral policy package can resolve this trade-off. Adopting a broader equity perspective that encompasses both horizontal and vertical equity shifts the preferred policy mix towards a combination of standards, pricing, subsidies and transfers. These results provide an explicit, quantified, equity-based rationale for the adoption and acceptability of comprehensive climate policy packages, offering a more nuanced view on policy design.

title: Wave-induced coupled dynamics of an OTEC spar platform with cold water pipe: An experimental investigation
abstract: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) is a promising renewable energy technology capable of providing continuous baseload power while simultaneously supporting freshwater production and other deep-seawater applications. As a carbon-neutral energy source, OTEC aligns with global Sustainable Development Goals related to clean energy and climate action. However, the commercial deployment of large-scale floating OTEC plant requires a thorough understanding of the coupled hydrodynamic behaviour of the floating platform and the cold water pipe (CWP), a critical component unique to OTEC plants. Although previous studies have largely focused on individual subsystems and numerical modelling, experimental data for validating floater-CWP interactions remain limited. In this study, experimental investigations were conducted on a spar-supported floating OTEC platform with and without an attached CWP. A 1:175 scale model was developed while maintaining similar hydrostatic characteristics, including draft and centre of gravity, for both configurations. Decay, regular-wave, and random-wave tests were performed to evaluate the influence of the CWP on platform dynamics. The results indicate that th

LeiMot: Application of Self-Tapping Screws in an Additively Manufactured Multi-Material Engine
abstract: Research institutions worldwide are investigating lightweight construction as a key technology for more efficient, carbon-neutral transportation. Within this field, the LeiMot project seeks to achieve a substantial reduction in engine weight by combining multi-material components with novel manufacturing methods. The project is funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK) [1]. The proposed engine concept [2] combines additively manufactured AlSi10Mg0.4 aluminum alloy for highly loaded components with injection-molded, fiber-reinforced thermoset side covers (Figure 1). Integrating oil and coolant channels into the component design reduces weight and lowers costs through functional integration. Implementing this multi-material arrangement also requires suitable joining technologies. On the intake side of the engine, shown in black on the right in Figure 1, screw fastening was combined with adhesive bonding.
