title: The pH and available phosphorus as primary drivers of compost-induced CO 2 emissions from Malaysian tropical soil: empirical relationships
abstract: Abstract. Confronting the global need for climate-smart agriculture, this study investigated the mechanisms controlling CO2 emissions from a Malaysian tropical soil amended with four composts. Multiple regression analyses identified soil available phosphorus (AP) and pH as the key interactive drivers of CO2 emissions, which followed the order: chicken dung compost (CDCS) > sludge compost (SLS) > goat manure-leaf compost (GLCS) > food waste compost (FWCS).The significantly higher emissions from CDCS were primarily due to its pronounced elevation of soil pH, likely stimulating microbial activity. The positive correlation with AP indicated that enhanced phosphorus availability further promoted microbial carbon mineralization. The findings demonstrate that compost is not a carbon-neutral amendment; its net climate impact depends on the specific physic-chemical changes it induces in the soil. This provides a scientific basis for optimizing compost selection to reconcile soil fertility improvement with greenhouse gas mitigation in tropical agroecosystems

title: Metagenomic Discovery of Neutral Lipid Metabolism Pathways in the Arctic Ocean Microbiomes Suggests a Potential New Role in Survival and Oceanic Carbon Cycling
abstract: The Arctic Ocean microbiomes experience extreme seasonal fluctuations in light, nutrient availability, and organic carbon supply. In this environment, neutral lipid storage may provide a key survival strategy. Here, we investigated the diversity, distribution, and ecological role of neutral lipid metabolism in Arctic microbiomes using metagenome-resolved analyses and global ocean comparisons. Arctic photic-zone microbiomes were strongly enriched in triacylglycerol (TAG) biosynthesis genes relative to other oceans, primarily due to picoeukaryotic phytoplankton, including the ecologically dominant Micromonas and Bathycoccus. In contrast, prokaryotic communities exhibited diverse TAG-degrading taxa and fatty acid transport systems, supporting a previously unrecognized lipotrophic bacterial guild exploiting phytoplankton-derived lipids as carbon and energy sources. title: The evolution of sustainable building governance: Comparative insights from global energy code systems and their forecasting by agentic AI system
abstract: This study proposes a novel Sustainable Building Governance Index (SBGI) integrated with an advanced Agentic AI-Based Forecasting Framework to evaluate and predict the future evolution of global sustainable building governance systems. The framework combines multidimensional governance indicators including building energy codes, HVAC governance, lighting efficiency, retrofit readiness, climate adaptation, envelope performance, and compliance mechanisms into a unified sustainability intelligence platform. Statistical validation confirmed strong framework reliability with a Cronbach Alpha value of 0.89, PCA variance explanation of 81%, and forecasting accuracy of 92%. The proposed Agentic AI model outperformed conventional machine learning approaches including XGBoost, Random Forest, LSTM, and ARIMA. Forecasting results indicate that global SBGI values will increase from 0.58 in 2024–0.91 by 2050, while net-zero readiness rises from 0.39 to 0.94. The study further predicts a 57% reduction in building-sector carbon emissions by 2050 through intelligent governance systems, retrofit integration, smart HVAC optimization, and AI-driven sustainability planning. title: Governance gap: How cities plan for climate neutrality without planning the end of fossil gas
abstract: Peer-reviewed paper 5-090-26 Many cities around the world have adopted a climate neutrality target. In the EU’s mission ‘Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities’, 100 cities are pursuing the target of achieving climate neutrality by 2030. To achieve this, there needs to be a phase-out of fossil gas. However, municipal strategies for coping with declining gas demand and for the future of gas distribution networks are often lacking. This paper compares six European mission-cities – Barcelona, Budapest, Copenhagen, Ljubljana, Mannheim, and Warsaw – to investigate how local governments address fossil gas dependency, govern heat system transformation and address the infrastructural and economic challenges associated with decommissioning gas networks. The study reveals a discrepancy between climate-neutrality commitments and tangible measures to phase out gas. While cities such as Copenhagen and Mannheim demonstrate integrated planning and substantial shifts towards low-carbon district heating (DH), others maintain gas grids as a long-term component of their heating supply and lack binding timelines or regulatory instruments for transformation or decommissioning. title: Thermochemical Conversion of Biomass for Hydrogen Production: A Review
abstract: The need to transit to a renewable and sustainable energy source from a fossil fuel-dependent energy system is significantly motivated by the imperatives of climate change, global warming, and the necessity for enhanced energy security. One of the edges of using biomass as a source over fossil fuels is that it is a fuel that is CO2 neutral and most likely cut carbon-dioxide emissions considerably. Biomass demonstrates considerable potential to meet the energy demands of contemporary societies. Hydrogen as an energy source is becoming more popular and could effectively substitute fossil fuels. The Biomass gasification technique is a versatile procedure employed for mass production of heat, electricity, biofuels, hydrogen, and various chemicals in the chemical industry. The process of thermochemical conversion of biomass for hydrogen generation is a promising system that will help generate clean energy for manufacturing industries. This process involves various methods, such as gasification, pyrolysis, and hydrothermal gasification, with each method having its own challenges and optimization advantages. title: Life cycle assessment of renewable hydrogen and bioenergy pathways transitioning from conventional to sustainable power generation
abstract: The transition toward climate-neutral energy systems requires robust comparisons of alternative electricity generation pathways based on consistent life-cycle frameworks. This study performs a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment of nine electricity production routes under Portuguese conditions, including seven renewable energy-based systems and two fossil-based systems. The renewable pathways comprise direct biomass combustion, upgraded biogas combustion, synthetic biomethane produced via carbon dioxide methanation with green hydrogen, and hydrogen-based electricity generated either from biomethane steam reforming or solar photovoltaic-powered water electrolysis. Hydrogen utilisation was evaluated through both combustion and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Environmental impacts were quantified across six categories, including global warming potential, acidification, particulate matter formation, human toxicity, land use and water consumption. Results show that fossil pathways remain the dominant sources of greenhouse gas emissions, with coal and natural gas producing approximately 1.28 and 0.79 kg CO 2 eq per kWh, respectively. title: Scoping Review of AI, Metrology, and ESG in the Semiconductor Sector: Implications for Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD)
abstract: The semiconductor sector faces a dual transition: scaling manufacturing execution through Artificial Intelligence (AI) while satisfying stringent sustainability mandates, such as the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). This paper presents a scoping review of 1,465 documents indexed in Web of Science and Scopus, spanning AI-integrated metrology, supply chain ESG, and federated industrial data spaces. Network analysis reveals a highly fragmented "core-periphery" knowledge structure, emphasizing a critical structural hole between AI-driven process optimization and downstream sustainability governance. To close these gaps, this study proposes a 6-layer Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) architecture grounded in a System of Systems (SoS) paradigm. By establishing distinct "grid-to-core" and "standards-through-supply-chain" integration pathways, the proposed framework demonstrates how virtual metrology (VM), localized federated learning, and defensive RegTech mechanisms can build provenance-aware data fabrics. title: Circular Design in Action: Practices, Networks, Education, and Research
abstract: The Circular Design in Action: Practices, Networks, Education, and Research conference - organized by Department Architecture and Design of University of Genova - invited scholars, researchers, designers, and practitioners to share their insights and innovative approaches in Circular Design. This event has been part of the CiD Project – Circular Design for Bio-based Innovation towards Climate-Neutral Cities, an initiative fostering sustainable solutions in architecture, product design, and urban transformation. In an era of pressing environmental challenges, design plays a fundamental role in shaping a sustainable future. The conference explored circular economy principles, bio-based materials, and innovative design methodologies that drive the transition toward carbon-neutral cities. Participants had the opportunity to showcase research, methodologies, and practical applications that redefine how materials, products, and built environments are designed, produced, and regenerated, within two tracks: + Track 1: Design for change + Track 2: Circular Cities The conference is part of the activities of the CiD Circular Design Innovation Alliance, coordinated by the Chair for Territorial

title: Targeted interventions can ensure environmental co-benefits from energy decarbonization
The timing of warming matters as much as its intensity for the annual carbon balance of a degraded raised bog
abstract: Abstract. Pristine peatlands act as natural carbon sinks, but disturbance — mostly anthropogenic drainage — turns them into CO2 sources, responsible for 2–5 % of annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions globally. Complex interactions between vegetation, soil, climate, and hydrology produce highly variable CO2 budgets on different types of peatlands and between years. Abandoned drained peatlands are considered low-hanging fruit for rewetting due to expected high GHG emissions and low resistance to repurposing yet remain underrepresented in research. To close this gap in literature we measured three years (2023–2025) of CO2 and CH4 fluxes alongside meteorological and hydrological conditions in a drained shrub-dominated ombrotrophic raised bog in NW Germany, investigating carbon flux budgets and the main seasonal drivers of fluxes. Methane fluxes were negligible throughout, likely due to consistently deep water tables (>15 cm). Annual CO2 budgets were highly variable: the site was a considerable source in 2023 and 2025 (131 and 86 gC m-2 a-1) but near-neutral in 2024. An anomalously warm spring in 2024 triggered earlier vegetation greening and substantially increased CO2 uptake capacity

title: The Electoral Impact of Housing Climate Policy: Evidence from Germany
abstract: Abstract The transition to carbon-neutral residential heating poses extraordinary policy challenges to societies in Europe and beyond. In this paper, we study the electoral consequences of an amendment to the German Building Energy Act (GEG) aimed at phasing-out fossil-based heating systems. We use granular building stock data to approximate heterogeneity in household compliance costs and apply difference-in-differences and triple difference models to estimate its impacts on vote shares at the municipal level. For the state elections in Bavaria and Hesse, we find relative gains for the far-right (+2.4 pp) and conservative opposition parties (+6.5 pp) and losses for the incumbent federal government parties (−2.9 pp) in the baseline specification of our model. For the latter two, the effects are more pronounced in rural municipalities. These findings highlight the importance of holistic climate policy approaches that account for salient and heterogeneous costs to mitigate political backlash.

title: CLIMATE ADAPTATION OF BUILDINGS AND CARBON FOOTPRINT REDUCTION: SEEKING A BALANCE IN LIFE CYCLE MANAGEMENT
abstract: The article examines the relationship between climate adaptation of buildings and reduction of their carbon footprint over the life cycle. It is shown that contemporary architectural and construction science is facing a methodological paradox: increasing concentrations of greenhouse gases intensify climate risks and increase the need for building adaptation measures; however, some of these measures require additional energy, materials and equipment, which may increase operational and embodied greenhouse gas emissions. The purpose of the article is to systematize Russian and international studies on this issue and to develop recommendations aimed at transforming the conflict between adaptation and decarbonization into synergy. The methodological basis of the study includes a systematized review of scientific publications, analysis of regulatory and methodological documents, and generalization of open climate data. A classification of adaptation measures according to their carbon effect is proposed, with conflict, neutral and synergistic groups of measures identified. title: South Arabian to Oman Pipeline
abstract: The Arabian Sea Strategic Corridor (ASSC) proposes a phased, climate‑positive infrastructure system beginning with a secure export route from the southern Saudi oil fields to the Arabian Sea via Oman. This initial “Phase Zero” corridor bypasses the geopolitical vulnerability of the Strait of Hormuz, where ~20 million barrels/day currently transit, creating a single point of global economic failure. The southern corridor integrates a hybrid steel/carbon‑fibre pipeline, SMR‑powered pumping and desalination nodes, and a 1,000 km ecological shield designed to stabilize desert terrain, reduce thermal stress, and generate carbon‑neutral export certification. This first phase forms a technically straightforward and politically stable backbone that can be extended northward into Iraq, creating a unified regional export spine independent of regional chokepoints. Beyond the Middle East, the ASSC architecture enables a scalable “Turnkey Oasis” technology package for deployment across the African Sahel, combining nuclear‑powered desalination, ecological stabilization, and micro‑irrigation systems. title: Hydrochar as a sustainable soil amendment
abstract: The increasing pressure on natural resources and the accumulation of organic waste highlight the urgent need for sustainable waste-to-resource strategies and effective soil restoration practices. Hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) has emerged as a promising technology for converting diverse waste streams into hydrochars—carbon-rich materials with the potential to improve soil quality, immobilize contaminants, and contribute to climate change mitigation. However, the scientific challenge lies in the considerable variability of hydrochar properties, which depend strongly on feedstock composition, HTC conditions, and subsequent modifications, thereby complicating the prediction of their environmental performance. This review comprehensively synthesizes advances published between 2017 and 2026 in the application of hydrochars as soil amendments. The assessment focused on three dimensions: (i) impacts on heavy metal immobilization, (ii) effects on soil microbiomes and respiration, and (iii) influences on crop productivity and greenhouse gas emissions. abstract: The accelerating pressures of climate change, rapid urbanization, resource depletion, and environmental degradation necessitate the development of integrative and forward-looking paradigms for sustainable urban transformation. This study explores the scientific perspectives underpinning the synergy between environmental engineering and eco-urbanism, emphasizing their collective potential to enable adaptive, low-carbon, and resilient urban systems. Environmental engineering, traditionally focused on pollution control, resource management, and infrastructure optimization, is increasingly intersecting with eco-urbanism, a multidisciplinary framework that prioritizes ecological integrity, human well-being, and sustainable spatial planning. The convergence of these domains fosters a systems-oriented approach to urban development, wherein technological innovation, ecological design, and socio-economic considerations are harmonized. This paper critically examines contemporary theoretical frameworks, methodological approaches, and practical implementations that exemplify this synergy. title: High-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage for low-carbon energy districts in Southern Europe
abstract: Seasonal thermal energy storage combined with district heating networks represents a promising pathway for reducing greenhouse gas emissions from urban heat supply. This study investigates the energy and environmental impacts of integrating a high-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage (HT-ATES) system into the district heating network of Tirano, northern Italy. The objective is to evaluate the contribution of HT-ATES to district heating decarbonization under hydrogeological conditions that are relatively unfavourable for thermal energy storage. The proposed system combines long-term thermal energy storage with renewable-based heat-supply technologies, including biomass boilers and a cogeneration plant, while retaining a diesel boiler solely as backup. System performance is simulated dynamically in TRNSYS 18 using real heating-demand data, whereas aquifer thermal behaviour is modelled in FeFlow to represent groundwater flow and heat transport. Despite the challenging storage conditions, the HT-ATES system achieves a thermal recovery efficiency of 25.2 % and enables the district heating network to operate with minimal reliance on fossil fuels. title: Organic Farming as a Pathway toward Carbon-Neutral Agriculture: Opportunities, Limits and Future Directions
abstract: Agriculture and agrifood systems are important contributors to anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions, with emissions arising from livestock, rice cultivation, land-use change, crop-residue burning and fossil-fuel use. This narrative review evaluates organic farming as a possible pathway towards carbon-neutral agriculture in comparison with conventional systems. The review synthesises evidence on carbon neutrality assessment, including emissions inventories, life-cycle assessment, carbon-footprint calculation, carbon sequestration measurement and third-party verification. It also examines organic practices such as crop rotation, cover cropping, biofertiliser use, green manuring, conservation agriculture and agroforestry. The evidence indicates that organic farming can improve soil organic carbon storage, reduce reliance on synthetic nitrogen fertilisers and lower nitrous oxide emissions through slower nitrogen release, reduced mineral nitrogen pools and more continuous plant cover. Comparative studies also suggest higher carbon sequestration efficiency under organic management, including 42.8 per cent under organic agriculture compared with 21.6 per cent under conventional manageme

title: What information on contemporary terrestrial carbon dynamics can an integration of current geospatial data confidently provide?
abstract: Abstract. The terrestrial carbon (C) cycle is a key global biogeochemical cycle, linked to climate change and regulation, provisioning and regulating ecosystem services and underpinning human livelihoods. To understand climate risks and to support the development of effective climate mitigation strategies requires rigorous, uncertainty bounded, systemic information on C dynamics and their underpinning ecological processes. Significant effort has been invested into attempting to quantify current C stocks and exchanges of C. These data are often incomplete in space and time, contain poorly characterised errors, and lack internal consistency checks, making the construction of a reliable global C budget a significant challenge. Here, we ask what information on contemporary terrestrial carbon dynamics can an integration of current geospatial data confidently provide? We present a global (0.5 × 0.5 deg), multi-decadal (2003–2024) analysis of the terrestrial C-cycle at a monthly time step. title: Evaluating perceived process performance and outputs in designing a national collaborative REDD+ governance program in Ghana
abstract: Integrated landscape approaches to Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) aim to balance competing land uses and address deforestation drivers outside the forest sector. Despite their conceptual appeal, implementation remains challenging due to the need for multi-level stakeholder alignment and cross-sectoral coordination. Collaborative governance regimes offer a promising mechanism to navigate these dilemmas; however, empirical evidence of their performance within Global South REDD+ contexts remain scarce. This study applies the Integrative Framework for Collaborative Governance (IFCG) to analyze the links between collaborative dynamics, perceived process performance, and policy outputs during the formulation of the Ghana Cocoa Forest REDD+ Program (GCFRP) from 2008 to 2019. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and comprehensive policy document analysis. title: Reimagining India 2047: AI, Sustainability and Inclusive Growth
abstract: Reimagining India 2047: AI, Sustainability and Inclusive Growth offers a forward-looking and interdisciplinary exploration of India’s transformative journey toward its centenary of independence. Authored by Amarpreet Kaur and Dr. Ankit Raj Singh, the book examines how emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence, can act as a catalyst for sustainable development and inclusive economic growth in a rapidly evolving global landscape. The book brings together perspectives from technology, economics, public policy, and environmental studies to present a holistic vision of India’s future. It critically analyzes the opportunities and challenges associated with AI-driven innovation across key sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, education, manufacturing, governance, and urban development. Emphasis is placed on leveraging digital technologies not merely for economic expansion, but for creating equitable outcomes that benefit marginalized and underserved communities. A strong focus on sustainability runs throughout the book, highlighting the need to balance technological progress with environmental responsibility. title: AI-BASED MARKET INTELLIGENCE AND PRICE PREDICTION FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE
abstract: Abstract: Market intelligence software gathers and processes information on demand, supply, competition and customers to help managers, farmers and other stakeholders in the value chain of agriculture. When such software is combined with artificial intelligence (AI) it becomes well-suited for predicting market movement and price fluctuation of farm produce. This integration encourages market orientation and enables stakeholders to identify opportunities and make strategic choices about what, when, where and how to produce, overcoming limitations associated with conventional pricing models and forecasting such as overlooking the impact of weather uncertainty, evolving consumer preferences, global trade shocks and policy actions. Artificial intelligence techniques of machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing facilitate the use of diverse datasets such as satellite imagery, transaction records, logistics data and digital signals with forecasting models. Radar reads business news continuously and extracts each funding announcement into structured fields: company, stage, amount, currency, investors and date. It then links the company to its record in a database of five million companies. This release covers startups worldwide, January 2019 to June 2026. It runs that output through a reproducible cleaning pipeline: repeated reports of one deal are merged, recaps of past rounds are dropped, and every amount is checked against the sentence it was read from. abstract: Global heavy industry and production agriculture face acute structural constraints: laborshortages, hazardous environmental exposure, escalating operational expenditures, andprohibitive cloud inference latencies. Benchmarked across 11 standard Embodied AI benchmark suites,Kò. yà achieves 100% feature coverage and sets state-of-the-art results across multi-modalperception, sequential planning, and bipedal field locomotion. We also detail the 12-GateCognitive Certification Framework, the Toshiba SCiB LTO power architecture, empiricalHumanoidBench evaluations, Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) models, and the commercialLetter of Credit (LOC) booking framework.

abstract: ntegrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems for health monitoring, smart energy, water quality assessment, and precision agriculture require compact, low-power hardware that can carry data and probe the surrounding environment at the same time. Hybrid plasmonic waveguides are promising building blocks for such platforms, since they confine light far below the diffraction limit while keeping propagation losses lower than those of purely plasmonic structures. This work numerically investigates an Ag/PTFE/Si hybrid plasmonic waveguide, in which a silicon ridge (400 nm × 300 nm) is separated from a silver film by a 30 nm low-index PTFE gap on a SiO₂ substrate. Two-dimensional finite-element eigenmode analysis in COMSOL Multiphysics at λ = 1550 nm gives a complex effective index of n_eff = 2.4618 − 7.4564×10⁻⁴ i, an effective mode area of A_eff ≈ 0.04 λ², and a propagation length of L_p ≈ 170 µm. The strong field concentration in the nanoscale gap makes the mode highly sensitive to changes in the local refractive index, which suits it to sensing, while the moderate loss supports on-chip data transmission. title: Computational Provenance and Reproducibility Record of Ammi Analysis in www.raisins.live
abstract: RAISINS (R and AI Solutions for INferential Statistics) is an advanced, user-friendly online platform for statistical analysis, seamlessly integrating the power of R, Python, and Artificial Intelligence. Specially designed for agricultural research, RAISINS enables students, researchers, and professionals to perform complex analyses and generate publication-ready results without the need for software installation or coding expertise. Simply choose your analysis module, upload your dataset, and receive instant, insightful outputs. RAISINS supports individual users across the globe as well as institutions in India and abroad. This Computational Provenance and Reproducibility Record documents the statistical computing environment, software dependencies, computational provenance, and bibliographic references associated with the RAISINS AMMI Analysis module. It is intended to support computational reproducibility and software transparency. Detailed statistical methodology, mathematical derivations, and user guidance are provided separately in the official module documentation. You can access the online cloud platform at https://www.raisins.live/

title: Evaluating domain generalization in agricultural deep learning through multi-seed LOSO validation and explainable AI
abstract: Abstract Conventional validation schemes may overestimate model robustness in agricultural deep learning when spatial domain shifts are not explicitly considered. This study evaluated convolutional neural networks for pasture biomass estimation using the CSIRO Image2Biomass dataset within a multi-seed Leave-One-State-Out (LOSO) framework. A total of 24 experiments combined four Australian geographical domains, two architectures (ResNet50 and EfficientNet-B0), and three random seeds (42, 123, and 2025). Performance was assessed using WRMSLE, MAE, RMSE, and R 2 . Seed-to-seed training variability was summarized using standard deviations across three random seeds, while 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for test WRMSLE were estimated by resampling the held-out test samples within each seed-level LOSO run. A metadata-based Random Forest was included as a non-image baseline. ResNet50 achieved mean test WRMSLE values ranging from 0.869 to 1.460 across held-out domains, whereas EfficientNet-B0 ranged from 0.911 to 1.519. title: Fusion Intelligence: A Paradigm for Merging Natural and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Abstract: This review paper presents fusion intelligence (FI), a bio-inspired paradigm that synergistically integrates the intrinsic sensory, cognitive, and locomotive capabilities of intelligent biological organisms with the computational scale, trend analysis, and supervisory control of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven systems. Conventional edge AI nodes deployed across Internet of Things (IoT) networks face severe operational bottlenecks due to high energy consumption, computational constraints, and network latency. Biological entities, in contrast, execute complex sensing, spatial mapping, and physical actuation within milliwatt metabolic power budgets. FI establishes a non-invasive, closed-loop cyber physical framework where edge sensors observe natural intelligence (NI), machine learning models interpret behavioral telemetry, and automated actuators deploy environmental incentives to guide biological entities toward target tasks. We review the taxonomy of bio integrated systems, present the theoretical closed-loop control dynamics, and analyze an applied agricultural case study demonstrating a approximately 50% net improvement in pollination efficacy.

title: SOCIAL MEDIA AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN AGRICULTURAL COMMUNICATION IN INDIA: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS, 2010–2025
abstract: Social media and artificial intelligence (AI) are changing the way agricultural information is shared in India; however, research on these two tools of communication has not been reviewed together. The present review examined the publication profile of Scopus-indexed research on social media and AI in Indian agricultural communication, the way this research has studied the two tools, and what the evidence shows about them. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus and OpenAlex were searched for the period 2010–2025, and every eligible study was checked for Scopus indexing one by one. Out of 2,735 records, 33 studies were included, coded by tool, research design, theme and actor, and synthesised narratively. The research is very recent, as 82% of the studies appeared in 2021–2025. Sixteen studies examined social media, mainly WhatsApp, 14 examined AI, mainly machine-learning analysis of Kisan Call Centre queries, and three applied AI to agricultural tweets. Content and data analytics was the most common design (52%), and none of the studies was a randomised trial. abstract: The rapid digitization of modern systems has increased the demand for intelligent, adaptive, and data-driven solutions across connected systems. However, these domains face persistent challenges such as heterogeneous datasets, limited labeled data, real-time processing constraints, privacy concerns, model interpretability, and poor generalization across environments. This review examines the application of major Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques for solving classification, prediction, optimization, anomaly detection, routing, image analysis, and decision-support problems. The empirical patterns across the literature are summarized cautiously across studies. General lessons that emerged across the reviewed domains were also presented. Overall, the review provides researchers with a concise foundation for understanding current AI methods, their practical limitations, and future research directions in the aspect of connected environments. This article has tried to clarify various aspects and overall issues related to the use of AI techniques in computer networks, image processing and computer vision, smart agriculture and related intelligent systems. title: When information is not enough: AI-enabled advisory and the fragile pathways of low-carbon transitions under system constraints
abstract: CONTEXT Low-carbon rice farming is widely recognized as a key strategy for agricultural decarbonization, yet adoption remains limited among smallholder farmers despite expanding AI-enabled advisory and increasing awareness of climate risks. Existing adoption-based models provide limited explanation for why improved information and awareness often fail to translate into low-carbon transition. OBJECTIVE This study explains how farmers translate information into transition intention under real-world constraints by conceptualizing low-carbon agriculture as a constrained system transition. It develops a process-based cognitive decision pathway linking risk perception, perceived feasibility, and decision confidence, while positioning AI-enabled advisory as cognitive infrastructure rather than a direct transition intention. METHODS Survey data were collected from 398 smallholder rice farmers in Vietnam's Mekong Delta. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to estimate a framework integrating sequential mediation and moderated mediation, with government support and market access modelled as system-level enabling conditions. title: AI for Sustainable Development: Exploring Opportunities and Overcoming Challenges
abstract: The rate of advancement in Artificial Intelligence presents a transformative opportunity that brings with it the hope of addressing challenging global problems and hastening progress toward the United Nations&s; SDGs. This paper considers the two faces of AI—both a source of sustainable innovation and a potential breeding ground for new ethical, environmental, and socio-economic issues. A comprehensive review of 15 Scopus-indexed scholarly articles is undertaken to investigate AI applications in vital sectors such as energy, agriculture, water management, urban development, and environmental conservation. The study elucidates how AI supports decision-making processes, resource efficiency, and climate resilience. In contrast, it also explores the issues raised by data privacy, job loss, and carbon emissions of AI systems. The research study advocates the comprehensive governance framework and interdisciplinary cooperation. Overall current research is important in the view of SDG&s;s and sustainable governance. abstract: The successful integration of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms in precision agriculture provided farmers with the means to identify potential issues, such as early disease detection or pest infestations, by making crop-related predictions. The new technological developments in this field improve the functioning of traditional agriculture by reducing the dependence on specialized human expertise and facilitating greater access to diagnostic procedures. However, most studies conducted in this area rely on centralized training of AI models, which leads to increased costs and raised privacy-related concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a compelling framework for collaboratively training machine learning (ML) models on distributed datasets without centralizing the data owned by each participant. FL offers significant advantages in the preservation of data privacy, facilitates the collaborative exploitation of geographically distributed data sources, and reduces the risks associated with centralized collection. title: U.S. Intermediate Oilseed Crop Yield Potential to Support Economic and Environmental Assessments
abstract: Cultivating intermediate oilseed crops during the fallow seasons of existing crop rotations is a strategy for producing high-quality lipid feedstocks with low impacts on existing agricultural production. The Department of Energy’s 2023 Billion-Ton Report (BT23) estimated a sustainable resource potential of more than 20 billion pounds of lipid oil per year from intermediate camelina, carinata, and pennycress. These supply estimates were based on county-scale crop yield estimates provided by University of Tennessee collaborators working on the Federal Aviation Administration’s Center of Excellence for Alternative Jet Fuels and Environment (FAA ASCENT) project. However, camelina, carinata, and pennycress have experienced only very limited commercial deployment to date, so assessments of sustainable supply potential are sensitive to uncertainty in regional crop yield estimates. Since the release of BT23, Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) has been working to update regional and county-scale yields for camelina, carinata, and pennycress as well as to generate county-scale yield information for winter canola, another promising intermediate oilseed crop in the mid-South region. title: PhD in Artificial Intelligence in India: Research Opportunities and Career Pathways
abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming industries by introducing new approaches to problem solving, Research, and Technological innovation. Fields such as Healthcare, Education, Agriculture, and Manufacturing increasingly explore intelligent systems to address complex challenges. For students interested in Research, developing a strong foundation in Mathematics, Statistics, Programming, and Algorithms is an important starting point. Academic projects and Interdisciplinary learning can help aspiring researchers understand how AI methods are developed, evaluated, and applied to real world problems. Research also encourages critical thinking, experimentation, and the ability to examine evidence before drawing conclusions. Exploring emerging areas such as Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, and Responsible AI can help students identify topics that match their interests. A clear research direction, consistent preparation, and curiosity about technological developments can support a meaningful academic journey. Understanding research expectations and exploring different specializations can also help prospective scholars prepare for the demands of advanced stu

title: Tool Equipment Design for an AI-Based Smart Watering System
abstract: Effective management of water resources has increasingly become essential against the backdrop of global climate change and requirements for sustainable agriculture. The conventional irrigation system is likely to lead to wastage of water and inefficient utilization, especially in areas where water scarcity is a problem. This study supplements the field of having a new innovative answer through the development of an AI-based smart watering system integrated with intelligent devices and sensors to improve water delivery. The core issue is the inaccuracy of traditional irrigation systems, which lack the potential of taking into account the soil moisture, weather, and water requirement of crops. The aim of this study is to design and validate a tool-based smart irrigation system with the ability to automatically water according to real-time environmental data. Using an experimental research paradigm, the system was constructed utilizing IoT-based hardware such as soil moisture sensors, a microcontroller, and a water pump controlled wirelessly.

title: A Framework for Enhanced Human-AI Collaboration in Dynamic Environments
AI-enabled hydroponics: a critical review of sensor-driven farming systems for sustainable global food security
Performance Evaluation of Human–Machine Collaboration in Smart Agriculture Using Statistical Modeling and Simulation
abstract: By introducing a data-driven human–machine collaboration performance evaluation Model (HMCPEM) that utilizes multiple regression and Monte Carlo simulation, the effectiveness and dependability of collaborative decision-making in smart agriculture were assessed in this study. The model combines big data analytics with cognitive computing concepts to assess human involvement, AI prediction uncertainty, and environmental fluctuations. The model was tested in a smart irrigation system in the Jianan Plain, Taiwan. The model successfully captured the balance between delay and risk, and it adaptively modified risk sensitivity through feedback learning. Its cognitive framework allows the model to enhance performance amid uncertainty by reducing the combined costs of delay and risk. This approach offers a transparent and replicable method for human-centered AI applications, with possible applications in smart manufacturing and healthcare decision-making systems.

title: Do digital agricultural tools improve women’s agency and well-being?
abstract: Key takeaways - Digital tools benefit women in agriculture in a variety of ways. Evidence from multiple countries shows gains in financial inclusion, decision-making power, access to credit, and well-being when services are designed to meet women’s needs. - Yet access alone does not guarantee benefits. Women gain the most when digital services are affordable, practical, linked to resources, and tailored to their priorities. - Women should help shape digital innovations. Involving women in the design, testing, and evaluation of digital and AI tools can make them more inclusive and effective.

title: Software Framework for Tiny Machine Learning
abstract: This chapter reviews the evolutionary path and future perspectives of software frameworks for tiny machine learning (TinyML), which enable the computation of innovative machine learning (ML) models on smaller, commodity devices. The chapter provides an introductory, concise overview of TinyML, its role in the Internet of Things (IoT), the edge computing era, and its global significance. It then addresses the unique challenges of building and deploying ML models on hardware with limited processing power, memory, and energy. This chapter provides an overview of commonly used software frameworks that address these challenges, outlining their application domains, architectural elements, and design principles. The chapter also emphasizes the solutions these frameworks provide for model development, training, and deployment. The current trends, research, and future directions within TinyML software frameworks, which hold promise for transforming edge AI applications in healthcare, agriculture, and industrial IoT, are also presented.

title: [Global Livingry Governance Architecture I Part 19]: Redefining National Defense in the Era of Hybrid Warfare: From Traditional Hardware Procurement to Infrastructure Autonomy Density, Bio-Logistics, and Autonomous Algorithmic Matrices.
abstract: The traditional NATO defense spending model of 2% of GDP faces a critical structural crisis. Channeling financial resources into standalone hardware and centralized ammunition depots creates a fragile defense architecture vulnerable to modern hybrid warfare. This paper argues that national security cannot be measured solely by lethal weapon quantity, but must instead be defined by: Infrastructure Autonomy Density: Localized autonomy in renewable energy microgrids and clean water supplies. Self-Sustaining Green Military: Transforming defense infrastructure into practical peacetime civic utilities to foster voluntary community participation. Biomedical Optimization: Eradicating Central Nervous System (CNS) fatigue in personnel using empirical biomedical data from PubMed. Algorithmic Chessboard Architecture: Utilizing real-time technological ecosystems (passive multisensor mesh and pre-launch AI analytics) to eliminate the "fog of war". Nature Restoration and Reproductive Value: Shifting budgets from weapon consumption to ecosystem restoration, easing household living costs, and resolving the trust crisis underlying declining birth rates. title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture
abstract: Abstract: Climate change, population growth, and increasing pressure on natural resources pose major challenges to global agricultural production. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising technology for addressing these challenges through precision farming, machine learning, robotic automation, and data-driven decision-making. This study examines the applications of AI in crop management, real-time monitoring, yield prediction, resource optimization, and sustainable agricultural production. The integration of AI with advanced genetic technologies can improve productivity, resource-use efficiency, and climate resilience. However, challenges related to technology, infrastructure, farmer awareness, data availability, affordability, and regulatory frameworks limit its widespread adoption. The study highlights the need for supportive policies, capacity building, digital infrastructure, and collaboration among farmers, researchers, industries, and policymakers. Overall, AI has significant potential to transform modern agriculture, enhance food security, and promote sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural development.

title: Computational Provenance and Reproducibility Record of Placket in www.raisins.live
abstract: RAISINS (R and AI Solutions for INferential Statistics) is an advanced, user-friendly online platform for statistical analysis, seamlessly integrating the power of R, Python, and Artificial Intelligence. Specially designed for agricultural research, RAISINS enables students, researchers, and professionals to perform complex analyses and generate publication-ready results without the need for software installation or coding expertise. Simply choose your analysis module, upload your dataset, and receive instant, insightful outputs. RAISINS supports individual users across the globe as well as institutions in India and abroad. This Computational Provenance and Reproducibility Record documents the statistical computing environment, software dependencies, computational provenance, and bibliographic references associated with the RAISINS Endogenous Switching Regression module. It is intended to support computational reproducibility and software transparency. Detailed statistical methodology, mathematical derivations, and user guidance are provided separately in the official module documentation. You can access the online cloud platform at https://www.raisins.live/

title: The Evolution of Biotechnology: Historical Discoveries, Major Milestones, and Recent Advances: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Biotechnology has evolved from ancient fermentation practices and the domestication of plants and animals into a multidisciplinary field that integrates molecular biology, genetics, engineering, and computational sciences.This review presents a comprehensive overview of the historical evolution of biotechnology, highlighting the major scientific discoveries, technological milestones, and recent advances that have shaped its development.Early contributions by Robert Hooke, Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, Louis Pasteur, Gregor Mendel, and Karl Ereky established the foundations of cell biology, microbiology, genetics, and industrial biotechnology.Subsequent breakthroughs, including the elucidation of the DNA double helix, recombinant DNA technology, recombinant human insulin, the Human Genome Project, and CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, revolutionized biological research and enabled transformative applications in medicine, agriculture, and industry.The review further discusses advances in genome engineering, viral and non-viral gene delivery systems, synthetic biology, regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, bioprinting, biofortification, cellular agriculture, and sustainable biomanufacturing

title: Trustworthy Explainable AI for Lettuce Growth Stage Prediction Using Sensor Data in Smart Agriculture
abstract: Background In precision agriculture, especially in hydroponic systems where environmental management affects both production and resource efficiency, interpretable modeling of crop phenological stages is crucial. Typical visualization-based approaches are generally expensive and ecologically dependent. To classify and visualize lettuce growth stages (Seedling, Vegetative Growth, Heading, Bolting and Senescence) using temperature, humidity, total dissolved solids (TDS) and pH, this study proposed XGB-StageVision, a sensor-powered machine learning setup combining supervised and unsupervised learning techniques. Using XG Boost, LightGBM, CatBoost, ExtraTrees, Random Forest and LSTM under an 80/20 train-test split, a dataset of 3,169 unique observations from 70 hydroponically grown lettuce plants was evaluated. Methods and Results XGB-StageVision achieved 99.86% test accuracy, a ROC AUC of 1.00, an MCC of 0.9982 and perfect precision, recall, F1 scores and specificity across all classes, performing competitively with the best baseline models, including LightGBM, which achieved statistically comparable cross validation performance. title: Artificial Intelligence for Environmental Sustainability and Climate Change Mitigation: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract Climate change and environmental degradation have emerged as two of the most pressing global challenges of the twenty-first century, threatening ecosystems, biodiversity, human health, and sustainable development. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed environmental research and management by enabling advanced data analytics, real-time monitoring, predictive modeling, and intelligent decision-support systems. This review critically examines the applications of AI in addressing environmental and climate-related challenges, including climate forecasting, air and water quality monitoring, biodiversity conservation, precision agriculture, renewable energy optimization, carbon emission assessment, waste management, and disaster risk reduction. Furthermore, The review also identifies current research gaps and highlights future opportunities for developing transparent, energy-efficient, and explainable AI systems that support evidence-based environmental decisionmaking. It concludes that AI has become a transformative tool for accelerating progress toward climate change mitigation, environmental sustainability, and the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Developme

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Rural Transformation
abstract: ABSTRACT Rural transformation - the multidimensional transition of demographic, economic, social, spatial, technological, environmental and institutional conditions in rural areas has traditionally been studied through periodic surveys, census decadal enumeration and retrospective mapping. This paper investigates whether artificial intelligence (AI) can fundamentally transform this analytical paradigm from retrospective description toward continuous, predictive and anticipatory spatio-temporal intelligence. Through a critical synthesis of the emerging GeoAI literature, analysis of primary Indian and international datasets, and development of an original conceptual framework-the AI-Enabled SpatioTemporal Rural Transformation Framework (AI-STRF) this paper argues that AI is not merely improving existing rural research techniques but may be creating a new paradigm of rural geographical analysis. The paper examines AI applications across demographic, agricultural, infrastructural, environmental and socioeconomic dimensions of rural change, identifies critical research gaps, and constructs evidence-based 2030-2050 future scenarios. title: From Endowments to Productivity: Brazil's Development Path to 2050
abstract: AbstractBrazil enters the second quarter of the twenty-first century with an unusual combination of constraints and opportunities. Its long-run economic performance has been marked by weak productivity growth, comparatively low investment, uneven human-capital formation, substantial informality, and persistent institutional and infrastructural frictions. At the same time, the country possesses a predominantly renewable electricity system, globally significant agricultural and mineral resources, established industrial capabilities, a large domestic market, and growing opportunities associated with artificial intelligence, digitalization, and the global transition toward low-carbon production. Three reports released in 2026 approach this conjunction from different analytical levels: Pereira da Silva et al.'s Brazil's Investment-Led Growth in the Ecological Transition, Roland Berger's Visao Brasil 2050, and McKinsey & Company's study of technology, AI, and advanced manufacturing. This article evaluates these reports jointly and subjects their major quantitative claims and causal propositions to independent evidence from official statistics and the scholarly literature. title: Artificial intelligence empowered NB-IoT systems: architectures, advances, and future perspectives
abstract: Abstract With an increasing number of devices being installed in agriculture, factories, hospitals, and cities, the need for intelligent, trustworthy, and energy-efficient communication systems is rising. This is one such system: Narrow Band Internet of Things, or NB-IoT, which connects devices at a long range with low-power consumption. But it also has a poor reaction time and is not adaptable to changing situations. This review discusses how artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML), deep learning, and other intelligent methods, are making NB-IoT more adaptable and predictive. By deploying lightweight AI models and edge computing—that is, processing locally on a device—systems are able to better manage wireless signals, save battery life, and improve overall performance. It also discusses several related real-world applications in the area of agriculture, healthcare, industry, and smart cities and achieves benefits such as saving water, early disease diagnosis, predictive machine maintenance, and environmental monitoring. The integration of AI with NB-IoT fosters digital solutions toward sustainability, security, and being human-centric. All the progress made

title: Agricultural Communication
abstract: Agricultural Communication: Advances in Agricultural Knowledge and Information Systems examines the transformative role of communication technologies in modern agriculture. It highlights the critical need for effective dissemination of agricultural knowledge and technologies to farmers, addressing the challenges posed by poor linkages between research and advisory services. The book explores the integration of indigenous technical knowledge (ITK) with advanced information and communication technologies (ICT) to empower farmers, enhance decision-making, and promote sustainable agricultural practices. Covering topics such as precision agriculture, drones, artificial intelligence, and mobile technology, it emphasizes the importance of timely and accurate information in overcoming market complexities, climate change, and resource constraints. Examines emerging trends such as robotics, AI, and precision farming, emphasizing their potential to revolutionize agriculture and address global challenges like climate change and food security. title: The Importance of Electronic Communication in the Use of Artificial Intelligence Programs and Applications in the Field of Smart Agriculture from the Point of View of Agricultural Extension Workers in Nineveh Governorate, Iraq
abstract: The study aimed to identify the level of importance of electronic communication among agricultural extension workers in using artificial intelligence (AI) programs and applications in the field of smart agriculture. It also aimed to identify the most frequently used electronic communication means by extension workers in employing AI programs and applications and rank them according to their relative importance; measure the contribution of electronic communication to improving extension workers' efficiency in using AI programs and applications in smart agriculture; identify individual differences in the importance of electronic communication and the use of AI applications according to selected independent variables, namely gender, educational qualification, years of service, training courses, level of Internet use, and willingness to use social networking sites concerning smart-agriculture technologies; and identify the obstacles facing extension workers in using AI applications in smart agriculture. title: Biomaterials for environmental control of AMR dissemination
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens human, animal, agricultural, and environmental health, driven by horizontal and vertical gene transfer. Conventional wastewater treatment removes 63-94% of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) but fails to eliminate ARGs and antibiotic-resistant bacteria, while generating toxic sludge. This review evaluates advanced biomaterials, including silver and gold nanoparticles, reactive oxygen species, magnetic nanocomposites, targeted disruption of metabolic pathways, carbon-based sorbents, biopolymers, metal-organic frameworks, functionalized enzymes/peptides, and engineered biofilms, for reducing ARG and resistant-bacteria loads, inhibiting horizontal gene transfer, and reducing the selective pressure exerted by residual antibiotics. These approaches offer enhanced performance across wastewater/agriculture/air/food supply chain systems. Challenges in scalability, ecological safety, and regulation remain, requiring integration with AI monitoring, CRISPR tools, and One Health strategies. Audio-Based Condition Monitoring for Agricultural Machinery: Stakeholder Needs, Adoption Barriers, and MVP Requirements
abstract: Failures of agricultural machinery are costly when breakdowns occur during narrow work windows and are discovered too late for planned service. Audio-based condition monitoring offers a low-cost retrofit sensing path because operators already treat abnormal sound as an informal diagnostic cue. Whether such systems are adopted, however, depends on how well they fit farm workflows, repair constraints, and stakeholder decision-making. This paper reports a stakeholder discovery study of audio-based condition monitoring for agricultural machinery. We synthesize semi-structured interviews with farm operators, dairy operators, dealership and service personnel, manufacturers, integrators, and domain experts, together with a short survey. Across sources, downtime avoidance emerged as the dominant value driver, and failures were most commonly recognized through unusual noise and loss of functionality. Survey responses further indicate a gap in maintenance visibility and low penetration of predictive tools. These findings narrow the opportunity from generic ``AI diagnosis'' to low-friction early warning and evidence generation for maintenance planning. Modern tractors appear to be a weaker in

title: The Role of Technology Spillovers and Economies of Size in the Efficient Design of Agricultural Research Systems
abstract: This paper reviews the efficient design of research systems-that is, the number, type. size, and location of research programs-—as functions of the potential for spillovers and spillins, and economies of size in research. Spillovers are found to be pervasive in agricultural technology generation, with greater potential for spillovers among biological technologies than previously believed. The paper also finds little empirical support for economies of size in producing varietal technologies. However, in a manifestation of the “small-country problem, market size are found to be critical in determining research efficiency”. The paper concludes with implications for policies to enhance research efficiency. For many types of research there is a strong case for central research programs ai the national, regional and international level whose mandate cuts across political boundaries to exploit agroecological similarities, and achieve economies of market size. However, innovative approaches are required to fund such programs.

title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1–3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4–10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2–6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11–15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. abstract: This thesis examines the economic efficiency of digitalizing the agro-industrial complex through the adoption of Smart Agriculture and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. The study analyzes indicators of resource efficiency, increased crop yields, and cost optimization achieved through the use of the Internet of Things (IoT), sensors, drones, and AI algorithms.

title: Agriculture 5.0: A Paradigm Shift Towards Intelligent and Sustainable Farming Systems - A Review
abstract: Agriculture has undergone a significant evolution, which progressing from manual and subsistence farming (Agriculture 1.0) to the high-tech interconnected systems of agriculture 5.0.Each phase of development reflects humanity's efforts to meet out the food requirements of a growing population and address environmental challenges through innovation.Agriculture 5.0 integrates advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain to optimize the productivity, sustainability and environmental stewardship.By leveraging precision tools like IoT-enabled sensors, remote sensing and big data analytics, it provides solutions to critical agricultural issues, including resource scarcity, climate change and food security.The adoption of robotics, variable rate technology (VRT) and smart irrigation ensures resource efficiency with minimum negative impacts on the environment.Despite its promise, Agriculture 5.0 faces challenges such as cybersecurity vulnerabilities and the technological adoption gap, requiring robust security measures, proactive policies and capacity building.This review explores the transition across different phases of agr

title: Design and Construction of Web-Based and Mobile Cattle Feed Management System and Cattle Health Monitoring System Using the Prototyping Method
abstract: Livestock management operations are often inefficient and error-prone because agricultural institutions frequently rely on manual recording of cattle feed and health data. This study aims to develop an integrated web and mobile information system for cattle feed management and health monitoring, implemented for the Herbal and Horticultural Science and Technology Park (TSTH2), Pollung, Humbang Hasundutan Regency, North Sumatra, Indonesia. The system was designed using a prototyping methodology through three iterative cycles, each involving stakeholder communication, rapid planning, design, modeling, prototype construction, and user evaluation. The resulting system includes 68 functional components: 24 for feed management and 44 for health monitoring. The web platform was implemented using React.js for the front end, with Express.js serving as the back end for the feed management subsystem and Django REST Framework for the health monitoring subsystem. In contrast, Flutter was used for the mobile platform of both subsystems. title: Citrus leaf pathology multi-class image dataset and a hybrid multi-branch attention fusion network for lemon leaf disease classification
abstract: Abstract The productivity of lemon (Citrus lemon) crops is severely undermined by foliar diseases, which constitute the leading cause of global harvest degradation. The conventional reliance on manual identification by experienced specialists poses a significant bottleneck, as these methods are both time-consuming and prone to human error under field conditions. Recently, deep learning techniques have been employed to identify and diagnose citrus foliar diseases from digital images, automating the classification process and providing non-experts with accessible diagnostic tools. While several deep learning applications have been used to classify lemon diseases with the aim of improving classification accuracy, most of these studies fail to achieve high accuracy and rely on datasets with an insufficient number of disease classes. In this paper, we introduced a dataset named “Citrus Leaf Pathology Multi-Class Image Dataset” with 14 different classes, and we proposed a Hybrid Multi-Branch Attention Fusion Network (HMAF-Net). title: White Paper on the Global Inclusive Natural‑Nutrition Module System — Reshaping the Paradigm of Global Food Security and Public Health (V9 Final Full Version)
abstract: This white paper presents an original, civilian-led top-level paradigm reconstruction for global food security and public health. It proposes a Global Inclusive Natural-Nutrition Module System based entirely on natural agricultural and livestock ingredients. The study addresses the long-standing global structural crises including disordered dietary structures, massive food waste, widespread diet-induced chronic diseases, overburdened healthcare systems, and nutritional inequity between rich and poor regions. The framework establishes a dual-track social operation model: medical systems for post-onset treatment and standardized nutrition modules for root-source prevention. It provides a complete, scalable, and implementable roadmap for global nutritional standardization, ecological pressure reduction, chronic disease prevention, and equitable public health governance. This work is an independent public-welfare conceptual deduction framework, containing no confidential data, no military-related content, and no AI-native generation. All core paradigms, logical architectures and innovation designs are independently conceived by the author.

title: Smart Agriculture Research in Date Palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) Production: A Comprehensive Bibliometric Study
abstract: The date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) is fundamental to food security, livelihoods, and agro-ecosystem sustainability across the Arabian Peninsula, yet its production is increasingly constrained by water scarcity, salinity, climate change, and biotic stresses. Smart agriculture technologies offer opportunities to improve crop monitoring, resource-use efficiency, and decision-making; however, their application in date palm production remains fragmented and insufficiently validated. This study evaluates the development, geographic distribution, technological focus, research approaches, and thematic structure of smart agriculture research on date palms in the Arabian Peninsula and other major date-producing countries. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using peer-reviewed English-language articles and reviews indexed in Scopus and Web of Science from 2016 to 2026, with 2026 representing a partial year. Following screening and duplicate removal, 164 published studies were retained. Publication output increased gradually, although the trend was not statistically significant (β = 1.25 articles year−1, p = 0.068; Mann–Kendall τ = 0.489, p = 0.060). title: AI is locking out Indigenous voices: Toward more equitable futures
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly helps communities make decisions related to healthcare, agriculture, education, and climate adaptation, yet most AI systems are built for people in connected, urban settings who speak dominant languages such as English. Indigenous and rural communities are often left out of the data, the model design, and the subsequent decisions that follow: a problem AI has not created, but has intensified. Using the Andes of Ecuador as a case in point, this commentary argues that this is a cyclical problem that is older than AI: where outside actors introduce a technology and decide how it will work without considering diverse cultures of people, often rural or Indigenous, who will use it. Unlike infrastructure projects such as a road or clinic which are commonly built in rural communities without prior consultation, commercial AI systems similarly are currently impacting communities but are controlled by distant companies, leaving community members with no clear local mechanism to contest or correct culturally inappropriate model outputs. title: Smart Crop Advisory System
abstract: The Smart Crop Advisory System is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform that uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies to assist farmers in making informed farming decisions. Traditional agriculture faces several challenges, including unsuitable crop selection, unpredictable weather conditions, crop diseases, and fluctuations in market prices. The proposed system integrates essential agricultural services, including crop recommendation, weather forecasting, crop disease detection, agricultural market price information, and an AI-based multilingual voice assistant. It also provides farmer profile management, crop price trend analysis, and rainfall trend visualization through an interactive dashboard. The crop recommendation module helps farmers identify suitable crops based on relevant agricultural parameters, while the disease detection module supports the identification of potential crop diseases. Weather and market information help farmers plan agricultural activities and make informed selling decisions. title: Promising Directions for Sorting Seeds of Various Crops: Improving Electric Field Methods and Integrating Them with Modern Sensor Technologies
abstract: Improving the germination capacity, purity, and uniformity of seed lots is a key task in seed production, yet pneumatic and mechanical sorting rely on only one or two physical traits, mass or size. This article reviews electric field sorting of agricultural seeds as an alternative that acts on several properties at once: mass, shape, density, electrical resistance, and dielectric permittivity. Published studies show that corona-discharge separation can improve seed purity and raise barley germination by 17.34%, and that an electrostatic separator can remove plastic film residue from seed cotton at up to 96.8% efficiency. Analysis of existing devices identifies a main limitation: electrode geometry is not matched to seed shape. To address this, a universal sorting device is proposed, with a polyethylene working body carrying screw-shaped channels and oppositely charged electrodes of triangular cross-section. Further directions are outlined: a hybrid electro-optical system combining electric field sorting with NIR/AI sensing, adaptive voltage control based on seed moisture, application to cotton seed cleaning, and sensor-based energy management. title: Large testing of AI-based camera traps on a forest defoliating pest in Europe
abstract: Background Recent advances in AI-based surveillance technologies have shifted agricultural pest monitoring from reactive to proactive, yet their application to forest pests remains limited despite the need for efficient monitoring across large, remote and difficult-to-access forest landscapes. The pine processionary moth, Thaumetopoea pityocampa , is one of the most damaging forest pests in the Mediterranean region and a species undergoing climate-driven distributional and phenological shifts. Methods We evaluated the performance of the AI-based camera system for monitoring the insect under field conditions. Automated traps were compared with conventional traps across four European countries (France, Italy, Portugal, and Slovenia), encompassing contrasting habitats and population densities. We assessed trapping efficiency, automated image recognition accuracy, probability of early detection, relationships between adult trap catch and local nest density, environmental drivers of flight activity, and non-target captures. title: Adaptability of Lightweight AI Models for Embedded Deployment: A Case Study of an Agricultural Monitoring Robot
abstract: Many artificial intelligence programs require powerful computing hardware, whereas agricultural robots, drones, and smart cameras rely on small embedded devices with limited computing power, battery capacity, and heat dissipation. Lightweight models reduce parameters and computational costs while maintaining acceptable accuracy, enabling AI deployment on resource-constraint network devices. This paper reviews key lightweighting methods, including compact network architectures, model pruning, model quantization, and knowledge distillation. It compares common platforms such as Jetson, Raspberry Pi, and microcontrollers. Using an agricultural monitoring robot as an example, this study proposes a system combining a camera, a lightweight YOLO model, Jetson, and a microcontroller for real-time crop monitoring. Experiments are designed to evaluate accuracy, speed, power consumption, temperature, and battery life. Rather than pursuing maximum model complexity, this paper focuses on explaining how to select a model that is truly suitable for the actual device. For agricultural robots, effective deployment requires sufficient accuracy, real-time performance, and low energy consumption.

title: Green blockchain frameworks for resource-constrained IoT systems
abstract: The explosive growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has allowed connecting everywhere in the healthcare, smart city, agriculture, and industry areas. Nevertheless, the rapid increase in the launch of IoT ecosystem presents essential issues of data privacy, security, trust, and interoperability. The potential of blockchain technology to solve the problem has become one of the prospects of this technology, as it is decentralized, immutable, and transparent. However, traditional blockchain systems tend to be energy-intensive and computationally intensive, which makes them inappropriate in resource-limited IoT devices with low processing power, storage, and battery capacity. To address this shortcoming green blockchain models have been put forward, with the aim of ensuring energy efficiency, scalability, and sustainability without compromising on the strong security guarantees. This chapter offers an in-depth discussion on energy-efficient blockchain paradigms optimized to be used in IoT systems. An AI Integration Framework for Social Innovation: A Cross-Case Analysis of AI System Configurations for the Triple-Zero Agenda
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly being applied to complex social and environmental challenges, but their implementation across different application domains requires appropriate combinations of computational techniques, data sources, deployment environments, user interfaces, and responsible-AI mechanisms. This study proposes an AI Integration Framework for examining and configuring AI-enabled social innovation systems in support of the Triple-Zero Agenda: zero poverty, zero unemployment, and zero net carbon emissions. The framework is derived from a qualitative multi-case analysis of five social enterprises operating in agriculture, healthcare, education, clean energy, and employment. The analysis examines the AI technologies employed, their development and deployment environments, accessibility mechanisms, data-collection approaches, privacy mechanisms, explainability practices, human-in-the-loop controls, ethical review mechanisms, and measurable impact indicators. The cases demonstrate the use of heterogeneous AI configurations, including predictive machine learning in mobile and cloud environments, natural language processing in application and SMS-based sy

title: How Underdog Brand Biography Mitigates Consumer Skepticism Toward AIGC: Evidence from AI-Generated Agricultural-Product Advertisements
abstract: While AIGC can improve operational efficiency in marketing, it may also erode consumer trust owing to widespread skepticism toward AIGC. Therefore, this study examines agricultural product advertisements to explore the impact of Underdog Brand Biography (UBB) disclosure on consumers’ purchase intentions. It also investigates the mediating roles of cognitive trust and affective trust, as well as whether these effects differ across product-price levels and production-background conditions. We conducted three experiments to investigate these relationships. The data were analyzed using t-tests, analyses of variance, and moderated mediation models. The findings indicated that UBB disclosure significantly increases purchase intention and that this effect is mediated by both cognitive trust and affective trust. The indirect effects via both pathways differed across product-price levels: both were significant in the high-price condition, whereas in the low-price condition only the affective pathway remained significant.
