title: "AgriSense AI \u2014 Hybrid Sequential Plant-Stress Dataset"
abstract: "This dataset was developed to support a hybrid deep learning research project on early, image-and-sensor-based plant stress classification. It combines real leaf photographs drawn from the public PlantVillage Plant Disease Classification corpus with a purpose-built, reproducibly generated sequential dataset that assigns those images to simulated plant timelines and pairs each timeline with four-channel environmental telemetry (soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and light intensity). Unlike a plain single-source image download, this is a genuinely combined, multimodal resource: real visual disease evidence joined with structured temporal context, organized for training and evaluating CNN+LSTM\/GRU sequence-fusion architectures under a leakage-safe, plant-level train\/validation\/test split. It supports research on multimodal plant-stress severity staging, modality-fusion design, and calibrated (confidence-aware) classification, and is intended as a reference resource for researchers and students working on agricultural computer vision, sensor-fusion deep learning, and precision-agriculture decision support."

title: Introduction AI, Renewable Energy, and the Path to Sustainable Intelligent Societies
abstract: The convergence of renewable energy technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) is redefining pathways toward sustainable and intelligent societies. This chapter highlights the urgency of renewable energy adoption in the context of climate change and digital transformation, tracing the parallel evolution of AI, automation, and clean energy from emerging concepts to global priorities. It outlines the foundations of intelligent, sustainable societies, including smart grids, data infrastructures, and digital governance models. The chapter emphasizes the mutually reinforcing relationship in which AI enhances energy generation, storage, and distribution, while renewable sources support expanding computational demands. Applications span smart cities, agriculture, healthcare, and industry. Policy, ethical considerations, and alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goals are examined, along with technical, socio-economic, and geopolitical challenges and future research directions toward equitable and resilient sustainable societies by 2050.

title: YOLO-Based Leaf Disease Detection in Smart Agriculture: Evolution, Task Adaptation, and Deployment Challenges
abstract: Computer vision-based leaf disease detection has become an important technical approach in smart agriculture and agricultural inspection services. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning have provided effective solutions for automated leaf disease monitoring, and You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based detectors have attracted increasing attention for balancing detection accuracy and inference speed. However, leaf disease detection remains challenging because lesions often occupy small regions, exhibit subtle visual features, have blurred boundaries, and appear against complex backgrounds, with considerable variation under field conditions. To address these challenges, numerous studies have improved lightweight backbones, feature fusion mechanisms, attention modules, detection heads, loss functions, and training strategies. This critical narrative review examines YOLO-based leaf disease detection, organizing reported adaptations by task characteristics and interpreting their outcomes in relation to datasets, annotations, and evaluation conditions. title: Multistage AI Crop Inspection and Segmentation Framework (MACISF)
abstract: Abstract Crop quality assessment is one of the most critical components of modern agriculture, which directly influences yield optimization, post-harvest management, and food security. Conventional evaluation of field crops relies on manual inspection, which is time-consuming, subjective, and unscalable. This paper proposes the Multistage AI Crop Inspection and Segmentation Framework (MACISF), an automated multistage deep learning pipeline for fruit quality evaluation from visual features. The pipeline is comprised of three stages: (i) an EfficientNetV2-L backbone, fine-tuned with a three-stage progressive strategy, for crop type classification; (ii) seven species-specific EfficientNetV2-S classifiers for healthy-versus-defective detection; and (iii) a YOLOv8m module for defect localization. Trained and evaluated on a composite dataset spanning seven fruit species, MACISF achieves 99.23% crop type accuracy (macro F1-score 99.23%, macro AUC-ROC 0.993), 99.39% mean health state accuracy with 99.51% mean defective-class recall, and a projected grading mAP@0.5 of 92.3%. title: AI-DRIVEN OPTIMIZATION OF A SMARTPHONE-BASED COLORIMETRIC METHOD FOR SIMULTANEOUS DETERMINATION OF MULTIPLE HEAVY METAL IONS IN ENVIRONMENTAL WATER OF BABIL GOVERNORATE, IRAQ
abstract: Copper, lead, cadmium, mercury, chromium, zinc and nickel reach rivers, irrigation canals and groundwater from industrial effluents, agricultural drainage, urban wastewater and corroding distribution pipes, and several of them are harmful at microgram-per-litre levels. Their routine determination still depends on atomic absorption and inductively coupled plasma instruments, which are expensive, need trained operators and are rarely available near the sampling site. This research plan describes a low-cost method in which a six-reagent chromogenic array (4-(2-pyridylazo)resorcinol, Zincon, micellar dithizone, 1,5-diphenylcarbazide, dimethylglyoxime and xylenol orange) is prepared in a 96-well microplate and photographed with a smartphone inside a closed enclosure with controlled LED lighting. Color values will be extracted from every well in the RGB, HSV, HSL and CIELAB spaces after correction against a reference card. Reaction pH, reagent concentration, reaction time and sample volume will be screened with a Box–Behnken design and refined by Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization. title: Toward Resilient Rural Resource Governance: A Cost-Effective, Data-Driven IoT System for Sustainable Beehive Monitoring and Management
abstract: Beekeeping occupies a challenging intersection: it is economically vital across vast, under-served rural areas, yet the tools available to manage it rarely match that scale. This paper presents a low-cost, solar-powered IoT system designed to address this gap. Rather than treating beehive management as a narrow agricultural concern, the system frames it as a case study in distributed, data-driven resource governance. Each hive is fitted with an ESP32-based sensor node that tracks temperature, humidity, and equivalent CO2 (eCO2), while solar-powered base stations provide GPS positioning and intrusion detection. All components are connected through a tiered wireless architecture: a 100 m 2.4 GHz RF sensor link connects individual hive nodes to solar-powered base stations, which forward aggregated telemetry to the cloud over a 120 m Wi-Fi or cellular uplink. The system was evaluated in an active apiary across five hives and two solar-powered base stations, which operated continuously for two weeks without failure, including during periods of darkness. title: Sustainable Agriculture and Food Security
abstract: Agriculture and food security are central to sustainable development in Bangladesh and South Asia, where millions of smallholder farmers depend on agriculture for their livelihoods and where food systems face increasing pressures from climate change, natural resource degradation, population growth, market volatility, and changing dietary needs. Ensuring long-term food and nutrition security requires a transition towards agricultural systems that are productive, resource-efficient, climate-resilient, inclusive, and environmentally sustainable. Sustainable Agriculture and Food Security examines the interconnected dimensions of sustainable agriculture and resilient food systems, with particular emphasis on Bangladesh and relevant experiences across South Asia. The book explores climate-smart agriculture, agroecological approaches, soil health, sustainable water management, efficient irrigation, biodiversity conservation, circular agriculture, and environmentally responsible farming practices. title: Ontologies in Precision Agriculture—A brief Survey on Reproducibility
abstract: Combined with machine learning techniques, ontologies have recently been applied widely to enhance decision-making, reasoning, knowledge management and representation, and information retrieval in various domains. Likewise, the popularity of ontologies is increasing in the rapidly evolving field of precision agriculture due to the ability to encode general domain knowledge and specialized knowledge of farmers and utilize it within data processing and analytics pipelines. Although the research on ontologies applied to precision agriculture problems is increasing, adopting published solutions is rather cumbersome, mainly due to low reproducibility of these works. This article is intended to survey the current applied research in ontologies within the agricultural domain, by investigating the used methodologies, technologies and evaluation approaches, the availability of the data, ontologies and source codes developed. It was found that the used data sources, the developed ontologies and the developed source codes are available only in 14%, 9% and 7%, respectively, of the selected 85 articles. title: Deep chemometrics for retrospective auditing of the water-nutrient nexus in olive oil via 1D-CNN and explainable AI
GREEN TECH PARADOX An Analysis of AI in Environment Sustainability
abstract: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into environmental sustainability strategies presents a critical dilemma known as the "Green Tech Paradox." While AI offers unprecedented capabilities to optimize resource allocation, predict climate patterns, and enhance energy efficiency across industrial sectors, its deployment carries substantial, often overlooked, ecological costs. This research provides a critical analysis of the dual role AI plays as both a catalyst for eco-innovations and a significant contributor to environmental degradation. On the positive frontier, AI-driven applications accelerate sustainability by enabling smart power grids, improving carbon capture systems, facilitating precision agriculture, and modeling complex environmental crises. Machine learning algorithms enhance operational efficiency, reducing waste and carbon footprints in manufacturing and logistics. However, these beneficial outcomes are counterbalanced by the escalating physical footprint of AI infrastructure. title: IoT-Enabled Autonomous Agriculture Monitoring Rover for Smart Farming: A Comprehensive Literature Review
abstract: The rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT), autonomous robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), embedded systems, wireless communication, and precision agriculture has created new opportunities for improving agricultural productivity and resource utilization. Conventional agricultural monitoring relies extensively on manual field inspection, which is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and often unable to provide continuous information about crop and soil conditions. Autonomous agricultural rovers provide an alternative approach by enabling mobile sensing, real-time environmental monitoring, crop observation, navigation, and precision agricultural operations. This paper presents a comprehensive literature review of IoT-enabled autonomous agricultural rovers for smart farming, with particular emphasis on recent developments reported in IEEE literature. Existing research is analyzed according to rover architecture, sensing technologies, navigation techniques, communication technologies, IoT platforms, agricultural applications, AI integration, and autonomy levels. title: An Agricultural Skid-Steering Robot for Tomato Leaf Disease Detection and Targeted Pesticide Spraying: An Updated Prototype and Current Technology
abstract: Agricultural workers may be exposed to pesticides during conventional crop-protection operations, while timely identification of leaf diseases remains important for effective crop management. This paper presents an updated discussion of an agricultural skid-steering robot originally developed for tomato-leaf disease identification and targeted pesticide spraying. The prototype combines a four-wheel skid-steering platform, ultrasonic sensing, an MPU6050 inertial sensor, Arduino Nano control, ZigBee communication, MATLAB-based image processing, K-means clustering and an artificial neural network (ANN) classifier. Tomato-leaf images representing healthy leaves, bacterial spot, early blight, late blight and leaf mold are processed through image acquisition, preprocessing, colour-space transformation, clustering, segmentation, feature extraction and classification. The detected disease condition is then communicated to the robot controller, which activates the pump for the corresponding programmed spraying interval. title: Climate Risk Assessment and Vulnerability Mapping in Border Regions
abstract: Border regions are especially vulnerable to climate change because they commonly combine socioeconomic gaps, environmental dangers, international resource demands, and geopolitical tensions. This chapter discusses border climate risk assessment and vulnerability mapping approaches, ideas, and frameworks. The book covers climatic data analytics, remote sensing, GIS, machine learning, susceptibility indicators, risk modelling, hazard identification, and exposure analysis. Transboundary water management, climate-induced migration monitoring, infrastructure development, disaster risk mitigation, and agricultural resilience are covered in this chapter. We also address data accessibility, government coordination, and international collaboration. Digital twins, climate intelligence systems, and AI-powered predictive vulnerability assessments are prioritised. Vulnerability mapping and climate risk assessment can improve adaptive capacity, sustainable development, and resilience in environmentally and politically sensitive border regions.

title: Wild boar collision data and satellite computer vision refine habitat suitability mapping across France
abstract: Abstract Wild boar (Sus scrofa) populations have expanded rapidly across Europe, leading to escalating human-wildlife conflicts (HWCs), notably wildlife-vehicle collisions (WVCs), increased agricultural damage and disease transmission. In continental France these issues are compounded by the species’ ecological adaptability exhibiting increasing overlaps with urbanization and transportation networks. In this study, we leverage time-series environmental data, computer vision and Species Distribution Modeling (SDM) to predict wild boar habitat suitability and investigate its spatiotemporal drivers. We use presence-only data from WVC reports on the national railway and road networks, along with publicly available GBIF observation collections, as complementary occurrence streams in our SDMs, while addressing inherent sampling biases of these datasets with tailored corrections. A key innovation of this study is the integration of national scale, annually updated high-resolution land cover predictors explicitly focused on wild boar resource preference. title: Using AI-powered modelling for drought forecasting in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea
abstract: Context The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is vulnerable to drought due to monsoon-driven variable precipitation that affects agricultural production and water security. Reliable multi-timescale drought forecasting aids risk mitigation; however, nonlinear non-stationary drought signals are hard to capture indata-scarce regions. Aims This study developed and validated a Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise-Long Short-Term Memory (CEEMDAN-LSTM) hybrid Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) drought forecasting model. Its performance is systematically compared against a standalone LSTM for multiple SPEI timescales under DPRK climatic conditions. Methods Monthly meteorological records from 10 stations collected over a period of 60 years were used to derive SPEI time series. CEEMDAN decomposed SPEI into intrinsic mode functions for noise reduction and trend extraction as LSTM inputs; hyperparameters were optimised by Bayesian optimisation. title: The innovative application of plasma technology in food and medicine homology resources
abstract: Abstract Food and medicine homology resources are increasingly constrained by climate-driven production instability, chemical-residue control, postharvest deterioration, and the demand for function-oriented products. Low-temperature plasma (LTP), also referred to in the literature as cold plasma or non-thermal plasma, is a non-equilibrium physical technology that generates reactive oxygen species (ROS), reactive nitrogen species (RNS), charged particles, electric fields, and ultraviolet (UV) photons under ambient or near-ambient bulk-temperature conditions. This review establishes an end-to-end LTP application framework for plant-, animal-, and microbial-derived food and medicine homology resources. Different from single-sector reviews, the present framework distinguishes substrate-specific regulatory logic across the whole value chain. In plant-derived resources, LTP mainly acts through physical signal-mediated stress priming, secondary metabolism regulation, microbiome modulation, postharvest quality maintenance, detoxification, sensory improvement, and waste valorization. title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Advancing Biotechnology: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Abstract - The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and biotechnology is revolutionizing scientific research, healthcare, and industrial applications. This paper examines how AI techniques, like computer vision, machine learning, deep learning, and NLP, are revolutionizing important biotechnology fields like drug discovery, genomics, personalized medicine, agricultural innovation, and industrial bioprocessing. AI enables faster data analysis, accurate prediction of biological behaviors, and automation of complex tasks, significantly accelerating the pace of innovation. We also discuss commonly used AI tools in biotechnology and highlight the growth of AI-driven biotech startups. The incorporation of AI presents a number of obstacles despite its transformative potential, such as the requirement for transparent algorithms, ethical issues, and data privacy concerns. The goal of the article is to provide a thorough review of the state of affairs, recent developments, and potential future progress in the nexus of biotechnology and artificial intelligence.

title: AI-Driven Optimization of Sustainable Soil Stabilization: A Kernel Learning Approach for Makuba-Treated Lateritic Pavements
abstract: The stabilization of lateritic soils using agricultural waste materials, such as locust bean pod ash (LBPA) locally known as "Makuba" presents a sustainable alternative for improving pavement subgrades. However, predicting optimal stabilizer dosage and geotechnical performance remains challenging due to complex nonlinear interactions between soil composition, stabilizer chemistry, and compaction conditions. This preliminary proof-of-concept study develops a physics-guided, stabilization-anchored kernel machine learning framework to predict unconfined compressive strength (UCS), California bearing ratio (CBR), and plasticity index (PI) of Makuba-stabilized lateritic soil. The approach integrates experimental data (six mix proportions: 0–12% Makuba) with material science principles through a stabilization-anchored feature set incorporating clay fraction, linear shrinkage, CaO, and SiO₂ content. Three kernel regression models Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) were implemented with hyperparameters optimized via grouped 5-fold cross-validation to prevent data leakage. Results demonstrate that GPR with stabilization-anch

title: How Reliable Are Large Language Models for Soil Organic Carbon Assessment? An Australian Benchmark
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is an indicator of agricultural soil condition and carbon storage, but numerical outputs from large language models (LLMs) require validation before use in monitoring or management. We evaluated seven general-purpose LLM configurations on three direct-response tasks: estimating 0--10 cm SOC concentrations for 308 Australian paddocks under two information conditions, calculating SOC stock in 120 matched scenarios, and comparing 300 paddock pairs. References were measured SOC records or deterministic calculations; response validity, repeated-call dispersion and estimated API cost were assessed separately. Additional measured soil attributes reduced concentration mean absolute error by 13--62\% across configurations, although high-SOC underprediction and paddock-specific errors persisted. Six configurations were highly accurate in stock calculations using equation-native units without coarse fragments, but accuracy declined with physically equivalent alternative units. Pairwise accuracy was 90.5--94.6\% overall and 59.1--70.9\% for 52 closely separated pairs; some configurations were sensitive to presentation order. Nearly all outputs were parseable, without

title: Integrating Weather and Potato Price Market Data into AI-Driven Hybrid Models for Climate-Smart Agricultural Forecasting
White Paper on the Global Inclusive Natural‑Nutrition Module System — Reshaping the Paradigm of Global Food Security and Public Health (V1Final Full Version)
abstract: This white paper presents an original, civilian-led top-level paradigm reconstruction for global food security and public health. It proposes a Global Inclusive Natural-Nutrition Module System based entirely on natural agricultural and livestock ingredients. The study addresses the long-standing global structural crises including disordered dietary structures, massive food waste, widespread diet-induced chronic diseases, overburdened healthcare systems, and nutritional inequity between rich and poor regions. The framework establishes a dual-track social operation model: medical systems for post-onset treatment and standardized nutrition modules for root-source prevention. It provides a complete, scalable, and implementable roadmap for global nutritional standardization, ecological pressure reduction, chronic disease prevention, and equitable public health governance. This work is an independent public-welfare conceptual deduction framework, containing no confidential data, no military-related content, and no AI-native generation. All core paradigms, logical architectures and innovation designs are independently conceived by the author.

title: Evaluating Approaches for Identifying and Classifying Plant Diseases
abstract: Plant diseases are caused by a wide range of microorganisms, including fungi, viruses, bacteria, mycoplasmas, and nematodes. Among these, major plant-pathogenic microbes are responsible for significant crop losses, leading to both direct and indirect economic damage. In the context of global climate change and the increasing virulence of newly emerged transboundary pathogens, traditional agricultural practices, such as the repeated use of the same crop varieties, reliance on the same plant protection chemicals, and the import/export of planting materials, have become increasingly vulnerable. Early detection, accurate diagnosis, and proper identification of disease-causing microorganisms are therefore critical for enhancing annual crop productivity. This chapter highlights various methods for plant disease detection and classification, encompassing traditional techniques such as visual inspection, microscopy, nucleic acid-based methods [e.g., polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and gene sequencing], and serology-based approaches [e.g., enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), dot immunobinding assay (DIBA), tissue blot immunoassay (TIBA), and immunosorbent electron microscopy (ISEM)],

title: Advances in Precision Agriculture Using AI
abstract: Precision agriculture (PA) is revolutionizing modern farming by integrating advanced digital technologies to optimize agricultural productivity, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. The infusion of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms, has further transformed PA, enabling real-time decision-making, predictive analytics, and automation across the agricultural value chain. This chapter presents an in-depth overview of the core technologies that underpin AI-driven PA, including ML techniques, deep neural networks, Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, blockchain, and remote sensing. Further, this chapter explores how these technologies converge to support critical agricultural applications such as precision sowing, smart spraying, harvest optimization, pest and disease control, and crop health monitoring. Further, interoperability standards and the need for cohesive data frameworks are examined to ensure seamless integration of diverse PA tools. Challenges related to adoption, cost, data governance, algorithmic bias, and geospatial disparities are discussed, along with strategies for equitable technolo

title: Transforming Agriculture through Emerging Technologies for Sustainable Productivity
abstract: The convergence of robotics and precision agriculture (PA) marks a transformative shift in modern farming practices aimed at enhancing productivity and ensuring long-term sustainability. This chapter explores the integration of advanced robotic systems into agricultural operations to address critical challenges such as labor shortages, resource inefficiency, and environmental degradation. It provides an in-depth analysis of various robotic applications, ranging from autonomous tractors, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) (drones), and robotic arms to artificial intelligence (AI)-driven monitoring systems that contribute to site-specific crop management, precision irrigation, pesticide application, and harvesting. The chapter emphasizes how robotics, when combined with sensor technologies, data analytics, and machine learning (ML), enables real-time decision-making and optimized farm management. Furthermore, it discusses the socio-economic and environmental benefits of adopting robotic solutions, along with the barriers to implementation and future research directions. By offering a comprehensive overview, this chapter aims to serve as a foundational reference for researchers, practiti

title: Integrating Rice Husk Ash- Material Science and Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Cementitious Material Design
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable and low-carbon construction materials has intensified research into supplementary cementitious materials derived from agricultural residues. Rice husk ash (RHA), owing to its high amorphous silica content, pozzolanic activity, porous morphology, and potential to reduce Portland cement consumption, represents a promising alternative for developing sustainable cementitious composites. Nevertheless, the engineering performance of RHA-based mixtures is governed by multiple interacting factors, including ash composition and reactivity, burning conditions, particle size, replacement ratio, water-to-binder ratio, curing regime, mixture proportions, and environmental exposure. The nonlinear interactions among these variables make conventional experimental optimization costly, labor-intensive, and difficult to generalize. Demand for low-carbon materials has increased interest in Rice Husk Ash (RHA) as SCM due to its high amorphous silica, pozzolanic activity and cement-saving potential. However, RHA performance depends on many interacting factors - burning conditions, particle size, replacement %, w/b, curing and exposure - making trial-and-error optimi

title: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Framework for Paddy Leaf Disease Detection Using an Enhanced Pretrained Novel EfficientNet-Lite4 Model
abstract: The correct and prompt detection of leaf diseases in paddy crops remains essential for protecting agricultural output and yield stability and reducing major losses that occur during severe disease outbreaks. The widespread use of conventional centralized machine learning techniques becomes impractical for real-world agricultural applications, as their effectiveness diminishes under three main conditions: data privacy limitations, delayed transmission of information, along with reduced performance accuracy from non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data properties across different agro-climatic regions. This research develops a decentralized diagnostic system which combines Federated Learning with an Enhanced Pretrained Novel EfficientNet-Lite4 model designed for paddy leaf disease classification. The Paddy Doctor dataset served as training material for the system which contained 16,225 RGB images that classified 12 disease types alongside healthy categories. The proposed model reached 98.7% classification accuracy and 98.5% precision and 98.6% F1-score while maintaining a final loss of 0.21 after 100 communication rounds. The system underwent field testing which dem

title: Data Management and Integration in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Precision agriculture (PA) leverages modern technologies to enhance productivity, optimize resource use, and reduce environmental impact. Efficient data management and integration play a critical role in PA, as large volumes of data are generated through Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS), and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analytics. This chapter explores various methodologies used to manage, integrate, and utilize agricultural data effectively, emphasizing cloud computing, blockchain, and decision support systems (DSS). We discuss the challenges and future directions of data-driven agriculture to promote sustainability and efficiency. In recent years, a wide range of technologies has been integrated into PA to enhance crop monitoring and management. These advancements aim to improve sustainability while maximizing yield and quality. However, many available technologies and standards have yet to be fully incorporated into these practices. As a result, the potential synergy between breeding and agronomic expertise, electronics, and computing has not been entirely realized. Emerging and established technologies, such as the In

title: Reconciling the Discordance Between Human Privacy and AI Systems
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has had a gradual advent ever since the inception of technology. On one hand, it is providing for extensive forums for making life easier by saving time and human labour through development of leading-edge systems and technological arrangement, while on the other hand, it is posing boundless perils to humankind and all that it values as private. Once considered as the exclusive territory of human control, tasks including writing, research, communication, identity verification, education, agriculture, stock market trading, even life planning, among a plethora of other domains now stand transferred to the ambit of AI systems. Through such immersion, AI has, to an extent, led to emancipation from human co-dependency. Yet a balanced synchronicity of humanity and AI systems is under question. The recent trends of Deepfake, Studio Ghibli Art, voice cloning, photograph morphing, AI-generated influencers, emotional AI chatbots, even AI impersonation of deceased individuals, et alia , has introduced a constellation of unprecedented threats to human dignity and legal rights. This encroachment by AI systems is visibly shaking the fundamental human rights which saf

title: Comparative Deep Learning and RISE-Based Explainable AI Framework for Orange Fruit Disease Detection
abstract: Orange diseases significantly threaten fruit quality and agricultural productivity, resulting in substantial economic losses. Traditional diagnostic methods are limited by their labor-intensive nature, high costs, and reliance on subjective expert evaluation, increasing the demand for automated solutions. This study systematically compared three state-of the-art deep learning architectures-EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16)-on the Orange Fruit dataset, which comprises healthy, citrus canker, and melanose samples. To enhance generalization and mitigate overfitting, transfer learning with ImageNet pretraining was combined with advanced data augmentation strategies like Mixup and Cutout. Experimental results demonstrated that the ConvNeXt-Tiny architecture, supported by these techniques, achieved superior performance, reaching 98.76% Accuracy, 99% F1-Score, and 99.95% ROC-AUC. Beyond numerical metrics, model transparency was investigated using Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). The study evaluated the widely used Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) method alongside Randomized Input Sampling for Explanation (RISE), which, to the

title: Precision Agriculture
abstract: Precision agriculture (PA) is transforming traditional farming practices through the application of modern technologies, including geographic information systems (GIS), artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and automation. These tools allow site-specific crop management by monitoring soil conditions and crop health in realtime. The adoptionof PA improves productivity and promotes the efficient use of agricultural resources, thereby supporting sustainability. This chapter explores how PA has changed over time and discusses the core methodologies and practical applications. It places particular emphasis on the economic and environmental impacts of these technologies. Additionally, the challenges, such as high initial investment costs, limited technical knowledge, and infrastructure deficiencies in developing countries that hinder the adoption of PA are emphasized. Future directions and case studies are also discussed, offering practical knowledge for policymakers, researchers, and practitioners. As PA continues to evolve, it has the potential to address global food security challenges and promote sustainable farming practices in the context of climate change and concerns about reso

title: Role of AI and Robotics in Germplasm Collection and Conservation
abstract: Germplasm collection and conservation are vital for securing agricultural biodiversity and ensuring future food security. Traditional methods, however, face challenges such as human error, inefficiencies, and the risk of genetic erosion. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics offers innovative solutions to enhance these processes. AI can automate germplasm identification, improve data management, and enable predictive analytics for storage optimization. Robotics can streamline seed sorting, viability testing, cryopreservation, and sample retrieval/distribution. Major genebanks like the Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research (CGIAR), the Svalbard Global Seed Vault (SGSV), and national/regional repositories play a crucial role in conservation efforts. Future prospects involve advancements in AI-driven conservation techniques, although ethical and logistical challenges must be addressed. In the end, robots and AI have the ability to completely transform germplasm management, guaranteeing the long-term preservation of plant genetic resources.

title: Automation in Precision Agriculture
abstract: The global demand for food production is intensifying owing to rapid population growth, climate variability, and the finite availability of arable land. In response, precision agriculture (PA) has led to a major transformation, enabling farmers to optimize inputs and outputs with unprecedented accuracy. At the core of this evolution is automation, which isdriven by advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, the Internet of Things (IoT), machine vision, and data analytics. This chapter explored the critical role of automation in enhancing the efficiency, sustainability, and precision of modern farming practices. It takes a close look at today’s most advanced farming tools, from driverless tractors and robotic harvesters to drones that monitor crops and AI systems that help make smart decisions. It also explores how all these technologies are coming together to form a connected, digital approach to agriculture. The discussion highlights how smart automation helps farmers make better predictions about crop yields and use resources more efficiently. Just as importantly, it supports environmental health by cutting down on waste and reducing the excessive use of fertilizers

title: Smart Farming with AI
abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in agriculture is reshaping conventional farming into a more intelligent, efficient, and sustainable endeavor. This chapter explores the transformative impact of AI technologies, particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and computer vision, on critical areas such as crop health monitoring, plant breeding, soil and water management, and precision agriculture (PA). AI-driven systems enable early detection of crop diseases and stresses, optimized irrigation, resource-efficient fertilization, and advanced trait prediction for plant breeding, thereby enhancing productivity and resilience. Enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT), drones, satellite imagery, and sensor networks, AI facilitates real-time decision-making and automation across the agricultural landscape. The chapter also highlights enabling technologies like robotics, autonomous machinery, and agricultural data platforms, along with recent innovations and global case studies that illustrate AI’s growing role in diverse agri-ecosystems. Despite ongoing challenges such as data privacy, model refinement, and adoption costs, AI offers immense potential to revolu

title: USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DESIGNING ROBOTIC MODELS USING ENGINEERING GRAPHICS
abstract: The article examines the possibilities of using generative artificial intelligence in teaching the discipline “Engineering and Computer Graphics” in the design of robotic models for the processing industry. The feasibility of integrating generative artificial intelligence models into the design process of robotic systems as a means of developing spatial thinking, graphic competence, design skills, and digital skills of agricultural university students is substantiated. It is established that modern generative systems (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, Claude, DALL·E, etc.) support all stages of educational design, from developing technical specifications and generating product concepts to creating drawings and three-dimensional models, visualizing designs, preparing technical documentation, and analyzing possible design solutions. A methodology for using generative artificial intelligence in the educational project “Design of a Robotic Manipulator” is proposed. The methodology is based on the principles of project-based learning, STEM education, the competency-based approach, and the use of CAD systems. A structural model for integrating generative artificial intelligence into th

title: Innovative Approaches and Emerging Trends in Sensing and Monitoring Systems for Smart Agriculture
abstract: The agricultural sector is undergoing a paradigm shift driven by the integration of advanced sensing and monitoring technologies that enable precise, data-informed decision-making. This chapter explores innovative approaches and emerging trends in Smart Agriculture, focusing on how cutting-edge technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), wireless sensor networks, remote sensing, artificial intelligence (AI), and big data analytics are revolutionizing conventional farming practices. By enabling real-time monitoring of soil health, crop conditions, environmental factors, and livestock behavior, these systems significantly enhance agricultural productivity, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. The chapter highlights key applications, architectures, and case studies that demonstrate the transformative potential of technology-driven agriculture. It also addresses the challenges related to scalability, affordability, interoperability, and rural connectivity, offering insights into future research directions. This comprehensive overview serves as a valuable resource for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers seeking to harness digital innovations for a more

title: Federated Learning and Transformer Model‐Based Hybrid AI Model for Predicting Crop Yields
abstract: Timely and efficient management of agricultural practices and subsequently predicting crop yields are fundamental elements in the quest to mitigate global food insecurity. Conventional sampling and secondary historical records, which are usually relied upon, tend to be inaccurate and inflexible to current trends. This paper proposes a hybrid artificial intelligence model that aims to achieve higher prediction accuracy with the aid of USDA Crop Scape data. We rely on a Federated Learning (FL) framework, which allows for different nodes in the network to work together to construct a common model without the need to transfer any training data to the nodes. After federated training, Transformer-based NLP technologies were used to process and fuse unstructured data (weather reports) and structured data (soil properties) typologically into one format, taking into account long-range contextual relations and enhancing the information content of the model. This multicenter multimedia architecture presented a significant advantage over the traditional approaches by integrating spatial and text data in an optimal way. Afterwards, a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA) was employed to opti

title: Enhanced crop yield estimation in smart agriculture via AI and IoT using the GODL geo-optimized algorithm
abstract: Abstract Precision agriculture is one of the major breakthroughs which has been adopted to counteract some of the major challenges facing contemporary agriculture, such as maximizing crop yield, maximizing resource efficiency, and sustainability. The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) technologies can go a long way in enhancing crop yield prediction through data obtained from multiple sources, including satellite images, ground sensors, and weather stations. This research paper proposes a next-generation crop yield prediction system called Geo-Optimized Deep Learning (GODL) algorithm. The GODL algorithm integrates geospatial information with deep learning algorithms for crop yield analysis and prediction. This combination of deep learning and geospatial data allows accurate and scalable crop yield predictions using geospatial and sensor information. In order to ensure model optimization in terms of accuracy and efficiency, the GODL Algorithm makes use of advanced hyperparameter optimization methods that include Adam and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). The research paper highlights the efficiency of the GODL Algorithm by conducting extens

title: Smart water management in agriculture: convergence of sensors, imaging, AI, precision irrigation, and robotics systems
abstract: Agricultural irrigation systems can bear the heavy losses of water through runoff, evaporation, and deep percolation. Crop water requirements vary with crop species, growth stage, soil properties, evapotranspiration, weather, and plant water status; therefore, irrigation scheduling based on a single parameter is insufficient. Conventional water management systems often rely on uniform application, fixed scheduling, and limited real-time information, which overlooks spatial and temporal variation in soil, crop, and weather conditions and can result in water loss, over-irrigation, and under-irrigation. This review highlights studies on the integration of AI-driven sensing and imaging technologies, IoT-based precision irrigation, variable-rate technologies, digital twins, and agricultural robotics for crop water management. These approaches integrate field, crop, weather, and spatial information to support water-demand assessment, crop-stress monitoring, irrigation scheduling, site-specific application, and automated water management. The reviewed studies report water savings, improved water-use efficiency, crop performance, and more site-specific irrigation and input application acro

title: Artificial Intelligence in Agricultural Extension and Advisory Services: A Scoping Review of Applications, Explainability, Trust and Farmer-Centred Adoption
Plant Leaf Disease Detection Techniques
abstract: Diseases in plant leaves have been a serious problem to the agricultural productivity in terms of crop yield and soil wellness. As soon as it is detected, it is important to avoid extensive destruction in order to have sustainable agriculture. The chapter gives traditional and advanced methods of plant leaf disease detection. Conventional approaches to the identification of pathogens consist of visual observations, microscopic observations, culturing of pathogens, and indicator plant tests, which are effective but may be labor-intensive and time-consuming. Recently, plant disease detection has undergone a revolution with the utilization of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches with the improvement in technology. Support Vector Machines (SVM), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and k-nearest neighbors (kNN) have done well in the accuracy test in classification tasks. Imaging modes such as hyperspectral imaging, fluorescence imaging, thermal imaging, MRI, and 3D imaging, among others, have further improved accuracy in identifying the disease. A case study in detecting potato and tomato leaf blight using the PlantVillage dataset proved that DL models work efficien

title: 3D modeling for crop applications in precision agriculture: a review
abstract: Background Advances in data acquisition and information processing have strengthened the role of precision agriculture (PA) in enhancing agricultural productivity and sustainability. Among emerging technologies, 3D crop modeling offers detailed representations of agricultural scenes, supports crop phenotyping, and enables autonomous operations such as harvesting, fertilization, and pruning. However, despite the rapid development of hardware and software for 3D modeling, a comprehensive synthesis of the available approaches and their applications in PA remains limited. Purpose This review aims to examine the broad range of 3D modeling approaches used in PA, focusing on their methodological characteristics, practical applications, advantages, and limitations to support the selection of suitable solutions for different agricultural requirements. Methods A total of 168 publications, identified through a Scopus literature search covering studies published up to March 2026, were reviewed. The analysis examines 3D data types and sensing technologies, sensor platforms and application environments, and data processing methods, including data registration techniques and methods for insight e

title: Advances In Assisted Reproduction In Ruminants
abstract: Livestock sector has been showing advancing trends in India’s economy with its increasing contribution year-on-year to the Agriculture and Allied Sector Gross Value Added (GVA) in the last 15 years or so which has been validated by reports. This growth rate can further be increased by usage of Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) so as to explore the potential of vast indigenous genetic diversity of various farm animals in India. ART have completely changed modern dairy farming. They have transitioned simple breeding methods to advanced reproductive technologies. Three main tools used to improve dairy animals currently are Artificial Insemination (AI), Sex-sorted semen and In Vitro Fertilization-In Vitro Embryo Production-Embryo Transfer (IVF-IVEP-ET). There are various standard operating procedures for each method to mimic the in vivo conditions occurring in animals. Additionally, these methods tend to enhance the quality of results as it would be obtained by using conventional natural mating technique. By using these methods correctly, veterinarians and farmers can get better pregnancy rates, speed up the breeding of superior animals and avoid the monetary losses caused by un

title: High-Throughput Technology for Accelerating Genomics
abstract: High-throughput genomics is revolutionizing contemporary agriculture by facilitating quick, accurate, and inexpensive exploration of crop genomes. With world demand for food rising and climate variability increasing, there is an urgent need to produce high-yielding, stress-tolerant, and nutrient-dense crop varieties. With technologies such as PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore PromethION, and 10x Genomics single-cell platforms, it is possible today to resolve plant genomes at base-pair resolution and link them to agronomically relevant traits. Sequencing is now less than $500 per genome, and the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) prediction models enables breeders to streamline selection cycles by as much as 50%. This chapter critically analyzes how high-throughput technologies, especially when combined with AI, are transforming the next generation of precision breeding and digital agriculture. Through real-world examples in crops such as wheat, rice, maize, and tomato, we emphasize how genomics is transcending gene discovery to facilitate predictive, data-driven decision-making (DDDM) in breeding pipelines. This chapter discusses the technological, computational, and applied

title: Artificial intelligence and informal employment: evidence from China’s agricultural transfer population
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is profoundly reshaping labour markets, but its relationship with informal employment remains unclear. This study focuses on the agricultural transfer population (ATP), a major group engaged in informal employment in China. Using data from the China Labour-force Dynamics Survey (CLDS), we systematically examine the association between AI and informal employment among the ATP and explore potential channels. We find that AI is significantly and positively associated with informal employment among the ATP. The observed association is primarily consistent with the job-creation and empowerment channels, while evidence for the substitution channel is insufficient. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that the positive association is more pronounced among female and younger ATP workers and those employed in the service sector. After distinguishing between two types of informal employment, we find that AI is positively associated with informal self-employment, whereas its association with informal wage employment is not statistically significant. In addition, the positive association is weaker among the ATP who have received skill training, particularly those w

title: Deep Learning Approaches for Plant Disease Detection: A Review of Convolutional Neural Networks and Emerging Techniques
abstract: Plant diseases pose a significant threat to global food security, crop yield, and agricultural sustainability. Traditional disease diagnosis methods, relying on expert visual inspection and laboratory analyses, are often time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly, limiting their scalability. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, offer automated and accurate solutions for plant disease detection. This review synthesizes current research on deep learning–based approaches, focusing on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), hybrid CNN-transformer models, attention mechanisms, and generative data augmentation techniques. CNNs have demonstrated strong capabilities in extracting hierarchical features from leaf images, capturing complex patterns such as lesion shapes, color variations, and textures, thereby outperforming conventional machine learning and rule-based methods. Hybrid architectures and transformer-based models enhance feature extraction, particularly for subtle or visually similar disease symptoms. Data augmentation strategies, including generative adversarial networks (GANs), help address class imbalance and improve model generalization. Desp

title: An Artificial Intelligence Framework for Food Supply Chain Management: Policy Implications for UAE Public-Sector Agricultural Authorities
abstract: Artificial intelligence offers significant potential to strengthen food supply chain management in countries facing resource constraints and food security pressures. This study develops and empirically evaluates an AI framework within the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority and derives policy implications for UAE public-sector agricultural authorities. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered to operational employees. Of 500 questionnaires distributed from a population of 1,506 employees, 402 valid responses were retained after data screening. The data were analysed using SPSS and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling. The model examined four AI capabilities, namely Expert System, Machine Learning, Agent-Based System, and Artificial Neural Network, in relation to three food supply chain outcomes: Production and Sourcing, Logistics and Distribution Efficiency, and Safety and Quality Control. Six of the twelve hypothesized relationships were supported. Artificial Neural Network was significantly associated with all three outcomes, Expert System with Production and Sourcing and Safety and Quality Control, and Agent-Based System with Logistics an

title: Summer Compound Hot-Drought Extreme Events over Northwest China: A Review of Recent Studies
abstract: Under global warming, compound extreme events threaten ecosystems and socio-economic systems more than individual extremes. As a typical arid and semi-arid region, Northwest China has witnessed continuous increases in concurrent summer hot and drought conditions, threatening regional water security, agriculture and ecological stability. Based on observation and reanalysis data since 1961, this paper reviews recent progress on the definition, spatiotemporal variation and formation mechanisms of Summer Compound Hot-Drought Extreme Events (CHDEE) in Northwest China. Results show that the fusion scheme of daily drought and heatwave indicators, as well as the Copula joint probability framework, perform well in regional CHDEE detection. CHDEE frequency has increased significantly, with a pronounced acceleration since the late 1990s. Spatially, CHDEE show a pattern of high values in the west and low values in the east. Affected areas expand from the arid core to the northern margins and southern high-altitude regions. CHDEE are controlled by multi-scale factors: the westerly circulation, the East Asian summer monsoon and the thermal forcing of the Tibetan Plateau. The positive soil moistu

title: EcoGrow Smart Irrigation System (EGSIS) A solar-powered, AI-enabled irrigation and water management system with live monitoring, alarms and ESG reporting for climate-smart food production, water resilience, land-based aquaculture and the circular economy
abstract: The EcoGrow Smart Irrigation System (EGSIS) is a low-cost, solar-powered irrigation controller and water management system designed for small-scale vegetable production. It replaces calendar-based or manual watering with irrigation that responds to the actual moisture condition of the soil. Water is applied only when the crop needs it, and the entire system runs on solar energy stored in a long-life LiFePO4 battery. Agriculture is both a major user of freshwater and a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions, while small-scale growers in South Africa face unreliable electricity, rising energy costs, drought risk and limited access to technology. EGSIS addresses these pressures with a compact, affordable and measurable solution that links renewable energy, automation and intelligent water use. EGSIS also includes an AI and software layer. Machine-learning models adapt irrigation to different crops, growth stages and weather, while a web and mobile app gives growers live data on tank levels, solar generation and soil moisture, a dashboard of key performance indicators, and triggers and alarms for faults. The same data feeds automated ESG (environmental, social and governance) r

title: The relationship between artificial intelligence and food production in South Africa
abstract: This study examines the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) and food production in South Africa. Annual data for 1995–2024 are analyzed using the autoregressive distributed lag bounds-testing approach. The bounds test confirms a long-run relationship among food production, AI patents, inflation, population growth, and household income. The estimates indicate that AI has a positive and statistically significant association with food production in both the short and long run, although the magnitude is modest. The results remain robust when a COVID-19 dummy is incorporated: the AI coefficient remains positive, while the pandemic has a negative effect on food production. These findings suggest that AI innovation can support domestic food production, but its contribution depends on complementary infrastructure and adoption capacity. Policy should therefore prioritize reliable digital and energy infrastructure, agricultural data systems, technical skills, and affordable access to AI-enabled technologies, particularly for smaller producers.

title: Replication archive: Reusing field-trial evidence in agricultural decision support: a deterministic check of provenance and trial conditions for soybean sulfur rules
abstract: Code, frozen inputs, saved results and verification scripts for the Technical Note of the same title (submitted to Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture). Contains the representation-layer evaluations HG-V3, HG-V4, HG-V4.1 and HG-V5, a verifier that recomputes the reported results from the saved records, and scripts for re-execution in a clean copy. The evaluations are post hoc and were not blind; much of the code was written with an AI coding assistant under the authors' direction. The source trial dataset is not included (https://doi.org/10.15482/USDA.ADC/28611506.v1).

title: Digital Agricultural Transformation under Climate Risk: A Policy and Financing Perspective within the National Economy Model
abstract: Today, the global food system is undergoing a multidimensional transformation driven by climate change, population growth and rising food demand. Irregular precipitation regimes, increasing water scarcity and ecosystem degradation are making agricultural production increasingly unpredictable and fragile. In addition to these ecological pressures, shrinking arable land, the ageing agricultural labour force and rising input costs further challenge the sustainability of conventional farming systems. The growing frequency of extreme weather events demonstrates the vulnerability of existing production models and highlights the need for structural transformation in agriculture. Digital agriculture offers a potential solution through a technology-oriented paradigm shift. Technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision support systems, remote sensing and precision agriculture enable site-specific resource management, reducing environmental impact while improving productivity. However, the adoption of these technologies is constrained by high investment costs and financial uncertainty, particularly for small and medium-scale producers. Therefor

title: White Paper on the Global Inclusive Natural‑Nutrition Module System — Reshaping the Paradigm of Global Food Security and Public Health (V2 Final Full Version)
abstract: This white paper presents an original, civilian-led top-level paradigm reconstruction for global food security and public health. It proposes a Global Inclusive Natural-Nutrition Module System based entirely on natural agricultural and livestock ingredients. The study addresses the long-standing global structural crises including disordered dietary structures, massive food waste, widespread diet-induced chronic diseases, overburdened healthcare systems, and nutritional inequity between rich and poor regions. The framework establishes a dual-track social operation model: medical systems for post-onset treatment and standardized nutrition modules for root-source prevention. It provides a complete, scalable, and implementable roadmap for global nutritional standardization, ecological pressure reduction, chronic disease prevention, and equitable public health governance. This work is an independent public-welfare conceptual deduction framework, containing no confidential data, no military-related content, and no AI-native generation. All core paradigms, logical architectures and innovation designs are independently conceived by the author.

title: Tracking AI Advisory Drift Before It Reaches the Farms: Measuring Contextual Reliability in LLM-Generated Advice Across the Agricultural Landscape
abstract: Agricultural advice intended to protect the land is sensitive to local context because a best management practice (BMP) designed for one location might be risky elsewhere. This risk is addressed in the U.S. by Cooperative Extension experts stationed in different geographic regions, who can benefit from the ability of general-purpose large language models (LLMs) to produce plausible answers quickly at a low marginal cost; however, these answers must remain locally reliable. We evaluated local reliability by examining whether advisory behaviors in LLM responses repeatedly conformed to relevant BMPs. We analyzed this conformance in 288 LLM responses to eight publicly available Cooperative Extension inquiries. These inquiries were submitted by people in different locations who were concerned that local water could harm plants. Because the locations differed in plant types, water composition, soils, and how the inquiry was framed, responses from twelve LLMs at three low-temperature settings allowed us to examine the potential for unnecessary risk. We analyzed this risk using descriptive text metrics and an inductively developed advisory scorecard to identify BMP nonconformances, includi

title: Wearable Sensors for Smart Agriculture: From Sensing Mechanisms to Crop Phenotyping and Harvesting Applications
abstract: Global food security faces severe pressures from population growth, climate change and resource shortages. Traditional agricultural monitoring relies on manual sampling and offline laboratory testing, which involve considerable time delays and cannot realize continuous, in situ dynamic tracking of crop physiological status, field environment and agricultural product quality. Among the various sensing platforms for agriculture, flexible wearable sensors represent an important branch, featuring light weight, conformability, low power consumption and real-time response. It should be noted that rigid-substrate and silicon-based sensors remain indispensable in many agricultural applications, and this review focuses specifically on flexible wearable sensors while acknowledging the broader landscape of agricultural sensing technologies. Through conformal contact with plant surfaces or wearable integration, they can convert physical, chemical and biological signals of agroecosystems into readable electrical/optical signals via specific sensing transduction mechanisms. This review systematically categorizes wearable sensors for smart agriculture into two main types, optical and electrical,

title: AgriSkill-Agent: A Skill-Guided and Knowledge-Enhanced Agent Framework for Leaf Disease Diagnosis and Management
abstract: While visual recognition and multimodal language models have improved leaf disease identification, most systems remain focused on recognition rather than integrated diagnosis and management. Practical support must connect symptoms, lesion extent, evidence-grounded diagnosis, and crop-specific guidance. We present AgriSkill-Agent, a skill-guided and knowledge-enhanced single-agent framework for leaf disease diagnosis and management. A central large language model activates task-specific procedural skills to coordinate visual analysis, external knowledge, and structured reporting. The main contribution is a unified diagnosis-to-management workflow integrating stage-specific skill contracts, deterministic lesion measurement, literature retrieval, and a pesticide-use knowledge graph. Image-derived measurements remain separate from language-model interpretation, while literature and structured pesticide-use knowledge provide traceable support. We evaluated AgriSkill-Agent on 140 image-based cases across 10 crops. The framework achieved higher diagnostic accuracy and produced more complete and better-grounded reports than direct multimodal baselines. Ablation analysis indicated that proc

title: Multistage AI Crop Inspection and Segmentation Framework (MACISF).
abstract: Abstract Crop quality assessment is one of the most critical components of modern agriculture, which directly influences yield optimization, post-harvest management, and food security. Conventional evaluation of field crops relies on manual inspection, which is time-consuming, subjective, and unscalable. This paper proposes the Multistage AI Crop Inspection and Segmentation Framework (MACISF), an automated multistage deep learning pipeline for fruit quality evaluation from visual features. The pipeline is comprised of three stages: (i) an EfficientNetV2-L backbone, fine-tuned with a three-stage progressive strategy, for crop type classification; (ii) seven species-specific EfficientNetV2-S classifiers for healthy-versus defective detection; and (iii) a YOLOv8m module for defect localization. Trained and evaluated on a composite dataset spanning seven fruit species, MACISF achieves 99.23% crop type accuracy (macro F1-score 99.23%, macro AUC-ROC 0.993), 99.39% mean health state accuracy with 99.51% mean defective-class recall, and a projected grading mAP@0.5 of 92.3%. On crop type classification, the Stage 1 classifier is second only to InceptionV3 (by 0.15 percentage points) among s

title: The Institutional Topology of "Simulated Prohibition": Rent-Seeking, Logistics Enclosures, and Regulatory Theater from the Volstead Act to Frontier AI Governance
abstract: 【Abstract】This institutional economics and technology governance monograph deconstructs the structural mythology of total legal bans through a comparative analysis of the 1920s United States National Prohibition Act (the Volstead Act) and contemporary regulatory frameworks targeting frontier artificial intelligence. Challenging the conventional narrative that the Volstead Act represented an absolute moral prohibition, this paper reveals that the statute functioned as a "Simulated Prohibition"—an elaborate regulatory theater embedding lucrative, state-sanctioned loopholes (medicinal whiskey prescription monopolies, sacramental exemptions, industrial alcohol diversions, and private agricultural transport corridors). Under the classical "Baptists and Bootleggers" dynamic, moral crusaders provided ideological legitimacy while established logistics networks, pharmaceutical trusts, and corrupt enforcement cartels extracted enormous monopoly rents from artificial scarcity. This monograph proves that modern maximalist AI governance regimes reproduce this identical topology: under the moral imperative of catastrophic safety, incumbent technology conglomerates execute regulatory capture, cre

title: Agriculture and Farmer Digital Assistant: An AI-Based Digital Decision Support Platform for Smart Farming
abstract: Abstract Farmers frequently make decisions under uncertain weather, incomplete agricultural information, changing soil conditions, and limited access to timely expert guidance. The Agriculture and Farmer Digital Assistant (AFDA) is a web-based digital decision-support platform designed to bring agricultural data, artificial intelligence, recommendation services, weather information, and role-based administration into a single system. The platform accepts agricultural inputs from farmers and processes them to provide crop recommendations and basic farming guidance. The design also considers soil analysis, pest and disease support, market information, notifications, multilingual assistance, and future sensor integration. The implemented project version focuses on user registration and login, agricultural data input, crop recommendation, basic weather guidance, and a recommendation dashboard, while several advanced capabilities remain future extensions. A layered architecture separates the user interface, application logic, AI processing, database, and notification/recommendation functions. The project further defines functional and non-functional requirements, data-flow and entity re

title: Expanding plant model systems: Classical references, emerging species, and a trait‑centric framework for modern plant science
abstract: For decades, plant biology has relied on a narrow set of classical model organisms—such as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays —to uncover core physiological, developmental, and molecular pathways. These systems enabled foundational discoveries, yet their glycophytic, annual, and domesticated life histories limit their relevance for studying many adaptive traits found across global plant diversity. Key innovations—including CAM and C4 photosynthesis, extreme salinity and desiccation tolerance, perennial wood formation, specialized secondary metabolism, and parasitic interactions—remain largely inaccessible within classical frameworks. Recent advances in third‑generation long‑read sequencing (PacBio HiFi, ONT Duplex), telomere‑to‑telomere (T2T) phased assemblies, pangenomics, single‑cell and spatial transcriptomics, and multi‑omics integration are dismantling these historical barriers. Together, these technologies enable high‑resolution characterization of polyploid, structurally complex, and ecologically specialized genomes, allowing previously intractable species to be developed as functional models. title: A Comprehensive Review on Artificial Intelligence-Based Control Strategies for Drone BLDC Motors
abstract: The application of brushless direct current (BLDC) motors in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has revolutionized modern uses of drones by enabling greater levels of performance efficiency, light weighting, and high torque-to-weight ratio that are particularly valuable for aerial systems. The motors also enable high speed at low maintenance, which is particularly valuable for propulsion in UAVs. But the UAV control in real situations usually faces difficulties due to parameter changes, unstructured environments, external disturbances like wind, and system nonlinearities inherent to the system. In such situations, conventional control methods like PID controllers and linear feedback approaches, although useful in structured and stable environments, tend to lack robustness and adaptability for dynamic and uncertain environments. To overcome these deficiencies, artificial intelligence (AI)-based control methods have appeared as revolutionary solutions. Methods such as fuzzy logic controllers, artificial neural networks, reinforcement learning methods, and hybrid intelligent control architectures are increasingly being utilized in UAV flight control and propulsion. title: Teaching Process-Based Clay Modification: An AI-Based Illustrative Approach for Environmental and Technical Applications
abstract: The rapid expansion and structural complexity of applied clay science create a pressing need for process-oriented educational frameworks to replace traditional descriptive instruction. To address this challenge, this technical note introduces an illustrative, process-based approach supported by generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools to clarify clay mineral modification pathways. Utilizing AI-enhanced prompt workflows integrated with literature synthesis, we developed a systematic "toolbox" framework that visually categorizes key physical and chemical pathways, including acid/alkali etching, thermal activation, mechanochemical milling, organo-functionalisation, and nanoparticle decoration; They link directly to property outcomes and target applications. Furthermore, we map the innovation pathway from laboratory synthesis to commercial production, detailing critical high-attrition failure points along the translation process. This AI-powered visual strategy bridges fundamental clay mineralogy with real-world technological, environmental, and agricultural applications.

title: Smart farms, virtual mirrors: AI-powered digital twins reshaping modern agriculture
abstract: Sustainable agriculture is increasingly threatened by a combination of factors, including inadequate food security, deteriorating land quality, shifting climate patterns, and a rapidly expanding population.Digital twin (DT) technology has emerged as a transformative tool in modern agriculture, allowing the development of real-time virtual representations of physical farming systems to support data-informed decision-making and sustainable resource use.The present study examines the concepts, frameworks and practical applications of digital twins in agriculture, emphasising their integration with the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, machine learning and remote sensing techniques.Key application areas of DT in agriculture include land cultivation, digital twin-empowered drones, controlled environment agriculture, disease detection, hydroponics, smart irrigation, livestock farming, and beekeeping.Reports from multiple studies show that DTs significantly enhance the prediction accuracy of crop yield, the detection of pests and diseases, irrigation efficiency, and livestock health monitoring, while reducing labour, resource waste, and environmental impact.Despite the advantag

title: Humans and Robots in Agriculture
abstract: Research in agricultural robotics has garnered increasing attention over the past decade. Simultaneously, Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) has emerged as a possible solution to increase automation and reduce the lack of human labor in the field. This chapter presents a study of research trends in HRI focusing on Artificial Intelligence (AI), human factors, and ergonomics in collaborative agricultural tasks. For example, we talk about the importance of robotics and the application of the different AI-based methods for HRI in field applications. Moreover, we emphasize situation awareness, stress, sleepiness, sleep quality, and distraction. We also explore various crucial and innovative topics related to HRI in agriculture, including safety, human factors, ergonomics, awareness, productivity, and management. This analysis shows that HRI paradigms can be effectively applied in agricultural applications, yielding promising production, safety, and farm management benefits, such as increasing productivity and reducing human workload.

title: Index
AI adoption for smart urban development - Policy model for digitalized and sustainable society
abstract: By 2030, it is projected that residents living in cities will additionally increase and this will place a great strain on infrastructures, natural resources, transportation, healthcare, economy, etc. As such the notion of smart cities are rapidly developing as a potential solution to address several challenges faced in urban environments such as pollution, reduced economic growth, etc. Hence, it is important to address societal growth by adopting disruptive technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enable a more digitalized and sustainable society. Evidence from the literature reveals that AI has been adopted in different sectors such as in healthcare, finance, agriculture, transportation, manufacturing, education, etc. Despite the possible benefits of AI, there are several factors that can influence the adoption of AI in society. This article aims to provide an extensive assessment on the applications of AI and barriers faced by smart cities in adopting AI. Through a systematic literature review, this study undertook an in-depth exploration of AI's impact and employed content analysis to present the techno-social factors that inhibit the adoption of AI in society. title: Ensemble machine learning for climate-smart cultivation zoning of Glycyrrhiza glabra L. under CMIP6 climate scenarios
abstract: Accurate habitat suitability projections under climate change are essential for climate-smart cultivation planning and sustainable production of medicinal plants. However, conventional species distribution modeling (SDM) approaches often overlook the combined effects of algorithmic uncertainty, edaphic–topographic heterogeneity, and dynamic habitat turnover, limiting their effectiveness as decision-support tools for agricultural planning. Here, we developed an ensemble machine learning framework integrating six complementary machine-learning and Bayesian algorithms (RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, MaxEnt, BART, and SVM), four CMIP6 global climate models (GCMs), four future time horizons, two Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP245 and SSP585), and high-resolution (∼1 km) climatic, edaphic, and topographic predictors to identify suitable cultivation zones for Glycyrrhiza glabra L. across Iran. The performance-weighted ensemble achieved high predictive performance (AUC = 0.835; 95% CI: 0.720–0.951) while substantially reducing algorithmic uncertainty (mean SD = 0.020–0.028). In contrast, variability among GCMs represented the dominant source of projection uncertainty (SD = 0.045–0.072). Althoug

abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence (AI) and agricultural big data, the adjustment of agricultural economic structure has shifted from empirical judgment to data-driven decision-making. This study uses the provincial panel data of agricultural economy in Hubei Province from 2010 to 2023 to construct a comprehensive framework of prediction and optimization. The forecasting layer uses the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model to capture the dynamic relationship among agricultural GDP growth rate, main crop output, rural employment structure, agricultural product price index, financial subsidies and agricultural infrastructure investment. The optimization layer uses the prediction results as parameters. It defines three objectives. overall agricultural benefit, structural deviation and food security risk. It also includes restrictions on cultivated land area, budget, labor supply and food security. Based on these backgrounds, the adjustment scheme of agricultural economic structure was formulated.
