title: Farmland Transformation Reshapes Ecosystem Services Through Multi-Level Landscape Reconfiguration: Evidence from China’s Songnen Plain
abstract: Global agricultural expansion has profoundly reshaped terrestrial landscapes, yet the ecological consequences of farmland transformation across multiple spatial scales remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates how farmland dynamics influence ecosystem service (ES) provision in China’s Songnen Plain by integrating long-term land-use trajectories, remote sensing data, and landscape ecological analysis. Using annual 30 m land-use/land-cover datasets from 2000 to 2020, we identified diverse farmland transformation pathways, including stable cultivation, reclamation, abandonment, fallow, afforestation, and urban encroachment. The InVEST model was applied to quantify three key ecosystem services: food supply, soil conservation, and carbon storage, while grid-level Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR) was employed to identify their major drivers. Results revealed substantial spatial and temporal heterogeneity in ecosystem services. Food supply and soil conservation generally increased during the study period, whereas carbon storage exhibited a declining trend. title: Spiking neural networks for apple quality monitoring
abstract: Sustainable agriculture is a global priority due to its role in food security and economic development. Nevertheless, food waste remains a critical challenge, with UNEP reporting 1.05 billion tons wasted worldwide in 2022, including over 24 million tons in México. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine vision have advanced agricultural inspection and quality control, yet conventional neural networks often consume significant energy. Neuromorphic computing, inspired by the human brain, offers superior efficiency and parallel processing, making it a promising alternative for fruit quality assessment. A spiking convolutional neural network (SCNN) was developed and trained using the Fruit360 dataset, which includes apples under diverse conditions such as damage, worm infestation, and varying maturity stages. Preprocessing techniques—including Local Binary Pattern (LBP), HSV filtering, and kernel-based feature extraction—were applied to enhance classification accuracy. The system was simulated in Google Colab and tested with the BrainChip Akida AKD1000 coprocessor under Ubuntu 22.04, despite integration challenges with TensorFlow and CUDA libraries. title: Venture-backed indoor farms 2010-2022: outcome-blind sample frame, status evidence and competing-risks analysis code (v1.0)
abstract: Outcome-blind sample frame of 100 venture-backed controlled-environment agriculture (indoor and vertical farming) firms whose first observed funding announcement falls in 2010-2022, built from trade-press funding announcements rather than from a list of failures. Each row carries status at October 2026 (operating, closed, acquired, unknown), exit year, disclosed funding, entry cohort and a source URL for every filled field. Includes the screened candidate list, funding-mention and status-evidence tables, the earlier 54-venture source-verified database with codebook used to fill fields, the closure-cause coding files (rule-based first coding and an LLM second pass, reported as such), the full survival output (Kaplan-Meier, Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence, cause-specific Cox models with closure and acquisition as competing exits), a post-hoc power note and the Python pipeline and analysis scripts that reproduce every number and figure in the accompanying article. Raw third-party article text is not redistributed; the fetch scripts are included. title: Adoption decision-making of AI digital humans for agricultural regional public brands in short videos
abstract: Introduction This study examines the adoption of AI digital humans (AI-DHs) by agricultural regional public brands in short-video promotion. Methods A complex network evolutionary game model is developed in which brands interact on a scale-free network and update their strategies through the Fermi rule. The model considers AI-DH production and generation costs, real-human promotion costs, consumer preference, recommendation priority, and network size. For each parameter scenario, 100 stochastic simulation runs are conducted, and mean adoption trajectories with 95% simulation intervals are reported. Results Higher AI-DH-related costs reduce the relative payoff of AI-DH promotion and suppress adoption, whereas higher real-human promotion costs make AI-DH promotion comparatively more attractive. Consumer preference produces the most pronounced change in the evolutionary outcome, with higher preference shifting the system toward broader AI-DH adoption. Higher recommendation priority helps sustain AI-DH adoption during the evolutionary process but does not independently determine the final adoption state. abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, computer vision, Internet of Things (IoT), satellite navigation, remote sensing, and autonomous control systems is transforming the design and operation of modern agricultural machinery. Agricultural machinery is increasingly evolving from conventional mechanical equipment into intelligent cyber-physical systems capable of sensing field conditions, processing large volumes of data, making operational decisions, and executing agricultural tasks with limited human intervention. This article examines the application of artificial intelligence and automation technologies in tractors, harvesters, sprayers, robotic platforms, unmanned aerial vehicles, and other agricultural machinery. The study is based on a systematic analysis of scientific publications, international institutional reports, and documented agricultural technology adoption data. Particular attention is given to autonomous navigation, machine vision, precision spraying, variable-rate application, crop monitoring, yield prediction, robotic weeding, harvesting, and safety systems. title: Impact of digital economy development on the sectoral employment structure in China: Analysis of direct and mediating effects
abstract: The digital economy is a crucial driver of economic transformation and exploring its impact on the employment structure is important for optimizing regional labor resource allocation. However, previous studies focused on the growth patterns of the digital economy, while neglecting its impact on employment structures across different sectors and its mediating effects. This study implements an evaluation system for the digital economy based on seven dimensions (mobile phone user numbers, internet broadband access volume, telecommunications business volume, express delivery business volume, Baidu search index for AI, number of AI enterprises, and the Digital Inclusive Finance Index) to analyze the spatiotemporal evolution of China’s digital economy and its influence on the sectoral employment structure. The results indicate that the digital economy experienced continuous growth from 2011 to 2022, although the growth rate exhibits a downward fluctuating trend. title: Nanoparticles, Artificial Intelligence, and the Future of Agriculture
abstract: Growing population, climate change, competing land needs for biofuel production, and a decline in soil quality are significant challenges to global food security. Sustainable agriculture is crucial for satisfying the present and future needs of the rising global population. To cope with this situation, researchers are working enthusiastically on synergistic approaches to integrate knowledge from various fields, such as informatics and material science. Nanotechnology and artificial intelligence (AI) both are emerging fields of science, and their fusion is reshaping agriculture by offering innovative solutions to longstanding challenges. In combination, an AI-driven data system analyzes data collected from various sources to determine the specific needs in real time, and nanoparticles respond accordingly, allowing farmers to make informed decisions about farm practices. These innovations support sustainable agriculture by conserving resources, minimizing waste, and enhancing production. This chapter discusses nanoparticles and AI’s significant role and their synergistic impact on sustainable agriculture. Despite their potential applications, some challenges still exist. title: Microencapsulation Technologies: Recent Advances in Drug Protection, Controlled Release and Targeted Therapeutics
abstract: Active pharmaceutical ingredients, biologics, or living organisms are incased in protective polymeric, lipid, protein-based, or hybrid coatings in microencapsulation, a sophisticated drug delivery method. Microcapsules, which are typically between 1 and 1000 μm in size, shield delicate materials from light, moisture, oxygen, temperature, and pH fluctuations. Additionally, they avoid medication incompatibilities, hide offensive taste and odor, turn liquids into powders, and offer targeted, controlled, or prolonged drug release. Release can happen by osmosis, diffusion, dissolution, degradation, or reactions to temperature and pH. Ionic gelation, fluidized-bed coating, solvent evaporation, spray drying, interfacial polymerization, and coacervation are common preparation techniques.While synthetic polymers like PLGA, PLA, PCL, and Eudragit provide greater mechanical qualities and tunable release profiles, natural polymers like alginate, chitosan, gelatin, and pectin offer biocompatibility and biodegradability. Microscopy, particle-size analysis, FTIR, DSC, TGA, XRD, zeta-potential measurement, drug-loading investigations, and stability testing are all used to characterize microcapsule

abstract: The rapid convergence of the Internet of Things (IoT), Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) is fundamentally reshaping the landscape of modern digital infrastructure. While each of these paradigms has individually driven massive technological leaps, their true transformative power lies in their synergy. IoT acts as the sensory network collecting real-world data, Blockchain provides an immutable layer of security and decentralized trust, and AI/ML serves as the cognitive brain processing this information to enable real-time, autonomous decision-making. title: A review of remote sensing for agricultural drought: technologies, indices, modelling advances and future prospects
abstract: Agricultural drought is a complex hazard that jeopardises food security and progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed English-language literature published between 2015 and 2025, focusing on Remote Sensing (RS)-driven agricultural drought monitoring and prediction. Eligible studies were identified from the Web of Science and Scopus databases (last searched in August 2025); review articles, duplicates, and irrelevant studies were excluded, resulting in 181 articles. This review critically examined the evolution of sensors, drought indices, modelling approaches, and emerging technologies used to assess agricultural drought across diverse agro-ecological regions. abstract: The growing adoption of digital technologies in agriculture is opening new opportunities for improving productivity, sustainability and resource efficiency through data-driven decision making. This paper presents the integrated precision-agriculture framework developed by RFSAT Limited within the H2020 AgriBIT project and currently being further enhanced through the ENACT project. The framework combines Internet-of-Things (IoT) sensing, centimetre-accuracy Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning, high-resolution multispectral remote sensing and Artificial Intelligence (AI) analytics into a single smart-farming solution. A key enabler is a low-cost, centimetre-accurate GNSS receiver developed by RFSAT, which allows precise georeferencing of aerial and ground observations and, in turn, the generation of high-resolution multispectral 3D models of crop canopies with spatial resolution exceeding 1 cm/pixel. These digital representations support detailed monitoring of crop growth, canopy development, biomass distribution and plant health throughout the season. title: Temporal generalization evaluation of deep semantic segmentation models for UAV-based wheat lodging monitoring under transfer learning
abstract: Temporal domain shift is a major barrier to the reliable application of agricultural artificial intelligence (AI) models in long-term field monitoring. Although deep learning models have achieved high accuracy in UAV-based crop lodging monitoring, their performance often declines across years, phenological stages, illumination conditions, and sensor platforms. This study developed a temporal generalization evaluation framework for deep semantic segmentation models for UAV-based wheat lodging monitoring under transfer learning. Five years of UAV imagery were organized with 2023 as the source domain and 2019, 2020, 2021, and 2024 as temporal target domains. Class-wise Bhattacharyya distance, RBF maximum mean discrepancy (RBF-MMD) of frozen ResNet50 features, and Wasserstein distance of lodging proportions described appearance, deep-feature, and label-distribution shifts, respectively. Nineteen representative models were first evaluated for source-domain convergence; nine converged models were retained, and eight further passed within-year generalization for direct cross-year deployment and target-domain fine-tuning. abstract: Long-tailed macaque (Macaca fascicularis) infestations have reduced corn production from a potential 7–9 tons to only 4–5 tons per growing season (±40%), while conventional deterrence methods such as loud noise and shooting have proven ineffective. This study developed an Internet of Things (IoT)-based pest repellent system using audiosonic waves, an HC-SR501 sensor, and an ESP32-CAM module, incorporating YOLOv8 and EfficientNet-B0 to replace the previously used YOLOv3 Tiny model, with the aim of improving detection accuracy and distinguishing long-tailed macaques from humans. Since population density at the partner's farmland was insufficient to construct an adequate dataset, image data were collected at Kembang Island, South Kalimantan, which serves as a natural habitat supporting a large and observable population of long-tailed macaques, thereby enabling the acquisition of visually representative and diverse training data. A total of 3,083 images were annotated using Label Studio under two classes (human and long-tailed macaque), then divided at an 80:10:10 ratio without augmentation. title: Occlusion-Aware Watermelon Size Estimation Using YOLO11-OBB and Amodal GAN
abstract: In the cultivation of watermelon, the prevention of fruit thinning and the selective removal of smaller fruits to ensure optimal nutrient allocation for superior specimens are critical for optimizing yield and quality. For accurate size estimation, AI is used to identify high-potential fruits and optimize field management and harvesting strategies in precision agriculture. However, precise watermelon size estimation in open-field environments is challenging due to frequent occlusion from leaves, vines, soil, and overlapping fruits. In addition, conventional detection and modal segmentation methods capture visible regions, resulting in systematic underestimation of fruit size under partial occlusion. To address the limitations, an occlusion-aware watermelon size estimation framework was developed in this study by integrating You Only Look Once 11-based localization, ellipse-based geometric modeling, and a two-stage generative adversarial network for instance segmentation. For effective learning, a reference dataset of full-shape watermelon images with ground-truth masks was constructed, and realistic synthetic occlusion was generated by overlaying leaf patches onto unoccluded fruits

title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND AUTOMATION TECHNOLOGIES IN MODERN AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, computer vision, Internet of Things (IoT), satellite navigation, remote sensing, and autonomous control systems is transforming the design and operation of modern agricultural machinery. Agricultural machinery is increasingly evolving from conventional mechanical equipment into intelligent cyber-physical systems capable of sensing field conditions, processing large volumes of data, making operational decisions, and executing agricultural tasks with limited human intervention. This article examines the application of artificial intelligence and automation technologies in tractors, harvesters, sprayers, robotic platforms, unmanned aerial vehicles, and other agricultural machinery. The study is based on a systematic analysis of scientific publications, international institutional reports, and documented agricultural technology adoption data. Particular attention is given to autonomous navigation, machine vision, precision spraying, variable-rate application, crop monitoring, yield prediction, robotic weeding, harvesting, and safety systems. Evidence from the United States demonstrates substantial growth in precision-agri

title: Random vs spatial cross-validation in machine-learning environmental mapping: how large is the gap and what drives it? Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models are widely used to map spatially distributed environmental and agricultural variables. Their accuracy is usually assessed with random k-fold cross-validation (CV), which assumes independent observations; with spatially autocorrelated data random CV may be optimistic, whereas spatial CV (spatial blocks, buffered/leave-location-out, target-oriented validation, NNDM/kNNDM) may be pessimistic, and single studies report gaps from negligible to dramatic. This systematic review and multilevel random-effects meta-analysis (PRISMA 2020) will estimate the pooled size and direction of the discrepancy between random and spatial CV (delta R2, log RMSE ratio, delta AUC) in original studies that evaluate the same model and dataset with both schemes, and identify what drives it (sampling design, block size vs autocorrelation range, CV type, model, domain, sample size). Only original peer-reviewed articles are eligible. title: From Compost Intelligence to Farm Decisions: A Review of Explainable AI for Organic Manure Maturity and Management
abstract: Composting of animal manure and agricultural organic waste represents a significant strategy for nutrient recycling, soil improvement and sustainable waste management. However, an accurate evaluation of the compost maturity and quality is a challenging task due to the number of physical, chemical, biological and environmental factors involved in the process. Conventional approaches usually rely on laboratory analyses and individual maturity indicators which can often be time-consuming and difficult to integrate with practical decision support systems. Thus, recent studies have explored the use of machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI), spectroscopy, the Internet of Things (IoT), and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to predict compost maturity, quality parameters and environmental emissions. This paper aims to review 20 studies published between 2020 and 2026 on manure composting, compost maturity prediction, spectroscopic monitoring, microbial additives, greenhouse-gas emissions, artificial intelligence, sensor-based systems and agricultural waste management. The reviewed literature revealed that Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, AdaBoost, ANN and adaptive

title: Editorial: Green biomanufacturing by industrial microorganisms: precise regulation and system optimization
abstract: A first theme concerns the design of green catalytic systems that improve the physicochemical properties of high-value bioactive compounds. The contribution by the group exemplifies this direction through the whole-cell-catalyzed cinnamoylation of phillyrin (Yang et al., 2026). By combining Aspergillus oryzae whole cells with hydrophobic natural deep eutectic solvents (NADESs) in co-solvent systems, the authors achieved conversion rates of 97.32-99.00% and excellent 6′-regioselectivity (>99%) under optimized conditions. Importantly, the biocatalysts retained 80.09-97.95% of their original activity after six consecutive cycles. This work underscores how the rational pairing of biocatalysts with sustainable reaction media can expand the chemical space accessible to biotransformation. Future research could extend this system to bioreactor scale-up, examine NADES recycling, and elucidate the molecular basis of membrane permeability changes.A second theme addresses the stability and productivity of industrial enzymes. title: XAI-OPL Risk Prediction Dataset — 31 Studies on AI/ML for Occupational Postural and Lumbar Risk
abstract: This dataset is the complete reproducibility package accompanying the systematic review and meta-analysis "Explainable and interpretable machine learning for occupational postural and lumbar risk prediction: A systematic review and meta-analysis" (PROSPERO registration: CRD420261530250). The review is, to our knowledge, the first to explicitly evaluate the role of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in AI/ML-based occupational postural and lumbar risk prediction. The package contains the full raw data extraction matrix for all 31 included studies, the meta-analysis input data and outputs (pooled accuracy, pooled AUC, subgroup analyses by model type, sector-level performance, and publication bias tests), the PROBAST risk-of-bias assessments, and Python scripts that regenerate every figure and table reported in the manuscript. The dataset is designed to support full analytical reproducibility — any researcher can reproduce the manuscript's results by re-running the scripts against the provided CSVs, without requiring access to the original study data. The 31 included studies were published between 2017 and 2026, span six occupational sectors (Industrial/Manufacturing, Construct

title: Screening of antiparasitic agents against fish ectoparasite Argulus coregoni using deep-learning-based motility analysis
Applying Artificial Intelligence for the Sustainable Development of Aquaculture
abstract: Aquaculture farms may find it more challenging to manage each culture system and make optimal decisions due to recent advancements in automation and intelligence, which have opened new avenues for digital fishery farming. In this scenario, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) can assist with real-time decision-making and agricultural monitoring. AI results from computers being provided with sufficient contextual data to perform tasks that require human intelligence. Blockchain technology has enabled ML to track a fish&s;s entire journey through the supply chain and quickly determine its origin on a customer&s;s “stable.” Fisheries and aquaculture could benefit from this, leading to increased commercial viability and environmental sustainability. This chapter discusses future trends and the application of AI and ML in the fishing and aquaculture sectors. A comprehensive investigation of ML applications in aquaculture is conducted, including biomass assessment, fish 2 identification and classification, behavioral analysis, and prediction of water quality parameters.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things in Smart Agriculture: A Bibliometric and Thematic Review of Data Infrastructures and Sustainability Implications
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping smart agriculture through prediction, automation, resource optimization, and data-driven decision-making. However, its effective and sustainable deployment depends on reliable Internet of Things (IoT) data infrastructures supporting sensing, connectivity, data acquisition, transmission, and distributed processing. This review maps research at the intersection of AI, IoT, and smart agriculture and examines its data-infrastructure requirements and sustainability implications. Drawing on 441 Scopus-indexed, peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2017 and 2025, the study combines bibliometric performance analysis, science mapping, and content-based thematic interpretation to identify publication trends, intellectual foundations, influential research fronts, emerging themes, and deployment challenges. The bibliometric analyses characterize AI–IoT research in smart agriculture, while IoT data infrastructure provides the principal analytical lens, and sustainability and responsible deployment are examined through interpretive synthesis. The findings reveal rapid publication growth and prominent themes involving connected sensing, predict

title: EL-RAKHAWI BEACON THE SYMBIOTIC CONVERGENCE SYSTEM FOR HUMAN SURVIVAL AND DIGNITY A COMPREHENSIVE TECHNICAL AND PHILOSOPHICAL FOUNDATION DOCUMENT FINAL HARDENED OPEN HARDWARE EDITION WITH REALISTIC ENGINEERING SPECIFICATIONS

title: From farmer acceptance to engineering requirements: a systematic review and design crosswalk for autonomous agricultural machinery
abstract: Retrospectively registered systematic review (searches 27–28 September 2026; citation searching 7 October 2026; review completed 8 October 2026). The review synthesises primary empirical studies on the acceptance, trust, perceived risk, usability, workload and stated requirements of farmers, operators and agricultural stakeholders regarding mobile agricultural machines whose control is shifted away from an on-board operator (teleoperation, operator-assisted automation, supervised autonomy and full autonomy). The question was framed with SPIDER and reporting follows PRISMA 2020. Findings are synthesised thematically by level of autonomy and translated into engineering requirements through a design crosswalk, the Human-centred Acceptance-to-Engineering Requirements (HAIER) crosswalk. Expected outcomes: a map of human-centred evidence across levels of autonomy, drivers and barriers of acceptance, evidence-based design requirements for AI perception, human–machine interfaces, safety and service models, and a research agenda for smallholder and wetland farming systems.

title: Computational Provenance and Reproducibility Record of PBD in www.raisins.live
abstract: RAISINS (R and AI Solutions for INferential Statistics) is an advanced, user-friendly online platform for statistical analysis, seamlessly integrating the power of R, Python, and Artificial Intelligence. Specially designed for agricultural research, RAISINS enables students, researchers, and professionals to perform complex analyses and generate publication-ready results without the need for software installation or coding expertise. Simply choose your analysis module, upload your dataset, and receive instant, insightful outputs. RAISINS supports individual users across the globe as well as institutions in India and abroad. This Computational Provenance and Reproducibility Record documents the statistical computing environment, software dependencies, computational provenance, and bibliographic references associated with the RAISINS PBD module. It is intended to support computational reproducibility and software transparency. Detailed statistical methodology, mathematical derivations, and user guidance are provided separately in the official module documentation. You can access the online cloud platform at https://www.raisins.live/

title: Artificial Intelligence Research in Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: This paper reviews AI research associated with Bosnia and Herzegovina from 2021 to 2026. It analyses 15 representative studies across healthcare, Bosnian-language NLP, energy, agriculture, finance, robotics, education, and AI governance, identifying major trends, methodological weaknesses, and future research priorities.

title: Smart agriculture improves nitrogen use efficiency yield prediction and sustainability in dryland mixed crop livestock systems
abstract: Mixed crop-livestock systems in dryland regions play a critical role in ensuring food security in the Global South; however, they are confronted with several challenges, including unpredictable rainfall patterns, nutrient depletion, and low productivity levels. The integration of advanced agricultural technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and remote sensing, presents transformative opportunities for enhancing the efficacy of these systems. This paper investigates how intelligent agricultural tools can improve nitrogen management, boost productivity in both crops and livestock, and promote overall farm sustainability. Strategies such as intercropping alfalfa with corn silage, utilizing remote sensing for real-time monitoring, and implementing precision fertilization techniques directly address fundamental issues such as nitrogen use efficiency (NUE), soil health, and feed quality. Additionally, the application of intelligent yield estimation models and nutrient recovery methods further optimizes resource utilization. The integration of machine learning algorithms with satellite data enhances the accuracy of yield predictions, thereby facil

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI GRAND THEORY OF REGENERATIVE BLOCKCHAIN ARCHITECTURE AND SOVEREIGN TRUST ECOSYSTEMS From Blind Decentralization to Mathematically Proven Ecological and Ethical Consensus
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Grand Theory of Regenerative Blockchain Architecture and Sovereign Trust Ecosystems (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23235300) transforms distributed ledger technology from an extractive mechanism into a sovereign, regenerative foundation for global trust. title: How IoT Is Revolutionizing Aquaculture: A Dive into Automated Fish-Feeding Systems
abstract: Smart aquaculture, also known as aquafarming, has emerged as a transformative approach to the cultivation of fish and other aquatic species, driven by the integration of advanced technologies and real-time data analysis. This chapter explores the pivotal role of sensors and monitoring devices in tracking essential environmental parameters, empowering farmers to optimize feeding, disease prevention, and overall management practices. Leveraging the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) 40 technologies further enhances system capabilities by automating tasks and reducing manual intervention. Through IoT-enabled fish feeders, for example, precise feeding schedules and portions are programmed based on various factors, resulting in enhanced feeding efficiency, reduced waste, and improved water quality. Real-time monitoring enables adaptive strategies, fostering healthier fish and increased productivity. Moreover, smart aquaculture extends to aquaponics systems, which integrate aquaculture with hydroponics to maximize agricultural output in confined spaces while minimizing environmental impact. By revolutionizing efficiency and sustainability, smart aquaculture offers

title: The Future of Climate-Smart Water Management: A Systematic Review of the Convergence of Artificial Intelligence, Nature-Based Solutions, and Adaptive Governance in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Climate change is intensifying water insecurity across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), threatening agricultural productivity, ecosystem integrity, and sustainable livelihoods. Climate-smart water management (CSWM) has consequently emerged as an important approach for strengthening water security and climate resilience. This scoping review maps the existing evidence on the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Nature-Based Solutions (NbS), and adaptive governance in supporting climate-smart water management across SSA. Guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), a systematic search of peer-reviewed and grey literature published between 2000 and 2026 identified 1265 records, of which 15 studies met the inclusion criteria. The review found that the evidence base remains limited and fragmented but reflects growing scholarly interest in integrating technological, ecological, and governance approaches to climate adaptation. The included studies reported AI applications primarily in remote sensing, predictive analytics, climate forecasting, decision support systems

title: ICT as an Emerging Tool for Sustainable Development in the Fisheries Sector
abstract: Information and communication technology (ICT) tools are of great importance in fish production and management, an emerging field within the fisheries sector, enabling the sustainable use of available resources to a greater extent. Fisheries are a fast-growing sector with strong potential to address challenges related to food security, poverty, and unemployment. This sector contributes 1% to the national GDP and 6.44% to agricultural GDP, with consumption rates of up to 77.84 kg per capita per year in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the lowest consumption rate, 0.05 kg per capita per year, in the Union Territory (UT) of Ladakh. To maintain nutritional security, fish and seafood products are good sources of essential amino acids and minerals, which are important for metabolic and growth activities in children and adults. To ensure a quality food supply, the fisheries sector uses ICT-based tools for high-stocking fish production, feeding, disease management, and water quality management. It is observed that important ICT tools, such as mobile phones, radio and television, GPS–sonar, and other advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT)-based tools, such as

title: EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF RESILIENT ISLAND INNOVATION CONVERGENT RESEARCH FRAMEWORKS FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, CLIMATE ADAPTATION, RENEWABLE ENERGY, MEDICAL VALUE CHAINS, AND APPROPRIATE AGRITECH IN SMALL ISLAND DEVELOPING
abstract: EL-RAKHAWI RESILIENT ISLAND INNOVATION: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY This monograph establishes the El-Rakhawi Doctrine of Resilient Island Innovation for Small Island Developing States (SIDS), addressing resource constraints through five pragmatic pillars: (1) Lightweight AI Applications (not foundational models); (2) Climate Vulnerability & Marine Bio-Economics; (3) Renewable Energy & Electric Mobility; (4) Medical Value Chain Upgrading (not drug discovery); (5) Low-Cost Appropriate Agritech (not expensive Western precision agriculture). Critical innovations: **Hybrid Adaptation Financing** (Blue Bonds, Debt-for-Climate Swaps) addressing sovereign debt constraints; **Brain Drain Mitigation** via diaspora engagement; and the **Revised IRICI** correcting multicollinearity by replacing Digital Divide with Brain Drain variable (B), using realistic proxy metrics from World Bank/UNESCO/FAO. Mathematical framework: Weighted Geometric Mean with Operational Floor (x'=max(x,0.15)). Released under **CC BY 4.0** with mandatory attribution to **Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi**. title: Proof-of-concept for a deep learning-based automated system for deep-sea fish stomach content analysis
abstract: In fish dietary analysis, reducing the substantial time and effort required is essential for accelerating the accumulation of ecological knowledge. Recent advances in machine learning have enabled development of highly accurate object detection models. Here, we aimed to establish a foundational technology for automating stomach content analysis by developing an automated prey detection system based on YOLO, a general-purpose object detection model. Stomach contents from demersal fish collected by bottom trawling were photographed using a stereomicroscope, and a training dataset comprising 682 images (1655 instances) across 18 classes was constructed. The developed model successfully detected prey items across a wide range of digestion states, including highly degraded and amorphous prey that are difficult to identify visually. Despite the challenging nature of this task, the class-average precision, recall, and class assignment error rate were 41.3% ± 8.4%, 37.2% ± 7.6%, and 34.1% ± 7.2%, respectively. Among all classes, precision was highest for the ‘Fish(eye)’ class at 88.3%, whereas recall was highest for ‘Decapoda(shrimp)’ at 70.5%. In addition to these conventional metrics, we

title: Research on Embedded Hypervisor Technology Selection: Requirements Analysis and Capability Comparison for Extreme Environment Application Scenarios
abstract: As embedded devices grow more complex, running multiple operating systems on a single device—and deploying virtualization beyond data centers into embedded systems—has become standard. This paper focuses on the hypervisor Virtual Machine Monitor and examines its selection challenges in extreme environments: disaster rescue, space exploration, deep-sea and polar operations, and security confrontations. We propose a four-layer analytical framework—"Scenario → Threat → Requirement → Capability"—to systematically compare mainstream embedded hypervisors across key dimensions. The framework is validated through real-world cases: the Mars Pathfinder mission, AWS Snowcone edge devices, and the DARPA HACMS red-team experiment. Results show no one-size-fits-all hypervisor for extreme settings, optimal selection depends on specific application context, security needs, and system constraints. In safety-critical domains, certification standards (e.g., DO-178C, ISO 26262) and formal verification—once limited to military applications—are now spreading to critical infrastructure. title: Underwater LiDAR (ULi) point cloud data (.las) of different target materials acquired under laboratory fresh-water conditions
abstract: With the global expansion of underwater infrastructure elements such as port facilities, offshore wind turbines, pipelines and submarine cables, the demand for a fast, precise and high resolution monitoring solution is growing. While acoustic systems like echosounders only offer a low accuracy in the range of centimetre, passive optical technologies such as cameras depend on illumination, which limits their application particular in deep sea environments. In contrast, active optical LiDAR technologies, known for their superior speed and accuracy, offer a promising alternative. Nevertheless, water also introduces challenges for active optical systems, including turbidity as well as a limited range. The underwater laser scanner ULi, developed by the Fraunhofer IPM, aims to address these limitations. To assess whether the technical specifications provided by the manufacturer, especially with regard to the achievable resolution can be meet, various tests in a basin with clear water were carried out. By using targets consisting of different materials and surface characteristics, a first statement to which extend ULi is suitable for practical underwater monitoring applications, can be ma

title: Comprehensive Review of Lithium: Resources, Extraction Technologies, Recycling, Environmental Impacts, and Machine Learning
Beyond the Northern Sea Route: can China sustain Arctic partnerships with Nordic states while maintaining cooperation with Russia?
abstract: This paper examines whether China can maintain cooperation with Nordic states in an era of sanctions, securitisation, and mistrust. The analysis begins from the observation that China’s access to Arctic resources, transport corridors, and industrial projects remains largely mediated through Russia’s Arctic regions (LNG, Northern Sea Route, port infrastructure). Nordic states have become increasingly cautious towards both Russian presence and Chinese strategic investment since 2022. This creates a structural dilemma for China’s Arctic policy. Empirically, the paper traces three arenas where this dilemma becomes visible: First, energy and LNG supply chains, through Novatek’s Arctic LNG projects to European and Asian buyers. Second, maritime and port infrastructure in the European Arctic, including the regulation of access, data, and dual-use technologies. Third, scientific and technological cooperation, while Nordic partners tighten investment screening in critical infrastructure and apply stricter safeguards to sensitive research. title: Innovative Logging-While-Drilling and Measurement-While-Drilling Technologies Enable Successful ERD Well Geosteering in High Gamma Ray, Low Resistivity Pay
abstract: Abstract Typical oil reservoirs containing radioactive minerals, characterized by high gamma-ray readings and low resistivity logs, are developed within the ZJ1 Formation of the WC16 Oilfield, offshore South China Sea. Due to the lack of effective reservoir evaluation and geosteering technologies, this oilfield has remained undeveloped since its discovery. In 2026, to unlock reserves and enhance production, four horizontal wells were planned to develop this complex reservoir. All wells were classified as extended-reach drilling (ERD) due to the reservoir's shallow true vertical depth (TVD) and the resulting high step-out ratio. Geosteering and formation evaluation were critical for achieving the project's objectives, as the target sands exhibited only minimal resistivity and gamma ray (GR) contrast relative to adjacent layers. The target zone resistivity ranged from 1.5 to 2.0 Ω·m, while surrounding siltstones had slightly lower resistivity (1.1 Ω·m), and the water zone was measured at 0.9 Ω·m. Meanwhile, GR readings for the target zone were nearly indistinguishable from those of neighboring mudstones. These factors made delineating the complex target interval, and thus achieving o

title: Replication Data for: The Opacity Trap: Why States Wait to Govern Emerging Technologies
abstract: Arms control overwhelmingly concerns technologies that states already possess rather than those they might one day develop. Why do states prefer to control today’s technologies tomorrow instead of controlling tomorrow’s technologies today? I argue that technological secrecy produces an opacity trap: states must conceal technological details that could betray important discoveries to rivals, but mutual secrecy obscures who is actually ahead. Thus, the very secrecy states need to compete is also what blinds them to whether technological competition is worth preventing. I formalize this logic with an endogenous learning model, showing how the information needed to make anticipatory control attractive usually only arises through competition itself. By the time states realize they are ensnared in unwinnable competitions, the technologies they are competing over have already been produced. The theory is tested with archival research into two little-known cases—environmental-modification weapons and deep-sea missile launchers—alongside original data on nearly 250 weapons governance agreements since 1850. The findings explain why states can foresee the dangers of emerging technologies yet

title: GRAVIDRO: deep sea underwater gravity battery parks scalable toward TWh energy storage capacity
abstract: Energy reservoirs are an ongoing challenge for renewable/green energy production system based on non- programmable sources, like wind or solar energy. Several solutions are being studied and implemented, from hydro-reservoirs to mechanical energy storages, from hydrogen to electrical batteries. Gravity batteries are also being tested: here we present a conceptual study of an underwater gravity battery park in deep sea waters, that we name Gravidro, which appears well suitable to be scalable towards very large energy levels, that is the TWh scale (a few Petajoules). Gravidro involves well established technologies and negligible ecological impact, joined to no usage of land and extremely low accident relevance even in case of severe faults. At the TWh energy storage level, for a mid-size developed country consuming routinely about 40 GW of electrical power, besides maintaining the available energy continuity on a day by day basis as well as the seasonal energy coverage, Gravidro could guarantee a stored energy sufficient to run for a day even in case of a severe electrical black-out. Gravidro parks would make intermittent energy generation systems (solar, wind) the most favorable sou

title: Mega-Decommissioning Environmental Liability and Forward-Dated Compliance
abstract: The Mega-Decommissioning Environmental Liability and Forward-Dated Compliance represents a massive structural, financial, and predictive paradox in heavy infrastructure, nuclear energy, offshore oil production, and deep-sea mining mega-programs. Unlike standard project lifecycles that conclude with the delivery and handover of an operational asset, mega-programs involving hazardous or highly intensive physical extractions face an inverted lifecycle challenge. At the terminal end of the asset's active operational lifespan—which typically extends between forty to eighty years—the organization is legally bound to execute a comprehensive, reverse-construction decommissioning phase to safely dismantle, decontaminate, and bury the asset. The core project management dilemma stems from the fact that planners must estimate costs, design engineering protocols, and allocate environmental risk contingencies today for a phase that will occur decades in the future, within a landscape where future environmental regulations, carbon taxes, and disposal technologies are entirely unknown. Mechanistically, this long-term temporal disconnect shatters the validity of traditional lifecycle financial audi

title: Rising spillover risk: Lessons from the Andes hantavirus outbreak
abstract: The unprecedented expansion of human activity boundaries is turning spillover from a chance event into a foreseeable ecological and epidemiological certainty. Using the 2026 Andes hantavirus cruise ship outbreak as an entry point, this study examines it within a broader driver framework: nearly all emerging infectious disease events in humans in recent decades have originated from wildlife transmission; under climate-change and land-use scenarios, approximately 3139 mammal species are projected to aggregate in new combinations by 2070, causing an estimated 4000 cross-species viral transmission events. The rapid expansion of tourism into ecologically fragile regions — sub-Antarctic waters, the deep sea, and primary forests — the persistence of habitat fragmentation and animal trade, and the reshaping of wildlife distribution and vector dynamics by extreme climate events together constitute “novel contact amplifiers” that accelerate contact at the human–animal–environment interface. title: Thermal performance regulation of micro-textured interfaces via multi-scale topology optimization and numerical simulation
abstract: The critical challenge of excessive junction temperature caused by ultra-high heat flux densities (> 100 W cm −2 ) in deep-sea LED fish-attracting lamp (FAL) arrays is addressed. This study proposes a hybrid thermal management scheme integrating interfacial micro-texturing, chimney effect convection, and heat pipe phase change heat transfer, achieving the unification of passive high-efficiency heat dissipation and pressure-resistant sealing. The FAL housing structure is reconfigured using topology optimization to construct chimney effect enhanced flow channels integrated with heat pipe bundle arrays, thereby establishing efficient heat conduction pathways from the phenolic resin substrate (PRS) to the structural periphery. Micro-element texture (MET) arrays are fabricated at the PRS thermal interface to enhance interfacial thermal conductance. Based on multi-physics coupled numerical simulation, a parametric mapping model correlating geometric topology with thermal performance is established through response interface methodology, enabling the parametric optimization of micro-texture configurations. A thermal interface performance-testing platform is constructed to validate the acc

title: Correction: Using an inclusive bioeconomy framework in support of indigenous peoples and local communities living in mountains
abstract: The ecological health of global mountains today is intimately connected with the current health and future well-being of people and nature on Earth. Mountains cover about 17-20% of the planet's terrestrial surface (Korner et al., 2021), yet highlands harbor over half of all global biodiversity hotspots and 30% of Key Biodiversity Areas (Payne et al., 2020). Montane regions provide disproportionately rich habitats for birds, mammals, and amphibians (Rahbek et al., 2019), and mountain ecosystems offer an array of important ecosystem services. Humans living in highlands have developed rich biocultural traditions and lifeways over centuries and today, some 500 million people dwell at 1500 meters or more above sea level, about 6.5% of all people on Earth (Tremblay and Ainslie, 2021). Links between people and nature are found everywhere in mountains. Upstream, highlands sequester a significant amount of carbon in soils and vegetation that need to be protected for climate change mitigation (Zomer et al., 2023), while downstream, some 20-25% of people on Earth depend on freshwater originating from the world's "water towers" (Viviroli et al., 2020).Yet, global montane regions are under incr

title: Creative Education Utilising a Newly Built Training Vessel: A Proposal for PBL Utilising the Marine Research Equipment on Board the Training Vessel Wakashio-maru
abstract: In March 2026, the Wakashio-maru, a new training vessel for the National Institute of Technology, Toyama College, was completed. Operating primarily in Toyama Bay, which features deep-sea areas exceeding 1,000 metres, the vessel continues a tradition of marine surveys and observation activities carried out for many years by its predecessor. Building on this tradition and past research, the new Wakashio-maru is equipped with state-of-the-art instruments for marine observation and research and is expected to further enhance educational and research activities. During marine surveys aboard the Wakashio-maru, students use observation equipment to collect actual data on water quality, ocean currents and marine life. By analysing and interpreting the data, they experience the entire process, from identifying issues to drawing conclusions. This practical learning environment is believed to contribute markedly to developing data science thinking and problem-solving skills and cultivating creativity – the ability to generate new perspectives and solutions to unfamiliar challenges. Seawater‐Operable Photoelectrochemical Solar‐Blind UV Detectors Enabled by Epitaxial Perovskite Oxide Heterostructures
abstract: ABSTRACT Real‐time, high‐precision underwater monitoring and optical communication are critical for marine resource exploration yet remain hindered by the lack of photodetectors capable of stable, autonomous operation in harsh seawater environments. Herein, we report a robust, self‐powered photoelectrochemical (PEC) deep‐ultraviolet (DUV) photodetector based on an epitaxial La‐doped SrSnO 3 (LSSO)/SrRuO 3 (SRO) architecture. The single‐crystalline epitaxial LSSO film and the high‐quality LSSO/SRO interface suppress defect‐induced recombination and enable efficient separation and transport of photogenerated carriers. Through systematic optimization of La‐doping concentration and operating bias, the device achieves a remarkable peak responsivity of 459.84 mA W −1 in natural seawater, alongside rapid response speeds (rise/fall times of 2.98/2.22 ms). The device shows excellent long‐term stability in natural seawater during PEC operation, with the photoactive surface directly exposed to the electrolyte. title: Is The GKCC the Cradle of Civilization?
abstract: 1 Executive summary 1.1 Overview and Discovery The Gulf of Khambhat Cultural Complex (GKCC) represents a major submerged archaeological discovery located 20 to 40 meters below sea level in the Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay), approximately 20 km off the coast near Hazira. Originally identified during 1999–2000 marine geophysical and pollution-monitoring surveys conducted by the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) under the Department of Ocean Development, the site was brought to light using advanced oceanographic instrumentation. 1.2 Technological Methodology and Scientific Profiling The investigation leveraged a rigorous, multi-disciplinary toolkit to map and evaluate the site, distinguishing itself through strict scientific validation: Marine Geophysics: Side-scan sonars, sub-bottom profilers, multibeam echo-sounders, and caesium vapor marine magnetometers detected expansive rectilinear grids, citadel-like structural basements, granary footprints, and drainage features aligned along paleochannels. title: Which Barriers Drive the Others? Modelling the Interdependencies of Integrated IoT-Blockchain-Big Data Analytics Adoption in Emerging-Economy Maritime Logistics
abstract: Integrated Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and Big Data Analytics (BDA) offer substantial potential to improve visibility, trust, coordination, and decision-making in maritime logistics. However, their combined adoption remains constrained by interdependent technological, organisational, and environmental barriers, particularly in emerging economies. This study identifies these barriers, examines their causal relationships, and develops a sequenced implementation framework for integrated digital transformation. A systematic literature review of 32 studies produced 12 barriers, which were subsequently evaluated through Fuzzy-DEMATEL using judgments from 18 maritime experts. The analysis classified seven barriers as causal drivers and five as dependent outcomes. Lack of management commitment and organisational capability emerged as the strongest driver, followed by limited stakeholder participation and weak ecosystem coordination. The dependent barriers comprised interoperability limitations, inadequate connectivity, resistance to change, scalability constraints, and cybersecurity-related risks. title: Applying Cloud Processing and Big Data Platforms for Global Forest Monitoring
abstract: Climate change is one of the foremost significant global challenges of our day, and its effects are having an impact all across the world. The increasing risk of climate change has led to a growing reliance on modern technology to understand and regulate its profound repercussions. In the past few years, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have been recognized as strong tools for addressing these difficulties by facilitating the creation of innovative climate change adaptation techniques. AI has the potential to analyze enormous amounts of data from simulations of the climate, satellite images, and other sources, providing useful insights that may improve decision-making and help us anticipate the consequences of climate change. Traditional forest-monitoring methods are often too slow and localized to inform timely, large-scale resilience strategies. This chapter explores the synergistic integration of advanced AI, scalable cloud computing, and Big Data platforms as the transformative solution for next-generation global forest monitoring. abstract: Climate change in the form of global warming is taking place. The impact of it on society is severe and unpredictable. The most noticeable evidences are: rise in land and sea temperatures (in particular in summer time), rise in sea levels, and wet winter combined with flash flooding. Dry summers and wet winters are the main contributors to many of the natural disasters in the world, witnessed in the last few decades. These disasters are directly or indirectly associated with soils (i.e., ground) which immediately response to any climatic changes. Soil is also an integral part of the modern infrastructure such as embankments, retaining walls, sub-base for roads and railway tracks, and many more. These structures are often referred to as Geo-Infrastructure. The impacts of climate change on the infrastructure are far-reaching. Policy makers and practicing engineers are fully aware of the consequences of climate change and investing resources to develop adaptation technologies to limit the impact and reduce repair and maintenance costs. title: Designing the Future Port Experience: Architectural Typologies, Space, Place, Technologies and Rituals of Cruise Tourism on the Red Sea
abstract: This thesis examines ports as transitional spaces that shape user experience, as complex urban and cultural spaces where logistical functions intersect with contemporary human experience. A significant lack of literature has been observed concerning port spaces and transit experiences, as well as the factors influencing them, including visual sequencing, boundaries, identity, culture, and the sensory experience of tourists and users within these spaces, in addition to their future roles. Jeddah is used as a case study to frame the changes between the past and present in the port arrival experience. To achieve a deeper understanding of these spaces and develop future port typology models that transcend traditional understandings, this study employs research by design methodology as a flexible research tool. It combines mixed qualitative approaches, such as case studies, ethnographic studies (including mind mapping and drawing maps), and interviews. The study contributed to expanding the use of these analytical tools and developing and testing them through exploratory design scenarios based on speculative design theory within the framework of "what if" questions, resulting in the gen

title: Using Stochastic Processes and Machine Learning to Solve Environmental Challenges : Applications in renewable energy and remote sensing
abstract: This thesis investigates the application of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and environmental statistics to address challenges in renewable energy optimization and environmental monitoring. Environmental systems are inherently complex, dynamic, and uncertain, making data-driven methods particularly valuable for modeling and analysis. Advances in remote sensing technologies and the increasing availability of large-scale environmental data have further enabled the development of AI-based approaches capable of extracting spatial and temporal patterns from heterogeneous and incomplete datasets.The first part of this thesis focuses on the optimization of Wave Energy Converters (WECs). Ocean waves represent a promising renewable energy source due to their high energy density and predictability, but efficient energy extraction requires adaptive system design under stochastic sea conditions. Using statistical models of ocean wave behavior, Papers I and II investigate the optimization of a WEC system developed by the company Waves4Power.% In Paper~I, a simplified model is used to optimize accumulator pressure in the power take-off (PTO) system based on sea state characterist

title: Genotyping of Sea Buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.) Varieties Using Targeted Deep Sequencing
abstract: Abstract Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.) is a valuable berry crop. To improve breeding efficiency and control varietal purity in sea buckthorn collections, it is advisable to use modern genetic technologies. Using whole-genome sequencing data for sea buckthorn varieties, we identified the regions of six genes from the KAS, SAD, and FAD families, which are involved in fatty acid synthesis. We then designed primers to amplify these regions and performed targeted deep sequencing on the Illumina platform for 60 Russian sea buckthorn varieties with breeding/economic value, identifying DNA polymorphisms. Each of the studied varieties had a unique DNA polymorphism profile, allowing us to distinguish them using the proposed approach. The developed approach is promising for genetic certification of sea buckthorn varieties, assessment of varietal purity in collections, selection of parental forms for crosses, control of planting material purity, and protection of breeder’s rights.

title: FSARNet: A network for SAR ship detection based on channel weighted fusion and flexible rotating frame regression
Deep Learning-Based Prediction of Black Sea Nearshore Wind
abstract: Machine learning technologies are increasingly being used in data analysis as potential tools for assessing natural resources. The goal of this study is to determine how successfully the recently released Time Series Modeller (MATLAB R2026a) predicts wind conditions in the Black Sea basin’s nearshore zones. Ten years of hourly ERA5 data (2016–2025) were considered, with the predicted parameters being related to wind speed (at 100 m height) and the corresponding wind direction. A number of deep learning models were evaluated, and the findings were presented using statistical metrics such as RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error), relative error, and the Weibull distribution. The ERA5 and anticipated wind speed showed fair agreement, with the exception of extremely low (<3 m/s) and high wind speeds (>18 m/s), which may have been inflated by the statistical indicator used. The wind dispersion was examined on a monthly and hourly basis. In terms of wind direction, it was discovered that deep learning models are unable to replicate wind conditions from the north sector; nevertheless, this appears to be an issue with models based on RMSE prediction.

title: Collaborative multi-stakeholder approach for preliminary exploratory trials of mesopelagic resources in the Indian EEZ
abstract: This study reports findings from preliminary commercial trials conducted in India’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) to explore the commercial potential of mesopelagic resources in the south-eastern Arabian Sea along the Karnataka coast. Two modified commercial multiday trawl vessels equipped with navigation and fish detection systems conducted 15 midwater trawl hauls at depths of 300-800 m, during night time over a three-month period (January, April, and May 2025). The trials employed a midwater trawl with a 70 m headline, 45 mm mesh, and 20 mm codend mesh, specifically designed for mesopelagic operations, targeting species exhibiting diel vertical migration. A participatory framework involving fishers, boat owners, and industry stakeholders, was adopted to improve operational efficiency, facilitate technology adoption, and support value-chain development. The fishing trials yielded a species-rich catch comprising 40 species belonging to 38 families and 20 orders, with Ophidiidae (23.32%), Pentanchidae (15.94%), and Trachichthyidae (15.05) being dominant families. title: Phytochemicals and pharmacological activities of sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.) leaves: A comprehensive review
abstract: As a high-value byproduct of the medicinal and edible plant sea buckthorn ( Hippophae rhamnoides L.), its leaves are rich in diverse bioactive constituents, including flavonoid glycosides, polyphenols, polysaccharides, and triterpenes. Their total phenolic and flavonoid contents are significantly higher than those found in the fruits, indicating considerable potential for development and utilization. In recent years, green extraction of bioactive compounds, elucidation of their pharmacological mechanisms, and exploration of multi-sector applications have become research hotspots in natural product science. This review summarizes the major bioactive components of sea buckthorn leaves and provides an overview of recent advances in green extraction technologies, including maceration, enzyme-assisted extraction, supercritical CO 2 extraction, ultrasonic-microwave synergistic extraction, and deep eutectic solvent (DES)-chitosan-based ultrasonic-assisted extraction. title: Recent advances in underwater in situ mass spectrometry: instrumentation, deep-sea applications, and challenges
abstract: The ocean is a major component of the Earth system and contains abundant biological, mineral, and energy resources. Conventional laboratory-based analytical methods are limited in underwater environments because sample collection, preservation, and transportation can alter the original chemical composition. In contrast, underwater in situ mass spectrometry enables adaptive sampling and analysis across temporal and spatial dimensions, achieving real-time feedback for in situ , long-term monitoring while significantly reducing labor and material resource consumption. These technologies facilitate qualitative and quantitative monitoring of dissolved gases in aquatic systems, characterized by rapid response and high sensitivity. These systems provide important analytical support for marine environmental monitoring, biogeochemical studies, and resource exploration. This review outlines the core components of underwater in situ systems, including membrane introduction systems, ionization systems, and miniaturized mass spectrometers. title: Retrofitting Acoustic Monitoring; a Wireless Revolution in Brownfield Well Integrity Surveillance
abstract: Abstract Acoustic monitoring technologies, both long and short range are systems that can be placed anywhere in an existing well, usually below a sealing barrier. Encoded pressure, temperature messages and programming commands are sent acoustically across the barrier and well construction elements without disturbing the barrier integrity. These acoustic messages are decoded in real time with surface receivers in dry wellheads or with sub-sea transponders. The data received can be accessed remotely using cloud-based platforms. During a well workover in Europe, the Acoustic Barrier Verification System (ABVS) provided wireless communication over 1300 meters to surface while pressure testing deep-set dual barriers in a gas cavern. Another ABVS was installed inside the upper completion for the workover period to monitor the barriers integrity while pulling the old completion out of hole. This solution ensured safety and real time data knowledge throughout the operations, delivering more efficient and cost-effective barrier monitoring. title: System Integration and Sea Trials of a Containerized Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion Prototype
abstract: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) is a promising renewable energy technology for remote islands, offshore platforms, and maritime infrastructure, yet its commercialization is constrained by low cycle efficiency, high auxiliary energy demand, and the engineering challenges associated with large-scale seawater transport. This study presents the integration and experimental evaluation of a 20 kW class containerized OTEC prototype using R134a in a closed Rankine cycle. The working fluid circulates within the power-generation module, while warm surface seawater supplies the evaporator and cold deep seawater is pumped through an insulated intake pipe to the container-mounted condenser. The prototype integrates a radial-inflow turbine, stainless-steel heat exchangers, circulation pumps, and a programmable logic controller-based control system. Land-based commissioning tests, conducted at initial warm-to-cold-water temperature differences of approximately 20–25 °C, produced a peak electrical output of 11 kW in one run and approximately 5 kW for 11 min in another. title: From Global Bibliometric Insights to Local Action: Advancing Citizen Science and AI for Biodiversity Education and Conservation in Indonesia
abstract: Citizen science has experienced exponential growth since 2010, now contributing over 80% of data to global biodiversity repositories and fundamentally transforming biological inventory systems. However, this growth is accompanied by persistent biases—geographic, taxonomic, and methodological—that limit its full potential. This keynote synthesizes three interrelated strands of work. First, a bibliometric analysis of 200 highly cited publications (2000–2025) from the LeapSpace database reveals strong Global North dominance (USA 59.5%, UK 9.2%), severe taxonomic chauvinism favoring birds (54% of papers), and underrepresentation of tropical rainforests, deep-sea, and soil ecosystems. Advanced methods such as machine learning and spatial bias correction appear in less than 5% of titles, indicating methodological fragmentation. Second, these global findings are translated into local action through community dissemination: training 48 secondary school teachers in the Solo Raya region on AI-assisted species identification using PlantNet and iNaturalist, as well as supporting school leaders in integrating citizen science into school policies. title: Reply on RC2
abstract: Abstract. Ocean monitoring is a crucial component of Earth's observation systems. These systems have evolved to achieve a global scope and an exceptionally high level of complexity, encompassing not only observation programs but also data centres for collection and storage, as well as computational facilities where predictions and re-analyses of oceanic conditions are generated using coupled ocean-atmosphere circulation models. The products generated by the different components of the oceanic observation systems are of paramount importance for the knowledge of the environmental state of the oceans, their variability ranges, the impact of natural and anthropogenic stressors (such as climate change) and, in summary, the appropriate governance of the sea and the sustainable use of its resources. Given the diverse nature of the data (collected through a wide range of technologies, instruments, and institutions across multiple countries), it can be challenging to maintain a comprehensive overview of existing observation programs and datasets. title: The Forced Clan-Drift Theory (FCD): A Universal Interdisciplinary Model for Pleistocene Island Colonization by Early Hominins
abstract: The discovery of Lower Paleolithic stone tools on deep-sea islands such as Flores (approx. 1 million years old) and Crete (approx. 130,000–170,000 years old) presents a fundamental paradox in modern paleoanthropology. Throughout the Pleistocene, these islands were separated from the mainland by deep tectonic trenches (e.g., the Wallace Line and the Hellenic Trench), rendering land-bridge crossings geologically impossible. Established hypotheses—namely deliberate watercraft construction and accidental individual rafting on single logs—fail due to cognitive, physical, and population-biological constraints. This paper introduces the Forced Clan-Drift Theory (FCD), a universal, interdisciplinary model that explains island colonization without attributing advanced seafaring technologies to early hominins. FCD posits that large, resilient, and non-capsizable natural platforms made of intertwined riverine vegetation (such as papyrus or giant bamboo rhizome mats) served as passive oceanic vectors. title: HCTGS v40 Africa — The Largest Infrastructure the World Has Yet to Build
abstract: Abstract Africa withdraws about 270 billion cubic metres of water a year for 1.4 billion people, and the continent's population is projected to reach 3.2 billion by 2070. Most of that withdrawal is agricultural and most of it sits in the basins — the Nile, the Niger, the Senegal, the Congo — where every additional litre is taken from a fixed quantity that already has users. This concept describes a source that adds rather than divides, placed where the coastline already is, and states what it does not reach as plainly as what it does. The architecture is a gravity-fed seawater thermal cascade. Magnesium burns behind a ceramic wall and carries the pipe it heats to about 2,200 °C, with process steam rising inside that pipe at some 20 bar against a wall at 1,500 °C; the steam there is the plant’s own condensate, so the hottest ceramic face stays clear of salt. Rotation comes from the hydrogen–oxygen burner, which meets the water directly, entering horizontally and tangentially below the waterline, with steam injected at twenty to thirty times the flame mass, and the column rotates. title: Flow-particle coupling characteristics and parameter optimization of a dual-jet hydraulic collector based on Box-Behnken design
abstract: The deep-sea floor abounds with polymetallic nodules, effective exploitation of these nodules can alleviate the pressure of terrestrial resource depletion and meet industrial demands. As one of the high-efficiency hydraulic collection approaches, dual-jet technology has been widely adopted. Nevertheless, most existing studies neglect the interaction effects among multiple factors. Accordingly, this study employs the CFD-DEM model combined with the Box-Behnken Design (BBD) to systematically investigate flow-field and particle dynamic characteristics and analyze the weight of parameter influences. The results demonstrate that jet velocity is the dominant factor determining internal flow-field structures. Quantitative analysis within the investigated parameter range shows that jet velocity contributes approximately 65% to vortex formation, while collection height and nozzle spacing account for about 35%. Single-particle analysis reveals that pressure-gradient force and drag force serve as the primary driving mechanisms for particle motion, whereas the Magnus force and Saffman force mainly function at the initial jet-impact stage. title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Driven Remote Sensing and Predictive Analytics for Illegal Underwater Activity Detection
abstract: Although underwater ecosystems have many species and provide economic benefits, they are now being threatened by actions such as unregulated fishing, smuggling by sea, underwater attacks, and violations of boundaries. Older ways of surveillance find it tough to follow what happens in these big and complex waters due to equipment obstacles, changes in the environment, and the secrecy of the activities. And thanks to artificial Intelligence (AI), remote sensing, and predictive analytics joining forces, there is now a better way to deal with threats at sea and in the ocean. The chapter highlights the importance of systems that can respond smartly to new problems and situations, to get early notice and identify threats. This section highlights convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), DRL (deep reinforcement learning), and anomaly detection algorithms to show how they power the extraction of useful insights from sonar information, underwater sounds, and sensor data. title: Enhancing Sustainability of European Floating Structures Through Renewable Energy Integration
abstract: The deployment of renewable energy technologies is a key pathway for exploiting offshore resources and supporting the transition toward sustainable power generation. Floating offshore structures enable energy extraction in deep-water environments where conventional fixed systems are not feasible. This study presents an evidence-based assessment of the renewable energy potential associated with floating offshore structures in European seas and proposes an integrated framework for evaluating their sustainable design. The analysis is based on a curated dataset of European offshore energy projects, including installed capacity, spatial distribution, and technology-specific development indicators. A statistical approach is applied to characterize regional variability and identify dominant deployment trends. The results show a rapid expansion of floating offshore wind capacity, accompanied by the emergence of floating photovoltaic systems and hybrid wave–wind–solar configurations, while revealing significant regional differences in technological maturity, project scale, and growth rates. title: Identification of Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) Along Kerala Coast, India
abstract: Parameters that refer to fish existence can be identified by remote sensing techniques using satellite sensor data. Identification of potential fishing zones with the aid of remote sensing technology is a crucial need for the fisher flocks to get profitable catch by less fuel consumption, effort, and time as well. In this study, two different parameters, chlorophyll concentration and sea surface temperature (SST), were taken from satellite-derived data. For this purpose, Aqua MODIS data were used for chlorophyll concentration, and NOAA-AVHRR data were used for SST extraction. The chlorophyll concentration in the deep-sea area is 0.2 mg/m3 to 0.3 mg/m3; however, at the close of the Kerala coast, the chlorophyll concentration is around 0.4 mg/m3. For sea surface temperature, the obtained range is from 21 °C to 31 °C. Using SST and Chlorophyll, the potential fishing zone (PFZ) is mapped over the Kerala coast, India. title: Biosynthetic Diversity of Marine-Derived Streptomyces Natural Products: Integrating Genome Mining, Multi-Omics, and Translational Drug Discovery Strategies
abstract: Marine-derived Streptomyces are among the most prolific producers of structurally diverse and biologically active natural products. Adaptation to unique marine environments, including deep-sea sediments, hydrothermal vents, mangrove ecosystems, marine invertebrates, and hypersaline habitats, has promoted the evolution of specialized biosynthetic systems capable of generating a broad spectrum of secondary metabolites. These metabolites include polyketides, non-ribosomal peptides (NRPs), ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), terpenoids, alkaloids, and hybrid compounds with significant antibacterial, antifungal, antiviral, antiparasitic, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. Recent advances in genome sequencing, bioinformatics, genome mining, metabolomics, synthetic biology, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted discovery have substantially expanded marine natural product research by enabling the identification and prioritization of previously inaccessible biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs). title: Mattering~with
abstract: Those who tire easily of saltwater struggle with Abdulrazak Gurnah&s;s writing too. Not that the briny matter is visible everywhere in Gurnah necessarily; it is easy, in fact, to lose sight of it in the compulsive meanders of his raconteurs. But the dampness follows us around every bend, muddies the dust of the East African interior and the concrete of urban England on every page, until it errs its way back into colonial and migrational environments. The saltwater builds houses, fills up rooms and exposes its furniture to mould, evokes and erodes memories of the slave trade, drifts the migrant across the seas and enters their worst nightmares in the pang of mob violence, like a mirage that strangles the horizon of arrival. It is, maybe, for this ubiquitousness that water lingers on as the one unreadable element in Gurnah&s;s imagination. This book follows this somewhat counterintuitive logic, for it aims to de-emphasise a state of alterity in Abdulrazak Gurnah&s;s writing as part of the Indian Ocean&s;s cultural politics and instead approach his literary geographies as sites of material porosity, where history is understood in the dynamic interface of human and nonhuman matters.
