title: Porosity Prediction in Tight Reservoirs via Elastic Decoupling Factor-Constrained Prestack Density Inversion: A Case Study from the Bohai Bay Basin
abstract: The Paleogene deep tight glutenite reservoirs in the Bohai Sea area feature strong heterogeneity and complex pore structures, posing significant challenges to the seismic prediction of sweet-spot reservoirs. Uncertain reservoir-sensitive factors and insufficient large-angle information from seismic gathers, together with the low accuracy of conventional prestack density inversion, lead to considerable porosity prediction errors and make it difficult to identify high-quality reservoirs. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel prestack density inversion method constrained by an elastic decoupling factor (EDF) for porosity prediction in tight reservoirs. First, rock physics modeling is performed using a variable aspect ratio Xu–White model, based on which a reservoir-type indicator and a porosity-sensitive factor are constructed to establish differentiated solution equations among density, Poisson’s ratio, and porosity. Second, to overcome the strong dependence of density inversion on large-angle information, an EDF is formulated to decouple density from S-wave impedance, thereby reducing inversion non-uniqueness. title: Factor effect analyses on radionuclide release rate from a spent nuclear fuel transport cask submerged in deep sea for surrogate model development
abstract: In Korea, maritime transportation of spent nuclear fuel (SNF) is considered as a highly plausible management option. It is necessary to develop technology to assess the radiological impact of SNF cask submersion accidents to manage the risk caused by the maritime transportation of SNF and to find the optimal transport route to minimize the risk. In our previous work, a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was developed to accurately evaluate the mass release rate of radionuclides from a submerged cask. The final goal of this study is to establish a methodological framework to develop a surrogate model of the developed CFD model and integrate it as a subroutine into the SNF maritime transportation risk assessment code. This paper addresses several key aspects, including the definition of the input space and the determination of the surrogate model's validity domain, in order to ensure accurate predictions across a wide range of accident and transport scenarios. title: Parametric study of CO2 sequestration in Sleipner field using MRST simulator
abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) capture and storage (CCS) is an important technology for reducing CO₂ emissions and mitigating climate change. Geological storage in deep saline formations offers significant potential for long-term CO₂ sequestration due to their large storage capacity. This thesis investigates CO₂ storage in the Utsira Formation at the Sleipner field in the North Sea using the MATLAB Reservoir Simulation Toolbox (MRST) and the MRST-co2lab module. A Vertical Equilibrium (VE) modelling approach is employed to simulate the migration and distribution of injected CO₂ within the reservoir. Three injection scenarios of 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 Mt CO₂/year are examined, with injection occurring for 100 years and the subsequent CO₂ behaviour simulated over a total period of 1000 years. The study focuses on the effect of injection rate on CO₂ plume evolution and long-term storage behaviour. The simulations evaluate the spatial distribution and migration of the CO₂ plume and the role of geological trapping mechanisms, particularly structural and residual trapping. title: Techno-solutionism and the use of emerging technologies in pushing frontiers of mining
abstract: This chapter focuses on the concept of extractivism and the increasing role of emerging technologies (such as AI, drones, and satellites) in the expansion of resource frontiers. Techno-solutionist promises often quickly fall apart when discussing the actual possibilities of application. However, mining is a sector where the promises have kept growing and attracting large investments. Mining companies have touted the use of emerging technologies in geological surveying as vital for the green transition, while these technologies allow for the expansion of extractive frontiers to remote places, including the deep sea and outer space. From the perspective of extractivism, this is not surprising: a new technology is being used to find new directions for its advancement. This chapter analyzes the claims that companies and proponents of using emerging technologies for mining exploration and expanding mining use to sell their services and justify mining expansion. It focuses in particular on the cases of Kobold Metals in Zambia and Fleet Space Technologies in collaboration with Barrick Gold in Pakistan. title: Unrepeatered remote Φ-OTDR system with single-ended amplifier using hollow-core leading fiber
abstract: Phase-sensitive Optical Time Domain Reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) is widely used for monitoring critical infrastructure. However, conventional Φ-OTDR systems are limited by fiber nonlinear effects, which restrict the probe pulse energy and thus limit the sensing distance. To overcome this bottleneck, this paper innovatively proposes a Φ-OTDR scheme that uses a hollow-core fiber as a leading fiber (LF-HCF). The design leverages the low nonlinearity and low transmission loss of HCF to transmit high-power probe pulse light to a remote fiber under test (RFUT) and to return the backscattered signal generated by the RFUT back to the detection end. In this way, it overcomes the power threshold limitation of conventional Φ-OTDR systems and achieves ultra-long-distance unrepeatered sensing. Moreover, the extremely low transmission delay of the HCF further broadens the system’s vibration response range. Experimental results demonstrate that, over a total transmission distance of 280 km (consisting of 230 km of LF‑HCF and 50 km of RFUT), the system maintains a 1‑meter spatial resolution at the RFUT. title: Anode-Layer Ion Source-Assisted Deposition and Bias Voltage Tuning of CrWNbTaMoVSiN High-Entropy Nanostructured Coatings
abstract: In extreme working conditions such as deep-sea and aerospace, failure due to friction and wear of key metal components is very frequent. Traditional binary or ternary nitride protective coatings are unable to achieve a coordinated improvement in terms of hardness, wear resistance, and structural stability. In this manuscript, a high-entropy composite nano-coating of CrWNbTaMoVSiN with an alternating structure of metal and nitride layers was prepared by using anode layer ion source-assisted magnetron sputtering technology. The influence of substrate bias voltage on the microstructure, phase structure, surface chemical state, friction and wear properties of coatings was systematically studied. The findings demonstrate that the substrate bias voltage has a substantial impact on the structure and performance of the CrWNbTaMoVSiN coatings. As the bias voltage increases, the coating deposition rate and thickness decrease, while the grain growth morphology gradually transitions from directionally aligned columnar crystals to equiaxed crystals. title: From the Deep Sea to Canvas: Using Art to Engage Youth with Ocean Technology
abstract: Oceans Unmined is a science communication and conservation advocacy platform co-founded by a marine scientist and an artist, built on a single conviction: that the deep sea cannot be protected by people who have never been given the chance to imagine it. Our flagship program – the science-art workshop – brings together deepsea scientific imagery, expedition footage, and acoustic recordings from the ocean floor, and invites participants to respond creatively. The workshop is not a drawing class or a science lecture. It sits deliberately between the two. We begin with technology. Participants are introduced to instruments that allow scientists to reach the deep sea. We show footage from actual research expeditions We play sounds. Then we give participants paper, pencils, paint, cameras, whatever medium they prefer and ask them one question: What do you see?

title: Investing in people, infrastructure, and meaningful collaboration is key for deep-sea biodiversity research and management in South Africa
abstract: Abstract After over a century of global research in the deep ocean, many nations continue to face barriers to developing and sustaining deep-sea research and management in their own waters. This prevents sound environmental management and limits nations’ potential to derive benefits from the deep sea. In this perspective paper, we draw on the experiences of established and early career researchers and managers in South Africa, to reflect on key obstacles limiting deep-sea biodiversity research and management in the country and propose potential solutions to strengthen the field. Challenges range from a lack of equal opportunity, cultural barriers, and poor retention of expertise, to limited financial support, low exposure to and perceived irrelevance of the deep sea, limited access to vessels and technology, and inequitable international standards and partnerships. Key enablers to support capacity development and increase equal opportunities in South African deep-sea biodiversity research and management include increased early exposure to the ocean and deep sea, financial and academic support, access to vessels and technology, and development of meaningful collaborations. title: Essay on Blue Economy Diversification
abstract: The Blue Economy provides a strategic framework for coastal nations to decouple economic growth from environmental degradation through blue economic diversification. This study examines the shift from traditional, mono-sectoral dependence on offshore oil and gas or artisanal fishing toward a multi-dimensional maritime portfolio. By analyzing emerging sectors such as marine biotechnology, offshore renewable energy, and sustainable aquaculture, the research evaluates how diversification mitigates the economic volatility inherent in extractive industries. Findings suggest that diversification is not merely an expansion of industrial activity but a transition toward a circular maritime economy that integrates "blue carbon" sequestration with high-value eco-tourism. The study identifies technology transfer and maritime spatial planning as the primary drivers of this transition. However, significant bottlenecks persist, including high capital requirements for deep-sea innovation and the overarching threat of climate-induced sea level rise. title: Study of an Automatic Control and Management System for Air Intake and Exhaust in Submersible Net Cages
abstract: To mitigate the challenges of excessive tilting angles and the risk of overturning during the submersion and ascent of the net cage, this study developed an automatic control and management system for submersible net cages. The system employs proportional–integral–derivative (PID) control technology, optimizing PID parameters through tilt signals and control algorithms to adjust actuators, thereby enabling automatic regulation of the net cage tilt angle. The accompanying management system integrates several functionalities, including submersion and elevation control, suspension control, water level monitoring, pressure data monitoring, current velocity measurement, water quality monitoring, GPS positioning, and underwater camera surveillance. Through a series of experiments, the most suitable buoyancy-to-gravity ratio for the net cage was determined to be 1.2. Experimental results identified optimal PID parameters for submersion (P = 100, I = 1000, D = 0) and ascent (P = 50, I = 800, D = 0), and suspension control was achieved using a compressed air pressure of 0.40 kPa. title: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Underwater Vision Enhancement Techniques for Sustainable Water Management Applications
abstract: Introduction: Sustainable management of marine and freshwater environments requires effective monitoring. However, in underwater visual data acquisition, the effects of light attenuation and scattering vary with wavelength, degrading image quality. Methods: In this study, the latest underwater image enhancement algorithms were systematically evaluated on 5 publicly available databases (UIEB, Sea-Thru, RUIE, SUIM and URPC2020). Altogether, 3 main method categories (classical processing, physical model-based approaches and deep learning methods) are compared in terms of the following objective performance metrics: mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5), Underwater Image Quality Measure (UIQM), Underwater Color Image Quality Evaluation (UCIQE), processing time and memory consumption. results: This benchmark is an entire indication of how image enhancement technologies are critical towards supporting effective visual surveillance systems in water management applications. title: Cascaded Dual‐Load Wireless Power Transfer Technology With Power and Frequency Independent Characteristics
abstract: ABSTRACT The deep‐sea environment is complex, necessitating the development of cluster systems to meet diverse tasks. Due to variations in power levels, a single wireless power transfer (WPT) system struggles to meet the energy requirements of multiple devices. Designing separate WPT systems for each device would significantly increase the entire complexity. Therefore, in this letter, a cascaded dual‐load WPT system is proposed to address this challenge. The topology comprises a primary resonant network for high‐power transmission and a secondary resonant network. The latter harvests energy from the third‐harmonic current to deliver a stable output voltage for low‐power loads. The cascaded structure enhances the system's power density. Furthermore, as impedance isolation between the two loads is achieved through a dedicated mechanism, independent frequency and output power adjustment of the two resonant networks is allowed, thus enhancing design flexibility.

title: The Opacity Trap: Why States Wait to Govern Emerging Technologies
abstract: Abstract Arms control overwhelmingly concerns technologies that states already possess rather than those they might one day develop. Why do states prefer to control today’s technologies tomorrow instead of controlling tomorrow’s technologies today? I argue that technological secrecy produces an opacity trap: states must conceal technological details that could betray important discoveries to rivals, but mutual secrecy obscures who is actually ahead. Thus, the very secrecy states need to compete is also what blinds them to whether technological competition is worth preventing. I formalize this logic with an endogenous learning model, showing how the information needed to make anticipatory control attractive usually only arises through competition itself. By the time states realize they are ensnared in unwinnable competitions, the technologies they are competing over have already been produced. The theory is tested with archival research into two little-known cases—environmental-modification weapons and deep-sea missile launchers—alongside original data on nearly 250 weapons governance agreements since 1850. title: Review on Generation Mechanisms, Monitoring Methods and Control Technologies of Underwater Noise from Offshore Wind Power
abstract: Offshore wind power development is expanding from nearshore fixed projects to large-capacity, clustered and deep-sea floating projects. As a result, underwater noise generated during construction, operation and decommissioning activities has become a key constraint in environmental impact assessment and engineering permitting. Based on relevant journal studies published publicly from 2016 to 2025, this paper systematically compares the acoustic characteristics of impact pile driving, structural vibration during operation, floating mooring systems and decommissioning operations along the chain of "sound source - structural transmission - marine propagation - monitoring characterization - ecological response - engineering control". It summarizes the applicable boundaries of empirical models, parabolic equation models and structure-fluid-acoustic coupling models, and concludes the combined application of hydrophones, vibration sensors, passive acoustic monitoring and acoustic telemetry. The review shows that relatively complete technical systems have been formed for the prediction and bubble curtain control of impulse noise during construction. Sustainable Aqua-Tech: Transforming Aquaculture in Bangladesh Using Modern Technological Innovations
abstract: Aquaculture in Bangladesh is primarily characterized by smallholder inland freshwater carp, pangas, and tilapia farming in ponds, as well as some shrimp and prawn farming in coastal areas. It is quite different from the large-scale offshore systems frequently discussed in global technology reviews, so there is a gap between the available innovations and what is feasible locally. This review covers technologies like IoT, Cloud computing, Artificial intelligence, Robotics, Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS), Integrated Multi-Trophic Aquaculture (IMTA), aquaponics, and Alternative protein feeds for fish. The technologies are assessed for their suitability to the size, infrastructure, and economics of Bangladeshi aquaculture. The results indicate that the most feasible alternatives for the present are the use of low-cost sensor-based aeration, mobile and SMS management tools, small-scale biofloc-assisted RAS for hatcheries and high-value species, and plant or insect-based feed alternatives. title: A New Stage of Capitalism Has Been Born
abstract: In the present chapter, I introduce readers to the theory of Thana Capitalism, giving not only some fresh examples, but numbers how the cultural entertainment industry revolves around death. From this perspective, I conduct a review of the Risk Society in Ulrich Beck and the end of the Precautionary Principle. The birthdate of Thana Capitalism should be traced back to the turn of the 20th century, a stage of uncertainty marked by the Twin Towers’ collapse. This event shocked the world but was accompanied by global dangers that placed postmodern society between the wall and the deep blue sea. I take the opportunity to review the classic essays of the founding fathers of sociology, Marx/Durkheim/Weber, to explain how leisure has changed from industrial society to Thana Capitalism. I propose that tourism has evolved in three stages: classic tourism, sustainable tourism, and the rise of new morbid forms of tourism. Lastly, I identify death-seekers, as this emergent class was baptized in this book, who correspond with a new group more prone to consume death, in many cases through visual and virtual high technology.

title: Editorial: Rapid change in polar pelagic ecosystems: new challenges on causes and effects of climate variability
abstract: Polar pelagic ecosystems are undergoing rapid change as climate variability intensifies and human pressures increase. These waters support productive and diverse communities whose dynamics are closely linked to sea ice, water-mass structure and extreme seasonal variation in light. The Arctic and Southern Ocean differ markedly in their physical oceanography, and these contrasts influence how each region responds to environmental change (Meredith et al., 2019). As climate-driven pressures increase, regional differences are becoming more pronounced, contributing to shifts in biodiversity, food-web structure and ecosystem functioning, with implications for global biogeochemical cycles (IPCC, 2022).Pelagic species are responding rapidly to changing environmental conditions and are increasingly recognised as indicators of ecosystem change. Altered sea-ice regimes, changing upper-ocean structure and ocean warming affect species distributions, migration patterns, dietary preferences and seasonal life cycles, with consequences that propagate through food webs (Atkinson et al., 2019). title: ENVIRONMENTAL ASPECTS OF COMBINED DEPRESSURIZATION AND ELECTROMAGNETIC HEATING METHOD FOR HYDRATE EXTRACTION
abstract: Deep-sea natural gas hydrate resources have attracted widespread attention as a new type of energy source, and how to develop natural gas hydrates safely and effectively is currently the focus of research. The most commonly used extraction method for deep-sea natural gas hydrates is the depressurization method, but it faces problems such as the formation of secondary hydrates in the wellbore during the later stages of extraction. Therefore, we have incorporated electromagnetic heating technology into the depressurization extraction method. This method uses electromagnetic heating to controllably raise the temperature inside the wellbore, effectively inhibiting and eliminating the formation of secondary hydrates and ensuring unobstructed flow channels within the wellbore. Compared with traditional methods, electromagnetic heating technology has advantages such as fast response speed, uniform heating, and ease of control, solving the problem of secondary hydrate formation in the wellbore. title: Hyperspectral Technology: A Method Framework for the Estimation of Metal Content in Cobalt-Rich Crusts
abstract: Cobalt-rich ferromanganese crusts are an important deep-sea mineral resource, and the ore grade is a key indicator for evaluating their resource potential. Conventional ore-grade assessment relies on representative samples and extensive laboratory analyses, posing significant challenges due to limited sampling opportunities, high operational costs, and the pronounced structural heterogeneity of the crusts. To enable rapid estimation, the study combined uncalibrated hyperspectral radiance data acquired under natural daylight (without conversion to reflectance) with high-resolution electron probe micro-analysis (EPMA) measurements from the MED69A sample collected from the Magellan Seamounts to construct a sample-scale spectral–chemical dataset. This dataset was used to systematically compare spectral preprocessing methods, feature band selection strategies, and machine learning models. Based on the overall evaluation, the CR-CARS-MLP framework was selected as the optimal approach for spectral feature extraction, informative band selection, and metal concentration estimation under the current acquisition conditions. title: Distributed Fiber Optic Sensing as a Next-Generation Platform for Acoustic UHE Neutrino Detection
abstract: Emerging optoacoustic sensing technologies offer a promising pathway for advancing the acoustic detection of ultra--high energy (UHE) neutrinos in the deep sea. Distributed Fiber Optic Sensing (DFOS), and in particular Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS), enables the transformation of standard submarine telecommunication fibers into dense arrays of virtual hydrophones, with measurement points spaced at the meter scale along tens of kilometres. Recent developments in DFOS on subsea telecom cables have demonstrated the capability to monitor acoustic fields over basin scale distances, providing continuous, wide aperture coverage well suited for detecting impulsive pressure waves expected from neutrino induced thermoacoustic cascades. Within this context, the INFN cabled seabed network installed offshore Capo Passero (South-East Sicily) serving the KM3NeT neutrino telescope may represent an ideal testbed for next generation neutrino acoustic detection. A DAS system is already operating using the 100 km long main electro optical cable to monitoring underwater soundscape up to 500 Hz. title: Transient numerical reconstruction and multi-parameter safety regulation of liquid accumulation–slug flow coupling behavior in deep-sea flexible risers for underwater compressed gas energy storage
abstract: Underwater compressed gas energy storage (UWCGES) is an emerging marine energy storage technology, yet liquid accumulation and slug flow in flexible risers pose critical threats to operational safety and stability. This study establishes a full-size numerical model of an American Petroleum Institute (API)-compliant 18-layer flexible riser for 500 m water depth UWCGES systems and reproduces realistic subsea operating conditions using the Offshore Lagrangian Gas and multiphase Analysis multiphase flow platform. A series of graded gas flow rates is adopted to conduct 36-h continuous simulations, systematically revealing the spatiotemporal evolution of liquid accumulation, the dynamic characteristics of slug flow, and the coupled pressure response mechanism. Results show that liquid accumulation initiates at the elbow and gradually spreads to the inclined section, with liquid holdup negatively correlated with gas flow rate but limited by a critical threshold. Slug flow exhibits a four-stage periodic motion: accumulation, outflow, ejection, and backflow, which induces severe periodic pressure fluctuations and reverses the pressure distribution between the inlet and elbow. title: Single‐Atom Catalysts in Harsh Environments: Activity, Stability, and Structural Dynamic
abstract: Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as promising materials due to their exceptional catalytic activity, well‐defined active sites, and near‐maximum atomic utilization efficiency, showing great potential in energy conversion and environmental protection. However, under harsh operating conditions, SACs face significant challenges related to catalytic activity and structural stability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the recent progress and future prospectives of SACs functioning under harsh environments, including high temperatures, strong acidic/alkaline media, and high‐energy radiation fields. We systematically analyze the intrinsic characteristics of SACs that make them susceptible to atomic migration, aggregation, and coordination structure disruption in these harsh environments. Particular emphasis is placed on recent advances in operando characterization techniques such as in situ transmission electron microscopy, X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, and multiscale simulations, which have provided critical insights into the relationships between of structure and performance. Despite progress, SACs still struggle with the trade‐off between activity and stability

title: Effects of stress on CO2 hydrate sequestration stability in deep-sea sediments: A molecular dynamics simulation study
abstract: Hydrate-based CO 2 sequestration technology represents a highly promising strategy for deep-sea carbon storage. The stability of CO 2 hydrate sequestration within the confined space of deep-sea sediments is a critical factor determining its feasibility. In this study, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were utilized to investigate the effects of shear, compressive, and shear-compressive coupling stress on the structural stability, phase transition, rheological behavior, and mechanical properties of CO 2 hydrate within clay nanopores of various sizes. The results indicate that under shear stress, CO 2 hydrate undergoes dissociation progressing from the periphery towards the center, with the extent of dissociation directly proportional to the shear rate. Additionally, the bound water layer coating the clay surface exhibits shear-thinning behavior. Under compressive stress, the CO 2 hydrate displays overall structural destruction. Under shear-compressive coupling stress, the dissociation of CO 2 hydrate is accelerated, but the destruction is primarily dominated by compressive stress-induced dissociation. title: Colloidal Quantum Dots‐Based Bioinspired Reconfigurable Photoelectrochemical Device for Broadband Underwater Imaging and Photosynaptic Memory
abstract: ABSTRACT Underwater artificial visual systems that couple visual perception with memory capabilities are of great significance for intelligent marine environmental monitoring, autonomous underwater robotics, and deep‐sea resource exploration, thereby requiring intelligent optoelectronic devices with broadband spectral adaptability and multifunctional photodetection (PD)/photosynaptic (PS) functionalities. Here, inspired by the spectral adaptation and homing memory of Pacific salmon, we report a reconfigurable photoelectrochemical (PEC) device based on near‐infrared (NIR) CuInSeS/ZnSe (CISeS/ZnSe) quantum dots (QDs), in which the Ag incorporation enables spectral adaptation through redshifted absorption while weakening non‐adiabatic coupling (NAC) of QDs to suppress non‐radiative recombination. title: Proactive Service Composition Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: With the development of cloud-network integration technology, how to compose cloud-network services with similar functions but inconsistent Quality of Service (QoS) to meet the diverse needs of users in different scenarios, such as space, air, land, and sea, has become an important research topic in the field of service computing. However, traditional service composition approaches ignore the importance of actively selecting the nearest server for service composition by perceiving user’s mobility, which may lead in delayed delivery of results to users after service composition is completed. Moreover, these approaches ignore the geographic spatial characteristics in the cloud-network environment. When facing a massive number of cloud-network services, individual servers may struggle to meet users' QoS requirements, leading to inefficient proactive service composition. To address these issues, this paper proposes an innovative service composition approach, called Proactive Service Composition Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (PSCDRL). title: China in the Horn of Africa: Connectivity, Security, and the Limits of Regional Integration
abstract: The Horn of Africa region is a key geopolitical and geoeconomic intersection in the transforming world order of the 21st century. The proximity of the Red Sea, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Gulf of Aden, and the Suez Canal makes the region strategically significant for global trade, energy security, and great-power competition. At the same time, the region is characterized by persistent political instability, inter-state and internal conflicts, weak institutional capacities, and low levels of regional integration. The study examines the extent to which China’s originally primarily economic and infrastructural presence in the region is shifting into a broader security-development role, and its impact on the region’s development and regional integration. The analysis is based on frameworks of world order transformation, geoeconomics, and regional integration, with particular attention to the Chinese Belt and Road Initiative and the strategic role of infrastructure and connectivity. Ethiopia emerges as a prominent case study: both the Addis Ababa light rail and the Addis Ababa–Djibouti railroad illustrate the transformative potential and limitations of Chinese-funded infrastructure. title: From Empire to Arsenal: Structural Parallels in British Naval Procurement and Post-WWII U.S. Defense Acquisition
abstract: Procurement systems are not administrative machinery. They are structural organisms. They evolve not through deliberate design but through recursive adaptation, institutional sedimentation, and the gradual consolidation of contractor-state symbiosis. This paper examines two procurement systems separated by two centuries and an ocean: British naval procurement from the Restoration (1660) to the end of the Victorian era (1900), and U.S. defense procurement from the Second World War to the present. The comparison is analytical, not genetic. It identifies structural recurrences: patterns of contractor-state symbiosis, bureaucratic routinization, credentialized expertise, narrative legitimization, finance-logistics coupling, and long-cycle budgetary recursion that appear across both cases despite vast differences in technology, scale, and political structure. Seven structural parallels are established. First, contractor-state symbiosis: in both systems, the state depends on private contractors for essential capabilities, generating mutual dependence and, therefore, capture. title: Analysis of Challenges in the Mechanical Design of Offshore Wind Turbines
abstract: This article examines the key engineering challenges associated with the mechanical design of offshore wind turbines operating in harsh marine environments. The study discusses the main structural categories–foundations, towers, and rotors–emphasizing their suitability for different sea depths and geological conditions. Mechanical factors that significantly influence structural reliability are analysed, including loads, corrosion, fatigue, vibration, and aerodynamic as well as mechanical noise. The research also highlights current technological trends such as the increasing use of composite materials, hybrid tower structures, anti–corrosion solutions, floating platforms for deep–water installations, and smart monitoring systems supported by artificial intelligence. Additionally, the paper evaluates international experience and its relevance to the Baltic Sea region, focusing on Lithuania’s potential and engineering priorities for offshore wind development. The findings show that the integration of modern materials, digital diagnostics, and advanced foundation technologies can considerably improve operational efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, and extend structural lifespan.

title: GoNorth 2022 Cruise Report
abstract: The Norwegian part of the Arctic, including Svalbard, is undergoing major climatic changes, affecting sea ice, the ocean, and marine life. Yet substantial knowledge gaps remain, particularly in the central Arctic Ocean, where accessibility is limited and conducting research activities requires specialised equipment. On longer time scales, the Arctic Ocean has also undergone major geological changes. Evolving from being an isolated, partly freshwater basin, the Arctic Ocean is now an integrated part of the global ocean. When and how this transition occurred is still unclear, largely due to limited geological and geophysical data. The GoNorth project aims to reduce these knowledge gaps through four multidisciplinary cruises onboard of RV Kronprins Haakon between 2022 and 2025. The project will also provide extensive training opportunities and will help build Arctic research capacity. The first GoNorth cruise took place from 14 October to 19 November 2022 and was divided into two legs. The first leg (14 October–3 November 2022) started and ended in Longyearbyen including 29 scientists and research engineers from nine institutions. The study area lay north of Nordaustlandet and Kvitøya

title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND FINTECH ON TRADE ROUTE MANAGEMENT
abstract: It has been set out to explore how the digital revolution and the rise of Fintech are fundamentally changing the way global trade routes are managed. The goal is to see if these new tools could fix the old headaches of international trade—think sky-high costs, shadowy processes, and constant security worries—and replace them with supply chains that actually work better, stay safe, and respect the planet. Instead of just looking at numbers, we took a deep dive into qualitative insights by combing through academic papers, latest industry trends, and real-world case studies. It is paid close attention to the heavy hitters: blockchain, smart contracts, digital payments, and AI-powered logistics. To make it practical, we looked at how these technologies are performing in the real world across vital trade links like the Black Sea, the Middle Corridor, and the New Silk Road. The result of the paper is to going digital makes everything smoother. It cuts down waiting times, handles boring paperwork automatically, and finally lets everyone see what’s happening in the supply chain in real-time. It was also found that Fintech is a game-changer for smaller businesses (SMEs) and developing areas

title: What the Sea Pushes Against: Choosing a coastal energy system when the site, not the technology, makes the decision
abstract: A coastal machine should be selected by what it pushes against, and paid for by what it produces — and electricity is rarely the best product. Coastal and island communities with weak grids or none pay some of the highest electricity prices on earth and sit beside one of the largest untapped energy resources on earth. The obvious response is to build a machine that turns waves into electricity. That framing has produced four decades of prototypes and very few installations, because there is no box to buy: a wave machine is at least three things — a structure that takes the load, a conversion and transmission chain, and a store — and each is chosen independently, from different constraints, by different people. Change the site and any one can flip while the other two stay put. This document is therefore a selection guide rather than a design. It organises converters into three families by what they react against — BEDROCK against the seabed, BULWARK against the shore, DRIFTER against itself — gives a compatibility table showing which conversion chains and stores each family can actually take, and screens sites twice: once on what the site can supply, and once on what the community w

abstract: This theme includes research focusing on the development, optimization, and application of deep learning (CNNs, MLPs, Transformers, YOLO, etc.) for leaf segmentation, detecting crop diseases, and pests. Papers here cover both detection/classification and segmentation using advanced computer vision techniques.Qiu et al track movements and behaviours of the litchi pest (Thalassodes immissaria), a major pest in litchi and longan fruit tree orchards, in 3D using a binocular vision observation system for nighttime observation and thermal infrared imagery using YOLOX-GMM and SORT-Pest algorithms to reconstruct movement trajectories. The YOLOX, SORT-Pest, and GMM algorithms are widely applied motion target detection algorithms in image processing. YOLOX is a high-performance, open-source object detection model that has revolutionized the YOLO family by transitioning to an anchor-free architecture to simplify the detection process, enabling faster inference. title: 3D-Printed Biomimetic Sponge-Based Broadband and Highly Efficient Terahertz Absorber
abstract: With the rapid advancement of terahertz technology, electromagnetic interference has become a critical issue that compromises device performance, creating an urgent demand for high-performance terahertz absorbers. Three-dimensional (3D) printing, characterized by flexible structural design, monolithic fabrication, and mold-free processing, has emerged as a promising technique for producing terahertz absorbers. In this work, inspired by the structural and functional characteristics of deep-sea sponges, we propose a bioinspired absorber design that integrates a porous topology with 3D printing. By optimizing the rotation angle and the hollowed array, the absorber establishes multiple internal reflection paths, which, combined with the structural matrix and the graphene conductive coating, enable highly efficient dissipation of electromagnetic energy. Experimental results show that the fabricated sample achieves an absorptivity exceeding 99% over the 0.5–2.0 THz frequency range, while also exhibiting wide-angle absorption and polarization-insensitive performance. The influence of pore size and graphene concentration on the absorption properties is systematically revealed. This work fu

title: Military policy – challenges of high technologies
abstract: This article examines the peculiarities of the influence of modern high technologies on military policy and national security of the state. The author notes that there has been a transition from the three-dimensional environment of military confrontation to a multidimensional – spatial one. The space of struggle is becoming not only the aerospace, marine and land environment, but also the deep rear, the information environment and the psychology of the masses. In this area, which is unusual and undeveloped for subjects of military policy, high-tech means of warfare are beginning to play a leading role, that is, weapons based on new information technology and physical principles, including artificial intelligence. The author refers to modern technologies of military policy as technical means – unmanned aerial, land and sea vehicles, as well as concepts of a socio-informational nature, called “soft power”, “smart power”, “hard power” in the West. The results of a sociological study conducted by the Department of Political Sciences at Saratov State University confirmed the influence of modern technologies on military policy. title: Aural Augmented Reality for Ecological Storytelling: Sonic Heritage, Sensory Embodiment, & Situated Knowledge in Maastricht's Natural Heritage Landscape
abstract: Aural augmented reality is a burgeoning sub-field in the area of digital humanities and digital storytelling, reflecting a broader turn towards multimodal and sensory approaches to narrative, cultural heritage, and embodied digital experiences (Hagedoorn & Sauer 2018). While much digital humanities research privileges textual (and to some degree visual) communication, a recent emphasis in sound as a medium for exploring geographical or spatial narratives, embodiment, and the materiality of place and space indicates a warming towards experimenting with other forms of narrative creation and expression (Zhang, Song, & Liu 2024; Münster & Terras 2019; Hall 2011). Podcasts, sound walks, audio guides, and other forms of auditory engagement have risen in popularity, and the current edge of experimentation lies in creating innovative and creative digital experiences through the use of sound. Technological developments in regard to wide-spread geolocation, affordability of data, increased accessibility to digital devices, and the release of increasingly more user-friendly mobile augmented reality platforms have made it possible for researchers to engage with a new form of site-specific inte

title: DeepLitterAI: Automated detection and quantification of deep-sea benthic plastic and macrolitter with field validation in waters around Japan
abstract: Deep-sea imagery is a non-destructive tool for monitoring seafloor litter, but manual inspection limits its scalability. DeepLitterAI, a YOLOv11x-based detector combined with BoT-SORT tracking, was developed to automatically detect and quantify deep-sea benthic macrolitter. The model was trained with J-Litter, a dataset of 12,029 annotated images extracted from footage acquired by the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC) between 1983 and 2025. J-Litter includes small litter objects and non-litter images. DeepLitterAI was compared with a model trained only on large, clearly visible litter to evaluate training-data bias. On realistic test images containing small objects, DeepLitterAI achieved average precision (AP), which summarizes precision-recall performance, of 0.79-0.81 and F 1 scores, defined as the harmonic mean of precision and recall, of 0.71-0.76 for plastic films, plastic bottles, and beverage cans (mean AP@0.5 = 0.80 and mean F 1 = 0.73), with AP values averaging 1.6-fold higher than those of the large-object model. Analysis of Smart Port Practices Across the Globe to Evaluate the Status of Bangladeshi Ports and Future Perspectives
abstract: Maritime routes ensure connectivity between nations with several goods flowing through them, while ports are the junctions in this network as they manage a wide spectrum of commodities from raw materials to finished goods. Ports also generate employment across several sectors and support a variety of industries. A seaport is a maritime facility featuring docks, cranes, and storage for international trade, where ships load or unload cargo, container and passengers. Key functions of seaports include customs, warehousing, and ship services, with major ports like Shanghai, PSA, DP World or Rotterdam handling massive volumes of goods around the globe. On the other hand, ports in Bangladesh (Chittagong, Mongla, Payra) are vital for regional commerce. Presently, ports, the prime movers of economic operations, are acknowledged as essential capital infrastructure. Smart ports are automated facilities which leverage advanced digital technologies such as sensors, big data analytics, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), augmented reality (AR), digital twins, Internet of Things (IoTs), Big-data, and various automation systems to optimize overall operational e

title: Governing the Deep Sea: Legal, Technological, and Environmental Challenges in the Exploitation of Polymetallic Nodules under the UNCLOS/ISA Regime
abstract: The commercial exploitation of polymetallic nodules in the International Seabed Area poses governance challenges under international law. This article examines the adequacy of the normative framework established by the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), as administered by the International Seabed Authority (ISA), amid pressure driven by geopolitical competition and unilateral state action. Four dimensions are evaluated: gaps in the draft Mining Code, assessed through Part II of the ISA's 30th Session (July 2025); Sponsoring State responsibility when authorising contractors with prior risk records; emerging extraction and mitigation technologies (including artificial intelligence, autonomous underwater vehicles, satellite monitoring, digital twins, and high-resolution sonar) and their capacity to minimise environmental impacts; and the geopolitical rupture generated by the April 2025 United States Executive Order to expedite seabed mining permits in the international Area. title: Editorial: Innovations and research applications for marine conservation and maritime sustainability
abstract: To e_ectively close the gap between ecological reality and legislative action, maritime governance must first be firmly based on high-resolution, empirical data (Levin et al., 2009). Precision science converts qualitative field observations into actionable, quantitative, and reproducible metrics.Evaluating anthropogenic impacts requires tracking species interactions with environmental hazards across highly complex spatial dimensions. In the Mediterranean's Calabrian Ionian Sea, Menniti et al. advance the field by moving from broad pollution reporting to high-resolution targeted prevention. By spatially overlapping cetacean sighting tracks (including Tursiops truncatus, Grampus griseus, and Stenella coeruleoalba) with macro-litter mapping, they identify critical zones posing the highest impact risks. This high-resolution mapping is essential to transition conservation to knowledge-based prevention at the source, directly supporting the management programmes of adjacent Special Areas of Conservation.Similarly, multidisciplinary investigations by Modugno et al. in Albania's Vlora Bay demonstrate the profound value of modelling spatial ecology within coastal governance. title: A universal and facile design strategy for ultrasensitive strain sensors with a 3.365 με detection limit
abstract: Abstract Precise small-strain detection is critical for various applications, yet most existing technologies lack conformability, environmental robustness, high performance, and fabrication simplicity. Here, we introduce a material-independent design strategy to prepare ultrasensitive stretchable sensors that leverage two cracking mechanisms: cut-through cracks abruptly rupture dominant conductive pathways, while mesh-like cracks drive the progressive degradation of auxiliary conductive pathways, collectively leading to a rapid and stable resistance increase under small strains. The resulting sensor possesses an ultrahigh gauge factor (~430), an ultralow detection limit (0.0003365% strain), and high durability (> 5,000 tensile cycles). Through conformal, in situ, and real-time structural monitoring with a high signal-to-noise ratio (> 50 dB), the sensor reliably captured a small compressive strain signal for deep-sea equipment under extreme hydrostatic pressure (50 MPa). Our design offers a general, scalable route for ultrasensitive sensing in aerospace, ocean engineering, and precision manufacturing.

title: Ratification and Implementation of the BBNJ Agreement by Switzerland: Consultation Response
abstract: This report contains a response to the consultation procedure opened by the Swiss Federal Council on the ratification and implementation by Switzerland of the High Seas Agreement (the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction; BBNJ Agreement). We explain why the proposed Federal Act on the Implementation of the High Seas Treaty (Loi sur la protection de la haute mer, LPHM; Hochseeschutzgesetz, HoSG) is a good and necessary first step toward implementing those obligations in Switzerland. The proposed Act correctly identifies the principal areas in which domestic rules and obligations are required. However, the analysis reveals that the draft law must be strengthened. In its present form, the Acts relies strongly on (i) general references of the BBNJ Agreement, (ii) self-assessment and -reporting by regulated actors, and (iii) the subsequent adoption of implementing ordinances. Several essential questions concerning the scope of Swiss responsibility, environmental assessment, benefit-sharing, traceability, public participation, access to justice, supe

title: Tunisian Mediterranean Coastal Marine Litter and trash Dataset: Drone-Based Real-World Images for Detection, Classification and Segmentation
abstract: Dataset Description The Tunisian Mediterranean Coastal Marine Litter and trash Dataset (TUN-MarineLitter) is a real-world image dataset developed from drone-based aerial surveys conducted along selected coastal areas of the Tunisian Mediterranean Sea. The dataset was created to support research and development in marine litter detection, classification, and instance segmentation using computer vision and deep learning. The database contains high-resolution aerial images acquired in real coastal environments and includes seven major marine litter categories: Cardboard, Fabric, Glass, Metal, Other, Plastic, and Wood. Objects are annotated using polygon-based labels in normalized YOLO segmentation format, enabling direct use with modern YOLO-based detection and segmentation architectures. This version of the dataset is divided into 80% training, 15% validation, and 5% test sets. Data augmentation is applied exclusively to the training set using controlled ROI rotation (−15° to +15°), light exposure variation (−13% to +13%), and 10% salt-and-pepper noise. The validation and test sets remain unaugmented to ensure reliable and unbiased model evaluation. The images were collected from sel

title: A review of the current research status of deep-sea LiDAR detection technology
abstract: LiDAR detection technology, characterized by high spatial resolution, strong directionality, and fast response, has become an important technical means for marine bathymetry, underwater target identification, interconnection of deep-sea nodes, and seabed environmental sensing. In recent years, with the development of high-sensitivity detectors, miniaturized optomechanical systems, and high-speed deep-sea optical links, deep-sea LiDAR technology has gradually advanced from the stage of feasibility verification to the stage of system integration and scenario-oriented application. Current frontier research mainly focuses, on the one hand, on optimizing deep-water detection and imaging performance within the 532 nm blue-green optical window, and, on the other hand, on introducing single-photon detection, array-based reception, and high-speed data links to enhance detection capability under weak-return conditions and to improve the level of engineering deployment. Overall, the parallel development of mature and emerging devices, together with the gradual integration of sensing links and communication links, has become a major characteristic of this field. title: In situ deep-sea surface-enhanced Raman scattering sensor reveals cyanide as a key factor in cold seep nitrogen cycling
abstract: Deep-sea hydrothermal vents and cold seeps, typical ecosystems characterized by abundant carbon but limited nitrogen, support thriving microbial activities. The source of nitrogen has long been a key focus in scientific research. Although cultivation experiments have confirmed the presence of diverse nitrogen-fixing microorganisms, direct in situ evidence has been lacking. Therefore, a deep-sea in situ surface-enhanced Raman scattering sensor has been developed. It can adapt to extreme environment (≥350°C and ≥2000-m depth and LOD < 10 −7 M) and has excellent deep-sea application potential. Crucially, the sensor achieved the in situ detection of cyanide (-CN) (>5.7 μM) at cold seep, providing direct evidence for an energy-efficient nitrogen fixation pathway in the microbial communities. Concurrently, the gradient detection results indicated that CN was consumed as a microbial “circulating currency.” This finding offers critical in situ evidence for understanding the coupling mechanisms of cold seep carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycles, marking a substantial breakthrough in deep-sea sensing technology.

title: Traditional Weather Forecasting in the Age of Climate Change: Folk Meteorology, Indigenous Knowledge, Disaster Preparedness, and Coastal Resilience in the Philippines
abstract: Despite increasing attention to disaster risk reduction and climate adaptation in the Philippines, limited research has examined folk meteorology as a culturally embedded system of local ecological intelligence among coastal communities. Existing studies often prioritize scientific forecasting technologies while overlooking how Indigenous environmental interpretation continues to shape preparedness and resilience in everyday life. Addressing this gap, the study explored how coastal Bicolano communities interpret environmental warning signs, transmit traditional forecasting knowledge, and integrate folk meteorology with modern disaster forecasting systems. Using a qualitative research design grounded in hermeneutic phenomenology and narrative inquiry, in-depth interviews, narrative conversations, participant observation, and field immersion were conducted among coastal residents, fisherfolk, and disaster survivors from typhoon-prone communities in Camarines Sur, Albay, and Catanduanes, Philippines. Reflexive thematic analysis revealed that folk meteorology remains deeply embedded within community life and disaster anticipation practices. Participants identified sea behavior, atmosph

title: Mining minds before mining metals: a comparative analysis of deep-sea mining talent cultivation and China's strategic pathway in a contested international regime
abstract: Deep-sea mining (DSM) has moved abruptly from a long-horizon prospect to an immediate arena of strategic competition. In 2026 the International Seabed Authority (ISA) again failed to adopt its exploitation regulations (the “Mining Code”), while the United States—outside the ISA framework—moved to fast-track commercial seabed mining through a domestic permitting route. Against this backdrop, this paper argues that the decisive variable in the emerging order is not capital or even technology, but human capital: the people who can engineer seabed systems, draft technical standards, and negotiate the rules. Focusing on China and comparing it with the United States, Japan, Germany, France and the Republic of Korea, the study (i) reviews the fragmented literature on DSM technology, environment, governance and marine education; (ii) develops a three-pillar analytical framework and a transparent, ordinally-coded Deep-Sea Mining Talent and Capacity Index (DSM-TCI) built exclusively on sourced indicators; and (iii) analyses China’s position using authoritative ISA, treaty and national data. Results show that China leads on resource base, research output and policy support, but lags on a dedi

title: Progress and applications of superconducting-nanowire single-photon detectors
abstract: Photon detectors connect optical and electrical systems by converting light to electrical signals. Single photon detectors detect single photons which measure ultra-weak light. Traditional semiconductor single-photon detectors suffer from high dark count rates, low infrared detection efficiency, and poor temporal resolution. Superconducting-nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) overcome these limitations using the hotspot effect. SNSPDs have created a solid foundation for optical technologies and become key in quantum information, LiDARs and Deep-Space Communications. This paper reviews working principles and performance metrics: system detection efficiency, dark count rate, recovery time, and timing jitter. The study summarizes applications in quantum information (quantum key distribution, optical quantum computing), single-photon LiDAR, and deep-space optical communication, replacing most single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs). Recent experiments show that SNSPD-based systems can achieve meter-scale detection of sea fog, interplanetary laser communication over billions of kilometers, and boson sampling with 20 photons. Ongoing research is expected to improve performance in ma

abstract: Abstract. Ocean monitoring is a crucial component of Earth's observation systems. These systems have evolved to achieve a global scope and an exceptionally high level of complexity, encompassing not only observation programs but also data centres for collection and storage, as well as computational facilities where predictions and re-analyses of oceanic conditions are generated using coupled ocean-atmosphere circulation models. The products generated by the different components of the oceanic observation systems are of paramount importance for the knowledge of the environmental state of the oceans, their variability ranges, the impact of natural and anthropogenic stressors (such as climate change) and, in summary, the appropriate governance of the sea and the sustainable use of its resources. Given the diverse nature of the data (collected through a wide range of technologies, instruments, and institutions across multiple countries), it can be challenging to maintain a comprehensive overview of existing observation programs and datasets. title: Analysis of multiphase coupling in hydraulic collection heads considering sediment effects for deep-sea mining
abstract: In deep-sea mining operations, the presence of sediment has a significant impact on hydraulic extraction performance. However, existing studies generally assume a rigid substrate, failing to reflect the effects of real sedimentary environments. To evaluate the adaptability of different hydraulic extraction technologies under sediment-laden boundary conditions, this study coupled VOF interface tracking, discrete element particle dynamics, and a non-Newtonian rheological model to establish a jet-particle-sediment multiphase numerical method. It systematically compared the extraction performance of three mainstream extraction heads: suction-lift, wall-following jet, and jet-flushing. The results indicate that sediment significantly inhibits extraction efficiency. Among the methods, the suction-lift method is most severely affected. The wall-following jet method causes the least disturbance to the environment. However, its extraction capacity is limited. The jet-flushing method is least affected by sediment. It also exhibits the best overall performance. Furthermore, particle dynamics analysis reveals two typical modes of collection failure: escape and retention. Escape failure stems f

title: Manned Spacecraft Designed for Mars Long-term Space Mission
abstract: The structural system of a manned spacecraft must ensure safe environmental conditions and safe operation during every stage of the mission. The complexity and difficulty of the design tasks, processes, and technologies for manufacturing such vehicles increases significantly in the case of a spacecraft intended for long-duration space missions. Its design must provide the crew with adequate protection from the adverse effects coming from deep space and must incorporate structures that generate local microgravity conditions, allowing astronauts to experience gravity equivalent to that experienced on Earth at sea level. The main body of the proposed spacecraft has a compact geometric solid, with counter-rotating toroidal structures located within its interior. This paper presents the author's proposed structural system for a manned spacecraft that can successfully meet the key requirements for this type of space vehicle, which could be used in the near future for a flight to Mars and subsequent return to Earth. The proposed spacecraft could also serve as a manned space station orbiting Earth, the Moon, or another celestial body.

title: Sea Change
abstract: This chapter examines why emporia emerged at a certain time, and in a specific global situation. It examines the historical trajectory of the North European societies with a focus on the dynamics of maritime networks. I show how the adoption of sailing ships and deep-water sailing changed social strategies and patterns of interactions, and how this process is reflected in material culture. I argue that the growth of peaceable — as well as martial — maritime interaction, so often identified with the Scandinavian Viking Age, formed part of a wider change. I show how the widespread adoption of deep-water sailing, and of sail-powered ships, affected a plethora of norms, practices, and strategies that underpinned societies and changed their material culture. I approach these as a combinatorial technological evolution, in the sense of economist W. Brian Arthur. I demonstrate that changes were not a matter of sudden innovation, but rather a larger process in which existing patterns were recombined, modified, and scaled up. In this way, new technologies and new social worlds were able to emerge in tandem.

title: DEEP-SEA AND ESG: BALANCING CRITICAL MINERAL DEMAND WITH OCEAN SUSTAINABILITY
abstract: The global transition towards clean energy has significantly increased the demand for critical minerals, prompting growing interest in deep-sea mining as an alternative to terrestrial resource extraction. While deep-sea mining may contribute to securing essential minerals for renewable energy technologies, it also raises complex environmental, social, and governance (ESG) concerns. This article examines deep-sea mining through the ESG framework, highlighting the potential risks to fragile marine ecosystems, biodiversity, carbon sequestration, and coastal communities. It further analyses the governance challenges arising from regulatory uncertainty and the evolving role of the International Seabed Authority in managing seabed resources beyond national jurisdiction. The article argues that, despite its economic potential, deep-sea mining should be approached with caution until its long-term environmental and social consequences are better understood. A precautionary, transparent, and ESG-centred regulatory framework is essential to balance the growing demand for critical minerals with the imperative of protecting ocean sustainability.

title: Diversity and Bioprospection of Functional Proteins from Sea Anemone Heteractis magnifica Based on Multi-Omics Approach
abstract: Sea anemone venom has attracted increasing attention in biomedical research due to its multifarious compounds with biological activities. Although the venom is predominantly made up of proteins, the diversity and complexity of these proteins remain poorly understood. In this work, the proteins derived from the tentacle and column of Heteractis magnifica were investigated by integrating transcriptomic and proteomic technologies. A total of 3573 protein sequences from transcriptome databases were identified and clustered into nine functional categories. We also performed proteomic analysis on the proteins identified in H. magnifica, and 339 proteins were found to be present in both datasets. Notably, a comprehensive analysis of six typical categories was implemented, and the representative proteins were explored in depth using multiple alignments, homology modeling and molecular docking. Meanwhile, a few low-copy but functionally intriguing proteins were discovered, highlighting the presence of unconventional components in sea anemone venom. title: Bubble-triggered built-in liquid metal-based galvanic cell for gas pipeline microleak detection
abstract: Abstract The timely detection of pipeline micro-leakages in extreme environments such as deep-sea and extraterrestrial habitats remain a critical challenge due to the limitations of conventional delayed-response detection systems. Herein, we present an intelligent liquid metal bubble generator (LMBG) chamber capable of converting mechanical leakage signals into real-time electrical feedback through a self-powered transduction mechanism. The proposed system exploits the intrinsic electric potential difference of liquid metal (LM) and its oxide. The rupture of LM bubbles at leakage site activates a built-in galvanic cell between the metallic core and its oxide shell, achieving direct mechanoelectrical energy conversion without external power input. Notably, the system demonstrates ultrahigh sensitivity with linear voltage-volume (319.9 V·cm -3 ) and frequency-flow velocity (0.25 Hz·cm -1 ·s) correlations, rapid response characteristics (0.33 s latency). Meanwhile, the exceptional detection resolution for micro-leakages as small as 1.0×10 -3 cm 3 . title: A flexible hydrogel-based SERS sensor for multi-target detection of microbial metabolites in deep-sea environments
A Survey of Enterprise Supply Chain Management with Digital Transformation Artificial Intelligence Technologies Applications
abstract: Enterprise supply chain management (ESCM) is undergoing a sea change due to technological advancements such as digital twins, cloud computing, big data analytics, blockchain, and the IoT. Businesses may see improvements in their supply chains' transparency, efficiency, cooperation, agility, and resilience after implementing these technologies. This review delves into the history and evolution of corporate supply networks, as well as the digital and intelligent supply chain architecture. As a result of digital transformation, organizations are able to automate processes, make data-driven decisions, monitor in real-time, and anticipate risks. Stakeholders in the supply chain can utilize digital twin technology to enhance real-time system presentation, scenario simulation, resource optimization, and collaborative decision-making. In addition, tasks like transportation, distribution, inventory management, forecasting, and manufacturing are all improved by AI technologies including deep learning, machine learning, large language models, natural language processing, and generative AI. Robot Fish and Robot Ethics: Design and Dynamic Shape Control of Soft Propulsors for Bioinspired Swimming and Policy Considerations for Consumer Robots
abstract: From exploring previously inaccessible deep sea environments to providing accessible in-home care to elderly and disabled individuals, emerging robotic technologies promise transformative impacts to several industries. However, for these technologies to deliver on their promises, their development and proliferation must account for their broader impacts to effect positive change while minimizing harm. In this thesis, I present three studies, spanning technology-oriented and policy-oriented approaches to improving the impacts of two disparate classes of robots: 1) underwater robots for marine exploration, and 2) consumer social robots. In the first two chapters of this dissertation, I describe technological approaches to advancing the capabilities of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) through the integration of soft robotic technologies. By using soft propulsors and bioinspired swimming mechanisms, AUVs can become better equipped to safely traverse underwater environments while minimizing their potential for disrupting marine ecosystems. title: 4D technology and virtual reality as an innovative strategy for education
abstract: El presente trabajo de grado desarrolla la creación de Deep Sea, un modelo de negocio innovador que integra tecnología 4D y realidad virtual como estrategia educativa y de entretenimiento sostenible. La propuesta surge como respuesta a la aún limitada integración de tecnologías inmersivas en procesos educativos en Colombia, donde, según reportes de organismos como UNESCO, su adopción sigue siendo incipiente. Esta situación se ve reforzada por brechas en el acceso a tecnologías digitales, especialmente en contextos regionales, donde, de acuerdo con el DANE, los niveles de conectividad en zonas rurales de Colombia pueden ser inferiores al 30%, asimismo como las críticas documentadas hacia los acuarios tradicionales, relacionadas con su bajo nivel de interacción pedagógica y el uso de animales en cautiverio, ampliamente discutido por organizaciones como World Animal Protection. El objetivo es diseñar y validar un emprendimiento que sensibilice a niños y jóvenes frente a la conservación ambiental, promoviendo un aprendizaje ético, experiencial y alineado con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS 4 y ODS 14). title: Field Application of a Hybrid Point-The-Bit Rotary Steerable System in Shallow Unconsolidated Reservoirs and Deep Hard-Formation Sidetracking
abstract: Abstract Offshore oil and gas development plays a pivotal role in China's petroleum exploration and production, yet the high cost of operations demands exceptional drilling efficiency. In the South China Sea, conventional rotary steerable systems (RSS) face two persistent challenges: (1) inadequate trajectory control in shallow unconsolidated formations, where some wells require a consistent dogleg severity (DLS) exceeding 4°/30m to meet anti-collision and geological targeting objectives; and (2) low success rates in deep hard-formation sidetracking operations caused by the limitations of conventional motors and standard rotary steerable tools. To overcome these limitations, a hybrid point-the-bit RSS was upgraded with key enhancements. The tool was modified to be battery-powered, eliminating its dependency on mud flow for activation and ensuring reliable operation. Furthermore, the system was equipped with enlarged stabilization components to maintain effective wall contact even in washed-out sections. title: Biogeochemical Profiling of Red Sea Waters Offshore Rabigh for Assessing the Feasibility of Subsea Desalination
abstract: Seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) is one of the main technologies used for freshwater production in arid regions such as Saudi Arabia. However, conventional surface seawater intakes are often affected by biofouling and particulate fouling, increasing pretreatment requirements, operational costs, and membrane cleaning frequency. Subsea reverse osmosis (RO), which utilizes deep seawater as feed water, has emerged as a potential solution for applications where onshore desalination facilities or freshwater transport are impractical, such as offshore energy installations, remote islands, and future autonomous marine infrastructure. Subsea RO may also offer advantages, including reduced shoreline infrastructure and lower environmental impacts in sensitive coastal areas. Deep seawater is generally expected to have lower biological activity and fouling potential than surface seawater; however, limited information is available regarding the suitability of deep Red Sea water for subsea RO applications. title: PROFESSIONAL FISHERMEN AS THE GATEWAY TO THE MEDITERRANEAN BATHYAL REALM: TWO CENTURIES OF RESEARCH IN THE LIGURIAN SEA
abstract: How did the Mediterranean deep sea become a scientific object? This paper addresses that question through a historical reconstruction of bathyal research in the Ligurian Sea between the early nineteenth and the late twentieth centuries. Rather than attributing the emergence of Mediterranean bathyal ecology solely to scientific discoveries or technological innovations, it demonstrates that the progressive exploration of the deep sea resulted from a long-lasting collaboration between marine zoologists and professional fishermen. From Antoine Risso and Jean-Baptiste Vérany to Raffaele Issel, Enrico Tortonese, Lucia Rossi, Lidia Orsi and Giulio Relini, successive generations of researchers incorporated the practical knowledge and fishing technologies developed by Ligurian fishermen into their scientific investigations. The introduction of mechanised deep-water trawling in 1930 enabled Issel to establish the first systematic programme devoted to Mediterranean bathyal ecology, while the uninterrupted collaboration with the Ligurian fishing communities ensured the continuity of this research tradition for almost two centuries. title: Simulation modeling of the Adjustable Buoyancy Device for open ocean low trophic aquaculture, part I: Test of a submersible long tube unit
abstract: Abstract Open‐water low‐trophic aquaculture (LTA) is a sustainable method for producing ocean‐based food and providing ecosystem services. An effective system design is critical for mitigating risks posed by deep ocean forces. Developing submersible cultivation technology requires quantitative risk analysis and modeling to address offshore challenges while ensuring sustainability and efficiency. This paper presents a numerical model developed using OrcaFlex software to simulate the Adjustable Buoyancy Device (ABD) technology for cultivating LTA species. The ABD multi‐body system includes a submersible Long Tube Unit (LTU), pulley, buoy, cultivation dropper line, and pulley rope anchored to the seabed and interacting hydromechanically in the open sea. The submersible LTU consists of eight internal units filled with either air or water to regulate its depth of submersion. The system was tested using North Sea meteorological data, high‐energy waves, and environmental loads from currents. A First Principal Multi‐Physics analysis was employed to derive the key parameters for the model. OrcaFlex was used to evaluate the system's performance under various conditions. title: Research on in situ fidelity sampling, dissociation mechanisms, and green extraction technologies for deep-sea hydrothermal vent polymetallic sulfides
abstract: Deep-sea hydrothermal vent polymetallic sulfide deposits exhibit significant enrichment in strategic metallic elements, including copper, zinc, gold, and silver, and critical rare-earth elements, such as cobalt, selenium, tellurium, and indium, which represents the most economically valuable mineral resources of the 21st century. These deposits, formed through complex hydrothermal processes involving mid-ocean ridge systems and back-arc spreading centers, demonstrate metal concentrations frequently exceeding conventional terrestrial ore deposits by several orders of magnitude, rendering them essential for future mineral resource security. Nevertheless, the harsh deep-sea environment characterized by water depths of 1500–5000 meters, extreme hydrostatic pressures up to 50 MPa, aggressive marine corrosion, and complex sulfide mineral assemblages presents formidable technical challenges throughout the complete “sampling—dissociation—extraction” processing chain for sustainable resource development. title: Feasibility study and system architecture optimization of tidal current turbine technology for integration into newly-built offshore oil and gas platforms
abstract: Driven by the global energy transition and China’s “dual carbon” goals, substituting clean energy for conventional power on offshore oil and gas platforms has become a strategic priority. This paper systematically investigates the feasibility of integrating tidal current turbine (TCT) technology into newly-built offshore platforms. The distribution of tidal energy resources in China’s offshore areas, especially the South China Sea, is analyzed. Technical principles, structural classifications, and marine environmental challenges of TCT systems are reviewed. Considering the design characteristics and energy demands of newly-built platforms, an assessment is conducted from three perspectives: technical compatibility, structural integrated design, and economic feasibility. A “diesel-tidal-storage” multi-energy complementary microgrid architecture is proposed, which can be embedded as a standard module during the platform design phase, significantly reducing offshore construction and installation costs. title: Undergraduate and graduate education in ocean acoustics at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography, University of California San Diego
abstract: Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO) at UC San Diego offers comprehensive education in ocean acoustics at the undergraduate, M.S., and Ph.D. levels. Instruction and research span the physics of sound propagation and scattering, acoustical oceanography, marine bioacoustics, acoustic signal processing and data science, and the development of innovative acoustic technologies. Students receive rigorous training and research experience, including unique opportunities for at-sea fieldwork, through close collaboration with world-renownedfaculty in a highly interdisciplinary environment, contributing to a deeper understanding of the oceans. Ocean acoustics education at SIO is embedded within its undergraduate majors and graduate curricular groups, such as Applied Ocean Sciences and Biological Oceanography. Strong links also exist with the UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering, particularly with the Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (MAE) and the Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) departments. title: Key Drilling Technologies for Mesozoic Strata in a Certain Area of the Central Bohai Sea
abstract: Abstract With the increasing exploration intensity in the shallow layers of the Bohai Sea, the deep volcanic rock formations in the Bohai Sea have been highly anticipated for oil and gas exploration. However, the Mesozoic volcanic rock strata in the Bohai Sea are characterized by complex geological conditions and pose significant drilling challenges, with frequent occurrences of complex drilling situations. This paper elaborates on the geological structural features of the block and deeply analyzes the problems encountered during drilling operations, including high risk of fluid loss, complex pressure systems, high difficulty in cementing, and insufficient approved drilling windows, among others. In response to these challenges, research and development efforts have been made in drilling technologies, including fluid loss prevention and plugging technology, precise pressure control technology, pressure-controlled cementing technology, and subsea wellhead retention technology. Through the integrated application of these technologies, significant achievements have been made in the exploration drilling practice of this block in the Bohai Sea, effectively enhancing drilling efficiency
