title: Meldrum's acid derivatives as promising platforms for nanotechnology applications
abstract: Meldrum's acid derivatives have emerged as versatile molecular platforms with significant potential for nanotechnology applications due to their unique structural, photophysical, and functional properties. Although traditionally employed as synthetic intermediates in organic chemistry, recent advances have demonstrated their relevance in the development of smart fluorophores, biosensors, molecular probes, and stimulus-responsive systems. This review discusses the structural characteristics of Meldrum's acid that underpin its remarkable synthetic versatility, including the highly acidic methylene group, the gem-dimethyl effect, and the cyclic gem-diacetal framework, which enable extensive molecular functionalization and the construction of π-conjugated systems. The photophysical behavior of arylidene derivatives, particularly their donor–π–acceptor architecture and intramolecular charge transfer mechanisms, has enabled the design of enzyme-responsive fluorescent probes and bioimaging agents with high sensitivity and selectivity. title: AI-Facilitated Discovery of Microbiome-Originated Antimicrobial Peptides: A Perspective on Combating Antibiotic Resistance Within Public Health and Food Safety Frameworks
abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) demands innovative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotics. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), particularly those originating from the human, animal, and environmental microbiome, represent a promising frontier within public health microbiology and microbial food safety. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have revolutionized the discovery pipeline, enabling high-throughput mining of metagenomic data and de novo generation of novel peptide sequences. This perspective review synthesizes recent breakthroughs in AI-driven discovery of microbiome-originated AMPs, examines their preclinical efficacy against multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens under One Health and climate-sensitive frameworks and application in infectious disease treatment and discusses translational challenges including pharmacokinetics, toxicity, manufacturing scalability, and applications in food preservation and water safety. title: Introduction to Regeneration
abstract: Regeneration encompasses a variety of processes across biological, urban, and technological domains. This chapter explores the theories, types, and future prospects of regeneration, emphasizing physiological regeneration, urban regeneration through smart technologies, and the potential of regenerative medicine. By synthesizing recent literature, this study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of regeneration’s multifaceted nature and its implications for sustainable development. This chapter reviews existing theories and methodologies, highlighting the importance of regeneration in various contexts, and presents a comprehensive exploration of regeneration, beginning with its historical and conceptual underpinnings and extending into its molecular, genetic, and clinical dimensions. We discuss the major theoretical frameworks that explain regenerative mechanisms, including epimorphosis, morphallaxis, compensatory regeneration, and stem cell-mediated models, alongside concepts like positional information and cellular reprogramming. title: Amino Derived Drug Precursors for Drug Developments Using Biocatalyst
abstract: Amino acid-derived drug precursors are essential intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis because they provide structurally diverse and stereochemically defined building blocks for the development of modern therapeutics. Biocatalysis has emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional chemical synthesis by enabling highly selective and environmentally friendly transformations. This review evaluates the role of biocatalysts in the synthesis of amino acidderived drug precursors and highlights recent advances, pharmaceutical applications, industrial translation, emerging technologies, and future perspectives. A narrative review was conducted by critically analyzing recent literature on amino acid-derived drug precursors, enzyme classes, biocatalytic strategies, pharmaceutical applications, industrial process development, and emerging technologies. Relevant studies were synthesized to provide a comprehensive overview of current progress and future opportunities. title: Cyanobacteria in sustainable agriculture: from bioactive metabolites toward mechanistically validated biostimulants
abstract: Cyanobacteria are emerging as multifunctional components of sustainable agroecosystems, with the potential to influence nutrient cycling, soil structure, plant-associated microbiomes, and crop responses to environmental stress. This review integrates current knowledge of the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying these effects, emphasizing nitrogen fixation, nutrient mobilization, phytohormone biosynthesis, extracellular polymeric substances, biocontrol-related metabolites, and stress mitigation. Despite the growing number of cyanobacterial metabolites and traits associated with plant growth promotion and stress tolerance, direct functional and causal evidence linking specific compounds or pathways to plant responses remains limited. The work therefore critically evaluates the evidence supporting cyanobacterial biostimulant functions, distinguishing associative observations from functional and causal validation, while considering translational evidence from controlled experiments to field conditions. title: VoroDuce: Massively Parallel 3D Voronoi Simplification with Volume-Aware Edge Collapse
abstract: 3D Voronoi diagrams provide a powerful mathematical framework for representing volumetric functions and geometry with applications to Materials Science, Biology, Simulation and Astrophysics. However, accurately resolving fine structures often requires millions of cells, imposing severe computational and memory constraints. Traditional mesh decimation or point cloud simplification techniques fail to account for the effects re-meshing has on neighbouring cells. In this work, we formalize the Voronoi reduction problem and propose a greedy edge-collapsing algorithm on the dual Delaunay tetrahedralisation that accounts for changes in the local geometry. Further, we demonstrate a novel volumetric error approximation technique that models convex cell intersections as truncated prismatoids, circumventing computationally prohibitive exact volume calculations and enabling massive GPU parallelization. Evaluations across Synthetic, Medicine and Material Science data demonstrate that VoroDuce decimates models with up to a million primitives, successfully compressing the representation while preserving the underlying data better than naive decimation approaches.

title: The Chemistry Behind the Cure: Organic Chemistry in Drug Design and Action
abstract: The living systems are, at their core, extraordinarily sophisticated organic chemistry laboratories. Every biological process including DNA replication, enzyme catalysis, signal transduction, metabolism is executed through the same functional-group chemistry taught in an introductory organic course: nucleophiles attacking electrophiles, acids donating protons to bases, electrons flowing through conjugated systems. This review examines how organic chemistry principles explain the structure and behaviour of biomolecules, how biological catalysis mirrors and inspires laboratory reactivity, and how this shared chemical language is exploited across the drug development pipeline right from target identification and hit discovery to lead optimization, pharmacokinetics, and clinical translation. The boundary between "organic chemistry" and "biology" is, in a real sense, artificial. Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids are organic molecules governed by the same rules of bonding, stereochemistry, and reactivity as any small molecule on a laboratory bench. title: The Potential of Self‐Maintainable Living Materials
abstract: Engineered living materials (ELMs) are emerging as a new class of autonomous and self-maintainable systems that integrate metabolically active organisms within structural scaffolds to create materials capable of sensing, self-repair, adaptive response, and long-term functional persistence. Unlike conventional smart materials, which remain externally programmed and limited in regenerative capacity, ELMs leverage the intrinsic capabilities of microorganisms, fungi, algae, and mammalian cells to support continuous environmental interaction and feedback-regulated behavior. These systems retain metabolically active biological components that can grow, sense, communicate, adapt, and, in some cases, self-repair and self-regenerate, positioning autonomy as the defining capacity of these next-generation materials. Recent advances in synthetic biology, including programmable gene circuits, quorum-sensing communication, and metabolic engineering, enable living components to execute closed-loop decision-making and maintain functionality with minimal external input. These capabilities are driving innovations across construction, agriculture, environmental remediation, bioenergy, and biomedicine

title: Divine, Familial, and Human-Value Inspirations for Artificial Intelligence: A Conceptual Framework Linking Genetic Algorithms, Particle Swarm Optimisation, Artificial Neural Networks, and the Krishna and Rama Archetypes
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has repeatedly borrowed from nature, biology, and human society: genetic algorithms (GAs) from heredity and evolution, particle swarm optimisation (PSO) from the social behaviour of flocks, and artificial neural networks (ANNs) from the brain. This article proposes a conceptual and philosophical framework that reads these techniques through the lens of Indian spiritual traditions and everyday human relationships. God and human parents serve as the source of inheritance and guidance, Lord Krishna and Lord Rama as archetypes of wise counsel and righteous conduct, and fifteen values and relationships of daily life as design inspirations for learning systems. These ideas are synthesised into a unified construct, FFMBSTANDEMHRKLSPHIAI, expressed as a multi-objective training objective with human-set weights, together with three derived archetypes: Parents-Inspired AI, Krishna AI, and Rama AI. To show that the objective is operational, a small and fully reproducible demonstration embeds a fairness-type value term in the fitness functions of a GA and of PSO on synthetic data. title: A Heuristic Model for Computational Leverage and Human Domain Depth: V = D · Lᶜ
abstract: Current technological discourse vacillates between two flawed extremes: viewing artificial intelligence as uncredited synthetic plagiarism, or attributing sovereign creative agency to computational systems. This paper presents an operational heuristic, V = D · Lᶜ, to model the boundary conditions of human-machine production. We formalize final deliverable value (V) as the product of non-computational human biological mass — Domain Depth (D) — and Machine Leverage (L) scaled exponentially by the operator's Clarity (C). Through analysis of boundary states (D = 0, C = 0), the "stenographer illusion" with Joseph Gordon-Levitt's Donald Duck analogy, structural biology milestones (AlphaFold - Hassabis, Jumper, Baker 2024 Nobel Prize), and grounding thought experiments (physicist vs tricycle driver in Cagayan de Oro), we demonstrate that computational throughput in the absence of mortal accountability, domain scars, and physical maintenance yields zero durable systemic value. Software provides frictionless leverage; functional reality requires a biological creature with skin in the game (Taleb 2018). title: Bridging the Markush Gap in Optical Chemical Structure Recognition via a CLIP-Derived Visual Backbone and Synthetic Data Generation
abstract: Abstract The rapidly growing chemical literature contains invaluable information for pharmaceutical research and molecular biology, yet manual extraction on a large scale is increasingly impractical. Optical chemical structure recognition (OCSR), which converts molecular depictions into machine-readable representations, provides a key route toward automated chemical information extraction. However, existing OCSR methods remain limited in recognizing Markush structures, which are widely used in chemical documents, particularly pharmaceutical patents, because of their structural complexity and the scarcity of annotated data. Here, we introduce CLIP-OCSR, an encoder-decoder framework that integrates a domain-adaptively pretrained CLIP-RN50 vision encoder with a transformer decoder for chemical structure recognition, with a focus on Markush representations. To address data scarcity, we developed a synthetic data generation strategy that produces diverse Markush images paired with pseudo-SMILES representations encoding substituent, frequency, and position variations. Benchmarking demonstrates that CLIP-OCSR achieves competitive performance on standard OCSR benchmarks and shows strong ca

title: CMD-Net: A Hybrid CNN-Mamba Denoising Network for NMR Spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is essential for chemical and biological analysis, yet its inherent insensitivity frequently yields noise-corrupted spectra that complicate weak signal detection and quantitative measurements. Here, we propose CMD-Net, a hybrid CNN-Mamba denoising network, to recover clean NMR signals closely approximating the high-SNR reference spectrum acquired with a large number of scans. The architecture integrates CNN-based local feature extraction with Mamba-2 global context modeling within a U-shaped encoder–decoder framework, enabling direct noise reduction in the frequency domain. Trained solely on synthetic 1D NMR data, CMD-Net can be applied to 1D heteronuclear spectra and 2D/3D NMR data sets. Extensive validation demonstrates that CMD-Net consistently outperforms state-of-the-art denoising methods across multiple noise levels, achieving superior weak peak preservation and artifact suppression. With a balance between performance and model size, CMD-Net holds promise for low-SNR spectral analysis and protein structural studies in chemistry, biology, materials science, and life science.

title: Synthetic genome shuffling of poxviruses in yeast generates novel poxvirus candidates with potential oncolytic properties
abstract: Oncolytic viruses represent a promising class of biotherapeutics, yet their clinical performance is often constrained by limited cytolytic potency and insufficient immune activation. To address these limitations, we developed a synthetic biology framework that applies genome-scale recombination in yeast to generate chimeric poxviruses derived from multiple non-human-pathogenic poxvirus lineages. We first established the near-complete assembly of a vaccinia virus genome within yeast and demonstrated its ability to yield a functional virus in human cancer cells, providing a modular foundation for genome engineering. Building on this platform, we combined genomic inputs from different poxvirus species to create a diverse library of chimeric constructs, a subset of which could be recovered as infectious particles. Phenotypic characterization revealed substantial variation among chimeras, including distinct plaque morphologies, spreading behaviors, and activity across human cancer cell lines, indicating the emergence of functional diversity rather than incremental modification. abstract: Protein engineering is a rapidly developing field of biotechnology that involves the modification or redesign of proteins to obtain improved, altered, or novel properties. The ability to engineer proteins has significantly expanded their applications in industrial biotechnology, medicine, agriculture, food technology, environmental biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Protein engineering approaches can broadly be classified into rational design, directed evolution, and semi-rational approaches. Rational design utilises knowledge of protein structure, sequence, function, and molecular interactions to introduce specific modifications, whereas directed evolution employs iterative cycles of genetic diversification and screening or selection to identify proteins with desirable characteristics. Semi-rational strategies combine structural and computational information with directed mutagenesis to reduce the experimental screening requirements. Recent advances in structural biology, bioinformatics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and high-throughput screening have further enhanced the efficiency and precision of protein engineering. title: Elucidating the molecular mechanism of tryptophan‐derived indole metabolite biosynthesis in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DPUL ‐ S164
abstract: BACKGROUND: Our previous research has revealed that the Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DPUL-S164 metabolizes tryptophan (Trp) to produce indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and indole-3-carboxaldehyde (I3C). This study systematically elucidated the molecular regulatory mechanism of this strain for the metabolism of Trp to produce ILA, I3C and IAA through genome-wide functional annotation, bioinformatics analysis, high-performance liquid chromatography, and real-time fluorescence quantitative polymerase chain reaction. RESULTS: Under Trp-enriched conditions, the three indole derivatives showed significant time-dependent cumulative effects, with ILA biosynthesis exhibiting the most significant up-regulation. Molecular mechanistic studies have shown that the metabolic pathway involves synergistic regulation of multiple gene modules. The genes involved in Trp metabolism of DPUL-S164 was found to include genes encoding aromatic amino acid transaminases (AraT), genes encoding lactate dehydrogenase (ldh or ldhA) and genes encoding aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALD). title: A review on MMP-2 modulating agents from natural and synthetic sources and their role in inflammatory bowel disease
TANGO: RNA Topology and Geometry Co-Design
abstract: Designing RNA sequences that satisfy target tertiary-structure objectives is an important problem in RNA engineering, with broad applications in synthetic biology and therapeutics. Existing 3D RNA design methods have made substantial progress, but they largely treat the target fold as a geometry-only objective. This is incomplete for RNA, whose functional folds are specified not only by tertiary geometry but also by secondary base-pairing topology. We therefore formulate RNA inverse design as a topology-and-geometry co-design problem and propose TANGO, a multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for this task. TANGO adopts a staged curriculum: it first learns a topology-aware policy from secondary-structure targets, then transfers this policy to tertiary-structure targets to train a general co-design model, and finally applies frontier-guided fine-tuning to refine target-specific trade-offs among secondary-structure fidelity, tertiary-structure fidelity, and sequence diversity. Experiments show that TANGO generates diverse and novel designs, improving tertiary- and secondary-structure performance by 18.3% and 52.7%, respectively, over the strongest baseline.

title: PrimeStack editors enable efficient and site-specific integration of large multigene cargos in plants
abstract: Precise, site-specific integration of large DNA sequences into plant genomes is a long-standing goal of crop biotechnology and synthetic biology, yet remains constrained by random insertion, inefficient homologous recombination, and gene targeting. Here, we present PrimeStack, a DSB-independent platform that integrates PE with the unidirectional large serine integrase Bxb1, leveraging evolved variants for enhanced activity, to achieve the programmable insertion of multigene, multikilobase cargos at predefined genomic safe harbors (GSH) in rice (Oryza sativa). Optimized prime editors first install attP landing sites with high fidelity and heritability followed by Bxb1-mediated recombination that generates irreversible integration of genetic information. PrimeStack enabled targeted large-cargo integration in regenerated rice plants with efficiencies of up to 45%, as determined by junction-specific PCR analyses. No obvious morphological differences from WT plants were observed at 5 weeks after transfer to soil under the evaluated conditions. Engineering next-generation CAR-NK cells for hematological malignancies: genome editing, synthetic biology, and precision immunotherapy
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment by enabling engineered immune cells to selectively recognize and eliminate malignant targets, with CAR-T cells establishing the first major clinical success in this field. However, severe associated toxicities, logistical complexities of autologous manufacturing, and high rates of antigen-loss relapse have accelerated the development of alternative effector platforms such as CAR-NK cells. CAR-NK cells combine antigen-directed cytotoxicity with the innate antitumor functions of natural killer cells, offering a potentially safer and more readily available off-the-shelf therapeutic strategy. Nevertheless, the clinical efficacy of CAR-NK therapy is constrained by key biological and translational hurdles: brief in vivo persistence, inadequate trafficking and solid tumor infiltration, severe susceptibility to tumor microenvironment-mediated immunosuppression, and antigen escape driven by tumor heterogeneity. title: Engineering of bacterial outer membrane vesicles for biotechnological applications
Engineered Bacteria for Bioremediation of Organic and Inorganic Water Pollutants
abstract: Because of rapid industrialization, urbanization, and intensive agriculture, complex mixtures of organic and inorganic pollutants are released to aquatic environments, significantly affecting ecosystems and human health. Conventional systems designed originally for bulk organic and nutrient removal are increasingly ineffective for pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and other emerging contaminants. Many of the emerging pollutants have proved to be persistent and biologically active, even at trace concentrations, and are highly resistant to treatment by conventional physicochemical methods, which are energy-intensive and may cause secondary pollution. This chapter critically discusses the potential of engineered bacteria as an advanced tool for the remediation of organic and inorganic water pollutants. It covers a broad view of pollutant classification, physicochemical behaviour, and challenges of biodegradation, with a subsequent in-depth review of microbial bioremediation principles. title: The Glial Coupling in the Developing Brain: Astrocytes, Oligodendrocytes and Myelin Formation
abstract: Astrocytes and oligodendrocytes contribute to the metabolic, homeostatic and structural organization of the developing brain, yet their interactions evolve across development and remain incompletely characterized during the earliest stages of life. This narrative review examines astrocyte–oligodendrocyte coupling in relation to myelin development and addresses the question of which cellular and metabolic mechanisms support oligodendrocyte maturation and white-matter metabolism before mature astrocytic functions are fully established. Evidence from preterm and ill term neonates is considered together with experimental and adult or elderly studies used exclusively for secondary mechanistic comparison. Astrocytes and oligodendrocytes participate in interconnected metabolic, developmental and homeostatic processes, while perinatal white-matter injury may combine reactive astrogliosis, pre-oligodendrocyte injury and maturation arrest. title: Advances on Anti-Cancer Combination Therapies Targeting DNA Repair Pathway, Epigenetics, Microbiomes and the Immune System
abstract: Modern pipelines integrating multi-omics data, chemical libraries, structural biology information and artificial intelligence are currently accelerating drug discovery and precision medicine. Aligned with these advances, the multi-omics profiling technologies enable the identification of unique genetic and epigenetic signatures for stratification of patients based on cancer specific target and vulnerability. Targeted therapies to specific receptor or enzyme mutated or overexpressed often fail because cancer cells can adapt quickly. Tumor cells overgrow driven by new gene mutation and parallel crosstalk of signaling pathways. Patients with cancer and the hereditary syndrome targets such as BRCA1/2, and emerging targets such as ATR, CHK1, WEE1, and POLθ, are hypersensitive to ionizing radiation and PARP inhibitors. Combining synthetic lethality inhibitors, chemotherapy and immunotherapy effectively kill cancer cells by breaking multiple survival signaling pathways. Antibodies to immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting molecules like PD-1, PD-L1, and CTLA-4 can improve survival of patients, though predictive immunotype remains challenging. title: Living Hydrogels: Ultra-High-Molecular-Weight Hyaluronan and the Emergence of Adaptive Regenerative Macromolecules
abstract: Hyaluronan (HA) has traditionally been viewed as a structural component of the extracellular matrix, valued primarily for its viscoelastic, lubricating, and hydrating properties. However, accumulating evidence suggests that ultra-high-molecular-weight hyaluronan (UHMW-HA) functions far beyond passive tissue support, acting as a dynamic regulator of inflammation, mechanotransduction, immune homeostasis, cellular senescence, and regeneration. In this narrative review, we examine HA and specifically focus upon UHMW-HA operating as a “living hydrogel”, an adaptive regenerative macromolecule that continuously interacts with its microenvironment to shape tissue function and resilience. We examine evidence spanning evolutionary biology, glycobiology, biomaterials science, and regenerative medicine to examine how polymer size encodes biological activity and how UHMW-HA influences stem cell behaviour, extracellular matrix remodelling, and responses to injury and ageing. Attention is given to unique biological models, including the naked mole-rat, whose exceptional longevity and cancer resistance have been linked to abundant UHMW-HA, offering insights into the relationship between extracellu

title: Retinoid biology from embryonic patterning to adult tissue homeostasis: metabolism, RAR signaling, disease mechanisms, and clinical translation
abstract: Vitamin A gives rise to functionally distinct retinoids that regulate vision, embryonic patterning, and adult tissue homeostasis. The principal endogenous transcriptional ligand, all-trans-retinoic acid (ATRA), activates RARα, RARβ, and RARγ within RAR-RXR heterodimers; this mechanism is distinct from direct RXR activation by synthetic rexinoids. Tissue retinoic acid homeostasis is maintained through tightly coordinated regulation of vitamin A absorption, storage, transport, intracellular metabolism, and degradation. We integrate these pathways across embryonic development and adult physiology, with emphasis on the eye, adipose tissue-liver immunometabolic axis, pancreas, lung, heart, and skin. Recent single-cell, spatial, metabolomic, and multi-omic studies show that retinoid responses depend on cell state, tissue architecture, dose, and timing. We further compare retinoid and rexinoid therapies across chromophore replacement, acute promyelocytic leukemia, dermatologic and musculoskeletal disorders, and RXR-directed indications, focusing on receptor selectivity, efficacy, pharmacokinetics, resistance, and toxicity. title: Phosphorus(V) Umpolung Converts Electrophilic Phosphates into Nucleophilic H-Phosphonates
abstract: Ubiquitous in chemistry, biology and medicine, phosphate groups form the backbone of DNA and RNA, and their analogues like phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotides provide frontier therapies for challenging genetic disorders. However, the inherent electrophilicity of phosphorus(V) and thermodynamic stability of native P–OH bonds preclude their direct, latestage conversion into phosphate analogues. Here, we introduce a polarity-reversal (umpolung) strategy for converting electrophilic phosphates into nucleophilic H-phosphonates. This approach proceeds through two stages: P–OH thiolation into a thiophosphate followed by radical P–S cleavage, which generates the P–H bond. This sequence converts diverse phosphate substrates, such as complex drug scaffolds and nucleotides, into H-phosphonates that can undergo further phosphorus functionalization. The thiolation step also enables direct, one-pot conversion of P–OH into P–SH in nucleotides, providing a chemical route to the phosphorothioation of native phosphate backbones associated with bacterial and archaeal DNA defense. abstract: Abstract Background Circadian clocks are evolutionarily conserved systems that orchestrate daily rhythms in human physiology, tissue behavior, and cellular function. In circadian research, the NanoString nCounter platform has emerged as a robust alternative to microarray and RNA sequencing. However, raw instrument output requires specialized preprocessing to handle technical noise. Furthermore, while harmonic regression is widely used to detect periodic signals in biological time-series data, evaluating rhythmicity remains highly challenging in clinical studies characterized by sparse sampling and small sample sizes. Results To address these limitations, we developed rhythmCI, an easy-to-use R package that integrates established normalization methods with a complete workflow for circadian data analysis. The package incorporates a bootstrapping procedure to estimate confidence intervals for harmonic regression amplitudes, offering a statistically transparent way to quantify rhythmicity in small-cohort studies. rhythmCI provides an end-to-end workflow for NanoString nCounter data, including automated preprocessing, normalization, and visualization. title: Biological Characteristics and Research Progress of the Rice Leaf Beetle Oulema oryzae (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae: Criocerinae)
abstract: The rice leaf beetle, Oulema oryzae, is a pest across eastern Asia and eastern Russia; both its larval and adult stages cause considerable yield losses through foliar consumption. Its obligate diapause ensures population persistence through adverse seasons, but this strategy also hampers outbreak predictability and compromises timely interventions. This paper combines a narrative review with original observations. We first presented original observations on the developmental biology of O. oryzae. The morphological traits of all developmental instars, instar-specific diagnostic features, molting behaviors, and the complete prepupal-to-pupal transition, were described. These observations provide key criteria for accurate field identification and optimal timing of control measures. We then synthesized current knowledge on the biotic and abiotic drivers that shape population dynamics and phenology, as well as evolving integrated pest management (IPM) protocols integrating chemical, biological, and cultural tactics. Finally, we identified critical research frontiers, including the molecular regulation of diapause and development, genomic responses to climate change and cropping intensif

title: Concatenation, Splicing and Insertion–Deletion Operations on Cyclic DNA Molecules
abstract: Splicing systems (H-systems) and insertion-deletion systems are well-studied DNA computing paradigms inspired by biological operations observed in nature. They are modelled in a formal, information-theoretic manner. In these systems, splicing, insertion and deletion operations are used. In this paper, we study these operations on circular words, which naturally model cyclic DNA molecules, focusing on the relationship between algebraic operations and biologically inspired string transformations. In particular, we formally compare concatenation with circular splicing and insertion. While the splicing operation has already been defined and used for circular words in the literature, for insertion–deletion systems, e.g., circular insertion was defined to insert a linearized variant of a circular string (cyclic molecule) into a linear (ordinary) string (or linear molecule that can be represented by a string). In this paper, we provide a formal definition of insertion operators acting on circular words. title: WRN helicase addiction in MSI-H colorectal cancer: biomarker-guided pharmacology, resistance evolution, and implications for other gastrointestinal cancers
abstract: Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) and mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) cancers are enriched for dependence on Werner syndrome RecQ helicase (WRN), a synthetic-lethal vulnerability mechanistically linked to expanded TA-dinucleotide repeats, non-B DNA structures, and replication-associated genome instability. However, WRN dependence is not universal among dMMR/MSI-H tumors, indicating that MSI status is an enrichment biomarker rather than a complete predictor of biological dependency. In this review, we synthesize recent advances in WRN structural and molecular pharmacology, with particular emphasis on colorectal cancer, where the strongest functional and pharmacological evidence currently exists. We distinguish four translational biomarker layers: pretreatment predictors of WRN dependency, target-engagement and DNA-damage pharmacodynamic markers, early treatment-response biomarkers, and acquired-resistance markers. We further examine reversible and covalent WRN inhibitors, mechanisms of primary and therapy-emergent resistance, immune and replication-stress-based combinations, and the expanding early-phase clinical landscape. title: ΔNAzyme: A Foundational QM/MM Δ-Machine Learning Potential for Nucleic Acid Enzyme Catalysis
abstract: Abstract Nucleic acid enzymes (NAzymes), including ribozymes, DNAzymes, and XNAzymes, are programmable biocatalysts that catalyze diverse chemical reactions and provide unique platforms for investigating catalysis and engineering molecular function. Their central roles in biology and evolution, together with emerging applications in biotechnology, synthetic biology, and medicine, have created an urgent need for predictive computational design frameworks. Although multiscale computational enzymology integrating ab initio quantum mechanics can, in principle, provide predictive insight into these systems, current approaches remain computationally prohibitive for large, complex NAzymes and high-throughput design workflows. Machine learning potentials have the potential to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of multiscale modeling approaches, but QM/MM contexts in which the MM environment is highly polarizing remain challenging. Nucleic acid enzymes present a particularly demanding case: experimentally relevant predictions require an accuracy that semiempirical QM/MM methods alone cannot reliably deliver in their often large, highly charged, metal-dependent active sites. abstract: Graphviz sources and Python scripts that regenerate every figure in the article Artificial intelligence–enabled digital twins for forecasting cancer burden from oral nicotine pouches: a review and expert opinion (submitted to AI Biology & Medicine), together with the framework pseudocode, sample data schema, and validation and reproducibility checklists from its Supplementary Methods. The article proposes a hypothesis-generating framework. No model was fitted to real data; the data-style figures plot synthetic placeholder values that illustrate output structure only.

title: Decoding Biofilm Complexity: Artificial Intelligence, Advanced Imaging, and Multi-Omics for Precision Antibiofilm Strategies
abstract: Microbial biofilms are highly structured multicellular communities that exhibit remarkable tolerance to antimicrobial agents and host defenses, contributing to persistent infections, industrial biofouling, food contamination, and environmental challenges. Conventional microbiological approaches have greatly advanced our understanding of biofilm formation but remain insufficient to resolve the spatial, molecular, and functional heterogeneity that underpins biofilm resilience. This review discusses how recent advances in high-resolution imaging, multi-omics technologies, single-cell and spatially resolved analyses, and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming biofilm research from descriptive observation to precision microbiology. We critically examine state-of-the-art analytical platforms, including confocal and super-resolution microscopy, electron microscopy, Raman-based imaging, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and emerging spatial multi-omics approaches, highlighting their complementary roles in deciphering biofilm architecture, regulatory networks, and metabolic specialization. title: High temperature ligation enables in vitro assembly of eukaryotic genes
abstract: Abstract Our ability to efficiently construct synthetic DNA products is essential to studying and engineering biology. There is an abundance of widely adopted DNA assembly technologies suitable for generating synthetic constructs from diverse DNA inputs, but these techniques suffer from low specificity of connection during assembly, which decreases the accuracy, efficiency, and throughput of construction. Here we propose a broadly applicable paradigm for DNA assembly, High Temperature (HighT) assembly, that lowers misconnection rates by ligating complementary single strand DNA overhangs at reaction temperatures significantly higher than their predicted melting temperatures. By expanding the concept of melting temperature to demarcate smaller association fractions of DNA duplexes, we characterize HighT and demonstrate 40 percentage points increase in accuracy, and 4 orders of magnitude increase in yield of transformants when applying the technique to conventional assembly technologies. title: Organoid-Guided Synthetic Micropeptide Therapeutics to Target Ovarian Cancer Stem Cells
abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecological malignancy, largely due to high recurrence rates and the development of therapy-resistant disease. Cancer stem cells (CSCs) contribute to treatment failure by promoting chemoresistance through signaling pathways such as Wnt/β-catenin, Hedgehog, and Notch, as well as through dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment (TME). Ovarian CSC (OCSC)-associated biomarkers, including CD44, CD24, CD133, and ALDH, have expanded opportunities for specific tumor characterization and biomarker identification. Effective targeting of OCSCs requires experimental models that preserve cellular plasticity and hierarchical organization. Development of synthetic matrices and chemically defined media has improved the reproducibility and scalability of three-dimensional (3D) organoid cultures for preclinical drug testing. CSC-derived organoids, established by enriching cells positive for CSC markers directly from patient tumor material, provide a 3D platform for studying OCSC-associated phenotypes and therapeutic responses. title: Biological trajectories toward universal computation: Transposons and chaperone-assisted folding as models of molecular logic
abstract: The question of whether biological systems implement computation-like processes is central to synthetic biology and theoretical biophysics. This paper proposes a formal conceptual framework in which two well-characterized molecular mechanisms-transposable elements ("jumping genes") and chaperone-mediated protein folding-are modeled as computational systems. We argue that transposons, exemplified by the ONSEN retrotransposon in Arabidopsis thaliana, implement signal-responsive genome state transitions formally analogous to probabilistic finite-state machine computation, with capacity for computational expressiveness consistent with that of a linear-bounded automaton (LBA) under explicit assumptions of bounded memory, state-dependent branching and heritable epigenetic memory (a hypothesis, not a proof). Simultaneously, molecular chaperones such as heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70) and GroEL/GroES realize an analog computation paradigm, navigating protein energy landscapes through iterative, constraint-driven optimization. title: The Evolutionary Conservation, Structural Organization, and Cancer-Associated Polymorphisms of the Human Vitamin D Receptor: An Integrative Bioinformatics Review
abstract: Abstract Vitamin D exerts its pleiotropic biological effects primarily through the Vitamin D Receptor (VDR), a ligand-activated transcription factor of the nuclear receptor superfamily. Beyond its long-established role in calcium and phosphate homeostasis, VDR-mediated signalling regulates cell proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, immune function, and inflammation, and its disruption has been repeatedly linked to cancer susceptibility, progression, and mortality. This review synthesizes current literature on the evolutionary conservation, structural organization, and cancer-associated genetic polymorphisms of the human VDR gene and protein, drawing on comparative genomic, structural biology, and genetic-association evidence. We summarize evidence for strong evolutionary conservation of the VDR DNA-binding and ligand-binding domains across vertebrates and primates, describe the multi-promoter organization of the human VDR gene and the two-domain architecture of its protein product as resolved by X-ray crystallography, and review the functional and epidemiological evidence linking the FokI (rs2228570), BsmI (rs1544410), ApaI (rs7975232), and TaqI (rs731236) polymorphisms to alt

title: Efficient approximate Bayesian inference for large, heterogeneous biological datasets
abstract: Abstract Simulation-based inference (SBI) offers a route to connect biological data with mechanistic models. At the frontier of biology, datasets continue to grow in scale and richness, and increasingly record heterogeneity between individual observations that a mechanistic model can take into account. Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) remains a popular approach to SBI due to its ease of use, but incorporating this heterogeneity often requires a separate simulation of each observation, which is prohibitively expensive at scale. A previously proposed technique, minibatch Sequential Monte Carlo ABC (SMC ABC), reduces this cost by simulating a fixed-size random subset of observations for each proposal, at the price of sampling noise that limits precision. Here, we present an adaptive minibatch approach that uses small batches during early exploration and increases the batch size as the posterior is refined. The adaptive batch size is set by the target precision and does not grow with the size of the dataset, so the savings over full-data SMC ABC increase for larger datasets. title: Asymmetric $q$-Gaussian Distributions from Tsallis Maximum Entropy
abstract: Within the framework of non-extensive statistical mechanics, $q$-Gaussian distributions arise as maximum-entropy solutions of Tsallis entropy under suitable escort moment constraints. Although widely used in physics, biology, geology, finance, and related fields, standard $q$-Gaussians are intrinsically symmetric and cannot capture asymmetric fluctuations often observed in empirical data. We ask whether asymmetry can arise from the Tsallis maximum-entropy principle without externally skewing or joining distributions. We show that this is achieved by retaining the Tsallis entropy and imposing a global escort mean together with distinct downside and upside escort semi-variances. The key step is to reformulate the problem of maximum Tsallis entropy in terms of the escort density. The nonlinear escort constraints then become affine, while maximizing Tsallis entropy becomes equivalent to maximizing a strictly concave functional over a convex feasible set. Consequently, any admissible stationary solution is the unique global maximizer of the corresponding variational problem. title: Finite POLGB Capacity Exposes a Conditional Gain Boundary in POLG Catalytic-Subunit Turnover
abstract: Background: POLG disease-biology interpretation can conflate catalytic-subunit import, total POLGA abundance, POLGB association, active DNA engagement and synthesis readouts. A finite accessory-capacity model creates a narrower question: whether exact total-POLGA and synthesis trajectories can identify assembly, loss and capacity parameters, and which gain calibration remains unresolved. Objective: This working paper retains the selected question: In a declared POLG catalytic-subunit turnover model with finite POLGB, known imported input and absolute total POLGA, which assembly, loss and capacity parameters are conditionally recoverable from a constant-gain synthesis signal, which activity quantity still needs gain calibration, and how does the matched pseudo-first-order buffered limit erase the nonlinear coefficient information? Methods: Current primary-literature verification and archived primary texts were used only to bound claims. title: Biological possibility: a mechanistic account
abstract: Abstract Current projects in synthetic biology, universal biology, and the origin-of-life study have posed a pressing issue regarding the nature of biological possibility. This essay proposes a novel account of biological possibility, which highlights the role of mechanism: X is biologically possible just in case there is a possible life-defining or life-participating mechanism that actualizes X, and such mechanisms determine the features that individuate X. This mechanistic account captures a broad scope of biological possibilities while affording sufficient constraints in delivering them, thus being superior to three previous accounts (the “Library of Mendel,” combinatorial, and law-based accounts).

title: Analytical perspectives on RNA aptamer switch-based biosensors
abstract: RNA aptamer switches are programmable tools that enable ligand-responsive control of gene expression, making them valuable as genetically encoded biosensors in synthetic biology, diagnostics, and therapeutic applications. RNA aptamer switch functionality is often evaluated through changes in reporter gene expression following ligand recognition; however, analytical methods used to characterize RNA aptamer switch activity vary across studies, making it difficult to compare between platforms. This review examines analytical approaches to evaluate RNA aptamer switch-based biosensors, highlighting how each method captures different aspects of switch performance and how molecular, cellular, and experimental factors shape output. We also discuss considerations for experimental design, including normalization, controls, assay context, and sensitivity. By comparing the strengths and limitations of different analytical readouts, we provide suggestions for selecting appropriate measurement methods. Finally, we discuss current challenges in standardization, with the goal of improving quantitative and predictive evaluation of RNA aptamer switch-based biosensors.

title: The Synthetic Biology Containment and Hyper-Accelerated Life-Cycle
abstract: The Synthetic Biology Containment and Hyper-Accelerated Life-Cycle represents a profound ethical, operational, and structural paradox at the frontier of bio-engineering, advanced pharmaceutical project management, and ecological risk governance. This challenge manifests when an enterprise initiates complex bio-manufacturing or agricultural projects driven by engineered, self-replicating synthetic organisms designed to optimize target yields, synthesize complex molecules, or clean environmental toxicity. The core managerial dilemma stems from the intense conflict between the commercial urgency to accelerate delivery timelines and the high-consequence risk of unpredicted, self-replicating biological mutation if these synthetic matrices escape strict physical laboratory containment boundaries. Mechanistically, the project execution pipeline is forced into an operational trade-off. To satisfy institutional venture funding milestones and meet rapid market demand, project managers compress validation windows and push for large-scale open-air test plots or decentralized pilot production facilities. Engineering Escherichia coli Nissle as a Safe Chassis for the Production of Therapeutic Peptides
abstract: Abstract Synthetic biology enables the installation of programable genetic functions in microorganisms, positioning them as versatile platforms for therapeutic applications. However, clinical translation requires chassis organisms that integrate safety, genetic stability, and precise control over the activity. Here, we present an innovative engineering framework for the probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle (EcN) that transforms EcN into a safe, efficient, and non-proliferative chassis for therapeutic production. The native EcN plasmids pM1 and pM2 were cured and repurposed to encode two functional modules: a CRISPR-Cas12 chromosome-shredding device that prevents bacterial propagation and a programable circuit for payload expression, thereby generating a non-proliferative therapeutic-producing system. To broaden the range of therapeutic payloads, we developed an artificial-intelligence-guided bioinformatic pipeline to predict anticancer cell-penetrating peptides (ACCPPs). As a proof of concept, a candidate identified through this workflow was produced in the engineered EcN chassis and evaluated in human cell culture for anticancer activity. title: THE EL-RAKHAWI UNIFIED THEORY OF BIO-SYNTHETIC AUTONOMOUS ECOSYSTEMS AND PLANETARY NEURO-DIGITAL HARMONY Unifying Synthetic Biology, Autonomous Space & Transport, Nano-Pharmaceuticals, and Neuro-Digital Twins for a Carbon-Negative, Self-Healing Planetary Infrastructure
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Unified Theory of Bio-Synthetic Autonomous Ecosystems and Planetary Neuro-Digital Harmony (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23280910) unifies synthetic biology, autonomous transport, nano-pharmaceuticals, and neuro-digital twins for a carbon-negative, self-healing planetary infrastructure. It features four pillars: (1) Bio-Synthetic Propulsion, turning vehicles into carbon-scrubbing "planetary lungs"; (2) The Environmental Nano-Pharmaceutical Grid, strictly for ecological detoxification and environmental prophylaxis, excluding non-consensual human medication; (3) Neuro-Digital Twins with XR/BCI interfaces for intuitive management; and (4) Bio-Regenerative Semiconductors, providing near-perpetual, self-healing hardware with biochemical kill-switches. Central is the Regenerative Autonomous Neuro-Integration Index: RANI=(B×A×N×V)/[(B×A×N×V)+E×D+ε]. Under the Weakest-Link Axiom and Asymptotic Perfection Principle (max ≈0.9901), it proves systemic collapse if biological regeneration fails. Released under the Ferial Zayed Humanitarian License.

title: A Frequency-Based Biological Computer: From DNA Sequence to RF-Controlled Chemical Signaling
abstract: Background: Remote control of cellular behavior without genetic modification of target tissues remains a challenge in synthetic biology. Light-based approaches such as optogenetics suffer from limited tissue penetration, while chemogenetic methods lack spatial resolution and require systemic drug delivery. Radio-frequency (RF) signals offer an alternative due to their deeper tissue penetration, but a framework for translating DNA sequences into RF-controlled chemical outputs has not yet been established. Results: We present a frequency-based biological computer that encodes DNA sequences into RF patterns and converts them into chemical signals for controlling natural cells. A 64-codon frequency table was designed using four RF frequencies (10, 20, 30, and 40 MHz), four pulse counts, and four pulse durations. A bidirectional compiler was developed to encode DNA sequences into RF patterns and decode them back with full accuracy. A biological computer was then simulated, incorporating an RF receiver, a logic circuit (AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOT), a memory unit, and a chemical signal generator. Tissue-level simulations compared artificial and natural signaling under defined parameters. Und

title: The Kayser–Cuny Tables: a composition descriptor (p × n × e)/4 applied to the chart of nuclides and the genetic code
abstract: AbstractI present a dimensionless descriptor, F = (p × n × e)/4, computed solely from the numbersof protons, neutrons and electrons. For a neutral atom it reduces to F = Z²N/4: each isotopicfamily becomes an arithmetic progression with step Z²/4, whose origin is the neutron-freemember (F = 0).We apply this descriptor to a compilation of 11,996 compositions (Z = 1 to 118), annotatedaccording to their status in reference databases (stable, radioactive, studied in the literature,hypothetical). By combining it with the semi-empirical Bethe–Weizsäcker formula to set thebinding limits, we identify 3,957 candidate compositions on the neutron-rich side, an order ofmagnitude consistent with estimates of the isotopes still unknown.Applied to the nucleobases, the same calculation reorganises the 64 codons into 20 classes.The differences between bases, +96.5 (between 96 and 97) (C→T), +1 (T→A) and +128(A→G), each have an identifiable atomic origin. The descriptor contains neither bindingenergy nor biological function: it provides a reproducible reading framework, whosepredictive power will be assessed against future discoveries. title: NEMUCO: The In Vitro 4D NMJ as an Innovative Powerful Tool to Study Nerve and Muscle Cell–Cell Communication
abstract: Chronic muscle unloading, following denervation, aging, long-term bedrest as either spaceflight analog or actual spaceflight missions, results in a decline of neuromuscular junction (NMJ) structure and function, resulting in muscle mass decline and impaired fine motor control. Similar changes are also observed in several neuromuscular diseases and myopathies with signs and symptoms related to impaired movement control. Here, we report on a powerful 3D co-culture experimental model developing NMJ-like structures, as a novel in vitro platform for functional/regulatory studies during time (4D co-culture) for basic and translational research purpose. Murine NErve (NSC-34 motor neuron) and MUscle (C2C12 myoblast) cell CO-cultures (NEMUCO) were grown on either synthetic or biological three-dimensional (3D) scaffolds. The co-cultures were analyzed using a significant array of molecular and cellular biology tools, based on NMJ-specific molecular marker expression combined with muscle- and nerve-cells specific differentiation biomarkers. Specialized cell-cell contacts were present starting at day 2 of co-culture. Triple immunostaining indicated neurofilament-positive axonal nerve terminals

title: 1100 Synthetic Benchmark Problems for Dynamic Modeling of Cellular Processes
abstract: Abstract Motivation Systems biology strives to unravel the complex dynamics of cellular processes, often with the help of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). However, the sparsity of measured data and the strong non-linearity of common ODEs introduce severe numerical problems in typical modeling tasks. This gave rise to the development of many computational algorithms that must be systematically evaluated to ensure optimal method choices. Currently, the amount of well curated models for such benchmarking efforts is insufficient, as building and calibrating biologically reasonable models based on experiments requires years of work. Results We present a large-scale collection of 1100 synthetic modeling problems, generated based on the ODE systems and experimental designs of 22 published modeling problems. This is achieved by extending a recent method for simulation of time-course data for randomly generated observation functions to also include realistic measurement patterns across multiple experimental conditions. By analyzing data and model characteristics, optimization performance and parameter identifiability, we show that the synthetic problems provide both a realistic and d

title: Adaptive dark-field interferometric scattering microscopy for label-free imaging of nanoscale systems
abstract: Interferometric scattering microscopy (iSCAT) enables label-free detection of nanoscale entities by interfering weak scattered light with a reference field, yielding high sensitivity for single-particle mass photometry, three-dimensional tracking, and kinetic studies of proteins, viruses, and nanoparticles—dynamics elusive to traditional optics. Nonetheless, its efficacy hinges on rigorous background suppression, coherence management, and calibration. We advance dark-field iSCAT (DF iSCAT), merging interferometric precision with dark-field illumination to augment contrast, attenuate coherent artifacts, and enhance detection of ultraweak scatterers. This facilitates non-perturbative visualization of diminutive biomolecules and synthetic nanostructures, sans photobleaching. DF iSCAT emerges as a scalable, high-fidelity modality for nanoscale imaging, with profound implications in structural biology, nanomedicine, proteomics, and materials characterization.

title: History, Introduction, and Principles of Gene Cloning in Plants
abstract: Genetics is the study of genes and the factors that influence their expression, or the study of heredity. The contribution of Gregor Mendel in the middle of the 19 th century marked the beginning of the scientific history of genetics. Prior to Mendel, genetics was purely based on theoretical concepts, but later on, the field of genetics expanded to incorporate experimental genetics. Advances in genetics and genome technologies were made in the first half of the 20th century, laying the foundation for further developments in molecular genetics. The development of gene cloning in the latter part of the 20 th century as a vital tool for genetic research and crop enhancement has brought about revolutionary advances in the field of plant molecular biology. This chapter thoroughly covered historical evolution, theoretical underpinnings, and core principles of gene cloning in plants. Furthermore, it also explores the methodologies and mechanisms involved in plant gene cloning, including the selection of target genes, the construction of cloning vectors, and the transformation of plant cells using both physical and biological methods. Novel Treatments of Cancer
abstract: Cancer treatments have evolved over the years and have given hope to cancer patients by extending and improving their quality of life. The field is moving towards more personalized treatments with less toxicity. One of the areas that has been rapidly expanding in the recent years involves next-generation immunotherapies, including CAR-T cell therapies, TCR-T therapies, and bispecific antibodies. In the area of immunology, personalized neoantigen vaccines have also been developed and used for cancer treatment. Other therapies involve tumor microenvironment (TME) modulators, such as myeloid therapies and microbiome-based therapies. Gene editing of both immune and cancer cells has also been utilized for cancer treatment. Another type of cancer treatment involves targeted protein degradation, which has aided in designing therapeutic strategies against undruggable targets. RNA-based therapies, including siRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, and RNA-binding small molecules are also used for cancer treatment. Researchers have also taken advantage of synthetic biology approaches. Oncolytic viruses engineered to selectively infect and destroy cancer cells have been tested in several cancer typ

Biochemical classification and structural insights into snake venom proteins and peptides
Cloning Vectors: Types, Features, and Uses
abstract: Cloning vectors are indispensable molecular tools for transferring and maintaining foreign DNA in a host organism, and are crucial for genetic engineering, recombinant DNA technology, and synthetic biology. The basic characteristics of a useful cloning vector include an origin of replication (Ori) for independent DNA replication, selection marker genes for screening of the transformed cells, and a multiple cloning site (MCS) that allows insertion of foreign DNA using restriction enzymes. The selection of a vector is dependent on the size of the DNA to be inserted, compatibility with the host, and the nature of the experiment, i.e., gene expression, mutagenesis, or genome mapping. Cloning vectors are of different types: plasmids, which are frequently used for small-scale cloning; bacteriophage vectors such as the λ phage, which are used for intermediate-sized DNA inserts; cosmids, which combine plasmid cloning features with bacteriophage properties; bacterial artificial chromosomes (BACs) and yeast artificial chromosomes (YACs), which are used to clone larger genomic fragments. Environmental Bioethics and Law: Duties of Care, Intergenerational Justice and the Legal Protection of Life Systems
abstract: Environmental bioethics provides a normative framework for examining the legal regulation of human intervention in ecological and biological systems. Its significance extends beyond the traditional boundaries of biomedical ethics, encompassing questions concerning ecological risk, scientific uncertainty, intergenerational justice, biodiversity, non-human life, technological intervention and the distribution of environmental burdens. This study examines the manner in which these ethical concerns are translated into legal principles, duties and institutional mechanisms within international, European and human rights law. Particular emphasis is placed on the precautionary principle as a legal response to scientific uncertainty and potentially serious or irreversible environmental harm, as well as on the transformation of prevention, proportionality and environmental assessment into instruments of ecological responsibility. The study further analyses intergenerational justice as a temporal dimension of environmental law, requiring present decision-making to account for irreversible ecological costs imposed upon future generations. Biodiversity protection is examined in connection with

title: Integrating Technologies for Synthetic, Systems, and Spatial Approaches in Cancer Research
abstract: Abstract Emerging tools for spatial analysis, systems biology, and synthetic biology offer opportunities to observe, dissect, and perturb cancer mechanisms, to design strategies for the prevention of oncogenesis, and to identify therapies that lead to durable tumor control. Here, we summarize perspectives from the virtual Innovation Lab on “Synthetic and Systems Approaches to Interrogate Spatiotemporal Processes in Cancer” (S3) hosted by the National Institutes of Health (NIH), which assembled interdisciplinary experts to discuss cancer spatial organization and dynamic cellular interactions and how they can be addressed by leveraging novel synthetic and systems biology approaches. These discussions focused especially on cancer initiation, which results from a failure of systems control. To catalyze innovation across the research community, we summarize key insights from these events into a vision for integrated synthetic, systems, and spatial approaches in cancer research.

title: The prenylation code regulating estrogenic activity of synthetic and natural product derivatives of resveratrol
abstract: Abstract Prenylation of phenolic and aromatic natural products across plants, bacteria, and higher organisms contributes to their lipophilicity and bioavailability. The process also enhances host defense and serves as a building block for chemical diversity, with medicinal chemistry mimicking these effects to create more effective compounds. While phytoestrogens, particularly those from licorice, are established as key natural regulators of estrogen receptor (ER) biology, the specific mechanisms by which prenylated polyphenolics in licorice regulate ER ligand binding and activity remain unknown. Herein, we show that the widespread prenylation of stilbenes from two commonly used licorice species reveals a broad spectrum of ER interaction profiles in the context of different scaffolds. To identify structural rules for how prenylation modulates ligand binding, we synthesized sixteen constitutional isomers of mono- or diprenylated stilbenes based on common resveratrol or dihydroresveratrol cores. These variously prenylated stilbenoid compounds exhibited ER agonistic effects on cell growth with a remarkable five-log range of cellular potencies. X-ray crystal structures of these compound

title: Sense-and-response to intracellular signaling via nucleocytoplasmic localization control of a synthetic transcription factor platform
abstract: Many therapeutically relevant signaling pathways are sensed inside the cell, yet a modular synthetic biology platform for responding to intracellular signaling at the post-translational level is lacking. Signaling pathways control the nuclear localization and activity of native transcription factors via phosphorylation of nuclear localization/export or cytoplasmic anchor sequences. Here, we apply this concept to develop a platform of nucleocytoplasmic localization tags (NCtags) that control the nuclear translocation of a synthetic transcription factor (synTF) for transgene induction in engineered cells. We identify human-based synTF components that are basally cytoplasmic and induce transgenes under the control of NCtags with minimal background. We demonstrate the modular nature of this platform through transcriptional reporter induction in response to a calcium-inducible NFAT-derived NCtag, and development of novel NCtags responsive to hyperosmolarity, cAMP, or logical combinations of cAMP and calcium. Multiple factors in the tumor microenvironment elevate cAMP in T cells, leading to reduced function. We demonstrate that NCtag-synTF fusions expressed in T cells can respond to endo

title: Directed evolution of a thermostable family-A DNA polymerase into a reverse transcriptase for 2’-modified RNA
abstract: Abstract RNA-based therapeutics increasingly rely on nuclease-resistant xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs), but engineering polymerases capable of reading and amplifying these non-canonical substrates remains a major challenge. Natural DNA polymerases cannot process C2’ sugar modifications, and the complete structural determinants governing this limitation remain poorly understood, limiting rational design strategies. In this study, we apply directed evolution methods to Thermus thermophilus DNA polymerase using a microfluidic implementation of the Compartmentalized Self-Replication (CSR). We identify an engineered variant, termed E5, capable of reverse transcribing C2’-modified RNA, a previously inaccessible activity for this enzyme. Next-generation sequencing allow us to track evolutionary trajectories across nine rounds of evolution. Through an integrated analysis combining statistical methods, protein language models, and crystallographic data, we reveal unknown epistatic networks controlling polymerase function. This large-scale experimental dataset (>196,000 thermostable enzyme variants) provides a robust basis for predicting sequence-to-function relationships, accelerating developmen

Biological Management of Root Development in Regenerative Endodontics: Pulp Biology, Clinical Protocols, and Translational Challenges
abstract: Immature permanent teeth that lose their pulp to necrosis pose a particular problem: root development stops, the dentinal walls are thin, and the apex remains wide open. Regenerative endodontics addresses this in a minimally invasive way, relying on apical and periapical tissues that often retain their capacity for repair and can support further root development. Heavy instrumentation is avoided, which protects the fragile walls as well as the stem and progenitor cells of the apical papilla and keeps the local environment favorable for healing. Disinfection is deliberately controlled: lower-concentration irrigants, EDTA conditioning of dentin, and a cell-friendly medicament such as calcium hydroxide aim to bring bacteria under control without sacrificing viable cells or the bioactive signals stored in dentin. Bleeding induced from the periapical tissues fills the canal with an autologous blood clot that serves as a natural scaffold. Platelet-rich plasma, platelet-rich fibrin, and concentrated growth factor (CGF) offer fibrin-rich alternatives carrying mediators that support cell migration, angiogenesis, and tissue organization. title: Motif‐Selective DNA Recognition and Promoter‐Dependent Transcriptional Repression by a Cyclic Pyrrole/Lysine Polyamide
abstract: Sequence-selective control of gene expression by synthetic DNA-binding molecules is attractive for developing chemical biology tools and potential therapeutic applications. Here we report a cyclic pyrrole/lysine polyamide (cPKP) that preferentially binds AT-rich DNA, with selective recognition of ATAT and ATGT motifs. In a HeLa nuclear extract-based transcription system, cPKP repressed transcription in a promoter-dependent manner, showing stronger inhibition of a cytomegalovirus (CMV) core promoter than of the human c-MYC promoter. RNA sequencing showed that cPKP was associated with downregulation of genes whose proximal promoters were enriched for ATAT and ATGT motifs, while causing limited perturbation of global cellular homeostasis in HeLa cells. Together, these results establish cPKP as a motif-selective DNA-binding scaffold that can modulate transcription in a promoter-dependent manner with limited global transcriptomic perturbation in human cells.

title: Efficient Generation of Single- and Multigene CRISPR-Cas9 Knockout in Human Cells
abstract: The CRISPR-Cas9 system has revolutionized genome editing, but generating multiple gene knockouts (multi-KOs) remains challenging. This study presents an improved method for efficient generation of multi-KOs using sgRNA DNA strands and the CRISPR/Cas9 system. The method was tested on genes involved in the apoptosis pathway of HEK293T cells. The crRNA for each target gene was designed from Exon 1, near the starting codon ATG, such that a small deletion or insertion in this region would lead to a premature STOP codon and functional knockout. The T7 endonuclease I assay confirmed the high editing efficiency of sgRNAs in both single- and multiple-gene knockouts. Deep sequencing analysis revealed frameshift mutations and premature stop codons, indicating successful loss-of-function mutations. Using the sgRNA DNA strands provided a more uniform and efficient editing profile compared to other methods. This improved protocol offers a simpler, faster, and cost-effective approach for generating multigene knockout clones, with implications for functional genomics, therapeutic development, and synthetic biology.

title: SelCal: selection-aware calibration of scanned-lag dependence tests
abstract: SelCal tests lagged dependence between two time series when the lag is chosen by scanning a pre-declared set of candidate lags. It repeats the complete lag search inside every circular-shift surrogate, can enumerate the whole circular group exactly (null circular_shift_exact_v1), refuses plans whose smallest attainable p-value exceeds alpha (for a lagged-Pearson scan of L lags over the complete circular group the exact p-value cannot fall below L/n), and keeps verifiable, replayable records. Command-line workflow: selcal validate, run, verify --replay, report. Version 0.1.2 is a clarification release for the accompanying software paper. The scientific-assumption advisory printed by selcal validate, the HTML report and the local interface now states the condition the error-rate guarantee needs: under the null, the joint distribution of (X, Y) is invariant under every circular shift of X with Y held fixed; stationarity, matching endpoints or detrending alone do not establish it. The release also ships the paper's exact-enumeration example and a paper-to-evidence manifest (docs/paper/selcal_softwarex_manifest.json). The calibration code and the lagged-Pearson results are those of 0.1.

title: Synthetic strategies toward 3-arylcoumarins: From classical condensation to sustainable C–H arylation
abstract: 3-Arylcoumarins are important coumarin derivatives with diverse applications in medicinal chemistry, materials science, and chemical biology. However, efficient and selective construction of the C3–aryl bond remains a significant synthetic challenge. This review provides a focused and critical analysis of methodologies for synthesizing 3-arylcoumarins, including classical condensation, transition-metal-catalyzed cross-coupling and annulation, radical-mediated, visible-light photoredox, mechanochemical, and emerging sustainable approaches. Rather than presenting a chronological compilation, the reported methods are compared in terms of reaction mechanisms, catalyst systems, substrate scope, functional-group tolerance, efficiency, selectivity, recyclability, scalability, and green chemistry aspects. Recent advances are evaluated alongside established strategies, highlighting the shift toward atom-economical, metal-free, recyclable, and energy-efficient processes. The review further identifies key limitations and challenges while highlighting future opportunities in photoredox and electrochemical synthesis, heterogeneous catalysis, mechanochemistry, and continuous-flow technologies. title: Optical Thermometry with Organoeuropium(II) Complexes
abstract: The measurement of temperature is of critical importance to a diverse array of fields and industries, such as heating, ventilation, and cooling, nutrition, molecular biology, medicine, engineering of all denominations, chemistry, climate science, and computing technologies, to name a few. As technologies in all these areas progress, measuring temperature more accurately and precisely under increasingly challenging conditions is an ever-evolving problem. One strategy to address these challenges is optical thermometry, which correlates changes in the optical characteristics (e.g. luminescence intensity, emission lifetime, colour, etc.) of a thermosensitive system to changes in temperature. In contrast to common thermometric methods employing thermistors, thermocouples, or even infrared thermography, optical thermometry is a remote-detection, minimally invasive technique with very high attainable spatial resolution, making it well-suited to probing temperature in difficult environments and sensitive systems. Due to their favourable (magneto-)optical properties, lanthanide-based materials are well-studied as optical thermometers. However, most of these materials operate via a ratiometr

title: The Future of Environmental Biotechnology: Innovations for a Sustainable World
abstract: Environmental biotechnology is at the forefront of scientific advancements aimed at addressing global sustainability challenges. This field integrates biological processes with technological innovations to develop eco-friendly solutions for pollution control, waste management, and resource conservation. Recent breakthroughs in synthetic biology, genetic engineering, and microbial applications have revolutionized bioremediation, bioenergy production, and sustainable agriculture. Innovations such as engineered microbes for wastewater treatment, bio-based alternatives to plastics, and carbon capture technologies hold immense potential to mitigate climate change and reduce environmental degradation.

abstract: The El-Rakhawi Grand Treatise on Legal-Scientific Convergence and Normative Operationalization (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23233877) presents the first unified framework bridging European digital legislation (GDPR, EU AI Act, Data Governance Act) with computational enforcement. title: Ecological Restoration: Using Biotechnology to Revive Damaged Ecosystems
abstract: Human activities such as deforestation, urban expansion, illegal mining, and industrialization have led to the widespread degradation of natural ecosystems, resulting in habitat loss, reduced biodiversity, and disruption of ecological functions. These environmental pressures have created an urgent need for innovative and sustainable restoration strategies. Biotechnology offers significant potential in this context by utilizing biological processes and molecular techniques to rehabilitate damaged ecosystems in an environmentally responsible manner. Through the use of genetically modified organisms and engineered microbial strains, biotechnology enables effective bioremediation, phytoremediation, and enhancement of soil and water quality. Microbial biotechnology, in particular, contributes to ecosystem recovery by breaking down pollutants, facilitating nutrient cycling, and supporting plant growth in contaminated or degraded environments. Additionally, advancements in synthetic biology and ecological engineering have made it possible to design organisms with targeted capabilities for addressing specific environmental challenges, such as heavy metal contamination or oil spills.
