title: Rheumatoid Arthritis: Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, Clinical Characteristics, and Contemporary Therapeutic Approaches – A Narrative study
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive joint destruction, and multiple extra-articular manifestations.The disease significantly contributes to functional disability, reduced quality of life, and increased healthcare burden worldwide.Although the precise etiology remains incompletely understood, evidence suggests that RA develops through a complex interaction of genetic predisposition, environmental exposures, epigenetic modifications, and immune dysregulation.Advances in molecular biology and immunology have improved the understanding of disease mechanisms and facilitated the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.Conventional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), biologic agents, and targeted synthetic DMARDs have substantially transformed disease management and clinical outcomes.This article provides a comprehensive overview of the epidemiology, etiopathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, treatment strategies, and recent trends in drug utilization among patients with RA.Additionally, emerging therapeutic perspectives and future research directions a

title: Environmental Biotechnology: Navigating Policy, Regulation and Ethical Dilemmas
abstract: Environmental biotechnology is rapidly reshaping how societies manage pollution, conserve resources, and transition toward sustainable systems. As these technologies advance, they increasingly intersect with complex policy frameworks, regulatory requirements, and ethical considerations. This review examines the evolving governance landscape surrounding applications such as bioremediation, waste-to-energy conversion, and engineered microbial systems. It explores how national and international regulations aim to balance innovation with environmental and public safety, highlighting gaps in oversight for emerging tools like synthetic biology and gene-edited organisms. Ethical dimensions—including risk– benefit evaluation, community participation, data transparency, and long-term ecological impacts—are critically analyzed to guide responsible decision-making. By integrating scientific progress with policy analysis, this review emphasizes the need for adaptive regulatory mechanisms, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and inclusive governance. Ultimately, the paper underscores that navigating environmental biotechnology requires harmonizing technological promise with societal values and ro

title: Transfer Matrix and Tensor Approaches to Nucleic Acid Secondary Structure Thermodynamics *
abstract: Abstract Nucleic acid secondary structure thermodynamic models have great utility for the analysis and design of nucleic acid structures, devices, and systems, yet their complexity and piecemeal development over decades pose challenges to further innovation. Employing different functional forms for each loop type within a structure, existing nearest neighbor (NN) models necessitate numerous loop-specific dynamic programming recursions in order to calculate physical quantities of interest. Here, we derive and implement a new class of models based on transfer matrices, yielding a single functional form for the free energy of all loop types (as the trace of a matrix product) and a single dynamic programming recursion for calculating physical quantities of interest. This new class of models has additional attractive properties: 1) incorporating a subensemble of states describing proximal interactions within each loop, 2) approximating logarithmic entropic scaling for all closed loops, 3) offering the opportunity to model correlations between the subensembles of neighboring loops by generalizing transfer matrices to tensors, and 4) providing a basis for systematically adjusting the numb

title: Engineering CAR-T cell therapies for digestive tract cancer: advances, challenges, and strategies to overcome tumor heterogeneity and immunosuppressive barriers
abstract: CAR-T therapy yields remarkable clinical efficacy against hematological malignancies, yet its translation to solid tumors, particularly gastrointestinal cancers, is impeded by multiple bottlenecks including antigen heterogeneity, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments and metabolic inhibition. This review systematically summarizes coping strategies for these barriers. Claudin-18.2, B7-H3 and c-Met represent attractive therapeutic targets eliciting tumor-specific cytotoxicity in gastric, colorectal and esophageal cancers. Structural modifications such as dual-targeted CARs, cytokine-expressing constructs and logic-gated receptors improve antigen specificity and mitigate off-tumor toxicity. Combination regimens with radiotherapy, immune checkpoint inhibitors and TME-modulating agents synergistically boost CAR-T infiltration, persistence and effector activity. Unresolved hurdles still involve antigen loss, production scalability and inconsistent clinical responses, which may be tackled by γδT-based platforms, synthetic biology and universal CAR designs. title: Synthetic Biology and Genetic Engineering for Environmental Solutions
abstract: The escalating environmental crises of the 21st century—including climate change, pollution, biodiversity loss, and resource depletion—demand innovative and sustainable solutions beyond conventional technologies. Synthetic biology and genetic engineering have emerged as powerful, transformative tools that harness biological systems to address complex environmental challenges. By enabling the design, construction, and reprogramming of biological organisms, these technologies offer novel approaches for pollution mitigation, carbon sequestration, waste treatment, renewable energy production, and biodiversity conservation. This chapter provides a comprehensive exploration of synthetic biology and genetic engineering in the context of environmental applications. It presents the fundamental principles, key techniques, and core tools of these disciplines, including CRISPR-based genome editing, genetic circuits, biosensors, and metabolic pathway engineering. Furthermore, it highlights pioneering applications such as microbial bioremediation of pollutants, engineering algae for biofuel production, carbon capture through enhanced photosynthesis, and the development of biodegradable bioplasti

title: Harnessing Biotechnology: A Pathway to Environmental Sustainability
abstract: Biotechnology has emerged as a transformative tool for addressing environmental challenges by offering innovative solutions for sustainable development. Advances in genetic engineering, synthetic biology, and bioinformatics have enabled the development of eco-friendly technologies for agriculture, waste management, renewable energy, and ecosystem restoration. This review explores how biotechnological approaches contribute to environmental sustainability through genetically modified crops, biofertilizers, and biopesticides, reducing the ecological footprint of agriculture. Additionally, industrial biotechnology is revolutionizing green manufacturing by producing biodegradable materials, biofuels, and bio-based chemicals, minimizing reliance on fossil fuels. Bioremediation technologies, including microbial degradation and wastewater treatment, provide efficient methods for pollution control. Furthermore, biotechnology plays a crucial role in climate change mitigation through carbon sequestration strategies, algae-based carbon capture, and bioenergy production. title: Whole-cell filamentous fungal biocatalysts for biodiesel production: Mechanistic insights, process integration, and industrial perspectives
abstract: Biodiesel has emerged as a sustainable alternative to fossil-derived fuels, while whole-cell filamentous fungal biocatalysts have attracted increasing attention because of their intrinsic lipase activity, lipid accumulation capacity, and adaptability to heterogeneous feedstocks. Distinct from existing reviews, this review develops an integrated mechanism-to-process-to-industry perspective on fungal whole-cell biodiesel production. Literature was systematically retrieved from major databases using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, and recent advances were critically synthesized across strain engineering, catalytic mechanisms, bioprocess development, substrate utilization, reactor engineering, and industrial implementation. Particular attention is given to the relationships among lipase function, fungal morphology, metabolic regulation, mass transfer, and process conditions, and their effects on catalytic performance and stability. Major challenges, including mass-transfer limitations, methanol toxicity, catalyst deactivation, feedstock variability, and scale-up constraints, are evaluated together with corresponding mitigation strategies. title: Editorial: Biosynthetic pathways and metabolic engineering of bioactive natural products from medicinal plants
abstract: Glycosylation plays a critical role in altering the solubility, stability, and bioactivity of plant specialized metabolites. Focusing on Dendrobium huoshanense, Liu et al. conducted a comprehensive genome-wide identification of the UDP-glycosyltransferase (UGT) gene family (Liu et al., 2026). title: Bioremediation: Harnessing Microorganisms for Environmental Cleanup
abstract: Bioremediation is an environmentally sustainable and cost-effective approach that utilizes the natural metabolic capabilities of microorganisms, plants, and other biological agents to degrade, detoxify, or remove pollutants from contaminated environments. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of bioremediation, beginning with its fundamental principles and importance in modern environmental management. Various types of bioremediation, including in situ and ex situ methods, are explored in detail, highlighting processes such as natural attenuation, bio-stimulation, bioaugmentation, landfarming, and composting. The chapter delves into the microbial mechanisms driving pollutant degradation, emphasizing the roles of bacteria, fungi, and algae, as well as the enzymatic pathways involved. Key factors influencing microbial activity and the potential of genetic engineering to enhance bioremediation efficiency are also discussed. Applications of bioremediation for addressing oil spills, heavy metal contamination, industrial waste disposal, and wastewater treatment are presented, alongside an introduction to phytoremediation. title: Protein-Based Engineered Living Materials: From Programmable Self-Assembly to Mechanical Reinforcement via Biomineralization
abstract: Abstract The convergence of synthetic biology and materials science has given rise to the field of engineered living materials (ELMs). ELMs move beyond inert biomaterials by incorporating genetically programmable cells that can sense, adapt, and respond to their environment. Designing ELMs requires consideration of both the genetic tractability and physiology of the cellular chassis and the synergies with the surrounding scaffold that houses them. To that end, protein-based scaffolds inspired by structural proteins such as curli, elastin, silk, and collagen provide a supportive environment for living cells due to their tunable mechanical properties, biocompatibility, and functionalization potential through fused bioactive domains. A hurdle for advancing ELMs from proof-of-concept systems to robust materials is their typical soft nature, which prevents their deployment in mechanically demanding engineering applications. abstract: *The Discrete Conscious Cosmos Ternary Tensor Matrix* is an exhaustive, four-volume unified treatise establishing a non-reductionist, zero-free-parameter cosmological architecture that bridges high-energy string mathematics, non-singular plasma astrophysics, cytoskeletal biophysics, and neuromorphic photonic hardware engineering. The work resolves the foundational crisis of modern theoretical physics—the **Platonic Rift**—by permanently rejecting the continuous, infinitely divisible spacetime manifold and the abstract, zero-dimensional Euclidean point ($r = 0$), which historically generated the mathematical breakdowns of black hole singularities, the Big Bang origin, and infinite renormalization. title: The chloroplast-mitochondria interaction under water extremes: Insights into metabolic tug-of-war
abstract: Plants respond to water extremes through dynamic, organelle-level reprogramming of resource allocation rather than metabolic shutdown. Recent advances suggest that drought and flooding induce coordinated metabolic reorganization between chloroplasts and mitochondria, shifting energy distribution from growth to stress acclimation via retrograde signaling pathways. These signals are integrated by the trehalose-6-phosphate (Tre6P)-sucrose non-fermenting 1-related protein kinase 1 (SnRK1)-target of rapamycin (TOR) network, a central regulatory hub that interprets carbon and energy status to modulate stress-responsive metabolic and physiological outcomes. This systemic coordination is also modulated by hormone reprogramming and shaping adaptive phenotypic responses. Emerging technologies, spanning from organelle-specific metabolomics to synthetic biology, provide a framework to engineer inter-organellar communication. title: Harnessing Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria for the Biocontrol of Phytopathogens in Sustainable Agriculture: A Review
abstract: Plant diseases significantly reduce worldwide agricultural production, causing yield declines of 21-30% for major crops, while excessive use of pesticides and chemicals poses serious health and environmental risks. Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) offer an environmentally acceptable, efficient biocontrol approach against phytopathogens. Through direct mechanisms, such as the synthesis of phytohormones and nutrients, and indirect mechanisms, including the synthesis of antibiotics and siderophores and the establishment of induced systemic resistance (ISR), PGPR support plant development and suppress infections. This paper examines the role of PGPR in sustainable agriculture, focusing on their interactions with plant roots, rhizosphere dynamics, and the rhizosphere microbiome, as well as their biocontrol efficacy against fungal, bacterial, and nematode diseases. Key mechanisms include niche exclusion, competition for resources, and the release of antimicrobial compounds. Large-scale PGPR application is hindered by limitations such as inconsistent field performance, environmental acceptability concerns, and regulatory issues. title: Synthetic cells: Potential benefits and risks of interactions with commensal and pathogenic microorganisms
abstract: Synthetic cells are shifting biology from the observation and modification of existing life toward the deliberate construction of cell-like systems. The term, however, includes two biologically different entities: bottom-up protocells assembled from nonliving molecular components and top-down cells whose natural genomes have been minimized, rewritten, or replaced. These two classes occupy the extremes of a much broader landscape of engineered living systems, one that also includes conventional bacteria, yeasts, and mammalian and immune cells carrying synthetic gene circuits, logic programs, and redesigned metabolic pathways. This Perspective is deliberately centered on the two extremes, because they bracket the range of biological autonomy and pose the sharpest contrast between a programmable chemical package and a self-replicating organism; the wider landscape is noted and is drawn upon throughout wherever it bears directly on interaction with microbial communities. Both approaches can clarify the minimum requirements for cellular organization, test hypotheses about the origin and evolution of life, expand biological chemistry, and support programmable sensing or therapy. title: Between Biology and Engineering : Philosophical Foundations of Design in Synthetic Biology
abstract: This dissertation explores methodological and philosophical questions concerning design in synthetic biology. Synthetic biology is a recent biological field that is often presented as a program that aims to make biology and biotechnology more like engineering. The dissertation analyzes the tensions and the philosophical implications that arise from moving from a metaphorical understanding of the design concept to an actual task of designing novel biological organisms. A central goal of the dissertation is to assess the promises of synthetic biology and make some of its claims more theoretically transparent and better grounded in the practice of synthetic biology. The dissertation is divided into two thematic parts. The first two articles focus on the methodological questions that arise from the design of biological systems. These articles explore the methodological commitments of various design approaches within synthetic biology, specifically contrasting engineering-inspired rational design with biology-informed evolutionary methods. Using a combination of philosophical analysis and case studies from synthetic biology, the dissertation investigates the heuristics and assumptions u

title: Mechanisms of Resistance and Susceptibility to Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4 (Foc TR4) in Banana: A Review
abstract: Abstract Banana (Musa spp.) is a globally critical staple food and cash crop, yet its production is threatened by Fusarium wilt caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense tropical race 4 (Foc TR4), a soil-borne pathogen with a broad host range and persistent virulence. This review synthesizes current knowledge of Foc TR4’s infection process, host immune responses, molecular mechanisms of resistance, pathogen evasion strategies, and breeding approaches for durable resistance. We highlight key findings from multi-omics studies, synthetic biology applications, and regulatory considerations for field deployment. Critical knowledge gaps include the molecular basis of Foc TR4’s broad host compatibility, the role of epigenetic modifications in resistance, and the long-term stability of transgenic resistance in diverse agroecosystems. Addressing these gaps is essential for developing sustainable management strategies to safeguard banana production against Foc TR4.

title: From Molecules to Cancer Immunogenomics: Can Integrated Systems Biology Enable the Future of Precision Cancer Therapy
abstract: The project highlights an integrative approach to treat cancer by simultaneously suppressing tumor growth and promoting tissue regeneration. The idea stems from the understanding that cancer progression arises from interconnected signaling networks and microenvironmental dysregulation that can be reprogrammed through a designed chimera of polyherbal bioactive molecules on a Nonabody scaffold. The goal seeks to achieve triple platform therapeutic model integrating systems biology, polyherbal chimera engineered on a Nonabody scaffold, and probiotics. This framework enables precise tumor suppression, immune modulation, and activation of regenerative pathways within a unified precision systems medicine approach. The vision advances a scientifically validated integrative oncology platform that supports transformative translational research for holistic cancer therapy and regenerative medicine. The mission focuses on coordinated suppression of oncogenic signaling, activation of immune surveillance, and modulation of the gut liver tumor axis. Methodologically, the approach develops chimeras of polyherbal peptides and bioactive molecules derived from Scutellaria baicalensis, Rubia cordifol

title: CsMT : a robust and streamlined CryoSPARC workflow for cryo-EM reconstruction of microtubules
abstract: Microtubules are cytoskeletal filaments that are involved in intracellular transport, cell division and motility. Despite their biological importance, determining their high-resolution structures via cryo-electron microscopy remains a significant technical challenge due to their polymorphism and pseudo-helical assembly. Current processing workflows are complex, often requiring the integration of multiple software packages and custom scripts, which creates a steep learning curve for many research groups. To address these limitations, we introduce CsMT, a streamlined workflow implemented entirely within the CryoSPARC environment and using synthetic references. CsMT simplifies microtubule reconstruction by utilizing a novel protofilament-pair classification approach, which effectively handles the inherent pseudo-symmetry and structural heterogeneity of microtubules with minimal manual intervention. Our workflow is versatile, and is capable of processing both undecorated and decorated microtubules while accurately determining seams and performing high-resolution refinement. title: APPLICATION OF FUNCTIONALIZED SYNTHETIC LIPIDS IN BIOLOGY AND MEDICINE
abstract: Beyond medical applications, FSL technology addresses fundamental biological questions, particularly in studying and modeling complement activation - a key mechanism of innate immunity. Using kodecytes modified with FSL constructs bearing specific glycans, it was confirmed that certain anti-glycan antibodies lack complement-activating capacity. Moreover, the hemolytic activity of complement in human serum was found to be twice as stable as previously assumed: 60% of activity was retained after one week at room temperature and two months at 4°C. Additionally, cholesterol-based lipid constructs enable targeted incorporation into lipid rafts - membrane microdomains central to cell signaling - opening perspectives for antigen-independent modulation of immune responses. Furthermore, fluorescent and biotinylated FSL constructs allow for the modification of enveloped viruses (e.g., influenza) for bioimaging of virions both in vitro and in vivo. A key advantage of FSL technology is its ability to modify virtually any surface, including non-biological ones, without prior chemical activation. Harnessing Microbial Metabolism for Sustainable Environmental Remediation
abstract: Environmental contamination caused by industrialization, urbanization, intensive agriculture, petroleum exploitation, mining, pharmaceutical production, and improper waste disposal has created persistent challenges for ecosystem stability and human well-being. Conventional remediation technologies, including chemical oxidation, thermal treatment, excavation, incineration, and physicochemical separation, can be effective but may require substantial energy, chemical inputs, infrastructure, and secondary waste management. Microbial bioremediation provides an alternative approach by exploiting the metabolic versatility of bacteria, fungi, archaea, algae, and their associated enzymes to transform, degrade, immobilize, or recover environmental contaminants. This review examines how microbial metabolism can be harnessed for sustainable remediation of organic and inorganic pollutants. Particular attention is given to hydrocarbon degradation, pesticide and pharmaceutical transformation, dye decolorization, heavy-metal immobilization, plastic degradation, and treatment of complex industrial wastewater. Microbial remediation mechanisms include aerobic oxidation, anaerobic reduction, hydrolysi

title: Integrated microbial and enzymatic strategies for waste valorization: From substrate depolymerization to bioproduct synthesis
Pine wilt disease as a holobiont disorder: microbiome assembly as a potential management target
abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by the pinewood nematode (PWN) Bursaphelenchus xylophilus, continues to expand globally despite decades of pathogen-focused management. Here, we propose that disruption of microbiome assembly within the pine holobiont may contribute to disease progression and help explain variation in disease outcomes and responses to microbial interventions. Drawing on recent advances in microbial ecology, multi-omics, and synthetic biology, we synthesize evidence of PWD-associated changes in host-associated microbial communities and examine how altered functional redundancy and pathobiome formation may contribute to disease progression. We propose that microbiome assembly, shaped by host traits, environmental filters, and biotic interactions, is a plausible and underexplored determinant of disease outcome. Building on this framework, we outline a shift from single-agent biocontrol toward assembly-informed microbiome engineering. To support reproducible design and future validation, we outline criteria for selecting candidate consortium members and assessing synthetic microbial community (SynCom) establishment, persistence and functional stability. title: Mangroves as a Source for Saponins
abstract: Mangrove ecosystems, which are found at the land-sea interface in tropical and subtropical regions, are an important source of bioactive substances, especially saponins, a natural glycoside pharmacologically important. In this review, we explore the botanical aspects of mangroves, the structure and classification of saponins, and progress made on extraction and analytical techniques. The article briefly highlights high-yielding mangrove species and examines the effects of geographic and seasonal variation on saponin content, as well as recent research detailing species-delimited saponin profiles. The future directions of the field include synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, newer delivery systems, and collaborative research projects to maximize the potential of mangrove saponins. This review has provided an important cross-disciplinary resource by filling in the knowledge gap and providing guidance for the sustainable development and industrial commercialization of saponins derived from mangrove habitats.

Retention and biosynthesis of diverse nitroarenes in Escherichia coli after combinatorial nitroreductase gene deletions
abstract: The instability of nitroaromatic compounds or nitroarenes in the presence of microbial cells has hindered the ability to biomanufacture these industrially and pharmaceutically relevant chemicals. Although nitroreductase (NTR) gene deletions have been linked to nitroarene stability, the extent of this effect is unclear. Here we perform a comprehensive analysis of bacterial NTR activity in cells by engineering strains of Escherichia coli that contain up to 15 knockouts of known and candidate NTR genes. We evaluate the stability of over 20 exogenously supplemented nitroaromatic compounds to wild-type and engineered strains. For several chemistries, such as di-nitro compounds and nitro-aldehydes, our engineered nitroaromatic reductase knockout strains enable retention of compounds. We leverage these tools and insights to improve or enable nitroaromatic compound biosynthesis, including the biocatalytic transformation of an amine precursor to a nitro compound, the biosynthesis of nitrobenzaldehydes and the combined semi-synthesis and site-specific incorporation of nitrophenylalanines from supplemented nitrobenzaldehydes. title: Ionizing radiation-induced repair foci identification using deep convolutional neural networks
abstract: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), visualized as ionizing radiation-induced repair foci (IRIFs), represent a severe form of DNA damage and are central to radiation biology, cancer research, and space health. Quantifying IRIF induction and repair is critical for biodosimetry but is traditionally performed using approaches sensitive to image variability. This study developed a robust and scalable method for accurate IRIF detection and quantification using deep learning. A modified U-Net architecture was employed for semantic segmentation of IRIFs in fluorescence microscopy images. The model was trained on 95,000 synthetically generated image-mask pairs designed to replicate signal, noise, and morphological characteristics of real microscopy data. Model performance was evaluated both on synthetic data and on a real-world dataset of 345 manually annotated mouse fibroblast images from the NASA GeneLab OSD-366 experiment, encompassing multiple radiation types and doses. Segmentation and foci detection performance were assessed using Dice coefficient, Intersection over Union (IoU), precision and recall. title: Monoacetyldiacylglycerols as emerging immunomodulatory lipids in chronic inflammation: mechanisms, biology, and translational potential
abstract: Chronic inflammatory diseases remain a major global health burden, with approximately 30–40% of patients responding inadequately to current cytokine-targeted biologics, Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors, or small-molecule immunomodulators. Beyond suboptimal efficacy, these therapies carry well-documented adverse effects, including infection and malignancy risks associated with JAK inhibitors, and act on single molecular targets, leaving upstream, membrane-proximal drivers of chronic inflammation largely unaddressed. Monoacetyldiacylglycerols (MacDGs), a structurally distinct class of partially acetylated triglycerides, have emerged as promising immunomodulatory lipids that act concurrently across multiple inflammatory signaling nodes, including STAT3/STAT6 and NF-κB pathways, macrophage polarization, and epithelial barrier integrity, offering mechanistic breadth that single-target therapies do not provide. Current evidence, derived predominantly from the synthetic analog palmitic–linoleic–acetyldiacylglycero (PLAG), demonstrates reproducible suppression of signal transducer and activator of transcription 3/6 (STAT3/STAT6) and nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cel

title: ARCANE: ‘A Reprogrammable Circuit Architecture for Non-model Engineering’ enables sophisticated metabolic control in Yarrowia lipolytica
abstract: The rational engineering of non-model microorganisms is often constrained by the scarcity of high-performance genetic regulatory tools. To overcome this limitation, we developed ARCANE – a reprogrammable circuit architecture for non-model engineering – featuring a cascaded design in which an inducer controls orthogonal bacterial transcription factors (bTFs), which in turn drive both activation and repression of endogenous promoters. This architecture provides strong insulation from host regulatory networks, minimizes leakage, and enables a broad dynamic range. As a proof-of-concept, we implemented ARCANE in the industrially significant non-model yeast, Yarrowia lipolytica . The resulting genetic switch exhibited exceptionally precise and tunable control over both single reporter genes and a multi-gene carotenoid biosynthesis pathway. Beyond providing a powerful regulatory tool for Y. lipolytica , ARCANE offers a versatile and transferable modular foundation for programmable gene control in emerging microbial platforms, paving the way for scalable synthetic biology in non-model systems.

title: Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
abstract: Hydrogen has been recognized as a key pillar of future energy systems in the global pursuit of carbon neutrality. However, hydrogen production processes still highly rely on fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production is a microbial-based process that converts biomass, organic waste, and solar energy into hydrogen via dark fermentation, photo-fermentation, or photolytic water-splitting pathways. It is a promising pathway to sustainable energy, with the potential for carbon-negative emissions under favorable feedstock and system-boundary conditions. Yet, the limitations of natural biological systems, such as poor energy conversion efficiency, huge carbon diversion, and poor operational robustness, have prevented its transition from laboratory research to industrial application. To resolve these bottlenecks, this review proposes a strategic shift from traditional biological conversion toward intelligent biomanufacturing via three enabling technologies: (1) synthetic biology to design microbial cell factories with a tailored hydrogen-centric metabolism; (2) nanomaterials engineering to create smart biotic-abiotic interfaces for overcoming the physical limitations of electron and mass transfe

title: Mangroves as a Source of Flavonoids
abstract: Flavonoids are well-distributed polyphenolics across families in the plant kingdom, including mangroves. The diversity of mangroves evolved in their adaptation to unique coastal ecosystems through exerting flavonoids in their adaptive process. These secondary metabolites have diverse pharmacological activities, including the antibacterial compound dalpanitin 134 isolated from Derris scancen s (minimum inhibitory concentration value of 23 μg mL-1 against S. aureus ), antineoplastic 3′,4′,5,7-tetrahydroxyflavone isolated from Sonneratia caseolaris against hepatoma cells with IC 50 value of 2.8 μg/mL, anti-plasmodial agent myricetrin 165 with IC 50 value of 50 μM, and quercetin 3- O -(2″- O -galloyl)- α -rhamnopyranoside 172 , antioxidant produced by Lumnitzera racemosa with IC 50 value of 7.20 μM. Researchers worldwide have made several attempts to elucidate their biosynthetic pathways and to develop combinatorial approaches for producing targeted synthetic flavonoids. title: Informational Ethics and Agency: Action, Responsibility, and Morality in an Informational Universe
abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for informational ethics and agency, wherein action, responsibility, and morality emerge not from biological substrates or material bodies, but from stabilized curvature domains, cognitive fields, and geodesic informational processes. Building on informational consciousness, post-material field organisms, synthetic biology, and informational civilizational theory, we demonstrate that ethical structures can be fully formulated as emergent informational phenomena. Within this framework, agency is defined as geodesic modulation, responsibility as curvature stabilization, and morality as systemic divergence reduction within collective informational networks, offering an algorithmically testable formulation of post-material normative dynamics. Keywords: Informational Ethics, Agency Dynamic, Curvature Stabilization, Divergence Reduction, Normative Curvature Fields, Graph Laplacians

title: Informational Ecology: Interaction, Competition, and Cooperation Between Informational Organisms
abstract: This paper establishes the foundational principles of informational ecology, a framework wherein ecological systems and multi-agent interactions emerge not from material substrates or organic chemistry, but from coupled informational fields, pressure gradients, and relational curvature domains. Building on synthetic informational biology and informational evolution theory, we demonstrate that ecological phenomena—such as resource competition, symbiotic field coupling, niche organization, and non-material trophic chains—can be fully modeled within discrete network topologies. The resulting framework provides a rigorous, algorithmically simulation-ready basis for evaluating the long-term stability and macrostructural emergence of large-scale, post-material ecosystems. Keywords: Informational Ecology, Multi-Field Symbiosis, Resource Competition, Trophic Field Transformation, Ecosystem Stability, Graph Laplacians

title: The Informational Universe II: Grand Unified Edition of Informational Physics, Biology, Consciousness, Cosmology, and Civilization
abstract: This monograph presents the Grand Unified Edition of the informational universe framework, integrating all previous foundational components—informational ontology, dynamics, waves, fields, geometry, consciousness, synthetic biology, evolution, ecology, cosmology, civilization theory, ethics, and technology—into a single, consistent, non-metric relational model. The universe is fully formulated as a dynamic informational process in which physical, biological, cognitive, cultural, and technological macrostructures emerge from stabilized curvature domains, pressure gradients, and coupled cognitive fields. This work establishes the definitive, comprehensive unified field theory of a non-metric informational cosmos. Keywords: Grand Unified Framework, Informational Field Theory, Emergent Reality, Relational Topology, Multi-Field Dynamics, Graph Laplacians

title: Informational Cosmology II: Cosmic Ecosystems, Field Organisms, and Large-Scale Informational Biotopes
abstract: This paper develops an extended informational-cosmological theory wherein the large-scale structure of the universe is formulated not as a material or geometric spacetime background, but as a dynamic network of coupled informational fields, pressure gradients, and relational curvature domains. Building on previous work on informational ontology, post-material field organisms, synthetic biology, and informational ecology, we demonstrate that cosmic filaments, galaxies, accretion disks, and pulsar magnetospheres act as computational informational biotopes. Within these macroscale field structures, non-material organisms emerge, interact, and evolve. The resulting framework provides a rigorous, algorithmically simulation-ready model characterizing the universe as a self-organizing cosmic informational ecosystem. Keywords: Informational Cosmology, Cosmic Biotopes, Macroscale Curvature Domains, Relational Ecosystems, Field Organisms, Graph Laplacians

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI THEORY OF PLANETARY SYMBIOSIS AND REVERSE METABOLIC ENGINEERING Breaking the Chains of Scarcity and Engineering a Bio-Quantum Civilization of Abundance A Groundbreaking Theoretical Framework Unifying Quantum Physics, Synthetic Biology, and Planetary Engineering to Transition Humanity from Extractive Scarcity to Regenerative Abundance
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Planetary Symbiosis and Reverse Metabolic Engineering (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211161) proposes a theoretical framework to transition humanity from extractive scarcity to a post-scarcity civilization. It introduces three bio-quantum pillars: (1) Quantum Atmospheric Osmosis, using bio-quantum MOFs for zero-energy water harvesting; (2) Hyper-Photosynthesis, harvesting ambient energy via non-equilibrium thermodynamics and passive radiative cooling; (3) Atmospheric Bio-Synthesis, converting CO2/N2 to food using AI-designed enzymes secured by molecular biocontainment (auxotrophic strains). It introduces the Planetary Abundance Coefficient (PAC), a mathematically bounded (0-1) metric rigorously normalized against per capita baselines and planetary boundaries to measure the shift from extraction to symbiosis. Serving as the material foundation of the El-Rakhawi Corpus, it offers a roadmap to end resource wars. Released under the Ferial Zayed Humanitarian License.

title: Informational Evolution Theory: Selection, Variation, and Emergence in an Informational Universe
abstract: This paper develops an evolutionary theory for an informational universe in which organismic structures emerge not from physical matter or genetic substrates, but from informational fields, pressure gradients, and localized curvature domains. Building on synthetic informational biology, informational consciousness, and post-material field organisms, we demonstrate that evolutionary dynamics can be fully formulated without genes, mutations, or biological matter. Informational evolution is driven by curvature selection, divergence selection, field coupling variation, and geodesic optimization. The resulting framework describes the generation, transformation, and long-term stabilization of complex organismic information structures within relational network topologies. Keywords: Informational Evolution, Curvature Selection, Divergence Penalty, Non-Genetic Variation, Speciation Dynamic, Relational Biology

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI THEORY OF UNIVERSAL CYBERNETIC HARMONY AND REGENERATIVE COMPLEX ADAPTIVE SYSTEMS From Synthetic Biology to Holistic Cosmic Decision Support
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Universal Cybernetic Harmony and Regenerative Complex Adaptive Systems (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23203404) unifies 23 cybernetic and AI domains into a regenerative ecosystem. Four pillars: (1) Harmonious Control, shifting from rigid command to dynamic, self-organizing adaptation; (2) Bio-Cybernetic Convergence, merging Synthetic Biology and Medical Cybernetics with Molecular Accountability and Genetic Kill Switches; (3) Soft Cognitive Intelligence, using Neural Networks, Fuzzy Systems, and Affective Computing for contextual perception and quantified empathy; (4) Macro-Systemic Regeneration, applying Cyber-Sociology and Holistic Decision Support via Decentralized Consensus and Human-in-the-Loop safeguards. Introduces the Cybernetic Harmony Index (CHI), measuring adaptability, synergy, regeneration, and empathy against systemic friction. Integrates with the El-Rakhawi Corpus on Regenerative Economics and Digital Sovereignty. Released under Ferial Zayed Humanitarian License.

title: Informational Technology: Field Modulation, Curvature Architecture, and Informational Pressure Engines
abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for informational technology wherein tools, engines, and technical systems consist not of physical matter or hardware, but of stabilized informational fields, pressure gradients, and curvature architectures. Building on informational consciousness, field organisms, synthetic biology, and civilizational theory, we demonstrate that technology can be fully formulated as an emergent informational phenomenon. Informational technology is defined as the controlled modulation of informational pressure, curvature, and cognitive fields to construct stable, functional structures within discrete network topologies, offering an algorithmically simulation-ready model of post-material engineering. Keywords: Informational Technology, Pressure Engines, Curvature Architecture, Field Modulation, Complex Relational Machines, Graph Laplacians

title: Informational Civilization Theory: Collective Intelligence, Culture, and Society in an Informational Universe
abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for informational civilizations wherein collective intelligence, cultural structures, and societal systems emerge not from physical matter or biological organisms, but from stabilized curvature domains, cognitive fields, and cooperative informational networks. Building on synthetic informational biology, informational evolution, and large-scale cosmology, we demonstrate that civilizations can exist completely independent of material or organic substrates. Informational civilizations are modeled as macroscopic collective field organisms whose internal dynamics are governed by geodesic optimization, symbiotic field coupling, and cultural information selection. The resulting framework provides a rigorous, algorithmically testable basis for describing the emergence of complex distributed societies, collective consciousness fields, and light-year-scale cosmic informational networks. Keywords: Informational Civilizations, Collective Field Organisms, Societal Field Coupling, Cultural Selection, Curvature Resonance, Graph Laplacians

title: Synthetic Informational Biology: Emergent Organismic Structures in an Informational Universe
abstract: This paper establishes the foundations of synthetic informational biology, a framework in which organismic structures emerge not from physical matter or organic chemistry, but from informational fields, pressure gradients, and localized curvature domains. Building on an ontology where space, dynamics, geometry, and consciousness are formulated as relational informational processes, we demonstrate that core biological concepts—such as cells, tissues, organisms, evolution, and ecology—can be fully reconstructed without material substrates. The resulting theory defines life as stabilized curvature domains whose internal dynamics are governed by geodesic optimization, entropic information selection, and field coupling, providing an algorithmically testable basis for post-material biological structures. Keywords: Synthetic Informational Biology, Informational Cells, Tissue Coupling, Non-Material Evolution, Curvature Domains, Graph Laplacians

title: Chemical Pharmacognosy in the Era of Integrated Natural-Product Discovery: From Traditional Knowledge to Therapeutic Translation
abstract: Natural products have played a central role in the development of medicines and continue to provide structurally diverse molecules, pharmacological leads, and molecular frameworks for contemporary drug discovery. Chemical pharmacognosy has traditionally focused on the isolation, characterization, and biological evaluation of constituents obtained from medicinal plants and other natural sources. The discipline has progressively expanded through advances in analytical chemistry, molecular biology, metabolomics, computational science, genomics, and biotechnology. Consequently, modern chemical pharmacognosy is increasingly positioned as an integrated discovery framework rather than a discipline restricted to the isolation of individual compounds. This review examines the transition from traditional knowledge-guided investigation toward a multidisciplinary approach that combines ethnopharmacological information, botanical authentication, chemical profiling, dereplication, metabolomics, molecular networking, bioactivity screening, genome mining, synthetic biology, and translational pharmaceutical development. title: Increasing Overhang GC-Content Increases Sticky-End Ligation Efficiency
abstract: The ligation efficiency of sticky-ends differs between overhangs generated by different restriction enzymes. Differences between the composition of these overhangs include length and GC-content, thus indicating that these properties may play a role in ligation efficiency. Although ligases are a common and widely used tool in molecular biology, a method to accurately quantify ligation efficiency has yet to be fully developed and standardized. In this study, ligation efficiency of synthetic oligonucleotides with four-nucleotide overhangs containing varying GC-content was quantitatively investigated using qPCR. Two sets of synthetic, double-stranded oligonucleotides with complementary overhangs were created. The complementary oligonucleotides were mixed with ligase, and the efficiency of ligation was quantified by measuring an increase in fluorescence intensity due to SYBR Green intercalation between amplified polymerase chain reaction products, where ligated oligonucleotide served as template. title: Chemical Diversity of Microalgae: Bioactive Compounds for Therapeutic, Nutraceutical and Cosmetic Applications
abstract: Abstract: Microalgae serve as a rich source of diverse secondary metabolites and macromolecules. These include carotenoids, polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), sterols, phenols, peptides, proteins, and polysaccharides. Besides their nutritional value, these bioactive compounds exhibit antihypertensive, antioxidant, anticancer, anti-obesity, and cardiovascular-protective properties. In addition to providing valuable products, microalgae are vital for carbon sequestration. Marine microalgae are exceptionally promising and economical sources of valuable compounds due to their ease of cultivation: they require only seawater, minerals, and essential salts, without soil. Indeed, they offer a sustainable and economically viable source of biofuels, bio-products, and animal feed with a minimal environmental footprint. Moreover, synthetic biology, omics, and artificial intelligence (AI) enable precise manipulation of growth regulators to increase yields of valuable metabolites. Some of these bioactive compounds also play a vital ecological function, such as chemical communication and defense against grazing. title: Highly multiplexed mammalian metabolic engineering with a shotgun approach
abstract: Mammalian metabolic engineering advances basic biology, bioproduction and cell therapy. However, as pathway complexity increases, so does the size of the combinatorial design space and required DNA constructs, rendering unbiased screens intractable. Here, we developed shotgun genetic engineering (SGE), which exploits the ease of delivering many barcoded small constructs-rather than a single large one-into mammalian cells. Each cell serves as an independent experiment, carrying a synthetic pathway that explores gene content, stoichiometry and organellar localization. Functional pathways are identified by sequencing barcodes from cells exhibiting the desired phenotype. Using SGE, we screened millions of pathway combinations to engineer essential amino acid biosynthesis, achieving near-wild-type growth without valine and enabling isoleucine-free growth in Chinese hamster ovary cells, as well as valine-free growth in Jurkat cells. Functional pathways favored mitochondrial localization and required the integration of tens of kilobases of synthetic DNA, beyond the scale of conventional screening. title: Harnessing CYP71 Enzymes for Terpenoid Indole Alkaloid Production: A Synthetic Biology Perspective from Discovery to Application
abstract: Abstract Terpenoid indole alkaloids (TIAs) are a class of structurally diverse natural products with important pharmacological activities. Recently, substantial progress has been made in elucidating TIA biosynthetic pathways, and these studies have revealed the central roles of CYP71 clan enzymes (CYP71s) in both the formation and the modification of the TIA scaffold. In this review, we trace the stepwise elucidation of representative TIA biosynthetic pathways and summarize the functions and catalytic principles of the CYP71s, with emphasis on the reaction types and mechanistic features that underlie their functional versatility. Nevertheless, reconstructing these extended multienzyme pathways in heterologous cell factories remains challenging, in large part because plant cytochrome P450 enzymes (P450s) frequently become rate-limiting owing to inefficient electron transfer and limited cofactor availability. We therefore review metabolic engineering strategies established for P450 systems and assess their applicability to the optimization of CYP71s and to TIA production. abstract: The escalating global crisis of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents one of the most formidable threats to modern medicine and public health, raising the prospect of a post-antibiotic era. As conventional small-molecule antibiotics increasingly fail against multidrug-resistant (MDR) priority pathogens, biogenic nanoparticles (BNPs) have emerged as promising, eco-friendly, and highly versatile nanoplatforms (Estevez et al., 2021). Synthesized via biological entities, including plants, bacteria, fungi, algae, and genetically engineered nanocompartments, BNPs provide a sustainable alternative to traditional chemical and physical synthesis routes. By leveraging natural cellular machinery and biological metabolites, green synthesis not only eliminates toxic chemical reductants and harsh reaction conditions but also imparts an intrinsic biomolecular capping layer that governs particle stability, surface charge, biocompatibility, and targeted nano-bio interactions.This Frontiers Research Topic brings together original research and critical reviews at the intersection of green nanotechnology, biomedical engineering, structural biology, and translational microbiology. Structural basis of eIF4E recognition of synthetic mRNA 5′ cap analogues links cap architecture to affinity and biological activity
abstract: Eukaryotic mRNAs carry a 5′-terminal 7-methylguanosine (m7G) cap that is recognized by multiple cellular proteins and is essential for mRNA self-discrimination, stability, and translation. The eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E (eIF4E) binds the 5′ cap and promotes recruitment of mRNAs to the ribosomal translation initiation complex, a critical step in cap-dependent translation. Beyond naturally occurring cap modifications that modulate mRNA interactions and fate, non-natural 5′ cap modifications can be used to finely tune diverse aspects of mRNA biology. This has gained particular relevance with the emergence of in vitro transcribed mRNAs as a powerful therapeutic modality for protein replacement therapies and vaccines. Here, we report binding data for a series of synthetic 5′ cap analogues interacting with eIF4E, together with X-ray crystal structures of eIF4E-cap complexes, providing detailed insights into the structural determinants of cap recognition by eIF4E. Furthermore, analysis of gene expression from mRNAs carrying different synthetic cap analogues in human cell lines and mice revealed a relationship between cap architecture and protein expression. title: Comparative Analysis of Inhibition Efficiency of Chimeric Antisense Oligonucleotides with Various Chemical Modifications and Their Application for Exogenous Control of Gene Expression in Escherichia coli
abstract: Background: Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) are synthetic nucleic acid analogs that can suppress gene expression through sequence-specific hybridization with target RNA. Enzymatic degradation, low bioavailability, and limited cellular uptake constrain their applications. Chemical modifications to the backbone and sugar moieties can enhance nuclease resistance, improve hybridization affinity, and extend in vivo half-life. This study compared the effects of structural and chemical modifications on the inhibitory activity of cell-penetrating peptide-conjugated ASOs in a bacterial reporter system. Methods: Seven ASO variants were evaluated, encompassing nucleotide deletions and additions, locked nucleic acid residues, 2′-O-methyl modifications, thiophosphoramidate morpholino (TMO) chemistry, and phosphorothioate (PS) linkages. We assessed inhibitory activity in Escherichia coli using a lacZ reporter assay. We quantified their effects by measuring residual β-galactosidase activity, providing a functional readout of reporter inhibition across the seven designs. title: β-Hairpin Fold Peptide Brush Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Peptide-brush polymers prepared via graft-through polymerization of peptide-based olefinic monomers form Protein-Like Polymers (PLPs) with demonstrated utility as chemical biology tools for modulating intracellular protein–protein interactions and are in development as a emerging class of therapeutic. This favorable bioactivity has been achieved in part by mimicking some of the structural and functional features of proteins, such as their dynamic, globular solution-phase structures, ability to insert into lipid membranes and enter cells, and tendency to enforce α-helicity in peptide side chains. However, because structure leads to function, insight into the structure of these proteomimetic polymers, particularly their overall tertiary structure and the extent to which this influences the brush peptide structure, is incomplete. To further this understanding, we prepared a set of brush polymers incorporating the trpzip2 peptide sequence, commonly used as a model system for protein folding. title: Mapping the research landscape of antagonistic microorganisms for fruit disease biocontrol: Global trends, thematic evolution, and emerging research frontiers (2000–2026)
Biomolecular Condensates in Horticultural and Field Crops
abstract: Membraneless compartments assembled by liquid–liquid phase separation have moved rapidly from a curiosity of in vitro biophysics to a working explanation for how crop plants sense temperature, water, ions and pathogens. In this review, we synthesize the physicochemical rules that govern condensate assembly in plant cells, trace how those rules are deployed across the horticultural pathosystems and stress physiologies that matter for food production and evaluate the emerging engineering and chemical toolkits — synthetic scaffolds, optogenetic phase regulators, condensate-targeting phytovirucides and condensate-aware breeding alleles — that aim to convert condensate biology into agronomic gain.

title: CLEAN Database: providing enzyme function coverage for over 55 million sequences
abstract: Enzyme function annotation is critical for decoding biological systems and enabling rational enzyme design. However, experimentally characterized enzyme functions remain available for only a small fraction of known protein sequences, resulting in a widening gap between rapidly expanding sequence space and reliable functional assignments. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated enzyme function annotation by facilitating accurate and high-throughput prediction from protein sequences. Here, we present CLEAN Database (CLEAN DB), a comprehensive resource encompassing >55 million enzyme function annotations across 1 098 305 strains, predicted by the CLEAN AI model. The database features an intuitive web interface that enables users to efficiently search, explore, and download enzyme function data through flexible query options. Additionally, powered by a protein language model, CLEAN DB supports mutation effect prediction through interactive heatmaps, structural overlays, and tabular data visualizations. We anticipate that CLEAN DB will serve as a valuable platform for advancing enzyme discovery and applications in synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, enzyme

title: RNA therapeutics in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and systemic sclerosis: a compartment-aware translational framework
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus/lupus nephritis (SLE/LN), and systemic sclerosis (SSc) remain major causes of chronic inflammation, disability, organ damage, and treatment burden despite therapeutic advances. RNA therapeutics offer programmable transcript suppression, network-level microRNA modulation, transient restoration of protective proteins, and targeting-ligand functions. Existing reviews largely catalogue modalities or individual delivery systems; this review instead asks whether a candidate forms an interpretable translational program across target biology, disease compartment, intended cell, productive intracellular access, direct target engagement, pathway pharmacodynamics, repeat-dose safety, and manufacturing feasibility. RA is primarily a synovial immune–stromal delivery problem in which RNA programs must also demonstrate an advantage over effective biologic or targeted synthetic therapies. SLE/LN offers interferon, B-cell, co-stimulatory, microRNA, messenger RNA (mRNA), and complement opportunities, but therapeutic nucleic acids and carriers must not intensify nucleic-acid sensing, interferon activity, or complement-associated injury. title: Bispecific Coiled-Coil Reporters Enable Rapid, Multiplexed Detection of Mycoplasma via Toehold Switch Sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT Cell-free synthetic biology offers a rapid prototyping environment for molecular diagnostics, yet the utility of these systems is often limited by the slow kinetics and restricted multiplexing capabilities of traditional protein reporters. Here, we report the BINOCULAR (BIspecific Novel Orthogonal Coiled-coil-Using LAteral flow Reporter) system based on supramolecular coiled-coil peptide conjugates that dramatically accelerates signal generation and enables robust multiplexing in cell-free transcription-translation reactions. Using BINOCULARs as toehold switch outputs, we achieve visible readout times of less than 5 minutes in lateral flow assays, achieving a ≥12-fold increase in speed compared to standard cell-free reporters like β-galactosidase or fluorescent proteins. To demonstrate the utility of this platform, we integrated the bispecific reporters with loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and a lateral flow assay for the detection of mycoplasma , a common adventitious agent in biomanufacturing. The integrated system demonstrates exceptional sensitivity, achieving a detection limit of 1 copy/µL for Mycoplasma 16S rRNA and a mammalian internal control gene. Ce

Understanding the control of perpetual flowering and continuous runnering in strawberry
abstract: Consumer demand for year-round strawberry fruit has increased the need to extend the cropping season. Perpetual flowering cultivars, which produce fruit continuously throughout the growing season, offer a promising solution. However, these cultivars typically exhibit reduced runner production, due to a genetic trade-off between flowering and runnering, presenting challenges for propagation and breeding efforts. Additionally, limited understanding of the mechanisms controlling these traits in the cultivated strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa) has hindered the application of advanced breeding or crop improvement tools. This PhD work aimed to better understand the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying perpetual flowering and continuous runnering in strawberry, to contribute to the development of perpetual flowering cultivars with extended fruiting periods and improved propagation potential. In this thesis the control of perpetual flowering was explored by functionally studying key f lowering genes TFL1 and FT1 in F. x ananassa seasonal flowering cultivar ‘Malling Centenary’ and perpetual flowering cultivar ‘Calypso’ using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing and phenotyping. title: Pectinase-Based Bioprocesses for Circular Bioeconomy and Sustainable Industrial Development.
abstract: Pectinases play a vital role in the degradation of pectic part of the plant cell wall and are considered in the group of hydrolytic enzymes. In the present scenario, demand of economically feasible and environment friendly techniques and approaches has significantly led the research on the microbial production, standardization of process parameters and improvements of pectinases. The development of pectinase-based bioprocesses has been found to promote sustainable industrial practices by reducing the use of chemicals, energy, and waste, thereby supporting eco-friendly production systems. The unique aspect of this review is that it explains traditional methods of pectinase production alongside novel methods, which include solid-state and submerged fermentation, recombinant DNA techniques, heterologous gene expression, protein engineering, CRISPR/Cas genome editing technologies, enzyme immobilization, and nanobiotechnological methods, which improve the production, stability, and performance of pectinases. It further demonstrates the increasing importance of the use of pectinases in sustainable manufacturing through decreasing the use of chemicals and energy, as well as reducing waste

title: CRISPR-Based Functional Characterization of Immune Genes Associated Pathogen Resistance in Aquaculture Species
abstract: Streptococcosis caused by Streptococcus agalactiae constitutes a serious challenge to Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) aquaculture with increased mortality and heavy economic burden. Elucidation of the underlying molecular mechanism in the host immune system is important for designing effective disease intervention strategies. In this experiment, the functions of three immune-related genes tlr2, myd88, and il1b on Nile tilapia defense response to S. agalactiae were analyzed using CRISPR-Cas9 technology. The in-silico screening of candidate guide RNA revealed a promising on-target efficiency (79.2-88.0%) and off-target specificity (88.5-95.0%) with il1b being the most favorable. The genome editing verified that all the selected target sites were successfully modified in 83.3% of fish per gene group. After infection, the expression of all three genes was significantly increased in the unedited fish while gene-edited groups exhibited transcriptional inhibition of their target genes. The gene-modified fish displayed lower immune downstream signaling, lower inflammatory markers, higher bacterial burden (6.50–7.00 log10 CFU/g), and lower survival rate (50.0-66.7%) than that of the co

title: A First-in-Class Chemical-Induced Proximity System Achieves Dose-Dependent Control of Tumor Protein P53 Gene Activation in Preclinical Models of Gastric Cancer.
abstract: The tumor protein P53 (TP53) gene has long been studied in cancer research with genomic and epigenetic aberrations playing a driving role in cancer pathology, yet even after decades of work, only a few methods have been developed to specifically target TP53 therapeutically. Some cancers are driven by loss-of-function TP53 mutations, while others have wild-type TP53 in a transcriptionally repressed state; the latter is exploitable by advances in epigenome editing. In our previous work, we demonstrated that deactivated CRISPR/Cas9 systems (dCas9), combined with an FK-506-binding protein (FKBP) recruitment protein tag and chemical epigenetic modifier (CEM) small molecules, can elicit gene-specific changes in expression in a dose-dependent manner. Here, we describe the development, application, and characterization of the dCas9-FKBP-CEM technology to increase TP53 expression. We demonstrate that catalyzing increased TP53 expression via dCas9-FKBP-CEM87 induced apoptosis, cell cycle arrest, and tumor growth inhibition in a dose-dependent manner in preclinical models of gastric cancer.

title: Protocol for eVLP-mediated CRISPR-Cas9 and prime editing in pancreatic cancer cell lines
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cell lines resist transfection, limiting gene-editing experiments. Here, we present a protocol for delivering CRISPR-Cas9 or prime editors into PDAC cell lines using retrovirus-derived engineered virus-like particles (eVLPs). We describe steps for generating eVLPs, packaging CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoproteins or prime editors with engineered prime-editing guide RNAs (epegRNAs), and transducing human PDAC cells. We use the HEK3 locus and NQO1 (NAD(P)H quinone dehydrogenase 1) exon 6 as example edits and controls, respectively. This protocol adapts readily to other genomic sites.

title: High-Throughput Screening of a Lipid Nanoparticle (LNP) Library Identifies Lead Formulations for CRISPR-Cas9 Ribonucleoprotein Delivery and Gene Editing
abstract: Delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) using synthetic materials can bypass the host translational machinery and limit the duration of genomic exposure, minimizing the risk of off-target mutations. Despite their advantages, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platforms for CRISPR-Cas9 RNP delivery that achieve highly efficient editing at low doses remain limited. In the present study, we developed a library of ionizable lipids (ILs) and corresponding LNPs to enhance the delivery and editing efficiencies of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP complexes. Following comprehensive in vitro screening and formulation optimization, an optimal LNP candidate containing the C12A9 IL (denoted as LNPC12A9) was identified that achieved ∼90% EGFP disruption in HEK293T-EGFP cells at an RNP concentration of 30 nM and ∼60% at 15 nM. The editing performance was consistently observed at an RNP concentration of 15 nM when editing the Gcgr and HPRT1 genes across multiple hepatic cell lines. Moreover, coencapsulation of RNP and a single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (ssODN) template for homology-directed repair (HDR) within LNPC12A9 induced an HDR rate of 37.8%. Programmable Enzymes for Large-Cargo Genome Engineering: From Targeted DNA Integration to Therapeutic Genome Writing
abstract: Genome engineering is undergoing a conceptual transition from the correction of individual sequence variants toward the programmable installation of larger functional genetic elements. CRISPR-associated nucleases established RNA-guided genome targeting as a broadly accessible technology, while base and prime editing subsequently demonstrated that precise sequence modification can be achieved without relying exclusively on DNA double-strand breaks. Nevertheless, efficient and controlled insertion of kilobase-scale DNA remains a substantially more difficult problem. Large-cargo integration is particularly attractive for genetically heterogeneous disorders because insertion of a complete coding sequence, a multi-exon therapeutic cassette, or another functional genetic module could restore gene activity across multiple pathogenic variants rather than requiring a separate editor for each mutation. Nature provides several mechanistically distinct solutions to large-scale DNA movement, including DNA transposases, site-specific recombinases, non-long terminal repeat retrotransposons, RNA-guided bridge recombinases, and CRISPR-associated transposases. title: The PD-1/PD-L1 axis in cancer: from immune evasion mechanisms to next-generation therapeutics
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade directed against the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) receptor and its ligand PD-L1 has markedly transformed cancer therapy, producing sustained clinical benefit and prolonged survival in selected patient populations across multiple tumor types. However, clinical responses remain highly heterogeneous, largely limited by low overall response rates, the development of both intrinsic and acquired resistance, and immune-related toxicities that restrict the durability of single-agent treatment. In this article, we systematically examine the PD-1/PD-L1 axis from a mechanistic perspective, spanning its roles in tumor initiation, disease progression, metastatic spread, and immune escape. We detail how PD-1/PD-L1 axis drives T cell exhaustion, impairs antigen presentation, reshapes the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and promotes epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), thereby enabling immune escape throughout tumor evolution. We further catalog recent innovations in PD-1/PD-L1-targeted therapeutics, spanning monoclonal antibodies, bispecific molecules, Fc-optimized biologics, and novel synthetic modalities—including RNA interference, CRISPR-based

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Cell-Based Therapies in Retinal Disease
abstract: Retinal degenerative diseases, including age-related macular degeneration (AMD), retinitis pigmentosa (RP), and Stargardt disease, represent leading causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide, collectively affecting hundreds of millions of people. Cell-based therapies, particularly those leveraging induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) transplantation, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, have emerged as promising treatment modalities that may preserve, replace, or partially restore retinal function. However, these approaches face significant challenges in patient stratification, manufacturing consistency, surgical precision, and long-term outcome monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and computer vision, is increasingly being integrated across the cell therapy pipeline to address these limitations. This review comprehensively explores the role of AI in enhancing cell-based retinal therapies, spanning disease diagnosis and patient selection, stem cell quality control and differentiation optimization, CRISPR off-target detection, retinal organoid characterization, scalable manufacturing, and po

title: Functional dissection of ultraconserved non-coding regions present near the Hoxd complex in vertebrates
abstract: Ultraconserved non-coding elements (UCEs) exhibit near-perfect sequence conservation across vertebrate genomes, implying severe evolutionary constraint and essential biological functions. Near the vertebrate Hoxd complex, a master regulator of axial patterning and limb morphogenesis, three Conserved Regions (CR1, CR2, and CR3), each longer than 200 bp, show exceptional sequence conservation and drive robust regulatory activity in transient reporter assays. To investigate their endogenous in vivo functions, we used CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing to generate a series of deletions of varying sizes spanning CR2 and CR3, individually and in combination, within hoxd complex in zebrafish. Screening thousands of founder embryos revealed a clear size and conservation-dependent relationship between deletion extent and viability: complete deletion of core CR2, CR3, or the combined CR2/3 loci could not be transmitted through the germline, whereas the smaller and least-conserved deletion, a 626-bp subregion of CR2, was the only allele to yield a stable, homozygous-viable line. title: CRISPR/Cas9 induced disruption of oca2 and tyr genes associated with pigmentation in Danio rerio
abstract: Targeted disruption of genes has been successfully carried out in several model and non-model fish species. In ornamental fish industries, Danio rerio (D. rerio) represents the most significant fish species and is available in several color varieties. Recently, CRISPR/Cas9 has been used to disrupt pigmented genes in several fish species, including D. rerio . However, there have been few reports on the use of CRISPR/Cas9 for the disruption of pigmented genes tyrosinase (tyr) and oculocutaneous albinism II ( oca2 ) in D. rerio to date. In this study, guide RNA (gRNA) constructs specific to the tyr (T1) and oca2 (T2) genes were designed and synthesized, while Cas9 mRNA was synthesized through in vitro transcription. Subsequently, both the Cas9 mRNA and the gRNA constructs were validated using gel electrophoresis and sequencing. The validated Cas9 mRNA and gRNA mixture was then co-microinjected into D. rerio embryos at the 1–2 cell stage, which were obtained through natural spawning and later reared under controlled conditions. The results of gel electrophoresis and sequencing confirmed the successful synthesis and validation of the T1 and T2 targeting Cas9 mRNA and gRNA constructs. Me

title: Development of an Efficient In Vitro Propagation Protocol for the Elite Bidah Pomegranate (Punica granatum L.) Landrace in Saudi Arabia
abstract: The Bidah pomegranate (Punica granatum L.) is an elite landrace native to Wadi Bidah in the Al-Baha region of Saudi Arabia. This cultivar is distinguished by its unique taste, high yield, genetic component, and phytochemical profile. In addition, its resilience to harsh environmental conditions aligns closely with national priorities in sustainable agriculture and food security. This study articulated the successful micropropagation of the Bidah pomegranate cultivar using both direct and indirect in vitro approaches. Phenolic exudation was effectively mitigated through sequential subculturing onto a plant growth regulator (PGR)-free medium. Shoot proliferation was highest for Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium supplemented with 3 mg/L benzyladenine (BA), resulting in a 95% shoot induction rate, which was significantly higher than those obtained with the other investigated media. Callus induction and bioreactor-based mass production were maximized on Woody Plant medium (WPM) containing 0.5 mg/L 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D), yielding significantly higher biomass than MS medium. title: VASP cooperates with zyxin to organize mechanically competent adhesions
abstract: Abstract Focal adhesions (FAs) are dynamic macromolecular assemblies that anchor the actin cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix via integrin receptors, thereby regulating cell morphology and migration. Here, we show that the vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP) cooperates with the mechanosensitive scaffold protein zyxin to maintain FA during maturation under actomyosin-generated tension. Using sequential CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing and cryo-electron tomography, we resolved the in situ nanoarchitecture of the FA-stress fiber interface. We establish that tropomyosin decorates the dorsal aspect of adhesion-associated stress fibers independently of VASP and zyxin. VASP and zyxin are required for the assembly of dense, aligned actin bundles with uniform polarity, oriented with their barbed ends toward the cell edge. Live-cell imaging and quantitative analyses of cells confined on micropatterns reveal that VASP and zyxin cooperate to preserve the mechanical coupling between FAs and the actin cytoskeleton under contractile load. abstract: Infant neuroblastoma (NB), defined by diagnosis during the first year of life, represents a clinically heterogeneous disease spectrum ranging from localized tumours with favourable outcomes and a capacity for spontaneous regression, to high-risk metastatic disease requiring intensive multimodal therapy. In infants, treatment intensity is determined by disease stage, tumor biology, MYCN status, risk classification, symptoms, response to therapy, and metastatic involvement, particularly relevant to high-risk disease, consequently the potential toxicity of intensive treatment is specific to high-risk disease, as compared to favorable risk tumors which can be managed with surgery, reduced frequency techniques, or observations. Important determinations of neuroblastoma biology and prognosis are genetic alterations involving MYCN and ALK, but the predominately investigated field with therapeutic feasibility of targeting these changes with CRISPR/Cas9 is in preclinical neuroblastoma models rather than in infants. title: Base Editing as a Therapeutic Strategy for Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease caused by Pathogenic UMOD Variants
abstract: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease caused by pathogenic UMOD variants (ADTKD-UMOD) is an untreatable monogenic kidney disease in which misfolded uromodulin is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and exerts a toxic gain-of-function effect. Here we systematically evaluate the full spectrum of base editing strategies targeting the UMOD locus. Base editors corrected a representative missense patient variant, p.Cys170Tyr, with A-to-G conversion efficiencies of up to 83.4%, restoring uromodulin trafficking to the plasmamembrane in cell lines and in human 3D kidney tubuloids. Mutation-agnostic inactivation wasachieved by four routes: premature stop codon introduction, splice-site disruption, allele-specific stop codon introduction and promoter attenuation. Maximum on-target efficienciesranged from 44.1% to 71.9%, providing a strategy set applicable across the UMOD allelicspectrum. Endogenous UMOD expression is rarely recapitulated in human cell models,leaving strategies that act on the endogenous gene difficult to assess in patient cells. title: CRISPR - CAS MEDIATED GENOME EDITING FOR HUMAN DISEASE THERAPY: EMERGING APPLICATIONS, ADVANCEMENTS AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
abstract: CRISPR - Cas - mediated genome editing has emerged as a transformative technology with considerable potential for the treatment of human diseases. The ability of CRISPR-Cas systems to recognize specific nucleic acid recognize specific nucleic acid sequences and modify targeted genetic regions has expanded the possibilities of precision medicine and gene therapy. This review provides an overview of the recent advancements in CRISPR - Cas - mediated genome editing and its emerging therapeutic applications in human diseases. Particular attention is given to conventional Cas 9 - based editing, and other programmable editing strategies that can enable more precise genetic modifications. The therapeutic potential of CRISPR - Cas technology is being investigated across a broad range of conditions, including inherited genetic disorders, hematological diseases, cancer, infectious diseases, metabolic disorders, and other complex diseases. The review also discusses important development in ex vivo and in vivo genome - editing approaches and the role of delivery systems in including therapeutic efficiency and tissues and specificity.
