title: Dynamic phosphorylation of DGCR8 regulates embryonic stem cell differentiation and microprocessor function
abstract: The Microprocessor complex, minimally composed of DROSHA and DGCR8, is ubiquitously required for microRNA biogenesis. It also regulates the balance between pluripotency and differentiation through mRNA alternative splicing and mRNA cleavage. However, how these various activities are regulated remains incompletely understood. Both DROSHA and DGCR8 are phosphoproteins, and phosphorylation has been reported to influence their molecular functions. In this study, we identified residues in DGCR8 by mass spectrometry that were differentially phosphorylated in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) before and after differentiation into neuronal cells. This included S95 that exhibited greater phosphorylation in undifferentiated cells, and S238 that exhibited greater phosphorylation in differentiated cells. By means of CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing of the endogenous Dgcr8 gene, we generated a homozygous S95A mESC clone and a heterozygous S238A/- mESC clone. Both mutants retained an mESC phenotype but exhibited altered Microprocessor-dependent functions and differentiation outcomes. When directed toward the neuronal lineage, the S238A/- mutant displayed elevated mRNA expression of neuronal

title: Anthropic's discovery will, at best, be just another gene-editing tool
CRISPR/Cas based genome editing for liver diseases: Promise and challenge
abstract: Liver disorders pose a severe threat to public health and impose a substantial burden on global healthcare systems. In recent years, the Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats/CRISPR-associated proteins (CRISPR/Cas) based genome editing technology has emerged as a promising approach for managing various liver pathologies. This review systematically summarizes the applications of these technologies in the treatment of liver diseases. We analyze the current development status of CRISPR/Cas based gene-editing tools and the available delivery systems, further summarize the latest research advances in the management of hereditary liver diseases, infectious liver diseases, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and finally discuss the challenges of CRISPR/Cas based editing for liver diseases management as well as the outlook derived from the above analysis. By integrating insights into both opportunities and obstacles, this review aims to provide a comprehensive framework to guide future research, subsequent clinical translation, and the rational application of CRISPR genome editing in liver disease management.

title: Advances in molecular and gene-based therapies for phenylketonuria: Mechanisms, therapeutic strategies, and clinical translation
abstract: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a prototypical inherited metabolic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) gene, resulting in toxic accumulation of phenylalanine and progressive neurological impairment. Although lifelong dietary restriction remains the standard of care, suboptimal adherence, nutritional imbalance, and incomplete neuroprotection limit its long-term effectiveness. Recent advances in gene therapy and genome-editing technologies have substantially advanced therapeutic strategies for PKU by enabling restoration of hepatic PAH activity at the molecular level. This review synthesizes the current understanding of PKU pathogenesis and critically evaluates emerging gene-based therapeutic approaches, including CRISPR/Cas9-mediated editing, base editing, prime editing, viral and non-viral gene replacement, and mRNA-based therapies. We further discuss translational challenges related to delivery, safety, durability, and patient stratification, and outline future directions toward personalized and potentially curative interventions.

title: Genetic improvement of rice for bacterial leaf blight resistance: Advances in resistance genes, breeding strategies and genomic approaches
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is a major staple crop that contributes substantially to global food and nutritional security. However, rice production is severely constrained by bacterial leaf blight (BLB), a destructive disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo). The disease can cause substantial yield losses, particularly under warm and humid conditions favorable for pathogen development and spread. Genetic improvement of rice for durable disease resistance is considered one of the most effective, economical, and environmentally sustainable approaches for managing BLB. Numerous resistance genes, commonly designated as Xa genes, have been identified from cultivated rice and wild relatives. Conventional breeding, marker-assisted selection, molecular breeding, gene pyramiding, quantitative trait locus mapping, genome-wide association studies, genomic selection, and genome-editing technologies have accelerated the development of BLB-resistant rice cultivars. The deployment of multiple resistance genes in a single genetic background has received particular attention because it can broaden the resistance spectrum and potentially delay the emergence of pathogen populations capable of

title: Advancing insights for possible future guidance on the environmental risk assessment and post‐market environmental monitoring of gene drive modified insects
abstract: Abstract Research and development on engineered gene drives (EGDs) has expanded rapidly over the past decade, driven in part by the advent of CRISPR‐Cas9 genome editing technologies. Much of this work has focused on insects, including plant pests, agricultural disease vectors, and species that transmit pathogens affecting humans, animals, and plants. As technological advances accelerate, so does the recognition of the need for a careful and forward‐looking evaluation of their potential impacts. Gene drive modified organisms, including insects, present characteristics that differ substantially from previously assessed genetically modified organisms (GMOs), prompting growing calls for thoughtful and robust environmental risk assessment (ERA) frameworks tailored to these novel technologies. In earlier work, the GMO Panel of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) identified several information gaps that would need to be addressed to provide an adequate foundation for possible future risk assessment guidance. This report brings together and synthesises key elements to help close those gaps, including: an overview of the molecular mechanisms currently being explored for gene drive mod

title: Hypocotyl acupuncture: an efficient and practical protocol for transformation and genome editing in Salvia miltiorrhiza
abstract: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge is a valuable medicinal plant, yet its genetic manipulation has been limited by the lack of efficient and practical transformation methods. Here, we report a simplified, tissue culture-independent strategy enabling Agrobacterium-mediated gene delivery under non-sterile conditions, termed hypocotyl acupuncture. The method employs needle-assisted inoculation of intact seedlings at the hypocotyl, completely bypassing callus induction, regeneration, and repeated subculture. Following inoculation, EGFP-positive hairy roots are selectively cultivated for approximately 4 months and then induced to regenerate shoots within one additional month, yielding transgenic plantlets in approximately 5 months. Systematic optimization achieved a transformation efficiency of approximately 55% (defined as the percentage of explants producing EGFP-positive regenerants). ACCC10060 was selected as the optimal strain based on efficiency and root morphology. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing generated mutation frequencies of 53.8%-88.9% with no off-target effects. Targeted mutagenesis of SmCPS1, a gene encoding a key rate-limiting enzyme in tanshinone biosynthesis, resulted in al

title: Loss of Nod25 function does not affect nitrogen-fixing symbiosis in Medicago truncatula
abstract: The formation of nitrogen-fixing symbiotic nodules is a complex process that involves extensive transcriptional reprogramming of legume roots to enable intracellular accommodation of host compatible rhizobia. This process requires coordinated regulation of hundreds to thousands of genes, including the induction of highly expressed genes, traditionally referred to as nodulin genes. While the functions of many nodulins have been elucidated, a substantial number remained poorly characterized, or their functions are still unclear. One such gene, NOD25, was originally identified based on differential hybridization between roots and nodules and is expressed at exceptionally high levels in Medicago nodules. MtNOD25-like proteins in IRLC legumes exhibit a repetitive modular structure flanked by conserved N- and C-terminal regions, with clade-specific repeat organization. To understand the role of NOD25 in symbiotic nitrogen fixation, we generated loss-of-function mutants in Medicago truncatula using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing. Four independent Mtnod25 mutant lines displayed normal growth under symbiotic conditions and showed no detectable defects in nodule colonization, symbiosome

title: Human Neural Cells Engineered In Vitro: Emerging Pathways for Neuroimmunology and Repair
abstract: Recent advancements in constructing human neural cells in vitro have unveiled significant therapeutic potential for treating neurological injuries and neurodegenerative diseases, such as traumatic brain injury, stroke, Parkinson’s disease, and Alzheimer’s disease. The pivotal role of stem cell technologies, particularly induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and neural stem cells (NSCs), is emphasized not only in modeling these disorders but also in facilitating cellular replacement therapies. The integration of gene editing techniques, such as CRISPR-Cas9, along with innovations in tissue engineering, substantially enhances cell survival and functional integration post-transplantation. Concurrently, emerging technologies like optogenetics and chemogenetics offer precise control over cell behaviors, further promoting effective neural circuit reconstruction. Although preclinical studies have demonstrated promising results, challenges including immune rejection, cellular heterogeneity, and long-term viability remain significant barriers to clinical translation. A comprehensive bibliometric analysis reveals a marked increase in research interest in this field, underscoring the urgent

title: Advances in precision medicine for the anterior segment: Therapeutic applications using CRISPR-Cas9
Improvement of micronutrient use efficiency and nutritional quality in crops by genome editing approaches
abstract: Micronutrients are essential for plant growth, metabolism, productivity, and nutritional quality. However, their availability and utilization are influenced by soil properties and complex regulatory mechanisms. Conventional breeding and transgenic approaches have contributed to improving micronutrient acquisition and accumulation; however, genome-editing technologies, particularly CRISPR/Cas systems, provide precise tools for modifying genes involved in nutrient uptake, transport, signalling, homeostasis and storage. Recent studies have demonstrated the potential of genome editing to improve iron (Fe), zinc (Zn), and boron (B) utilization and to reduce the accumulation of toxic cadmium (Cd) in crops. Editing genes such as OsIRO3, OsVIT2, OsZIP9, BnaA9.WRKY47, and OsNramp5 has provided valuable insights into micronutrient regulation and crop improvement. Genome editing has also been used to modify phytic acid and starch composition, thereby improving nutritional quality. Overall, genome editing offers a promising approach for developing nutrient-efficient, nutritionally improved, and safer crops.

title: Dynamic Mitochondrial Protein Succinylation Induced by Nutritional Intervention with Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids Elicits Growth Inhibition and Lethality in Prostate Cancer Cells
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) continues to present a significant therapeutic challenge due to its metabolic plasticity and resistance to conventional treatments. Although omega-3 fatty acids, especially high-purity eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), have demonstrated anticancer properties, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain inadequately understood. In this study, we provide evidence that EPA induces potent growth inhibition in PCa cells by modulating a mitochondrial succinylation network, thereby revealing three interconnected nodes of metabolic vulnerability. Through succinylomic profiling and functional validation, we identified SDHA, GOT2, and DAP3 as critical EPA-induced succinylation targets. Mechanistically, SDHA succinylation induces succinate accumulation and promotes widespread succinylation across mitochondrial proteins, thereby disrupting the homeostasis of mitochondria. This mitochondrial dysfunction converges on two lethal pathways in PCa cells: first, GOT2 hyper-succinylation inhibits aspartate biosynthesis, depleting dNTP pools and thereby stalling DNA replication; second, the function change in DAP3 may fail to save cell from ferroptosis. Here, by investigating the succin

title: Engineering A Mimetic Environment For Articular Cartilage Production
abstract: Human articular cartilage (AC), an anisotropic tissue lining the subchondral bone, functions to regularly resist deformational changes applied by daily activities such as walking, running, and more. Upon joint loading, a myriad of mechanical stresses and strains arise. Hydrostatic pressure is one of many mechanical factors that emerge from compression of the hydrated tissue that contains negatively charged proteoglycan that entraps water into the tissue matrix. Fluid shear stress is another mechanical loading type that is well represented from viscous synovial shears at AC surface as well as by interstitial fluid shears distributed throughout the tissue thickness. Modulation of these mechanical stimuli leads to a strengthened extracellular matrix (ECM) enriched with key proteins such as type II collagen and aggrecan that are resistive to mechanical straining. Innovative treatment options for osteoarthritis, characterized by articular cartilage (AC) degradation, are emerging through cartilage tissue engineering strategies. An essential feature in this field involves mimicking the cell microenvironment which provides cues for cell growth, fate, and role. This dissertation is focused

title: Targeting USP14 sensitizes glioma to radiotherapy through exacerbated reactive oxygen species accumulation.
abstract: Radiotherapy is one of the most effective treatments for glioma, but therapeutic efficacy is strongly limited due to intrinsic radioresistance, which is closely linked to reactive oxygen species. This research was designed to elucidate the role and underlying mechanisms of the deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific protease 14 (USP14) in reactive oxygen species Accumulation and radioresistance of glioma. Bioinformatics analysis demonstrated that upregulation of USP14 was associated with tumor progression, high levels of USP14 in glioma patients were correlated with a significantly poorer prognosis. Cytological experimental results demonstrated that radiotherapy could induce increased USP14 expression. Inhibition of USP14 disrupted intracellular protein homeostasis, leading to upregulation of endoplasmic reticulum stress-related proteins thereby exacerbating endoplasmic reticulum stress. This stress response further induced substantial reactive oxygen species generation and DNA damage accumulation, ultimately synergistically enhancing the tumoricidal effect of radiotherapy. In vivo, the combined application of b-AP15 (a USP14 inhibitor) and radiotherapy elicited potent antitumor effects,

title: Multivalent Antigen Display on Nanoparticles Diversifies B Cell Responses
abstract: Nanoparticles for multivalent display and delivery of vaccine antigens have emerged as a promising avenue for enhancing B cell responses to protein subunit vaccines. Here, we evaluated B cell responses in rhesus macaques immunized with prefusion stabilized Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) F glycoprotein trimer compared to nanoparticles displaying 10 or 20 copies of the same antigen. We show that multivalent display skews antibody specificities and drives epitope-focusing of responding B cells. Antibody cloning and repertoire sequencing revealed that focusing was driven by expansion of clonally distinct B cells through recruitment of diverse precursors. We identified two antibody lineages that developed either ultrapotent neutralization or pneumovirus cross-neutralization from precursor B cells with low initial affinity for the RSV-F immunogen. This suggests that increased avidity by multivalent display facilitates the activation and recruitment of these cells. Diversification of the B cell response by multivalent nanoparticle immunogens has broad implications for vaccine design.

title: Sequence-based artificial intelligence-guided inhibitory peptides to counteract AAV neutralizing antibodies in gene therapy.
abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors have demonstrated strong clinical efficacy across multiple monogenic disorders, yet neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) remain major barriers to vector redosing and durable transduction. To address this limitation, we developed a sequence-based artificial intelligence framework integrating Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Evolutionary Scale Modeling with Low-Rank Adaptation (ESM-LoRA) to identify human-tolerant, virus-specific motifs across human and viral proteins using sliding-window analyses and multi-layer fine-tuning. Using capsid-derived segments from AAV2 and AAV843, we prioritized surface-accessible, virus-polarized peptides as candidate decoys and evaluated their ability to block AAV-targeted antibodies. The models achieved high accuracy in distinguishing human versus viral fragments, and selected peptides bound AAV-specific antibodies with nanomolar affinity, competitively restored capsid binding, and recovered >60% of baseline transduction in the presence of NAbs. In mouse models with pre-existing or redosing-induced antibodies, coadministration of decoy peptides and an IgG-degrading enzyme reduced high-ti

title: Study on nutritional status and incidence of sarcopenia in elderly patients with chronic heart failure.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Elderly patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) are at high risk of malnutri-tion and sarcopenia. Therefore, nutritional screening, assessment, diagnosis, and management are particularly crucial for elderly CHF patients. Our study aims to investigate the nutritional status and the incidence charac-teristics and influencing factors of sarcopenia in elderly CHF patients. METHODS AND STUDY DESIGN: A total of 122 elderly CHF patients admitted to The First Hospital of Hebei Medical University from March 2023 to January 2024 were enrolled. Within 24 hours after admission, demographic data, body composition analysis, nutritional status assessments, and laboratory parameter testing were conducted for all participants. Patients were divided into sarcopenia and non-sarcopenia groups. RESULTS: A total of 122 patients were included, among whom 37 (30.33 %) were diagnosed with sarcopenia. The prevalence of malnutrition was significantly higher in sarcopenia group (p < 0.05). Patients with sarcopenia exhibited lower levels of albumin and hemoglobin, along with elevated Interleukin-6 (IL-6), Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII), Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte-Ratio (NLR

title: Multiscale mathematical models of drug and immune cell trafficking to support innovative cancer treatments
abstract: Recent advances in oncology have introduced increasingly sophisticated therapeutic strategies, including mRNA-encoded therapeutics, engineered immune cells, and advanced experimental platforms such as Organ-on-Chip systems. Although these technologies differ substantially in their biological mechanisms, they share a common challenge: therapeutic efficacy depends not only on the intrinsic activity of the therapeutic agent, but also on its ability to traffic across multiple biological scales, from systemic circulation to local interactions within the tumor microenvironment. Mathematical modeling provides a natural framework for integrating these interconnected processes and linking heterogeneous experimental observations to quantitative mechanistic predictions. This thesis develops a collection of multiscale mathematical models to investigate drug and immune-cell trafficking in innovative cancer therapies. The first contribution focuses on mRNA-encoded therapeutics and introduces physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models that describe the biodistribution of lipid nanoparticles, intracellular mRNA processing, protein translation, and systemic pharmacokinetics of the encoded

title: De novo design of protein binders targeting the human sweet taste receptor as potential sweet proteins
abstract: Excessive consumption of dietary sugars is a major contributor to metabolic disorders, driving global interest in finding alternative sweeteners with reduced caloric impact. Natural sweet proteins, such as brazzein, offer exceptional sweetness intensity with little caloric contribution. However, their widespread use is limited by restricted natural diversity, low stability, and high production costs. Recent advances in structural biology and de novo protein design provide new opportunities to overcome these limitations through rational engineering. In this study, we report an integrated computational pipeline for the de novo design of protein binders targeting the human sweet taste receptor subunit TAS1R2, a key component of the heterodimeric class C G protein-coupled receptor mediating sweetness perception. The workflow combines diffusion-based backbone generation (RFdiffusion), neural network-guided sequence design (ProteinMPNN), structure-based filtering using Boltz-1, and binding energy evaluation via MM/GBSA calculations. Using the recently resolved cryo-EM structure of the TAS1R2 receptor, protein binders were designed to target both the Venus Flytrap Domain and the cysteine-

title: PERTUMBUHAN DAN HASIL KORO PEDANG (Canavalia ensiformis L.) PADA PEMBERIAN DOSIS PUPUK KANDANG YANG BERBEDA
abstract: Jack bean (Canavalia ensiformis L.) is a legume that can serve as a source of vegetable protein, potentially replacing soybeans. Efforts to enhance its growth and yield include applying goat manure. This study aimed to determine the effect of varying doses of goat manure on jack bean growth and yield. The study used a randomized complete block design. The treatments consisted of goat manure doses of 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25 t ha⁻¹. Observed variables included growth components, yield components, and overall yield. The results indicated that different doses of goat manure did not significantly affect most growth variables, except for the number of leaves at 42 and 56 days after planting and plant dry weight at all observation times. However, goat manure dose significantly influenced the number of seeds per pod, the weight of 100 seeds, and the seed weight per plant and per plot. The optimal dose to increase jack bean yield was 10 t ha⁻¹.

title: Development and Evaluation of Ogi Produced from Selected Cereals, Soybean and Plantain Blends
abstract: Introduction: Ogi is a traditional fermented cereal-based food that serves as a staple breakfast meal in many parts of West Africa, including Nigeria. Traditional ogi is often low in protein, a crucial nutrient for growth, particularly in children. Study Design: A completely randomised design was used; six cereal-soybean-plantain blends were evaluated in triplicate for proximate, mineral, physical, functional, phytochemical and sensory properties. Place of Study: Department of Food Science, Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), Ogbomoso, Nigeria. Aim: The study aimed to produce fortified ogi by incorporating soybean and plantain into a mixture of cereals (maize, millet, sorghum, rice) to enhance its nutritional value. Method: The production of ogi involved soaking the cereals for 72 h, allowing fermentation for 72 h, wet milling, drying, and milling into flour. Soybean was soaked for 12 h and dried, while plantain was blanched for 5 minutes, dried, and milled into flour. The cereal flours and soybean flour were blended in a ratio of 4:1, and the composite ogi was blended with plantain flour in varying ratios of 100:0, 90:10, 80:20, 70:30, 60:40, and 50:50 to produce s

title: Beyond Conventional RP-HPLC: Quality-by-Design, Green Analytical Chemistry, and Regulatory Perspectives for Multicomponent Analysis of Antihypertensive Drug Combinations.
abstract: Multicomponent analysis of antihypertensive drugs sits at the intersection of pharmaceutical quality control, bioanalysis, pharmacokinetics, and clinical therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM). Conventional reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) remains useful because of its broad availability and flexible detection options; however, a method optimized for a synthetic mixture or tablet extract cannot automatically be transferred to plasma or serum, where endogenous components, concomitant medicines, protein binding, and low analyte concentrations can compromise selectivity and quantitative reliability. At the same time, method development is increasingly expected to demonstrate scientific understanding, robustness, lifecycle control, and reduced environmental burden. This review critically integrates analytical quality by design (AQbD), green analytical chemistry (GAC), chromatographic selectivity, sample preparation, detection, and regulatory expectations into a purpose-led framework for multicomponent antihypertensive analysis. Published bioanalytical examples demonstrate that LC-MS/MS can support targeted measurement of nebivolol in human plasma and simultane

title: Promoter Mapping Analysis Using a GFP Reporter Plasmid Suggests that the lac Promoter May Drive brka Expression on Plasmid pDO6935 in Escherichia coli
abstract: Autotransporters (AT) are a class of bacterial proteins that play a crucial role in bacterial virulence and pathogenesis. Understanding these proteins is essential to advance research in infectious disease and identify possible targets for therapeutic interventions. Bordetella pertussis autotransporter, BrkA belongs to the AT-1 subfamily of autotransporter proteins in Gram negative bacteria. Since its discovery, plasmids have been created to study brkA expression in various systems, pDO6935 being one of them. The mechanism by which brkA is expressed in pDO6935 is yet to be fully elucidated. We used a promoter trapping method to map the promoter regions that drive brkA expression. An analysis of pDO6935 gene sequence revealed the presence of a lac operon upstream of brkA. The lac operon is known to exhibit basal expression in the absence of lactose or the presence of a repressor. We studied whether the leaky expression caused by the lac operon may result in the expression of brkA in an Escherichia coli system. In our study, we utilized pSPPH21, a promoterless reporter plasmid that was designed to contain green fluorescent protein (GFP). Using this vector, we inserted regions of puta

title: Solid-State Lithium Sulfur Batteries: Protein Inspired Design
abstract: Abstract The development of high-specific-energy all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries requires simultaneous optimization of active materials, conductive networks, electrode interfaces, and lithium inventory. This study proposes a protein-inspired materials-design framework for an all-solid-state battery targeting a whole-cell specific energy of 1222 Wh kg⁻¹. The proposed architecture combines an rGO-supported elemental-sulfur cathode, a prelithiated silicon-rich MoS₂–Si composite anode, a carbon nanotube conductive network, and a Li₆PS₅Cl solid electrolyte. Graphene oxide-derived materials are considered for controlled surface functionalization and conductive-network optimization. In addition, a library of 15 peptide candidates is proposed to investigate potential improvements in electrode cohesion, carbon-surface interactions, and interfacial stability. The development methodology integrates computational screening, peptide production and characterization, controlled electrode fabrication, electrochemical evaluation, and iterative sequence optimization. abstract: The key reasons for disease and death global, cancer, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular, chronic inflammation, neurodegenerative and chronic kidney, liver, lung disorders are the top of chronic diseases, and treatments have faced several limitations as the reasons are based on multifactorial pathology, biological barrier, interpatient disease heterogeneity, poor accumulation of drugs in the lesion sites, general toxicity as well as the absent of drug-release mechanisms responding to changing microenvironment of the lesion site.The innovative smart drug delivery platforms of multi-stimuli-responsive nanoparticles have emerged in the field of drug delivery for combining two or more endogenous and/or exogenous stimuli to realize targeted release, spatially controlled drug release, and temporally controlled release.The endogenous stimuli, including decreased pH, redox gradient, ROS, enzyme, hypoxia, glucose, and ATP, can be combined with external stimuli, including temperature, light, magnetic field, and ultrasound, to trigger targeted delivery of nanoparticles and enhance the specificity of drug release.In the present work, the principles, classification, design principles, material s

Nonclinical Toxicology Strategy for Once-Weekly Basal Insulin Analogues: An ICH S6(R1)-Aligned IND-Enabling Case Analysis
abstract: Once-weekly basal insulin analogues represent a significant dosing-frequency innovation within an otherwise extremely well-established therapeutic class, reducing injection burden for adults with type 2 diabetes from daily to weekly administration through protein-engineering approaches that extend circulating half-life. Because insulin and its analogues are proteins rather than small molecules, this category falls under ICH S6(R1) rather than the conventional small-molecule nonclinical framework, with consequences that cascade through nearly every element of preclinical planning, including species selection, genotoxicity strategy, and safety pharmacology design. This article develops a complete, ICH S6(R1)-aligned, IND-enabling nonclinical toxicology strategy for this drug category, addressing test-article supply planning expressed in insulin units, species selection grounded in receptor conservation and pharmacologic relevance, subcutaneous route and formulation strategy matched to the clinical product, a genotoxicity strategy that substitutes impurity-focused testing for a conventional battery given the protein's expected biological inertness toward DNA, an integrated safety phar

title: Pengaruh Sistem Pemeliharaan dan Lokasi terhadap Kualitas Proksimat Telur Itik di Kecamatan Sumbang
abstract: This study aimed to determine the effect of rearing system (intensive and free-range) and village location (Karanggintung, Karangcegak, and Datar) on the proximate quality (crude protein, crude fat, moisture, and ash content) of duck eggs in Sumbang Subdistrict, Banyumas Regency. A 2×3 factorial Completely Randomized Design (CRD) was used, consisting of six treatment combinations and three replications, giving 18 experimental units. Proximate data were analyzed using Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), followed by the Least Significant Difference (LSD) test for significant effects. Results showed that rearing system, location, and their interaction had a highly significant effect (P<0.01) on duck egg moisture content. The highest moisture content was recorded in the intensive system in Datar Village (65.73%), while the lowest was in the free-range system in Karanggintung Village (58.81%). In contrast, rearing system, location, and their interaction did not significantly affect crude protein, crude fat, or ash content (P> 0.05). These findings indicate that moisture content is the proximate parameter most responsive to rearing management and location, whereas the macronutrient quality of

title: Rescuing the ompA Deletion Mutant Escherichia coli JW0940 by Reintroducing ompA in the TOPO Cloning Vector pBAD
abstract: OmpA is a transmembrane protein that has an essential function in protecting the integrity of the outer membrane of Escherichia coli, and provides a docking point for the donor pilus during conjugation. The plasmid TOPO cloning vector pBAD containing the ompA insert, whose expression is induced by arabinose, was previously designed as a tool to study the relationship between ompA expression and conjugation. The purpose of this study was to introduce the expression system into an ompA -deletion E. coli strain to improve the controlled inducibility of expression of ompA at the outer membrane. The insert orientation in the plasmid was verified through a restriction digest containing EcoRV and HincII. An ompA expression assay resulted in increased ompA expression as increasing arabinose doses were added to the culture medium, and confirmed the presence of OmpA in the outer membrane. Differential ompA expression was not linked with a difference in resistance to sodium dodecyl sulfate. The effects of varying the levels of expression of the ompA gene on the integrity of the outer membrane, and on F conjugation remain yet to be fully elucidated.

title: Multi-parameter optimization of recombinant protein secretion in Bacillus subtilis: a review
abstract: Abstract Bacillus subtilis is widely recognized as one of the most robust and versatile hosts for recombinant protein production. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the protein secretion pathway in B. subtilis , detailing its mechanistic basis and key limiting steps. We discuss the structural features of signal peptides (SPs) that govern efficient translocation and highlight recent advances in de novo promoter and signal peptide engineering. A particular focus is placed on the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) to predict and design optimal genetic elements. Drawing on findings from combinatorial and multi-parameter studies, we propose that future engineering strategies should move beyond maximizing individual parameters. Instead, achieving a dynamic balance across transcriptional, translational and secretion layers is essential to sustain high productivity while minimizing cellular secretion stress. This review offers a roadmap for systems-level engineering of B. subtilis as a next-generation protein production platform.

title: Effect of Different Nitrogen Levels and Varieties on Growth, Yield and Economics of Fodder Oat
abstract: Multi-cut fodder oat (Avena sativa L.) cultivation has gained prominence as a strategic approach to meeting the demand for high-quality forage in livestock production systems. This can be achieved by applying an optimum amount of nutrients, particularly nitrogen. Therefore, this study investigated the effects of different nitrogen levels and oat varieties on the growth, yield, quality, and economics of multi-cut fodder oat. The experiment was conducted during the rabi season of 2022-2023 at the All India Coordinated Research Project on Forage Crops, JNKVV, Jabalpur. The experiment was laid out in a split-plot design involving five varieties as main-plot treatments, viz., PLP 27, JO 05-304, JHO 20-3, OL 1949, and RO 19, and four nitrogen levels as sub-plot treatments, viz., 0, 70, 105, and 140 kg/ha. Observations on various crop growth and yield parameters were recorded at the first and second cuts. The results indicated that growth parameters and yield were higher at the second cut than at the first cut. Among the varieties, JO 05-304 was superior, recording higher LAI (4.04 and 4.25) and leaf:stem ratio (0.76 and 1.18), along with the highest green fodder, dry fodder, and crude pr

title: Heterojunctions for food freshness monitoring: interfacial engineering, sensing mechanisms, and intelligent packaging
abstract: The growing demand for real-time, non-destructive, and intelligent food quality assessment has spurred rapid advances in chemical sensors that monitor freshness deterioration during storage, transportation, and retail. Among emerging sensing platforms, heterojunction-based sensors are particularly attractive because their well-defined interfacial architectures regulate charge transport, surface adsorption, catalytic activation, and signal amplification. These features are highly desirable for detecting volatile spoilage biomarkers, including ammonia (NH 3 ), hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), trimethylamine (TMA), and other bioamines, which are continuously released during the microbial and enzymatic degradation of protein-rich foods such as meat, fish, seafood, and dairy products. This review first elucidates the formation mechanisms of key spoilage biomarkers, including NH 3 , H 2 S, TMA, and other bioamines, in high-protein foods (meat, aquatic products, and dairy products), and clarifies their basis as freshness fingerprints. We then systematically summarize major heterojunction-based sensing platforms, including metal oxide and sulfide heterostructures, noble-metal-modified heterostruc

title: Investigation of the pBR322 Exclusion Effect using Putative Rop Mutant pBR322 Plasmid pCAWK
abstract: Rop, repressor of primer, protein has been implicated in causing or contributing to plasmid pBR322 exclusion from Escherichia coli host cells. A recent study successfully created pCAWK, a putative mutated pBR322 plasmid with a non-functioning Rop protein. Whole cell PCR was performed with DH5α E. coli colonies respectively containing pUC19, pBR322, pCAWK1, and pCAWK2 (plasmids with different orientations of the 34 bp insert disrupting the rop gene) to compare plasmid copy numbers. Unique forward and reverse primers were designed through manual selection of sequences for each plasmid, complemented and optimized by analyses using primer3, REPFIND, and EMBOSS programs. Following PCR, the plasmid copy numbers of each plasmid were assessed by visual and quantitative agarose gel analysis to observe whether pCAWK in either orientation exists at a quantity that is higher, lower, or comparable to the other plasmids. Both pCAWK1 and pCAWK2 persisted poorly in host cells when compared to the parental pBR322 or pUC19, with pUC19 being most abundant. Although superficially these observations suggest that Rop may not be an important factor in the exclusion effect, the semi-quantitative technique

title: Construction of pBAD-clones using the TOPO TA Cloning System
abstract: Previous studies have shown that conjugation efficiency decreases when the outer membrane protein, OmpA, was inactivated in Escherichia coli. To study the role of modulated OmpA expression in conjugation, construction of a pBAD24- ompA clone that would allow controlled gene expression under the regulation of arabinose-inducible promoter was attempted in the past but had no success. To assess whether problems arose due to the cloning design or other intrinsic difficulties of cloning ompA, the current investigation attempted to use an alternate TOPO TA cloning system to construct pBADompA. Primers were designed to amplify ompA and restriction analysis verified that the PCR product was consistent with ompA ’s expected banding pattern. Transformation results showed successful recovery of several clones carrying pBAD constructs. Construct pKT10W4 had a higher molecular weight which suggested that it carried a large insert worth further investigation. Due to time constraints, the identity and directionality of the insert had yet to be confirmed as ompA. title: QUALITY BY DESIGN-BASED DEVELOPMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF CURCUMIN–PIPERINE NANOPARTICLES FOR ENHANCED ANTIOXIDANT AND ANTI-INFLAMMATORY ACTIVITY
abstract: The present study aimed to develop and optimize Curcumin–Piperine loaded Poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles using a Quality by Design (QbD) approach to enhance the therapeutic potential of these bioactive compounds. Optimization using a Box–Behnken Design (BBD). The optimized formulation was prepared by the solvent evaporation technique and characterized for particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), zeta potential, morphology, entrapment efficiency, in-vitro drug release, antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory activity, and stability. The optimized nanoparticles exhibited a particle size of 156.8 ± 4.2 nm, PDI of 0.214 ± 0.02, zeta potential of −28.6 ± 1.4 mV, and entrapment efficiency of 89.4 ± 1.8%. The formulation showed sustained drug release with 91.2 ± 2.1% cumulative release over 24 h. Antioxidant activity evaluated by DPPH assay demonstrated 84.3 ± 1.8% free radical scavenging at 100 µg/mL, while anti-inflammatory activity assessed by protein denaturation assay exhibited 81.6 ± 1.9% inhibition at the same concentration. Stability studies conducted for three months revealed minimal changes in physicochemical parameters, confirming formulation stability. Th

title: Antioxidant and biochemical markers as indicators of resistance to tobacco streak virus in cotton genotypes
abstract: Aim The study investigates the biochemical and antioxidant defense responses of five cotton ( Gossypium spp. L.) genotypes to Tobacco streak virus (TSV), an emerging pathogen threatening cotton cultivation in southern India. Study design To analyze the biochemical and antioxidant responses of different cotton genotypes upon TSV infection, aiming to identify potential biochemical markers and defense indicators suitable for resistance breeding and the development of integrated viral disease management strategies. Place and duration of the study This study was undertaken at the University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur. Methodology A total of 107 cotton genotypes screened under AICRP trials during Kharif 2024, Raichur (From 2 May 2024 to September 2024, Wet season) were categorized by disease response, and five representative genotypes were selected for analysis. Tobacco streak virus inoculum was prepared from infected leaves and confirmed through mechanical inoculation on cowpea seedlings. Pediatric Alexander Disease: Clinical Spectrum, GFAP Genotype–Phenotype Relationships, Molecular Pathogenesis, and Emerging Gene-Targeted Therapies
abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare, dominantly inherited astrocytopathy caused principally by heterozygous pathogenic variants in GFAP, the gene encoding glial fibrillary acidic protein. In children, the disorder spans a continuum from neonatal or early-infantile encephalopathy with severe cerebral white-matter disease, seizures, hydrocephalus and rapid developmental compromise to later childhood phenotypes with mixed cerebral, bulbar, pyramidal and autonomic involvement. The historical age-based categories of infantile, juvenile and adult disease are therefore increasingly complemented by clinically and radiologically grounded cerebral, intermediate and bulbospinal phenotypes. This critical narrative review integrates clinical natural-history data, magnetic resonance imaging patterns, GFAP genotype–phenotype evidence, mechanistic studies in human tissue, induced pluripotent stem cell models and animal models, and the translational development of GFAP-lowering therapies. Evidence published from January 2001 to 8 August 2026 was prioritised, with older foundational observations considered when necessary. title: Construction of pCAWK, a Novel pBR322-derived Plasmid with Insertional Inactivation of the rop Gene
abstract: The ColE1-type plasmid pBR322 is commonly used as vector tool in molecular biology. It has been observed that when Escherichia coli cells are co-transformed with pBR322 and pUC19 (another ColE1-type plasmid) pUC19 is retained and pBR322 is excluded. Several mechanisms have been proposed to explain this phenomenon, including the larger size of pBR322, absence of the rop gene in pUC19, and an existing point mutation in RNA II of pUC19 absent in pBR322. To examine the role of the repressor of primer (Rop) protein on the exclusion effect, previous studies have attempted to create a non-functional Rop protein by PCR-site directed mutagenesis but have been unsuccessful. The objective of this study was to create a Rop mutant by insertional inactivation of the rop gene. A 34-bp DNA insert was designed with (1) PvuII restriction digest sites flanking the ends; (2) one stop codon in each of six possible reading frames; and (3) a central EagI restriction site. This DNA was ligated into the rop gene of pBR322 so that Rop protein translation is terminated prematurely after the 50th amino acid, arginine. title: PathogenKG: Cross-Species Drug Repurposing via Heterogeneous Knowledge Graph Link Prediction
Building a Physically Interpretable Compressed Chemical Space via Grid-Based Optimization
abstract: Abstract In recent years, deep generative models have been increasingly adopted for molecular optimization and design. In many such models, molecules are encoded into latent spaces that provide compact representations of their features. However, these latent spaces remain difficult to interpret in physical terms, and it is unclear how much structural and molecular information is retained under compression. This limitation becomes especially important when molecular behavior depends on specific three-dimensional arrangements embedded in an environmental context. Here, we introduce COMPRESS (Compression Of Molecular Physical fields into Reduced Spatial Sites), an optimization framework that represents a small molecule using a fixed number of physically parametrized spatial sites. Each site is defined by three spatial coordinates and three interaction parameters, yielding a fixed-size representation that remains directly interpretable in physical terms. To preserve molecular information, COMPRESS representations are optimized to reproduce the density, electrostatic, and van der Waals fields of the corresponding all-atom molecule on discretized three-dimensional grids. title: InRegPep: a web server for modeling of parallel beta-sheet fibrillar aggregates of amyloidogenic peptides
abstract: Predicting the structures of peptide or protein aggregates that assemble into amyloid protofilaments remains one of the most challenging tasks in computational structural biology. Computational difficulties arise mainly from the large size of the modeled systems and the extensive timescales of aggregation processes. The InRegPep web server is designed for the multiscale structural modeling of peptide aggregates that preferentially adopt in-register parallel β-sheet architectures. The method employs the coarse-grained CABS model, which enables the assembly of a large number of aggregates composed of five interacting peptides. The best models are selected using clustering techniques combined with energy-based and model-symmetry criteria. Top-scoring models are subsequently refined at the all-atom level and further assessed using molecular dynamics simulations. Finally, short protofilament structures are assembled for conformationally stable aggregates. The performance of the InRegPep server was evaluated using a benchmark dataset comprising 15 experimentally determined protofilament structures. title: MAOMAO: an ontology-guided FAIR resource for harmonized peptide toxicity data
abstract: Therapeutic peptides have emerged as a rapidly expanding class of biomolecules with applications spanning antimicrobial, antiviral, anticancer, immunomodulatory, metabolic, and diagnostic settings (8). Their high target specificity, favorable safety profiles, and growing clinical success have positioned them as attractive alternatives or complements to traditional small-molecule therapeutics (36). The number of experimentally characterized bioactive peptides has therefore increased substantially during the last decade (38), supporting the development of specialized databases and computational resources for peptide discovery, functional annotation, and rational design (5,15,31,35). Despite these advances, toxicity remains a major limitation to peptide development and clinical translation, constraining candidate selection during early-stage screening and optimization (3).Peptide toxicity encompasses a broad spectrum of adverse biological effects that arise from the interaction between peptides and biological systems. Most toxicity phenotypes are routinely evaluated during peptide development including cytotoxicity, hemolysis, neurotoxicity, embryotoxicity, and ichthyotoxicity (19,27)

title: PLASMON-ENHANCED OPTICAL PROBES TOWARDS POINT-OF-CARE TESTING
abstract: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) is a common method for protein biomarker detection but requires venipuncture samples sent to central labs, causing delays of hours or days. In contrast, point-of-care (POC) devices like paper lateral flow strips (PLFSs) use finger-prick samples, deliver results within 20 minutes, enable immediate decisions during visits, allow longitudinal biomarker tracking, and improve accessibility in resource-limited settings. PLFSs are simple, low-cost, and easy to use; however, conventional PLFSs suffer from limited sensitivity and poor interference resistance, especially in blood samples. To address these issues, this dissertation develops plasmon-enhanced optical probes, studies plasmonic enhancement mechanisms, and engineers PLFS structures, resulting in improved sensitivity and reduced interference in human fluid testing. First, a sandwich-structured nanoparticle (Ag-core@silica@dye@silica-shell) has been designed as a visible-light plasmonic fluorescence probe for nasal swab fluids. title: GENETICALLY ENCODED RNA-BASED FLUORESCENT AND BIOLUMINESCENT SENSORS
abstract: Genetically encodable fluorogenic RNA (FR)-based sensors, containing primarily a light-up RNA aptamer able to specifically interact with a fluorophore, have been widely used in bioanalysis for the detection of various extracellular/intracellular targets, Unlike traditional sensors that have been developed based on fluorescent proteins (FPs), genetically encoded FR-based sensors have emerged over the past decade. Compared to protein-based sensors, the RNA-based ones are highly modular. Moreover, they are also promising for monitoring cellular levels, locations, and cell-to-cell variations of targets in living systems. In this regard, genetically encoded RNA sensors are becoming popular alternatives for both extracellular and intracellular analysis. In view of this, we have been dedicated to developing novel, versatile platforms based on FRs. These RNA molecules can be genetically encoded and synthesized on-site to serve as fluorescent markers for intracellular visualization. Our lab has significantly expanded the range of cellular applications for these FRs by assembling them into biosensors, enabling the monitoring and detection of a wide array of molecules both in vitro and in viv

title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies
abstract: Conspectus In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish enteroviral 2C as a tractable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development. Rather than relying solely on conventional phenotypic high-throughput screening, our initial studies focused on the rational optimization of reported 2C inhibitors identified from a drug-repurposing campaign. This strategy led to quinoline-based antivirals with substantially improved potency and selectivity against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), providing early medicinal chemistry insights into ligand recognition by enteroviral 2C and supporting the feasibility of chemically targeting this protein. Building on these findings, we subsequently developed pyrazolopyridine-based inhibitors, which evolved into one of the most potent classes of enteroviral 2C inhibitors reported to date. title: Development of a chimeric multi-epitope vaccine targeting surface-exposed proteins of Chlamydia psittaci through immunoinformatics and structural vaccinology
abstract: Chlamydia psittaci is an obligate intracellular zoonotic pathogen that causes psittacosis and severe respiratory illness in humans. Despite its clinical importance, no licensed vaccine is currently available, and antibiotic treatment may not provide long-term protection or prevent recurrent infection. To address this challenge, a computational strategy integrating structural vaccinology and immunoinformatics was used to design a multi-epitope vaccine targeting the major outer membrane porin and the virulence-associated pGP3-D protein of C. psittaci . Cytotoxic T-cell and helper T-cell epitopes were identified and screened to select antigenic candidates. The selected epitopes were joined using linker sequences together with β-defensin-3 and PADRE. The vaccine construct was evaluated using physicochemical analysis, three-dimensional structural modeling, interaction analysis with TLR2, a 500 ns molecular dynamics simulation, MM-GBSA binding free-energy analysis, immune simulation, and in silico cloning. title: Targeted Protein Degradation: PROTACs, Molecular Glues, and the Future of Drug Discovery
abstract: The ability to selectively eliminate pathogenic proteins rather than merely inhibit their activity has redefined contemporary drug discovery, positioning targeted protein degradation (TPD) as one of the most significant advances in chemical biology and precision therapeutics.By harnessing endogenous protein quality-control machinery, TPD offers a catalytic and event-driven pharmacological strategy capable of addressing limitations associated with conventional occupancydriven inhibitors, including poor target selectivity, transient target engagement, acquired resistance, and the inaccessibility of many disease-relevant proteins.Among the expanding repertoire of degrader technologies, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) and molecular glues have emerged as the most mature and clinically advanced platforms, each employing distinct mechanisms to recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases and direct selective protein degradation.Their rapid evolution has been driven by breakthroughs in structural biology, medicinal chemistry, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence, enabling the rational design of degraders with enhanced potency, selectivity, and pharmacokinetic performance.Beyond onc

title: INNOVATIVE NANODELIVERY SYSTEMS FOR PRECISE CANCER TREATMENTS
abstract: The effective delivery of therapeutic agents remains a major challenge in biomedical research, as biological barriers such as cellular membranes and intracellular trafficking often limit bioavailability and functional outcomes. This dissertation focuses on the design and engineering of nanocarrier delivery systems to overcome these limitations and enable efficient transport of biologics and small molecules. First, cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CMNPs) were developed to investigate alternative cellular uptake mechanisms. The system demonstrates a significant enhancement in the intracellular delivery efficiency via membrane fusion, suggesting broad potential for this delivery strategy across diverse therapeutic areas. Building on this concept, artificial cell-derived vesicles (ACDVs) were engineered as a platform for delivering functional membrane-associated proteins. This approach enables direct modulation of cell surface properties, allowing the presentation of bioactive proteins such as receptors and enzymes without genetic modification. title: Retrotransposons: A New Frontier in In Vivo Genome Engineering
abstract: Genome engineering has transformed cell therapy, but clinical implementation remains largely confined to ex vivo workflows followed by adoptive cell transfer. These approaches require costly manufacturing, often rely on viral vectors, and carry risks associated with unwanted genomic alterations. Recent advances in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable genome-editing components to be delivered directly to specific cell populations in vivo, eliminating the need for ex vivo manufacturing. Several RNA-based genome-editing approaches have entered clinical trials. Nevertheless, current in vivo approaches remain largely limited to gene disruption or small sequence modifications. Conventional integration of large payloads generally requires DNA donors, which can be immunogenic, have limited nuclear access, and pose substantial LNP formulation challenges. When expression of therapeutic proteins such as chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) is required, LNP-based approaches predominantly deliver mRNA, leading to transient expression, whereas many applications require durable expression through stable genomic integration. title: Delivery of transgenes into Gαo-rich subcortical structures of the mouse brain with potential applications for GNAO1 encephalopathy
abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors are widely used for transgene delivery into the mouse brain in preclinical studies, yet AAV methodology requires customization for each neurological disease. In this study, we aimed to identify the optimal approach for AAV-mediated transduction of brain regions with high expression of GNAO1 , which encodes the signaling protein Gαo. Mutations in GNAO1 cause the neurodevelopmental disorder GNAO1 encephalopathy. Using whole-brain confocal imaging, we identified the highest density of Gαo-positive neuronal somata in the striatum, thalamus, cerebellar Purkinje cell layer, and pyramidal layer of the hippocampal CA2 field in the adult mouse brain. We compared intracerebroventricular and intravenous administration of neurotropic AAVs expressing fluorescent reporters in wild-type mice. Intracerebroventricular injection into neonatal mice resulted in poor penetration into deep Gαo-rich brain regions. In contrast, retro-orbital administration of AAV9 in adult mice led to uniform vector distribution across Gαo-positive cortical and subcortical regions. title: Breaking the Potency Barrier: A Practical Recipe for QSAR Extrapolation
abstract: Predicting compounds that are more potent than those represented in the training data remains a difficult and practically important problem for quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling. This challenge is particularly relevant during lead optimization, where the goal is to design or identify analogs that are more potent than compounds already measured. To address this problem, we developed a new Pairwise-Difference QSAR (PD-QSAR) approach that learns changes in biological activity from differences in molecular descriptors between compound pairs. We evaluated three strategies for aggregating the resulting PD-QSAR predictions: mean aggregation, k-nearest-neighbor aggregation (k = 3), and 10% quantile aggregation, and compared their performance with Direct QSAR and Chemprop using a benchmark derived from publicly available ChEMBL 35 data. The primary benchmark included 103 human single-protein target datasets, comprising 33,707 activity records. For each target, the 10% most potent activity records were withheld for external validation. title: Deciphering the Redox-Mediated Interplay Along the Gut–Lung–Brain Axis: Macrophage and Microglia Hyperactivation in Systemic Inflammation
abstract: Emerging paradigms in systemic immunology have illuminated the intricate, bidirectional communication networks linking distant organ systems, which are conceptualized as the gut–lung–brain axis. The homeostasis of this anatomical triad is primarily disrupted by localized and systemic oxidative stress, which serves as a potent driver of chronic inflammatory cascades. This comprehensive narrative review comprehensively delineates the redox-sensitive molecular cross-talk between peripheral tissue-resident macrophages (alveolar and intestinal) and central nervous system microglia. Environmental insults or microbial dysbiosis trigger the overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which compromise epithelial and endothelial barrier integrity, thereby allowing inflammatory mediators to breach the blood–brain barrier and trigger neuroinflammation. Herein, we systematically evaluate the mechanistic evidence demonstrating how this systemic redox disequilibrium drives coordinated myeloid hyperactivation. Sequence-Activity Relationships and Integrated In Silico and In Vitro Mechanistic Study of the Antimicrobial Peptide PEP-4 against Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Abstract The rise of antimicrobial resistance among ESKAPE pathogens demands novel therapeutic strategies. Here, we evaluate a panel of five synthetic peptides through integrated in vitro and in silico analyses, highlighting PEP-4 as a promising antibacterial lead peptide. Our findings demonstrate the key role of C-terminal hydrophobic patterning in antimicrobial efficacy. PEP-4 exhibits strong antibacterial activity (MIC 15.6–62.5 μg mL–1, corresponding to ∼10.5–41.9 μM) and consistently shows bactericidal effects against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains. Molecular dynamics simulations show sustained, charge-selective interaction of PEP-4 with an anionic S. aureus-like bilayer and only intermittent association with a zwitterionic mammalian model, supporting electrostatically driven membrane recognition as the initial step of its mechanism; no bilayer destabilization was observed in either system over the simulated time scale. Additionally, molecular docking suggests potential secondary intracellular protein targets. title: Clinical–Histopathological Concordance of Surgical Triage and the Unexpected Acute Phenotype in 773 Consecutive Laparoscopic Cholecystectomies
abstract: Background and Objectives: Surgical triage and final histopathological classification do not always fully overlap. This study evaluated their concordance, the frequency of unexpected acute pathology among electively scheduled patients, and associated preoperative characteristics. Materials and Methods: This single-center, single-surgeon retrospective cohort included 773 patients whose cholecystectomy was completed laparoscopically between 1 January 2022 and 30 June 2026. Surgical triage was classified as emergency or elective, and histopathology as acute or chronic inflammatory pathology. “Unexpected acute pathology” denoted acute histopathology in electively scheduled patients, irrespective of clinical suspicion. Multivariable logistic regression was performed in 627 elective patients with complete data. Model A included previous biliary attack and preoperative radiological gallbladder wall thickening; Model B additionally included the C-reactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR). abstract: Abstract Background Athletes are often subjected to sleep disruptions due to factors including extensive training load and training hours. Insufficient sleep impairs several physiological and psychomotor functions essential for optimal recovery, performance, and injury prevention in athletes. With growing interest towards whole-food nutritional strategies, alpha-lactalbumin (ALAC), a whey protein from cow’s milk, presents promising potential for sleep improvements. ALAC contains high amounts of the amino acid tryptophan which promotes its availability to the brain and positively influences endogenous melatonin production. However, little is known about the effect of ALAC on sleep improvement in poor sleepers. Additionally, most previous interventions implemented a low-protein antecedent meal, posing potential concerns regarding its practical application. The present study aims to investigate whether ALAC supplementation improves sleep, mood, and cognition in athletes with sleep difficulties. title: Ga3+ Replacing of Fe3+ as a “Trojan Horse” Antimicrobial Strategy: Modeling the Process within Bacterial Catalase–Peroxidase KatG
abstract: Abstract Replacement of Fe3+ by Ga3+ has emerged as a promising “Trojan horse” antimicrobial strategy in response to the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Because many bacterial proteins hijack host iron to sustain essential redox processes, substitution with redox inactive Ga3+, which closely resembles Fe3+ in ionic radius but possesses only one oxidation state, can disrupt their activity. Among potential targets, bacterial catalase-peroxidase shows particular sensitivity to Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange. However, the structural determinants and thermodynamic driving forces governing this substitution remain poorly understood. Here we combine ad hoc force field development, molecular dynamics simulations, alchemical free energy calculations, and QM/MM methods to elucidate the molecular basis of Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange in the bacterial catalase-peroxidase KatG. Our simulations show that the axial coordination environment of the heme B cofactor is largely preserved upon metal substitution, while the distal ligand dynamically alternates between histidine and a coordinated water molecule. title: EVALUATION OF GROWTH PERFORMANCE OF Clarias gariepinus POST FINGERLINGS FED Leucaena leucocephala LEAF MEAL AS REPLACEMENT FOR FISHMEAL
abstract: Fish meal (FM) which is the main source of animal protein in fish feed has continued to challenge the aquaculture industry due to its rising high cost. Therefore, this study evaluated the potentials of replacement of fishmeal with Leucaena leucocephala leaf meal at varying inclusion levels on the growth performance of Clarias gariepinus post fingerlings. The experiment was carried out in a Completely Randomized Design (CRD). Five (5) experimental diets were formulated comprising of the control diet (T0) which contained 100% fish meal (FM), (four (4) Leucaena leucocephala leaf meal (LLlM) experimental diets (T1: 25%; T2: 50%; T3:75%; T4:100%) The feeding trial was conducted across 15 experimental plastic tanks with a 100L water carrying capacity for each tank. Each treatment had three replicates, and the fishes were fed twice a day for 16 weeks (112 days) under controlled conditions. Growth performance indices, including mean weight gain (WG), mean length gain, specific growth rate (SGR), were assessed. Water parameters like pH, temperature, and dissolved oxygen were measured. title: Novel pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine–hydantoin hybrids as selective anticancer agents: Synthesis, cytotoxicity, structural activity relationship (SAR), and molecular docking studies
abstract: Cancer remains one of the most serious global health challenges, and the limited selectivity and high toxicity of many current chemotherapeutic agents highlight the urgent need for new, more effective anticancer drugs. In this study, a novel series of pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine derivatives incorporating hydantoin, thioacrylonitrile, and thiophene moieties was designed and synthesized as potential selective anticancer agents. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their cytotoxic activity using the MTT assay against human liver carcinoma (HePG-2) and breast adenocarcinoma (MCF-7) cell lines, in addition to normal VERO and WI-38 cells. Structure–activity relationship (SAR) analysis was performed to identify key structural features responsible for biological activity. Furthermore, molecular docking studies were conducted against human DNA topoisomerase (PDB: 1T8I) to investigate the possible binding modes and molecular interactions of the most active compounds. The novelty of this work lies in the rational hybridization of the pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine scaffold with hydantoin and thioacrylonitrile functionalities to enhance anticancer potency and selectivity. title: PHARMACOLOGY OF RECEPTORS AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF DRUG SEARCHING: INTEGRATED CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY, PHARMACODYNAMIC, PHARMACOKINETIC, PHARMACOTHERAPEUTIC, PHARMACOGENOMIC, THERAPEUTIC DRUG MONITORING, EVIDENCE-BASED, AND PRECISION MEDICINE APPROACHES
abstract: Receptors are dynamic macromolecules that transduce chemical signals into biological responses and serve as the principal targets of modern therapeutics. This review surveys current concepts in receptor pharmacology and their application to drug discovery and development. Receptor-mediated signal transduction is examined across the major receptor families, including G protein–coupled receptors, ligand-gated and voltage-gated ion channels, nuclear receptors, and receptor tyrosine kinases, with emphasis on the second messengers, kinase cascades, and transcriptional programs that they engage. Classical receptor theory is reviewed alongside modern extensions that incorporate receptor efficacy, constitutive activity, receptor reserve, allosteric modulation, and biased agonism. Intracellular signal propagation is discussed as a network-level phenomenon shaped by cross-talk, feedback regulation, scaffold proteins, and compartmentalised signalling, providing the conceptual basis for network pharmacology. title: Smiling in influencer marketing: how smiles shape authenticity and consumer engagement
abstract: Purpose Many influencer marketing campaigns feature smiling influencers. However, whether smiling is always beneficial, and under which circumstances it might not be, remains underexplored. This paper aims to examine how an influencer’s smile (vs no smile) affects consumer engagement with influencer posts. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted a field study and several online experiments. In the field study, they analyzed 802 influencer campaigns with a total of over 125 million consumer interactions (i.e. liking and commenting). In the experiments, participants viewed influencer posts featuring commonly promoted products such as headphones (nStudy2 = 192, nStudy4 = 231), sunglasses (nStudy3 = 304) and protein bars (nStudy5 = 236, nSupplemental = 247). Findings The authors show that a smile (vs no smile) in influencer posts can backfire. Smiling can lead to lower engagement by reducing perceived authenticity. However, this negative effect is contingent upon influencer type (micro vs macro) and sponsorship presence (sponsored vs. non-sponsored). title: Conceptual and translational pitfalls of modified messenger RNA drug design with public health impact
abstract: Abstract Updated safety warnings for base-modified messenger RNA (mmRNA) vaccines—such as increased risks of life-threatening myo(peri)carditis and the increased appearance of colorectal cancer in young adults—prompted our comprehensive review of this approach. Careful analysis of RNA biology textbook materials and the scientific literature identified serious conceptual, procedural, and translational issues that explain the shortcomings and potential public health risks of these injectables. The primary issues include using artificial pseudo-uridinated and methylated nucleosides based on the misleading information that these modified bases occur naturally and in sufficient numbers in eukaryotic mRNAs. In mmRNA vaccines, approximately 50% of the bases are modified with N1-methyl-pseudouridine, whereas eukaryotic mRNA typically contains a much lower percentage of pseudouridine, ranging from 0.2% to 0.6% (Ψ/U ratio), without methylation with intronic (non-coding) properties. This practice, meant to stabilize mRNA and prolong its half-life, disregards the biological safeguard of rapid natural mRNA breakdown. title: Optimization of Enzymatic Hydrolysis and Leuconostoc mesenteroides MKJW Fermentation of Gryllus bimaculatus Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: Gryllus bimaculatus (GB) is a promising sustainable protein source, and its bioprocessing performance is strongly influenced by processing conditions. Enzymatic hydrolysis and lactic acid bacterial fermentation represent complementary approaches for modifying GB components and developing value-added products. In this study, response surface methodology (RSM) with a Box–Behnken design was used to optimize two GB bioprocesses: Neutrase-mediated enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation with Leuconostoc mesenteroides MKJW. For enzymatic hydrolysis, GB concentration, Neutrase concentration, and hydrolysis time were evaluated using degree of hydrolysis (DH) as the response. The model-derived condition associated with a high predicted DH within the tested range was 20% (w/v) GB, 136.2 U/mL Neutrase, and 31 h, under which the experimental DH was 78.59% compared with a predicted value of 87.03%. For fermentation, GB concentration, sucrose concentration, and fermentation time were simultaneously evaluated using viable cell count and in vitro α-glucosidase inhibition (AGI) as responses. title: Engineering allosteric regulation in ionotropic glutamate receptors to generate molecular tools for investigating synaptic functions
Structural basis for loop-dependent inhibition by AcrIIC1 anti-CRISPR proteins
abstract: Most characterized anti-CRISPR proteins act via well-defined core inhibitory mechanisms, yet how auxiliary structural elements modulate and potentiate these canonical processes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that AcrIIC1Boe represses Nme1Cas9 activity through an integrated, loop-coupled regulatory mode. Based on canonical occlusion of the HNH catalytic site, the extended loop of AcrIIC1Boe provides an additional coupled regulatory layer to remodel sgRNA spacer arrangement and R-loop progression, thereby enhancing Cas9 inhibition. Loop deletion largely abrogates robust inhibition, indicating that this loop module is indispensable for full AcrIIC1 inhibitory potency. Consistently, transplantation of this functional loop into the weakly active AcrIIC1Nme1 efficiently elevates its inhibitory performance. Our findings identify a loop-mediated regulatory strategy that potentiates the canonical HNH occlusion mechanism, clarify the structural basis for functional divergence across AcrIIC1 homologs, and offer a modular engineering principle for the rational design and optimization of anti-CRISPR proteins with enhanced potency. title: The Genetic Discovery (GeDi) resource: Deep characterization of a multi-ancestry panel of human reference iPSCs for functional genomic studies
abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are essential tools for disease modelling, drug discovery, and functional genomics, yet the field remains anchored to a small number of reference lines, limiting our understanding of how genetic background shapes cellular phenotypes across human populations. Here we describe the Genetic Discovery iPSC panel (GeDi), eight clonal iPSC lines reprogrammed from male and female donors that broadly span global human population diversity. Ancestry analysis confirmed that each line's genetic profile is concordant with donor self-reported ancestry. All GeDi lines are pluripotent and passed comprehensive quality control, demonstrating Sendai virus clearance, intact p53 pathway integrity, reproducible proliferative capacity, and compatibility with standardized genome editing workflows. Transcriptome profiling across five differentiated lineages covered 80% of annotated protein-coding genes and revealed stable donor-intrinsic variability in gene expression within each lineage. title: Enhancing the stability and translatability of synthetic circular RNA: design strategies and emerging challenges
abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed RNA molecules with exceptional intrinsic stability and when properly designed, purified, nucleoside-modified, and delivered, show reduced unwanted innate immune activation, endowing them with unique advantages for vaccines, cancer immunotherapy, and protein replacement therapies. Synthetic circRNAs can be generated via enzymatic ligation, chemical ligation, or ribozyme-mediated circularization; however, efficient translation and scalable manufacturing remain major bottlenecks. In this Review, we survey current production strategies and therapeutic applications of synthetic circRNAs, and delineate engineering approaches that enhance molecular stability through nucleoside modification and sequence optimization, as well as strategies to improve translational efficiency, including internal ribosome entry site (IRES) and cap-mimicking elements, epitranscriptomic modifications, and rational sequence design. We further examine how these optimizations intersect with immunogenicity and process development, highlighting the critical quality attributes that govern circRNA product consistency and performance. title: Synergistic Integration of Biosynthesized and Synthetic Nanomaterials
abstract: Conventional synthetic nanomaterials like metal hydrides and engineered carbon structures have high precision, tunable properties, and strong hydrogen adsorption potential, but often suffer from high production cost, toxicity concerns, and environmental impacts. Biosynthesized nanomaterials derived from biological systems offer economically friendly synthesis routes, unique porous structures, and improved sustainability, though their processing, performance, and reproducibility can sometimes be their limitation. The synergistic integration of biosynthesized and synthetic nanomaterials is a hybrid strategy to tackle advanced hydrogen storage applications. Herein, we reviewed the emerging connections between both material classes and highlighted how hybridization can enhance surface area, porosity, catalytic activity, and hydrogen uptake kinetics. Various synthesis approaches including co-synthesis, sequential functionalization, in-situ coating of bioderived scaffolds, and metal doping among other techniques are discussed as practical design strategies for creating high-performance hybrid systems. title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate–dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of Saccharomyces cerevisiae ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles.
