title: Rationally Designed Phenyl- and Phenanthryl-Based Imidazole Hybrids for the Treatment of Breast Cancer—A Structure–Activity Relationship Study
abstract: A series of 11 compounds of phenyl–imidazole–pyrrole and 9 compounds of phenanthryl–imidazole–pyrrole were synthesized and evaluated against breast cancer cell lines differing in the expression of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor (HER)-2, viz., BT-474 (ER+, PR+, and HER2+), T-47D and MCF-7 (ER+, PR+, and HER2−), and MDA-MB-468 and MDA-MB-231 (ER−, PR−, and HER2−). The analysis of the results indicated that the most active compounds were 5d and 5k from the phenyl–imidazole–pyrrole series and 6b and 6i from the phenanthryl–imidazole–pyrrole series (IC50 < 50 µM). Molecular docking (MD) and molecular dynamics simulation (MDS) studies demonstrated that the active compounds exhibited high binding affinity to the 7NH5 (a co-crystal structure of Akt1 and its specific inhibitor) protein, which is overexpressed in many breast cancer types. The active compounds 6b and 6i reduced the viability of MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 cells by inducing cell death mechanisms. Both compounds halted the proliferation by arresting cells in the G0/G1 phase of the cell cycle. The results are similar to those of traditional Cisplatin. Intraperitoneal admini

title: Immunoinformatics-Based Design of a Chimeric Vaccine Against Necator americanus Targeting the Na-APR-1, Na-GST-1, and Na-ASP-2 Vaccine Candidates
abstract: Hookworm infection, caused predominantly by Necator americanus, is a soil-transmitted helminthiasis that disproportionately affects impoverished communities across tropical and subtropical regions, with an estimated 406-480 million people infected globally. Control continues to rely largely on mass drug administration, an approach challenged by rapid reinfection, the absence of durable protective immunity, and growing concern over reduced drug efficacy. While the leading recombinant protein antigens Na-APR-1, Na-GST-1, and Na-ASP-2 have demonstrated clinical safety and immunogenicity, the withdrawal of Na-ASP-2 after triggering allergic reactions in individuals with prior natural exposure revealed both the promise and the risk of single-antigen approaches, underscoring the need for a rationally designed multi-antigen vaccine. We used an immunoinformatics approach to design a novel chimeric vaccine candidate by combining carefully selected B-cell and T-cell epitopes from the major clinical-stage hookworm protein antigens with an immunostimulatory adjuvant sequence. The candidate's 3D structure was predicted, refined, and validated using established bioinformatics approaches, and its

title: Macronutrient Distribution and Frailty According to Energy Sufficiency
abstract: Background/Objectives: Nutritional status is a potentially modifiable factor associated with frailty in older adults. However, the association between macronutrient balance and frailty remains understudied and may differ by energy intake sufficiency. We examined the association between adherence to the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges (AMDRs) and frailty by energy intake sufficiency. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 2803 adults aged ≥65 years who participated in the 2022 and 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Macronutrient intake was classified using the 2025 Korean AMDRs for carbohydrate (50–65%), protein (10–20%), and fat (15–30% of energy). AMDR adherence required all three ranges to be met. Energy sufficiency was defined as ≥30 kcal/kg/day, and frailty was assessed using a modified Fried phenotype. Survey-weighted logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses accounted for complex sampling design. Results: Among 925 energy-sufficient and 1878 energy-insufficient participants, frailty prevalence was 6.1% and 9.5%, respectively. AMDR non-adherence was associated with higher odds of frailty in energy-sufficient par

title: Molecular dynamics simulations in protein design and engineering
Dietary betaine supplementation improves oxidative status and ameliorates the negative effects of heat stress in lambs
abstract: Heat stress challenges livestock welfare, production and sustainability and is expected to intensify with climate change. Betaine has been shown to alleviate heat stress, but its efficacy under sustained heat load with restricted nocturnal cooling remains unexplored. This study is among the first to evaluate dietary betaine when warm nights prevent thermal recovery. Forty-eight crossbred [(Merino × Border Leicester) × Dorset] lambs (6–10 months) were assigned to a 2 × 2 factorial design: thermoneutral (TN: 18–21 °C, 45–55% relative humidity (RH)) or heat stress (HS: 28–38 °C, 40–60% RH daytime, 26–28 °C and 45–55% RH overnight) for 14 days, with a control (CON) or betaine (BET; 2 g/day, previously shown effective in heat-stressed sheep) diets. Rectal temperature (RT) and respiration rate (RR) were measured thrice daily; blood and muscle samples were collected for plasma metabolites and antioxidant enzyme activities. Under HS, BET lambs had lower RT at 0900h (39.7 vs. 39.6 °C; p = 0.014), and 1300h (40.2 vs. 40.1°C; p = 0.043), and lower RR at 1300h (194 vs. 181 bpm; p = 0.013) compared with CON lambs. Plasma cortisol was lower in BET lambs on day 7 (20.3 vs. 15.8 ng/mL; p = 0.016).

title: Advanced Biosynthesized Nanomaterials for Hydrogen Storage
abstract: Biosynthesized nanomaterials are environmentally friendly and a novel solution for improving hydrogen storage performance through improved design, mechanisms, and applications of advanced nanomaterials that are produced through biological routes. The main biosynthesis techniques and various classes of biologically derived nanomaterials, including bio-metals, bio-carbon structures, metal hydrides, and bio-derived metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), were explored. As well as how biological agents influence morphology, surface functionalization, porosity, and catalytic properties, which are critical for enhancing hydrogen adsorption and release. The fundamental mechanisms that govern hydrogen storage, including physisorption, chemisorption, spillover effects, and thermodynamic and kinetic considerations, were not left out. Biologically synthesized Pd nanoparticles, green-synthesized MgH 2 nanostructures, and protein-assisted MOFs are analyzed as they demonstrate improved storage capacity and reversibility. Furthermore, the integration of these materials into fuel cells and portable hydrogen storage systems, as well as safety, scalability, and environmentally sustainable issues, was evalu

title: Role of machine learning in drug discovery and therapeutic protein design
MOFI reveals dynamic multi-omics coordination during cell fate progression
abstract: Cell fate decisions are shaped by dynamic coordination across transcriptomic, chromatin, and protein layers. Time-series single-cell multi-omics assays now enable these molecular layers to be profiled across developmental stages, yet each cell is still observed only once, and the continuous multi-omics trajectories connecting discrete snapshots remain unresolved. A central challenge is therefore to jointly integrate paired omics measurements while reconstructing their shared developmental progression. Here we present Multi-Omics Fate Inference (MOFI), a dynamically constrained multi-omics integration framework designed to reconstruct continuous cell fate transitions from paired multi-omics snapshots sampled across multiple time points. MOFI jointly models omics-specific state dynamics, cross-omics correspondence, and shared population growth within a unified framework, enabling cross-omics perturbation response analysis and identification of candidate cross-omics transformation programs. Across simulated benchmarks and paired RNA-ATAC/RNA-protein time-series datasets, MOFI reconstructed continuous fate transitions, population dynamics and cross-omics changes consistent with observe

title: An in silico Molecular Docking Study of Andaliman (Zanthoxylum acanthopodium DC.) Phytochemicals against the HER2 Kinase Domain through Re-Docking Validation
abstract: Aims: To evaluate the predicted interactions of six andaliman (Zanthoxylum acanthopodium DC.) phytochemicals, namely quercetin, 4-coumaric acid, isorhamnetin, berberine, ferulic acid, and kaempferol, with the HER2 kinase domain using a molecular docking protocol validated by re-docking. Study Design: A computational in silico study using a structure-based molecular docking approach. Place and Duration of Study: Computational analysis using molecular structures obtained from the RCSB Protein Data Bank and PubChem. No physical study site was involved. Methodology: Chain A of the HER2 kinase structure (PDB ID 3PP0) was used as the receptor. The docking protocol was validated by re-docking the co-crystallised ligand 03Q using AutoDock Vina 1.1.2. The grid box was centred at 17.098971, 16.548676, and 26.600647 Å with a size of 20 × 20 × 20 Å³ and an exhaustiveness of 16. Heavy-atom RMSD was calculated using Open Babel obrms. The six phytochemicals, together with the reference ligands lapatinib and TAK-285, were then docked into the same binding site. Binding affinity and ligand–protein interactions were analysed using PyMOL. Results: Re-docking of 03Q yielded a heavy-atom RMSD of 0.7035

title: Computational and Experimental Approaches in Protein Engineering and Design
Assessing Genotype × Environment Interactions for Yield Stability and Grain Quality in Spring Barley Under Contrasting Agro-Ecological Conditions for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Increasing climate variability is placing growing pressure on cereal production systems, highlighting the need to identify stable and resilient genotypes for sustainable crop production. This study evaluated phenotypic variability, grain yield, yield stability and grain-quality traits in 25 spring barley (Hordeum vulgare subsp. distichon (L.) Körn.) genotypes, including varieties and advanced breeding lines, under contrasting agro-ecological conditions in Romania. Field experiments were conducted over two growing seasons (2024–2025) at Turda and Fundulea using a randomized complete block design with three replications. The evaluated agronomic, phenological, and quality traits included plant height, heading and flowering time, thousand-kernel weight, grain yield, and grain protein and starch contents. The effects of year, location, genotype and their interactions were analyzed, and GGE biplot analysis was used to examine genotype performance and stability across environments. Across the 300 plot-level observations, grain yield ranged from 1631 to 7730 kg ha−1, with an overall mean of 5283 kg ha−1 and a descriptive CV of 21.99%, reflecting overall variability across the dataset rathe

title: Advances in enhanced sampling simulations of G-protein-coupled receptors
abstract: G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest family of membrane proteins involved in cellular signaling. Although X-ray crystallography and cryo-Electron Microscopy (cryo-EM) have provided valuable structural insights into GPCRs, these experimental techniques primarily capture static conformations and cannot fully resolve the dynamic transitions that underlie activation, allostery, ligand recognition, and signaling of GPCRs. In this perspective, we highlight Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations of GPCRs using enhanced sampling methods. These computational approaches have provided mechanistic insights into receptor activation and deactivation mechanisms, allosteric communication networks, ligand and peptide binding and dissociation pathways, and GPCR–G protein interaction kinetics while revealing transient intermediate states that are often inaccessible to experiments. Together, these advances provide a powerful framework for understanding GPCR signaling mechanisms and accelerating the rational design of selective therapeutics with improved efficacy and reduced side effects.

title: Neurovascular, Structural, and Molecular Mechanisms of Cognitive Impairment in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with cognitive impairment and neurodegenerative changes in addition to its established metabolic and vascular complications.Evidence indicates that retinal and cerebral microvascular abnormalities, structural brain alterations, impaired neurovascular coupling, and metabolic and molecular disturbances may contribute to cognitive vulnerability in individuals with T2DM.This systematic review synthesized evidence on the neurovascular, structural, cognitive, metabolic, molecular, and genetic factors associated with cognitive impairment in T2DM.The review was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework.A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was performed using predefined eligibility criteria.Study selection and data extraction were undertaken independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved through discussion and consensus.Ten studies comprising cross-sectional, observational, neuroimaging, longitudinal, genetic, and Mendelian-randomization designs were included.Risk of bias was assessed using stud

Preparation of Antioxidant Peptides from Hippocampus Abdominalis via High Hydrostatic Pressure-Assisted Enzymolysis: Evaluation of Their Protective Effects Against Male Reproductive Dysfunction in Mice
abstract: Hippocampus abdominalis (H. abdominalis) is an important marine teleost fish with diverse functional activities. Accordingly, the present research was designed to isolate and prepare innovative antioxidant peptides derived from H. abdominalis and to assess the protective and restorative impacts of its protein hydrolysates (HAPH) against reproductive injury caused by triptolide (TP) in male mice. Notably, pepsin was ultimately identified as the optimal protease among seven screened proteases. High hydrostatic pressure (HHP) pretreatment significantly increased peptide yield and antioxidant activity of pepsin hydrolysates. Subsequently, the optimal enzymatic hydrolysis conditions were established as E/S of 3% (w/w), hydrolysis time of 3 h, S/L of 1:25 (w/v), HHP pressure of 200 MPa, and 9 min of HHP time using single-factor experiments and response surface methodology. The peptide fraction with a molecular weight below 3 kDa (HAPH-1) exhibited stronger antioxidant activity and excellent stability against pH, temperature, and simulated gastrointestinal digestion. Furthermore, animal experiments revealed that HAPH-1 alleviated triptolide-induced impaired spermatogenesis and testicular

title: Introduction to the principles of protein engineering
Protein Deimmunization with a Generative Diffusion Model
abstract: Protein immunogenicity is a major cause of biologic drug failure, leading to the production of anti-drug antibodies (ADA) that accelerate drug clearance, rejection of repeated doses, abolished efficacy, and sometimes life threatening anaphylaxis in patients. These responses constrain the clinical use of synthetic protein therapeutics from non-human origin. To efficiently deimmunize protein therapeutics, we developed a generative discrete diffusion model (MESSI), which takes protein structures as input and outputs sequences that preserve structure without containing peptides predicted to bind major histocompatibility complex class II molecules. MESSI designs sequences with high structural recovery and down to 0 predicted epitopes for specified MHC molecules at higher efficiency than post-hoc filtering approaches. Experimentally, we first applied MESSI to deimmunize a luciferase and a de novo designed mini-binder against PD-1, resulting in variants with no predicted epitopes and higher activity than their parents. Lastly, we coupled MESSI with evolution guidance to deimmunize uricase, a clinically approved enzyme with severe immunogenicity, and found deimmunized variants with higher

title: Harnessing the ubiquitin-proteasome system: advances and challenges of PROTACs in breast cancer
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most significant health issues in the world, and resistance to treatment and a lack of targets that can be addressed with drugs limit the effectiveness of the existing treatment options. The development of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) has shifted the concept of occupancy-based inhibition toward event-based targeted protein degradation. Avoiding ubiquitin-proteasome hijacking, PROTACs target disease-relevant proteins to E3 ligases, allowing them to be catalytically degraded, thereby eliminating formerly undruggable or resistant targets. Their modular design, consisting of a warhead, linker, and E3 ligase ligand, eases rational design, but there are still difficulties, including hook effects, poor pharmacokinetics, and off-target toxicity. PROTACs have been known to undergo evolution, such as PHOTACs, CLIPTACs, and RIBOTACs, which have expanded therapeutic approaches. Clinical trial molecules such as ARV-471 have demonstrated an effective role in the degradation of ER+, showcasing their broader significance in HER2 by degrading BRD4, CDK, and PD-L1. However, a knowledge gap exists that limits our understanding of E3 ligases, constraining their

title: Techniques and applications of directed evolution
STING Agonist-Functionalized LNPs Enhance mRNA Vaccine CD8+ T-Cell and Antibody Responses in a Th1/Th2 Bias-Dependent Manner
abstract: Abstract Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines delivered by lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) can elicit strong antibody responses but comparatively limited cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell immunity. STING agonists can enhance cross-presentation and T-cell priming, but systemic administration is toxicity-limited. We engineered mRNA LNPs bearing the cyclic dinucleotide STING agonist STG968, which was surface-conjugated through a linker designed to be susceptible to cathepsin-mediated cleavage. In THP-1 dual-reporter cells, LNP-STG968 induced robust, dose-dependent IRF signaling with minimal NF-κB activation and partial suppression of protein expression. In mice, LNP–STG968 preserved local antigen expression while increasing early systemic IFN-α, IFN-γ, IL-6, IP-10, and MCP-1. Interestingly, these innate cytokine responses were mRNA-payload dependent. In prime-boost vaccination model with SARS-CoV-2 Delta S2P mRNA, LNP-STG968 enhanced adaptive immune responses in a Th1-/Th2-immune background-dependent manner relative to control LNP. These findings support further evaluation of STG968-functionalized LNPs as a formulation strategy for modulating innate and adaptive immune responses for next-generation mRNA vacc

title: Design of short-sequenced collagen type III-derived peptides with GPR56 dependent biological activity
abstract: We have previously shown that activation of G protein-coupled receptor 56 (GPR56) by its endogenous ligand collagen type III (Coll III) improves pancreatic β-cell function and potentiates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS). In the current study, alignment of Coll III and GPR56 genomic DNA revealed three complementary nucleotide regions, enabling the design of three short peptides (NQGCKL.NH2, H.LLSSR.NH2 and NH2.GYYCG.COOH). The peptides in double or triple combinations markedly increased cellular cAMP levels, enhanced GSIS, and improved cell viability both in human (EndoC βH1 cells) and rat pancreatic β-cell lines (INS-1 832/13 cells). These effects were markedly absent in GPR56-knockdown (GPR56-KD) cells, supporting receptor-dependent specificity. The peptide mixtures also counteracted cytokine- and glucotoxicity-induced cellular stress, restoring cAMP generation and insulin secretion. Comparable effects were not observed with dapagliflozin while glibenclamide decreased cell viability under similar conditions. In hepatic cell lines (HepG2, Hep1-6), peptide combinations enhanced cell survival in a GPR56-dependent manner, consistent with a broader role of GPR56 in metaboli

title: Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in Escherichia coli
abstract: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of E. coli DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of E. coli . Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.

title: Controlled functionalization of cellulose nanocrystals directs polymer-specific protein coronas and immune cell interactions
abstract: Polymer coatings are widely used to suppress nonspecific protein adsorption and modulate nanoparticle-cell interactions. However, the biological outcomes of polymer-functionalized nanoparticles remain difficult to predict in complex biological environments because protein corona formation rapidly alters nanoparticle identity. This challenge is particularly pronounced when hydrophobic moieties are incorporated for imaging or therapeutic applications, as they can promote nonspecific interactions at the nano-bio interface. Herein, we establish a modular grafting-to platform based on cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) that enables systematic comparison of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based, zwitterionic, and acrylamide-based polymers with controlled grafting density and chain conformation on a common porphyrin-modified surface. We demonstrate that dense polymer brushes reduce nonspecific protein adsorption in single-protein assays. By contrast, all CNC surfaces form dynamic coronas upon exposure to serum proteins, while specific polymer coatings selectively enrich or suppress distinct protein populations. We further demonstrate that polymer-dependent immune cell interactions are substantially

title: Pineal Guardian Announces the Nationwide Launch of Flagship Formula Pineal Guardian X
abstract: Pineal Guardian X brings together botanical extracts, mushroom-derived compounds and a convenient liquid delivery format as consumers explore nutritional approaches to cognitive wellness, relaxation and healthy living. Pineal Guardian X is drawing attention to the role of botanical nutrition in everyday cognitive wellness through its liquid-drop dietary supplement. Featuring plant-derived ingredients associated with antioxidant nutrition, traditional herbal practices and cognitive-health research, the product is positioned for adults interested in maintaining mental clarity, supporting normal brain function and developing consistent daily wellness routines. The supplement combines ingredients such as lion's mane mushroom, bacopa monnieri, ginkgo biloba, pine bark extract, spirulina, chlorella, moringa and tamarind. These ingredients represent different areas of botanical and nutritional research, including antioxidant activity, cognitive function and general cellular wellness. Unlike conventional capsules and tablets, Pineal Guardian X is marketed in a liquid format that can be incorporated into an existing routine without extensive preparation. title: Upgrading the HIV vaccine paradigm: accounting for host-pathogen diversity through geotargeting-based vaccine design
abstract: Introduction Effective HIV vaccine development, with satisfactory levels of response and coverage, remains an elusive goal in immunology. In this context, considerations of host-pathogen interactions from a geotargeting perspective could enhance disease control efforts. Current HIV vaccine strategies increasingly seek to address viral diversity, but the combined effects of regional viral variation and host HLA diversity on antigen processing and presentation remain insufficiently considered. Here, we evaluated whether integrating these host–pathogen variables could support geographically informed prioritization of HIV vaccine targets. Methods Using NetMHCpan 4.1, NetChop 3.1, and the IEDB antigen-processing prediction tool, we evaluated antigen-processing and presentation steps for HIV epitopes associated with viral control. We recovered Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) alleles associated with HIV control and their frequencies, and the protein sequences for the most common HIV subtypes in different African countries. We created maps linking both sets of information for each specific region. We then predicted the impact of mutations associated with different HIV strain sequences on pro

title: RNA Interference-Mediated Suppression of RAGE
abstract: The receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE/AGER) is an important mediator of inflammatory signaling and has been implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with aging. Chronic low-grade inflammation (“inflammaging”) is a characteristic feature of biological aging, providing a rationale for investigating molecular regulators of inflammatory signaling such as RAGE. This study aimed to develop and validate short hairpin RNA (shRNA) constructs suppressing AGER/RAGE in human cell models. Five shRNA constructs targeting human AGER were designed, cloned into pLSL-puro, and verified by Sanger sequencing. Lentiviral vectors were produced in HEK293T cells and used to establish stable HEK293T, 786-O, and human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) populations with AGER knockdown. AGER/RAGE expression was assessed by RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. Silencing efficiency varied with the construct and the cellular model. sh1 produced the strongest suppression of AGER, exceeding 70% in selected models, whereas sh2 was effective in HEK293T and 786-O cells. Reduced RAGE expression was confirmed at the mRNA, protein, and cell-surface levels, identifying sh1 a

title: Cancer nanomedicine and RNA/Lipid nanoparticle platforms in oncology: developmental evolution, translational barriers, and precision-therapy opportunities
abstract: Nanomedicine has become an important translational platform in oncology by enabling altered pharmacokinetics, controlled exposure, reduced systemic toxicity, intracellular delivery of nucleic acids, and improved handling of complex therapeutic payloads. Early cancer nanomedicines, including pegylated liposomal cytotoxics and albumin-bound drug products, demonstrated that nanoscale formulation design could improve the clinical utility of established anticancer agents. More recently, lipid nanoparticles, RNA therapeutics, individualized neoantigen vaccines, gene-regulatory approaches, and immune-modulating delivery systems have expanded the role of nanoparticles from passive drug carriers to programmable oncology platforms. This narrative review examines the developmental evolution of cancer-focused pharmaceutical nanoparticles, with emphasis on liposomes, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), albumin-bound systems, polymeric particles, polymeric micelles, nanocrystals, nanoemulsions, solid lipid nanoparticles, inorganic particles, extracellular vesicles, and hybrid delivery technologies. Each platform class is treated systematically, covering representative approved products, formulation char

title: The Preterm Brain Is Also What It Eats: A Systematic Review of Nutrition and Neuroimaging Outcomes in Preterm Infants
abstract: Background: Nutrition is one of the most modifiable determinants of brain development in preterm infants. Although increasing evidence supports associations between early nutritional exposures and neurodevelopment, studies remain heterogeneous regarding nutritional interventions, imaging biomarkers, and long-term outcomes. This systematic review aimed to summarize contemporary evidence on the relationship between nutrition and brain development in preterm infants using neuroimaging as the primary assessment tool while proposing an integrated translational framework to guide future research. Methods: Following a PECO framework, a systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL: population, infants born before 37 completed weeks of gestation; exposure, any enteral or parenteral nutritional exposure, supplementation strategy, fortification approach, or individualized nutritional intervention; comparator, an alternative nutritional strategy, lower or absent exposure, standard care or, when relevant, a term-born reference group; outcomes, MRI- or CUS-based measures of brain growth, maturation, connectivity, or injury. title: Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles as Biomimetic Drug Delivery Systems: Design, Therapeutic Applications, and Translational Challenges
abstract: Biomimetic cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CM-NPs) have emerged as a promising class of nanocarriers that integrate the tunable physicochemical properties of engineered nanoparticles with selected biological features of naturally derived cell membranes. By retaining membrane-associated proteins, lipids, glycans, and receptors, CM-NPs have demonstrated the potential to modulate immune recognition, prolong systemic circulation, improve biocompatibility, and facilitate disease-specific targeting; however, these effects depend on the membrane source, nanoparticle composition, coating integrity, fabrication method, and biological context. This review critically examines major membrane-engineering strategies, including lipid insertion, covalent conjugation, metabolic glycoengineering, and genetic modification, together with fabrication methods such as extrusion, sonication, electroporation, in situ polymerization, and microfluidics. Particular emphasis is placed on nanoparticles coated with erythrocyte, platelet, stem cell, immune cell, bacterial, cancer cell, and hybrid membranes. title: Computational protein design approaches for understanding and combating antimicrobial resistance
Drug-centric knowledge graph: representing therapeutic modality, pharmacology and multiscale biology
abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs link targets to mechanisms, diseases and phenotypes, but target-centered representations omit much of what distinguishes therapeutic interventions. We introduce a drug-centric knowledge graph, whose identity model, schema and information-selection priorities are organized around the therapeutic intervention, and a graph built on this design. Each intervention has one identity, linked through relation types shared by all compounds, including target actions, indications, adverse effects, classifications, half-life and direct links to pathways, Gene Ontology concepts, cells and anatomy, and through modality-specific relation types describing small-molecule chemistry, antibody sequences and formats, protein-therapy sequences and antibody-drug conjugate components. Integrating 38 source resources, the graph contains 166,261 nodes of 27 types, 8,106,906 directed edges of 129 relation types and 18,429 compounds in eight therapeutic categories. Construction combines source-specific extraction, compound-identity resolution, language-model-assisted vocabulary and predicate mapping, confidence scoring and connectivity filtering; an expert-reviewed workflow adds inv

title: Immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a recombinant HtsA-SLOdm fusion protein against Group A Streptococcus infection
abstract: Group A Streptococcus (GAS) is a major human pathogen responsible for a broad spectrum of diseases, yet no licensed vaccine is currently available. Heme-transfer lipoprotein A (HtsA) and streptolysin O (SLO) are key virulence-associated factors involved in iron acquisition and host cell damage, respectively, making them attractive vaccine targets. Here, we designed and evaluated HtsA-SLOdm, a recombinant fusion protein comprising HtsA and a detoxified mutant of SLO, to assess its immunogenicity and protective efficacy against GAS infection. The fusion protein retained the antigenicity of both components and exhibited negligible hemolytic activity without detectable histopathological toxicity in immunized mice. Immunization with alum-adjuvanted HtsA-SLOdm elicited robust antigen-specific antibody responses, with endpoint IgG titers ranging from 1:312,500 to 1:1,562,500. In a murine skin infection model, HtsA-SLOdm vaccination improved survival, reduced lesion size and bacterial load, and alleviated tissue damage, accompanied by enhanced collagen deposition and angiogenesis. Antisera from immunized mice also mediated opsonophagocytic killing of GAS. Mechanistically, HtsA-SLOdm promot

title: Lower oxidative balance score and higher systemic immune-inflammatory indices are associated with current asthma
abstract: Whether the oxidative balance score (OBS) and complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices are associated with current asthma, relative to a correctly defined never-asthma comparison group and accounting for the survey's complex sampling design, has not been investigated. This cross-sectional study used data from a nationally representative health survey cycle (August 2021-August 2023). Current asthma (n = 517) and never-asthma (n = 3725) groups were defined using validated lifetime-diagnosis and current-status questions; a former-asthma group (n = 308) was analyzed descriptively. Six CBC-derived indices (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammatory response index, eosinophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio) were calculated from absolute blood counts. Survey-weighted logistic regression, incorporating NHANES sampling weights, stratification, and primary sampling units, estimated odds ratios (ORs) for current asthma per 1-standard deviation increase in OBS and each index, with exposure-specific covariate adjustment and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction across

title: Effects of organic nutrient sources and NPK fertilizer on soil fertility, yield, and rhizome quality of ginger
abstract: Soil fertility improvement using locally available nutrient sources is essential for sustainable ginger production in low-input tropical agroecosystems. A two-year field study was conducted in 2023 and 2024 at two sites in Owo, Ondo State, southwestern Nigeria, to evaluate the comparative effects of animal manures, green biomass amendments and NPK fertilizer on soil properties, growth, yield and rhizome quality of ginger ( Zingiber officinale Roscoe). Eight treatments comprising pig manure, cow dung, poultry manure, goat manure, Tithonia diversifolia , Chromolaena odorata , NPK 15-15-15 fertilizer and an unfertilized control were arranged in a randomized complete block design with three replications. All nutrient sources were applied at an equivalent rate of 120 kg N ha − 1 . Data were subjected to analysis of variance, and treatment means were separated using Duncan’s multiple range test at p ≤ 0.05. Organic amendments generally increased soil pH, organic matter, total N, available P and exchangeable K, Ca and Mg, while reducing bulk density and improving soil moisture compared with the control and NPK fertilizer. Poultry manure produced the highest rhizome yields of 20.5 and 21.8

title: The advances and challenges of mRNA-LNP application in fields of hematology and oncology therapeutics
abstract: The rapidly global deployment of COVID-19 mRNA-LNP vaccines established the clinical feasibility of combining RNA medicine with LNP delivery systems, transforming a long-standing experimental concept into a scalable therapeutic modality, previously considered impossible. Currently, the value of mRNA-LNPs has been expanding from infectious disease vaccines to cancer immunotherapy, personalized neoantigen vaccination, in vivo immune-cell engineering, protein replacement therapy, mRNA-encoded biologics and genome editing, with particular relevance to hematology and oncology. However, in hematologic and oncologic settings, therapeutic success is constrained by biological barriers that less prominent in prophylactic vaccination. Systemically administered LNPs are strongly influenced by hepatic sequestration, protein corona formation and mononuclear-phagocyte clearance; solid tumors additionally present heterogeneous vasculature, variable enhanced permeability and retention, dense extracellular matrix, elevated interstitial pressure and limited intratumoral diffusion. title: In silico approach to Helicobacter pylori vaccine design
abstract: Abstract Helicobacter pylori , a Gram-negative microorganism, infects over half of the human population worldwide. Its extensive genetic variability and capacity to bypass host immune defences continue to impede the creation of an effective vaccine. Nonetheless, contemporary progress in computational biology and immunoinformatics has introduced innovative methodologies that can substantially support and accelerate vaccine design against this pathogen. In the present work, an in silico strategy was employed to develop a multi-epitope vaccine targeting H. pylori . The FlaA, UreB and PSA D15 proteins were chosen as primary antigens due to their strong immunogenic potential, critical roles in bacterial physiology, and comparatively low sequence variability among strains. Using advanced bioinformatics and immunoinformatics pipelines, potential epitopes for both B-cell and T-cell were identified and assembled through rational protein engineering approaches to generate the final vaccine construct. title: Identification of Novel Potential Tubulin-Targeting Heterocyclic Compounds via Integrated Virtual Screening and In Vitro Studies
abstract: Background: The development of novel tubulin-targeting agents remains a promising strategy in anticancer drug design. In the present study, novel heterocyclic tubulin-targeting compounds were identified using a complex in silico/in vitro workflow. Methods: An in-house library of approximately 8000 structurally diverse heterocyclic compounds was screened for antiproliferative activity, yielding 260 experimentally validated hits. These compounds were docked against the colchicine, vinca, and taxane binding sites of tubulin. Selected compounds were also tested for their effects on cellular β-tubulin protein levels in Jurkat cells. Results: Docking analysis indicated that 42 compounds matched or exceeded colchicine’s binding energy, 3 compounds were comparable to vinblastine, and 18 compounds surpassed paclitaxel, suggesting the colchicine and taxane sites as preferred targets. Five top-scoring compounds (Les-6370, Les-4272, Les-4309, Les-4403, and Les-1419) were further analyzed via molecular dynamics simulations, confirming stable binding—particularly at the colchicine site—and favorable hydrogen-bonding and lipophilic interactions. At 10 µM, Les-1419 and Les-4309 reduced total cellu

title: Porous geopolymer from cyanobacterial sludge and coal fly ash as shape-stabilizing matrix for thermal energy storage using phase change paraffin
abstract: The consumption of fossil fuels drives both the energy crisis and greenhouse gas emissions, while the accumulation of solid wastes such as coal fly ash (CFA) and cyanobacterial sludge (CS) exerts considerable ecological pressure. This study explores the utilization of CS and CFA as raw materials, employing egg white powder as a surfactant and hydrogen peroxide as a blowing agent to fabricate a highly porous geopolymer (CCG). The organic fibers in CS act as pore templates and reinforcing agents, while their partial degradation in the alkaline environment participates in the gelation process. The optimal formulation comprises a 9 mol/L sodium hydroxide solution, 3 wt% egg white powder, 7 wt% hydrogen peroxide, a CS:CFA mass ratio of 2:8, and a sodium silicate to sodium hydroxide solution ratio of 2.5:1. Following synthesis, CCG underwent vacuum impregnation with phase change paraffin (PCP). The capillary forces within the porous matrix effectively encapsulate the molten PCP, yielding a shape-stabilized phase change composite (CCGP). Relative to CCG the CCGP exhibits a thermal conductivity enhancement of 0.081-0.168 W/(m·K). The solidification and melting enthalpies of the CCGP were 6

title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. OH AWCs mediated the transport pathways, enabling the membrane to deliver a NaCl rejection of 99.2 ± 0.3%, an NDMA rejection of 93.9 ± 0.1% that surpassed the existing upper bound of permselectivity, and an ultrahigh pure water permeance (4.5 ± 0.2 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1) that exceeded that of state-of-the-art RO membranes. Within the OH AWCs, the hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules and the -OH resulted in a short residence time and a high jump frequency of water molecules, enabling the formation of dynamic and continuous OH-H2O networks that facilitated rapid water movement. In contrast, NaCl and NDMA faced high trans-channel energy barriers, which significantly hindered their transport through the OH AWCs. The r

title: Principles, methods, and computational approaches to enhance protein stability and solubility
Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition
abstract: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR- Psp Cas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence by Psp Cas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion. Psp Cas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that Psp Cas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of Psp Cas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise

title: L-amino acids and their derivatives supplementation enhances growth and metabolic responses in Labeo catla (Hamilton, 1822)
abstract: Improving feed intake is a key strategy for enhancing the production efficiency of the culture system. The present work was conducted to evaluate the efficiency of selected amino acids and their derivatives as feeding stimulants and attractants on growth and physio-biochemical parameters of Labeo catla. Four hundred and eighty (30.95±1.86 g) fish were distributed in a completely randomised design for a 60-day feeding trial. Eight iso-nitrogenous (30%) and iso-caloric (375 Kcal 100g–1) practical diets were formulated: control (no supplementation), Ala (1.5% supplemental alanine), Arg (1.25% supplemental arginine), Bet (0.5% supplemental betaine), Glu (1% supplemental glutamic acid), Gly (1% supplemental glycine), Hyp (1% supplemental hydroxyproline) and Lys (1.5% supplemental lysine). Dietary supplementation significantly (p < 0.05) improved feeding response, weight gain (WG), weight gain percentage (WG%), protein efficiency ratio (PER), average daily gain (ADG), and specific growth rate (SGR), with the highest growth performance observed in the Hyp group followed by Arg, Ala and Bet. title: Benzoylaconine suppresses colorectal cancer progression by modulating the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis
abstract: Background Colorectal cancer (CRC) has a high incidence, and both metastasis and drug resistance remain formidable challenges in clinical management. Owing to their multi-target activity and favorable safety profiles, natural products have become a prolific source for anticancer drug discovery. Benzoylaconine (BAC) is a secondary metabolite of aconitine with markedly attenuated toxicity that retains anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antitumor properties; however, its antitumor effects and the underlying molecular mechanisms in CRC are poorly defined. This study was designed to systematically characterize the impact of BAC on the malignant phenotypes of CRC cells and to identify its potential molecular targets. Methods HCT116 and SW480 cells were used as model systems. Proliferation was assessed by MTT and EdU assays; migration and invasion by wound-healing and Transwell assays, respectively; cell cycle and apoptosis by flow cytometry. Network pharmacology was applied to predict core targets and construct a protein–protein interaction network. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations examined binding; SPR verified direct binding to CDK2 and MMP2. RNA-seq identified differentially

title: Decoding Clade-Specific bNAb-HIV-1 Env Interactions Using Machine Learning
abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) exhibits extensive genetic diversity, posing a major challenge to AIDS vaccine development. Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) isolated from HIV-1-infected individuals offer valuable templates for designing broadly protective immunogens. Here, structural and energetic descriptors extracted from experimentally resolved bNAb/HIV-1 Envelope (Env) protein-protein complexes were used to develop machine-learning (ML) models predicting binding free energies (∆G) and dissociation constants (KD) across multiple HIV-1 clades. Among the algorithms evaluated, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) achieved the best predictive performance, with training and test R2 values of 0.92 and 0.658, respectively. Applying the optimized model to HIV-1 datasets revealed clade-dependent binding patterns, with clade B showing the greatest variability and clade G exhibiting signatures associated with reduced neutralization potency. Predicted ∆G of different bNAb classes followed the trend gp120-gp41 interface ≈ fusion domain > CD4 binding site (CD4bs) > V1V2 loop ≈ V3-glycan, consistent with experimentally reported affinity profiles of benchmark bNAbs. title: EZPro-Fit: A Thermophile-Informed Cross-Modal Generative Framework Integrating DNA Language and Protein Structure for Enzyme Mutant Design
Towards the construction of a chitin-binding domain BioBrick®: PCR Amplification of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa chiC chitin-binding domain
abstract: Historically, the chitin-binding domain (CBD) of the PA01 strain of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Chitinase C (ChiC), has been employed as a protein tag in purification processes. However, there remains a need for CBD tags with new properties, such as increased temperature stability or binding affinity. The CBD of PAO1 ChiC is a novel CBD showing promise for purification assays as it could have the aforementioned properties. This study aimed to design a gene block of the PAO1 ChiC CBD and insert it into an expression vector to confirm CBD functionality separate from its native protein and its potential as a tag. This gene block was also designed for cloning into a BioBrick® vector, a standardised vector for interchangeable parts. Insertion into a BioBrick® would allow a standardised protocol for tagging proteins with a CBD, through different combinations of BioBrick® parts. Furthermore, because the cysteine residues within the CBDs of other organisms have been critical to proper domain folding, the functional relevance of the sole ChiC CBD cysteine in PAO1 was also explored. To do this, a second gene block was designed with the substitution of alanine for cysteine. This study describes t

title: Splicing-guaranteed artificial introns enable efficient homology-directed repair at internal exons and streamlined cell engineering
abstract: Selection-marker-assisted homology-directed repair (HDR) efficiently edits coding sequence termini but is poorly suited for internal exons. Here, we developed artificial reporter intron-based HDR (ARI-HDR), which inserts a selectable intron into target exons to enable precise internal-exon editing. Although designed for scarless removal by splicing, ARIs frequently exhibit inaccurate splicing. Using a random mutagenesis reporter assay, we identified intron upstream sequences (IUS) as key determinants of splicing fidelity and screened degenerate IUS variants to obtain reliably spliced ARI donors. ARI-HDR successfully introduced site-specific mutations into five human genes. Combining long single-stranded DNA donors with conversion-tract optimization increased editing efficiency to over 80%. This efficiency enabled 'Dirty-Editing,' a streamlined workflow that generates precisely edited mixed-cell populations without single-cell cloning. Together, ARI-HDR extends selection-based enrichment to internal exons across protein-coding genes, while our splicing-optimized intron design offers a broadly applicable solution for artificial intron-based technologies.

title: ProtyQuant: A Step-by-Step Protocol for Label-Free Protein Quantification in Data-Dependent Acquisition (DDA) Shotgun Proteomics—From Raw Spectra to Comparative Analysis
MYC targeted de novo binders impair tumor growth
abstract: MYC is one of the most frequently dysregulated oncogenic drivers across many cancers, yet direct therapeutic targeting has remained difficult because its function is mediated by disordered regions and transient protein-protein interactions. Here we design proteins that bind epitopes within regions of MYC whose sequence is conserved between human and mouse, including intrinsically disordered motifs required for oncogenic activity. In vitro, the designs bind MYC with nanomolar affinity and in cells they engage MYC, disrupt interactions with MAX, and remodel MYC-associated protein complexes. Expression of the binders decreases cell proliferation across diverse MYC-dependent hematopoietic, liver, pancreatic, and patient-derived tumor models, and in an orthotopic pancreatic cancer model, binder-expressing tumor cells were selectively depleted. This work establishes de novo protein design as a generalizable strategy to therapeutically target intrinsically disordered transcription factors.

title: Molecular Characterization of Gene-Product Relationships in the Wheat Gluten Complex for Reduced Immunogenicity Wheat Development
abstract: Immune-mediated reactions to wheat gliadins, including celiac disease and wheat allergies, affect ~1% of the U.S. population and are prevalent worldwide. Reducing the risk of inadvertent gluten exposure for individuals with celiac disease or wheat allergies requires the development of reduced immunogenicity wheat varieties which are suitable for human consumption. This study was designed with a view to improve our understanding of gene protein relationships at the complex wheat Gli1/Glu3 and Gli2 loci, and to develop genetic and molecular resources for breeding reduced-immunogenicity wheat lines. We conducted comprehensive genomic, biochemical, and immunological analyses of diverse wheat genetic resources, including aneuploid stocks, chromosome deficiency and interstitial deletion lines, Wasko omega null, the landrace San Pastore, Pegaso near isogenic lines lacking Gli1/Glu3/Gli2 loci, and progenies derived from a Wasko mega null X Pegaso(6A/6D) alpha null. Genomic characterization involved the targeted GlutEnSeq approach and PCR based DNA markers while biochemical and immunological analyses employed acid-urea PAGE, SDS PAGE, and ELISA. Integration of these complementary approaches

title: Harnessing the BrkA Autotransporter to Surface Display the Zinc-Binding Domain Tetrahymena thermophila Metallothionein MTT5 on Escherichia coli for Zinc Biosorption Evaluation
abstract: Heavy metal contamination, particularly zinc, poses significant environmental and health concerns. Surface expression of metal-binding proteins in easily culturable bacteria such as Escherichia coli presents a promising bioremediation strategy to mitigate heavy metal pollution. We investigated the surface expression of Tetrahymena thermophila metallothionein (MTT5), a 10.5 kDa metal-binding protein, using the BrkA autotransporter system in E. coli. We designed a recombinant BrkA-MTT5 plasmid (pADKT5) and confirmed MTT5 expression via western blot analysis. Further investigation utilizing a trypsin accessibility assay suggested the potential for BrkA-mediated export of MTT5. Additionally, the zinc-binding capacity of BrkA-MTT5 was evaluated by an Arabidopsis thaliana root growth assay which demonstrated statistically significant differences between bacteria-treated and non-treated conditions. Overall, these findings highlight the potential for BrkA-mediated export of MTT5 and lay the foundation for further research aimed at harnessing the bacterial surface display system for heavy metal bioremediation.

title: Bivalent Inhibitor Development for a Dynamic Epigenetic Tandem Reader Protein Using a Combinatorial Histone Code
abstract: Epigenetic readers are a class of proteins that recognize specific chemical modifications on histones to differentially regulate gene expression. Aberrant expression of readers can drive the progression of many diseases and cancers, making this protein class viable therapeutic targets. Understanding the landscape of histone modifications recognized by reader domains, and the structural mechanisms that drive these molecular recognition events, is crucial for guiding the design of pharmaceutically relevant chemical probes. BPTF contains a plant homeodomain (PHD) finger and tandem bromodomain (BRD). Here, we expand upon previous studies that found the BPTF BRD can engage acetyllysine modifications on the N-terminus of histone H3. We uncover H3K4me 3 K14ac as the specific modifications recognized by the PHD BRD cassette, which is confirmed by crystallography. Using orthogonal methods, our work explores how these modifications can be read cooperatively, including in cis . We report the first experimental evidence proposing a ligand-induced conformational change between the two reader domains of BPTF, supporting previous computational approaches that have predicted a macromolecular rearr

title: Screening of Modular Self‐Assembling Peptides for Targeting the MDM2 Protein
abstract: The MDM2-p53 signaling axis governs the homeostatic balance between cell proliferation and apoptosis, and its aberrant activation drives tumor onset and progression. Disruption of this pathway therefore represents an effective strategy to suppress malignant growth. Here, the one-bead one-compound (OBOC) peptide library is designed to identify self-assembling peptide leads that specifically target MDM2. Differently from conventional static inhibitory peptides, the identified peptides exhibit unique target-triggered self-assembly behavior upon specific binding to MDM2 protein. The peptides first bind MDM2 with high nanomolar affinity and subsequently assemble into dense nanofibrous structures in situ, which sterically and efficiently disrupt the MDM2-p53 interaction. In vitro cellular assays demonstrate that these self-assembled peptide nanofibers remarkably suppress tumor cell proliferation and migration. Collectively, this work discovers a novel class of MDM2-targeting peptides with programmable self-assembly property, providing an innovative structural design strategy and promising precursor candidates for future MDM2-p53 pathway-targeted antitumor research.

title: Retroviral CA subdomains encode their immature assembly properties independently of strict subdomain co-pairing
abstract: Retroviral capsid (CA) proteins display a conserved two-domain architecture consisting of independently folded N-terminal (CA-NTD) and a C-terminal (CA-CTD) subdomains. Despite a strong CA protein fold conservation, different retrovirus species are employing remarkably variable geometrical solutions to stabilize the CA lattices that form the immature virus particle. For instance, while HTLV-1 has been reported to use the CA-NTD to stabilize its immature lattice, HIV-1 relies on a contiguous structural unit formed of the CA-CTD together with the short spacer peptide 1 (SP1). This raises the question whether immature assembly phenotypes are modular features encoded independently into individual CA subdomains, or if they are emergent features requiring strict co-pairing or co-evolution between CA subdomains of a given species. To test for these two options, we have designed chimeric proteins pairing the CA subdomains of HTLV-1 and HIV-1. Our results show that the CA subdomains of HIV-1 and HTLV-1 can be clearly distinguished into assembly-passive and assembly-driving categories. Moreover, pairing assembly-driving subdomains from the two retrovirus species still allows them to independ

title: In Silico Design and Comprehensive Evaluation of a Novel Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Chandipura Virus
abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV), an emerging arthropod-borne member of the Rhabdovirdae family, is an acute neurotropic pathogen responsible for explosive outbreak of acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) predominantly in pediatric cohorts. with mortality rates exceeding 70%, seizures, and death within 24 to 48 hours. the complete lack of approved antiviral therapies or preventive vaccine makes this a severe global health threat. to address this ,our study utilized a computational reverse vaccinology approach to design and structurally evaluate a novel epitope-based vaccine construct. and computationally validate a 104-amino-acid chimeric peptide vaccine candidate targeting immunoinformatics screening confirmed that the construct possesses strong predicted protective antigencity (VaxiJen >0.40) complete absence of allergenicity across multiple machine-learning models (AllerTopv2.0 and AllergenFP v1.0),and zero cellular or hemolytic toxicity (ToxinPred SVM regression score < 0.0). physicochemical characterization via EXPASY ProtParam established an 11.76 kDa construct comprising 1,653 atoms, with a theoretical isoelectric point of 7.78 an instability index of 39.92 (classifying the protein as p

title: ELiAH2: update of the atlas of E3 ligases in human tissues by integrating tissue-specificity and docking properties of ligands for targeted protein degradation
abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD), including proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), requires coordinated selection of E3 ligases, target proteins, and ligands to achieve efficient and tissue-selective degradation. However, current TPD resources provide limited support for integrating tissue-specific transcriptomic evidence with structural compatibility during early candidate prioritization. Here, we present ELiAH2, an expanded database for transcriptome- and structure-guided prioritization of TPD candidates. ELiAH2 integrates GTEx RNA-seq profiles across 24 human tissues to characterize tissue-specific expression patterns of E3 ligases and target genes. Compared with the previous version, ELiAH, current update presented over 200% of expansion for the number of covered tissues and samples. Previously, E3 ligase-target gene associations were inferred using mutual information-based network analysis, enabling users to explore transcriptomic relationships. To further support structural evaluation, ELiAH2 provides large-scale docking datasets comprising 827,385 E3 ligase-target protein pairs and 7,800,521 protein-ligand docking models, including E3 ligase-ligand and target protein-li

title: From Tariffs to the Dinner Table: US Beef Prices Under 2025 Tariff Policies
abstract: ABSTRACT The 2025 US tariff policies provide a natural experiment to examine how import restrictions affect domestic prices. We construct a partial‐equilibrium Armington model in which the pass‐through of a tariff into retail prices decreases with a product's domestic supply elasticity and increases with its import dependence. We test these predictions using 2024–2026 US metropolitan‐level price data and a difference‐in‐differences design that compares beef products against alternative protein products and other consumer items. We find that tariffs significantly increased beef prices by approximately 8%–11% ($1.7–$2 per pound), with larger effects when domestic supply was more constrained and import dependence was higher, as the model predicts. These findings imply tariff assessments should weigh uneven consumer incidence, not aggregate price effects alone.

title: Subpocket-Aware Fragment-Based Docking Pipeline for Kinase Ligand Design: Methodology and a PKA Case Study
abstract: Abstract Protein kinases regulate signal transduction through phosphorylation, and their dysregulation drives diseases like cancer, autoimmune disorders, and Alzheimer’s, making them key drug targets. Fragment-based drug design offers a powerful route to kinase inhibitors but often neglects kinase-specific structural insights. While KinFragLib, a library consisting of 7486 fragments derived from kinase-ligand complexes, provides a rich resource, exhaustive recombination of its fragments is computationally demanding. Here, we present an efficient exploration strategy that integrates subpocket-guided fragment growing with template docking to navigate this vast chemical space. Our automated pipeline prioritizes kinase-specific structural information, enabling targeted generation of chemically diverse ligands. Applied to the PKA kinase, the approach produced 33758 candidate molecules with promising docking scores, of which 15 were synthesized. Seven molecules reduced kinase activity by more than 50% at an inhibitor concentration of 100 μM, and five of these compounds also showed promising efficacy at a concentration of 10 μM. title: Comparative silane surface functionalization strategies for enhanced Bloch surface wave biosensing of anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies
Genotype-specific molecular and functional trajectories in NGLY1 deficiency: a comparative multi-omics study of patient-derived iPSC neurons
abstract: Background NGLY1 deficiency is an ultra-rare congenital disorder of deglycosylation with prominent neurodevelopmental impairment and marked allelic heterogeneity. Prior human neuronal models have characterized NGLY1 loss largely within single genetic backgrounds, leaving open whether distinct patient genotypes converge on a shared molecular state or follow divergent routes. Because clinical presentations overlap across genotypes, resolving this question requires a direct, within-system comparison of multiple genotypes rather than characterization of any single line. Methods We generated iPSC-derived glutamatergic neurons from three patients carrying distinct biallelic NGLY1 genotypes (R401X/R401X, Q208X/G310G, L318P/R390P) and two healthy controls, and profiled them head-to-head using matched transcriptomics and proteomics at day 28, RNA to protein concordance and differential exon usage analysis, pathway and phenotype network integration, and longitudinal multielectrode array (MEA) recordings during early network maturation. title: ScopeNovo: a De Novo Peptide Sequencing Method Using Spectrum-Spectrum Similarity to Refine the Prediction Accuracy
abstract: MOTIVATION: De novo peptide sequencing from tandem mass spectra is essential for characterizing unknown proteins, identifying novel post-translational modifications, and analyzing samples without reference databases. While recent deep learning models have improved the predicted peptide accuracy, they typically select the predicted peptide sequence based solely on sequence-level decoding scores. Very often, high scores are assigned to peptides without the direct support from the observed mass spectrum. RESULTS: We present ScopeNovo, a de novo peptide sequencing method that improves predicted peptide accuracy by using spectrum-spectrum similarity between the input spectrum and the "representative" spectrum corresponding to the predicted peptide sequence. ScopeNovo generates multiple candidate peptides using an existing peptide de novo sequencing learning model and reranks candidates based on spectrum-spectrum similarity. To test our method, we use π-PrimeNovo as the base learning model. Experimental results on the standard nine-species benchmark datasets V1 and V2 show that ScopeNovo can substantially improve the prediction accuracy. title: Phospholipase Fluorogenic Probes and Molecular Determinants of Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate–Adenosine Monophosphate Binding to Cyclic Oligonucleotide-Based Antiphage Signaling System CapV
abstract: Cyclic oligonucleotide-based antiphage signaling systems (CBASS) protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection by producing cyclic nucleotide second messengers that activate downstream effector proteins. Cyclic guanosine monophosphate-adenosine monophosphate (cGAMP)-activated phospholipase in Vibrio (CapV) is a prevalent CBASS effector whose activity is commonly monitored using the commercially available fluorogenic substrate resorufin butyrate; however, this probe is hydrolyzed by both basal and activated CapV, limiting its usefulness in CapV-related studies. Here, we report the rational design and evaluation of a series of resorufin ester probes with varying acyl chain lengths to improve the fluorogenic assay used to monitor CapV (from Acinetobacter baumannii and Vibrio cholerae) activation. While resorufin butyrate and pentanoate exhibited substantial cGAMP-independent hydrolysis, resorufin octanoate and decanoate provided an optimal balance between catalytic turnover and activation-dependent discrimination, displaying over 5-fold and approximately 10-fold increases in hydrolysis, respectively, upon 3',3'-cGAMP activation. Using resorufin octanoate as a fluorogenic reporter, we

title: KARAKTERISTIK FISIKOKIMIA KERUPUK TELUR BERBASIS TAPIOKA DENGAN PENGGUNAAN TELUR AYAM (GALLUS GALLUS DOMESTICUS) DAN TELUR BEBEK (ANAS PLATYRHYNCHOS DOMESTICUS)
abstract: Tapioca crackers are traditional food products whose physicochemical properties are influenced by the composition of their ingredients, including the type of egg used. Differences in the functional properties of proteins in chicken eggs (Gallus gallus domesticus) and duck eggs (Anas platyrhynchos domesticus) are expected to affect the physicochemical characteristics of the resulting crackers. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of chicken and duck eggs on the physicochemical characteristics of tapioca crackers. A single-factor experimental design was employed using two treatments, namely chicken eggs and duck eggs, with ten replications for each treatment. The observed parameters included color (L*, a*, and b*), texture, and soluble protein content. Data were analyzed using an Independent Samples t-test at a 95% confidence level after fulfilling the assumptions of normality and homogeneity. The results showed that the type of egg had a significant effect (P<0.05) on the a* and b* color values but had no significant effect (P>0.05) on the L* value, texture, or soluble protein content. title: Distribution Characteristics and Prognostic Analysis of Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes and Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Malignant Melanoma
abstract: Context.— Several studies have reported the prognostic and therapeutic response value of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in patients with melanoma. However, the prognostic correlation of these markers assessed by immunohistochemistry staining remains contradictory. Objective.— To investigate the impact of TILs and TLSs on progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) across melanoma subtypes. Design.— Immunohistochemical staining for CD3, CD4, CD8, forkhead box protein 3 (FOXP3), CD20, and PD-L1 (programmed cell death–ligand 1) was combined with automated image analysis for density quantification. Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis evaluated the effects of PD-L1 expression and TIL and TLS distribution on PFS and OS. Results.— Clinicopathologic subtypes differed in multiple factors including TILs and immune cell counts. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed high intratumoral CD3 + (iCD3 + ), intratumoral CD8 + (iCD8 + ), and intratumoral CD20 + (iCD20 + ) cell counts and low peritumoral FOXP3 + (pFOXP3 + ) cell counts correlated with shorter OS; and high iCD8 + and iCD20 + cell counts and low intratumoral FOXP3 + (iFOXP3 + ), pe

title: What the Controlled-Vocabulary Layer Cannot Say About Where a Depression Biomarker Was Measured: A Meta Research Analysis of MeSH Sampling-Compartment Coding, January 2024–June 2026
abstract: Background: Peripheral biomarkers for major depressive disorder are accessible but correspond poorly to central nervous system processes, a point the evidence base can address only if its record registers the compartment in which each marker was measured. To determine, by meta research rather than evidence synthesis, whether the indexed record of recent depression biomarker research registersthe peripheral-central distinction, separating omission by indexers from absence mandated by the controlled vocabulary. That peripheral markers are imperfect proxies for central processes is established prior knowledge; the question here concerns the bibliographic infrastructure through which that literature is retrieved. Methods: PubMed records published between 1 January 2024 and 30 June 2026 matching a title/abstract query for depression and biomarker terms were retrieved (Tier 1, n = 1166); the MEDLINE-indexed subset formed the analysable corpus (Tier 2, n = 825). We extracted marker-level descriptors and site qualifiers, determined from the 2026 MeSH descriptor file whether /blood and /cerebrospinal fluid are allowable per descriptor, and stratified by publication type. title: Development and evaluation of herbal biotin gummies as an innovative nutraceutical delivery system
abstract: The growing demand for plant-based nutraceuticals and consumer-friendly dosage forms has driven the development of innovative formulations that combine efficacy, safety, and improved patient compliance. The present study focuses on the formulation and conceptual development of Herbal Biotin Gummies, designed as a palatable, plant-based alternative to conventional biotin supplements. Biotin (Vitamin B7) plays a vital role in maintaining healthy hair, skin, and nails, as well as supporting metabolic processes involving carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids. However, conventional biotin supplements are often available in tablet or capsule form, which may be less acceptable to certain populations and may contain animal-derived ingredients such as gelatin.In this study, a gummy formulation was conceptualized using plant-based gelling agent such as agar, natural sweeteners and herbal extracts rich in bioactive compounds. The formulation aims to enhance the bioavailability and acceptability of biotin while incorporating the additional benefits of herbal ingredients, including antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. The approach integrates principles of pharmaceutical formulation, nutr

title: In Vitro Assessment of Anticancer and Antiulithiatic Potential of Canna Indica L. Flowers
abstract: The present study was designed to evaluate the anticancer and antiurolithiatic potential of Canna indica L. along with molecular docking analysis to identify possible bioactive interactions. Anticancer activity was assessed using in vitro cytotoxicity assays against selected cancer cell lines, while antiurolithiatic activity was evaluated through inhibition of calcium oxalate crystallization. The extract exhibited significant anticancer activity with an IC₅₀ value of 60.24 µg/mL and a maximum inhibition of 60% at 100 µg/mL concentration. It also showed considerable antiurolithiatic activity with 75% inhibition of calcium oxalate crystal nucleation and aggregation and 50% dissolution activity. Molecular docking studies revealed strong binding affinities of phytoconstituents such as rutin and oleanolic acid with target proteins, showing docking scores ranging from −7.0 to −9.4 kcal/mol. The findings suggest that Canna indica L. possesses promising anticancer and antiurolithiatic therapeutic potential.

title: Integrating Gaussian Accelerated Molecular Dynamics, β-Variational Autoencoders, and Markov State Models Reveals the Activation Landscape of FGFR3 Kinase
abstract: Abstract Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) kinase plays a crucial role in cellular differentiation, proliferation, and skeletal development. Activation of the kinase domain through phosphorylation regulates the downstream signaling cascades, and its dysregulation leads to human dwarfism, skeletal dysplasia, and multiple cancers. However, the mechanistic basis of FGFR3 regulation by phosphorylation and ligand binding remains unclear. Here, we introduce an integrated GaMD-βVAE-MSM pipeline, a hybrid physics-ML framework for studying kinase activation. Gaussian-accelerated molecular dynamics (GaMD) enhances simulations by reducing the energy barrier. The variational autoencoder with tunable regularization was used for nonlinear dimension reduction and identifying slow collective variables. The Markov state model (MSM) was used for identifying metastable states spanning active-inactive conformations. Our results show that phosphorylation drives pronounced domain rearrangement and activation-loop dynamics.
