title: K9HeartCircDB: A circRNA Atlas of Tachypacing-Induced Canine Dilated Cardiomyopathy
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), a major cause of heart failure (HF), exhibits ventricular dilation, impaired systolic/diastolic function, arrythmias, and adverse cardiac remodeling. While genetic causes of DCM have been extensively studied, non-genetic and acquired forms of DCM-like HF are less well characterized, especially with respect to non-coding RNA regulation.Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are stable, covalently closed non-coding RNAs that regulate cellular function via sequestering miRNAs, RNA-binding proteins, or translation. Their role in canine HF that recapitulates features of non-genetic DCM remains largely unexplored.To address this, we developed K9HeartCircDB (https://www.k9heartcircdb.com/), a publicly accessible database that catalogs circRNAs expressed in canine left ventricular (LV) tissues under tachypacing-induced HF, a model of non-genetic DCM-like disease, and healthy control conditions. The online interface enables users to query and explore circRNAs based on exon composition, predicted miRNA binding sites, protein-coding potential, siRNA targets, and primer design for experimental validation.

title: Rationally Engineered Self-Assembling Protein Nanoparticles for Allergen-Specific Peanut Allergy Immunotherapy
abstract: Peanut allergy is a prevalent immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated food allergy that can cause life-threatening anaphylaxis. Current treatment options provide limited efficacy and variable durability of protection. While allergen-displaying virus-like particles (VLPs) have shown promise, their development is often constrained by limited design flexibility and manufacturing complexity. Here, we develop self-assembling protein nanoparticles (SApNPs) displaying the major allergens Ara h 2 and Ara h 6 as a modular platform for peanut allergy immunotherapy. Using the 60-mer TIP60 scaffold, we engineer nanoparticles by expanding particle size through α-helical insertion and replacing the human myosin-X segment with evolutionarily distant catfish homologs, followed by structure-guided and evolution-inspired optimization to enhance thermostability while minimizing human sequence content. Formulated with a Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist, these allergen-displaying SApNPs confer robust protection against peanut-induced anaphylaxis in both prophylactic and therapeutic settings. Mechanistically, SApNPs exhibit prolonged lymph node retention, sustained presentation on follicular dendritic cells,

title: A composite, host‐participatory haustorium links host compatibility to defence bifurcation in Alectra vogelii (Orobanchaceae)
abstract: Societal Impact Statement Parasitic weeds of the family Orobanchaceae are among the most damaging constraints on food production in the tropics, draining water and nutrients from their hosts and threatening the livelihoods of millions of smallholder farmers. Yellow witchweed ( Alectra vogelii ) can destroy entire legume harvests across sub‐Saharan Africa, where these crops are a primary source of dietary protein and household income. By revealing how a compatible host enables this parasite to develop, our work pinpoints the developmental and metabolic steps that turn an attachment into a damaging infection—knowledge that can guide the breeding of resistant crops and the design of more sustainable, targeted control of parasitic weeds. Summary Yellow witchweed ( Alectra vogelii Benth., Orobanchaceae) is an obligate hemiparasitic weed and a major pest of grain legumes across sub‐Saharan Africa, where it causes severe crop losses and threatens smallholder food security, yet its developmental biology and mechanisms of host compatibility remain poorly understood. By combining phenotypic, anatomical and transcriptomic analyses, we show that host compatibility in Alectra is expressed prima

title: Chickpea growth, nutrient acquisition and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal responses under contrasting phosphorus supply
abstract: This dataset contains individual plant-level measurements from a controlled pot experiment investigating the effects of phosphorus (P) supply and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal (AMF) inoculation on chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) growth and nutrient acquisition. The experiment followed a factorial design combining four chickpea cultivars, two P supply levels (0 and 30 mg P kg⁻¹ soil), and three AMF inoculation treatments: an uninoculated control, a single-species inoculum of Rhizophagus irregularis, and a four-species Rhizophagus inoculum. Each treatment combination included five replicates, resulting in 120 experimental units. The dataset includes shoot and root biomass, shoot P and N contents, AMF DNA abundance quantified by qPCR (gene copies ng⁻¹ root DNA), and glomalin-related soil protein (GRSP) concentration. AMF DNA abundance was not reported for uninoculated controls, and the corresponding entries are retained as missing values. A separate dataset contains 12 observations from a preliminary P dose–response experiment used to select the P supply level for the main experiment. These observations correspond to treatments without additional nitrogen supply and were used to fit a s

title: Peptide agonist design from GPCR sequences
abstract: Simplifying protein agonists into peptides, or identifying alternative peptide agonists, could substantially enhance the pharmaceutical utility of many GPCR and is therefore highly desirable for biomedical applications. However, de novo peptide design for these receptors remains challenging, as agonism requires both binding to and activation of the targe; such ontarget activity is difficult to incorporate by current approaches that primarily aims at binding. Here we report that based on cross-attention mechanism, our new model GRADE accurately predicts agonist-GPCR pairing using only sequences, and designed peptide agonists across multiple targets with success rates of 20%-40%. Further with the CCR/CXCR family as a focal group, GRADE resulted in agonist with expanded agonistic spectrum than natural chemokines, as well as target-specific agonists. Structural determination revealed GRADE-designed agonists bind to CCR5 orthosteric pocket with novel, reversed polarity of natural chemokines. In a murine model of tumor immune clearance, selected agonists activated CCR5-expressing CD8+ T cells and anti-tumor immunity, in particular the CCR5-specific agonist removed crossreactivity that is

title: Effects of Dietary White Ginger (Mondia Whitei) Root Meal on Growth Performance and Haemato-Biochemical Indices of Broiler Chickens
abstract: A 56-day feeding trial was conducted using 150-day-old broiler chicks to evaluate the effects of dietary white ginger root meal (WGRM) on growth performance, haemato-biochemical parameters. The birds were randomly allotted to five dietary treatments, consisting of 30 birds with three replicates of 10 birds, in a Completely Randomized Design (CRD). The experimental diets were supplemented with WGRM at 0 g/kg, 1.0 g/kg, 1.5 g/kg, 2.0 g/kg, and 2.5 g/kg, respectively. Inclusion of WGRM had no significant (P>0.05) effect on most growth performance parameters except for FCR, which was significantly better (P<0.05) in birds fed 2.0 g/kg 2.67±0.60 and poorer 3.59±0.55 at 2.5 g/kg inclusion levels. PCV, haemoglobin concentration, and RBC count were significantly (P<0.05) higher in birds receiving 1.0 and 1.5 g/kg WGRM than those on the other treatments. Birds fed diets with 2.5 g/kg WGRM recorded a significantly (P<0.05) lower WBC count than those fed 1.5 and 2.0 g/kg diets. Lymphocyte count was significantly (P<0.05) higher at 1.0 g/kg WGRM inclusion. Monocyte count was significantly (P<0.05) reduced in birds fed the control and 2.0 g/kg diets. title: Dual-graph deconvolution of enzyme fitness: an interpretable framework to identify and explain catalytic modulators
abstract: Models trained on protein sequences can predict mutational effects, but their outputs represent a convolution of different phenotypes. Isolating stability-independent activity effects is essential for rational enzyme design, allosteric drug design and functional annotation, yet existing pLM-based deconvolution methods lack interpretability. Here, we introduce a hybrid framework that pairs stability predictors with probabilistic graphical models of coevolution. Benchmarked on all enzymes with available multidimensional deep mutational scanning data, our framework isolates stability-independent activity effects with a fidelity that matches analogous pLM-based approaches. Crucially, we reveal biophysically plausible communication pathways that align with previous knowledge and that we validate with experimental data across a diverse set of targets. This hybrid approach merges statistical and geometric deep learning into a zero-shot, explainable tool for targeted engineering and mechanistic discovery.

title: Targeting TMEM16F‑Driven Membrane Remodeling: A Promising Strategy for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Development
abstract: With the continuous rise of epidemics with potential for global threats, the need for antiviral drug development continues to be essential. Most drugs approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) are direct-acting agents (DAAs), targeting specific viral proteins, thus restricting the range of applications of the antiviral. Due to the constant evolution of viruses, DAAs regularly have to be optimized or modified to maintain their inhibitory effect against emerging resistant variants. An alternative therapeutic approach to DAAs are host-directed agents (HDAs) which instead target host processes to inhibit viral infection. They offer more potential for broad-spectrum use if the targeted host processes are conserved across viral families. They are also more resistant to viral mutations. However, research has to be done to identify such strategic host targets. Previous work done on TMEM16F, a cell membrane Ca2+-activated scramblase, has identified it as an interesting candidate for host-directed antiviral strategies. TMEM16F’s role in phosphatidylserine (PS) translocation from the inner leaflet of the cell membrane to the outer leaflet is essential for microvesicle secretion. Howe

title: Translational insights from FAPI-conjugated nanoparticles: a systematic review of current applications and future directions
abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is overexpressed in the tumor microenvironment (TME), bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), and stromal fibroblasts, making it a highly effective target for therapeutic intervention. The crucial novelty of conjugating FAP inhibitors (FAPIs) to nanoparticles (NPs) compared to conventional FAPI-based systems, as a next-generation targeted system, depends on the combination of FAP–targeted specificity with enhanced drug or radionuclide loading, prolonged tumor retention, and multifunctional theranostic capability using a single structure. A comprehensive systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar up to June 29, 2025, using MeSH terms and keywords such as “Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitor” OR “FAPI” AND “nanoparticles” OR “nanoparticle”. Duplicates, book chapters, non-English articles, reviews, and conference abstracts were excluded, and titles and abstracts were screened to select studies on FAPI, conjugated with NPs (FAPI-NPs). Evidence was synthesized based on study characteristics. This systematic review initially identified 106 studies from available datasets; after screening an

title: Mechanistic insights into NET1–UNC5B complex formation and Its targeted disruption by NP137 fab and NET1 peptide competitors
abstract: Netrin‑1, a secreted protein initially characterized for its role in axon guidance, has emerged as a critical mediator of cancer progression. Preclinical studies with the anti‑netrin‑1 antibody NP137, which blocks the netrin‑1–UNC5B interaction, have demonstrated reactivation of tumor suppressor functions and sensitization of cancer cells to chemotherapy. Here, we identified the molecular binding interface of the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex using integrative structural and quantitative biophysical analyses. We then determined how NP137 binding inhibits this interaction by sterically blocking key contact points within the interface. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we rationally designed peptides that disrupt the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex through interfering with heparin-mediated stabilization of the complex by binding to shared heparin-binding sites. This comprehensive structural and mechanistic analysis advances understanding of netrin‑1 signaling and establishes strategies for therapeutic intervention in netrin‑1-driven malignancies. Netrin-1 signaling controls cell fate and is a key target in cancer research. Here, authors describe the structural basis of netrin-1–UNC5B signaling a

title: A CXCR4-Targeted Dual-Acting Nanoconjugate Combines Protein-Toxin and Small-Molecule Warheads for Synergistic Cytotoxicity
abstract: Abstract Self-assembling multivalent protein nanoparticles with an architecture based on His-metal coordination and specific binding to cancer stem cells have emerged as promising tools for the selective delivery of microbial toxins in oncology, reaching precise cytotoxic effects. The incorporation of small-molecule drugs aimed at improving drug potency has so far been limited by the loss of stability and especially the loss of selectivity of the final products. Here, we have explored a site-specific conjugation method based on the Staphylococcus aureus sortase A, by which a CXCR4-targeted, engineered form of the diphtheria-toxin-derived protein warhead has been covalently enriched with the anti-tumoral agent monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). The resulting dual-acting nanoscale conjugate exhibits enhanced cytotoxicity over CXCR4+ cells without compromising selectivity in the intracellular delivery process. Interestingly, the combination of the microbial toxin and MMAE, empowered by the multivalent display of the CXCR4-ligand T22, shows significant synergistic cytotoxicity over the target cells. title: Advances in Substrate Recognition, Catalytic Mechanisms, and Engineering Applications of Alginate Lyases
abstract: Alginate lyases depolymerize alginate via β-elimination and serve dual roles in brown-algal biorefining and antibiofilm therapy. Brown-algal and bacterial alginates differ substantially in O-acetylation, yet this key structural distinction and its implications for enzyme performance remain underappreciated. This review systematically integrates the complete causal chain from alginate polymer structure through enzyme recognition, catalytic mechanism, and protein engineering to bidirectional applications. We cover PL family classification, the structural basis of substrate specificity, engineering strategies including two-step activity stability optimization and AI-assisted design, and recent progress in tailored alginate oligosaccharide preparation and cystic fibrosis treatment. Our central analysis identifies a widespread substrate mismatch, as most enzymological characterization relies on non-acetylated sodium alginate, whereas the clinical target is heavily acetylated bacterial alginate. title: Data from Dual-MEK Inhibitor Atebimetinib Displays Broad Activity in RAS- and RAF-Mutant Tumors via Deep Cyclic Inhibition and Resisting RAF Bypass
abstract: Abstract Inappropriate activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway, often stemming from activating mutations in RAS or RAF, represents one of the most common oncogenic events in human cancer. However, currently approved RAS/RAF inhibitors target specific mutants that are only present in a small proportion of RAS- or RAF-activated tumors. Current MEK inhibitors (MEKi) are associated with class-effect toxicities and tumor escape via CRAF bypass of MEK blockade. To address these issues, we designed atebimetinib to resist CRAF-mediated bypass and enable a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic profile termed deep cyclic inhibition (DCI), an approach that transiently but deeply suppresses oncogenic signaling while allowing daily physiologic reset. Unlike chronic or intermittent approaches, DCI optimizes depth and duration of MEK suppression on a daily cycle, blunting rebound signaling while preserving recovery windows for normal tissues. Functioning as an allosteric, selective MEKi, atebimetinib potently inhibited ERK phosphorylation in vitro and in vivo, resisted CRAF bypass, and was well tolerated and more efficacious in xenograft models of cancer compared with current

title: Clinical and Functional Outcomes of Single-Stage Posterior Surgical Management of Dorsal and Lumbar Spinal Tuberculosis: A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: Study Design: Prospective observational single-centre study.Purpose: To evaluate the clinical, functional, neurological and radiological outcomes of single-stage posterior surgical management of dorsal and lumbar spinal tuberculosis.Methods: Thirty consecutive patients with dorsal or lumbar spinal tuberculosis operated between November 2024 and May 2026 were studied. Surgery was indicated by a Comprehensive Spinal TB Score (CSTS) >6.5, progressive neurological deficit, instability or failed conservative therapy. All underwent posterior transpedicular decompression, debridement and pedicle screw fixation with peri-operative anti-tubercular therapy. The Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), Frankel grade, Cobb angle, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) were recorded pre-operatively and at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. Paired t-tests and the chi-square test were used.Results: Mean age was 35.6 years with equal sex distribution; 18 lesions were thoracic and 12 lumbar. ODI improved from 78.87±15.83 to 21.33±16.79 (−57.53; t=21.87) and VAS from 7.37±1.27 to 1.47±0.51 (−5.90; t=26.03), both p<0.001. Kyphosis corrected from 25.63°±18.25° to 10

title: Endogenous protein adsorption and functional presentation at bone-regenerative biointerfaces
abstract: Bone-regenerative materials rapidly acquire proteins from blood, marrow fluid, and the surrounding tissue. The resulting interface depends on protein quantity, identity, orientation, conformation, and exchange, rather than total adsorption alone. This narrative critical review examines selected mechanisms through which these features influence receptor recognition and responses relevant to bone repair. We use the descriptive term interfacial protein state and propose a joint reporting profile for comparisons made under matched exposure and sampling conditions. Primary evidence is distinguished by protein source, experimental setting, causal perturbation, and limits of interpretation. The strongest mechanistic examples concern fibronectin presentation and integrin signaling, selected fibrinogen-dependent inflammatory pathways, and material-assisted presentation of exogenous growth factors. Quantitative examples of surface density, accessibility, dissociation, and retained BMP-2 dose are reported with their experimental conditions. title: Countering Nipah Virus: A Review of Pathogenesis, Countermeasure Design, and Biosecurity Challenges
abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a zoonotic pathogen classified by the World Health Organization as a priority pathogen with epidemic potential.Driven by distinct viral lineages in Malaysia and Bangladesh, this pathogen can induce severe respiratory illness and lethal encephalitis, with human mortality rates ranging from ~40% to ~75% across outbreak zones, depending on the strain.This review paper focuses on the zoonotic origins and molecular mechanisms underlying NiV infection while highlighting both current medical countermeasures and emerging translational avenues to counter NiV's capacity for host immune evasion.By mapping out how these novel therapeutic strategies target the host-pathogen interface, we aim to inspire future countermeasure development and improve clinical outcomes for this biosecurity-relevant disease. title: Data from Inhibition of Acetyl-CoA Carboxylase Induces Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and Augments the Efficacy of Anticancer Therapies
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Increased dependence on de novo fatty acid synthesis is a key feature of metabolic rewiring in cancer cells. Acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) is the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo fatty acid synthesis. We examined the anticancer activity of the ACC inhibitor, PF-05175157, alone and in combination with approved anticancer therapies. Experimental Design: PF-05175157 activity was assessed in high-throughput cell line screen and in mouse xenograft experiments. Drug–drug interactions were tested with 166 Food and Drug Administration (FDA)–approved agents. Mechanistic studies included lipid profiling and evaluation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and unfolded protein response (UPR) markers and downstream effects on cellular metabolism and viability. Results: PF-05175157 showed broad anticancer activity including in cells resistant to targeted therapies and inhibited tumor growth in xenograft experiments. Combination studies demonstrated enhanced efficacy with multiple FDA-approved anticancer drugs, including tyrosine kinase inhibitors and chemotherapy agents. title: GESP-MD: A Web for Automated Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Protein–Ligand Complexes
abstract: Reliable molecular dynamics (MD) simulation of protein–ligand complexes requires laborious, error-prone preparation steps, from quantum-mechanical charge derivation to system assembly, which limits its accessibility in medicinal chemistry research. Here we present GESP-MD, a web-based platform that automates the complete workflow starting from only a protein–ligand complex structure, a Gaussian input/output for GESP electrostatic potentials, and standard MD parameter files. The pipeline integrates RESP charge fitting (antechamber), GAFF parameterization (parmchk2/tleap), topology conversion (acpype), docking-pose-faithful complex assembly with automatic atom-order reconciliation, solvation, ion neutralization, energy minimization, NVT/NPT equilibration and production MD with the Amber99SB-ILDN force field, featuring job queuing, real-time log monitoring and one-click packaged outputs ready for downstream binding free-energy analysis. By converting a multi-day manual protocol into a single web submission, GESP-MD improves reproducibility and lowers the computational barrier for structure-based drug design.

title: Bottom-Up Simulation, Reconstruction, and Quantification of Macromolecule Sequences from Experimental Polymerizations
abstract: Motivated by the canonical sequence–structure–function paradigm, tools to characterize chemical patterning in natural biomacromolecules, from proteins to nucleic acids, have grown exponentially in recent years. However, analogous strategies for synthetic macromolecules remain in nascent stages, complicated by sequence polydispersity and analytical limitations. To address this, we have developed a comprehensive and open-source Python package, PRISM (polymer rate insights and sequence modeling), an end-to-end workflow that provides a path from experimental kinetics measurements to quantitative and qualitative metrics for describing chemical patterning in stochastic polymers. First, a numerical integration strategy was constructed to simulate and fit experimental data from reversible addition–fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization kinetics, enabling the facile estimation of relevant reactivity ratios. title: Protein‐Engineered Iron Nanoclusters as Hybrid Theranostic Materials for MRI Monitoring and Treatment of Cardiac Fibrosis
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating diagnostic imaging and therapy within a single platform remains a major challenge in precision medicine. Existing approaches mainly rely on multi‐component nanoparticles, increasing formulation complexity and limiting modularity. However, versatile platforms combining imaging and therapeutic functionalities remain limited. Here, we present protein‐engineered iron nanoclusters (Prot‐FeNCs) as hybrid protein‐based systems combining Hsp90‐targeted antifibrotic activity with high‐performance T 1 ‐weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) contrast. Using engineered proteins displaying cysteine‐based coordination sites, we develop a green aqueous synthesis route to ultrasmall iron nanoclusters that provide strong positive T 1 MRI contrast, comparable to gadolinium‐based agents in a biocompatible iron‐based system. Physicochemical characterization confirms metal coordination and structural and functional integrity of the protein scaffold, supporting its use as a template for hybrid materials fabrication. Prot‐FeNCs exhibit minimal iron release, robust stability, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling sustained T 1 contrast in vitro. In a physiologic

title: The combination of microbial agent, organic fertilizer, and silica powder enhances oat yield and quality through regulating rhizosphere processes
abstract: Aims Soil salinization is a global challenge for sustainable agricultural development. Composite modifiers have the potential to boost the agricultural productivity of salinized soils. However, it’s still unclear whether it outperforms single modifiers in regulating rhizosphere soil properties, microbial communities, and forage yield and quality of different oat varieties ( Avena sativa L.) and the mechanisms. Methods In this field experiment in 2023–2024 in the arid western China, five modifier treatments, namely CK (control group without any modifier), TJ (microbial agent), TF (organic fertilizer), TG (silica powder), and TJFG (microbial agent + organic fertilizer + silica powder), were designed for two oat varieties (TY 60, Tianyan 60; MST 2, Musite 2). Then, their effects on salinized soil properties, rhizosphere microbial communities, and the interaction between soil nutrient cycling and microbial composition were explored. Results The crude protein (CP) content of the two oat varieties peaked under the TJFG treatment. title: Advancing precision oncology: a critical review of in Silico tools for nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems
abstract: The advent of in silico approaches has added a new dimension to the design of nanoformulations for targeted drug delivery, particularly in cancer therapy. Such computer simulation-based methodologies offer an economic and efficient means for the targeted design and optimisation of drug delivery systems. With the growing interest in computational nanoformulations, owing to their potential to increase the delivery, bioavailability, and therapeutic efficacy of anticancer drugs, scaffolding tools in silico have become essential for their rational design. Through the simulation of molecular interactions, in silico models provide essential information on the dynamics of nanoparticles in biological systems, allowing the prediction and optimisation of their target efficiency and therapeutic efficacy. These computation-based methodologies are also essential for the design of personalised medicine, as they can reduce the systemic toxicity and side effects of conventional cancer therapies. The integration of in silico methodologies into drug nanoformulation research is a significant step toward more efficient, patient-specific therapy. title: C-Reactive Protein and Routine Coagulation Studies in Obstetric Patients with and without Recorded Clinical Complications in Ibadan, Nigeria
abstract: Background: Pregnancy alters inflammatory and haemostatic profiles, complicating the interpretation of routine laboratory measurements. Aim: This study compared C-reactive protein (CRP), prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time with kaolin (aPTTK) in obstetric participants with recorded clinical complications and apparently healthy pregnant controls in Ibadan, Nigeria. Study Design: Comparative case-control study. Place and Duration of Study: Adeoyo State Hospital, Ring Road, Ibadan, Oyo State, Nigeria. Data collection commenced in November 2025 following ethical approval and took place within the approved study period of 12 November 2025 to 11 November 2026. Methodology: The study included 250 participants, 150 in the clinical group and 100 controls. The clinical group comprised participants with various obstetric and medical conditions. CRP was measured by latex-enhanced immunoturbidimetry on the Abbott ARCHITECT c4000. PT and aPTTK were measured by duplicate manual clot-endpoint procedures. title: Mango Peel Fermented with Ethanol-Industry Yeast Waste and Urea Modulates In Vitro Rumen Fermentation, Nutrient Degradability, and Methane Concentration
abstract: This study evaluated mango peel co-fermented with fresh yeast waste from the ethanol industry and urea (YUFMP) as a ruminant supplement using the in vitro gas-production technique. A 2 × 4 factorial arrangement in a completely randomised design was used, with two roughage-to-concentrate (R:C) ratios (40:60 and 60:40; rice straw as roughage) and four YUFMP levels (0, 2%, 4%, and 6% of substrate dry matter, DM). Co-fermentation raised the crude protein of mango peel from 4.39% to 17.00% DM and reduced its total phenolic content from 100.30 to 73.49 mg GAE/g extract. The 40:60 ratio gave higher in vitro degradability of DM, organic matter, neutral detergent fibre (IVNDFD), and true DM (IVTD) than the 60:40 ratio at 12 and 24 h (p < 0.01), and higher total volatile fatty acids (VFA) at 24 h (65.56 vs. 57.16 mmol/L; p < 0.01). YUFMP increased asymptotic gas production from 87.85 to 100.47–102.58 mL/0.5 g DM (p < 0.01) and cumulative gas production at 12–96 h (p < 0.05), with linear and quadratic trends. At 24 h, IVNDFD and IVTD were highest at 6% YUFMP (47.90 and 69.30%; p < 0.05). The protozoal population declined linearly with YUFMP (12.75 to 9.00 × 105 cells/mL at 24 h; p < 0.01), as

title: Biological Complexity and Cryptographic Secrecy: Reproducible Key Recovery and a Structured Evidence Audit of Bio-Derived Key Schemes
abstract: Bio-derived key schemes build cryptographic keys from biological material: protein structures, DNA and RNA sequences, amino-acid chains, proteinoid assemblies. This paper audits the class against a protocol drafted prospectively, refined during a pre-specified pilot, and frozen before the main screening and extraction, and tests its central claim empirically. No audited study reported a defensible attacker-conditioned min-entropy for its complete secret; the key-space figures instead measured an output or encoding-table size, a descriptor length, or a parameter-range product. A structured evidence audit of twelve studies finds that the biological material rarely holds the secret, that the evidence concerns the randomness of outputs rather than the secrecy of keys, and that no study provided a publicly linked runnable implementation. On three schemes (the two whose secret is a selection from a public set and one encoding scheme) we recover keys from the first two and bound the entropy of the third. Urinary biomarkers in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: translating multiplex and genomic liquid biopsies into clinical practice
abstract: Urinary biomarkers have long promised to reduce the cystoscopy burden in bladder cancer, but a persistent gap separates assay performance from clinical practice. This review synthesizes the shift from protein-based tests to multiplex, genomic, and extracellular-vesicle liquid biopsies, including minimal residual disease detection and therapy selection, and sets out an implementation roadmap spanning pre-analytical standardization, decision thresholds, and pragmatic trial design.

title: Engineering Protein Stability in Dissolving Microneedle Patches: Mechanistic Principles, Polymer Engineering, Formulation Strategies, and Clinical Translation for Insulin and Other Biologics
abstract: Protein therapeutics such as insulin, monoclonal antibodies, peptide hormones, cytokines, enzymes and vaccine antigens have revolutionized the treatment of chronic and complex diseases, but are currently constrained by adherence issues with frequent injection, cold-chain requirements and their intrinsic vulnerability to structural degradation. Dissolving microneedle (DMN) patches have recently been identified as a transdermal platform which allows minimally invasive, self-administered drug delivery and solid-state stabilization of fragile biologics. However, it is a significant challenge to keep the structural integrity and biological activity of proteins when developing the formulation, fabricating the microneedles, drying, storing the fabricates, and applying them to the skin. The mechanisms of molecular degradation (e.g., unfolding, aggregation, fibrillation, oxidation, deamidation, interface-induced denaturation) and stabilization (e.g., water replacement, vitrification, preferential hydration, and molecular confinement) all contribute to the stability of proteins in DMN matrices. title: Integrated single-cell and experimental analyses identify HMGA1 as a candidate regulator of lactate-responsive metabolic–immune crosstalk in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by extensive metabolic reprogramming, and immune evasion is closely linked to dysregulated lactate metabolism. However, the tumor-intrinsic mechanisms that translate extracellular lactate signals into Treg-associated immune remodeling remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic and multi-omics data to identify candidate mediators of lactate-linked metabolic–immune crosstalk in HCC. Methods Single-cell transcriptomic data were used to construct a cellular atlas of HCC and identify enriched immune subsets. Candidate genes were prioritized by intersecting Treg-related differentially expressed genes, TCGA-LIHC differential expression profiles, and a literature-curated set of lactylation-associated genes. Diagnostic performance and expression patterns were assessed in TCGA-LIHC and GSE25097, and survival associations were evaluated in TCGA-LIHC. Functional enrichment, protein–protein interaction network analysis, and virtual knockout simulations were also performed. title: Nanoimaging, Spectroscopy, and Biosensor Assays for Alternatively Spliced RNA Isoforms in Disease Diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Alternative splicing (AS) generates distinct mRNA isoforms, and frequently distinct proteins, from single genes; its dysregulation is established in cancer, neurodegeneration, and immune disease. Sequencing now nominates candidate splice events at scale, but a nominated event does not become a usable measurement until an isoform-discriminating sequence has been converted into a physical signal. Existing AS reviews concentrate on sequencing workflows, computational event calling, or disease catalogs; the assay-engineering step that follows target nomination remains comparatively underserved, and it is where most translational failures occur. This review addresses that gap. We group postsequencing detection into five classes defined by the physical origin of the signal: (i) fixed-tissue in situ localization, (ii) live-cell RNA imaging, (iii) plasmonic and spectroscopic readouts, (iv) label-free nanophotonic biosensing combined with site-specific RNA processing, and (v) protein-level proteogenomic confirmation. These classes are compared on target definition, reported analytical performance, multiplexing, matrix compatibility, perturbation risk, and clinical readiness. The re

title: Yijing Decoction improves oocyte quality and inhibits lactate accumulation in mice with diminished ovarian reserve
abstract: Background Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is characterized by a decline in both oocyte quantity and quality, leading to compromised fertility. Yijing Decoction (YJD) has demonstrated promising therapeutic potential in DOR management. Nevertheless, the mechanisms driving this phenomenon are still largely unclear. This study is designed to comprehensively assess the effects of YJD on ovarian reserve function and oocyte quality in DOR mice, while investigating its potential underlying mechanisms of action. Methods A DOR mouse model was established by administering cyclophosphamide via a single intraperitoneal injection. The therapeutic efficacy of YJD was systematically assessed through multiple functional and histological parameters, including ovarian index, estrous cycle regularity, serum sex hormone levels (FSH, LH, E 2 , AMH, and INH-B), and follicle counts, as well as the number, quality, and spindle morphology of metaphase I (MI) oocytes. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, ATP levels, pyruvate uptake, and lactate production were further quantified using commercially available ATP, pyruvate, and lactate assay kits. title: Replacement of Sugar with Stevia and Erythritol in Basundi (Indian Sweet)
abstract: Background: Basundi is a traditional concentrated milk sweet commonly prepared with added sucrose. Aims: To optimise the formulation of experimental basundi by evaluating the levels of stevia, erythritol and a stabiliser blend using response surface methodology (RSM) and to evaluate the quality characteristics of the optimised product. Study Design: The study was carried out using a face-centred central composite design (FCCD) within response surface methodology to evaluate and optimise the formulation of experimental basundi. A completely randomised design (CRD) was used to select a suitable flavouring agent. Place and Duration of Study: Dairy Technology Department, SMC College of Dairy Science, Kamdhenu University, Anand, Gujarat, India, from August 2025 to July 2026. Methodology: The milk concentration ratio (2.4-fold) and the rate of addition of caramel flavour (0.2 ml/kg of the final product) were fixed based on sensory evaluation. Accordingly, caramel flavour was added in each experimental run with varying levels of stevia, erythritol and the stabiliser blend. The responses considered for RSM included sensory attributes of basundi, namely flavour, body and texture, colour and

title: Enzymatic PET depolymerization: a review of engineering biocatalysts and systems for efficient plastic deconstruction
abstract: The ever-increasing accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste poses a severe threat to global ecosystems and human health. Biological upcycling (integrating enzymatic depolymerization with microbial conversion of the resulting monomers) has emerged as a promising approach to overcome the limitations of traditional mechanical and chemical recycling. This review provides a systematic and critical synthesis of recent advances in PET bio-upcycling, covering the period from 2016 to 2026. We first discuss the discovery, classification, structural features, and catalytic mechanisms of PET-hydrolyzing enzymes, highlighting the rate-limiting constraints imposed by glass transition temperature, substrate crystallinity, interfacial interactions, and product inhibition. We then evaluate protein engineering strategies that have dramatically enhanced thermostability, substrate binding, and multi-enzyme synergy, yielding benchmark variants capable of near-complete depolymerization of post-consumer PET within hours to days. Concurrent innovations in whole-cell biocatalysis, enzyme immobilization, surface display, and microbial consortia are examined, with emphasis on how metabolic div

title: Restoration of p53 function via hybrid strontium sulfite nanoparticles modified LNP improves the antitumor efficacy in breast cancers
abstract: The astounding success of mRNA empowers the diverse application of mRNA therapeutics in multiple genetic disorders. Besides the vaccines, the rational design of mRNA drugs has been explored widely to target the undruggable gene therapy for managing cancer. Restoration of the p53 tumor suppressor gene via introducing foreign p53-mRNA therapeutics may inhibit the growth and development of tumors. Since the development of mRNA transporting vehicles, liposome-based nanoparticles are the mainstay and are widely used in several ex vivo and clinical studies. But the delivery of mRNA outside the immune cells and hepatocytes for protein replacement therapy through systemic administartion is very limited and requires additional optimization. Here, we modified classical LNP (lipid nanoparticles) with SSNs (strontium sulfite nanoparticles) and complexed the LNP with p53 mRNA to improve the delivery efficiency of p53 mRNA. We assumed that restoration of p53 function in breast tumor cells might improve antitumor efficacy against breast cancer. We screened the SSNs-LNP to get the favorable physicochemical properties and to improve the delivery efficiency. The SSNs-LNP showed a threefold increase

title: Construction of SIGEX duo-directional reporter plasmid pSPPH21
abstract: Substrate-induced gene expression (SIGEX) methods use gene reporter systems to screen metagenomic libraries and identify novel catabolic genes. Commonly, these reporter systems incorporate promoter-less fluorescent protein genes downstream of an overhang-producing restriction site which allows metagenomic DNA fragments to be inserted and analyzed. SIGEX methods, however, lack the ability to detect genes which are inserted in the reverse orientation based on the unidirectional design of the SIGEX vector as determined by the overhangs produced during the cloning process. The insertion of a second oppositely oriented fluorescent reporter gene and a blunt-end producing restriction site would circumvent this limitation. In this study, we adapted a vector design from UBC iGEM to construct a duo-directional SIGEX plasmid reporter system (pSPPH21) containing green fluorescent protein (GFP) and red fluorescent protein (RFP) reporter genes. To build plasmid pSPPH21, a 766 base pair DNA fragment containing an NruI restriction site and an RFP gene was synthesized, digested, and cloned into the pSB1C3 vector containing a GFP and chloramphenicol resistance gene to construct the duo-directional r

title: The multifaceted role of 3-methyladenine in cancer therapy
Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
abstract: Abstract Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed

title: Nayancode Workbench: open-source bioinformatics and cheminformatics in the web browser
abstract: Free, open-source analysis studios that run entirely in the web browser: sequence analysis and cloning, read mapping (minimap2 and samtools in WebAssembly), variant interpretation, RNA-seq differential expression for any experimental design (validated against edgeR and limma) and enrichment, single-cell clustering, microbiome diversity, cheminformatics and QSAR, structure analysis and maximum-likelihood phylogenetics. Files are analysed on the user's computer; every result records its provenance and methods text. Published by Vivofold (https://vivofold.in).

title: Conservation guided reverse vaccinology for the design of a broadly immunogenic multi-epitope vaccine against monkeypox virus
abstract: Mpox, caused by the Monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a global public health concern following outbreaks beyond its traditional endemic regions. Although existing smallpox-derived vaccines provide partial protection, their limitations and declining population immunity highlight the need for safer and more targeted vaccine strategies. This study aimed to identify conserved antigenic targets and design a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against MPXV using a conservation-guided immunoinformatics approach. A dataset of 27 complete MPXV genomes (2001–2025) from diverse geographic regions was analyzed to identify highly conserved viral genes. Conserved surface-exposed proteins were prioritized for epitope prediction, including cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes. High-confidence epitopes were selected based on binding affinity, antigenicity, immunogenicity, toxicity, allergenicity, and absence of human sequence homology. Promiscuous epitopes with broad human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding were curated to maximize population coverage. Three multi-epitope vaccine constructs were designed using appropriate linkers and adjuvants. Structural modeling, molecul

title: Overcoming Barriers to Heterologous Gene Expression Uncovers Regulatory Constraints in the Mucoralean Pathogen Rhizopus delemar
abstract: Rhizopus species are a leading cause of mucormycosis, an aggressive and life-threatening invasive fungal disease that affects immunocompromised individuals. Despite their clinical importance, mucoralean pathogens, especially R. delemar, are difficult to manipulate genetically because of coenocytic growth, multinucleate hyphae, difficulty with transformation, and limited selectable markers. These obstacles hinder the study of innate stress resistance and disease mechanisms. Previous efforts to express heterologous genes or implement gene-editing systems with vectors designed for model fungi have been largely unsuccessful or inefficient in R. delemar, suggesting unique requirements for gene expression in this organism. In this study, we tested nuclear-targeted fluorescent protein expression and identified differences in proline and arginine codon usage between heterologous and endogenous coding sequences. We then evaluated gene expression efficiency using various combinations of heterologous and endogenous regulatory elements and coding sequences, including six promoters, two terminators, three histone fusion proteins, and two fluorescent reporters, with or without an exogenous nucle

title: YAP-dependent transcriptional responses in tenocytes under cyclic tensile loading: a conditional knockout RNA-sequencing study
abstract: Background Tendon injuries are prevalent across various populations and significantly impair quality of life, presenting substantial healthcare challenges. Purpose This study aimed to characterize Yes-associated protein (YAP) -dependent transcriptional responses in tenocytes under cyclic tensile loading, using a conditional YAP knockout approach combined with RNA sequencing. Given that tenocytes in vivo are continuously exposed to mechanical loading, this design was intended to identify genes whose regulation by YAP becomes critical under mechanical challenge. Methods Employing conditional gene knockout techniques with RosaCreERT2 YAP-floxed mice and mechanical loading protocols, alongside RNA sequencing and advanced bioinformatics analyses. Results We identified 54 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in tenocytes after YAP knockout, including six upregulated and 48 downregulated genes. Notably, upregulated genes included Gzmc and Gm28151, while downregulated genes included Car3 and Rgs2. title: Xenoglycosylation of the HIV-1 Glycan Shield Promotes Cross-Clade Neutralization and Diverse Human Antibody Lineages
abstract: Despite advances in HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein (Env)-based vaccine design, eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) remains a central challenge. Here, we identify core α(1,3)-fucose as a key modulator of neutralizing antibody (NAb) induction and breadth. Uncleaved prefusion-optimized (UFO) trimers and self-assembling protein nanoparticles (SApNPs) produced in High Five (Hi5) insect cells incorporate core α(1,3)-fucose into the Env glycan shield. Crystal structures of Hi5-produced BG505 UFO trimers in complex with bNAbs confirm native-like Env architecture and epitope presentation. In wild-type mice, these trimers and SApNPs elicit robust autologous and heterologous NAb responses. We then engineer Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells to co-express three insect- and plant-derived core α(1,3)-fucosyltransferases. The resulting immunogens carry fucosylated mammalian glycans and elicit cross-clade NAb responses in mice, supporting an important role for core α(1,3)-fucose in broadened neutralization. title: Synthesis and In Silico Studies of Benzofuran Ester Imines as Potential Antitubercular Agent System
abstract: Tuberculosis remains a major global health problem, and the emergence of drug-resistant strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis has intensified the search for new chemical entities with potential antimycobacterial activity. In this context, benzofuran derivatives represent attractive heterocyclic scaffolds in medicinal chemistry owing to their structural versatility and broad biological relevance. Herein, we report the synthesis and preliminary in silico evaluation of a small series of ten benzofuran ester imine derivatives designed as potential antitubercular agents. The target compounds were obtained in 45–89% yields via a Schiff base condensation reaction between an amino-benzofuran ester and benzaldehyde derivatives bearing substituents with varying electronic and steric properties. Notably, the products were isolated without column chromatography, highlighting the operational simplicity of the synthetic protocol. To complement the synthetic work, the benzofuran ester imines were evaluated using PASS online to estimate their probable biological activity spectrum. The prediction suggested potential antimycobacterial activity, supporting their further analysis through structure-bas

title: From Pollen to Plate: A Botanical Classification-Based Narrative Review of Fresh Fruit Allergy
abstract: Fruit consumption is a cornerstone of a healthy diet, providing essential micronutrients and bioactive compounds; however, fresh fruits may also trigger IgE-mediated allergic reactions, ranging from mild oral symptoms to potentially life-threatening anaphylaxis. Fruit allergy is a heterogeneous field characterized by diverse clinical phenotypes, botanical relationships, molecular sensitization profiles, and patterns of cross-reactivity. This narrative review organizes the available evidence according to 18 botanical families, adapting and extending an established botanical classification framework to the specific context of fresh fruit allergy. Botanical classification serves as a structured organizational framework rather than as a predictor of allergenic cross-reactivity, which is primarily determined by shared or homologous allergenic proteins and may occur both within and across botanical families. The review integrates botanical relationships with clinical manifestations, molecular allergen families, cross-reactivity, cofactors, diagnosis, and management. Clinical assessment should be individualized and based on the clinical history and appropriate in vivo and in vitro testing

title: Breathing the Lineage / Respirar el Linaje
abstract: Ancestral Transhumanism II argued that continuity of identity through a change of substrate is possible only where memory and process are not separable. That paper concerned the continuity of mind; this one concerns the continuity of body. If transhumanism's ambition extends to the flesh, redesigning respiration and the molecular base of life for environments the human body was never made for, it faces a parallel question: can the body be transfigured without severing the thread that makes it this lineage rather than a replacement that merely works? We argue that the answer turns on a distinction between two ways of redesigning: recovery, in which new function is read out of life's accumulated structural memory before it is written, and overwriting, in which it is specified against that memory. Structure-Based Design with Arylazopyrazoles to Enable High-Affinity Photoswitchable Inhibitors of N -Myristoyltransferase
abstract: Abstract Photopharmacology using photoswitches is a powerful way to reversibly control biological function with light, through the generation of photoswitchable synthetic ligands. While optimization of bioactive small molecules is increasingly driven by iterative experimental protein–ligand structures, structure-guided improvement in photoswitch photopharmacology using experimental structures remains rare. Here we report the development of the first photoswitchable inhibitors of the human enzyme N-myristoyltransferase 1 (HsNMT1), using an arylazopyrazole (AAP) as the switch motif. Through experimental structure-based design, we obtain inhibitors with single-digit nanomolar affinity for NMT, functional activity in cells, and good differential activity between E and Z photoswitch isomers. The availability of our highly potent ligands and protein–ligand structures, coupled with the excellent photoswitch properties of the AAP, allowed us to study the effect of protein binding on the switching events, including characterization of protein-bound Z → E photoisomerization kinetics for the first time. title: Duo-directionality of the substrate-induced expression screening vector pSPPH21 confirmed with a lac-operon screen
abstract: Within the microbial metabolic diversity lies the potential to utilize catabolic genes for medical, industrial and biotechnological applications. Substrate-induced gene-expression (SIGEX) screening vectors are promoter traps used to screen environmental metagenomic DNA libraries for novel catabolic genes. When a substrate-sensitive promoter is ligated into the plasmid and induced by a substrate, the host cell of the library will express a downstream promoter-less fluorescent reporter. Fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) can then be used to isolate positive clones for further study of the ligated promoter and to determine its associated catabolic genes. Despite their importance, traditional SIGEX vectors are limited to detecting promoters ligated in the same 5’ to 3’ direction as the reporter gene. This led to the development of pSPPH21, a duo-directional SIGEX plasmid, by Abrishamkar et al. It was designed to contain two oppositely oriented fluorescent reporters, green fluorescent protein (GFP) and red fluorescent protein (RFP) to allow for the detection of promoters ligated in either direction. title: The Stability–Release Paradox in Long-Acting Peptide and Protein Delivery: A Review of Material–Cargo Compatibility and Therapeutic Integrity
abstract: Long-acting peptide and protein delivery requires more than prolonged release; the therapeutic must remain chemically, physically, structurally, and functionally competent throughout processing, depot residence, and release. This review examines the stability–release paradox, in which material features introduced to extend residence can also alter cargo integrity. Rather than cataloging platforms or restating the need for biologic stabilization, the literature is organized around a cargo-specific compatibility question: whether a retention mechanism, depot microenvironment, and intended residence time remain compatible with preservation of therapeutic attributes required for activity. Published experimental studies and recent reviews available through 10 August 2026 were critically examined, with emphasis on poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) systems, hydrogels, affinity-based depots, self-assembling formulations, and translational studies linking release with stability or pharmacological performance. title: Beyond the Dominant Antigens: Computational Discovery and Experimental Validation of Cytomegalovirus T Cell Epitopes for Next Generation Vaccine Design (Preprint)
abstract: UNSTRUCTURED Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a ubiquitous beta herpesvirus that is usually controlled, but never cleared, by the immune system. It remains a major cause of morbidity in transplant recipients and the leading infectious cause of congenital disability. Cellular immunity, particularly CD8⁺ and CD4⁺ T cells, is the central arm of CMV control, and for three decades the tegument phosphoprotein pp65 (UL83) and the immediate early protein IE1 (UL123) have dominated T-cell epitope discovery, monitoring assays, adoptive therapy and vaccine design. Proteome wide mapping, immunopeptidomics and viral deletion studies now show that CMV specific T cells target a far broader set of viral proteins than this paradigm implies, including IE2, pp150, UL48, UL36, gB, UL86, UL138 and products of noncanonical open reading frames. In parallel, HLA specific machine learning predictors trained on mass spectrometry eluted ligands, protein language models and structure prediction networks have transformed the ability to nominate candidate epitopes in silico. title: Why sustainable protein transitions stall: the role of consumer attitudes in constraining plant-based meat adoption in South Africa
abstract: Purpose This study examines the dominant consumer attitudes limiting the sustained and frequent consumption of plant-based meat alternatives (PBMAs), specifically plant-based burger patties, among South African consumers. While prior research has focused on reducing barriers to initial trial, persistent psychological factors continue to constrain mainstream dietary integration. The study aims to identify these attitudinal barriers and assess their relative influence on regular consumption behaviour. Design/methodology/approach The study employs principal component analysis to identify and evaluate the dominant consumer attitudes, and regression analysis was used to determine their influence on PBMA consumption. Survey data from South African consumers were analysed to determine the extent to which specific psychological constructs predict reduced frequency of plant-based burger consumption. Demographic patterns associated with these attitudes were also examined. Findings Food technology neophobia and the belief that government, rather than individuals, should drive progressiveness in the food system emerged as the dominant psychological barriers to regular PBMA consumption. title: Nutritional Evaluation of Improved Maize Varieties and Their Effects on Broiler Performance
abstract: Maize is the principal dietary energy source in broiler production, but varietal differences may influence nutrient composition and productive responses. This study compared local maize, Abontem, and Honampa maize in broiler diets and evaluated their proximate composition, growth performance, carcass and organ characteristics, and haematological responses. Ninety 21-day-old Cobb 500 broilers were randomly assigned to three treatments in a completely randomized design, with three replicates of 10 birds, and fed for 35 days. Honampa had the highest crude protein (13.12%), ether extract (2.05%), and metabolizable energy (14.95 MJ/kg), while local maize had the lowest values for these variables. Birds fed Honampa recorded the highest daily feed intake (133.29 g/bird/day), daily weight gain (66.03 g/bird/day), gain-to-feed ratio (0.50), and final live weight (3.18 kg). Mortality did not differ among treatments. Honampa-fed birds also had the highest dressed carcass weight (2.70 kg) and breast muscle percentage (10.27%). title: The Effect of Warm Acupuncture Combined With Anti-Infective Therapy on Postoperative Recovery in Patients Undergoing Prostate Resection
abstract: Introduction The present work was designed to examine the impact of warm needle acupuncture administered alongside anti-infective agents on the postsurgical recuperation of individuals with benign prostatic hyperplasia who had undergone transurethral plasma kinetic prostatectomy (TUPKP). Methods Sixty-eight male patients were randomly divided into a control group (CON, short-term anti-infective therapy ≤48 h) and an observation group (OBS, CON plus warm acupuncture daily for 14 days), 34 each. title: Prehospital Point-of-Care GFAP for Detection of Intracranial Hemorrhage in Acute Nontraumatic Coma
abstract: Importance: Rapid identification of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with acute nontraumatic coma is critical to guiding triage and early management; however, prehospital diagnostic tools remain limited. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of prehospital whole-blood point-of-care measurement of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) for detecting ICH. Design, Setting, and Participants: This diagnostic study used data collected by a UK physician-paramedic helicopter emergency medical service between January 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. A consecutive sample of adult patients (aged ≥16 years) presenting with acute nontraumatic coma, defined as Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 12 or less, who underwent prehospital rapid sequence induction (RSI) of anesthesia with clinical suspicion of ICH were eligible for inclusion. Patients with traumatic pathology and those without follow-up data were excluded. Patients were observed for up for 30 days from hospital admission. Data analysis was performed in June 2026. title: Targeting Nuclear Lipid Droplets: Expanding Host-Directed Antiviral Therapies for Emerging Viral Threats
abstract: The increasing emergence of viral threats underscores the urgent need for broad-spectrum antiviral therapies that are resilient to viral mutation. Traditional direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) targeting virus-specific proteins face limitations in adaptability and durability. Host-directed strategic targets (HDSTs), which modulate host pathways essential for viral replication and immune response, represent a promising alternative. Lipid droplets (LDs) have been shown to play pivotal roles in viral replication, assembly, and immune modulation. Pharmacological or genetic disruption of LD biogenesis has demonstrated antiviral effects against multiple RNA viruses, including HCV, flaviviruses, and SARS-CoV-2. This paper explores the largely uncharacterized role of nuclear lipid droplets (nLDs) in host-virus interactions. Unlike cytoplasmic lipid droplets (cLDs), nLDs reside in the nucleus and are associated with nuclear membrane remodeling, stress responses, and intrinsic immunity. Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking
abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometric deep learning (GDL), and generative molecular design are increasingly used to accelerate antiviral discovery, yet their performance is often inferred from general protein-ligand benchmarks dominated by non-viral targets. This review argues that respiratory RNA virus polymerases are a high-value but comparatively underrepresented class of antiviral targets and a complementary test case for evaluating AI-guided drug discovery. title: A Phase 2 Trial Evaluating the Immunogenicity and Safety of an mRNA-Based Seasonal Influenza Vaccine Candidate Encoding Hemagglutinin and Neuraminidase
abstract: Influenza vaccines targeting both hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) might offer broader protection than current vaccines, which primarily target HA. This randomized phase 2 study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of an investigational mRNA-based trivalent seasonal influenza vaccine encoding HA and NA from A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria (FLUm3HA-3NA). Participants aged 18–64 years (younger adults) or 65–85 years (older adults) received one of several mRNA vaccine formulations—each containing different influenza A and B HA mRNA doses—or an age-appropriate licensed seasonal influenza vaccine as a comparator. Four formulations per age cohort were tested in part 1 of the study, and one formulation per age cohort in part 2. Day-29 hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and NA inhibition (NI) responses were assessed as primary and secondary endpoints, respectively, safety/reactogenicity as the secondary, and virus neutralization as the tertiary endpoint.
